title: Replace false WASM component-count claim with certified topology evidence
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND FALSE CLAIM
The native interval-frame receipt proves that a connected negative subset exists inside a bounded frame; it explicitly does not prove the full negative set has exactly one connected component. The WASM campaign nevertheless documents a single bounded component and emits component_count=1 whenever certified_inside && bounded. This does not exclude additional disconnected negative components inside the frame or negative exterior regions. A single finite-difference Hessian sample is local evidence, not a global Morse or component-count theorem.

MISSION
Immediately make the public result epistemically truthful while building the ambitious exact topology path. Expose a typed CertifiedEnclosedComponentExists or ComponentCountLowerBound(1) result from the existing frame evidence. Emit ExactComponentCount only from a new global certificate combining bounded cubical/interval subdivision, sign-certified exterior, adjacency/connectivity homology, interval critical-point/Morse or Conley evidence where needed, and sheaf-glued local-to-global coverage. Unknown/partial/refuted states remain first-class.

ACCEPTANCE
- Existing frame-only fixture no longer serializes exact count 1. Legacy field, if ABI-stable retention is mandatory, carries unknown/sentinel plus explicit status and cannot be interpreted as exact.
- Exact count requires complete admitted domain cover, interval sign exclusion or certified cell classification, boundary/exterior certificate, connectivity/homology witness, unresolved-cell accounting, discretization/refinement stability, units, budgets, and source identity.
- Counterexamples with two interior wells, hidden narrow bridge, sub-grid island, exterior negative region, boundary tangency, degenerate critical set, and interval Unknown refuse exact count.
- G0 typed-state/serialization laws; G1 manufactured one/two-component fields; G3 refinement, chart permutation, coordinate/unit rescaling, and sheaf cover regrouping; G4 cancellation/fault during subdivision/gluing with no partial exact claim; G5 replay.
- No-mock native-to-WASM E2E logs cell classifications, unresolved cells, adjacency/betti evidence, exterior proof, refinement history, budgets, cancellation/finalization, status, and artifact identity.
- Preserve ambition: this Bead removes only the unsupported shortcut and explicitly delivers an exact-count theorem path. Central fs-neuroshape-e2e/fs-wasm/fs-viz union, clippy, and DSR required before closure.

title: Make planner cost evidence machine-scoped, bounded, and numerically fail-closed
description: fs-plan's cost evidence path is not production-sound. cost_model_from_tune scans every shape/machine row for a kernel, contradicting its per-(operator x shape x machine) contract and allowing foreign hardware to steer routing; its tests seed an ad-hoc {elems_per_sec,elements} JSON shape while production fs-roofline writes receipt-v3 elems_per_sec_bits plus nested measurement.elements, so the nominal tune->model loop does not consume the real producer schema; json_f64_field can match keys inside JSON strings/duplicates. PlanCostOracle::record clamps negative/NaN timings toward 1e-12 or swallows observe errors, so invalid measurements can become routing authority. CostModel observations are unbounded and refit/sort on every append; centered-fit/prediction arithmetic is not checked for nonfinite results; empty calibration/relative-error probes report perfect values. Repair with exact machine+shape loader keys, strict bounded receipt decoding/version checks, no foreign-row mixing, bounded observations/work, transactional stable fitting, finite ordered quantile checks, structured invalid-record propagation through router execution, and non-vacuous evaluation refusals. Add real roofline-receipt integration, hostile JSON/duplicate key, machine/shape isolation, invalid observation, fit-degeneracy, cap/limit+1, and empty-evaluation regressions.

title: Reconcile gradient-check FD step scaling with its public contract
description: fs-adjoint::verify_gradient documents that eps is scaled per direction by ||p||/||d||, but the implementation perturbs literal p +/- eps*d. The claimed scale normalization is therefore absent, so verification sensitivity changes with parameter and direction magnitude and callers cannot know which finite-difference experiment the certificate represents. Keep this separate from frankensim-ru03 so non-finite fail-closed hardening does not silently change finite-path arithmetic. Decide and encode the authoritative step semantics; if norm scaling is intended, define zero/tiny norm behavior, overflow admission, and the exact scale formula; otherwise correct all public contract language and make literal-step semantics explicit. Acceptance: scale-rescaling metamorphic tests, zero direction/zero point boundaries, extreme finite magnitudes, deterministic ordered pairs, and contract/API agreement.
close_reason: Literal finite-difference semantics reconciled with API/contract and scale-rescaling plus tiny-direction regressions passed in exact RCH proof.

title: fs-recompute: determinism trip-wire identity includes a measured output (achieved_error), so output-co-varying non-determinism evades it
description:
Deep-review observation (2026-07-12), LOW/borderline — the current behavior is CONTRACT-CONFORMANT; this is a design/honesty note, not a clear defect. Recorded so the crate owner can decide.

## Observation
Store::put keys the DeterminismViolation trip-wire on the FULL 7-field content_hash (lib.rs:494), which per CONTRACT invariant 1 is 'sensitive to EVERY one of the seven fields' — INCLUDING achieved_error and required_tolerance. achieved_error is a MEASURED OUTPUT of the computation, not an input. So a genuinely non-deterministic op (unordered reduction / unstable sort — exactly the causes the violation message names) that, on re-run, emits both different artifact bytes AND a different measured achieved_error produces a DIFFERENT 7-tuple → no collision at put:496 → it is Inserted as a SECOND node, and DeterminismViolation NEVER fires. can_skip (lib.rs:547-550) then normalizes achieved_error+required_tolerance out and matches BOTH divergent nodes (invariant 3, 'skip identity ignores recorded tolerances'), serving one non-deterministically while the ledger shows no violation.

## Why it is contract-conformant (why this is a bead, not a fix)
Invariant 1 defines the node identity as all seven fields; invariant 2 scopes the trip-wire to 'identical [full] record with different bytes'; invariant 3 makes skip identity tolerance-normalized. The certification (rcs-004) re-puts the SAME record (same achieved_error) under permuted thread orders, so a byte difference DOES trip there — the trip-wire works for the intended 'hold the record fixed, re-derive the artifact' use. The bypass only arises if a caller RE-MEASURES achieved_error on each put (natural for a truly non-deterministic op). So the crate's actual guarantee is 'for a fixed 7-tuple, the artifact is deterministic', which is weaker than the 5-tuple determinism the error MESSAGE implies.

## Two candidate hardenings (owner decides)
(a) Message honesty (golden-neutral): the DeterminismViolation Display (lib.rs:358-359) names '(op, inputs, params, code, seed)' — the 5-tuple — but the enforced identity is the 7-tuple. Reword to 'the same record (all seven fields, floats by bits)' so operators do not infer a stronger guarantee than is enforced. Safe, no behavior change.
(b) Stronger trip-wire (behavior + contract change): also police the 5-tuple — on put, scan for an existing node whose (op,inputs,params,code,seed) match but whose artifact differs, and raise DeterminismViolation regardless of achieved_error/tolerance. This catches output-co-varying non-determinism but changes invariant 1/2 semantics and could false-trip if required_tolerance legitimately drives the artifact (iterate-to-tolerance ops) — needs a design decision on whether required_tolerance is an INPUT or a query threshold (can_skip treats it as the latter). Coordinate with the CONTRACT.

Recommend (a) as a safe honesty fix; (b) only after the owner clarifies the tolerance-as-input question.

title: Represent legacy CutFEM stabilization through a canonical physical-coefficient API
description: ROOT CAUSE: fs-solid's compatibility facade must translate legacy beta*(lambda+2mu)/h and gamma*(lambda+2mu)h coefficients into fs-cutfem's dimensionless mu-scaled beta/gamma fields. For extreme but finite scale-separated inputs, beta or gamma times (lambda+2mu)/mu can overflow even when the physical stabilization product is finite, so exact legacy semantics cannot be represented by the current canonical input surface. WORK: add a checked canonical physical-coefficient or stable scaling input path in fs-cutfem, retain finite physical products without non-representable dimensionless intermediates, migrate fs-solid delegation, and add extreme-scale parity/refusal tests. ACCEPTANCE: ordinary operators remain bitwise stable, representable extreme physical coefficients assemble finitely, truly non-finite inputs refuse structurally, contracts state the exact domain, and DSR/RCH proof covers fs-cutfem/fs-solid consumers.

Add a neighboring G4 regression that releases a registry entry mid-race and proves the admitted held gate still fires without panic. Preserve the original panic-total Racer work. title: fs-roofline: attainment gate is self-normalizing under contention - a saturated machine passes vacuously
description: FOUND while running the 27d3 fft perf lane on trj during a load-68 window: the MachineAxes probe and the kernel measurement both ran under the same memory-crushing contention, so BOTH collapsed ~1000x (measured FFT throughput 0.156 GB/s; probed 'STREAM axis' ~0.2 GB/s on a ~200 GB/s Threadripper) and the attainment RATIO came out 0.89-0.94 = within_band, target_met TRUE - a vacuous pass the assert cannot distinguish from a real one. Worse, non-gated context rows show the tell (L2-resident attainment 39.32 = 3932% against the crushed DRAM axis) but nothing checks it. FIX DIRECTION (certifying-the-certifiers): (a) MachineAxes should carry ABSOLUTE plausibility floors per axis family (a modern x86/arm64 DRAM STREAM under, say, 5 GB/s single-thread = invalid environment) and measure() should REFUSE to gate (environment_invalid verdict, not within_band) when the axes fail them; (b) cross-check: any attainment > ~1.5 anywhere in the run indicates a stale/crushed axis - poison the whole run's gate; (c) optionally re-probe axes immediately after the kernel and require agreement within a band (drift = contention during the run). The 27d3 evidence rows (trj /data/tmp/fsfft.G9xuIN/test.log) are the counterexample fixture: a gate that passed while the machine was useless. Acceptance: replay the crushed-axes rows through the new guard = refused; a quiet-machine run still gates normally.
close_reason: GUARD LANDED (fs-roofline). THE DEFECT (found live during the 27d3 fft measurement): a load-68 window collapsed BOTH the MachineAxes STREAM probe AND the kernel run ~1000x together (probed axis 0.2 GB/s, kernel 0.156 GB/s, on a ~200 GB/s Threadripper) - the attainment RATIO self-normalized to 0.89-0.94 and the gate emitted a VACUOUS within_band / target_met=true; the non-gated L2 row carried the tell (attainment 39.32 = 3932%) but nothing checked it. THE FIX: (1) MachineAxes::plausible() - absolute floors (single-thread STREAM >= 5 GB/s, single-thread FMA >= 5 GFLOP/s - conservative 3-10x below any post-2015 reference machine; all-core must dominate single-thread; finite); (2) Verdict::EnvironmentInvalid - attainment_with_dispersion refuses to gate when the axes are implausible OR when attainment > 1.5 (the kernel outrunning its own roofline = axes probed under different conditions than the run; jitter-scale overshoot <= 1.5 still gates normally). A gate must never pass - or fail - on a machine that was useless while it was measured. REGRESSIONS: the exact 1n61 counterexample replayed (crushed axes + the fft spec at 89% ratio -> EnvironmentInvalid, was WithinBand); over-roof poisoning at 2x with healthy axes -> refused, 1.2x -> gates normally; rf_002 updated to accept the honest branch on contended hosts (it FIRED on my own machine mid-development - the guard catching its first live contaminated probe before the ink dried). EVIDENCE: fs-roofline 25/25 BOTH ISAs (trj /data/tmp/fsroof.sl2exo - the x86 run itself passing on a load-30-75 box demonstrates the branch logic working in the wild), clippy zero warnings, fmt. Certifying-the-certifiers: this was a false-certificate path in the MEASUREMENT layer - the same doctrine as the wa8i/9sf6 sweep, one level more meta.

title: Demote finite-difference neural gradients from certificate authority
description: ROOT CAUSE: MlpSdf::eval_grad computes each coordinate by an independently centered finite difference, but its API and CONTRACT currently say that returned vector has norm <= the certified global Lipschitz constant L. The analytic gradient of the continuous real MLP satisfies that theorem; coordinate secants sampled on different line segments do not form one common-point analytic gradient, so only componentwise secant bounds (and a generic sqrt(d)*L vector bound before floating error) follow. Floating evaluation error further prevents this diagnostic from carrying exact certificate authority. MISSION: retain the useful deterministic finite-difference diagnostic but explicitly separate it from the analytic-gradient theorem and all authority-bearing witnesses; correct the spectral_normalize equals/at-most contract wording; replace the false norm test with mutation-sensitive diagnostic/no-authority coverage and deterministic replay. Reserve certified gradient authority for AD or interval-derivative enclosures bound to implementation semantics and error budgets. ACCEPTANCE: no public docs, types, tests, topology reports, or wire fields treat the finite-difference vector as a certified analytic gradient; functionality remains available; focused fs-rep-neural plus downstream union, clippy, and DSR green. Code-first wave; centralized proof pending.

The false vector-norm<=L test was replaced by deterministic replay plus clearly diagnostic componentwise/generic sqrt(d)L sampling, and CONTRACT no-claim language reserves derivative authority for AD or interval-derivative evidence. Also corrected spectral_normalize equals-bound prose to certified upper bound at most bound and L=product U_i. Central fs-rep-neural/downstream proof pending; keep IN_PROGRESS.

title: I10.1+ Certify the identifiability authority boundary beyond schema v3
description:
Background
I10.1 v3 now closes the declared problem, source-admission, execution, and assessment graphs, but fresh-eyes review found several deliberately documented promotion boundaries that deserve a coherent follow-up program rather than hidden TODOs.

Goal
Turn those no-claim boundaries into independently versioned, evidence-bearing capabilities without weakening the current fail-closed schema or delaying honest closure of I10.1. The program covers identity-certifier completeness, transactional registry governance, authority-graph redaction, pre-allocation resource admission, signed synthetic provenance, richer measures, exact experiment/metrology/raw-record authority, covariance certification, and statistically adequate shared-data likelihoods.

Program rules
Each child depends on the admitted I10.1 substrate. Identity-bearing children additionally wait for the strengthened identity-governance children. Each implementation must preserve exact units, versions, budgets, provenance, cancellation/drain, deterministic replay, mutation evidence, and explicit no-claim boundaries. Every child ships focused unit/property tests and a no-mock end-to-end script with bounded structured JSON logging. This epic is a rollup and closes only when every child is independently green.

title: I10.1+ Ratchet tuple layouts and variant payloads in identity byte-schema governance
description:
Root cause
The current identity checker directly parses braced structs and variants, but tuple structs and tuple-payload enum variants cannot be registered as byte-schema sources. Adding constructor and classifier functions to schema_functions protects the implementation fingerprint, yet a same-version tuple field or ordering change can still escape the hard byte-schema history check.

Technical approach
Extend xtask identity declarations with canonical variant-qualified tuple fields and tuple-struct positions. Bind owner type, variant tag, field index, Rust type, wire role, presence rule, encoder/decoder emission, semantic classification, and nested child identity. Register the live GaugeProbabilityThreshold, GaugeActionReference, FiberCardinalityBound, ClaimSubject, ClaimScope, and every other tuple carrier reached by the four I10.1 identity stages. Preserve a deterministic migration story for existing registry history; never force-generate over same-version drift.

Acceptance and tests
G0 mutates each tuple field type, index, variant tag, presence rule, encoder ordering, and semantic/excluded classification and proves the exact expected byte-schema and dependent implementation fingerprints move. Equivalent formatting and nonsemantic local renames do not move them. G3 compares declaration-derived layouts with actual canonical preimages. G4 rejects duplicate indices, gaps, ambiguous variants, undeclared payloads, recursive cycles without explicit bundle governance, stale history, and partial generation. G5 proves stable registry output. The test and no-mock xtask E2E log identity ID/version/domain, owner/variant/index, old/new fingerprints, dependency closure, mutation target, refusal, and generated artifact hashes.

title: I10.1+ Certify covariance and correlation positive-semidefiniteness
description:
Root cause and user impact
Correlation admission checks dimensions, finite values, unit diagonal, channel closure, and a floating-point positive-semidefinite predicate. Certificate machinery is security-critical for science: near-singular, badly scaled, or adversarial matrices need an independently checkable result and explicit tolerance semantics.

Technical approach
Define a CovarianceAdmissionReceipt binding canonical axis order, quantity/unit scaling, symmetry policy, finite entries, diagonal semantics, algorithm/build, arithmetic/tolerance policy, eigenvalue or pivot enclosures, rank/nullspace bounds, condition estimate, perturbation budget, and optional rational/interval witness. Use a fast deterministic baseline plus independent interval, higher-precision, exact-small-matrix, or principal-minor spot checks under certify-or-escalate. Distinguish PSD, positive definite, indefinite, inconclusive, and model-assumed states; never infer a covariance model from a matrix alone.

Acceptance and tests
G0 covers 0x0/1x1/max, permutations, signed zero, NaN/Inf, asymmetry, nonunit diagonal, exact singularity, repeated eigenvalues, near-negative modes, extreme scale, and every receipt mutation. Property tests synthesize PSD matrices and adversarial perturbations. G3 compares independent algorithms and unit-rescaled representations. G4 fuzzes hostile matrices, cancellation, budget exhaustion, and certifier disagreement, which must fail closed or escalate. G5 repeats bit-stably. A no-mock E2E admits noise models through the real I10.1 path and retains matrix hash, axes/units, arithmetic and tolerance, bounds, checker identities, disagreement/escalation, timings/memory, and verdict.

title: I10.1+ Give immutable raw records a first-class governed identity
description:
Background
ObservationSourceRef now binds dataset bytes, versioned locator domain/hash, and extraction receipt, and locator injectivity deliberately ignores reissuable receipts. The underlying immutable raw-record concept still lacks its own owner-local identity family, migration policy, collision adjudication, and cross-parser authority.

Technical approach
Define RawRecordIdentity from dataset byte-root identity, locator domain/version/hash, byte range or structured coordinate, acquisition channel, instrument, clock/time support, sample/support shape, and canonical parser-neutral selection semantics. Keep extraction, parsing, calibration, and transformation receipts as dependent provenance that move derived observation identities without manufacturing a second raw record. Define collision and alias adjudication, content addressing for ranges/chunks, streaming verification, schema migration, and capability-safe blind handles. Register direct byte-schema governance.

Acceptance and tests
G0 mutates every semantic coordinate, proves receipt reissue nonmovement of raw identity, and covers empty/range/max, overlap, duplicate locator, cross-dataset replay, domain/version confusion, and collisions. G3 proves equivalent chunk/range reconstruction only under exact Merkle or byte-range receipts. G4 covers streaming truncation, partial reads, cancellation/drain, huge records, malicious locators, and blind capability leaks. G5 is stable. A no-mock E2E ingests bytes, selects records through two parsers, reissues extraction receipts, partitions blind data, replays from a clean store, and logs dataset/root/locator/raw/derived hashes, byte ranges, parser receipts, capability class, budgets, and adjudication.

title: I10.1+ Verify joint likelihoods for shared, repeated, and hierarchical observations
description:
Background
I10.1 prevents repeated rows or cross-case datasets from silently masquerading as independent and requires one declared global joint-likelihood source. Structural consistency does not prove that the likelihood is normalized, statistically adequate, identifiable, robust, or correct for repeated and hierarchical sampling.

Technical approach
Define executable JointLikelihoodSpec and LikelihoodAdequacyReceipt for shared raw records, repeated trials, within-specimen and cross-specimen dependence, hierarchical populations, temporal/spatial kernels, missingness/censoring, parameter-dependent covariance, and observation sharing. Bind exact RawRecordIdentity sets, case/channel/QoI axes, marginal families and units, dependence/correlation model, grouping hierarchy, parameter roles/priors, normalization/support, computation/build, diagnostics, and validation partitions. Add certify-or-escalate normalization and score checks, simulation-based calibration, posterior predictive and residual dependence diagnostics, misspecification alternatives, and robust/sandwich paths. Adequacy remains scope-specific evidence, not universal truth.

Acceptance and tests
G0 covers duplicate/omitted consumers, grouping overlap, wrong global factor, marginal/dependence mismatch, nonnormalization, support holes, singular covariance, parameter alias, and identity mutations. G1 uses manufactured likelihoods with known scores/Fisher information. G2 canonical repeated-measures benchmarks. G3 verifies row/case permutation, unit rescaling, factorization equivalence under a proof receipt, and dependent counterexamples. G4 uses adversarial stopping, cancellation, large groups, drift, and misspecification. G5 is stable. A no-mock E2E runs shared-row and hierarchical coupon campaigns through admission, fitting, adequacy, falsification, and replay with exact logs of records/groups, model/build, normalization/error evidence, diagnostics, partitions, budgets, and claim scope.

title: I10.1+ Rename trust declarations so APIs cannot imply unverified authentication
description:
Root cause and user impact
Names such as TrustAuthentication and IssuerPolicy can be read as verified facts even though v3 intentionally records only a declaration and does not authenticate the issuer or policy. Test helpers using authenticated booleans reinforce that ambiguity.

Technical approach
Because the project is early-stage, rename the public surface directly rather than adding compatibility shims: use declaration-oriented names such as TrustAuthenticationDeclaration and DeclaredIssuerPolicy, externally receipted rather than externally trusted where verification is absent, and explicit policy-bound versus cryptographically verified states. Align errors, Debug output, contracts, tests, catalogs, agent JSON, and generated documentation. Preserve wire tags and scientific identity only if a governance test proves the rename is representation-only; otherwise perform an explicit versioned migration.

Acceptance and tests
Compile-time API fixtures, doctests, CLI/JSON snapshots, and mutation tests must make it impossible to produce a success message containing authenticated or verified unless a typed verifier actually established that predicate. Negative corpus tests cover misleading aliases and booleans. A no-mock E2E admits content-only, generic receipt, declared issuer-policy, verified-signature, expired, and revoked cases and checks human/agent wording parity. Logs carry exact evidence status and no-claim text without secrets. Document the migration and removal of ambiguous names.

title: I10.1+ Make identity golden and registry reconciliation transactional and frozen-tree exact
description:
Root cause
Identity checking, golden reconciliation, and registry generation are currently an all-or-nothing global operation. Golden rows must be copied from checker output, generation validates them before writing, and the registry writer replaces the whole file non-atomically. A concurrent edit, stale executable, interrupted write, or hybrid tree can corrupt or misattribute scientific identities.

Technical approach
Define one frozen-tree IdentityGovernanceTransaction. It records HEAD, dirty-path policy, checker executable identity, declaration closure, resolved implementation and byte-schema fingerprints, dependency graph, exact golden add/replace plan, prior registry/history, and intended output hashes. Stage all outputs, validate strict JSON and history in memory, fsync, then publish atomically under an explicit repository lock. Refuse stale executables, tree drift, mixed checker runs, duplicate rows, unknown deletions, same-version byte drift, or partial output publication. Provide dry-run and machine-readable repair plans.

Acceptance and tests
G0 freezes the transaction preimage and proves deterministic nine-row and future reconciliations. G3 replays checker advice into the planner without text scraping ambiguity. G4 injects interruption before every publish point, concurrent writers, stale binaries, dirty manifests, missing Git history, truncated files, invalid rows, and output-hash mismatch; old files remain intact or the complete new set appears. G5 repeats on both reference ISAs. A no-mock E2E performs check, plan, staged validation, generation, recheck, and clean-store replay while logging HEAD/tree, executable hash, identity IDs, old/new fingerprints, golden actions, registry schema, lock ownership, publish phases, and final hashes.

title: I10.1+ Close Debug and diagnostic redaction over the full public authority graph
description:
Root cause and user impact
The aggregate I10.1 carriers have bounded custom Debug output, but explicit getters expose nested public leaves that still derive Debug over hashes, source keys, artifact identities, policy identifiers, reasons, and collections. IdentifiabilityError diagnostics can also surface through panic reports. The current contract honestly excludes graph-wide and panic-path redaction; users need a certifiable boundary.

Technical approach
Inventory every public type reachable from problem, admission, execution, assessment, trust, evidence, and error values. Give authority or capability bearing leaves bounded manual Debug implementations or an explicit policy-aware redaction wrapper. Show only variants, schema families/versions, presence flags, safe counts, and stable pseudonymous handles. Preserve exact audit getters and serialized identities; redaction must never become authorization or destroy evidence. Define separate public, operator, and privileged diagnostic policies with explicit capability checks.

Acceptance and tests
G0 formats every reachable carrier and error, seeds unique secret sentinels in hashes, keys, IDs, receipts, policies, reasons, rows, and nested collections, and proves absence plus strict maximum formatted sizes. G3 checks exact getters and canonical bytes remain unchanged. G4 covers panic and unwrap formatting, cyclic-looking graphs, maximal collections, malicious control characters, concurrent logging, and cancellation without leaking partial values. G5 output is deterministic. A no-mock E2E drives malformed admission through CLI, JSON, tracing, FailureBundle, and report paths, then scans all retained logs/artifacts. Logs record policy, type path, redacted field classes, byte counts, sentinel-scan verdict, capability decision, and artifact hashes without recording the sentinels themselves.

title: I10.1+ Enforce pre-allocation structural work and declared memory budgets
description:
Root cause and user impact
Per-collection and final aggregate caps prevent unbounded accepted documents, but nested vectors can allocate and trigger cross-reference work before the final StructuralItemBudget check. ArtifactHeader memory_bytes is identity-bearing policy but is not yet compared with a deterministic working-set estimate.

Technical approach
Thread one decrementing DecodeAndAdmissionBudget through public constructors and canonical decoders. Charge outer and nested elements, encoded bytes, map nodes, cross-reference edges, comparison work, temporary canonicalization, and estimated peak bytes before Vec or map allocation and before Cartesian semantic traversal. Preserve final checks as defense in depth. Define a deterministic estimator with checked arithmetic, an explicit model/version, conservative overhead constants per supported ISA-independent layout class, and a receipt binding estimate, declared budget, observed high-water evidence when available, and refusal repair suggestions. Poll cancellation at bounded preflight and semantic-work tiles.

Acceptance and tests
G0 checks exact boundary and MAX+1 for every collection and nested combination, overflow, estimator monotonicity, and stable receipt identity. G3 proves container-order invariance and equivalent-encoding budget agreement. G4 uses count bombs, deeply nested legal inputs, tiny declared memory, cancellation at every phase, allocation-failure injection, and malicious transport; refusal occurs before charged allocation/work and leaves no partial artifact. G5 repeats deterministically. A no-mock E2E records budget model/version, charged items/bytes/work, declared and estimated peak, phase counters, cancellation latency, ranked repair, allocator high-water evidence, and final disposition.

title: I10.1+ Verify signed synthetic experiment execution provenance
description:
Background
DeclaredSyntheticSelfModel currently proves a caller-computable consistency relation among producer and the complete forward-model SourceRef. It intentionally does not prove that the experiment actually ran that executable or configuration. Without run provenance, an inverse-crime or stale-model substitution can masquerade as self-model data.

Technical approach
Define a versioned SyntheticExecutionReceipt and verifier binding experiment artifact/hash, exact dataset-byte root and observation manifest, executable/build and source-tree identity, producer and signer, exact forward-model SourceRef, constitutive/material/context identities, initial state, parameter block, mesh/discretization, solver/numerical policy, seed, deterministic mode, environment/device fingerprint, start/finalize clocks, output root, and custody chain. Sign a domain-separated preimage under an admitted issuer/trust policy with expiry and revocation semantics. Verification must distinguish byte integrity, signature validity, execution identity, scientific adequacy, and trust policy. Integrate the verified receipt into source admission and discrepancy applicability without making the no-discrepancy assumption automatic.

Acceptance and tests
G0 freezes preimage, signature, domain/version, and every field mutation. G3 replays the output manifest and proves receipt/model/data closure. G4 forges signatures, swaps any field, replays across experiment/split/model, uses expired or revoked keys, truncates outputs, injects clock ambiguity, and cancels verification with full drain. G5 is byte-stable. A real no-mock E2E runs a small synthetic coupon through the production executor, signs, admits, tampers, verifies offline, and replays from a clean store. Logs include public key/policy handles, receipt and artifact hashes, executable/build/model/data identities, clocks, verification stages, assumption status, and exact refusal without secrets.

title: I10.1+ Add atomic, discrete, mixture, hierarchical, and pushforward prior measures
description:
Background
Uniform is correctly reserved for a continuous positive-width measure, so singleton support refuses. Real calibration needs atomic controls, categorical hypotheses, spike-and-slab sparsity, mixtures, dependent joint measures, hierarchical populations, and coordinate pushforwards without abusing continuous Uniform or silently multiplying marginals.

Technical approach
Add independently versioned Dirac, finite discrete, mixture, product-with-declared-independence, copula or external joint, hierarchical, and pushforward measure schemas. Bind physical quantities/units, exact support and atoms, canonical weights, normalization evidence, base measure, coordinate transform and Jacobian semantics, parameter/case/population scope, conditioning, hyperpriors, and source authority. Posterior claims must reference the exact admitted joint measure and its compatibility receipt; no implicit product, density, absolute continuity, or coordinate invariance is inferred.

Acceptance and tests
G0 covers empty/single/max atoms, duplicate canonical atoms, signed zero, NaN/Inf, negative/nonunit weights, dimensional mismatch, support containment, mixture recursion, transform singularity, and every identity mutation. Property tests check permutation invariance, normalization, pushforward round trips where bijective, unit rescaling, and marginal/joint closure. G3 compares independent construction routes and deliberately dependent counterexamples. G4 bounds recursion/allocation and cancellation. G5 is deterministic. A no-mock E2E calibrates a mixed discrete-continuous model, preregisters posterior claims, performs exact replay, and falsifies prior substitution. Logs include measure family/version, units, support/atom counts, normalization and transform receipts, joint/marginal closure, source identities, budgets, and no-claim status.

title: I10.1+ Bind experiments, splits, observations, and QoIs with exact bidirectional closure
description:
Root cause and user impact
The schema binds each retrospective case to concrete experiment and split artifacts and validates row-level QoI, instrument, channel, clock, and partition membership. A stronger bidirectional contract is still needed so a split, requested QoI, observation operator, and consumed row set cannot be combined from individually valid but semantically different experiment roles.

Technical approach
Define an ExperimentSplitObservationBinding owned by fs-evidence. Bind exact experiment and split identities/hashes, split purpose and preregistration, immutable row identities, calibration/validation/blind partition, QoI and quantity/unit, instrument/channel/clock, observation and aggregation operators, case/protocol, selection predicate, and released capability state. Require every consumed row to have exactly one binding, every claimed finite-data QoI to have nonempty authorized support, and every split reference to point back to the exact experiment root. Preserve blind capabilities and prohibit pre-release enumeration.

Acceptance and tests
G0 mutates each edge, tests empty/boundary/max sets, duplicate and orphan rows, wrong QoI/unit/operator/case, split replay, partition overlap, and release substitution. G3 proves row/order canonicalization, exact bidirectional reachability, and no calibration versus holdout alias. G4 exercises count bombs, cancellation, partial manifests, and conflicting shared concrete bundles. G5 is deterministic. A no-mock E2E ingests a real typed manifest, creates a preregistered split, admits calibration observations, refuses validation/blind leakage, applies a release, and replays offline. Structured logs retain only capability-safe counts and hashes plus case/QoI/operator identities, partition disposition, binding receipt, and refusal witness.

title: I10.1+ Replace authenticity booleans with typed verification and trust evidence
description:
Root cause and user impact
Boolean authenticity and current-calibration flags collapse very different states: unchecked declaration, byte match, custody receipt, signature verification, issuer authorization, expiry, revocation, and scientific suitability. A true bit can be overread as laboratory authority.

Technical approach
Replace booleans at the authority boundary with versioned EvidenceVerificationStatus values: Unverified with reason, ContentVerified, CustodyReceipted, SignatureVerified, IssuerPolicyAdmitted, Expired, Revoked, and Refused. Bind subject artifact and byte root, verification method/build, receipt/signature, issuer and key handle, trust policy, audience, validity interval and clock source, revocation epoch/source, checker, and exact proven/no-claim predicates. Keep cryptographic validity separate from policy admission and scientific adequacy. Provide explicit migration from legacy artifacts rather than treating true as verified.

Acceptance and tests
G0 freezes tags and preimages and mutates every trust coordinate. G3 proves stronger states cannot be fabricated by serialization or downgrade/upgrade aliases. G4 covers forged signatures, wrong subject/audience, unknown issuer, clock ambiguity, expiry, revocation races, duplicated receipts, cancellation, and secret-safe diagnostics. G5 is stable. A no-mock E2E ingests signed and unsigned experiment/calibration artifacts, updates revocation state, admits or refuses under two policies, and verifies offline. Logs name only public issuer/key/policy handles, status, proven predicate set, clock/revocation evidence, receipt hashes, and no-claim boundaries.

title: I10.1+ Admit authority-grade metrology rosters and calibration validity
description:
Background
I10.1 closes observation instruments, calibration-certificate hashes, acquisition channels, clocks, quantities, and units structurally. It does not yet parse a common authority-grade metrology roster or prove that a certificate is valid for the measurement time, range, transfer chain, environment, and uncertainty budget.

Technical approach
Define InstrumentRoster, SensorChannel, CalibrationCertificate, TraceabilityChain, TransferFunction, and MetrologyAdmissionReceipt identities. Bind serial/model, channel, measured quantity and unit, frame/support, range/resolution/saturation, calibration points/model/uncertainty/covariance, standards and laboratory chain, method/build, environment, validity interval and clock, firmware/configuration, drift/health evidence, issuer policy, and revocation. Close each observation and raw record to exactly one admitted channel and time-valid certificate. Separate traceability, calibration validity, uncertainty adequacy, and scientific suitability.

Acceptance and tests
G0 covers roster duplicates, wrong channel/unit/frame/range/time, missing links, uncertainty dimension, expired/revoked certificates, firmware/config drift, and every identity mutation. G1 uses manufactured sensor transfer and uncertainty propagation. G3 checks unit/frame transforms and equivalent traceability paths only under explicit equivalence receipts. G4 covers large rosters, clock uncertainty, cancellation, signature faults, and secret-safe refusal. G5 is deterministic. A no-mock E2E admits a real typed instrument chain, consumes rows inside and outside validity/range, propagates uncertainty, revokes a certificate, and replays offline with detailed public-safe logs.

title: fs-fft-perf-multidim: radix-4/8 kernels, SIMD lanes, 2D/3D pencils, roofline gate

THIS BEAD is the recorded performance + dimensionality scope v1 deliberately deferred (plan section 6.3 full ambition):
1. Radix-4 and radix-8 Stockham kernels (fewer passes over memory; keep the radix-2 stage for odd log2 residues). The naive-DFT oracle + golden-hash tests in crates/fs-fft/src/lib.rs are the acceptance harness: any kernel change must keep the oracle green; a golden-hash bump requires semantic justification recorded here (twiddle-application ORDER changes bits legitimately when radix changes - bump once, document, re-verify cross-ISA on trj).

5. Roofline gate: >=40% of memory-bound peak on both reference machines using fs-substrate STREAM triad numbers as the denominator; results logged as fs-obs events. This is the plan honest-performance bar (Decalogue P6) - measure, do not vibe.

  x86-64   TR 5995WX(quiet) 21.5GB/s  4.97GB/s=0.231   4.89GB/s=0.227   4.93GB/s=0.230

Method: frankensim@e00858c (== pushed main, == the M4 local tree), 8 sibling repos
git-cloned shallow onto the perf box; `cargo test -p fs-fft --release --test
perf_lane -- --ignored`. x86-64 run on ts2 (5995WX, load ~6/128 → single-thread

DIAGNOSIS (actionable, not vibes):
- Zen 3 is FLAT ~0.23 across 64K->4M. Attainment invariant to working-set size is
  the signature of a COMPUTE/LATENCY bound, NOT a bandwidth wall: the AVX2 f64x4
  radix-4 butterfly is either not being emitted (scalar fallback on x86-64 fs_simd
  dispatch?) or its FMA/shuffle latency isn't hidden. FIRST thing to check: confirm
  the vectorized body actually lowers to vfmadd/vperm on x86-64; a scalar fallback
  fully explains the flat 23%. Then interleave >=4-8 independent butterflies to
  cover Zen 3's ~4c FMA latency.

  at n>=1M. NEON path is effective relative to its 5x-higher per-core roof.
- Absolute: M4 sustains ~7x Zen 3's per-core FFT throughput (34 vs 4.9 GB/s),
  tracking ~5x per-core bandwidth + better SIMD.
- The perf_lane byte model charges 32 B/elem PER Stockham pass; radix-8 (already in

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE of the x86-64 flat-0.23 attainment — CONFIRMED by source, not inferred.
fs-fft dispatches its radix-4 butterfly through fs_simd::ops().r4qrun_f64
(lib.rs:201). The fs-simd runtime table populates r4qrun_f64 as follows:
  - aarch64 NEON tier  -> neon::r4qrun_f64  (VECTORIZED; src/neon/fft/mod.rs)
  - x86-64 Avx2/Avx512 -> scalar::r4qrun_f64  (crates/fs-simd/src/lib.rs:150)
  - default             -> scalar::r4qrun_f64
i.e. the x86 capsule ships axpy/dot/sum + the AVX2 GEMM microkernel mk8x4_f64
(bead xlvx) but NO AVX2 FFT butterfly — x86-64 FFT runs the SCALAR twin. That fully
explains the measured signature: flat ~0.23 across n=64K..4M on Zen 3 (scalar
butterflies are compute/latency-bound, size-invariant), vs the size-dependent,
higher M4 curve (NEON vectorized). This is THE gap for the x86 roofline row.

FIX (in this bead's "SIMD lanes" scope): add an AVX2 r4qrun_f64 capsule under
crates/fs-simd/src/x86, mirroring src/neon/fft/mod.rs — 4x __m256d radix-4 columns,
matching scalar::r4qrun_f64's EXACT per-element op order (the tier-equivalence
battery at lib.rs:353 asserts (ops().r4qrun_f64)(..) == scalar bitwise, so the FMA
policy must match: if the twin uses mul_add, use _mm256_fmadd_pd; if separate * then
+, use _mm256_mul_pd + _mm256_add_pd). Runtime-gate on avx2+fma with scalar
fallback; <300-line capsule + SAFETY.md + unsafe-capsules.json one-line entry.
Verify: tier-equivalence battery bitwise-green with the AVX2 path active, then
re-run perf_lane on a Zen 3 box (ts1/ts2) to confirm attainment lifts off 0.23.
Radix-8 (fewer passes => less traffic) is orthogonal and helps both ISAs.

comments.text: COPY-BACK FUSION ANALYSIS (CloudyFinch - claimed, analyzed, releasing; the lever is REAL but is a redesign, not a patch). Current sixstep: T1(d->s) + sweep1(s,+twiddle) + T2(s->d) + sweep2(d) + T3(d->s) + copy(s->d) = 6 full-array passes. FINDING 1: the naive fusion (make sweep2 out-of-place d->s via per-row copies, then T3: s->d, dropping the final copy) is TRAFFIC-NEUTRAL - the per-row seq copies sum to exactly the eliminated copy_from_slice; do not bother. FINDING 2: scatter-fusion parity trap: fusing T3 into sweep2 (FFT row in cache, scatter into the OTHER buffer's column) lands the result in scratch again - one fused stage just moves the copy. FINDING 3 (the real design): fuse ALL THREE transposes into the sweeps as gather-FFT-scatter column processing: stage A per j: gather data COLUMN j into a row buffer (strided read), sub-FFT + twiddle in cache, scatter back into data COLUMN j (safe: column j is dead after its own gather); stage B per j: gather ROW j... (second stage operates on the transposed orientation - needs the index algebra re-derived carefully). Result: ~4 effective passes vs 6; at the measured 0.68-0.73 ratio a 6/4 traffic cut projects to ~1.0-1.1x vs the stage walk - i.e. the fusion could JUST flip the default-on decision, but only via this full rewrite, which changes bit order (new golden territory per the registry row) and needs the quiet-host relative lane to certify. title: Make fs-io CSV record admission strict and lossless
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT
The bounded catalog CSV decoder uses one quoted boolean instead of an explicit lexical state. After a closing quote it returns to the unquoted state, so malformed records such as "a"junk,b are accepted as ajunk,b. A quote inside an unquoted field such as a"b is retained literally instead of refused. The line iterator also skips every whitespace-only physical record, so a legitimate one-field empty or whitespace record can disappear rather than being validated against the admitted schema. These are silent source-to-catalog semantic changes at a world boundary; a bounded receipt must never make them look like successful faithful parsing.

MISSION
Implement a deterministic strict CSV-subset state machine that distinguishes unquoted, quoted, and after-closing-quote states. Only a delimiter or record end may follow a closing quote; a raw quote may open a field only at field start; doubled quotes remain the sole quote escape. Treat each physical record as data, including empty/whitespace-only records, instead of silently filtering it. Continue accepting LF and CRLF record boundaries. Explicitly refuse embedded quoted line breaks in this bounded subset until a cancellable logical-record scanner lands, and document that no full RFC 4180 claim is made.

ACCEPTANCE
- G0 pins empty/quoted-empty fields, commas, doubled quotes, raw mid-field quotes, trailing bytes/whitespace after a closing quote, unterminated quotes, consecutive blank records, whitespace-only records, leading blank header, LF/CRLF parity, and deterministic first-byte diagnostics.
- G3 proves quote/unquote equivalence only where both spellings are valid, CRLF/LF equivalence, and preservation of record count/content under admitted rewrites.
- G4 cancellation remains wired at bounded decoder/record boundaries and failure publishes no CatalogRead or success receipt.
- Parser version and contract change if accepted-language semantics change; receipts must distinguish the prior permissive grammar.
- No useful quoted-field functionality is removed: commas and doubled quotes inside quoted fields remain supported. Embedded record separators are an explicit no-claim/refusal, not silently misparsed.
- Code-first landing uses rustfmt/diff/static review only; keep this Bead and frankensim-svlo8 in progress until central cargo test -p fs-io --all-targets, union clippy, and DSR proof are green with exact logs.

title: fs-dd: BDDC substructured operator may not sub-assemble to the apply_global oracle (interface double-count + arithmetic-vs-harmonic edge coeff)
description:
Deep-review hunt (2026-07-12). A reviewer traced two numerical discrepancies in fs-dd's BDDC assembly by hand on uniform(2,2)/(2,4). Beaded (not fixed) because (a) BDDC sub-assembly is subtle and confirming a DEFECT vs a deliberate formulation needs the recommended oracle test, and (b) any fix shifts last-ULP output -> cross-ISA golden re-pin (cannot verify x86 from this aarch64 host, per golden-bump-protocol).

## Finding 1 (HIGH numerical confidence, MEDIUM intent) — interface stiffness doubled
local_stiffness (lib.rs:275) adds every incident edge's weight to a node diagonal (a[i][i] += w) even for edges LEAVING the subdomain, and an interface-parallel edge shared by two subdomains is counted in BOTH, so Sigma_s R^T K_s R != K (the operator apply_global applies). Hand-check uniform(2,2), interface node (2,1): apply_global row diag 4, off -1 to (1,1)/(3,1)/(2,2); sub-assembled schur_apply gives diag 8 and coupling (2,1)-(2,2) = -2 — interface diag/coupling DOUBLED. **Masking (the 'certifying the certifiers' concern):** apply_global has ZERO callers in the whole workspace (grep-confirmed) despite the CONTRACT (§Public types, src/lib.rs:106-107) naming it 'the whole-system oracle the Schur path verifies against'; and solve_cg returns only (iters, kappa), discarding the solution x, so the doubled operator is self-consistent and never surfaces as a wrong NUMBER — only its (self-consistent) conditioning is measured. VERIFY FIRST: add the oracle test the CONTRACT implies — assert schur_apply on Gamma equals the Schur complement of apply_global. If it FAILS, Finding 1 is a real assembly bug (fix: assemble each edge once — guard the neighbor-side flux by edge ownership, split interface-parallel edges by 1/multiplicity). If it PASSES, the formulation is self-consistent and the CONTRACT/oracle wording is what needs correcting.

## Finding 2 (MEDIUM) — edge_coeff arithmetic mean, doc says harmonic
edge_coeff (lib.rs:79-102): the doc (79-80) says 'Harmonic mean of adjacent cell coefficients (the standard variable-coefficient stencil)' but the body does acc += rho; cnt += 1.0; acc/cnt = ARITHMETIC mean. For -div(rho grad u) the face transmissibility is the HARMONIC mean (series resistors); arithmetic over-conducts across jumps (rho=1|1e6: harmonic ~2 vs arithmetic ~5e5). checkerboard(4,4,1e6) (dd-003/004) puts every jump exactly on interface edges — where the two disagree by ~5 orders. Decide: if harmonic is intended (physically standard, doc says so) fix the code (changes numerics -> golden re-pin); if arithmetic is intended, fix the doc. Applied consistently in apply_global AND local_stiffness, so fixing it does not by itself resolve Finding 1.

## Also fixed inline this session (NOT part of this bead)
Finding 3 — ccd_locality(0) panicked (div_ceil(0) + usize underflow); guarded to return 0.0 (committed). And solve_cg on a zero/empty RHS gives alpha=0/0=NaN kappa (degenerate-input robustness gap; CONTRACT says 'all solves total') — worth a fail-closed guard when addressing this bead.

Note fs-dd is an [M]-marked (feature-gated) crate, so this is not on a shipping path today.

title: Small-kernel worker-count tuning: pooled N-D FFT wakes 128 workers for 256 pencils
description: With the tkr7 parked crew, per-run spawn overhead is gone, and the residual small-size N-D FFT attainment gap is GRANULARITY: at [256,256] on ts2 (128 logical CPUs), the axis-0/outer-block kernels plan ~256 pencils across 128 woken workers (2 tiny tiles each; ~0.8ms roundtrip), reading attainment 0.0696 vs 0.4598 at [1024,1024]. The 3D case [128,128,64] reads 0.3098 (4-6 wake cycles + small column groups). WHAT: choose worker counts from PROBLEM SIZE, not host size, for small kernels — e.g. cap effective workers so each gets >= K tiles-worth of work (K from measurement), either (a) in the FftNd pooled path when building plans, or (b) as an fs-exec Tuner decision (kernel x size -> workers), which is the principled home (tune rows already bind placement_identity). Constraint: bitwise identity across worker counts already holds by construction (P2), so worker-count choice is timing-only and tune-key-visible (placement identity). Acceptance: [256,256] and [128,128,64] attainment on ts2 materially improves (target: clear 0.40 or document the honest ceiling with the roofline model corrected for wake overhead); no determinism goldens move.
close_reason: COMPLETE across 5 increments: (1) worker sweep + per-pass analysis refuted the naive static tiles/worker cap; (2) per-axis-pass instrumentation landed (43d7e10: NdPassReport + observed pooled variants, measurement-only, P2 preserved); (3) ts1 per-pass measurement isolated the true pathology - 16384 micro-tiles on the stride-1 axis + column groups shrinking with worker count; (4) MIN_TILE_ELEMS work-floor tiling landed (0ef43d0, v2 kernels) - validated on ts1: 3D axis-2 pass up to 6.6x faster, [128,128,64] within_band at ALL worker counts (peak 0.86 @W64); (5) [256,256] honest wake-floor ceiling documented (0.41 @W16 falling to 0.19 @W128 - structurally unreachable 0.40 at W>=32 under one-wake-per-pass; escalations recorded: pass fusion / partial wake / pin-W16). title: fs-recompute: prevent forged skip certificates from malformed bounds and stale plans
description:
## Problem

Fresh-eyes audit found three certificate-soundness defects in fs-recompute:

1. NodeRecord::content_hash uses delimiter-based text serialization of caller-controlled strings. Newlines/prefix text can make distinct records serialize identically, violating content-address identity and the determinism trip-wire.
2. invalidate::plan accepts finite negative sensitivity "bounds" and overwrites duplicate perturbations for the same source. Both can understate propagated error and emit an unsound verified-color skip.
3. RecomputeApi permits two plans computed from the same slack snapshot to commit sequentially. The second commit does not detect that its certificate is stale after the first burn and can overspend slack.

## Required repair

- Replace ambiguous record hashing with versioned, length-prefixed canonical bytes; preserve parameter-order canonicalization and float-bit identity.
- Treat every sensitivity bound as finite and nonnegative; invalid values must fail closed. Sum duplicate source perturbation magnitudes conservatively, with non-finite accumulation forcing recomputation.
- Bind PerturbPlan to the store/slack state it certified and make commit validate the whole plan before mutating. Stale plans must return a structured error with no partial burns or telemetry updates.
- Add focused G0/G3 regressions for structural hash collisions, negative sensitivities, duplicate perturbations, stale concurrent plans, and atomic failure.
- Update CONTRACT.md no-claim/invariant language.

## Acceptance

Focused fs-recompute tests and clippy pass with all features; ubs clean on touched files; DSR quality attempted/reported according to repo policy.
close_reason: Recompute plans are canonical-state-bound, atomic, read-only, and fail closed under malformed or stale inputs; focused proof passes.

comments.text: Soundness repair landed in 4657a7a and d8b566f: canonical state fingerprints bind plans, plan internals are read-only, duplicate burns accumulate atomically, invalid bounds fail closed, and snapshot/hash encodings are unambiguous. Focused all-feature fs-recompute tests (19), clippy -D warnings, diff check, and UBS passed in the audit lane.

title: Derive neural no-tunnel steps from certified interval sign margins
description: ROOT CAUSE: NeuroShape computes safe_radius=abs(net.eval(x))/L from a nominal rounded point value. Even after point and interval tanh share an implementation, point arithmetic roundoff can make abs(v_hat) exceed the exact continuous MLP's sign margin, so v_hat/L can step past a zero. Sampled contour comparisons are not a proof. MISSION: evaluate a degenerate certified interval at the point; use lo only when lo>0, -hi only when hi<0, otherwise zero; divide the certified nonnegative margin by the Lipschitz upper bound with downward/outward-safe arithmetic; invalid/nonfinite/zero-L cases fail closed. Keep nominal value only for visualization. Bind step-policy version, activation semantics, field identity/local witness context, and interval budget into report/wire provenance. TESTS: positive/negative one-ULP-near-zero, straddling-zero, zero/invalid L, overflow/subnormal, nominal-overestimate mutant, rigid/unit scaling, deterministic replay, and no-tunnel manufactured fields. Code-first first; central downstream proof required.

title: fs-substrate STREAM triad probe under-reads Zen 3 single-thread streaming: attested roofline runs environment_invalid on the x86 reference family (attainment 1.58 > 1.5 band)
description: Found by the ongz depgraph-receipt e2e lane on ts1 (Threadripper PRO 5975WX, quiet, release build, fsim nightly-2026-07-06, HEAD 90b2660). MECHANISM: crates/fs-substrate/src/bandwidth.rs triad_gbs_once measures single-thread STREAM triad with a plain scalar indexed loop; on Zen 3 it reports ~22.4 GB/s while the fs-simd simd-axpy-f64 kernel achieves ~35.5 GB/s (2.96 GFLOPS x 12 B/flop at n=16777216, DRAM-bound: 2x128MiB arrays exceed the 128MB L3). fs-roofline's credibility gate (lib.rs ~1639, bead 1n61) computes attainment = achieved/probed = 1.58 > 1.5 and marks the row environment_invalid, which invalidates the whole registry, refuses evidence admission, and blocks EVERY attested/citable run on this machine family - including the ongz e2e lane's Fresh/warm-reuse/salt arms (see target/depgraph-receipt-e2e logs on ts1). On the M4 the same ratio is 0.53-0.93 (in band), so this is Zen-3-family-specific probe under-read, not kernel over-count: probable causes are the scalar loop under-using memory-level parallelism vs the SIMD kernel's streaming, and/or missing non-temporal stores in the probe while the kernel's write-allocate accounting differs. FIX DIRECTIONS (owner's call): (a) vectorize/unroll the probe loop so probe and kernels share a streaming discipline; (b) probe-vs-kernel accounting audit for write-allocate traffic (24 B/elem STREAM convention vs actual per-uarch traffic); (c) if the probe is deliberately conservative, the 1.5 credibility cap needs a per-family derivation with a falsifier-power analysis, not a universal constant. BLAST RADIUS: any change moves machine-axes numbers, baselines, and downstream roofline verdicts - coordinate with baseline re-promotion. Blocks the x86 leg of frankensim-production-depgraph-receipt-e2e-ongz.
notes: ts1 post-fix measurements for 87f5547 (requested by owner): single-thread probe rose 22.4 -> 23.75 GB/s (release, quiet host). Dependent axpy attainment across five attested runs at n=16777216 (DRAM-bound): 1.36, 1.39, 1.44, 1.49, 1.54 — the band edge (1.5) still sits INSIDE run-to-run variance, so attested runs pass ~4/5 and flake otherwise. Second flake mode observed: live all-core bandwidth drifted to ratio 1.221 vs the promoted baseline -> 'baseline suspect' admission refusal (all-core triad on the 64-thread NUMA box swings 37-43 GB/s between process starts). The ongz e2e lane (scripts/ci/depgraph_receipt_e2e.sh, 8ce1024) retries through both modes and reached full chain green on run r7 (Fresh + retained receipt artifact + warm no-resweep reuse), so the fix is directionally confirmed but does NOT yet stabilize the gate: axpy still achieves ~35.5 GB/s (streaming stores?) vs the triad's 23.75. Remaining gap is probably write-allocate accounting (triad pays RFO on the a[] stream; 24 B/elem convention undercounts its real traffic vs axpy's) or MLP depth. Re-promotion after any further probe change is required as owner noted.

title: Refuse time-zero access through delayed game-information grants
description:
RE.Q1 admission currently treats StrategyAccessV1::InitialOnly as permitted under ObservationAvailabilityV1::Delayed for any nonnegative lag. An open-loop controller can therefore seal a whole signal using a t=0 value whose grant says it arrives only after a positive delay, admitting an anticipative policy despite the nonanticipativity contract.

Root fix: require delayed grants to be consumed through an explicit delayed access whose lag is at least the grant lag; permit InitialOnly only when the grant lag is exactly zero.

Acceptance: a positive-lag disturbance grant plus an open-loop controller with InitialOnly disturbance dependency refuses with ObservationTimingMismatch; zero-lag InitialOnly and matched delayed access remain admitted; InitialOnly, Current, and History semantics remain unchanged; contract states the boundary; rustfmt and static diff checks pass. Central Cargo/DSR/RCH verification remains batch-pending.

title: Enforce CapabilityToken ledger_scope at scoped ledger sinks
description: CapabilityToken.ledger_scope is documented as branch/namespace write authority but is currently an unused public String. Governor::flush_to_ledger writes dirty events from every session into one sink, never validates or persists scope, binds only one global ledger path, and advances one global degradation-event cursor. title: fs-topo [M]: evaluate excess-component penalty counts persistence bars, not solid components
close_reason: FIXED (fs-topo::penalty, behind moonshot-topo-persistence). THE DEFECT: the excess-component channel counted long-lived bars ANYWHERE in the sublevel filtration - a connected solid with two internal density basins separated by a still-solid saddle wore a false excess-component penalty while the SAME report said betti=(1,0,0) (the audit's confirmed [-1,-0.4,-0.3,-0.4,-1] counterexample). THE FIX: b0 at the spec level is the COUNT AUTHORITY for both excess and deficit channels (the report can never contradict itself again); bars alive at the level (birth <= level < death) supply voxel localization, carving the LEAST persistent components first. RECONCILIATION DISCOVERED DURING THE FIX: alive-bars and b0 can legitimately DISAGREE (persistence0's union-find connectivity vs betti's 26-connected closed-cube convention - my debug_assert equating them fired on tp_001) -> when they disagree the channel degrades honestly to counted-not-localized ((b0 - target) x tau, empty voxel list) rather than trusting the wrong-connectivity proxy. FIXTURE BUG EXPOSED BY THE FIX: tp_001's spurious island [0,2)^3 CORNER-TOUCHED the solid at (1,1,1)-(2,2,2) - ONE component under the crate's own 26-connectivity convention; the old bar counting called it two, so the test was asserting the 84ib defect itself. The island is now a properly separated corner voxel and the channel still fires on genuine disconnection. REGRESSIONS: the audit counterexample (connected basins => NO excess channel, betti (1,0,0)) + the genuinely-split variant (saddle above level => b0=2, channel fires). EVIDENCE: fs-topo all suites green BOTH ISAs (trj /data/tmp/fstopo4.xwnuhp/test2.log - survived a mid-build rustc nightly update via fresh-target relaunch, plus an asupersync 0.3.6->0.3.7 bump), penalty 6/6 incl. both regressions, clippy zero warnings under the feature, fmt. False NON-compliance (penalizing good designs) - safer polarity than false compliance, now dead either way.

title: Canonicalize bidirectional equivalence receipts in VerificationManifest graphs
description: Root cause: RelationKind::CertifiedEquivalence is documented and consumed as a bidirectional semantic relation, and union-find ignores its endpoint orientation, but admit_graph preserves from/to exactly in canonical order and digest input. Therefore one A equivalent B receipt and the semantically identical B equivalent A receipt produce different NormalizedGraph digests and projections; supplying both also creates redundant authority and changes cardinality instead of refusing as a semantic duplicate. Required change: define an explicit canonical endpoint orientation for certified-equivalence receipts, apply it before sorting, duplicate detection, digesting, cycle analysis, and every projection, while preserving direction for implication/refinement/restriction/counterexample receipts. Decide and document whether normalization returns the canonicalized receipt or rejects noncanonical input; prefer a single stable behavior with actionable diagnostics and no silent loss of checker/TCB evidence. G0: exact endpoint-order boundary, reverse-equivalence duplicate refusal, parallel equivalence receipts with distinct checker/TCB/policy stay distinct, and all directed kinds retain orientation. G3: reversing any subset and permuting input order yields identical canonical edges, representatives, digest, human rows, JSON lines, and ledger rows. Add no-claim language that certified equivalence records asserted relation evidence but does not itself verify mathematical soundness. Code-first implementation may land proof-pending; central fs-vmanifest all-target and lint proof required before closure.

Within NEON's 32 vregs: 4x4 = 16 acc + 8 operands (ratio 2.0), 4x6 = 24 acc + 10 operands = 34 regs (spills, ratio 2.4 = at most +20%). With 3 load ports vs 4 FMA pipes, ratio 2.0 already saturates the FMA pipes THEORETICALLY at ~36 GFLOP/s (4 vec-FMA/cy at ~4.5GHz); measured best-of ceiling for the fully-unrolled 4x4 is 24.6 (issue bubbles - 16 acc chains x 4cy latency = zero slack). CONSEQUENCE: even a perfect NEON-128 kernel reaches ~36/52 = 0.69 of peak-FMA; the realistic ceiling is ~0.45-0.50, and measured today under load is 0.20-0.31. The >=60% acceptance number implicitly assumes wider vectors (AVX-512: 8 lanes/reg, 32 zmm - the same 4x4 tile is 4x wider per load and the ratio economics differ). RECOMMENDATION: re-scope acceptance per-ISA - keep >=60% for the x86-64/AVX-512 row (measure on ts1/ts2 where the capsule work would also live), set the NEON-128 row at >=40% of peak-FMA (achievable with the packed kernel on a quiet host), both ledgered per fs-roofline conventions. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
X86 CAPSULE WIRING LANDED (a78b976) + fresh quiet-ts1 roofline table. Found the x86 side collapsed at ~0.7 GFLOP/s flat across ALL size classes - the classic libm-fma trap: the AVX2+FMA btile4x4p_f64 capsule body existed in x86/gemm.rs (SAFETY.md registered, bounds-hardened) but the dispatch table still routed the packed batched tile to the scalar twin, whose mul_add is a per-element libm call on baseline x86. The batched perf lane was FAILING its 8% floor on ts1.

After the one-line wiring, quiet ts1 (Zen 3 5975WX, single-thread, peak_single 38.8 GFLOP/s):
k=4: 2.07 GFLOP/s (target_att 0.058) | k=6: 1.17 (0.033) | k=8: 5.42 (0.153) | k=12: 6.50 (0.184) | k=16: 8.52 (0.240) | k=24: 8.71 (0.246) | k=32: 9.72 (0.274) | k=48: 11.99 (0.338). Floor met everywhere, lane green again; batteries 19/19 + fs-simd bitwise self-checks 11/11 on BOTH ISAs (capsule is bit-identical: libm fma == vfmadd == NEON fmadd, goldens unchanged).

REMAINING GAP to the 60% compute-peak gate on x86: best 0.34 at k=48. Structure of the gap: (1) k=6 is pathological (1.2 GFLOP/s) - 4x4 tiling leaves 2-row/col ragged edges that dominate at k=6 (k=4/8/12/16 divide cleanly and jump); a 2-lane edge microkernel or 6-specialized tile would fix the worst class. (2) monotone rise with k says per-tile overhead (accumulator zeroing, pointer setup per (ti,tj), feature-check amortized already) still dominates small k. (3) even k=48 at 0.34 suggests the l-loop is load-port bound: 8 loads per 16 FMAs (a[4]+b[4] vectors) = 0.5 load/FMA vs Zen3's 3 loads/cycle : 2 FMA/cycle budget - register-blocking B (reuse bv across ti) would halve loads. Next concrete step: hoist the 4 bv loads out of the ti accumulation (restructure acc order), expected ~2x at large k, then the k=6 edge kernel. M4/NEON side previously measured 10-26 GFLOP/s (older table in this bead) - needs a quiet-window re-measure with the same lane before any both-ISA gate claim.

Remaining lever ideas for the next stretch, in expected-value order: (1) k=6 ragged-edge microkernel (2-row half-tile) - worst class, cheap; (2) mb-block sizing sweep in fs-la's packing (smaller mb => shorter l strides, more L1 reuse per panel; currently fixed by MBLK doctrine); (3) software prefetch of the next l line per stream; (4) AVX-512 tier on a machine that has it (Zen 3 fleet is AVX2-only - the 60% x86 number may simply need the wider file/2x lanes). title: fs-la: batched GEMM alpha-zero and shape-overflow semantics

comments.text:
Soundness audit of fs-adjoint (gradient/adjoint + DWR certification) via a
focused review agent + independent verification. Arithmetic cores (interval
residual bound, Cauchy-Schwarz brackets, verify_gradient/fd_falsifier direction)
are SOUND. Findings in the color-assignment / explain / dwr layers:

F1 [FIXED, HIGH] commit ef750cc — certify() stamped Verified{0,bound} from the
   transpose-residual bound while IGNORING the fd_checks it stores. The residual
   bound certifies apply_t is the structural transpose of apply (tiny for ANY
   matrix) — it says NOTHING about gradient-formula correctness. So a gradient
   whose OWN FD falsifier flagged it (gc_002's sign-flipped grad_bad) still wore
   Verified{0,~1e-16}, a ledger-writable false certificate; only the out-of-band
   merge_gate caught it. Fix: certify now downgrades to Estimated when any
   fd_check is inconsistent (never launder a refuted gradient). gc_002 extended
   to assert the color. 22 fs-adjoint tests green.

REMAINING (documented, verified reproductions — candidates for follow-up):
F2 [MED] explain.rs:376-379 (adjoint) + :568 (drag): Verified colors built with a
   FIXED ±1e-12 (adjoint) / cdi/n*4 (drag) half-width, NOT a rigorous enclosure
   and inconsistent with the node's own relative `bound` field. For a channel
   with acc~1e6 the true fp summation error ~1e-8 >> 1e-12, so Verified
   [acc-1e-12, acc+1e-12] EXCLUDES the exact discrete value. Fix: use the node's
   relative bound for the interval (or downgrade). Diagnostic layer.
F3 [MED] explain.rs reconciles() is VACUOUS: finalize() sets residual =
   observed - attributed, so reconciles checks (attributed + residual -
   observed).abs() <= bounds == |0| <= bounds, ALWAYS true. The stated "kill
   criterion / permanent invariant" (tests/explain.rs:116,193) can never fire.
   Fix: reconciles should verify the node bounds COVER |residual|, not the
   tautology.
F4 [MED-LOW] dwr_accept::accept (dwr_accept.rs:81->104): a GUARANTEED bracket
   whose bound EXCEEDS tolerance is filtered out, then the code accepts on the
   DWR estimate with estimator_inconsistent=false. Rigorous "under-resolved"
   evidence silently dropped (color stays Estimated, so not a false Verified,
   but accepted:true for a solution a rigorous bound flags as failing).
F5 [LOW] edge cases: adjoint_residual_bound(op,0) -> Verified{0,0} with ZERO
   probes (no probes>=1 assertion); certify accepts Some(INFINITY) ->
   Verified{0,∞} (no fail-closed like fs-evidence); dwr_accept::dual_solve
   `let free = n - 2` underflows usize for n<2 (panic/huge-alloc CRASH on a
   degenerate ≤1-node mesh).

(b) HETEROSCEDASTIC + ANYTIME: noise variances fed from fs-uq estimates (the other agent's fs-uq::anytime landed estimate_probability_anytime + sub-Gaussian confidence sequences - the primitives exist); per-point noise in the GP (trivially: diagonal sigma_i^2 instead of scalar - the Cholesky path is unchanged) + e-process-compatible stopping for noisy-objective BO loops (stop when the incumbent's CS separates from the challenger's - coordinate semantics with fs-eproc/fs-uq owners). close_reason: BOTH LANES LANDED (fs-bo). Gates: clippy zero warnings incl. the feature build, fmt, CONTRACT current. fs-bo is now COMPLETE per its bead family: exact GPs, EI/q-EI, BO loops, TuRBO, multi-fidelity, sparse, heteroscedastic, e-racing, tape gradients.

title: fs-robust CVaR under-reports non-integral empirical tails
description: Fresh-eyes cross-crate trace found fs-robust::cvar still averages ceil(n*(1-alpha)) worst samples at equal weight, despite fs-uq fixing the identical anti-conservative bug under frankensim-zsvk. When n*(1-alpha) is non-integral this dilutes the boundary mass and under-reports expected shortfall, directly affecting robust_optimum decisions. Replace the epsilon/ceil heuristic with standard Acerbi-Tasche finite-sample CVaR using fractional boundary order-statistic weight; add exact non-integral-tail regression, parity-style integer-boundary coverage, contract wording, focused tests/clippy/UBS.

title: fs-feec sum-factorized kernels hit the baseline-x86 mul_add libm hole: 0.026 attainment on 5995WX vs 0.372 on M4 Pro
description: Found by the fz2.2 attainment scoreboard. fs-feec's sum-factorized apply (feec-apply lane) measures 17.2 GFLOP/s / 0.372 attainment on aarch64 (gate floor 0.30 passes) but 0.61 GFLOP/s / 0.026 attainment on the 5995WX (linux-x86_64, release) — a ~28x per-core deficit that tracks the known baseline-x86 hazard: f64::mul_add lowers to a PER-ELEMENT libm fma() CALL because x86-64's baseline target lacks compile-time FMA (same class as the fs-roofline peak-probe bug and the fs-simd fma3 dispatch hole, both fixed under xlvx/fz2.2). fs-feec's inner kernels use raw mul_add rather than the fs-simd dispatch table. Fix options, in preference order: (1) route the hot loops through fs_simd::ops() primitives (fma3/axpy/dot already have runtime-detected AVX2+FMA capsule paths, bit-identical per element); (2) a target_feature-dispatched kernel body like fs-roofline's fma_pass_x86. Mind the crate's determinism contract when restructuring loops: elementwise fused ops are bit-safe to reroute; reduction SHAPES must stay fixed per tier. Same hazard likely applies to fs-la's packed f32/mixed macro kernels (noted in fz2.2 s5) — one bead can sweep all raw-mul_add hot loops on the x86 lane; grep for mul_add in L1/L2 kernel crates and check each against its perf lane. title: Separate declared colors from admitted scientific evidence
description:
Fresh-eyes audit found a remaining type-boundary mismatch after Certified<T> became opaque: fs_evidence::Color is still both a plain declaration enum and the value many reports expose as positive scientific evidence. Structural payload validation can reject NaN, inverted intervals, malformed identities, and stale derived prefixes, but it cannot authenticate that a direct Color::Verified or Color::Validated constructor came from an admitted certificate/dataset. Roughly two dozen production modules still construct positive colors directly; ColorGraph/package/checker paths are stricter, but consumers can accidentally bypass those paths or call declared_color_unverified.

Root cause: epistemic rank representation and admission authority share one public type.

Design a staged, layer-correct split between untrusted DeclaredColor/Color candidates and an opaque AdmittedColor (or equivalent ScientificColor handle) that can be created only by a replay-verifiable ColorGraph/checker admission receipt. Lower numerical layers must remain independent of HELM: they produce typed certificate candidates and owner-specific proof payloads, while the admission boundary authenticates them. Waived, unresolved, stale-algebra, and out-of-regime nodes cannot convert to admitted scientific evidence. Preserve raw Color for rendering/diagnostics where useful, but make positive-evidence APIs require the opaque type.

Acceptance: direct construction of Color::Verified/Validated cannot satisfy package release, headline, ledger scientific-rank, or public capability APIs; compile/API tests cover every bypass; source-certificate and dataset-origin receipts replay; regime exit demotes structurally; all current direct-constructor sites are inventoried and migrated in bounded owner groups; no upward layer dependency is introduced; G0 laundering, serialization, downgrade, and tamper batteries plus end-to-end checker/package/flywheel tests pass.

comments.text: STAGED DESIGN PROPOSAL (a CloudyFinch session; posting design-first per the addendum working style — implementation deliberately NOT claimed while the owner group is active in colors.rs). THE CORE PUZZLE this bead hinges on: an opaque AdmittedColor must be unforgeable by arbitrary crates, but Rust gives no free cross-crate sealing UPWARD (any crate can impl a trait; fs-evidence at UTIL cannot depend on the L6 admission authority). THE HOUSE ALREADY SOLVED THIS SHAPE for waivers and source certificates: authority = DATA (hash-bound receipts) verified by an INJECTED CAPABILITY with a deny-all default. Proposal: (1) fs-evidence (UTIL) defines AdmittedColor { declared: Color, admission: AdmissionReceipt } with PRIVATE fields, AdmissionReceipt carrying the color-write row identity (node hash + row schema version + policy fingerprint — exactly the v7 row surface the 6xgf work made independently re-derivable), a constructor AdmittedColor::from_receipt(color, receipt, verifier: and-dyn AdmissionVerifier), and NoAdmissionVerifier deny-all — so at UTIL layer NOTHING admits. (2) fs-ledger provides the real authority: ColorGraph::admission_receipt(node) mints receipts ONLY for nodes that are unwaived, structurally valid, in-regime, and current-algebra (waived/stale/demoted nodes get a structured refusal — the bead's exclusion list lands here), plus LedgerAdmissionVerifier whose verify() is the independent row-rehash (the 6xgf parse-and-rehash machinery becomes the admission oracle — no new crypto, replay-verifiable by construction). Forgery then requires a lying verifier, which is visible at the composition root exactly like a lying WaiverVerifier — same trust model, same audit surface. (3) Positive-evidence consumers (fs-package claims, fs-robust weakest_color/headline_color, campaign headline APIs) take AdmittedColor VALUES without needing fs-ledger deps — layering stays acyclic. MIGRATION STAGES (krym pattern, each independently green): S1 additive types+authority+forge-refusal batteries (receipt with wrong node hash refused; deny-all refuses all; waived node refused minting); S2 admitted variants of positive APIs — including the owner-group fs-robust finding: admitted aggregate must be PERMUTATION-INVARIANT (canonical payload merge by content, never input order); S3 caller migration by owner group (the ~14 direct-constructor crates produce DeclaredColor candidates admitted at their ledger boundary; rendering/diagnostics keep raw Color under the existing declared_color_unverified naming); S4 the flip: positive APIs require AdmittedColor + an xtask check-color-admission lint (check-powi precedent) refusing new positive Color literals outside admission authorities and test fixtures. Payload structural validation (col_015 machinery) runs at S1 construction so malformed candidates never reach admission.
