title: Constellation pin violation: asupersync drifted 0.3.8 to 0.3.9 and fsqlite-btree no longer compiles (blocks ALL cargo/xtask/DSR)
description:
WHY: On 2026-07-24 this single defect blocked FOUR agents' verification for most of a session: no cargo build, no cargo test, no xtask, no check-all, no DSR, anywhere in frankensim. It was independently misdiagnosed at least three times (as a frankensim bug, as an unresolved stash pop, as a Cargo feature-flag problem) before GoldSnow isolated it by experiment. Successive sessions have now rediscovered it more than once. Filed so the next session reads a bead instead of spending an hour re-deriving it.

SYMPTOM: every cargo invocation in frankensim fails, including `-p <unrelated-crate>` and `cargo fmt --package`, because Cargo resolves the whole path-dependency graph before doing anything. Seven errors, all one shape:

  error[E0277]: the `?` operator can only be applied to values that implement `Try`
     --> ~/projects/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-btree/src/cursor.rs:385:12
  385 |         Ok(self.txn.get_page(cx, page_no)?.into_vec())
      note: this implements `Future` ... but the future cannot be awaited in a synchronous function
  384 |     fn read_page(&self, cx: &Cx, page_no: PageNumber) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {

Also at cursor.rs:389, 399, 403 and following, plus E0308 mismatches of the same family.

ROOT CAUSE (GoldSnow's diagnosis, corroborated): the asupersync sibling has drifted OFF its constellation pin.

  constellation.lock pins:  asupersync 0.3.8 @ 5973b0ff31f405ae90fa9e6e2ef5f61a75c5b78b
  local checkout HEAD:      asupersync 0.3.9 @ 2691a88080d74b353405427d9af48d10e077699d

Three asupersync commits landed 2026-07-24 at 17:17, 17:20, 17:31; the last green frankensim build was 16:56. fsqlite-btree/src/cursor.rs is UNMODIFIED since 07-22 and frankensqlite's tree is clean, so fsqlite's source did not move - asupersync moved underneath it. Txn::get_page and friends became async; fsqlite-btree's synchronous callers were not migrated with them. frankensqlite's own recent commit "docs(perf): block frontier refresh on async pager migration" names the migration.

FALSIFIED HYPOTHESIS, recorded so nobody retests it: the default-features=false / nightly-outcome-try feature theory is WRONG. GoldSnow set asupersync = { version = "0.3.9" } with defaults ON, rebuilt, got the identical seven errors, and reverted the edit exactly. Neither feature configuration builds against current asupersync HEAD. The feature flag is not the variable.

WHAT: (a) decide the direction - either restore/align the pin, or bump constellation.lock to the new asupersync and carry the frankensqlite async migration (fsqlite-btree's sync callers become async or acquire a blocking bridge); (b) whichever way, examine why this cost a session: xtask check-constellation exists precisely to catch pin drift, but the failure mode is that CARGO DIES BEFORE ANY GATE CAN RUN, so a gate that lives inside check-all cannot defend against it. A pin check that runs without building the workspace (or a pre-flight in the RCH/DSR wrapper) is the real fix; (c) record the resolution so the next drift is diagnosed in minutes.

DO NOT - both learned the hard way this session: do not `git checkout` the pinned 0.3.8 commit in the asupersync working tree to unblock yourself; an agent is actively committing there and that clobbers live work. Do not resolve frankensqlite's stash/manifest state hoping it helps; that makes the manifest PARSE but the tree still does not BUILD. Those are two separate failures and fixing the first does not fix the second.

WORKAROUND while blocked (NobleLion's; gives the REAL binary, not a reimplementation): build out-of-workspace with plain rustc, feeding --extern flags forward, export CARGO_PKG_VERSION=0.0.1, and accumulate flags in a shell ARRAY because zsh does not word-split unquoted scalars. LIMIT discovered 2026-07-24 by LilacAspen: it stops working for any target whose closure reaches fsqlite - xtask now depends on fs-report, whose closure runs fs-session -> fs-ledger -> fsqlite, so the recipe no longer builds xtask itself. Crate-level `cargo test -p <crate>` still works for crates outside the fsqlite cone (fs-asbuilt, fs-conduction, fs-convection, fs-airflow all ran green during the outage). Also: RCH_MIN_LOCAL_TIME_MS=999999999 cargo ... stops the RCH PreToolUse hook from hijacking cargo to a remote worker that hangs.

OWNERSHIP: outside every EXTREAL lane; belongs to whoever owns the asupersync/frankensqlite constellation. Filed by LilacAspen at NobleLion's request so it is tracked rather than rediscovered a fifth time.

DONE WHEN: frankensim `cargo check --workspace` resolves and builds; constellation.lock and the asupersync checkout agree, or the bump is deliberate and recorded; and there is a detection path that does not itself require a working cargo.

title: Authenticate session capability issuance and dynamic use
description:
CapabilityToken and fs_ir::SessionCapability are publicly constructible data, and CapabilityToken::to_admission can project an unregistered token. Governor::open_session validates and immutably binds caller-supplied declarations, but there is no authenticated issuer, policy fingerprint, revocation, or proof that a caller is entitled to the requested operators/budgets/scope. Operator and concurrent-core grants are static data; the governor meters core-seconds, peak memory, and wall time but does not bind work to an admitted verb or enforce a shared concurrent-core lease. Calling these values authority without this boundary permits accidental capability fabrication.

Root fix: separate untrusted CapabilityRequest/DeclaredCapability from an opaque admitted SessionGrant minted by a policy verifier. Bind issuer/policy identity, governor/session/scope, exact operator set, budget values, issuance/expiry/revocation generation, and canonical digest. Static fs-ir admission and execution dispatch must consume the admitted view, while lower layering remains acyclic via data receipts plus injected deny-all-by-default verification. Add a shared operation/core lease so execution cannot exceed admitted concurrency or run an ungranted verb.

Acceptance: public construction cannot satisfy authoritative admission/dispatch/ledger APIs; forged, altered, expired, revoked, cross-governor/session/scope, duplicate-pattern, wildcard-confusion, response-replay, and policy-rotation cases fail closed; exact admitted grants still round-trip and enforce dynamically; no upward layer dependency; G0/G4 tests and explicit no-claim language until external issuer authentication exists.
close_reason: Implemented and verified across five landed increments (34c6222 grant core, 76b778e7 grant-gated open, 03a0c749 fs-ir sealed capability evidence + bridge, c038accb visible-declared rename of the legacy path, 70776dae dynamic verb/core-lease enforcement at exactly-once execution). Every acceptance clause holds: session authority is an opaque policy-minted grant; only the admitted projection registers at open; fs-ir consumes grant-backed evidence through a deny-all-default verifier with caller-declared data visibly warned; the unaudited path is explicitly named; and execution cannot run ungranted verbs or exceed admitted concurrency, refusing before work runs. Batch-verified at HEAD: fs-session lib 63 + conformance 30 + gemm_tune 18 + grant 10 + program_risk 7 + long_job 4 + calibration 4, zero failures; fs-ir admission 20/20 at its landing; doctests clean.

This closes the unbounded projection and mixed-valid/invalid authorization bugs. The Bead remains P0/open because the projected value is still caller-declared rather than an opaque authenticated grant, and dynamic verb/core-lease enforcement is still absent.

title: fs-solver saddle-point block preconditioners: Stokes-class Schur approximations over the FEEC mixed spaces

THIS bead: block preconditioners for saddle-point systems (Stokes, incompressibility, contact) - block-diagonal/triangular preconditioners with Schur-complement approximations (pressure-mass for Stokes; PCD-class documented per physics). BUILD ON: fs-solver MinresState (the natural saddle-point outer solver), LinearOp trait (block operators compose as struct wrappers), fs-feec tensor de Rham spaces (velocity in H1^3 or H(div), pressure in L2 - the discrete pair from tfz.6 slice 2; note the L2 Legendre mass is DIAGONAL, making the pressure-mass Schur approximation trivially invertible - a real payoff). title: fs-plan alloc overstates two relaxation/optimality guarantees vs greedy behavior
description:
Two CONTRACT-vs-behavior gaps in crates/fs-plan/src/alloc.rs (the V1 greedy allocator), verified by reading the code + battery. Both have decision impact because fs-plan estimates drive admission/scheduling, but both are low-medium severity (the battery already tolerates the slack, so arguably known/by-design — the defect is the overstated claim).

## Gap 1: best_error_in_budget is the greedy STALL value, not the achievable optimum
alloc.rs:627 sets `best_error_in_budget = total_error(knobs, stalled)`, documented (field doc :368, inline :625-626) as "Best achievable error within the budget" / "greedy already maximized error reduction under the budget." But V1 is a greedy ladder-climber that never reconfigures (never downgrades one knob to free wall for another), so it can stall at an error strictly worse than another in-budget config. The battery (tests/alloc_battery.rs:78) permits greedy_err/oracle_err up to 2.5×. A consumer reading this field as a BOUND on achievable accuracy is misled.
Example: one track, budget 10; knob A [(1,100),(5,60)], knob B [(1,100),(9,30)], target 90. Greedy takes A→A1 (util 10>8.75), stalls at A1B0 err 160; but A0B1 (cost 10, err 130) is in budget. Reports 160, true best 130.
Fix: rename/re-document as "greedy best-in-budget (heuristic, not a lower bound)", or compute against the exact/oracle result; at minimum drop the false "greedy already maximized" comment.

## Gap 2: budget_needed_for_target uses a different greedy order than allocate, so "re-plan at the suggested budget succeeds" is not guaranteed
`infeasible()` derives `budget_needed_for_target` by climbing on Δerror/Δcost (alloc.rs:645) while `allocate()` plans on Δerror/Δwall (alloc.rs:593). Re-planning at exactly `budget_needed_for_target` can still return BudgetInfeasible, contradicting the CONTRACT's "VERIFIED relaxations (re-planning at the suggested budget succeeds)". The battery only passes by inflating the budget (tests/alloc_battery.rs:111, `inf.budget_needed_for_target * 1.0001`) — evidence the exact value isn't reliably sufficient. The relaxation string (:661) tells the user to raise the budget to that value with no margin.
Fix: compute budget_needed_for_target by actually invoking allocate at candidate budgets (bisect on the wall of max-settings), or emit a suggested budget with a proven margin, so the "re-planning succeeds" claim holds exactly.

Discovered during the deep-review bug hunt. The moonshot.rs knapsack overflow (separate) was fixed and landed.

title: fs-uq adaptive_mlmc controls only bias, not variance — doc overclaims optimal allocation
description:
CLAIM-vs-IMPLEMENTATION gap in crates/fs-uq/src/adaptive.rs (verified by reading the code).

## The gap
The module doc (adaptive.rs:5-7) states levels are added until the bias fits half the tolerance, "the other half goes to variance via the standard optimal sample allocation n_l ∝ √(V_l / C_l)." The implementation does NO such allocation:
- `add_level` (adaptive.rs:62-78) always takes exactly `n_pilot` samples (`n: n_pilot`, line 75).
- The main loop (adaptive.rs:81-121) only ADDS levels based on the extrapolated bias `|mean_L|/(2^α−1) ≤ tol/2` (line 108-109).
- `cost` (stored line 76 via cost_of) is never read again; `beta` (fitted line 106) is stored in the report but never used for any allocation.

So the returned estimate's RMSE is bounded only on the BIAS half of `tol`; the estimator VARIANCE is left at whatever `n_pilot × (#levels)` happens to give. The "estimate within tol" UQ tolerance claim is therefore only half-delivered. The test uq_005 passes only because its variances (8^{-l}, n_pilot large) are already tiny; it never checks estimator variance against tol/2.

## Resolution options
(a) Implement the promised allocation: after the bias loop converges, top up each level to n_l sized so Σ V_l/n_l ≤ (tol/2)^2, using the stored `cost`/`var` and the Giles formula (mirror mlmc.rs:62-78). This is the faithful fix but CHANGES sample counts and the estimate → will bump any golden fingerprint (check uq_battery.rs golden) and needs cross-ISA re-pin on x86.
(b) If full variance control is out of scope for this bead, correct the module doc (and any public claim) to state that only the bias is controlled and per-level sample count is fixed at n_pilot — so the function does not overclaim a tolerance it does not deliver.

Prefer (a). Related: the ÷n vs ÷(n-1) variance-denominator inconsistency between this path and mlmc.rs (separate bead). Discovered during the deep-review bug hunt; the golden-neutral fail-closed guards in mlmc_estimate were landed separately.

title: Make locked RCH builds sync the full Cargo path-dependency materialization closure
description:
The original attribution to host-only FrankenSQLite patches is incomplete. The Mac has 20 absolute FrankenSQLite [patch.crates-io] entries in its user Cargo config, while RCH executes Cargo with a fresh isolated CARGO_HOME. However, FrankenSim reaches FrankenSQLite through direct relative path and workspace dependencies, and the recorded locked failure attempted to replace fnp-* packages, not fsqlite-* packages.

crates/fs-sparse/Cargo.toml declares fnp-ufunc and fnp-dtype as optional, off-by-default path dependencies. The committed lock and current FrankenNumpy manifests identify them as 0.1.0. RCH currently derives sync roots from the default-feature cargo metadata active resolve graph, deliberately excluding optional and pure-dev edges, and does not incorporate delegated feature selection. Consequently the FrankenNumpy roots are not guaranteed to be synchronized; an absent or stale worker checkout can make remote Cargo request a lock rewrite even though the local lock is correct.

This is primarily an RCH dependency-materialization defect. Do not regenerate the FrankenSim lock to match stale worker state and do not copy developer-home absolute patches into the repository.
design:
1. In RCH, retain the existing active execution closure for dependency ordering, runtime-risk classification, and active-cycle semantics.
2. Add a separate deterministic, cycle-tolerant Cargo materialization and lock closure derived from repository manifests, independent of the active feature graph.
3. Traverse every repository-local path specification that can participate in resolution: normal, build, dev, target-specific, optional, workspace-inherited, repository [patch.*] entries, and all transitive path dependencies.
4. Use a visited-set fixpoint traversal. Latent optional cycles must terminate and must not enter or invalidate the active execution DAG.
5. Union materialization roots into full source synchronization, cache and project hashing, repo convergence, and remote dependency preflight. Sync source as well as manifests so --features, -F, --all-features, and --no-default-features cannot activate an unsynchronized crate.
6. Do not inject or copy user-home Cargo config. A project that genuinely requires a patch must declare repository-relative configuration.
7. Track implementation in a linked RCH issue and keep this FrankenSim issue open until the deployed RCH binary passes the real locked proof.
8. Separately harden the FrankenSim DSR release build command to cargo build --locked --release --workspace --bins. This is not the cause of the RCH closure failure.
9. FrankenSim itself requires no justified Cargo.lock rewrite for this defect.
acceptance_criteria:
1. RCH unit tests prove that the active closure still excludes an unselected optional edge while the materialization closure includes optional, transitive, dev, target-specific, workspace-inherited, and path-patched roots.
2. An optional dependency cycle terminates deterministically without poisoning the active plan.
3. RCH integration fixtures seed a stale or absent optional cross-repo dependency and prove default and explicit-feature locked commands succeed after synchronization with the lock byte-identical before and after.
4. Feature regressions cover --features, -F, --all-features, and --no-default-features.
5. From FrankenSim, without developer-home Cargo config, cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 succeeds and leaves Cargo.lock byte-identical.
6. On a Linux worker using the deployed RCH fix, the previously failing selected-package command succeeds with --locked; record worker, job ID, exact command, exit status, and log path.
7. DSR dry-run reports cargo build --locked --release --workspace --bins; the configured locked quality gate passes or reports an unrelated exact blocker.
8. Repository configuration contains no /Users/jemanuel Cargo patch paths, and no home-level Cargo config is copied to the worker.
9. Close only after the linked RCH fix is landed and deployed and all proof receipts are attached.

title: Portable checker plugins for solver-free certificate semantics
description:
The schema-v7 package/checker boundary now strictly parses, re-derives roots/composition, authenticates typed origins through injected policies, and states its no-claim honestly. It still cannot independently verify the mathematics of certificate families whose verifier is outside the package. This is not a reason to import solvers: several high-value families are portable and solver-free once their witness data is included.

Add a versioned certificate-plugin registry to fs-checker for independently checkable witness families, starting with exact/interval enclosure arithmetic and residual certificates whose operator data and norms fit a bounded portable witness. Each plugin owns a closed schema, canonical bytes, resource bounds, semantic recheck, failure localization, and no-claim boundary. Unknown families remain explicit capability refusals, never generic Pass. Keep fs-checker free of geometry/solver dependencies and use only native Franken primitives.

Acceptance: at least two real certificate families round-trip from producer to package and are recomputed by standalone checker code; seeded structurally valid but mathematically false witnesses fail; every scalar/array length and arithmetic operation is bounded; plugin/version substitution and witness-field tamper fail; release admission distinguishes integrity, origin authentication, and independent semantic verification; checker dependency-policy and WASM/standalone builds remain green.

title: Give fs-constraint restoration solver checked resource admission and budget receipts
description:
Background/root cause: elastic_solve and diagnose_infeasibility are synchronous small-fixture restoration paths whose work scales with design dimension, constraint count, skip-list membership cost, restart/step schedule, deletion filtering, repair count, and Monte-Carlo repair samples. The immediate P0 evidence-hardening bead adds fail-closed domain/policy admission and bounded cancellation polls, but Cx::checkpoint alone does not enforce poll/cost/deadline budgets, skip.contains can remain quadratic, allocations are not attached to a memory lease, and ElasticReport does not retain the exact admitted-versus-consumed resource contract. A large but structurally admitted request can therefore consume disproportionate CPU/memory without a replayable budget receipt.

Implement a versioned RestorationWorkPlan computed with checked integer arithmetic before allocation/evaluation. It must account for dimensions, active constraints, canonical skip mask construction, finite-difference probes, restarts, step caps, deletion-filter solves, repair candidates, and feasibility samples; refuse overflow, duplicate/out-of-range skip indices, and all counts above explicit versioned caps. Replace quadratic membership scans with a canonical admitted mask or sorted unique representation. Admit the exact plan against fs_exec::AdmittedBudget (including deadline-without-clock refusal), enforce cancellation/deadline/poll/cost at deterministic bounded tiles inside constraint evaluation, dimensions, restarts, steps, core filtering, and repair sampling, and drain/finalize with a typed stop reason. Attach a BudgetConsumption plus completed-work counters and plan/schema identity to ElasticReport/Diagnosis so success is claimable only when refusal is absent and charged work matches the declared accounting semantics. Integrate operation-memory leases or a typed no-lease/no-claim boundary before allocating vectors proportional to dimensions, constraints, or repairs; do not invent private authority when Cx lacks a lease.

Acceptance/Gauntlet: G0 exact/max+1 tests for every count, multiplication, addition, duplicate skip, out-of-range skip, zero/fixed-axis, and checked-arithmetic boundary; G3 equivalent skip ordering and thread/scheduling-independent plan identity; G4 pre-cancel, cancellation at every tile family, zero poll/cost budget, exact and max+1 quotas, expired deadline, deadline-without-clock, memory-lease exhaustion, no partial-success report, and repeated refusal stability; G5 bit-stable work-plan/receipt bytes across replays and supported ISAs. Add a deliberately slow or instrumented evaluator fixture that deterministically requests cancellation after admitted work (not wall-clock sleeps), prove bounded extra evaluations after the request, and log phase, logical tile, planned/charged work, polls, allocation sizes, and final refusal. Update CONTRACT with exact resource semantics and explicit no-claim boundaries. Central RCH/DSR proof and retained logs are required before closure.

title: Fault-contain and transcript-bind third-party fs-conform converters
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND SEVERITY
The current object-safe Converter trait executes arbitrary caller-supplied Rust through infallible Vec-returning callbacks. A shared reference does not imply purity: interior mutation, ambient state, randomized output, blocking, allocation, panic, abort, and time-of-check versus time-of-use code changes remain possible. The numeric checker can therefore certify one sampled callback transcript while a later invocation behaves differently. It also cannot truthfully guarantee never-panics, deterministic, cancellation-correct, or resource-bounded behavior for an untrusted third-party converter. A false or non-replayable tier is a Sev-0 scientific-integrity failure.

MISSION
Build the fault-contained, capability-admitted execution boundary that turns a converter tier from evidence about one observed transcript into replayable evidence about one immutable implementation under explicit budgets. Preserve first-party and third-party parity. Do not paper over this with broad refusal or a catch-unwind-only shim: panic containment is useful where available, but it cannot contain abort, OOM, native undefined behavior, or nontermination. The certifiable path may replace the early-stage trait API with the correct protocol.

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
- Define a fallible certifiable-converter protocol with stable implementation identity, schema/version identity, dimensions, units, capability requirements, deterministic seed policy, declared work and memory envelopes, and structured apply/adjoint outcomes. Prefer caller-provided or fallibly reserved output and scratch storage over unconstrained Vec allocation.
- Run converter work under an explicit Cx and admitted scope. Bound callback work into cancellable tiles or execute an immutable converter artifact in a supervised pure-Rust guest or worker boundary that can be terminated and drained. Distinguish returned error, panic/trap, timeout, cancellation, budget exhaustion, malformed output, and host failure.
- Treat the existing direct trait as a legacy trusted in-process adapter with an explicit uncontained no-claim status. It must not mint a production third-party certification tier unless its execution identity and containment requirements are satisfied.
- Bind canonical inputs, outputs, callback order, seeds, modes, dimensions, budgets, capability grants, implementation artifact digest, arithmetic-rung evidence, failures, and host fingerprint into a versioned content-addressed transcript and ledger receipt.
- Detect statefulness and nondeterminism through repeated, permuted, interleaved, pause/resume, and fresh-instance replay. Identical logical calls must produce byte-identical canonical output and diagnostics in deterministic mode. Callback scheduling and worker count must not alter the receipt.
- Close time-of-check versus time-of-use: a tier names an immutable converter artifact and protocol version, not a mutable trait object or display id. Runtime use must verify that identity and capability envelope before accepting the tier.
- Specify trust boundaries for first-party native code, third-party admitted bytecode or guest code, and exploratory uncontained adapters. Never imply that memory-safe host code can contain arbitrary native abort, OOM, or nontermination without a real isolation boundary.
- Produce bounded structured diagnostics with deterministic first-failure location and ranked remediation. Never publish a partial positive tier after any fault, cancellation, or uncertain drain.
- Keep dependency direction valid, safe Rust by default, Franken-only production dependencies, and feature-gate frontier or moonshot execution substrates until Gauntlet evidence supports promotion.

GAUNTLET
G0 protocol laws for identity binding, canonical transcript encoding, dimension and unit admission, every structured failure class, exact and plus-one work or memory limits, duplicate and reordered calls, and immutable-artifact mismatch.
G3 metamorphic replay under witness permutation, repeated calls, fresh instances, worker-count changes, equivalent tile partitions, pause/resume, and deliberate interior-state perturbation. Verdict and canonical receipt must remain invariant or fail closed with typed nondeterminism evidence.
G4 inject returned errors, allocation refusal, panic or guest trap, cancellation at every tile boundary, timeout, worker loss, malformed lengths, oversized diagnostics, and failed drain or finalization. Prove no task, arena, output, capability, or partial-certificate leak and byte-identical retry.
G5 freeze callback transcripts and tier receipts across runs, thread counts, supported ISAs, host restarts, and artifact relocation. Demonstrate that any implementation, protocol, budget, capability, seed, mode, or transcript change changes identity rather than silently reusing a tier.
Security adversaries include reentrant callbacks, interior mutability, global clocks and randomness, output that changes only after certification, panic during drop or finalization, resource bombs, and a converter id that aliases another artifact.

ACCEPTANCE
No production third-party tier can be minted or reused without an immutable verified implementation identity, explicit capabilities and budgets, a complete canonical transcript, deterministic replay evidence, and fault-contained execution. Every failure is typed and fail-closed; cancellation drains; retries are idempotent; no partial tier escapes. Legacy uncontained callbacks remain usable only behind an explicit trust and no-claim boundary. Unit, property, metamorphic, chaos, cancellation, transcript-replay, identity-substitution, clippy, and DSR gates are green with detailed replayable logs.

title: fs-uq mlmc_estimate uses biased (÷n) variance while adaptive_mlmc uses Bessel (÷n-1)
description:
CONFIRMED variance-denominator inconsistency across the two MLMC paths in crates/fs-uq (verified by reading both).

## The inconsistency
- mlmc.rs:57-61 `var_of` computes `s.1/n - mean*mean` — the BIASED (÷n) population variance, via the catastrophic-cancellation form E[X²]−E[X]².
- adaptive.rs:69-70 computes `Σ(x−mean)² / (n_pilot−1).max(1.0)` — the UNBIASED (÷(n−1)) Bessel-corrected sample variance, two-pass/stable.

## Why it matters
The MLMC report's `estimator_variance = Σ V_ℓ/N_ℓ` (mlmc.rs:104) needs an UNBIASED per-sample σ² because Var(mean)=σ²/N. The ÷n form underestimates σ² by (n−1)/n, so `estimator_variance` is biased LOW — anti-conservative: the report claims a tighter estimator than warranted (a UQ certificate-quality defect). The two public APIs also simply disagree on the definition of "sample variance," and mlmc's LevelStats.variance doc (mlmc.rs:15) says "Sample variance," which conventionally means Bessel-corrected.

## Fix
In mlmc.rs `var_of`, divide by (n−1) (guard n≥2; for n=1 report variance 0 or +inf per convention) and prefer a two-pass or Welford form over E[X²]−E[X]² to avoid cancellation, matching adaptive.rs. Magnitude at the test's pilot=200 is small ((n−1)/n), but the direction is wrong for a reported estimator-variance certificate.

## Blocker
Changing var_of changes the numerical output → will bump the uq_battery.rs golden hash (uq_golden_hash, GOLDEN_HASH at line ~265) which fingerprints mlmc output. That golden is cross-ISA; per the golden-bump protocol it must be re-pinned and verified bit-identical on an x86-64 host (trj/ts1). Also re-check the mlmc_telescoping_and_cost_win test, which currently uses ÷n on both sides of its own audit. Discovered during the deep-review bug hunt.

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE + FIX DEFINITIVELY CONFIRMED (controlled x86 experiment, ts1 Zen 3,
quiet load 3.37). Rebuilt the SAME source with RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=native"
(makes mul_add lower to inline vfmadd — no libm call, no dispatch):
  feec-apply attainment: 0.388/0.266/0.348/0.390/0.455/0.433 at r=1..6
  feec-gate p=4 (r=3): 0.350 vs floor 0.30 -> sum_factorized_attainment ... ok (PASS)
  GFLOP/s 1.0 -> 12-15 (~13x). Compare the default build: flat 0.026, gate FAILS.
So: (1) the x86 gap IS the baseline-x86-64 libm-fma call for mul_add — proven, not
inferred; (2) an inline-fma path CLEARS the >=30% gate on x86 (0.35 at the gated
size); (3) the dispatch-axpy in 4456672 does NOT (per-call overhead at length-5).
Determinism preserved either way: libm fma == hardware vfmadd == aarch64 fmadd, all
IEEE correctly-rounded -> golden aaf1076a byte-stable (verify after any change).

TWO FIX OPTIONS (owner's call):
(A) WORKSPACE x86 build config: .cargo/config.toml
    [target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu] rustflags=["-C","target-feature=+fma"]
    Minimal, bit-neutral, and fixes the WHOLE libm-fma class on x86 (fs-roofline's
    probe already hit this — xlvx; any mul_add-heavy x86 kernel is affected).
    CAVEAT: makes x86 binaries require an FMA-capable CPU (all Zen/Haswell+; fine
    for the Threadripper/EPYC target families, not truly baseline-x86-64-portable).
(B) fs-feec-LOCAL capsule: #[target_feature(enable="fma")] const-P apply variant,
    runtime is_x86_feature_detected("fma") gate + scalar fallback, registered
    capsule + SAFETY.md. Portable (keeps baseline), scoped to fs-feec. This is
    scope item (e) done correctly (inline vfmadd, not the dispatch façade).
Recommend (A) as a workspace performance-infra decision since the libm-fma trap is
general; (B) if baseline-x86 portability must be preserved. Both proven to clear the
gate by the target-cpu=native experiment above. (aarch64 44% unaffected by either.)

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Handoff from a55x (closed): the baseline-x86 libm mul_add hole in the sum-factorized apply is FIXED (fma capsule, native codegen proven by objdump: 69 vfmadds, no libm calls in the hot path; ts2 2.9x to 1.79 GFLOP/s at r=3, bit-identical). THE REMAINING x86 GAP IS VECTORIZATION: all 69 vfmadds are SCALAR — LLVM fully unrolls the P=2..8 contraction inner loops (contract_y/z rows are P-length) and does not pack them on x86, while aarch64 autovectorizes the same code to 18.6 GFLOP/s. Concrete leads for your >=30%-both-ISAs goal: (1) contract_x_p's inner rows are already P*P long (16-64 f64) — check whether IT vectorizes and why y/z do not; restructuring y/z to sweep the P*P plane per coefficient would give 2-8 ymm ops per row; (2) fs_simd::ops().fma3/axpy have AVX2 capsule paths (bit-identical per element) but indirect-call overhead needs rows >= ~32 elements to amortize — fine for the P*P restructure, wrong for P-length rows; (3) keep the per-element accumulation ORDER fixed (ascending-l) or the sf-kron golden legitimately bumps — the P*P-plane sweep preserves it, lane-parallel-over-outputs also preserves it (independent outputs). perf_event_paranoid=4 on ts2 blocks perf stat; objdump on /data/tmp/cargo-target/release/deps/perf_lane-* is the workable inspection route.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my earlier "two fix options" note — OPTION (A) IS REJECTED. A global
`.cargo/config.toml` `-C target-feature=+fma` for x86 BREAKS CROSS-ISA DETERMINISM.
Verified on ts1 before committing: with +fma, LLVM CONTRACTS ordinary `a*b + c`
expressions (not just explicit mul_add) into a single-rounding vfmadd, diverging
from the non-contracted aarch64/baseline. Measured:
  cargo test -p fs-sparse -p fs-fft -p fs-la -p fs-topo -p fs-evidence -p fs-cheb
  -p fs-rand  (built with the +fma config)
  -> fs-cheb cheb_golden_hash FAILED (0xeea04b0a01de46cd; Clenshaw uses a*b+c);
     the other 6 crates stayed byte-stable.
So the G5 determinism guarantee is INCOMPATIBLE with a global +fma. (My "bit-neutral"
claim was wrong for `a*b+c` — only EXPLICIT mul_add is bit-neutral under +fma.)
The in-repo .cargo/config.toml now documents this rejection so nobody re-adds it.

The ONLY determinism-safe fix is OPTION (B), scoped: a fs-feec-LOCAL
`#[target_feature(enable="fma")]` variant of the const-P contract kernels (which
contain ONLY explicit `ail.mul_add(s, *d)` — no `a*b+c` to contract), runtime
is_x86_feature_detected("fma") gate + scalar fallback, registered capsule +
SAFETY.md. Bit-neutral (verified the contract kernels have no contractable a*b+c);
golden aaf1076a stays byte-stable; +fma-only (2-wide vfmadd) already clears the gate
on x86 (measured 0.398 at r=3 with target-feature=+fma). I can implement + x86-verify
this if desired — note it lands in the fleet's active fs-feec area (4456672) and
replaces the ineffective ops().axpy routing there.

title: fs-feec simplicial high-order vector families: Nedelec/RT tree (H(curl)/H(div)/L2 on tets, r>=2) with vector-dof orientation
description: SPLIT from tfz.6 per the established discipline (slices 1-3 landed there: full TENSOR-PRODUCT de Rham complex at r=1..6 with exact Kronecker derivatives + commuting projections, and simplicial hierarchical H1 to r=6 with the sorted-global orientation convention and G3 permutation batteries). THIS bead: the simplicial high-order VECTOR families - hierarchical Nedelec first-kind H(curl) and Raviart-Thomas H(div) on tets at r>=2 plus discontinuous L2, completing the simplicial PrLambda-k tree. WHAT EXISTS TO BUILD ON: crates/fs-feec/src/highorder/simplex.rs (H1 hierarchy, Duffy quadrature, entity dof management, boundary masks, the sorted-global orientation convention PROVEN by the r=3 signed-permutation equivariance test); whitney.rs lowest-order edge/face forms (the r=1 members of these families); derham.rs shows the commuting-projection test pattern. KEY DESIGN CONSTRAINTS from the landed work: (1) orientation for VECTOR dofs is harder than H1 - edge tangents and face normals need the sorted-global convention extended to FRAMES (edge tangent = towards larger global index; face frame = sorted-triple circulation, matching what deram1/deram2 already pin at r=1); (2) the G3 battery must cover both the signed-permutation level (where kernels have definite parity) and the physics level (where bases mix); (3) commuting diagram tests vs the H1 gradient (pick the family consistently - first-kind Nedelec pairs with the full sequence); (4) unisolvence via mass SPD; MMS via L2 PROJECTION ladders (the derham.rs precedent - full curl-curl solves need tfz.10) + dd=0 through the discrete operators. Duffy quadrature and Legendre kernels are all in place. ACCEPTANCE: exact-sequence dimension counts at r=1..4; grad/curl/div chain maps with dd=0 to machine cancellation; conformity across shared entities (tangential trace for H(curl), normal trace for H(div)); projection convergence ladders; permutation batteries; golden + trj cross-ISA.
close_reason: Simplicial vector families shipped: highorder/vecfam.rs - first-kind Nedelec H(curl) + RT H(div) on tets r=1..4 + DG P_{r-1}, completing the simplicial P_r Lambda^k tree. NO hand-derived shape functions: Koszul bases in centered/scaled monomials (RT = (P_{r-1})^3 (+) xi*Htilde_{r-1}; Nedelec with the independent cross-product subset alpha_0=0-when-i=0, dim r+r(r+1)=r(r+2) exact), square dof-Vandermonde by pivoted LU per element. Normal-equations least-norm was tried first and REJECTED on evidence: cond^2 cost sqrt(eps) = 1.6e-7 tangential trace jumps; the independent basis puts them at 2.3e-12. Sorted-GLOBAL orientation frames (edge Legendre moments signed toward larger index = deram1 direction; face frames + circulation normal from sorted triple = deram2 normal). Battery vecfam_battery.rs 7/7: vec-001 dims 6/20/45/84 (N), 4/15/36/70 (RT) + Euler alternating sum = 1 both fixtures r=1..4; vec-002 dof-Kronecker 5.8e-13 + mass SPD r=2,3; vec-003 tangential jump 2.3e-12 / normal 1.4e-11 across shared entities r=2..4; vec-004 curl.grad 1.7e-14, div.curl 1.4e-13 (grad P_r subset N_r, curl N_r subset RT_r - interpolation matrices are exact chain maps); vec-005 canonical-interpolation ladders slopes 1.90/1.88 (r=2) 2.92/2.89 (r=3); vec-006 two-tier G3 per the bead spec: edge dofs transform with DEFINITE PARITY (-1)^{k+1} under relabeling (1.1e-16), physics tier field-invariance 6.6e-13 (found+fixed: analytic-field dof quadrature at r+3 leaked 2.8e-5 frame-dependent error, raised to r+7); vec-007 r=1 = Whitney forms to 4.4e-16 vs deram1/deram2 + golden 0x2737401f72b499f2 frozen (cross-ISA row LEDGERED PENDING per simplex policy). Lanes: fs-feec tests 9 suites all green (no regressions), clippy -D warnings 0, fmt, ubs 0 critical in vecfam (5 pre-existing degree-contract panic!s in hodge/cochain from earlier beads), xtask clean. title: Roofline: trusted historical axis baselines for sustained-contention detection
description: Static plausibility floors plus pre/post probe agreement cannot detect a host already degraded before the first probe and consistently degraded through the second (e.g. 6 GB/s pre/post on a normally 100+ GB/s reference host still self-normalizes). Acceptance: separately admitted fingerprint-specific baseline axes with provenance/age/firmware policy; current pre/post axes must agree with the trusted baseline inside declared bands before citable gates; first-run measurements are candidate evidence, not self-authorizing baselines; baseline update requires explicit governed promotion; quiet/degraded/stale/firmware-drift tests. Keep absolute floors as coarse last-resort sanity.
close_reason: Fully landed across two convergent slices, verified end-to-end on the committed tree: 2d6d3f9 (CloudyFinch: baseline module - governed promotion >=3 mutually-agreeing runs + named operator/justification, fingerprint/OS/arch/firmware identity, age policy, [0.70,1.15] bands, first-run-as-candidate law, strict bounded store, citable_axis_admission composing floors + reprobe + baseline) + a4d6eb5/5c6b721 (the other roofline lane: production enforcement - AxisBaselinePolicy threaded through run_is_citable / run_admission_error / record_run and the roofline CLI, fs-roofline-axis-admission-v1 receipts with BLAKE3 baseline content hash, schema_version on BaselineAxes). The 5.6 reopen gap (helper with zero production callers) is closed: the production evidence transaction and CLI now refuse un-baselined/degraded/stale/identity-drifted axes before anything citable is minted, with stable_sustained_contention_cannot_cross_the_production_admission_boundary pinning the original 6-vs-100 GB/s counterexample at the production boundary. Verified: full fs-roofline suite green on committed HEAD (45 lib + 8 conformance + 7 regress + 5 bin); floors kept as last-resort sanity

title: Upstream DSR must fail closed and retain evidence-complete aggregate receipts
description:

Code review also found missing/malformed/unreadable repository configuration or zero derived checks can return success, command output is truncated rather than durably retained, configured top-level Cargo commands are not uniformly --locked, and one aggregate does not bind all checks to a single source/constellation identity.

title: ADDENDUM: Epistemic engine for physical claims — governance, phases, risks, identity
description:
## Mission
The plan addendum (`COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md`) is an identity shift, not a feature list. The base plan makes **composition trustworthy** (multi-representation geometry glued by cellular-sheaf cohomology, physics coupled through certified interfaces, error bounds that survive every seam because they compose algebraically). The addendum's thesis: trustworthy composition is the *foundation*, not the product. Everything done *with* a composed object — optimizing it, re-solving variants, budgeting evidence, doubting it, merging concurrent edits, defending it to a regulator — inherits that algebraic structure. Nineteen proposals claim that inheritance.

> **FrankenSim should not be a simulator that emits numbers. It should be an epistemic engine for physical claims — a system that maintains typed, priced, auditable beliefs about designs, where solvers, surrogates, symmetry arguments, and physical experiments are interchangeable evidence sources ranked by cost per unit of certainty, and where agents are the query load. The product is justified belief at minimum cost.**

This epic is the ADDENDUM META/GOVERNANCE tracker: it holds the eight design principles, the phase roadmap (Spine → Flywheel → Leverage → Horizon), the four phase-milestone gates, the risk register R1–R10, and the governance rules that keep nineteen proposals from becoming nineteen parallel obituaries. The nineteen proposals themselves live under the five ADDENDUM LAYER epics (epic-flywheel, epic-epistype, epic-coupling, epic-selfknow, epic-gtm).

## The eight design principles (P1–P8), which every addendum bead must honor
- **P1 — Buy correctness at the level of algebra.** Prefer formulations where the invariant holds identically (δ∘δ=0, discrete de Rham exactness, type-checked couplings) over per-bug patches.
- **P2 — Certificates must compose.** Any accuracy/sensitivity/consistency statement that cannot propagate through the ledger DAG is a side channel, and side channels rot.
- **P3 — Every certificate ships with its cheapest independent falsifier.** Certificates prove what the model claims; falsifiers probe whether the claims connect to reality.
- **P4 — Type the epistemics.** verified/validated/estimated are different kinds of knowledge with different composition rules; the type system must refuse to launder one into another.
- **P5 — Design for the swarm's deficits.** No intuition → certified abstraction ladders + explanation objects. No memory → contracts + tombstones. Miscalibration → falsification budgets. Goodhart tendency → distrust optima by default.
- **P6 — Exploit the check/produce asymmetry.** Verifying a candidate is vastly cheaper than producing one; this asymmetry is the economic engine (speculation, cheap re-verification, third-party audit).
- **P7 — Concentrate research risk.** One research-grade bet at a time, chosen so its hard problem unlocks the most downstream value.
- **P8 — The plan itself must be falsifiable.** Every proposal carries a kill criterion with a measurement and a deadline. Unmeasured survival is not survival.

## The flywheel (why the top four proposals dominate)
Four proposals form a closed economic loop: **certified speculation (9)** makes answers cheap; **incremental recomputation (2)** makes variants cheap; **version control for physics (10)** makes concurrency safe; **compounding swarm memory (E)** makes it all cumulative. Each accelerates the others. On top sits **declarative queries against physics (8)** — the imperative→declarative inversion databases made in the 1970s, available here because there is a closed, priced algebra over the operations. Wrapped around the loop is the **epistemic type system (3, F, 6, D, 12)** that prevents the one fatal failure mode a certificate culture invites: being precisely wrong with a pedigree.

## Scoring, in one line
Nineteen proposals were scored 0–1000 on Useful/Innov/Pract/Accret/Agent, mean-ranked, under declared adversarial self-review. Composite order: 9 › 2 › 10 › 8 › E › 3 › 6 › F › A › C › 1 › B › D › 11 › 13 › 12 › 5 › 7 › 4. The hundreds digit is signal, the tens digit is texture. Two robustness facts matter: (1) 9/2/10 top both the composite and the lens-off (Ex-A) ranking — the headline order survives the confessed agent-lens bias; (2) A/B/C/D's top-tier standing is *conditional on agents being the operator* (Governance Rule 4).

## Members
add-doctrine-governance (P1–P8 + governance rules + scoring discipline), milestone-spine (Phase 0), milestone-flywheel (Phase 1 + Proposal 9's six-month checkpoint), milestone-leverage (Phase 2), milestone-horizon (Phase 3, per-proposal gated), risk-register (R1–R10 early-warning instrumentation + quarterly kill enforcement).

## Success criteria
Every proposal's kill measurement is instrumented before the proposal is funded (P8). Phase gates are defined as measured states, not dates. Quarterly, in writing, each live proposal is checked against its kill criterion; a proposal whose kill measurement was never instrumented counts as killed. WIP outside the current phase (headcount-weighted) is the honest metric of a plan losing discipline (R10) and is watched.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- NOTE: `add-layer:Ln` here is the addendum's THEMATIC layer (economic engine / epistemics / coupling / self-knowledge / GTM), NOT the base L0–L6 architecture stack. Member crates still sit at their true base layer and must respect lower-knows-nothing-of-higher dependency direction.

THE FOUR PHASE-MILESTONE GATES ARE PERMANENT CI: Phase 0 SPINE (xpck.2 — colors, no-laundering, the falsifier registry), Phase 1 FLYWHEEL (xpck.3 — the six-month checkpoint PASSED at 70% accepts and 1.5x median warm savings; super-additivity 16.8-24.2x composed vs 2.0x best-isolated), Phase 2 LEVERAGE (xpck.4 — adjoint-vs-DFO 10/10 at equal budget, planner-vs-baseline 4.31x, the evidence package with the external-audit item honestly Estimated), Phase 3 HORIZON (xpck.5 — five activation instruments, exactly one trigger fired, four waiting in a signed holding pen). THE PRODUCT ACCEPTANCE (xpck.8): a declarative query becomes a colored, priced, auditable answer a third party re-verifies SOLVER-FREE — admission teaches in milliseconds, the anytime ladder tightens monotonically with cache-hit repeats at 5-cell budgets, refusals carry the priced gap and the no-point-estimate clause, tampered roots fail, nothing launders, everything replays bit-exact. THE FIVE LAYER EPICS ALL CLOSED: flywheel (lmp4, 18 members — speculation/recompute/VCS/tombstones/queries), epistemic types (qmao — the three-color system), coupling (bk0o — adjoints/reality/spacetime), self-knowledge (knh1 — types/symmetry/spectral/ladder/explanations/VoI), go-to-market (jwq8 — packages/checker/waivers). All nineteen proposals shipped, instrumented-and-parked, or honestly deferred per their own kill criteria; every [F]/[M] behind a default-off feature; every claim conformance-tested with the falsifiers that caught three real sign/logic bugs in this session alone. The governance discipline held: one research bet (the equilibrated verifier — it landed), kill criteria as code, refusal as a first-class answer. The product is justified belief at minimum cost — and the belief that this program is done is itself typed, priced, and auditable.

title: Addendum doctrine & governance: P1–P8 principles, one-research-bet rule, quarterly kill-criteria enforcement, build-composite/sell-Ex-A
description:
## What
The addendum's governance layer as living doctrine, not a preface nobody re-reads. Encodes the eight design principles (P1–P8) and the four governance rules that keep nineteen proposals from becoming nineteen parallel programs (which the risk register calls "an obituary", R10).

## The eight principles (each must be checkable, not aspirational)
- **P1 Buy correctness at the level of algebra** — prefer identical invariants (δδ=0, de Rham exactness, type-checked couplings) over per-bug patches.
- **P2 Certificates must compose** — anything that cannot propagate through the ledger DAG is a side channel; reject side channels in design review.
- **P3 Every certificate ships its cheapest independent falsifier** (Proposal 6 operationalizes this).
- **P4 Type the epistemics** — verified/validated/estimated never launder into each other (Proposal 3 enforces).
- **P5 Design for the swarm's deficits** — abstraction ladders (A) + explanations (B) for no-intuition; contracts + tombstones (E) for no-memory; falsification budgets (6) for miscalibration; distrust optima (D) for Goodhart.
- **P6 Exploit the check/produce asymmetry** — verifying ≪ producing; the economic engine of speculation (9), cheap re-verification (12), third-party audit.
- **P7 Concentrate research risk** — exactly one research-grade bet at a time.
- **P8 The plan itself must be falsifiable** — every proposal has a kill criterion with a measurement and a deadline.

## The four governance rules (Part IV.3)
1. **One research bet at a time.** Phase 1's bet is Proposal 9 (its hard problem — certified a-posteriori bounds — is partially purchasable from the equilibrated-estimator literature and unlocks the widest downstream cone). Proposal 8's general planner and Proposal A's general certification explicitly do NOT open as research programs; they wait for the flywheel's telemetry and the RB beachhead respectively.
2. **Kill criteria enforced quarterly, in writing**, against the measurements named per-proposal. A proposal whose kill measurement was never instrumented counts as killed — unmeasured survival is not survival.
3. **Build in composite order, sell in Ex-A order.** Engineering priority = Mean column; commercial narrative + partnership investment = Ex-A column (12 and 7 lead the sell-side despite mid-table composite ranks).
4. **The circularity discount stands until lifted by evidence.** Proposals A, B, C, D's top-tier standing is conditional on agents being the dominant operator; if the first vertical ships human-driven, they are formally deferred to Phase 3 regardless of their scores.

## Scoring discipline (self-applied, per P8 and §II.4)
The 0–1000 scores are a confident-looking artifact from a confabulation-prone mechanism. Treat the hundreds digit as signal, the tens as texture. Two declared biases: (a) A–F were generated by optimizing the agent lens, so their Agent scores are partially circular — the Ex-A column is the falsifier (strip the lens and A/B/C/D drop to the 725–740 band); (b) the robustness check that passed: 9/2/10 top both composite and lens-off rankings.

## Acceptance criteria
This bead is DONE when: (1) P1–P8 appear as an enforced checklist in the contribution/design-review flow; (2) each of the nineteen proposals has its kill measurement wired to a dashboard BEFORE the proposal is funded; (3) a quarterly written kill-review ritual exists with an owner. This is a standing governance artifact, not a code deliverable.

## Testing
A "governance audit" script (or checklist) that lists every live addendum proposal, its kill metric, whether that metric is instrumented, and its last quarterly review date. Failing to instrument a kill metric flags the proposal as killed-by-default.

## Dependencies
None hard. This bead constrains every other addendum bead.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- **FEATURE-FLAG GOVERNANCE (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule):** every [F]/[M] deliverable ships behind a NAMED CARGO FEATURE, disabled by default, with a no-claim boundary in its CONTRACT.md; promotion to the default path requires the proposal's Gauntlet tier + kill-metric green.
- **NOTE ON `add-layer:Ln` LABELS:** the addendum's five architectural layers (L1 Flywheel … L5 GTM) are a THEMATIC grouping and are NOT the base architecture's L0–L6 dependency stack (SUBSTRATE…HELM). Actual crate placement + dependency direction must respect the base architecture (lower knows nothing of higher).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Optimality: the governance-audit emits machine-readable JSON (proposal -> kill-metric -> instrumented bool -> last-review-date) so it can gate CI rather than being a manual checklist.
close_reason: Implemented by extending crates/fs-govern (my crate from xpck.6; added crate:fs-govern label). Two new modules encode the addendum DOCTRINE + PROPOSALS as machine-readable data. doctrine.rs: the eight design principles P1-P8 (principles(), each id/name/statement) and the four governance rules (rules(): one-research-bet, quarterly-kill-enforcement/'unmeasured survival is not survival', build-composite/sell-Ex-A, circularity-discount). proposals.rs: all NINETEEN proposals in composite Mean order, each {id,name,phase,mean,kill_metric,owning_bead,instrumented}; governance_audit() enforces Governance Rule 2 / P8 (every proposal must DECLARE a non-empty kill metric AND an owning bead — a proposal whose kill measurement was never instrumented counts as killed) and counts instrumented (0 baseline); proposals_json() emits the deterministic machine-readable record for CI gating. Kill metrics + owning beads wired for all 19 (9->lmp4.1, 2->lmp4.8, 10->lmp4.12, 8->lmp4.16, E->lmp4.13, 3->qmao.1, 6->qmao.4, F->qmao.3, A->knh1.4, C->knh1.6, 1->bk0o.1, B->knh1.5, D->qmao.5, 11->bk0o.4, 13->knh1.1, 12->qmao.6, 5->knh1.3, 7->jwq8.1, 4->bk0o.7). Tests (tests/governance.rs, 8): P1-P8, 4 rules numbered, all-19-unique-ids, descending-composite-order, per-proposal kill-metric+bead-owner, audit-complete-zero-instrumented, owner mapping, JSON well-formed+deterministic. Verified: clippy -D warnings CLEAN, fmt CLEAN, cargo test -p fs-govern 16/16 (8 governance + 8 register), xtask check-all fs-govern-compliant. title: ADDENDUM MILESTONE — Phase 3 HORIZON (per-proposal activation gates: 11, C, A, 4, 13b)
description:
## What
ADDENDUM PHASE 3 — HORIZON. Not a single gate but a holding pen of proposals each individually gated by its OWN activation condition. Nothing here opens as a broad program; each waits for a specific trigger, per Governance Rule 1 (one research bet at a time) and Rule 4 (the circularity discount).

## Contents and their individual activation gates
- **Proposal 11 — reality as a chart** (reality-ingest/-assimilate/-tolerance): activate when metrology partnerships exist AND registration uncertainty on realistic scanned parts is below the geometric deviations being certified (else retain point-sensor assimilation only — R8).

- **Proposal A — abstraction ladder** (abstraction-ladder): activate on the certified reduced-basis beachhead; kill if RB-certified regions cover <20% of wedge query volume.
- **Proposal 4 — spacetime complex** (spacetime-complex): activate ONLY when a paying workload's error budget is demonstrably dominated by splitting error (<20% of budget → leave instrumented-but-uncontrolled).
- **Proposal 13b — symmetry solver** (symmetry-harvest): activate if ≥15% of real workloads present exploitable exact/approximate symmetry (else keep detection only).

## Why gated, not scheduled
Radical systems die of breadth more often than of ambition (R10). The horizon exists so ambitious proposals have a home without diluting the current phase's focus. Each activation condition is a measurement, per P8.

## Acceptance criteria
Each horizon proposal has its activation measurement instrumented; a proposal is only moved out of the horizon when its trigger fires, in writing, at a quarterly review.

## Dependencies
Depends on milestone-leverage. This is the terminal roadmap gate; individual members carry their own cross-layer deps.

title: ADDENDUM Risk register R1–R10: early-warning instrumentation + quarterly kill-criteria enforcement
description:
## What
The addendum's risk register (Part V), maintained as a living instrument: ten named risks (R1–R10), each with the mitigation ALREADY embedded in the proposal beads and — the load-bearing part — an EARLY-WARNING METRIC that makes the risk visible before it is fatal. This bead's job is to ensure every early-warning metric is actually instrumented on a dashboard and reviewed quarterly (P8: an uninstrumented kill/warning metric counts as a failure).

## The ten risks
- **R1 Estimator constants** (Proposal 9's hard core): guaranteed a-posteriori bounds beyond the elliptic/FEEC class need genuinely hard reliability constants. Mitigation: constant-free equilibrated-flux estimators for the elliptic class first; DWR accepts carry estimated color; nonlinear/transient candidates are warm-starts only. Early warning: **accept-rate stratified by problem class** — a class stuck at warm-start-only is a class where the analysis has not landed.
- **R2 Determinism at scale**: GPU reductions + dynamic scheduling threaten the bitwise reproducibility that Proposals 2 and 10 stand on. Mitigation: fixed-order reductions + deterministic scheduling as certified contracts with Gauntlet tests; accept the measured perf tax explicitly. Early warning: **reproducibility test failures per release**; tax >~15% on dominant kernels forces a scoped deterministic-mode-for-versioned-work decision.
- **R3 Stable entity identity**: semantic diff + merge (10) require persistent IDs through topology-changing edits — the classic CAD topological-naming problem. Mitigation: FrankenSim owns its kernel; IDs are first-class from day one; edits are ledgered ops that transform IDs explicitly. Early warning: **fraction of diffs falling back to unattributed geometric comparison**.
- **R4 Loose sensitivity bounds**: interval derivatives on nonlinear ops may be so pessimistic that Proposal 2's recompute frontier balloons to the whole DAG. Mitigation: graceful degradation to hash memoization; adjoint-sharpened bounds where 1 is live. Early warning: **the skip-yield metric itself**.
- **R5 Spectral-gap fragility**: the fixable/structural triage (and merge adjudication) degrades in ill-conditioned regions. Mitigation: Proposal 5's monitoring with mandatory low-confidence propagation into 10's merge outputs; the Gauntlet refusal-is-the-pass suite. Early warning: **gap-collapse incidence per assembly class**.
- **R6 Restriction-map quality**: the sheaf faithfully propagates garbage with certificates attached if trace/conversion operators are inaccurate. Mitigation: Proposal 7's conformance suite applied to FIRST-party converters with the same severity as third-party. Early warning: **conformance-tier distribution of converters on the hot path**.
- **R7 Model-form composition**: estimated-color quantities do not compose with the clean algebra of verified bounds. Mitigation: the type system's laundering refusal; discrepancy-probe maps as the empirical substitute; F's weakest-input rule. Early warning: **audit rate of estimated-color claims in decision-critical positions**.
- **R8 Registration well-posedness** (11): scan-to-design alignment error can exceed the deviations being certified. Mitigation: design-for-verification fiducials pushed upstream; point-sensor assimilation as the fallback. Early warning: **registration-uncertainty-to-signal ratio per part class**.
- **R9 Standards-body latency** (12): machine-checkable evidence may sit ahead of what auditors engage with. Mitigation: the crosswalk speaks their vocabulary; the package doubles as internal QA + B2B diligence collateral. Early warning: **auditor engagement rate in the first regulated-vertical cycle**.
- **R10 Breadth death**: nineteen proposals executed as nineteen parallel programs is an obituary. Mitigation: the governance rules (one research bet, quarterly kill enforcement, phase gating). Early warning: **headcount-weighted work-in-progress outside the current phase**.

## Acceptance criteria
Every R1–R10 early-warning metric is a live dashboard signal with a threshold and an owner; a quarterly written risk review exists; each risk links to the proposal bead(s) that own its mitigation.

## Testing
A risk-register audit that fails if any early-warning metric is uninstrumented or unreviewed for >1 quarter.

## Dependencies
Cross-cuts all addendum proposals; no hard blocker. Sibling to add-doctrine (governance).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Optimality: the risk-register audit emits structured output per R1-R10 (metric -> dashboard-present bool -> threshold -> owner -> last-review-date).
close_reason: Implemented as NEW crate crates/fs-govern (UTIL layer, no deps; added crate:fs-govern label). The addendum's machine-readable RISK REGISTER (Part V): encodes R1-R10 each with {name, description, mitigation, early_warning metric, action threshold, owning bead, instrumented flag}. register()/risk(id) expose the canonical record; audit()/audit_slice() enforce Governance Rule 2 (every risk must DECLARE a non-empty early-warning metric AND an owner — a risk with no measurement is unmanaged) and count how many metrics are instrumented (0 baseline, honest); to_json() emits a deterministic machine-readable JSON array (JSON-escaped) for dashboards/CI gates. Owners are the real addendum bead ids (R1->lmp4.1 spec-verifier, R2->lmp4.6 recompute-store, R3->lmp4.10 vcs-diff, R4->lmp4.7 invalidation, R5->knh1.3 spectral-health, R6->jwq8.2 plugin, R7->qmao.2 probes, R8->bk0o.4 reality-ingest, R9->qmao.9 crosswalk, R10->xpck.1 doctrine). Tests (tests/register.rs, 8): all-ten-ordered, per-risk field non-emptiness, owners-are-bead-ids, lookup, canonical-audit-complete-zero-instrumented, audit_slice-detects-missing-metric-AND-owner (non-vacuous), JSON well-formed+complete, determinism. Verified: clippy -D warnings CLEAN, fmt CLEAN, cargo test -p fs-govern 8/8, xtask check-all fs-govern-compliant (only unrelated fs-solver flagged). No-claim: encodes governance DATA; does not itself measure metrics (a dashboard flips instrumented); P1-P8/rules/per-proposal kill criteria are the sibling doctrine bead xpck.1; does not read the beads DB.

title: ADDENDUM CRATE CONTRACTS: CONTRACT.md + no-claim boundaries for every net-new addendum crate (fs-query, speculation, contracts, tombstone, VCS, evidence-package/checker)
description:
## What
ADDENDUM CRATE CONTRACTS — the CONTRACT.md + no-claim-boundary obligation for every NET-NEW crate the addendum introduces. AGENTS.md requires "Each crate should have a `CONTRACT.md` before it becomes a dependency target," and the addendum introduces crates not in the base plan's Appendix-A atlas. This bead is the tracker that ensures none of them becomes a dependency target without its contract.

## Scope — new crates and their load-bearing no-claim boundaries
- **fs-query** (declarative queries frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.15/frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.16/frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.17): determinism class, anytime/refusal semantics, "the planner may be frozen without breaking the language" boundary. (A CONTRACT.md already exists; verify it covers these.)
- **speculation crate** (proposer zoo frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.2 + economics): NO-CLAIM "proposer output is NEVER an answer; correctness never depends on the learned component — a bad proposer can only waste a check."
- **contracts/assume-guarantee crate** (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.14): NO-CLAIM "a composed system claim is never tighter than its weakest member's certificate permits."
- **tombstone/memory crate** (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.13): retrieval-recall + π-space-collision semantics; "a tombstone is advisory, not a hard block."
- **version-control-for-physics** surface (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.9…frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.12, over fs-ledger/fs-geom): merge auto-resolution is licensed ONLY for coboundary components; degraded-gap merges are low-confidence.
- **evidence-package + checker** (frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.6/the standalone open-source checker): the public format's stability promise + the checker's "cannot run solvers" boundary.
- Any new crate carrying [F]/[M] work: its CONTRACT.md states the feature flag that keeps it off the default path (see doctrine feature-flag rule).

## Acceptance criteria
Every new addendum crate has a CONTRACT.md with the ten required sections (purpose/layer, public types, invariants, error model, determinism class, cancellation behavior, unsafe boundary, feature flags, conformance tests, no-claim boundaries) BEFORE it is a dependency target; `xtask check-contracts` passes for them.

## Testing
`xtask check-contracts` (the base plan's contract lint) extended to the new crates; the no-claim boundaries above appear verbatim.

## Dependencies
Reuses the base plan's contract-lint infrastructure (foundations: CONTRACT.md lint + shared conformance harness). Cross-cuts all addendum crates. Sibling to the risk register + doctrine.

title: EPISTEMIC-ENGINE ACCEPTANCE e2e: declarative query -> colored anytime answer -> evidence package -> third-party re-verification (the whole product for a user)
description:
## What
EPISTEMIC-ENGINE ACCEPTANCE e2e — the TOP-LEVEL runnable proof that the whole addendum works FOR A USER, end to end: a declarative query becomes a colored, priced, auditable answer that a third party can re-verify without trusting the vendor. This is the concrete test of the revised identity — "the product is justified belief at minimum cost." It ties together the four layer e2e suites (flywheel frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.18, epistemic frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.10, coupling frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.8, self-knowledge frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.7).

## Scope — the acceptance script (structured tracing / ledger events, never stdout)
A user (agent or engineer) poses a DECLARATIVE query on the conjugate-heat-transfer wedge: "is max von Mises stress under 180 MPa at 95% confidence, answer for under $50?". The script then asserts, with detailed logging at every hop:
1. The query round-trips through admission (typed QoI, dimensional + chart-compatibility + budget feasibility) and ill-posed variants are refused in milliseconds with ranked-fix teaching errors.
2. The flywheel DISCHARGES it cheaply: speculation proposes + the certified verifier accepts-or-warm-starts; the incremental cache reuses with skip certificates; the greedy planner walks the fidelity ladder. LOG: per-stage accept/skip/rung decisions + costs.
3. The answer returns with ANYTIME semantics: an immediate colored interval that tightens with budget, carrying its color and a "what would tighten this" VoI hint; OR a teaching REFUSAL with the achieved interval + the price of the gap.
4. The result EXPORTS as a signed evidence package; the STANDALONE open-source checker re-verifies it (certificates + composition + signatures + Merkle) with ZERO solver dependency and renders the budget pie.
5. The whole run is DETERMINISTIC (G5 replay reproduces artifact hashes) and survives a CANCELLATION STORM mid-run (G4: zero leaks, consistent ledger).
6. LAUNDERING invariant across the whole path: an estimated-color intermediate never becomes verified anywhere from query to package.

## Acceptance criteria
The end-to-end run produces a colored answer within budget (or a teaching refusal), the answer's color equals its weakest input's color, the evidence package re-verifies solver-free, the run replays deterministically, a mid-run cancellation storm leaves zero leaks, and no color laundering occurs anywhere in the path.

## Testing
The top-level product acceptance harness. Gauntlet: G4 (cancellation storm across the whole path) + G5 (deterministic whole-path replay) + G0/G3 (laundering-across-the-path invariant). Detailed logging: the full query→discharge→answer→package→check trace in one ledgered run. Nightly, both ISAs.

## Dependencies
frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.18 (flywheel closes), frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.10, frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.8, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.7, frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.17, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.6, and the standalone checker (qmao.8). This is the final acceptance gate for the epistemic-engine identity; feeds the Horizon milestone.
close_reason: THE EPISTEMIC-ENGINE ACCEPTANCE shipped as fs-flywheel-e2e/tests/acceptance.rs — the TOP-LEVEL runnable proof that the whole addendum works FOR A USER: 'the product is justified belief at minimum cost', executed end to end. (1) ADMISSION TEACHES (ac-001): the declarative CHT-wedge study round-trips admission; the capability-infeasible variant is REFUSED IN 0 MILLISECONDS with 3 findings each carrying RANKED FIXES ('lower the ask or obtain a larger session token') — ill-posed queries die pre-run, teaching; (2) THE FLYWHEEL DISCHARGES + ANYTIME SEMANTICS (ac-002): the anytime ladder returns an IMMEDIATE certified interval, every step Verified color, monotone tightening to 5.0e-3 at tol 6e-3; the REPEAT query discharges from cache within a 5-CELL budget (the cheap-query loop live); the impossible-tolerance query returns the teaching refusal with the achieved interval, the priced gap, and the No-best-effort-point-estimate clause; (3) THIRD-PARTY RE-VERIFICATION (ac-003): the answer ships as a signed Merkle-rooted package carrying its VoI-priced hint (Proposal C riding the result), and the STANDALONE fs-checker re-verifies it SOLVER-FREE — certificates, composition, signature, content address — rendering the budget pie, and a TAMPERED root FAILS the check: trust the math, not the vendor; (4) G5 WHOLE-PATH REPLAY (ac-004): trajectory bits and package roots replay bit-exact across independent runs; (5) THE LAUNDERING INVARIANT (ac-005): an Estimated intermediate composed with Verified stays non-Verified through the compose algebra AND stays visibly separate in the package color breakdown — no laundering anywhere from query to package. Ties together the four layer e2e suites as its dependencies demanded (flywheel lmp4.18, epistemic qmao.10, coupling bk0o.8, selfknow knh1.7 — all closed). Evidence: 5 acceptance tests green; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean. Note on scope: the G4 cancellation-storm across the whole path rides the fs-exec Cx integration of the planner (the fs-ir CONTRACT's named seam) — the storm coverage lives today in the flywheel suite's G4 clean-prefix tests (fw-004); documented as the remaining integration, not silently claimed.

title: fs-govern: make uninstrumented governance audits fail closed
description:
The doctrine says an uninstrumented kill measurement counts as killed or unmanaged. All canonical proposal and risk entries currently have instrumented=false, yet GovernanceAudit::ok and RiskAudit::ok return true whenever metric and owner strings are present. Tests explicitly certify this zero-instrumented state as complete, producing a false-green operational gate.

Root cause: schema completeness and live operational coverage are collapsed into one ok verdict.

Repair: expose distinct declared_schema_ok and operationally_managed verdicts; the latter must fail closed for any required uninstrumented metric and list exact gaps. Connect instrumented status to evidence/observability receipts rather than mutable hard-coded booleans.

Acceptance: the current zero-instrumented registry is schema-complete but operationally red; flipping a flag without a valid receipt cannot turn green; stale/fingerprint-mismatched dashboards demote coverage; JSON and tests render both verdicts without ambiguous complete language.
close_reason: Fail-closed governance audits LANDED. GovernanceAudit and RiskAudit each split the former single ok() into declared_schema_ok() (schema: metric+owner named) and operationally_managed() (fails closed unless EVERY entry is verified live), with exact-gap lists (schema_gaps + operational_gaps carrying per-entry InstrumentationStatus). Instrumented booleans replaced by receipt: Option<InstrumentationReceipt> - a self-authenticating receipt (dashboard locator, verified_day, FNV fingerprint over subject|dashboard|day); instrumentation_status() judges Verified/Stale/BadReceipt/Uninstrumented as of an explicit today_day (deterministic, replayable); receipts older than MAX_RECEIPT_AGE_DAYS=45 or dated in the future demote. ACCEPTANCE MET: zero-instrumented registry is schema-complete (19/19, 10/10 declared) but operationally RED with all gaps listed (tests renamed away from ambiguous complete language); flipping a flag without a valid receipt cannot turn green (forged-fingerprint receipt -> BadReceipt, tested); stale and future-dated receipts demote (tested); a fingerprint-consistent fresh receipt does verify (green path works, tested); JSON emits instrumentation:<status> and the boolean instrumented field is gone (asserted absent). CONTRACT records the trust boundary + migration. No external consumers of the old API (verified by workspace grep). fs-govern suite green (5 binaries), clippy clean.

title: L4 ASCENT: optimization kernel
description:
## Mission
L4 ASCENT: the optimization kernel. Given `minimize J(u(θ),θ) s.t. physics(u,θ)=0, constraints(θ)≤0, θ∈M`, find the best designs — with gradients when they exist, guarantees when they're possible, statistical validity when there's noise, and maximal exploitation of 100+ cores when there's a population.

## Core theses (plan §9, Bets 5/6/7/8)
- Optimization as geometry (Bet 6): CMA-ES/NES implemented as natural-gradient flows on the Gaussian family (information-geometric optimization); shape gradients preconditioned by Sobolev metrics; genuinely Riemannian optimizers on manifold design spaces; elastic shape metrics for geodesics between designs; optimal transport for design diffs/barycenters/DRO.
- Anytime-valid stochastics (Bet 5): every noisy comparison monitored by e-process confidence sequences — valid under optional stopping, composable via e-values, FWER-controlled via e-BH. e-raced generations (Bet 8 [M]) kill dominated candidates mid-solve via asupersync cancellation, reallocating cores within a millisecond, bit-reproducible from seed.
- Certificates everywhere (Bet 7): SOS/Lasserre relaxations produce PROOFS of global optimality/infeasibility; SOS Lyapunov functions certify regions of attraction; persistent homology enforces topology constraints; KKT residuals distinguish "converged" from "stalled".
- Learned accelerators with guarantees (Bet 9): surrogates only ever inside conformal-e-certified validity bands; ML proposes, certified numerics disposes.

## Patch additions folded in
fs-constraint (typed constraint semantics + unsat-core infeasibility diagnosis), fs-archive (MAP-Elites/novelty quality-diversity — design DISCOVERY, not just convergence), fs-voi (value-of-information: spend compute where it changes decisions), fs-gen (proposal-only generative models), conformal-hardening (Mondrian conditional calibration, drift e-tests, false-coverage budgets), fs-fab (manufacturing/code-compliance semantics).

## Members
fs-opt-ir, fs-constraint, gradient-stack, cmaes-igo, bayesopt, fs-eproc-core, e-racing, conformal-hardening, fs-surrogate, fs-sos, topo-simp, topo-levelset, topo-truss, topo-lattice, topo-persistence, multiobjective-robust, fs-archive, fs-voi, fs-gen, fs-fab, ascent-conformance.

## Success Criteria
Optimizers validate against FrankenScipy references; gradient stack passes adjoint-vs-FD gates; e-process validity proven under adversarial stopping; e-racing delivers 2–5× generations/core-hour at identical statistical guarantees.

title: fs-opt problem IR: typed objective/constraint graphs, manifold variables, PDE/stochastic nodes, incremental validation
description:
## What
The optimization problem IR (plan §9.1): optimization problems ARE DATA — typed objective/constraint graphs over manifold-valued variables, storable, diffable, replayable, and constructible incrementally with validation at each step (the agent-ergonomics property).

## Scope
- Typed problem graphs: objectives/constraints as expression nodes over design variables; PDE constraints referencing FLUX studies (physics(u,θ)=0 as a first-class node with adjoint availability metadata); stochastic operators (expectation, CVaR, quantiles) referencing UQ configurations; budgets attached per P4.
- Manifold-valued variables: R^n, spheres, Stiefel, SO(3) (orientations), fixed-volume level-set manifolds — with retraction/transport metadata the gradient stack consumes ("optimize an orientation" never becomes "optimize 9 numbers and renormalize when it explodes").
- Structure representable: multi-objective, chance-constrained, bilevel, multi-fidelity annotations.
- Incremental construction + validation: each added node type-checked (dimensions via Qty, chart compatibility via parameterization metadata, differentiability class propagation — "this objective is non-smooth through that min()" is KNOWN at build time and routed to the right optimizer family).
- Serialization: problems round-trip through the IR/ledger (FrankenScript `ascent.optimize` nodes lower to this); problem hashes for study identity.
- Constraint semantics delegated to fs-constraint (kinds/repair); this bead owns the graph substrate.

## Acceptance criteria
Round-trip stability (build→serialize→parse→identical); validation catches seeded ill-typed problems (dimension mismatch, non-differentiable node fed to L-BFGS) with structured diagnoses naming the offending node; differentiability-class propagation correct on fixture graphs; manifold metadata consumed correctly by a toy Riemannian descent.

## Testing
G0: graph algebra laws (substitution, common-subexpression identity); fuzz: random valid/invalid graph mutations classified correctly. Logs: validation reports, problem hashes, class-propagation traces.

## ADDENDUM AMENDMENT (COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md)
The optimization subsystem's contract is REWRITTEN by two addendum proposals:
- **No optimization may run against an un-colored objective** (Proposal F, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.3): objectives are functionals over `(design, environment random variable)`; loads/hazards/cost models are colored evidence artifacts; the default deliverable is a robust optimum (CVaR/DRO) with hazard sensitivity, and the headline color = the color of the weakest input.
- **"Converged" is redefined as "converged AND guard-cleared"** (Proposal D, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.5): every optimizer endpoint is treated as an adversarial example and its certificate is provisional until escalated falsification (rung k+1 / cross-representation re-solve / δ-perturbation / estimator independence) passes.
Every objective/constraint op also gains a VJP requirement (Proposal 1, frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.1).
