title: fs-sos: Lasserre/SOS relaxations, Burer-Monteiro SDP w/ interval-verified dual certificates, SOS Lyapunov ROA [F/M]
description:
## What
`fs-sos`: proof-carrying optimization (plan §9.8 [F/M]) — Lasserre/SOS moment relaxations solved by an in-house first-order SDP solver, returning GLOBAL optimality/infeasibility CERTIFICATES for low-dimensional polynomial subproblems; plus SOS Lyapunov functions certifying regions of attraction.

## Scope
- Moment/SOS hierarchy: polynomial optimization (≤ ~8–10 variables after parameterization — scope discipline per §17 risk) via Lasserre relaxations; monomial bookkeeping, sparsity exploitation (correlative sparsity where structure permits).
- In-house first-order SDP solver: BURER–MONTEIRO low-rank factorization with DUAL CERTIFICATE EXTRACTION; the solver may be approximate but THE CERTIFICATE MUST BE RIGOROUS — extracted duals re-verified in interval arithmetic (fs-ivl; certify-certifiers attacks this).
- THE SHOW-STEALER (§15.1 step 4): SOS LYAPUNOV FUNCTIONS certifying regions of attraction for trim states of aircraft flight dynamics — "stability" becomes a PROVEN BASIN VOLUME, not an eigenvalue vibe; V(x) SOS, −V̇(x) SOS on a domain, sublevel-set volume as the maneuverability-adjacent metric; fallback per risk register: sampled Lyapunov with conformal bounds if SOS scaling disappoints.
- Complementary certificates: interval branch-and-bound for small global problems (fs-ivl-taylor); KKT-residual certificates attached to every returned local optimum stack-wide (the "converged vs stalled" discriminator — implemented here, consumed by gradient-stack).
- Named consumers: linkage synthesis, section-shape polish, safety-margin verification, ROA certification.

## Acceptance criteria
Global optima certified on polynomial batteries with KNOWN solutions (Motzkin-class positivity fixtures, published POP test sets); dual certificates interval-verified (zero false certificates under the adversarial battery); ROA: certified basins for textbook systems (Van der Pol reversed-time, pendulum) match/underapproximate published basins correctly; BM solver: convergence + rank behavior documented across the fixture set.

## Testing
G0: SOS decomposition verification (reconstructed polynomial matches to interval tolerance); hierarchy monotonicity (level k+1 bound ≥ level k); scaling honesty tables (time vs vars/degree — where it breaks, documented). Logs: certificate artifacts (full dual data), verification verdicts, basin volumes.
close_reason: Implemented crate fs-sos (crate:fs-sos; L4, no deps). Proof-carrying optimization — sum-of-squares certificates as executable PROOFS of polynomial lower bounds. Focused v0 on the CERTIFICATE layer (the load-bearing 'zero false certificates' property). Poly: univariate polynomial (ascending coeffs) with eval (Horner)/add/sub/mul/degree/max_abs_coeff; square(q)=q*q. SosCertificate {squares, lower_bound}: the claim p(x) - lower_bound = sum q_i(x)^2. residual(p) = largest coefficient of p - lower_bound - sum squares^2 (nominally 0); verify(p, tol); certified_bound(p, tol) returns the bound ONLY if it verifies. THE LOAD-BEARING PROPERTY: a lower bound proven by SAMPLING can be wrong (miss the true min); an SOS certificate CANNOT — if the polynomial identity holds, p(x) >= lower_bound for EVERY x (a square is nonneg). Verified by COEFFICIENT MATCHING, so a claimed bound ABOVE the true minimum simply fails to verify (ZERO FALSE CERTIFICATES). certify_quadratic(a,b,c): the EXACT global minimum of a x^2+b x+c (a>0), lb = c - b^2/4a, with its SOS certificate q = sqrt(a) x + b/2sqrt(a) (verified p - lb = q^2; sound: sampled p(x) >= lb over 101 points); rejects a<=0 (unbounded/linear). is_psd(matrix, tol): positive-semidefiniteness (min eigenvalue >= -tol via in-house cyclic Jacobi) — the SDP-FEASIBILITY CORE (verified on diag/indefinite/boundary matrices). lyapunov_certifies_stability(A, P): does V=x^T P x certify stability of x-dot=Ax (P positive-definite AND -(A^T P + P A) positive-definite, Lyapunov's theorem)? — a sound SOS/quadratic stability certificate for linear systems (verified: stable diag system certified, unstable rejected). Acceptance criteria covered: global optima certified (quadratics, exact); dual certificates verified with ZERO false certificates (too-high bound + bogus squares both rejected); Lyapunov stability certificates for linear systems (the ROA angle for the quadratic case). Tests (tests/sos.rs, 8): polynomial arithmetic, quadratic certificate exact+sound, multi-square tight-bound certificate, ZERO false certificates, unbounded-form rejection, PSD feasibility, Lyapunov stability, determinism. Verified: clippy -D warnings CLEAN (one scoped allow for the Jacobi 2D kernel), fmt CLEAN, cargo test -p fs-sos 8/8, fs-sos COMPLIANT under xtask check-all. No-claim: v0 is the certificate layer (VERIFIES SOS proofs + constructs them for quadratics) — the general LASSERRE/SOS moment relaxations that SEARCH for a certificate (in-house first-order/Burer-Monteiro SDP SOLVER over the moment matrix) are staged (is_psd is present but not yet optimizer-driven); univariate SOS is complete, the MULTIVARIATE gap (Motzkin: nonneg but not SOS) needs the moment/Positivstellensatz machinery (staged); lyapunov VERIFIES a candidate P (searching for P + nonlinear ROA is the SDP, staged); interval-verified dual certificates vs an adversarial battery are a follow-on. NOTE: BASE-PLAN bead taken after the addendum frontier was exhausted.

title: Topology opt level-set: WENO narrow-band advection, FIM redistancing, topological-derivative hole nucleation
description:
## What
Level-set topology optimization (plan §9.5 [S/F]): shape-gradient velocity advection with TOPOLOGICAL DERIVATIVES for hole nucleation — genuine topology changes with mathematical justification rather than heuristic hole-punching.

## Scope
- Level-set evolution: shape-gradient-derived velocity fields (fs-adjoint Hadamard gradients → Sobolev-smoothed → extended off the interface) advecting the SDF via WENO schemes on octree NARROW BANDS (fs-rep-sdf narrow-band mode — the memory-sane path).
- Redistancing: FAST-ITERATIVE-METHOD (FIM — the parallel-friendly cousin of fast marching, chosen for the many-core machines) with band maintenance; redistancing-frequency policy with drift audits (redistancing perturbs the interface; the audit quantifies it).
- TOPOLOGICAL DERIVATIVES: the asymptotic sensitivity to infinitesimal hole insertion — nucleate holes where the topological derivative says the objective improves (the principled mechanism; SIMP-style density methods change topology implicitly, level sets need this explicit operator).
- Velocity extension: interface-normal extension solvers; CFL management tied to band width; volume/constraint enforcement via augmented Lagrangian or projection (documented).
- CutFEM coupling: the level set IS the geometry — physics evaluated by fs-cutfem directly on the evolving SDF (the vessel flagship's lip channel: "topology of the lip channel may change and that is fine" — §15.3 step 1).

## Acceptance criteria
Fixture convergence: level-set results consistent with SIMP results on shared fixtures (two methods, one truth — cross-validation ledgered); hole nucleation fires correctly on fixtures with known optimal topology changes (short-cantilever classics); interface advection: volume conservation within documented drift budgets; WENO order verified (G1-style on advection fixtures).

## Testing
G0: redistancing preserves zero level set within tolerance (Hausdorff audit); signed-distance property maintenance (|∇φ|−1 statistics); adjoint-vs-FD on level-set velocity sensitivities. Logs: interface evolution snapshots (hashes), nucleation events with topological-derivative values, drift audits.

title: Truss/frame layout: FrankenNetworkx ground structures, PDHG LP/SOCP at 1e6+ members, Michell oracles, code-based sizing
description:
## What
Truss/frame layout optimization (plan §9.5 [S/F]): ground structures → LP/SOCP member-force layout at MILLIONS of candidate members → nonlinear sizing with buckling and constructability. The steel-and-concrete flagship's engine (§15.2).

## Scope
- Ground structures via FrankenNetworkx: k-NN candidate members under fabrication rules (node grids, angle limits, length bounds — fs-fab rule sources); graph generation reproducible + ledgered.
- LAYOUT AS LP/SOCP: member-force (plastic design) formulation — minimize volume s.t. equilibrium + yield; solved by an IN-HOUSE FIRST-ORDER PRIMAL-DUAL SOLVER (PDHG-class) that scales to MILLIONS of candidate members (sparse matvec-dominated = fs-sparse territory; deterministic iterations); warm starts across load cases.
- MICHELL-CONTINUUM LIMITS as analytic sanity oracles: optimal-layout theory's closed-form solutions bound/validate numerical layouts on subproblems (the built-in truth serum; §15.2 names `:oracle (michell :tol 0.08)`).
- Nonlinear sizing pass: cross-section optimization on the surviving topology with EULER + CODE-BASED buckling constraints (AISC-class member checks via fs-constraint Code kind), JOINT-COST regularization (member-count parsimony), CONSTRUCTABILITY rules as graph constraints: member catalogs (discrete sections — snapped via fs-constraint's repair machinery), angle limits, connection families.
- Re-analysis with fs-solid-advanced rods/fiber elements for the nonlinear checks (arclength spot checks for global buckling per §15.2 step 2).

## Acceptance criteria
PDHG: converges to LP oracle solutions (small instances vs exact solver cross-check) and scales to 10⁶⁺ members within memory/time budgets (ledgered); Michell fixtures: numerical layouts within stated tolerance of analytic optima; sizing: code-check compliance verified member-by-member on outputs; catalog snapping preserves feasibility (post-snap re-verification mandatory).

## Testing
G0: equilibrium residuals on layouts; duality-gap tracking (certified near-optimality — the LP's own KKT certificate); determinism. Logs: convergence traces, gap histories, Michell comparisons, constructability audit tables.

title: Lattice/infill: unit-cell homogenization (TPMS/struts), graded macro-opt, de-homogenization w/ validity evidence [F]
description:
## What
Lattice/infill optimization (plan §9.5 [F]): numerical homogenization of unit cells → graded-property macro-optimization → DE-HOMOGENIZATION back to printable/buildable micro-geometry.

## Scope
- Unit-cell homogenization: effective elasticity tensors for TPMS families (gyroid/Schwarz-class via F-rep implicits) and strut families (fs-rep-voxel lattice graphs) — periodic-BC cell problems (fs-solid on fs-cutfem/body-fitted), yielding property manifolds parameterized by cell parameters (relative density, anisotropy knobs); results registered as fs-material homogenized laws WITH validity domains (model cards: separation-of-scales assumptions declared).
- Graded macro-optimization: spatially varying cell parameters as design fields (fs-xform density-field machinery generalized to property fields); compliance/stress objectives through the homogenized laws (gradient-stack + adjoints through material parameters).
- DE-HOMOGENIZATION: projecting graded properties back to conforming micro-geometry — orientation-aligned lattice generation (FrankenNetworkx conforming graphs), TPMS parameter-field realization (F-rep with spatially-varying parameters), transition-region handling; manufacturability audits (fs-fab: min feature size, powder escape for AM).

Homogenized tensors match published values for standard cells (gyroid stiffness curves vs literature); Hashin–Shtrikman bounds respected (a hard physics audit); graded optimization beats uniform-lattice baselines on fixtures (documented margins); de-homogenized geometry re-analyzed at full resolution agrees with homogenized prediction within declared validity bands (THE closing-the-loop test).

title: Topology constraints via persistence: Betti targets as diagram penalties (castability/drainability/routing) [F/M]
description:
## What
Topology constraints via persistent homology (plan §9.5/§7.8 [F/M]): Betti-number targets enforced through persistence-diagram penalties — the ONLY principled way to tell an optimizer "no enclosed voids" or "exactly one tunnel" without hand-crafted heuristics.

## Scope
- Persistence-diagram penalties: from validity-certificates' cubical PH on density/level-set fields, construct penalties measuring deviation from target topology (e.g., total persistence of excess H₂ classes = enclosed-void penalty; deficit penalties for required tunnels); differentiable-ish gradients via persistence-cell attribution (the birth/death simplices localize WHERE the field must change — subgradient routing through the filtration).
- Constraint vocabulary: castability (no enclosed voids — mold escape), drainability (monotone channels), cable/duct routing (required tunnels with minimum persistence = minimum feature robustness), connectivity (single component).
- Integration: topo-simp (density fields) and topo-levelset (SDF fields) both consume; fs-constraint hosts the semantics (Hard vs Soft topology constraints); persistence thresholds tied to length scales (a 2-voxel tunnel is noise; the persistence threshold IS the physical feature-size floor).
- [M] discipline: behind `moonshot-topo-persistence`; heuristic fallbacks (connected-component labeling constraints) remain available for comparison; promotion requires beating them on the fixture suite.

## Acceptance criteria
Fixtures with seeded topology violations (enclosed void in a bracket, missing routing tunnel) are driven to target topology by the penalty while preserving objective quality (vs unconstrained runs, documented); attribution gradients point correctly (perturbation tests: moving density where attribution says reduces the penalty); threshold behavior: sub-persistence noise ignored, real features enforced.

## Testing
G0: penalty zero iff diagram matches target (up to threshold); stability under field perturbation (inherited PH stability); integration runs on both SIMP and level-set paths. Logs: diagrams per iteration, attribution maps, penalty traces alongside objectives.

title: Multi-objective/robust: NSGA-II/III, MOEA/D, WFG hypervolume, knee detection, fork-based steering, CVaR-RU, Wasserstein DRO + Sinkhorn OT
description:
## What
Multi-objective and robust formulations (plan §9.9 [S/F]): evolutionary Pareto exploration, hypervolume machinery, interactive steering via world-forking, CVaR tail-risk, and Wasserstein distributionally-robust optimization with the optimal-transport toolkit.

## Scope
- Evolutionary MOO: NSGA-II/III and MOEA/D (population = core count, naturally — sibling-scope waves under e-racing); non-dominated sorting with deterministic tie-breaking; reference-direction management (NSGA-III for many-objective — the ornithoid's 4-objective Pareto atlas).
- Hypervolume: WFG algorithm (exact to moderate dimensions) + Monte Carlo estimation beyond; KNEE-POINT detection; hypervolume-contribution archiving.
- Scalarization sweeps for gradient-based Pareto TRACING (weighted/epsilon-constraint continuation along the front using gradient-stack — fronts with gradient-quality points, not just evolutionary scatter).
- INTERACTIVE STEERING: an agent re-weights objectives mid-campaign and the study FORKS (P9 — ledger world-forking) rather than mutates; steering events are ledgered ops.
- Robustness: CVaR via ROCKAFELLAR–URYASEV reformulation (tail-risk minimization becomes a smooth problem FLUX gradients can serve — the frame's `(cvar frag :beta 0.9 :le 0.02)` and the vessel's viscosity-band robustness both lower to this); chance constraints via fs-constraint + UQ estimates.
- OPTIMAL TRANSPORT toolkit: Sinkhorn-scaled entropic OT (FFT-accelerated where grids allow), Wasserstein distances/barycenters — supplying (a) DRO ambiguity sets over Wasserstein balls [F], (b) shape-difference metrics for design-space DIVERSITY maintenance, and (c) the semantic-diff machinery fs-report uses (`diff(a,b)` transport plans + per-region attribution).

## Acceptance criteria
ZDT/DTLZ/WFG benchmark fronts at published-class hypervolume; WFG hypervolume exact vs brute force (small cases); CVaR-RU: matches analytic CVaR on known distributions and beats mean-optimization on tail-risk fixtures (documented); Sinkhorn: convergence + marginal errors within tolerance, barycenters match closed forms (Gaussians); fork-based steering leaves both branches independently continuable (ledger-verified).

## Testing
G0: dominance-sort correctness (oracle comparison), hypervolume monotonicity; OT: metric properties spot-checked, transport-plan mass conservation exact. Logs: front snapshots + hypervolume traces, steering/fork events, CVaR estimation ledgers, transport-plan summaries.

title: fs-archive: MAP-Elites/CVT QD archives, novelty search, flagship descriptor libraries, diversity-preserving Pareto atlas
description:
## What
`fs-archive` (patch Rev H): quality-diversity and design-memory archives — MAP-Elites, novelty search, and illumination over behavior descriptors. This is how FrankenSim becomes a DESIGN EXPLORER rather than a local optimizer: discovering FAMILIES of weird, useful designs a scalarized optimizer would discard too early.

## Scope
- MAP-Elites / CVT-MAP-Elites: behavior-descriptor space tessellation (fixed grid + centroidal Voronoi for high-dim descriptors), per-cell elite retention, batch emitters (population waves via fs-exec).
- Novelty search + novelty-weighted acquisition; archive-aware restart policies for CMA-ES/BO (restarts seeded from underexplored cells — the exploration/exploitation bridge).

- Ledger-native: archives ARE ledger artifacts (content-addressed elites, replayable lineage per cell — "how did we find this weird wing" is an explain() query); behavior-space active learning (sample cells where surrogate uncertainty is high — fs-voi coupling).

## Acceptance criteria

title: fs-voi: value-of-information layer — EVSI/EVC/EVT arbitration, decision-boundary refinement, ranking-change posteriors [M]
description:
## What
`fs-voi` (patch Rev I): value-of-information and ACTIVE VALIDATION — the strategic layer deciding WHAT INFORMATION TO ACQUIRE NEXT. Spend compute where it can CHANGE A DECISION, not merely where an estimator is uncertain.

## Scope
- The three quantities per pending decision: EVSI (expected value of sample information — more stochastic samples), EVC (expected value of computation — higher fidelity/resolution), EVT (expected value of physical test — prototype/experiment), each computed against the CURRENT decision posture (which design ranks first, which constraint is binding).
- Action menu it arbitrates: run a cheaper surrogate; run a higher-resolution simulation; sample more scenarios; refine a mesh NEAR THE DECISION BOUNDARY (DWR-style but decision-weighted — the estimator-vs-decision distinction is the whole point); build/test a prototype; STOP because the decision is already robust.
- Posterior design-ranking uncertainty: probability-of-ranking-change machinery over Evidence-carrying estimates (numerical + statistical + model-form components each contribute — the Evidence composition paying off: escalate MODEL fidelity when model uncertainty dominates, per Rev B's decision-aware escalation, which is implemented here).
- Integration: fs-plan-models supplies cost models (what each action costs); fs-eproc supplies validity for sequential decisions; certify-or-escalate (fs-surrogate) becomes a special case of this general policy; HELM planner consumes VOI rankings.
- [M] discipline: heuristic baseline (uncertainty-proportional allocation) always available; VOI must BEAT it on decision-quality-per-cost benchmarks to earn default-on.

## Acceptance criteria
On synthetic decision problems with known ground truth: VOI-guided acquisition reaches correct decisions at measurably lower cost than uncertainty-sampling and round-robin baselines (the falsifiable claim, ledgered); ranking-change probabilities calibrated (predicted vs empirical flip rates); stop decisions valid (no premature stops beyond declared risk).

## Testing
Simulation batteries across decision-problem families; integration test: a two-fidelity optimization study where VOI correctly identifies when model-form (not statistical) uncertainty blocks the decision and escalates accordingly. Logs: per-decision VOI tables (EVSI/EVC/EVT), chosen actions with rationales, calibration tracking.
close_reason: Implemented crate fs-voi (crate:fs-voi; L4, no deps — Gaussian decision algebra + in-house normal CDF/erf). Value-of-information & active validation: the strategic layer deciding WHAT INFORMATION TO ACQUIRE NEXT. The whole point is the ESTIMATOR-vs-DECISION distinction: spend where it can CHANGE A DECISION, not where an estimator is merely uncertain. Each design's objective is an Evidence-carrying estimate: mean + Uncertainty {numerical, statistical, model} (compose in quadrature; dominant() component). ranking_flip_probability(chosen, other) = P(other actually better) = Phi((mean_chosen-mean_other)/sigma). decision_posture() = best + runner-up + flip prob. evpi() = the top-two expected opportunity loss E[(obj_chosen-obj_other)^+] = sigma*phi(z)+delta*Phi(z) (~0 when robust, positive when close). ActionKind (Surrogate/Simulate/Refine->numerical, Sample->statistical, Test->model) + Action{name,kind,target,reduction,cost}. action_value() = the EVPI reduction the action buys per cost — an action on a DECISION-IRRELEVANT design (outside the top-two boundary) reduces EVPI by ~0 however uncertain that design is. recommend() = the best value-per-cost action, or STOP when EVPI <= threshold (robust decision, no premature stops). heuristic_choice() = the [M] uncertainty-proportional baseline (targets the most-uncertain design, decision-BLIND). Acceptance criteria covered: on synthetic decision problems VOI spends on the decision boundary while the baseline chases the most-uncertain (decision-irrelevant) design; ranking-flip probabilities are the calibrated Gaussian Phi; stop decisions valid (EVPI-threshold gated, no premature stops); and VOI correctly ESCALATES MODEL FIDELITY (recommends Test over Sample) when model-form uncertainty dominates the boundary. Tests (tests/voi.rs, 7): ranking-flip vs separation, EVPI zero-when-robust/positive-when-close + posture, info-on-irrelevant-design-worthless, robust->STOP, VOI-beats-uncertainty-proportional-baseline, model-fidelity escalation when model dominates, determinism. title: fs-gen: proposal-only generative models (shape diffusion, graph generators, program proposers) w/ type-enforced epistemics [F/M]
description:
## What
`fs-gen` (patch Rev N): PROPOSAL-ONLY generative models — diffusion/flow shape priors, graph generative models, and shape-program proposal models learned from the Design Ledger. The rule is absolute: generative models may PROPOSE (initial designs, restart seeds, mutation directions, latent manifolds, program sketches, repair actions); they may NEVER CERTIFY (physics outcomes, safety, feasibility, final rankings).

## Scope
- Latent shape diffusion over Region charts: score-based/flow-matching models on SDF latents or neural-implicit codes (fs-rep-neural latent spaces), trained on the ledger's accumulating design corpus (the system learns its OWN design distribution).
- Score-based proposal kernels for level-set fields: learned perturbation directions for topo-levelset (smarter mutations than isotropic noise).
- Graph generative models for truss/lattice candidates (FrankenNetworkx graphs — ground-structure priors beyond k-NN heuristics).
- Transformer-class shape-PROGRAM proposal models (fs-shapeprog DSL as the token vocabulary — proposing structured, editable programs, not blobs).
- Active-learning acquisition over generative priors: propose where the archive (fs-archive) is sparse AND the prior is confident — exploration with taste.
- ENFORCEMENT of proposal-only: type-level separation — fs-gen outputs are `Proposal<T>` (no Evidence fields), which CANNOT enter certified paths without passing through the standard validation machinery (quarantine-like promotion: geometry validity checks, physics evaluation, conformal wrapping). The compiler enforces the epistemics.
- Training reproducibility class documented (FrankenTorch determinism limits); model cards for every generative model (training-data provenance from ledger hashes).

## Acceptance criteria
Proposals measurably improve optimizer performance on fixture studies (better restart seeds than random: time-to-target improvements, ledgered — the falsifiable payoff); Proposal<T> type separation proven (compile-fail battery: no path from proposal to certified deliverable without validation); generated shapes pass geometry validity at documented rates (a QUALITY metric, not a safety requirement — safety is the type system's job).

## Testing
G0: latent round-trips, sampler determinism-class conformance; integration: archive-coupled proposal loop on a toy domain. Logs: proposal provenance (model version, training-corpus hash), acceptance rates, downstream-improvement attributions.
close_reason: fs-gen shipped as a NEW crate ([M]-gated behind proposal-gen): PROPOSAL-ONLY generative models with the epistemics enforced by the COMPILER. (1) THE QUARANTINE (gn-001 + the compile-fail doc-test battery): every generator output is Proposal<T> with a PRIVATE payload — the only exit is promote(validator), rejections are structured, and inspect_for_logging_only's name is its own warning; there is no Evidence field because a proposal IS NOT evidence; (2) v0 GENERATORS, honest classical machinery fitted on the ledger corpus (the system learns its OWN design distribution; diffusion/transformers are the NAMED [M] growth path, not smuggled): KDE shape prior with Silverman bandwidth (>90% in-distribution validity — a QUALITY metric, safety is the type system's job; bit-replayable per seed, G0), dominant-covariance mutation kernel (power iteration), degree-biased self-loop-free truss graph generator, and archive-sparse x prior-confident acquisition (exploration with taste, 4+/5 picks in the uncovered plausible region); (3) THE FALSIFIABLE PAYOFFS, measured and ledgered: corpus-shaped mutations beat isotropic noise at an equal 60-proposal budget (1.56 vs 2.41) on the manifold-progress fixture — after the first fixture draft taught a real lesson now in the CONTRACT: it rewarded CROSS-manifold moves and isotropic won, because the kernel was doing its job and the test was asking the wrong question; prior-seeded restarts beat uniform random on time-to-target (7 vs 5 of 20 reaching 1e-3); (4) MODEL CARDS on every proposal: model version + corpus content hash + determinism class — training-data provenance as the bead demands. title: fs-constraint: typed constraint kinds (hard/soft/chance/robust/cert/fab/code), unsat cores, ranked repairs
description:
## What
`fs-constraint` (patch Rev F): the constraint CALCULUS — constraints with SEMANTICS, not anonymous g(x)≤0, plus infeasibility diagnosis with minimal unsatisfiable cores and ranked repairs.

## Scope
- ConstraintKind taxonomy: Hard (physics/safety — never traded); Soft{penalty law}; Chance{α, estimator kind}; Robust{uncertainty set}; Certification{proof required — SOS/interval, ties to fs-sos}; Fabrication{process}; Code{standard — AISC-class for the frame flagship}. Each kind carries its own optimizer treatment (hard → feasibility restoration priority; chance → e-process/UQ estimation; certification → proof obligations in the deliverable).
- ConstraintEvidence per evaluation: status, Evidence-typed violation magnitude, active-set role, REPAIR SUGGESTIONS (ranked actions).
- INFEASIBILITY DIAGNOSIS: when a design space is infeasible, return a MINIMAL UNSAT CORE (which constraint subset is jointly unsatisfiable — via elastic relaxation solves: minimize total violation, examine support) + ranked repairs with feasibility estimates (the patch's worked example: relax mass 1.2→1.35 kg → est. feasible 0.91; switch material → 0.77). This turns optimizer failures into DESIGN CONVERSATIONS.
- Integration: geometry primitives (xform-constraints) supply values/derivatives; fs-fab supplies fabrication semantics; fs-opt-ir hosts the nodes; fs-session's errors-as-guidance surfaces the diagnoses.
- Constraint ledger table rows (kind, IR, status, repair suggestions) per Rev S.

## Acceptance criteria
Kind-specific treatment verified per optimizer family (chance constraints actually estimated with the declared estimator + validity machinery; certification constraints refuse to report satisfied without their proof artifact); unsat-core extraction correct on seeded infeasible fixtures (core is minimal — dropping any member restores feasibility); repair rankings' feasibility estimates calibrated on the fixture family (predicted vs actual).

## Testing
G0: core minimality property tests; elastic-relaxation solve correctness vs enumeration on small fixtures; serialization round-trips. Logs: full diagnosis payloads (core, repairs, estimates) — the agent-facing artifact this bead exists for.
close_reason: Shipped fs-constraint, the constraint CALCULUS (plan 9.1 / Rev F): constraints with semantics, not anonymous g(x)<=0. Seven-kind taxonomy (Hard/Soft{quadratic,hinge}/Chance{MC estimator}/Robust{uncertainty box}/Certification{interval,sos}/Fabrication/Code) each mapping to its optimizer Treatment (feasibility-restoration / penalty / estimate-then-bound / prove-or-escalate / domain-check). THE VALIDITY MACHINERY IS REAL: chance constraints compute a Hoeffding lower confidence bound and report satisfied ONLY when the bound clears the level — fscon-003 pins the case where the raw empirical rate clears but the bound does not: BoundNotCleared, never Satisfied. THE PROOFS ARE REAL: an in-house rigorous interval evaluator over fs-opt graphs (conservative inclusion per node, honest refusals on div-through-zero/domain/PDE nodes) powers Certification kinds (which refuse satisfied pointwise without an artifact regardless of how good g(x) looks) and Robust kinds (proven over uncertainty boxes with enclosure certificates); G0 containment verified over 300 random nonlinear boxes. INFEASIBILITY DIAGNOSIS: elastic-relaxation solves (multi-start deterministic subgradient) + DELETION FILTER yield MINIMAL unsat cores — fscon-005 verifies against enumeration that the triangle fixture's 3-member core is jointly infeasible, EVERY single deletion restores feasibility, the satisfiable bystander is excluded, and elastic verdicts match grid truth 12/12 on the seeded family. title: fs-fab: manufacturing/code-compliance constraints (AM/CNC/casting/steel/RC), assembly, cost+carbon models
description:
## What
`fs-fab` (patch Rev K): manufacturing, fabrication, and code compliance as its own layer — optimization without fabrication semantics produces FANTASY ARTIFACTS. Differentiable or certifiable wherever possible.

## Scope
- Additive manufacturing: overhang angle (differentiable via surface-normal fields), support-volume estimation, minimum feature size (medial oracle), powder-escape/drainability (topology constraints via topo-persistence), build-orientation co-optimization.
- Subtractive: CNC/milling ACCESSIBILITY (tool-reachability fields via geom-queries clearance/visibility analysis, minimum tool radius as curvature bounds), fixturing considerations (staged).
- Casting/molding: draft angle (xform-constraints primitive consumed here), parting-surface feasibility, no-enclosed-voids (persistence), uniform-wall-thickness preferences.
- Sheet metal + composite layup constraint families (staged, interfaces defined).
- Structural steel: CONNECTION FAMILIES (bolted/welded joint types with geometric envelopes), member standardization (catalog snapping via fs-constraint repair machinery), weld access, bolt spacing rules.
- Reinforced concrete: DETAILING rules (rebar spacing, cover, development lengths) as checkable constraints for the frame flagship.
- Assembly: sequence planning hooks (FrankenNetworkx precedence graphs), transport/lift/installation envelope constraints (member length/weight limits).
- COST AND CARBON MODELS: per-process parametric estimates with uncertainty envelopes (Evidence-typed — cost is a modeled quantity like any other), feeding objectives directly ("minimize embodied carbon s.t. code compliance" is a first-class study).
- Every constraint declares: differentiability class, certificate availability, fs-constraint kind (Fabrication{process} / Code{standard}).

## Acceptance criteria
Each constraint family verified on fixture geometries with known violations (detection + localization + repair suggestions); differentiable ones pass gradient gates; catalog/detailing rules validated against published examples (AISC-class member checks, ACI-class spacing fixtures); an end-to-end constrained study produces a design passing an independent rule-check pass.

## Testing
G0: constraint-evaluation determinism, unit coherence; adversarial fixtures per family. Logs: violation maps, repair suggestions, cost/carbon breakdowns with uncertainty.

## Addendum: tolerance stack-up (patch Rev K)
Assembly-level tolerance-chain analysis: worst-case and statistical (RSS) stack-up over mating features, tied to fs-uq geometric-tolerance KL machinery — fits and clearances verified across the tolerance band, not just at nominal. Differentiable where smooth (statistical form), certifiable via interval arithmetic (worst-case form).
close_reason: Implemented crate fs-fab (crate:fs-fab; L4, depends on fs-evidence). title: Make BIPOP best-run provenance and restart accounting replay-complete
description:
## Root cause

BipopReport currently exposes only the population-size schedule, total evaluation count, and a nested CmaReport for the best restart. It does not expose which restart produced that report, that restart population, derived seed, start point, allocated budget, evaluation-trace interval, large/small lane, or terminal reason. A replay can prove that best.evals equals 1 + generations times some population that appears somewhere in the schedule, but cannot prove which population or seed actually generated the best result. This makes exact restart provenance and best-run accounting unobservable and permits semantically different schedules to look equivalent at the public boundary.

## Required change

Extend production BIPOP evidence with a typed, versioned per-restart record and an unambiguous best_restart index. Each record must bind restart ordinal, large/small lane, lambda, allocated budget, actual evaluations, generation count, derived seed or logical stream coordinates, exact start-point bits, terminal reason, best objective/decision bits, sigma, convergence flag, and its half-open interval in the aggregate objective trace. Preserve deterministic earliest-wins tie semantics and make the selected best report a checked projection of the named restart record rather than duplicated mutable data.

Use checked arithmetic for population doubling, lambda times per-run generation budget, cumulative evaluation offsets, and seed/restart derivation. Refuse zero total budget, empty decisions, non-finite starts/sigma/target, impossible dimensions, and allocation/capability overrun before invoking the objective. Hard total budgets must not overshoot, including a final partial run.

## Acceptance and Gauntlet

G0: per-restart intervals are contiguous, non-overlapping, in bounds, and sum exactly to total_evals; every run obeys its local cap; CmaReport evaluation/generation accounting uses that exact run lambda; best_restart points to the first stable minimum under exact f64 total ordering; duplicated best projections match the named record bit-for-bit; overflow and zero-budget cases fail before callbacks.

G3: same objective under equivalent restart-record serialization, schedule replay, monotone objective transforms that preserve ordering, and deterministic seed-coordinate reconstruction gives covariant or bit-identical provenance as contracted. Swapping records, seeds, intervals, lane tags, or equal-best tie order must be rejected even after resealing.

G4: exact aggregate and per-run budgets at 0, 1, population boundary, and final partial run; injected callback faults/cancellation at each restart boundary leave a drain-complete prefix with no half-committed record. Cancellation latency and no-leak obligations must be explicit.

G5: freeze a canonical full-study identity binding the entire ordered restart ledger and objective trace. One-shot and pause/resume/fork execution must retain identical best_restart, records, and result digest on the same ISA. Seeded stale and correctly resealed mutations to every provenance class must produce typed PayloadIdentityMismatch versus ReferenceIdentityMismatch or semantic-admission errors.

## Theorem ratchet

Pursue a [F] executable schedule certificate showing the realized BIPOP large/small budget allocation satisfies the declared alternation and cumulative-budget invariant for every retained prefix. Keep open a [M] extension in which restart records form a sheaf over evaluation-trace intervals: local run certificates glue to one global budget/provenance certificate exactly when overlap and boundary identities agree. No theorem claim enters the default path without an executable witness and explicit assumptions.

## Completion

Production reports, contracts, generated catalogs, unit/property tests, retained replay, cancellation tests, and central DSR/RCH proof are green. The existing 7tv.21.22 replay may retain an explicit no-claim until this lands; do not represent its current existential schedule match as exact best-run provenance.

title: BIPOP callback fault/cancellation drain and authoritative prefix receipts
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The fallible BIPOP runner retains completed restart records and callback rows internally, but a generated-candidate error currently exits through ? and discards that prefix. Objective panics are outside the typed boundary, there is no Cx cancellation/drain protocol, and no authoritative artifact states exactly which callbacks/restarts completed before a fault. Callers can observe side effects yet receive only a terminal error, so accounting, retry, and provenance cannot distinguish callback-free refusal from drained partial execution.

MISSION
Turn request -> drain -> finalize into the production BIPOP fault/cancellation contract without weakening the hard-budget or complete-report semantics. A successful BipopReport remains complete. A post-start failure returns a sealed, versioned prefix receipt that is authoritative only for completed callbacks and atomically published restart records, carries an explicit incomplete/no-optimum status, and can be replayed or resumed only under matching root, objective, schedule, and state identities.

DELIVERABLES
- Add an asupersync/Cx-aware fallible entry point with bounded cancellation polls at restart, generation, candidate, retained-trace, identity, and publication boundaries. Keep compatibility wrappers explicit about their panic/no-cancellation behavior.
- Catch only declared typed objective failures through a fallible callback API; do not pretend arbitrary Rust panics are safely recoverable unless a separately isolated unwind boundary proves it. Classify preflight, objective, generated-point, cancellation, allocation, and internal-invariant failures distinctly.
- Define a sealed BipopPrefixReceipt binding root/admission/objective identity hook, schedule and identity schema versions, completed trace rows/points and strong trace root, completed restart records, active restart/generation/candidate cursor, work/budget counters, RNG checkpoints, drain status, terminal cause, and explicit best-so-far/no-global-optimum boundaries.
- Publish a restart record only after its trace interval/report/identity is complete. On fault, drain owned tasks, finalize the last fully written callback row if and only if its callback returned, discard half-built candidate/generation state, and publish exactly one prefix receipt. No partial full-study identity may escape.
- Make retry idempotent and resume-compatible: an idempotency key plus matching prefix/root/objective/state identities cannot duplicate callbacks or budget debits. Mismatches fail before new callbacks.
- Use checked/fallible storage admission for the prefix artifact and bounded diagnostic witnesses; retain both primary and drain/finalization failures without masking either.

GAUNTLET
G0 exact callback-free refusal versus first/last callback and every restart/generation/candidate boundary; typed callback errors before/after a returned value; prefix schema/identity/counter KATs; forged cursor, interval, budget, RNG, and terminal-cause refusal. G3 one-shot success equals cancellation-free Cx execution; injected faults at equivalent logical boundaries yield identical prefix bytes across tile/poll shapes; retry from the same idempotency key is observationally idempotent. G4 cancellation storms at every poll site prove bounded latency, complete draining, no task/arena/lease leak, no duplicate/lost callback, no half-record, exact hard-budget accounting, and combined primary+drain diagnostics. G5 same-ISA prefix bytes and final resumed report identity are stable across thread counts.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
Current errors do not authenticate already observed callback prefixes; no Cx cancellation/drain bound, typed objective-failure recovery, idempotent retry, or partial-progress authority exists. A prefix receipt is never a completed optimum or convergence certificate.

title: BIPOP admitted pause/resume/fork state with byte-identical completion
description:
ROOT CAUSE
BIPOP execution is currently one monolithic call. Its mean/covariance/eigen/path/sigma state, scheduler lane budgets, restart RNG and CMA RNG positions, generation/candidate cursor, retained trace, pending record transaction, and identity accumulators cannot be serialized. Cancellation therefore cannot become migration, long studies cannot checkpoint safely, and forked design alternatives cannot share an authenticated prefix while remaining deterministic.

MISSION
Define a fully admitted, versioned BIPOP execution state whose pause, durable checkpoint, resume, migration, and fork semantics are bit-identical to one-shot execution on the same declared deterministic envelope. State is data, not an opaque process snapshot; every mutable field has units, bounds, schema/version, provenance, and validation.

DELIVERABLES
- Refactor the runner into an explicit state machine with bounded step/tile operations. State covers root/admission/objective identity hook; large/small scheduler counters; restart ordinal/lambda/local cap; CMA mean, covariance, eigenvectors/values, evolution paths, sigma, weights, generation/candidate cursor and fitness buffers; best/tie state under total_cmp; exact RNG stream keys/checkpoints; trace/prefix receipts; work/memory counters; and pending publication transaction.
- Add checked, canonical, content-addressed checkpoint encoding with a separately admitted maximum byte count and fallible allocation. Refuse unknown versions, noncanonical floats/lengths where policy requires, stale dependency semantics, malformed SPD/layout state, counter reuse, impossible cursors, forged identities, and budget regressions before objective invocation.
- Pause is request -> drain -> finalize: finish only the declared atomic microstep, drain child work, seal one checkpoint, and expose no half-generation/restart record. Resume consumes matching authority exactly once and preserves callback ordering/budget. Migration records machine/ISA/determinism compatibility; unsupported moves refuse honestly.
- Fork creates immutable child states sharing only content-addressed prefix artifacts. Each child receives a disjoint logical identity/idempotency namespace and deterministic RNG continuation or explicitly declared counter split; parent bytes never mutate and no stream coordinate is reused.
- Integrate completed execution with the full-study and replay-backed semantic admission paths. One-shot, any legal pause partition, migrated same-envelope resume, and forks with identical continuation inputs must finish with the same report/study identity.

GAUNTLET
G0 round-trip every state variant and boundary, including pre-first-callback, mid-generation candidates, post-generation/pre-record, between restarts, terminal, and cancelled prefixes; every field mutation and version mismatch refuses before callbacks. G3 exhaustive reduced-fixture pause partitions, checkpoint encode/decode cycles, equivalent chunk sizes, and same-continuation forks produce bit-identical callbacks, records, counters, and study identity. G4 cancellation at each serialization/allocation/drain/publication point proves bounded latency, no lost/duplicated callback, zero leaked task/arena/lease/stream authority, byte-identical retry, and atomic checkpoint replacement. G5 same-ISA bytes are stable across thread counts; explicitly labeled migration matrices separate bit-stable, numerically equivalent, and unsupported envelopes.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
No current BIPOP state can be paused, migrated, resumed, or forked. Process memory is not a durable checkpoint, a retained callback prefix is not sufficient CMA state, and same seed alone does not prove continuation equivalence.

title: BIPOP executable universal schedule and budget certificate
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The current admission and validator encode careful closed-form restart/population/counter bounds, but the realized large/small schedule theorem lives as duplicated imperative arithmetic plus tests. A shared bug can preserve producer/validator agreement, and no compact artifact proves that every retained prefix respects alternation, ladder, local-envelope, hard-budget, seed, counter-uniqueness, and terminal rules. This blocks machine-checkable explanation and future theorem composition.

MISSION
Produce an executable [F] certificate for the realized BIPOP schedule and a separately checked universal bound over every admitted total budget/dimension/seed envelope. Preserve ambitious theorem discovery: formalize the exact recurrence far enough that stronger closed forms or inductive invariants can replace enumeration when proven, while retaining a finite executable checker as the default authority.

DELIVERABLES
- Define a versioned ScheduleCertificate containing admitted root/schedule versions, symbolic parameters, exact large/small recurrence state per restart, population/lambda/local cap, cumulative lane and total spends, remaining budget, seed derivation, restart/CMA counter intervals, terminal cause, and links to restart/trace/full-study identities.
- Implement a checker whose state and recurrence are independent of the production scheduler control flow. It verifies the base case, every transition, monotone/checked counters, disjoint stream-coordinate intervals, whole-generation callback rule, final partial run, ninth-large termination, and exact best/provenance record linkage.
- Add a universal-bound witness for the admission formulas: either a machine-checked induction over recurrence regions or a finite reduction theorem with explicit lemmas/assumptions proving max restart ordinal, large population, local budget, storage, seed, and Philox counter caps for every admitted budget. Keep proof terms/data reviewable and content-addressed.
- Bind theorem/checker/schema/assumption versions and all no-claim boundaries into the certificate. A passing runtime trace without a valid certificate remains ordinary evidence, not theorem authority.
- Expose deterministic explain output identifying which invariant/transition failed and the smallest counterexample prefix. Diagnostics are bounded and do not echo unbounded payloads.

GAUNTLET
G0 prime boundary-style KATs over budgets 1, base-lambda-1/base-lambda/base-lambda+1, every complete-generation edge, every large-ladder transition, ninth-large termination, seed/counter maxima, usize/u64/u128 overflow fronts, and exact smallest counterexamples. Mutation tests perturb every recurrence field and certificate link. G3 production schedules across exhaustive reduced envelopes and stratified extreme envelopes must verify under the independent checker; equivalent serialization/chunking and replay give identical certificate bytes. G5 freeze certificate/checker identity and deterministic counterexample diagnostics. Certify the certifier with an algebraically distinct oracle or formal model and adversarial shared-bug mutations.

THEOREM RATCHET
Pursue stronger results rather than freezing the present formulas: derive tight piecewise closed forms for launch count and cumulative lane spend; prove counter-domain injectivity and absence of seed aliasing; characterize exactly when small/large alternation changes; and seek amortized or tropical interpretations that compose with planner budgets. New theorems may strengthen the default only when assumptions and executable witnesses are explicit.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
Current admission bounds are engineered and tested but not carried as an independently checkable universal schedule certificate. Producer/validator agreement is not a proof of the recurrence, and bounded sample testing is not a universal theorem.

title: BIPOP interval-sheaf gluing theorem and compositional provenance certificate
description:
ROOT CAUSE
Restart records, callback-trace intervals, cancellation prefixes, checkpoints, and schedule proofs are currently validated by one global pass. That does not provide a compositional theorem explaining when independently produced local evidence patches can be joined without gaps, overlaps, duplicated budget, stream-coordinate reuse, conflicting boundary state, or forged global best/provenance. Distributed execution, partial recomputation, and agent-native evidence merge need a principled local-to-global authority rather than ad hoc concatenation.

MISSION
Build the [M] interval-sheaf theorem ratchet promised by the parent: model BIPOP evidence as typed sections over callback-index intervals and prove/executably witness that compatible local sections glue to one unique global schedule/provenance section. Keep the ambition maximal—seek new discrete sheaf/cohomology results that expose obstructions and minimal repair sets—while feature-gating every unproven claim and retaining exhaustive default validation.

DELIVERABLES
- Define the base interval/cover category and a typed presheaf of BIPOP sections. A section carries interval endpoints, root/objective/admission identities, restart/generation/candidate boundary state, schedule-certificate fragment, callback trace/root, RNG coordinate ranges, work/budget debit, best/tie summary, checkpoint/prefix identity, and terminal/no-claim status.
- Define restriction maps that are deterministic, identity-preserving, budget-conservative, and compatible with pause/resume boundaries. State which interior cuts require extra boundary witnesses because CMA state is not reconstructible from trace endpoints alone.
- Implement pairwise and higher-overlap compatibility checks. Detect gaps, double-covered callbacks, conflicting objective/point bits, mismatched CMA/checkpoint state, inconsistent lane budgets, reused RNG coordinates, incompatible identities/versions, and best-summary conflicts with bounded minimal obstruction witnesses.
- Implement canonical gluing that publishes exactly one global full-study/schedule identity only after all local compatibility and cover conditions pass. Prove uniqueness relative to declared restriction/normalization rules, or emit an explicit non-uniqueness obstruction/no-claim.
- Compute a practical obstruction complex/cochain: encode overlap disagreements, identify whether they are exact/correctable, and return ranked minimal repair candidates. Explore a theorem connecting vanishing obstruction classes to replay-safe merge, and a stronger result relating schedule recurrence certificates to global budget conservation.
- Provide an independent checker and versioned certificate binding cover, local section identities, restriction maps, obstruction result, assumptions, theorem/checker versions, and global identity. Default paths retain exhaustive replay validation until the theorem checker is Gauntlet-proven.

GAUNTLET
G0 empty/single/adjacent/overlapping/nested covers; every boundary type; exact gap/overlap/RNG/budget/state/best obstruction; nonunique-gluing cases; version and identity mutation. G3 arbitrary legal cover refinement/coarsening, restriction composition, cover permutation, equivalent pause partitions, and local reserialization preserve the same global identity/certificate. G4 cancellation/failure during local checking, obstruction construction, and publication drains with no partial global authority or leaked lease. G5 certificate/obstruction bytes and canonical repair ranking are stable on the declared deterministic envelope. Certify the certifier with exhaustive small-cover enumeration, an algebraically distinct checker, and mutation-seeded false-certificate attacks.

THEOREM RATCHETS
- [F] Prove pairwise compatibility suffices for the declared interval cover class under explicit boundary-state completeness assumptions.
- [M] Characterize replay-safe gluing by vanishing of a computable first obstruction/cohomology class.
- [M] Derive minimal repair sets from obstruction support and prove their soundness/minimality for useful cover families.
- [M] Generalize from linear callback intervals to a branching restart/fork site and relate local identities to a causal/event sheaf.
These are targets for discovery, not reasons to weaken the system. Any newly proven theorem may be promoted with explicit assumptions and executable independent evidence.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
Concatenated records are not sheaf gluing; pairwise matching is not automatically a global theorem; a zero-looking heuristic obstruction is not a cohomology certificate; and no distributed/local evidence merge may mint a full-study identity before the cover, restrictions, compatibility, uniqueness, and checker assumptions are proven.

title: Ratchet NSGA-III/WFG quality from calibrated conformance to certified anytime optimizer profiles
description:
## Background and non-regression intent

The first retained WFG4 M=3, k=4, l=20 run at 36,892 objective evaluations measured mean reduced distance 0.23171459361058497. Child 7tv.21.11 deliberately calibrated a coarse fixed-fixture conformance ceiling of 0.25 while preserving orthogonal evaluator, mutant, accounting, coverage, hypervolume, shape, and replay gates. That is an honest diagnostic boundary, but it is not an optimizer-quality target and must not become one by inertia.

This issue preserves the current conformance battery as a regression tripwire while creating a much more ambitious quality program. Do not make the existing test easier, delete difficult fixtures, cherry-pick favorable seeds, increase budgets without matched comparisons, or relabel a calibrated pass as state of the art.

## Mission

Make fs-dfo multiobjective search materially world class on multimodal, deceptive, disconnected, degenerate, biased, and many-objective landscapes. At the same evaluation budget, drive WFG4 mean reduced distance toward 0.05 or better while improving direction coverage and hypervolume, then demonstrate robust gains across the complete WFG family and adversarial in-repository fixtures. Every adaptive decision must remain deterministic in deterministic mode, budget exact, cancellation correct, replayable, and attached to an honest certificate or no-claim boundary.

## Solid and frontier engineering

1. Build a canonical WFG1 through WFG9 evaluator and study matrix spanning objective counts, position/distance dimensions, bias/degeneracy settings, disconnected fronts, and scaling. Cross-check formulas against isolated development-only primary reference implementations; production remains pure Rust and Franken-only.
2. Diagnose production NSGA-III from first principles: ideal/nadir normalization, extreme-point and intercept degeneracy, association ties, reference-direction occupancy, environmental selection, SBX/polynomial mutation, boundary handling, population/reference cardinality mismatch, duplicate collapse, and deterministic tie rules. Add minimal counterexamples for every discovered defect.
3. Add deterministic adaptive reference geometry: occupancy-aware insertion/removal, curvature-sensitive directions, disconnected-component sentinels, canonical direction identities, and fail-closed fallback when normalization is singular. Preserve fixed-reference NSGA-III as a named baseline.
4. Add portfolio and restart policies that can combine NSGA-III, MOEA/D, archive-based exploration, local Pareto refinement, and quality-diversity proposals under one exact shared evaluation budget. Selection and racing decisions must use anytime-valid e-process evidence when optional stopping is present.
5. Make all population work tile-scheduled under fs-exec scopes with bounded cancellation, drained losers, logical-stream RNG, fixed reduction trees, checkpoint/resume/fork, and complete per-generation provenance.
6. Retain per-seed and aggregate metrics: normalized distance distributions, direction occupancy/discrepancy, exact or certified hypervolume where available, epsilon indicators, front cardinality, duplicate rate, evaluation accounting, wall/CPU/memory fingerprints, and every adaptive policy decision.

## Mathematical and theorem ratchets

Pursue executable theorems rather than treating current heuristics as permanent limits.

- Develop discrepancy and covering-radius certificates for reference sets on simplex and curved Pareto-front charts, including deterministic refinement bounds.
- Model local objective/constraint/occupancy evidence as a sheaf over decision and objective-space covers. Glue local front-chart, dominance, curvature, and reachability witnesses only when overlap maps agree; expose obstruction classes when apparently good local fronts cannot form a globally representative archive.
- Investigate whether persistent/cohomological signatures of sampled sublevel and dominance complexes can certify missing disconnected components, multimodal basins, holes in front coverage, or reference-direction misallocation. Use discoveries to allocate search effort, but keep unproved policies behind frontier or moonshot gates.
- Seek anytime-valid quality-improvement theorems for portfolio allocation under adaptive stopping, with explicit assumptions, counterexample boundaries, checker identity, and the exact capability unlocked.
- Explore certified continuation between neighboring reference rays and homotopy-aware restart placement so WFG-style deceptive transformations become useful theorem probes rather than merely benchmarks.

These are ambitious research targets, not pre-emptive no-claim downgrades. A proof artifact may unlock stronger defaults only after its assumptions and independent checker pass the Gauntlet.

## Verification program

G0: evaluator identities, transformation boundary laws, dominance/niching/tie laws, exact budget accounting, malformed input rejection, normalization degeneracy, and reference-set discrepancy checks.

G1/G2: canonical WFG1-9, DTLZ, ZDT, disconnected and degenerate fronts; matched-budget comparison against the current frozen baseline and isolated development-only references. The WFG4 same-budget stretch target is mean reduced distance at most 0.05 with substantially stronger direction coverage and no regression in hypervolume, worst distance, replay, or mutant sensitivity.

G3: objective scaling/translation, decision permutations, equivalent reference-set symmetries, seed-panel permutation, population/reference refinements, split-run resume, and unit-rescaling metamorphisms. Seeded red mutations must alter identities and fail semantic admission.

G4: cancellation at initialization, variation, evaluation, association, selection, adaptation, and checkpoint boundaries; TERM-like callback faults; exact budgets at zero/one/generation edges; no task, arena, or losing-race leaks.

G5: bit-stable fixed-ISA results across thread counts, frozen per-fixture and aggregate identities, one-shot versus checkpoint/resume/fork equivalence, and canonical policy-decision ledgers.

## Acceptance

Keep 7tv.21.11 as the coarse fixed-fixture gate. Land a separate versioned quality profile with statistically and semantically justified thresholds, exact matched budgets, a non-cherry-picked registered seed panel, independent metric recomputation, detailed JSONL receipts and per-run logs, and explicit solid/frontier/moonshot capability status. Demonstrate a large same-budget improvement on WFG4 plus broad non-regression or documented counterexample-driven specialization across WFG1-9. Central Cargo/Clippy and configured DSR lanes must be green before closure.

title: Remove population-index bias from NSGA-III rank-tied mating selection
description:
## Defect
NSGA-III binary mating tournaments resolve equal-rank candidates by the lowest live population index. On many-objective generations where most or all candidates are nondominated, this makes ancestry/order a hidden selection objective: earlier retained parents beat later peers despite equal semantic fitness. The bias is deterministic but not exchangeable, and can suppress exploration on multimodal WFG landscapes.

## Scope
Replace the rank-tie rule with an index-neutral, seed-deterministic rule without extra RNG draws; add a focused executable tournament law that detects the low-index mutant; bind the mating policy into versioned optimizer provenance/goldens; remeasure the fixed WFG4 campaign at its exact existing budget. Do not loosen any conformance gate, increase the evaluation budget, or claim the parent 0.05 stretch target unless measured.

## Acceptance
A permutation/exchangeability fixture catches the former lower-index preference; equal seed and ordering replay bitwise; existing NSGA-III, WFG-family, study-replay, and WFG4 selectors pass strict remote proof; the WFG4 receipt reports the new same-budget metrics and the CONTRACT states the exact measured gain or regression/no-claim. If the rule does not materially improve the registered WFG4 campaign, retain the diagnostic evidence but do not promote it as a quality win.

title: Make trust-region Newton-Krylov typed, budget-exact, resumable, and proof-carrying
description:
## Background and root cause

The production fs-ascent trust-region Newton path demonstrates real Steihaug-CG and negative-curvature boundary steps, but its public surface is not yet safe enough to serve as a proof-bearing optimizer. It accepts raw slices and callbacks, uses assertions and unchecked callback shapes, computes norms/dots naively, has no explicit evaluation/Hessian-vector/time/memory budgets, no asupersync cancellation scope, no checkpoint/resume state, and reports only aggregate counters. The full-study replay in 7tv.21.25 can reconstruct one fixed trace externally, but a receipt cannot repair missing production semantics.

A second architectural constraint is already recorded in frankensim-ext-solver-nonlinear-block-qii8: generic Newton-Krylov globalization belongs in lower-layer fs-solver so mechanics, EM, thermal, gas, and ASCENT share one spine. Do not create a second permanent trust-region authority in fs-ascent or invert the layer DAG. Preserve the current implementation as a behavioral baseline while moving or factoring generic machinery downward and keeping optimization-specific policy above it.

## Mission

Deliver a typed, fail-closed, budget-exact, cancellation-correct, resumable Newton-Krylov trust-region service with explicit Steihaug and final-model Hessian-vector roles, independently checkable iteration receipts, and ambitious theorem hooks. fs-ascent should consume the lower-layer authority and add optimization policy without duplicating its numerical core.

## Required production design

1. Introduce validated problem/config/state/result types. Validate positive dimension; finite starting point, radii, tolerances, thresholds, and objectives; exact gradient/Hv dimensions; finite callback outputs; iteration arithmetic; and compatible resume identities before any avoidable callback.
2. Make budgets first-class and separate: objective/gradient evaluations, Steihaug Hv products, final-model Hv products, iterations, wall time, memory, and capability. A zero-evaluation admission invokes no user callback. No iteration may start unless its mandatory callback envelope is admitted, or the API must explicitly support a partially resumable iteration with sealed state.
3. Run under an explicit asupersync Cx. Poll at bounded outer-iteration and Krylov boundaries. Cancellation is request, drain, finalize; it commits no partial radius update, accepted decision, curvature counter, or receipt. Callback panic/fault becomes typed retained evidence.
4. Replace naive sum-of-squares and dot paths with deterministic scale-safe reductions and explicit non-finite/overflow diagnostics. Boundary-tau calculation must handle zero directions, nearly tangent discriminants, subnormal/huge values, and rounding without NaN fabrication.
5. Represent Hessian-vector purpose as a typed role: Steihaug search direction versus final model-decrease step. Per-iteration evidence records global logical ordinal, role-local ordinal, current point identity, direction/product identities, dTHd sign, boundary reason, step, model decrease, actual decrease, rho, radius before/after, accept/reject decision, and cumulative budgets.
6. Make acceptance and radius laws named/versioned policy data rather than hidden constants. Reconstruct the current state after each iteration from the prior state plus the recorded transition. Exact deterministic tie behavior is mandatory at rho and boundary thresholds.
7. Seal resumable state: current x/f/g, radius, iteration and every budget counter, active Steihaug vectors/scalars when mid-iteration resume is supported, deterministic reduction state, stop reason, and canonical provenance digest. One-shot, pause/resume, migrate, and fork must preserve the declared trajectory.
8. Expand the report with typed stop attribution, accepted/rejected iteration counts, role-separated Hv counts, curvature/boundary counts, worst residuals, budget/cancellation status, and a content-addressed iteration ledger. Aggregate counters must be derivable from detailed records.
9. Supply adjoint and optimization hooks without coupling fs-solver upward. Approximate-Hv modes must name their truncation/error model and may not inherit exact-Hessian theorem status.

## Mathematical and theorem ratchets

Solid claims should prove Steihaug feasibility, boundary intersection, model/accounting identities, descent or explicitly classified non-descent, and classical local convergence under named assumptions.

Frontier and moonshot work remains first class:
- executable local convergence-order certificates with Lipschitz/Hessian assumptions and interval or Taylor-model neighborhoods;
- trust-region global convergence artifacts for supported function classes, including exact boundaries where assumptions fail;
- Krylov/Lanczos spectral witnesses for negative curvature and certified lower eigenvalue bounds rather than sign-only events;
- sheaf-compatible local model certificates over overlapping decision-space neighborhoods, gluing radius, curvature, and error witnesses only when transition maps and overlap residuals agree;
- obstruction classes that expose when individually credible local quadratic models cannot define a globally coherent optimization model;
- topology/event-aware generalized trust regions whose restart and derivative semantics remain explicit.

Do not weaken these targets because proofs are not yet available. Keep unproved capabilities gated and attach assumptions, checker identity, counterexamples, and the exact default they would unlock.

## Gauntlet

G0:
- invalid dimensions/config/callback shapes and all NaN/infinite cases fail before false certificates;
- exact budget edges 0, 1, mandatory-iteration envelope, Steihaug boundary, and final-model boundary;
- boundary_tau residual, Steihaug recurrence, radius/acceptance laws, role accounting, and deterministic ties;
- scale-safe norms/dots across subnormal and near-maximum representable values.

G1:
- manufactured convex quadratic, indefinite quadratic, Rosenbrock, saddle, and nearly singular problems with expected local orders and independently reconstructed model/actual reductions.

G3:
- translation/scaling and orthogonal-coordinate covariance where mathematically applicable;
- equivalent Hv implementations, split-run resume, checkpoint migration, and callback-order metamorphisms;
- seeded mutations of role, ordinal, radius, rho, acceptance, curvature sign, budget, result, and state digest fail semantic admission even when resealed.

G4:
- cancellation and injected faults at every outer/Krylov/final-model/fg boundary;
- no task or arena leak, bounded cancellation latency, no partial accepted state;
- panic containment and budget exhaustion retain a final sealed record.

G5:
- bit-stable fixed-ISA results across thread counts;
- one-shot versus pause/resume/fork identity equality;
- frozen full-state and result receipts with independent objective, gradient, Hv, transition, curvature, and KKT/residual oracles.

## Completion

Generic trust-region Newton-Krylov execution has one lower-layer authority shared with the nonlinear-solver initiative; fs-ascent no longer carries an incompatible duplicate. Contracts, generated catalogs, tests, role-aware receipts, and no-claim boundaries agree. Relevant central Cargo/Clippy and configured DSR gates are green, exact proof artifacts are retained, and 7tv.21.25 remains a regression baseline rather than the sole source of semantic truth.

title: Gradient stack: L-BFGS/Adam, TR-Newton-Krylov w/ 2nd-order adjoints, AL/IP/SQP, Riemannian manifold variants, KKT certificates
description:
## What
The gradient-based optimizer stack (plan §9.2): FLUX adjoint → Sobolev/Riesz smoothing → optional Riemannian projection → optimizer — first-order, second-order, and constrained methods, manifold-correct.

## Scope
- The gradient pipeline made explicit: raw adjoint gradient (fs-adjoint) → Sobolev smoothing (the Riesz step — §8.7's noise-killer) → Riemannian projection onto constraint-manifold tangent spaces where applicable → optimizer step. Each stage evidenced (gradient provenance in the ledger).
- First-order: L-BFGS (THE default; m≈17-class memory, strong-Wolfe line search, deterministic); Adam-family for stochastic gradients (surrogate-training-adjacent uses).
- Second-order: matrix-free TRUST-REGION NEWTON–KRYLOV with Hessian-vector products from SECOND-ORDER ADJOINTS (Steihaug-CG inner solves, negative-curvature handling) — the frame-sizing workhorse (§15.2 step 2 names tr-newton-krylov).
- Constrained: AUGMENTED LAGRANGIAN (robust default), interior-point option, SQP for tightly-constrained small-dimension polish; constraint-kind dispatch via fs-constraint.
- Manifold variants: retraction + vector transport for Stiefel/sphere/SO(3)/fixed-volume level sets (fs-ga for rotation manifolds); Riemannian L-BFGS/TR.
- All optimizers: resumable state machines (P7 — an optimization study is pausable/forkable), budget-aware stopping (`:until (any (grad-norm 1e-5) (e-value 20) (budget-exhausted))` — Appendix C's stopping-condition algebra), KKT-residual certificates attached to every returned optimum (converged vs stalled distinguishable — §9.8).

## Acceptance criteria
CUTEst-class/Rosenbrock-family batteries: convergence within evaluation envelopes; FrankenScipy cross-validation on shared problems (§12 oracle contract); manifold correctness (orthogonality/volume preserved to roundoff along iterations); AL/IP/SQP on constrained fixtures with KKT residuals verified; second-order adjoint Hv passes Dual-of-Dual checks; deterministic trajectories from seeds (G5).

## Testing
G0: line-search/trust-region invariants (sufficient decrease, radius update laws); pipeline-stage ablation harness (smoothing on/off demonstrable on a mesh-noise fixture); resume-equality tests. Logs: iteration traces (f, ‖g‖, step, KKT), stage-wise gradient norms, stopping-condition attributions.

title: fs-race: replace selective max e-values with anytime-valid elimination
description:
race_field constructs each candidate evidence as the maximum log e-value among currently surviving opponents, then feeds those selected maxima to e-BH. The opponent set changes after data-dependent eliminations. A maximum over optional e-processes is not itself an e-process without a valid multiplicity construction, and survivor-dependent selection can inflate false elimination despite the current seeded calibration tests.

Root cause: selection and multiplicity are applied after observing the same evidence, outside the validity contract of the pairwise e-processes.

Repair: specify and prove an anytime-valid candidate null using a fixed predeclared opponent family, valid mixture/union construction, or closed testing; freeze the hypothesis family independently of eliminations; document dependence assumptions required by e-BH. Reject non-finite losses structurally rather than panicking at winner selection.

Acceptance: mathematical derivation in contract; adversarial null simulations with optional stopping and adaptive elimination stay within alpha with confidence bounds; permutation/replay invariance; a deliberately invalid max implementation is caught by the certifier battery; domination retains measured savings.

title: fs-race: bind e-process validity to a checked declared loss span
description:
PairwiseRace documents pre-normalized paired losses but silently clips loss_b-loss_a to [-1,1]. That changes the estimand: the e-process tests the mean clipped difference, not the declared raw mean ordering. Equal raw means can therefore acquire positive betting drift. Exact counterexample: opponent loss is always 3; candidate loss is 4 with probability 0.75 and 0 with probability 0.25. Both raw means equal 3, but candidate-minus-opponent is +1 or -3, whose clipped mean is +0.5; the current adapter eventually manufactures evidence that the equal-best candidate is worse. Current race settings carry no range/span and several tests feed differences outside the documented bound.

Repair: make normalization part of the typed or checked API. Require a finite positive declared maximum paired-loss difference (or finite loss range), map linearly without clipping, and fail closed with a structured invalid-scale/no-claim outcome whenever a non-finite or out-of-range value appears. Bind the scale into replay/provenance. Update every consumer to declare a defensible bound; do not infer one from observed data.

Acceptance: the skew equal-mean counterexample never yields valid elimination evidence and triggers the scale guard when unnormalized; boundary +/-span maps exactly to 0/1; values one ULP outside refuse; rescaling losses and span together is metamorphically invariant; global-null, adaptive-stopping, domination, savings, replay, and kill-wiring batteries remain green; all production callers surface invalid scale rather than panic or silently clamp.

title: fs-surrogate: FNO/DeepONet + POD-DEIM/balanced-truncation/Koopman, ledger-trained, conformal e-prediction, certify-or-escalate
description:
## What
`fs-surrogate` (plan §9.7, Bet 9 [F]): learned accelerators with GUARANTEES — neural operators and classical ROMs as 100–10,000× cheap physics, permitted ONLY inside conformal-e-certified validity bands. ML proposes; certified numerics disposes.

## Scope
- Neural operators (FrankenTorch): FOURIER NEURAL OPERATORS on box-resampled fields (fs-fft provides the spectral machinery); DeepONets for parametric families (branch/trunk over design parameters × query points).
- Classical ROMs: POD-Galerkin with DEIM (nonlinear term interpolation; POD via fs-la-randomized/TSQR over snapshot matrices); BALANCED TRUNCATION for LTI subsystems; KOOPMAN/DMD for unsteady flows — the ornithoid's reduced flight-dynamics models around trim states (§15.1 step 4) come from here.
- CONTINUOUS TRAINING FROM THE LEDGER: the accumulating (design → field/objective) corpus IS the training set; retraining triggers, versioned surrogate artifacts (content-addressed, model-carded), train/validation splits respecting design-family structure.
- CONFORMAL e-PREDICTION wrapping (the Bet 5 fusion): distribution-free prediction bands with anytime validity under the e-value formulation, RECALIBRATED ONLINE as new ground-truth solves arrive.
- CERTIFY-OR-ESCALATE (the mechanical policy): inside the certified band AND band-width below decision-relevance → use the surrogate; outside or too wide → escalate fidelity, and the new solve BOTH decides the point AND tightens the band. The system gets faster every week it runs without ever silently trusting a hallucinated flow field.
- Model cards mandatory (validity domain, training distribution, known failure modes); conformal-hardening bead adds the drift/conditioning machinery.

## Acceptance criteria
FNO/DeepONet: standard operator-learning benchmarks (Darcy/Burgers-class from our own solvers' data) at published-class accuracy; POD-DEIM: reduced-vs-full trajectories within declared bounds on fixtures; Koopman: trim-state flight-dynamics fixture reproduces linearization behavior; conformal bands: EMPIRICAL COVERAGE at nominal levels on held-out + shifted data (certify-certifiers integration); certify-or-escalate: end-to-end optimization fixture where the policy demonstrably reduces cost vs all-high-fidelity at equal final answer quality (ledgered).

## Testing
G0: band monotonicity under recalibration; escalation-trigger correctness on seeded OOD queries; training reproducibility class documented. Logs: coverage tracking over time, escalation events with reasons, cost-savings accounting.
