title: Conformal hardening: Mondrian buckets (by regime/fidelity/family), drift e-tests, false-coverage budgets, shift-adversarial validation
description:
## What
Conformal/e-process HARDENING (patch Rev M): the anytime-valid layer's assumptions made into explicit operational contracts — conditional calibration, drift detection, and false-coverage budgeting. The system must not advertise distribution-free protection while quietly violating exchangeability by changing design regimes.

## Scope
- MONDRIAN (conditional) calibration: conformal buckets by regime class (fs-regime's groups — the cross-layer payoff), fidelity level, geometry family, objective type, scenario cluster, solver settings — coverage guarantees PER BUCKET, not just marginal (marginal coverage can hide systematic per-regime failure).
- DRIFT DETECTION: ledger training distribution vs current candidate distribution → two-sample e-tests (sequential, anytime-valid — eating our own dogfood); on drift: automatic recalibration or escalation, surrogate validity domains SHRINK in response (Evidence validity_domain updates flow through).
- FALSE-COVERAGE-RATE BUDGETING: when thousands of candidates × objectives × constraints × time points are monitored simultaneously, coverage errors get an explicit ledger budget (analogous to the Error Ledger — e-BH machinery from fs-eproc applied to coverage claims); the budget is part of study admission (P4 extended to statistical error).
- Exchangeability accounting: which conformal claims assume what, declared on model cards; optimization-induced distribution shift (the optimizer MOVES toward regions the surrogate hasn't seen — the fundamental tension) handled by weighting/refresh policies with documented validity.

## Acceptance criteria
Per-bucket coverage verified empirically across regime shifts (certify-certifiers' shift scenarios pass); drift e-tests detect seeded covariate shift within documented sample budgets, and the escalation path fires; FCR budget accounting correct under simultaneous monitoring at flagship scale (simulation battery); optimizer-shift stress test: a deliberately surrogate-exploiting optimizer does NOT achieve silent invalid coverage (the adversarial test that matters most).

## Testing
Simulation batteries per mechanism with structured logs (bucket coverage tables, drift-detection latencies, budget ledgers); integration with fs-surrogate's online recalibration. Logs double as the calibration audit trail regulators-of-the-future would want.

title: L1 BEDROCK: numerical foundations
description:
## Mission
L1 BEDROCK: the in-house numerical foundations — dense LA (GEMM, batched small dense, factorizations, eigensolvers, randomized NLA), sparse formats/preconditioners, FFT, certified arithmetic (intervals/affine/Taylor models/exact predicates), function objects (chebfun-style), automatic differentiation, and RNG/QMC.

## Why in-house (plan §6)
Everything here is written in pure safe Rust with audited SIMD leaves because the entire point is kernels shaped for OUR data layouts (Morton tiles, SoA, arena packing) and OUR two machine families, not a 1979 Fortran calling convention. No BLAS/LAPACK/FFI (P1). FrankenScipy serves as the conformance oracle: where semantics overlap, our kernels must MATCH FrankenScipy in the Gauntlet and BEAT it on the roofline.

## Signature positions
- Batched small dense (6×6…48×48 FEM element matrices) is a first-class citizen with SIMD lanes across the batch — routinely 5–15× over loop-over-LAPACK.
- Mixed precision with iterative refinement is a default policy (factor f32, refine f64, escalate to double-double only where the Error Ledger demands).
- Matrix-free-native eigensolvers (LOBPCG/Lanczos) because modal/buckling/stability problems reduce to operator applications (P6).
- fs-ivl is what the word "Certified" means everywhere else in the system: outward-rounded intervals via next_up/next_down (thread-safe, no rounding-mode fiddling), Taylor models, Shewchuk exact predicates.

## Members
fs-rand-philox, fs-rand-qmc, fs-la-gemm, fs-la-batched, fs-la-factorizations, fs-la-eigen, fs-la-randomized, fs-la-mixed-precision, fs-sparse-core, fs-sparse-precond, fs-fft, fs-ivl-core, fs-ivl-taylor, fs-ivl-predicates, fs-cheb, fs-ad-forward, fs-ad-adjoint-infra, bedrock-conformance.

## Success Criteria
GEMM/SpMV/FFT within target roofline bands on both ISAs (see roofline-harness); G0 law suites green; FrankenScipy cross-checks green; deterministic mode bit-stable through all reductions.

title: fs-rand: counter-based Philox streams keyed by logical identity + deterministic distributions
description:
## What
`fs-rand` core: the in-house counter-based Philox-class generator + distributions (plan §6.7) — the foundation of P2's reproducible parallel randomness.

## Scope
- Philox-class counter-based RNG (in-house, P1): stateless function of (key, counter); streams keyed by LOGICAL work identity (seed, kernel_id, tile_id, iteration) so results are independent of which worker ran which tile. SIMD-friendly bulk generation (4×/8× lanes via fs-simd).
- Stream discipline: hierarchical key derivation (study → kernel → tile → draw) with collision-free composition; splittable substreams for nested parallelism; explicit stream provenance (keys are ledgerable values — Five Explicits' "seeds" pillar).
- Distributions: uniform (open/closed variants with correct rounding), standard normal (ziggurat with deterministic table + exact tail handling), exponential, gamma, beta, Dirichlet, categorical/alias method, von Mises–Fisher (for direction sampling in rendering/GA), truncated variants. All deterministic given (key, counter) — no rejection-loop thread-order sensitivity (rejection counts are part of the counter advance contract).
- Statistical quality gates: PractRand/TestU01-class battery reimplemented as needed in-house or via documented dev-only oracle (isolated per dependency policy), run nightly.

## Why
Counter-based RNG is what makes e-raced tournaments bit-reproducible, renders replayable, and MC/UQ results independent of scheduling — the load-bearing seed story of the whole system.

## Acceptance criteria
Known-answer tests vs published Philox vectors; stream independence (statistical + collision analysis); worker-shuffle invariance test (same logical work, different thread counts → identical draws); distribution correctness (KS/chi-square vs closed forms; moments to tolerance).

## Testing
Property: key-derivation injectivity on sampled subspaces; counter-advance contracts under rejection sampling. G5: cross-thread-count hash equality. Logs: battery results, per-distribution statistics tables, seeds everywhere.

title: fs-sparse preconditioners: Chebyshev smoothers, level-scheduled ILU/IC(0), SA-AMG coarse, capped supernodal
description:

title: fs-fft: Stockham mixed-radix, r2c/DCT paths, cache-blocked 3D pencils on tile executor
description:
## What
`fs-fft`: the in-house FFT (plan §6.3) — iterative Stockham autosort, mixed radix 4/8, real-input split paths, cache-blocked transposes, 3D via pencil decomposition on the tile executor.

- Real-input/real-output split-complex paths (r2c/c2r) — half the bandwidth for real fields (the common case: pressure/density/temperature).
- DCT-I/II/III via FFT folding — REQUIRED BY fs-cheb (Chebyshev transforms are DCTs; the function layer's performance rides on this).
- Multi-dimensional: cache-blocked transposes (tile-sized, 128 B-aligned), 3D pencil decomposition across fs-exec tiles with CCD-aware pencil ownership.
- SIMD via fs-simd/fs-tilelang for butterflies; deterministic mode = fixed butterfly/accumulation order (FFT is naturally fixed-shape; document the guarantee).
- Consumers (API shaped for them): spectral Poisson on boxes, Fourier neural operators (fs-surrogate), optimal-transport convolutions (multiobjective-robust Sinkhorn), rendering image ops, Chebyshev transforms.
- Roofline: ≥40% of memory-bound limit for in-cache 3D pencils (§14.1), ledgered.

Round-trip (forward∘inverse = identity·N) to tight ULP bounds across size sweep (powers of 2, mixed 4/8 sizes, prime-tail rejection with structured error listing supported sizes); Parseval verification; r2c/c2r consistency with complex reference; FrankenScipy cross-checks; perf targets on both ISAs.

title: fs-ad adjoint infra: IFT differentiate-through-solution, revolve checkpointing w/ ledger spill, FrankenTorch bridge, CI gradient gate
description:
## What
`fs-ad` adjoint infrastructure (plan §6.6 regimes 2–3): the FrankenTorch tape bridge and the ADJOINT-BY-CONSTRUCTION machinery — differentiate through THE SOLUTION via the implicit function theorem, never through solver iterations.

## Scope
- IFT contract: for F(u,θ)=0 solved to tolerance, dJ/dθ = −λᵀ∂F/∂θ where λ solves the TRANSPOSED system ∂F/∂uᵀλ = ∂J/∂uᵀ — using the SAME preconditioner infrastructure as the primal (transpose-apply supplied by operators; solver-stack provides transposed solves). Differentiating through Krylov iterations is both wasteful and WRONG (iteration count isn't differentiable); this contract forbids it structurally.
- Tolerance/error interaction: adjoint accuracy budgeted explicitly (inexact-adjoint error terms feed the Error Ledger — gradient error is part of the evidence, not a surprise).
- Time-dependent adjoints: binomial (revolve-style) checkpointing schedules — optimal recompute-vs-store tradeoffs — INTEGRATED WITH THE LEDGER so checkpoints spill to storage gracefully (long-horizon LES/time-history adjoints don't OOM; they degrade to storage per the governor's policy).

- Verification harness (THE MERGE GATE, §8.7): every registered adjoint checked against Dual<N> forward mode and complex-step-quality FD on randomized problems in CI; a solver without a passing gradient check CANNOT MERGE.

## Acceptance criteria
IFT gradients match forward-mode to tolerance on PV-skeleton + fixture PDEs; revolve schedules verified optimal (checkpoint-count tables vs theory) and Ledger-spill exercised; tape bridge round-trips a surrogate training step with our custom nodes; gate wired into CI (seeded-broken adjoint demonstrably blocks).

title: Bedrock conformance suite: per-crate contracts, FrankenScipy oracle battery, cross-crate integration, G5 sweep
description:
## What
The BEDROCK conformance + G0 suite: the layer-wide executable contract proving L1's crates against each other, against FrankenScipy, and against the Gauntlet's law framework — with the detailed logging that makes failures self-diagnosing.

## Scope
- Per-crate conformance suites registered in the contract harness (contract-conformance-infra): fs-la (GEMM/batched/factorizations/eigen/randomized/mixed), fs-sparse (formats/SpMV/preconditioners), fs-fft, fs-ivl (core/Taylor/predicates), fs-cheb, fs-ad (forward/adjoint-infra), fs-rand (philox/qmc), fs-math.
- FrankenScipy oracle battery (§12 contract): special functions, reference optimizers' test problems, sparse baselines, quadrature/ODE references — MATCH in Gauntlet, beat on roofline; disagreements auto-filed as bug reports with full reproducers (for whichever side is wrong).
- Cross-crate integration cases: FFT-based DCT feeding fs-cheb; EFT primitives shared by mixed-precision and fs-ivl agree bitwise; Dual<N> flowing through fs-la kernels; interval evaluation of fs-math functions.
- Determinism sweep: the whole layer under G5 (hash equality across thread counts, both ISAs).
- Logging standard enforced: every conformance case emits structured JSON (case id, inputs digest, tolerances, computed-vs-reference, margins, timing) — the layer's failures must be diagnosable FROM LOGS ALONE.

## Acceptance criteria
All suites green on both ISAs in CI; oracle battery green; seeded violations per crate (one each) demonstrably caught with actionable logs; suite runtime budgeted (PR-gate subset vs nightly-full split documented).

## Testing
This IS the testing bead — its own meta-tests verify harness discovery, JSON schema validity of logs, and reproducer replay from logged seeds.

title: fs-rand QMC: Sobol Joe-Kuo + Owen scrambling, rank-1 lattice CBC rules
description:
## What

## Scope

title: Make exact CBC construction budgeted, cancellable, resumable, and certificate-producing
description:
## Background

The exact CBC repair correctly removes floating-point candidate-order ambiguity by comparing arbitrary-precision Bernoulli-B2 numerator sums. That mathematical correction increases work and memory with n, dimension, candidate count, and exact-integer limb growth. The current synchronous Lattice::cbc API accepts u32 n and arbitrary usize dimension, allocates n exact products, performs O(n^2 times dim) visits with growing multi-limb arithmetic, uses panic-style resource failures, has no explicit work/memory budget or Cx, and cannot pause/resume. Large hostile or accidental inputs can monopolize a worker or exhaust memory even though the selected vector is mathematically correct.

## Mission

Retain exact canonical ordering while turning CBC into a budget-first tile program with typed admission, bounded cancellation, resumable state, progress receipts, and an independently checkable minimality certificate. Keep the simple tabled-size convenience API only as a clearly bounded facade over the same authority; do not reintroduce floating comparison as an escape hatch.

## Required architecture

1. Define typed CbcProblem, CbcBudget, CbcState, CbcProgress, CbcCertificate, and CbcError. Admission validates n, dimension, admissible units, checked size/work bounds, limb-growth bounds, memory/capability budgets, and units before allocating or evaluating.
2. Tile work by prefix, candidate block, lattice-point block, and limb block under explicit Cx. Poll cancellation at bounded tile boundaries. Cancellation is request, drain, finalize and returns a replayable prefix with no half-committed generator.
3. Preserve exact lowest-candidate tie ordering independently of worker count, tile size, and reduction order. Candidate-score reductions use fixed logical identities and exact addition; parallel scheduling may change timing but not bytes.
4. Serialize enough exact products, candidate accumulators, prefix index, logical tile cursor, budgets spent, and canonical identities to pause, migrate, resume, and fork deterministically. Validate every limb invariant and digest before resuming.
5. Use a work/memory estimator that includes n products, candidate blocks, maximum numerator bit width, prefix-dependent product limbs, score accumulators, and receipt/certificate size. Reject inadmissible work with ranked fixes such as lower n/dim, larger budget, or a separately named approximate no-certificate mode.
6. Produce a per-prefix certificate binding the chosen candidate, exact winning score, exact runner-up score or equality class, admissible candidate set, tie rule, common-denominator derivation, and reduction root. Provide an independent checker that need not rerun the entire construction when a compact proof is available.
7. Keep korobov_error_sq explicitly diagnostic f64 unless separately certified. Exact construction must never be described as an exact floating error value.

## Theorem ratchets

[F] Develop a certificate that unit-residue permutation proves z0=1 for every admitted n and that exact numerator ordering is equivalent to the declared rational Korobov objective at each prefix.

[F/M] Investigate symmetry-orbit pruning of candidates under the unit group modulo n with a proof that the quotient preserves minima and canonical lowest representatives.

[M] Treat candidate blocks and prefix certificates as a sheaf over the lattice-point/candidate cover. Local exact score sections glue into a global minimality witness only when overlap sums, denominator identities, and canonical tie cocycles agree. Explore proof-carrying branch-and-bound or number-theoretic transforms that asymptotically beat exhaustive O(n^2 dim) enumeration without weakening exactness.

[M] Pursue verified fast convolution/FFT or character-sum formulations with interval or modular reconstruction, Chinese-remainder witnesses, and deterministic escalation to arbitrary precision when bounds do not separate candidates.

## Gauntlet

G0: ExactNat arithmetic laws against independent bounded integers and multi-limb KATs; exact B2 numerator identity; unit-residue permutation theorem instances; canonical ties; overflow-free checked admission; zero budget invokes no work.

G1/G2: published lattice KATs and independent development-only exact oracles across prime and composite n; convergence/error diagnostics remain separated from exact selection claims.

G3: invariant under candidate enumeration permutation, tile partition, worker count, equivalent rational scaling, modular residue relabeling, pause/resume splits, and symmetry-orbit expansion. Seeded mutations to scores, limbs, ties, cursor, and certificate roots fail closed.

G4: cancellation at every tile class; budgets at 0, 1, prefix boundary, candidate boundary, and limb-carry boundary; allocation denial; injected faults; no leaks; no partial chosen component.

G5: bit-stable same-ISA vectors, states, and certificates across thread counts; one-shot equals pause/resume/fork; frozen reference identities for multiple prime/composite cases.

## Completion

Production code, contracts, generated catalog/admission, unit/property/conformance/replay tests, independent certificate checker, structured logs, and central DSR/RCH proof are green. Performance evidence records machine fingerprint and exact problem/work sizes. No approximate fallback may inherit the exact-canonical capability name.
notes:
EXECUTION TRANCHE LANDED+VERIFIED 4cea2f30 (CloudyFinch session e5556ba0, ts1 clone @ exact SHA, full fs-rand union 12 suites 0 fail). cbc_exec schema v1: CbcExecutor runs the byte-identical exact construction over a CbcAdmission — prefix/candidate-block/point-block tiling, CbcPoll observed only at tile boundaries (request-drain-finalize; committed prefix never half-commits), run-scoped work allowances slicing the admitted budget with exhaustion at named boundaries (Entry/PointBlock/CandidateBlock/Prefix), debits following the admission schedule at admitted widths (monotone, tile-independent, ScheduleOverrun fail-closed), product/score limbs reserved at exact admitted capacity (the admission contract's exact-capacity storage requirement — in-envelope arithmetic never reallocates). qmc.rs touched with visibility-only changes (pub(crate) ExactNat/helpers + reserve_exact_limbs). Battery cbx_001-007 proves: authority equivalence per case incl. the pinned n=257 [1,71,56,106,21] KAT; tile-shape invariance of BOTH bytes and debit totals; cancellation at many split points with committed-prefix-is-a-prefix + resume==one-shot; allowance pause/resume debit+byte identity; zero allowance invokes no work; debits <= admitted estimate; typed refusals.

REMAINING SCOPE: (a) item 4 serialization — CbcState bytes for cross-process pause/migrate/fork with limb-invariant+digest validation on resume (limb_len helper deliberately deferred to land with its consumer); (b) item 6 per-prefix minimality certificate (chosen candidate, exact winning + runner-up scores/equality class, admissible set, tie rule, denominator derivation, reduction root) + the independent compact checker; (c) memory metering of observed allocator capacity or proof the exact-capacity reserve suffices; (d) named approximate no-certificate mode (item 5 tail); (e) theorem ratchets [F] unit-residue z0=1 certificate + [F/M] orbit pruning + [M] sheaf/NTT tracks; (f) G5 cross-thread evidence (currently single-threaded, trivially bit-stable; formal freeze later); (g) wire Lattice::cbc as the bounded facade over the executor per the mission (facade must not bypass admission).

title: CBC executor atomic cancellation, budget, and limb-resume semantics
description:
ROOT CAUSE: the code-first CBC executor preserves exact arithmetic bytes but its control transaction is not cancellation-correct or budget-atomic. run() can return AllowanceExhausted before polling, so repeated allowance=1 calls can starve an already-requested cancellation forever and entry is never polled. Candidate/point tiling does not bound multi-limb ExactNat add/multiply work; there is no limb cursor, so latency and allowance overshoot grow with dimension/limb width. Product/score/z mutations occur before debit validation and debit stores an over-limit total before ScheduleOverrun, so an error can leave duplicate-on-resume state. A resumed candidate can also finish and start another full point block in one tile, exceeding the documented bound.

MISSION: make each admitted execution transition a fail-closed transaction with explicit simultaneous cancellation/allowance precedence, poll at entry and after every drained atomic tile, prepay checked work before mutation, and commit accounting only with the mutation. Add a limb-block tile dimension and resumable exact-operation cursor carrying source/factor/carry/normalization progress so request -> drain -> finalize latency is bounded by declared work. Either retain unchanged replayable state on schedule refusal or enter a typed terminal poisoned state that cannot resume or emit a lattice. Make nonzero allowance a strict cap over prepaid atomic units; if a soft quantum remains, name it honestly and retain an exact overshoot theorem. Maintain cross-call candidate/point/limb counters so tile limits include resumed work.

TESTS / GAUNTLET: G0 transition-state invariants and preflight-before-mutation checks; G3 one-shot equals arbitrary pause/resume and tile-shape changes; G4 pre-cancelled zero-work entry, cancellation plus repeated allowance=1, cancellation at every limb carry/normalization boundary, exact per-call debit <= allowance, forced ScheduleOverrun byte-identical pre/post state or irreversible poison, candidate-transition tile bounds, zero/one/boundary budgets, allocation/fault injection, no partial chosen component; G5 same-target state/lattice bytes across split schedules. Validate the Completed branch's lattice, not only status. Preserve exact lowest-candidate ties and no approximate fallback.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED: bounded cancellation latency, strict per-run work caps, replayable ScheduleOverrun, cross-process resume, or limb-bounded G4 evidence.

title: CBC admission/execution single schedule and honest peak-memory authority

ROOT CAUSE: CBC admission and execution do not yet share one mechanical schedule/layout authority. Admission schema constants and memory formulas live privately in cbc.rs while cbc_exec.rs duplicates scalar constants and reconstructs work. Existing cbx_006 proves only spent <= estimate, so missing/undercharged work passes. Product reserve_exact is not an exact-capacity theorem: ExactNat::mul_assign_factor uses mem::take plus a fresh resized Vec, discarding the reservation. This creates a concrete peak-overlap undercount for dimension=1: n pre-reserved product buffers remain live while a fresh output of up to P limbs is built, but admission charges nP plus only the one-limb previous product. The estimator also uses surrogate Vec/Option layouts rather than the actual ExactNat/ScanAccum/Phase/executor state, and allocator capacity may exceed requested reserve_exact capacity.

MISSION: define one checked CbcExecutionSchedule and actual storage-layout authority produced by admission and consumed verbatim by every executor/facade/certificate path. Remove duplicated constants/formulas. Model prefix-specific product widths, temporary overlap, scores, cursor/state, receipts/certificates, allocator rounding boundary, and every work class exactly enough to fail closed. Use capacity-preserving multiplication or charge the real fresh-output overlap. State clearly whether memory means requested payload, observed Vec::capacity, allocator usable size, or a conservative envelope; never call reserve_exact an exact actual-capacity proof. Couple Lattice::cbc bounded facade and certificate checker to the same admitted authority.

TESTS / GAUNTLET: exact prime/composite/dimension-one schedule and peak-memory KATs including n=3,d=1; mutation tests that change any admission constant/layout/schedule and force execution mismatch refusal; exact debit equality per work class (not only <=); boundary/off-by-one/usize-address-space cases; observed capacity or allocator-denial evidence under the declared memory semantics; G3 tile/resume invariance with identical admitted totals; independently recompute schedule/memory receipts and reject forged or stale authority. Preserve same-target ABI/layout no-claim where unavoidable.

title: CBC fallible exact storage and allocation-atomic arithmetic
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The CBC executor currently builds and grows Vec-backed ExactNat values, product tables, generator/certificate vectors, and replacement products through infallible allocation. CbcExecutor::new, reserve_exact, Vec::with_capacity, resize, clone, to_vec, and push can panic or abort rather than return a structured budget/capability refusal. Product and certificate transitions can remove or mutate authoritative state before later allocations complete. An admitted byte count is not useful if the implementation cannot fail closed when the allocator refuses it.

MISSION
Create one fallible storage authority for base exact-CBC execution. Introduce try_new and checked try-reserve/try-allocate paths; define whether the receipt governs requested payload, observed Vec capacity, allocator usable size, or a conservative arena/slab envelope. Prefer fixed-capacity/slab or capacity-preserving buffers so admitted operations do not reallocate. Make ExactNat add/multiply/normalize transitions transactional: preflight required limbs and allocation, compute into admitted scratch, then atomically commit, leaving source and executor bytes unchanged on any failure. Never use allocation panic as resource admission.

DELIVERABLES
- Typed allocation/storage refusal carrying storage class, requested/admitted/observed counts, phase/cursor, target layout identity, and ranked remediation.
- Fallible construction for product owners/payloads, scores, generator, scratch, and progress metadata.
- Capacity-preserving exact arithmetic or an explicitly charged old/new overlap protocol.
- A storage receipt whose schema/version/target assumptions are bound to the shared CbcExecutionSchedule authority from .20.4.
- A no-allocation hot transition once admission succeeds, or precisely metered separately admitted allocation points.
- No partial prefix, candidate, score, product, certificate, work counter, or progress mutation on refusal.

GAUNTLET
G0 exact required-capacity and one-under KATs for zero/one/maximum limb widths, n=3 d=1 overlap, composite/prime moduli, and every storage class. G3 one-shot versus arbitrary successful allocation schedule equality. G4 deterministic injected denial at every allocation point, byte-for-byte pre/post executor state, no leak/double drop/panic, and retry equivalence after capacity remediation. Include checked usize/address-space boundaries and allocator rounding observations under the declared semantics. Structured JSONL diagnostics must log phase, cursor, requested/admitted counts, schedule identity, and verdict without unescaped fields.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
No claim of allocation-failure recovery, exact actual allocator capacity, no-reallocation execution, or mutation-free storage refusal. This task does not by itself establish cancellation latency, strict run allowance, cross-process state, or certified-mode storage.

title: CBC limb microcursor and bounded exact-arithmetic polling
description:
ROOT CAUSE
Candidate_block and point_block bound outer loops but each ExactNat add-multiply, carry propagation, zero fill, comparison, normalization, and product replacement remains monolithic in limb width. Thus cancellation latency and allowance overshoot grow with dimension/product width even when point_block=1. Local candidate counters also reset across calls, so an already-running candidate plus new work can cross the intended observation envelope.

MISSION
Express every exact arithmetic primitive as a deterministic resumable microprogram with a persistent limb cursor. Extend the tile contract with limb_block and explicit operation classes. Each microstep must have a checked, prepaid schedule charge, bounded memory access, deterministic source/destination/carry state, and a well-defined commit boundary. Poll spacing must be bounded by admitted microsteps rather than by an unbounded big-integer operation. Persist candidate, point, source-limb, factor-limb, destination-limb, carry, zero-fill, comparison, and normalization progress as needed without changing final arithmetic bytes or lowest-candidate ties.

DELIVERABLES
- Versioned LimbCursor/ExactOpState enum with invariants for add-multiply, carry, compare, normalize, and product update.
- CbcTileShape limb_block or a typed nested tile budget with nonzero checked admission.

title: CBC strict transactional runner, cancellation precedence, and progress receipts
description:
ROOT CAUSE
run currently executes before its first poll, checks exhausted allowance before cancellation at a shared boundary, uses saturating subtraction so an atomic tile can overspend an arbitrarily small allowance, and debits after arithmetic/prefix mutation. debit stores an over-limit work_spent before returning ScheduleOverrun. These choices can starve a pre-requested cancellation, make nonzero allowance a soft threshold, and leave state changed after a refusal.

MISSION
Define and implement a fail-closed run transaction over the shared schedule and limb microcursor. Poll at entry. State an explicit simultaneous-event precedence, with cancellation observable even at an exhausted-allowance boundary. Preflight and prepay every atomic microstep before mutation; commit the work counter and state transition together. A strict allowance must never be exceeded. If a requested allowance is smaller than the next indivisible admitted step, return a typed NeedAllowance carrying the exact minimum without executing it. Schedule identity mismatch/overrun must leave replayable bytes unchanged or enter an explicit terminal poison state that cannot resume or publish results.

DELIVERABLES
- Versioned run protocol and precedence table for AlreadyComplete, invalid tile, pre-cancel, zero allowance, NeedAllowance, cancellation, completion, storage refusal, schedule mismatch, and panic/fault containment.
- Per-run progress receipt binding before/after state roots, schedule identity, allowance requested/used/remaining, exact transition counts, last boundary, poll count/maximum spacing, and finalization status.
- request -> drain -> finalize semantics; no silent drop and no result publication before final receipt.
- Exact per-call candidate/point/limb limits including carried work from prior calls.
- Mutation-free failure or irreversible typed poison with a checker-enforced publication ban.

GAUNTLET
G0 zero, one, exact, and one-under allowances for every charge class; pre-cancelled positive and zero allowance; cancellation-versus-allowance same-boundary precedence; Completed lattice validation; monotone exact counters. G3 one-shot equals repeated minimum-allowance calls and arbitrary pause/resume in result/state/progress roots. G4 ScheduleOverrun/storage/panic injection before every commit, byte-identical pre/post refusal, cancellation at every boundary, bounded poll spacing, drain completion, no leaks, and no duplicate-on-retry mutation. Logs must show structured before/after roots and exact charge evidence. G5 same-target receipt and result stability.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
Current AllowanceExhausted is a soft quantum, not a strict cap. Do not claim entry cancellation, cancellation precedence, mutation-free ScheduleOverrun, exact per-run work, or progress-receipt completeness before this task closes.

title: CBC canonical state serialization, resume, fork, and budget anti-reissuance
description:
MISSION
Make an in-flight exact-CBC construction a portable, authenticated, invariant-checked artifact that can pause, migrate, resume, and fork deterministically without reissuing consumed work/memory authority. The current executor value is process-local and explicitly makes no cross-process claim.

STATE CONTRACT
Canonical bytes must bind problem, admitted budgets, target/layout compatibility class, admission/execution/certificate schema identities, schedule digest, committed prefix, product/score exact limbs, phase, candidate/point/limb microcursors, carry/scratch state, work spent, allowance ledger, progress-chain root, certificate mode/storage authority, determinism mode, and implementation/theorem versions. Decode must be bounded and iterative; every length/count/product is checked before allocation. Normalize or reject noncanonical exact integers, signed zero/NaN where applicable, duplicate encodings, impossible cursor combinations, stale schedules, truncated/trailing bytes, and unsupported versions.

BUDGET / FORK SEMANTICS
A resume must not mint fresh admitted work or forget prior debits. Define non-reissuable budget authority and idempotent continuation keys. Forks share immutable source/admission identity but receive explicitly partitioned or newly authorized remaining budgets; a byte copy cannot double-spend authority. State roots and parent/fork lineage enter the ledger/progress receipt.

DELIVERABLES
- Versioned CbcState canonical encoder/decoder and collision-resistant domain-separated identity using project identity authority.
- Independent state checker that validates structural/arithmetic/cursor invariants without advancing the solver.
- pause/resume/migrate/fork APIs with explicit capability and target-compatibility refusals.
- Idempotent continuation/publication protocol and lineage receipts.
- Structured explain diagnostics and ranked fixes for stale version, incompatible target, insufficient budget, corrupt state, or ambiguous authority.

GAUNTLET
G0 canonical round trip for every phase/microcursor and empty/boundary state; exact byte goldens; malformed/noncanonical corpus; identity-field mutation matrix. G3 one-shot equals serialize/deserialize after every transition class, repeated migrations, and legal forks in final lattice/certificates/progress roots. G4 truncation/resource bombs, allocation denial, corruption, stale schedule/source, panic containment, duplicate continuation, fork double-spend attempts, cancellation during encode/finalize, and no partial publication. G5 bit-stable same-ISA bytes across thread counts; explicit cross-ISA compatibility/refusal evidence.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
No cross-process replay, authenticated resume, fork determinism, budget anti-reissuance, or durable progress identity. A raw Debug/serde-like snapshot is insufficient.

title: CBC separately admitted certificate execution and atomic publication
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The landed cbc_cert checker is a useful independent leaf, but CbcExecutor::enable_certificates currently exposes certificate production on the base executor while explicitly placing runner-up retention, tie-class growth, prefix clones, score to_vec, certificate Vec growth, and publication outside admission. Those allocations and copies occur after best.take in places, are not cancellation/limb bounded, are absent from state serialization, and can panic or leave a nonresumable transaction. Schema-v4 naming is already being consumed by base schedule/layout work, so certified mode needs an explicit distinct authority/version.

MISSION
Create a separately admitted certified-execution mode that accounts for every extra operation and byte, uses the same strict transactional runner/microcursor/storage/state authorities, and publishes each certificate atomically only after an independently checkable receipt is complete. Preserve the full minimality-by-exhaustion checker and its honest distinction from compact consistency; pursue compact subquadratic/sheaf-glued minimality proofs as a gated theorem ratchet, not as an excuse to weaken exhaustive checking.

DELIVERABLES
- Typed CbcCertificateBudget/admission receipt with separate schema identity and exact worst-case/prefix-specific tie, runner-up, prefix, limb, receipt, and output storage/work bounds.
- Fallible preallocated certificate construction; no clone/push/to_vec outside authority.
- Cancellation/resume/fork-aware certificate cursor and atomic publish transaction bound to base state/progress roots.
- Certificate identity binding n, exact reduction root/prefix, chosen/tie/runner-up scores, admissible/tie rules, denominator derivation, checker/schema/theorem versions, and execution schedule identity.
- Chain validation: a later prefix certificate is conditional on its declared root unless earlier selections are independently linked; no accidental claim that an arbitrary prefix is the canonical CBC history.
- Keep verify_consistency and audit_minimality names/no-claims precise; independently validate the first-component theorem or emit its explicit no-claim.

GAUNTLET
G0 exact certified-mode admission KATs including maximal tie classes and score widths; malformed/noncanonical limbs; first-prefix/root rules. G3 certified vs uncertified lattice equality and certificate equality across tile/allowance/resume/fork shapes. G4 injected denial at every certificate allocation/publication step, cancellation through tie/runner-up/copy/check phases, byte-identical retry, no partial certificate, no lost best, and strict work caps. Mutation batteries cover prefix/root/history, n, score limbs, tie completeness/order, runner-up minimality, rules, denominator, schema/checker identity, schedule identity, and retained content roots. G5 durable state/certificate bytes under admitted determinism.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
Base enable_certificates is not budget-covered or allocation-failure-safe. Consistency mode does not prove global minimality; an isolated later certificate proves selection only relative to its declared prefix unless history is linked. No compact subquadratic proof claim without its own checker and evidence.

title: fs-la GEMM: BLIS-style autotuned microkernel + packing, f64/f32/mixed, >=75% peak target

title: fs-la batched small dense: SIMD-across-batch 6x6-48x48 kernels (FEM hot loop), >=60% peak
description:
## What
`fs-la` batched small dense: the ACTUAL hot loop of FEM-adjacent work (plan §6.1) — element matrices are 6×6…48×48, and they dominate assembly-adjacent compute.

## Scope

title: Canonical rank-deficient TSQR theorem and gauge-stable Q/R certificates
description:
MISSION
Turn the currently over-broad statement that a nonnegative diagonal makes every QR factor unique into a substantially stronger and actually specified frontier theorem/program: define and implement a canonical, deterministic gauge for rank-deficient tall-skinny QR whose observable R, rank profile, null-space frame, and replay certificate are invariant under the admitted TSQR reduction schedule. This is an ambition ratchet, not a retreat. The goal is a reusable canonicalization primitive for Krylov bases, POD, inverse problems, certificate rank decisions, and distributed replay.

BACKGROUND AND ROOT ISSUE
For full-column-rank real A, positive diagonal conventions can select a unique thin QR under standard hypotheses. When A is rank deficient, rotations inside deficient subspaces and zero-diagonal columns leave gauge freedom; merely forcing a nonnegative diagonal does not prove uniqueness. Current fs-la documentation must therefore use a no-claim boundary until a stronger construction is defined and proven. The project should pursue that stronger construction rather than discard the capability.

MATHEMATICAL TARGETS
1. Specify the admitted equivalence relation over inputs, leaf partitionings, legal deterministic reduction schedules, floating-point execution modes, and signed-zero/NaN policy.
2. Define a canonical numerical rank profile using scale-aware thresholds carried with units/error budgets; never hide a tolerance as a dimensionful literal.
3. Define a deterministic gauge for dependent columns and null-space directions. Candidate ingredients include lexicographically pivoted rank profiles, orientation by first certified nonzero coordinate, exterior-power/Pluecker signatures, polar factors on rank strata, and interval-separated tie resolution. Explore and prove the strongest viable synthesis rather than prematurely fixing one method.
4. State theorem tiers separately: exact-arithmetic canonicality; correctly rounded or interval-certified canonicality when separation hypotheses hold; deterministic same-ISA bit stability; and explicit no-claim behavior in numerically undecidable near-rank transitions.
5. Produce proof obligations for idempotence of canonicalization, invariance under admissible TSQR tree regrouping, compatibility with full-rank positive-diagonal QR, stable behavior inside a fixed rank stratum, and structured escalation at rank-boundary ambiguity.
6. Investigate a sheaf-style interpretation: local leaf frames and transition gauges form local sections; successful global canonicalization is a glued section, while a nonzero obstruction/cocycle becomes an executable certificate that uniqueness is not currently justified. This moonshot route stays feature-gated until evidence supports it.

ENGINEERING DELIVERABLES
- A typed CanonicalQrPolicy carrying rank/error budgets, determinism class, tie policy, feature/capability gates, and versioned theorem identity.
- A result object separating canonical R, optional implicit Q action, certified rank profile, null-space/gauge metadata, residual/error bounds, and honest claim status.
- A compact independently checkable certificate or structured no-claim record; checker logic must not merely call the producer again.
- Deterministic replay identity over input artifact, policy, tree identity, arithmetic mode, implementation/theorem version, result, and certificate.
- Cancellation-correct tiled canonicalization with request -> drain -> finalize behavior and resumable state if the operation exceeds a single bounded tile.
- No unchecked shape products or infallible giant allocations in admitted paths.
- Contract and API language that distinguishes exact theorem, conditional certified theorem, deterministic implementation fact, numerical stability evidence, and open conjecture.

GAUNTLET AND TEST MATRIX
G0: full-rank compatibility; reconstruction and orthogonality; canonicalization idempotence; permutation/rank-profile validity; zero-row, zero-column, one-column, repeated-column, exact-zero, signed-zero, and maximally representable shape admission; checked-overflow and allocation-failure diagnostics.
G1: manufactured matrices with known rank, singular gaps, null spaces, and controlled perturbations; verify residual/error-bound scaling and convergence under precision/refinement escalation.
G2: Kahan, Hilbert/Vandermonde families, duplicated/nearly duplicated columns, graded singular spectra, and adversarial cancellation cases with detailed rank/gauge evidence.
G3: row-block repartitioning, admissible tree reassociation, column/unit rescaling, orthogonal left transforms, equivalent representation rewrites, pause/resume/fork equivalence, and certificate mutation rejection. Metamorphic properties must state which quantities are invariant versus covariant.
G4: cancellation at entry and every tile boundary, schedule exhaustion one-before/exact/one-after, panic/allocation fault containment, loser drain, leak checks, and mutation-free failed admission.
G5: bit-stable reruns across thread counts on the same ISA; explicit cross-ISA policy; golden replay identities tied to theorem and arithmetic versions.

ACCEPTANCE AND NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY
Do not restore an unconditional uniqueness claim merely because tests pass. Closure requires a written theorem statement with hypotheses, an implementation that matches those hypotheses, independent certificate checks, adversarial Gauntlet evidence, and explicit behavior when rank is ambiguous. If the sheaf obstruction or interval separation cannot certify one gauge, return a typed ambiguity/no-claim result and ranked escalation options such as more precision, stronger interval bounds, a changed budget, or an alternative policy. The default path remains the honest deterministic TSQR already established; frontier/moonshot canonicality stays gated until promoted by evidence.

title: fs-la eigensolvers: LOBPCG + Lanczos (selective reorth), matrix-free, resumable, adjoint hooks

title: fs-la randomized NLA: rangefinder/RSVD/Nystrom, sketch-precondition LS, Hutchinson/Hutch++ [F]
description:
## What
`fs-la` randomized NLA (plan §6.1 [F]): randomized range finders, randomized SVD/Nyström, sketch-and-precondition least squares, and Hutchinson/Hutch++ stochastic trace estimation.

## Scope
- Randomized range finder with adaptive rank determination (posterior error estimates, block power iterations for spectral-decay-poor cases); randomized SVD on top; Nyström for PSD kernels (GP approximations in bayesopt).
- Sketch-and-precondition least squares: sketch (subsampled randomized trig transform via fs-fft or sparse sign sketches), QR the sketch, precondition LSQR-style iterations — the modern fast path for tall dense LS.
- Hutchinson + Hutch++ trace estimators: log-det and tr(f(A)) machinery; the named consumer is SENSITIVITY AGGREGATION IN TOPOLOGY OPTIMIZATION and log-det terms in GP likelihoods. Variance-reduced (Hutch++) split with deterministic Philox probe streams — stochastic estimates are still replayable (P2) and e-process-monitorable (stopping when confidence sequence is tight enough, wired later via fs-eproc).
- All randomness through fs-rand keyed streams; all results carry probe counts + variance estimates as evidence metadata (Evidence<T> integration point).

## Acceptance criteria
Rank-r approximation errors within theoretical bounds (oversampling p → expected ‖A−QQᵀA‖ bounds) on synthetic spectra (fast/slow decay, gaps); Hutch++ variance beats Hutchinson at matched probe counts (demonstrated, ledgered); sketch-LS matches direct QR solutions to tolerance with the expected speed crossover documented.

## Testing

title: fs-la mixed precision: f32-factor/f64-refine policy engine, EFT/double-double ladder
description:
## What
`fs-la` mixed precision with iterative refinement AS A DEFAULT POLICY (plan §6.1): factor/precondition in f32, refine to f64, escalate to double-double only where the Error Ledger demands it.

## Scope
- Policy engine: given a target accuracy (from the caller's budget, P4) and a condition estimate, choose the precision ladder (f32 factor + f64 refine | f64 direct | f64 factor + dd refine); record the decision + achieved residual as evidence.
- Iterative refinement drivers for LU/Cholesky/QR-based solves with convergence monitoring (residual reduction per step; stall detection → escalate or report structured failure with diagnosis: "condition ~1e12 exceeds f32-factor regime").
- Error-free transformations (TwoSum/TwoProd/Dekker splitting) as the in-house building blocks; double-double arithmetic type (add/mul/div/sqrt with documented relative-error bounds) — shared with fs-ivl's high-precision oracle needs (single implementation, two consumers).
- Integration: solver-stack inherits the policy for Krylov inner/outer precision splits; fs-la-batched gets f32-storage/f64-accumulate variants; Error Ledger (fs-plan-models) receives per-solve precision provenance.

## Why
The bandwidth-starved reference machine (TR: ~3.4 GB/s/core) makes f32 storage a near-2× bandwidth lever; refinement buys back f64 accuracy for well-enough-conditioned problems — but ONLY as a policy with evidence, never a silent downgrade.

## Acceptance criteria
Refinement recovers f64-accurate solutions (componentwise residual targets) on condition-controlled batteries up to the documented threshold; escalation triggers exactly where theory predicts (threshold sweep test); dd arithmetic passes known-answer + property tests (error bounds).

## Testing
G0: EFT exactness properties (TwoSum invariants are EXACT — bitwise testable); refinement convergence-rate checks; policy-decision determinism. Logs: per-solve ladders chosen, residual trajectories, escalation events with reasons.

title: ADDENDUM L3 DIFFERENTIATION & REALITY: end-to-end adjoints, reality-as-a-chart, spacetime complex
description:
## Mission
ADDENDUM LAYER 3 — DIFFERENTIATION AND COUPLING TO REALITY. Transpose the ledger to get sensitivities, admit the physical world as one more representation, and extend the complex into time. Where Layer 1 makes the system fast and Layer 2 makes it honest, this layer makes it a *design engine* (gradients through every seam), a *metrology partner* (as-built vs as-designed as a sheaf δ), and — eventually — a *coupled-transient* engine (splitting error made visible in spacetime).

## The three proposals
- **Proposal 1 — End-to-end adjoints: transpose the sheaf** (Mean 770, Useful 950, Agent 950). The ledger composes error forward; the same graph, transposed, composes sensitivity backward — ∂(lift)/∂(spline control point) computed *through* the SDF conversion, *through* the mesh, *through* the solve. Adjoints exist per-solver today but die at every seam exactly the way error bounds do; a ledger-shaped system gets them almost by transposition because restriction maps are linear operators whose adjoints are free. A swarm with gradients is an optimizer; a swarm without them is a random-search farm. Unlocks F, 11, B, and 9's best proposer.
- **Proposal 11 — Reality is just another chart** (Mean 760, Accret 850). A CT scan of the manufactured part is one more representation with restriction maps, so as-built-vs-as-designed is a δ between two sections computed by the watertightness machinery; strain-gauge and wind-tunnel data assimilate through the adjoints. Commercial kicker: **adjoint-driven tolerance allocation** — spend tight manufacturing tolerances only where ∂performance/∂geometry is large, provably loosen everywhere else, deliver the savings as a certified GD&T statement a CFO understands.
- **Proposal 4 — Extend the complex into time** (Mean 590, ranks last). Coupled multiphysics glued in *spacetime*: time slabs as cells of the complex, so operator-splitting/coupling error lands in the ledger — measurable, localized, adaptively controllable. Ranks last not because wrong but because it is a refinement that pays only after strongly-coupled transient workloads are proven demand. Explicitly does NOT claim coupling *stability* (added-mass FSI instabilities are per-coupling analysis problems the sheaf does not solve).

## Cross-layer dependencies

title: Proposal 1 — End-to-end adjoints: TRANSPOSE THE LEDGER (per-op VJP registration, transposed BDDC/Krylov solves, revolve checkpoints in the CAS)
description:
## What
Proposal 1's CORE — END-TO-END ADJOINTS by transposing the ledger DAG. The ledger composes error FORWARD; the same graph, TRANSPOSED, composes sensitivity BACKWARD: ∂(lift)/∂(spline control point) computed THROUGH the SDF conversion, THROUGH the mesh, THROUGH the solve. This turns FrankenSim from a simulator into a DESIGN ENGINE. A swarm with gradients is an optimizer; a swarm without them is a random-search farm (Useful 950, Agent 950).

## Why a ledger gets this almost for free
Adjoint methods exist per-solver today but DIE AT EVERY SEAM exactly the way error bounds do — which is why industrial design optimization still runs on finite differences and surrogate hacks. A fragmented toolchain cannot chain adjoints; a ledger-shaped system gets them almost by TRANSPOSITION, since restriction/conversion maps are LINEAR operators whose adjoints are free.

## Scope (differentiate the DAG, not the codes)
- Every ledger op REGISTERS a vector-Jacobian product (VJP). This is the amendment: every op spec gains a VJP requirement OR an explicit non-differentiable declaration with color consequences.
- Restriction/trace/conversion maps: transposes of already-linear operators (nearly free — reuse fs-geom Convert receipts + fs-xform Jacobian actions).
- Solver ops: the DISCRETE ADJOINT of the linearized system, reusing the existing Krylov + preconditioning infrastructure with TRANSPOSED operators — NEVER differentiate through Krylov iterations (BDDC preconditioners transpose naturally). Extends the base plan's fs-adjoint (IFT differentiate-through-solution).
- Time-dependent ops: revolve-style optimal checkpointing, with checkpoints stored in the CONTENT-ADDRESSED store so adjoint sweeps and the incremental cache (Proposal 2) SHARE storage discipline.

## Acceptance criteria
Every registered op has a VJP (or a declared non-differentiable status with color consequences); a seam-crossing gradient (spline CP → lift, through SDF+mesh+solve) matches an independent finite-difference check within tolerance; solver adjoints reuse transposed Krylov/BDDC and never differentiate through iterations; revolve checkpoints live in the CAS and reproduce bit-equal gradients with/without spill.

## Kill criterion (Proposal 1)
If, on the wedge vertical, adjoint-driven optimization does not beat the best derivative-free baseline (CMA-ES or BO at equal budget) on ≥70% of the benchmark design tasks, the seam-crossing-gradient premise is failing in practice — scope adjoints DOWN to the single-representation paths where they demonstrably pay and stop paying the VJP tax on exotic ops.

## Testing
G0: ⟨Av,w⟩=⟨v,Aᵀw⟩ transpose-consistency suite (reuse fs-adjoint's); G3 adjoint-vs-FD along random directions across seams; end-to-end: a seam-crossing shape-gradient descent reduces the objective monotonically. Logs: VJP registry coverage, per-op transpose checks, seam-crossing gradient-check tables.

## Dependencies
Base plan fs-adjoint + solver infra (Krylov/BDDC) + Rep Router (differentiable routing — see adjoint-mesh) + fs-geom Convert + fs-xform Jacobians; Proposal 6 (FD falsifiers — see adjoint-certs); Proposal 2 (checkpoint storage). Unlocks Proposal F (hazard sensitivities), Proposal 11 (assimilation + tolerance allocation), Proposal B (attribution), Proposal 9's best proposer. AMENDS every op spec (VJP requirement) + the Rep Router fitness (differentiability term).

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- **Boundary vs base fs-adjoint (flux-tfz.24):** the base crate owns per-solver/per-op discrete adjoints, revolve, and Hadamard forms; Proposal 1 owns ONLY the ledger-DAG TRANSPOSITION that chains those per-op VJPs across representation seams (Convert/trace/restriction transposes). Revolve checkpoint storage is SHARED with Proposal 2's content-addressed store, not re-implemented.
- **Determinism (G5):** transposed reductions reuse the deterministic fixed-shape reduction trees (adjoint sweeps re-run the reduction structure in reverse); bit-equal gradients with/without spill.
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Missing-VJP fail-loud case: an op with no registered VJP and no explicit non-differentiable declaration that lands inside a differentiation path raises a STRUCTURED error and BLOCKS the gradient — never a silent-zero/partial gradient (a silently-zero seam gradient is a Goodhart trap). FD-falsifier tolerance is conditioning-aware so an ill-conditioned seam where adjoint and FD legitimately diverge does not fire a false falsifier hit.

title: Proposal 1 — End-to-end adjoints: NON-DIFFERENTIABLE MESHING MITIGATIONS (differentiability-as-routing / Hadamard shape forms / estimated-color+discontinuity flag)
description:
## What
Proposal 1's MESHING PROBLEM, handled HONESTLY. Remeshing is genuinely NON-DIFFERENTIABLE across topology events. Rather than pretend otherwise, apply three mitigations in order of preference — and turn the base plan's multi-representation architecture from a complication into the ASSET that provides differentiable paths where mesh-locked pipelines have none.

## Scope — three mitigations, in order
1. **Make differentiability a ROUTING REQUIREMENT**: the Rep Router PREFERS SDF/spline paths (naturally smooth) when a query requests gradients. This is the key reframing: multi-representation becomes the thing that PROVIDES differentiable paths. This is the amendment adding a DIFFERENTIABILITY TERM to the Rep Router's fitness function.
2. **Shape-derivative (Hadamard boundary-form) formulations** that avoid mesh sensitivities entirely where applicable (reuse fs-adjoint's Hadamard boundary shape gradients on FEEC traces).
3. **Where a remesh event is UNAVOIDABLE inside the differentiation path**: emit the gradient with **estimated color** (Proposal 3) + a declared DISCONTINUITY FLAG, rather than pretending the gradient is exact across a topology change.

## Acceptance criteria
A gradient query routes to an SDF/spline path when one exists (differentiability-aware routing); Hadamard boundary forms compute shape gradients without mesh sensitivities on the applicable fixtures; an unavoidable remesh inside the diff path yields an estimated-color gradient with a discontinuity flag (never a silently-wrong verified gradient).

## Testing
Property: gradient-requesting queries never silently traverse a non-differentiable remesh without downgrading color + flagging; Hadamard-vs-perturbation-resolve agreement on shape fixtures (sphere volume/compliance classics); router prefers smooth paths under a gradient request. Falsifier (Proposal 6): FD spot-check across a smooth path agrees; across a flagged remesh, the discontinuity is real. Logs: chosen paths, color/flag on each gradient, Hadamard-vs-FD tables.

## Dependencies
adjoint-vjp (the VJP framework); base plan Rep Router (AMENDED: differentiability term in fitness) + fs-adjoint (Hadamard shape gradients); Proposal 3 (estimated color + discontinuity flag). Sibling to adjoint-certs.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Boundary: a gradient query with NO differentiable path available returns estimated + discontinuity-flag (never a faked verified gradient); router tie-break on equal-fitness paths is deterministic.
close_reason: Meshing mitigations implemented as fs_adjoint::mitigate ([F]-gated behind diff-mitigations -> ledger-transpose; fs-adjoint gains fs-geom + fs-evidence deps, both legal L3->L2/L1): THE THREE MITIGATIONS IN ORDER OF PREFERENCE. (1) DIFFERENTIABILITY AS A ROUTING REQUIREMENT: DiffAwareOracle wraps any CostOracle and adds the differentiability term AT THE FITNESS SEAM — non-differentiable edges report a 1e6s penalty when gradients are requested, steering the Pareto planner onto SDF/spline paths with ZERO changes to fs-geom's router (the oracle IS the fitness; the amendment lands without touching another agent's crate surface). mg-001 proves the reframing: the identical router takes the cheap remesh path for a plain query and the pricier bezier-clip spline path under a gradient request; (2) HADAMARD BOUNDARY FORMS as the mesh-free path: mg-003 verifies the base crate's volume shape gradient against genuine perturbation-resolve (move every vertex by t*V, re-measure volume via element geometry) through the conditioning-aware FD falsifier — no mesh sensitivities computed anywhere; (3) UNAVOIDABLE REMESH: when every viable path crosses the declared non-differentiable edge, the gradient is graded EstimatedWithDiscontinuity carrying a Proposal-3 Color::Estimated with INFINITE dispersion (no spread claim across a topology event) and the crossing edges NAMED — mg-002 proves the downgrade fires and grade_ops applies the same rule to tape-level op chains (the review-round-3 boundary: never a faked verified gradient); (4) mg-004 shows the flag is REAL with a subtle finding: at the topology step the Richardson self-error EXPLODES (FD at h vs h/2 disagree by ~500) while the conditioning-aware falsifier from bk0o.1 correctly REFUSES to false-fire on the ill-conditioned point — the self-error explosion is itself the measurable discontinuity signature, and the two beads' round-3 requirements interlock exactly as designed; (5) mg-005: equal-fitness tie-breaks deterministic across 5 repeated plans. title: Proposal 1 — End-to-end adjoints: GRADIENT CERTIFICATES + FD falsifier spot checks (colors on gradients, no-merge-without-a-passing-check)
description:
## What
Proposal 1's GRADIENT CERTIFICATES — gradients are CLAIMS like any other and get COLORS like any other. A gradient without a certificate is folklore; this bead makes every gradient carry evidence.

## Testing

title: Proposal 11 — Reality as a chart: INGESTION (scan/point-cloud charts + restriction maps + ledgered registration + design-time fiducials)
description:
## What
Proposal 11's INGESTION — REALITY IS JUST ANOTHER CHART. A CT scan of the manufactured part is one more representation with its own restriction maps, so as-built-vs-as-designed becomes a δ between two sections computed by the WATERTIGHTNESS machinery. This closes the loop through the physical world: the "validated" color stops being a static stamp and becomes a living, regime-tagged belief state.

## Scope — ingestion
- Scan data (CT voxel grids, laser point clouds) admitted as a REPRESENTATION TYPE with restriction maps to interface trace spaces (extends fs-rep-voxel + fs-geom's chart zoo; the representation registry is explicitly OPENED to measured-data chart types — the amendment).
- REGISTRATION (alignment of scan to design) is itself an OPTIMIZATION WITH ERROR, so it is LEDGERED — made well-posed by physical fiducials/datums specified AT DESIGN TIME. This pushes a DESIGN-FOR-VERIFICATION requirement UPSTREAM into the geometry layer (the amendment: fs-geom gains fiducial/datum primitives).

## Scope — as-built diff
- The δ between as-designed and as-scanned sections under a MEASUREMENT-NOISE-AWARE tolerance, colored **validated** and anchored to the metrology INSTRUMENT'S CALIBRATION CERTIFICATE. Reuses the sheaf δ / watertightness machinery unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria
Scan data ingests as a chart with restriction maps; registration is a ledgered optimization with its error carried forward; fiducials/datums make registration well-posed on fixtures; the as-built diff is a validated-color δ anchored to the metrology calibration cert.

## Kill criterion (Proposal 11 — R8)
If REGISTRATION UNCERTAINTY on realistic scanned parts EXCEEDS the geometric deviations being certified (signal below noise floor), the as-built loop is premature for that part class — RETAIN assimilation of point-sensor data (strain gauges, thermocouples, which have no registration problem) and DEFER full-field scan integration. Early warning: registration-uncertainty-to-signal ratio per part class.

## Testing
Property: registration error is ledgered + propagated (never dropped); fiducial-based registration is well-posed on fixtures with known ground-truth pose; as-built δ colored validated + anchored. Falsifier: a known-good part scans to a within-tolerance δ; a known-defective part's δ localizes the defect. Logs: registration optimizations + errors, fiducial usage, as-built δ fields, calibration anchors.

## Dependencies
base plan fs-rep-voxel + fs-geom (AMENDED: measured-data chart types + fiducial/datum primitives) + the sheaf watertightness machinery; Proposal 3 (validated color + regime tags); metrology partnerships (the practical gate — Pract 500). Foundation for reality-assimilate + reality-tolerance. Owns risk R8.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Boundary: a scan with no fiducials (under-determined registration) is flagged ill-posed and falls to the point-sensor path rather than an over-confident delta.
close_reason: Implemented as NEW crate crates/fs-asbuilt (crate:fs-rep-voxel relabeled crate:fs-asbuilt; L2, depends on fs-evidence — collision-free vs the existing fs-rep-voxel). title: Proposal 11 — Reality as a chart: ASSIMILATION (weak-constraint 4D-Var via adjoints; as-built diff colored validated; registration-free point sensors as fallback)

title: Proposal 11 — Reality as a chart: ADJOINT-DRIVEN TOLERANCE ALLOCATION (certified GD&T report — the CFO deliverable)
description:
## What

GD&T (geometric dimensioning and tolerancing) today is assigned by convention and fear; this replaces fear with a certified sensitivity. A value proposition a CFO understands without a physics lecture.

## Scope
- Minimize manufacturing cost subject to P(performance ∈ spec) ≥ target, driven by ∂QoI/∂geometry SENSITIVITY FIELDS (Proposal 1) mapped through a FIRST-ORDER VARIANCE PROPAGATION.
- ROBUSTNESS-CHECK with Proposal 9's cheap re-solves at SAMPLED TOLERANCE-BAND EXTREMES (first-order variance propagation is only a linearization; the extremes check catches where it lies).
- Deliverable: a GD&T SUGGESTION REPORT where EVERY loosened tolerance carries the CERTIFIED SENSITIVITY that justifies it.

## Acceptance criteria
On a fixture with a known sensitivity structure, the allocator tightens tolerances where ∂QoI/∂geometry is large and loosens them where it is small, subject to the P(in-spec) constraint; the robustness check at band extremes confirms the linearized allocation (or flags where it fails); the GD&T report attaches a certified sensitivity to each loosened tolerance.

## Testing
Property: allocated tolerances are monotone in inverse-sensitivity (loosen where insensitive); the P(in-spec) constraint holds at the sampled extremes; report completeness (no loosened tolerance without a justifying sensitivity). Falsifier: Monte-Carlo over the allocated tolerance box confirms P(in-spec) ≥ target. Logs: sensitivity fields, allocated tolerances, extreme-sample checks, GD&T report.

## Dependencies
Proposal 1 (∂QoI/∂geometry sensitivity fields — HARD); Proposal 9 (cheap robustness re-solves); reality-ingest/assimilate (the as-built loop context). The metrology-facing deliverable of Proposal 11.

title: Proposal 4 — Extend the complex into time: time slabs as cells, splitting-error in the ledger, adaptive coupling controller [gated on splitting-error demand]
description:
## What
Proposal 4 — EXTEND THE COMPLEX INTO TIME. Coupled multiphysics is glued in SPACETIME: operator splitting hands data across TEMPORAL interfaces exactly as patches hand traces across SPATIAL ones, so making time slabs CELLS OF THE COMPLEX puts splitting/coupling error in the ledger — measurable, localized to specific coupling steps, and adaptively controllable. Ranks last (Mean 590) not because wrong but because it is a REFINEMENT that pays only after strongly-coupled transient workloads are proven demand (sequencing, not merit). Phase 3 horizon, activation-gated.

## Honest scope (what this does NOT claim)
Today, splitting error is INVISIBLE in every production multiphysics code — absorbed by convention and safety factor. Visibility-plus-control is a real step. But this proposal does NOT claim coupling STABILITY: added-mass-type instabilities in fluid-structure interaction and stiff time-scale pathologies are analysis problems about the coupled PDEs, solved per-coupling, the hard way. The sheaf guarantees consistent data TRANSFER, not convergent ITERATION.

## Scope
- Time slabs as CELLS of the complex; the coupling residual on a temporal interface measured as a DEFECT against the monolithic residual over the slab.
- An ADAPTIVE CONTROLLER that subcycles or tightens coupling iterations where the TEMPORAL COCYCLE is large.
- Ledger entries PER COUPLING STEP so the budget pie (Proposal 3) can show "your error is in the FSI handoff at t ∈ [2.1, 2.3]s".
- The parallel-in-time extension (coarse temporal propagators as coarse spaces — the same H⁰ pattern as BDDC) is NOTED and EXPLICITLY DEFERRED.
- Couples to the base plan's fs-time (variational/symplectic integrators, IMEX) + fs-couple (port-Hamiltonian Dirac interconnection).

## Acceptance criteria
Splitting error appears as a per-coupling-step ledger entry and localizes to the correct temporal interval on a fixture; the adaptive controller reduces the temporal cocycle where it subcycles; the budget pie attributes error to the coupling handoff.

## Kill / activation criterion (Proposal 4 — gate ACTIVATION on demand)
Build ONLY when a paying workload's error budget is demonstrably DOMINATED by splitting error. If, after instrumenting the first coupled-transient customer problems, splitting error is <20% of budget, leave it INSTRUMENTED-BUT-UNCONTROLLED (measure it, don't build the controller).

## Testing
Property: the temporal cocycle → 0 as coupling iterations tighten (consistency); budget-pie temporal attribution correct on a seeded splitting-error-dominated fixture. G3: results invariant to slab re-partition within tolerance. Logs: per-step coupling residuals, controller decisions, temporal budget-pie.

## Dependencies
Proposal 3 (budget attribution — HARD); base plan fs-time + fs-couple + the sheaf machinery (temporal interfaces reuse the spatial restriction-map algebra). Phase 3 horizon; instrument first, control only on demand.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- No-false-stability case (honoring the no-stability-claim scope): on an added-mass-unstable FSI fixture the system surfaces non-convergence honestly and emits NO passing coupling certificate — consistent data transfer is never mistaken for convergent iteration. Boundary: a monolithic/single-physics problem yields a temporal cocycle of EXACTLY zero; the controller at maximum subcycling reports the residual honestly rather than looping.

(1) THE TEMPORAL COCYCLE: each SlabEntry carries the split step's defect against the monolithic residual over the slab (Lie splitting on the canonical coupled two-field testbed, the coupling handoff exactly as two physics codes exchange boundary data once per step); ts-001 verifies CONSISTENCY — the cocycle shrinks ~2x per subcycle doubling (first-order splitting, defects 0.064 -> 0.029 -> 0.015 -> 0.008, ledgered); (2) THE BUDGET PIE POINTED AT TIME (ts-002): on the seeded fixture whose coupling spikes only in t in [2.0, 2.5], the top defect interval lands exactly inside the spike and the spike owns >80% of the splitting-error mass — 'your error is in the coupling handoff at t in [2.0, 2.5]', localized as the acceptance demands; (3) THE ADAPTIVE CONTROLLER (ts-003, measured): subcycles concentrate where the cocycle is large (64 inside the spike vs 2 outside), every slab meets the per-slab tolerance, and the controller spends 64 substeps where the uniform march needs 512 at equal accuracy — an 8x cost win; (4) G3 REPARTITION INVARIANCE (ts-004): 8-slab vs 5-slab partitions agree within the summed ledgered defect envelope (gap 1.5e-3 vs envelope 3.2e-2) — the ledger's envelope covers exactly the drift re-partitioning introduces; (5) THE ACTIVATION GATE AS CODE (ts-005): activation_report recommends INSTRUMENT-ONLY when splitting error is <20% of the budget and flips to control-justified when it dominates — the proposal's sequencing discipline (build only on demonstrated demand) enforced by the API itself. title: ADDENDUM L2 EPISTEMIC TYPE SYSTEM: three-color ledger, objective epistemics, falsifiers, Goodhart guard, evidence packages
description:
## Mission
ADDENDUM LAYER 2 — THE EPISTEMIC TYPE SYSTEM. The discipline that prevents the certificate culture's one fatal failure mode — **being precisely wrong with a pedigree** — and then turns that discipline into the product regulators buy. A pipeline that is watertight to ε, cohomologically consistent, and interval-certified end-to-end can still compute the wrong answer with great precision, because model-form error (wrong turbulence closure, wrong material law, fictional hazard model, folklore cost spreadsheet) dominates discretization error in most industrial practice and does NOT compose algebraically. A certificate culture that is not explicit about this boundary manufactures false confidence.

## The five proposals
- **Proposal 3 — The three-color ledger** (Mean 810). Every quantity carries a color: **verified** (interval-certified numerics), **validated** (anchored to experimental data in a stated regime), or **estimated** (cross-model discrepancy probes, surrogates). Composition rules are type-checked at ledger-write time so an estimate can never be laundered into a certificate. Load-bearing schema — Phase 0 spine.
- **Proposal F — Objective epistemics** (Mean 790). The three colors, applied to the *goal itself*: loads, missions, hazards, and cost models enter as typed evidence with their own colors and validation anchors — because in "cheapest earthquake-resistant building," the structural mechanics is the easy half and the ground-motion ensemble + cost spreadsheet + loss function determine the answer. No optimization may run against an un-colored objective.
- **Proposal 6 — Falsifier pairing** (Mean 790, Pract 900). No certificate ships without an attached independent falsifier — a different algorithm on a different code path that would catch the certificate being wrong — and agents carry a falsification budget allocated by consequence×doubt. Popper as infrastructure. Phase 0 spine.
- **Proposal D — The Goodhart guard** (Mean 770, Pract 850). Treat every optimization endpoint as an adversarial example by default: designs at optimizer convergence auto-trigger escalated falsification before their certificates are honored. An agent is, in the limit, a maximally creative adjoint optimizer that will find the cracks in the model and call them design. Phase 0 spine (pure policy over existing machinery).
- **Proposal 12 — Evidence packages** (Mean 720, Ex-A 775 — top of the *sell* ranking). Export any result as a signed, machine-checkable evidence package a third party can re-verify without rerunning the pipeline; make the auditor's checker open-source. The pitch to a regulator: "don't trust us; here is the checker."

## Why this layer is the spine
Three of these (3, 6, D) plus E-tombstones and 13's type checker constitute Phase 0 — weeks-scale schema and policy work over existing machinery (Pract ≥ 800 throughout). They ship first because the flywheel's cheap, aggressive machinery is only safe *inside* a type system that refuses to launder guesses into guarantees.

## Members
color-schema (3), color-probes (3), objective-epistemics (F), falsifier-pairing (6), goodhart-guard (D), evidence-packages (12).

## Success criteria
Laundering tests pass (adversarial pipelines that try to upgrade estimated→verified fail the type check); no-falsifier-no-ship gate live; the budget pie ("where is the error budget actually spent, by color") ships on every report; the first evidence package is engaged with by an external auditor as at least supplementary evidence.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- NOTE: `add-layer:Ln` here is the addendum's THEMATIC layer (economic engine / epistemics / coupling / self-knowledge / GTM), NOT the base L0–L6 architecture stack. Member crates still sit at their true base layer and must respect lower-knows-nothing-of-higher dependency direction.

SUCCESS CRITERIA VERIFIED BY RE-RUNNING THE SUITES NOW: (1) LAUNDERING TESTS PASS — three independent batteries all green this minute: the spine gate (fs-probe, 5 tests: estimated->verified refused with teaching text), the fs-epi-e2e suite (7 tests), and my ledger-sink battery (fs-checker epi_e2e: write-gate refusal + regime auto-demotion + signed-waiver provenance); (2) NO-FALSIFIER-NO-SHIP GATE LIVE — fs-evidence falsify suite green (12 unit + conformance): unpaired classes blocked by name, the standard registry pairs six certificate classes including adjoint-gradient, budget allocator monotone in consequence x doubt with cold-start max-doubt; (3) THE BUDGET PIE SHIPS ON REPORTS — fs-probe BudgetPie renders error-by-color with the operator verdict (the 'refining the mesh will NOT help' teaching line) and the solver-free checker renders it from evidence packages independently; (4) the fourth criterion (an external auditor engaging the first evidence package) is a REAL-WORLD milestone outside the repo — the machinery for it is complete (signed Merkle bundles, the open checker, the regulatory crosswalk) and the criterion transfers to commercial governance (jwq8/xpck tracking).
