title: Proposal 7 — Plugin surface: restriction-map SDK w/ sheaf-axiom-generated conformance suite (functoriality/adjoint-consistency/MMS) + tiered converter certification
description:
## What
Proposal 7's PLUGIN SURFACE — turn the architecture's WEAKEST POINT into its ECOSYSTEM PLAY. The RESTRICTION-MAP LAYER is where the hard engineering hides: the sheaf organizes bookkeeping GIVEN trace/conversion operators and will FAITHFULLY PROPAGATE GARBAGE WITH CERTIFICATES ATTACHED if those operators are bad (risk R6). So specify it as an SDK whose CONFORMANCE SUITE IS AUTO-GENERATED FROM THE SHEAF AXIOMS.

## Scope
- Specify the restriction-map layer as an SDK: third parties ship CONVERTERS (chart-to-chart trace/conversion operators — the Rep Router edges).
- CONFORMANCE SUITE auto-generated from the sheaf axioms:
  1. FUNCTORIALITY (composition, identity).
  2. ADJOINT CONSISTENCY (against Proposal 1 — the converter's transpose must be the adjoint the ledger uses).
  3. TOLERANCE HONESTY via MANUFACTURED SOLUTIONS with KNOWN interface traces (the converter's declared error model must not lie).
- The Gauntlet CERTIFIES converters into TIERS; certified converters carry their TIER in EVERY ledger entry they touch. The architecture's most dangerous dependency becomes its NETWORK EFFECT.
- R6 mitigation: apply this conformance suite to FIRST-PARTY converters with the SAME SEVERITY as third-party ones.

## Acceptance criteria
The SDK spec + auto-generated conformance suite exist; a converter is certified into a tier only by passing functoriality + adjoint-consistency + manufactured-solution tolerance-honesty tests; the tier is stamped on every ledger entry the converter touches; first-party converters run the identical suite; a deliberately dishonest converter (understated error model) FAILS tolerance honesty.

## Kill criterion
Inherits Proposal 7's commercial gate (wedge-selection). For the plugin surface specifically, R6's early warning is the CONFORMANCE-TIER DISTRIBUTION of converters on the hot path — if hot-path converters cluster in low tiers, restriction-map quality is the bottleneck.

## Testing
Auto-generated conformance suite IS the test: functoriality (composition/identity laws), adjoint consistency vs Proposal 1, MMS tolerance honesty. Adversarial: a garbage converter with a lying error model must fail. Logs: converter tier assignments, conformance-test results, hot-path tier distribution (R6 early warning).

## Dependencies
Bet 11 sheaf axioms (base plan fs-geom) + the Rep Router converter registry (base plan morph); Proposal 1 (adjoint consistency). Owns risk R6. Sibling to wedge-selection. Amends the base plan (restriction-map SDK + tiered converter certification as named components).

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- Tiers: functoriality (composition/identity) -> G0; MMS tolerance-honesty -> G1; dishonest-converter (understated error model) rejection -> G4 adversarial.

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Add the adjoint-consistency conformance test named in Scope but missing from Testing: a certified converter's transpose EQUALS the adjoint the ledger uses (against Proposal 1) — a converter that is functorial but adjoint-inconsistent silently corrupts every gradient routed through it. Optimality: encode BOTH accuracy AND cost in the converter tier so the Rep Router can route by tier.

title: Proposal 7 — WEDGE-VERTICAL BENCHMARK & TRACE CORPUS + kill-measurement harness (the shared artifact 6+ kill criteria measure against)
description:
## What
The WEDGE-VERTICAL BENCHMARK & TRACE CORPUS — the single shared, versioned, deterministic artifact that MANY addendum kill criteria measure against. Per Governance Rule 2 (doctrine), "a proposal whose kill measurement was never instrumented counts as killed" — so this corpus is what keeps at least SIX proposals from being killed-by-default for lack of an instrument.

## Why it must be its own bead
The following kill/exit measurements all reference "the wedge vertical's benchmark set / benchmark design tasks / recorded traces / swarm concurrency trials," yet no other bead owns the artifact:
- Proposal 8 planner ≥2× vs baseline on the query set (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.16).
- Proposal 1 adjoint beats derivative-free on ≥70% of benchmark design tasks (frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.1).
- Proposal A RB coverage ≥20% of wedge query volume (frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.4).
- Proposal 2 skip-yield ≥2× vs hash memoization on realistic edit traces (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.8).
- Proposal D guard catch-rate on endpoints vs random designs (frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.5).
- Proposal F robust-vs-nominal dominated-design check on the first vertical's set (frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.3).
- Proposal 9 accept-rate + warm-start on the elliptic/FEEC battery; Proposal 10 harmonic-conflict rate on swarm merge trials; Proposal E re-exploration rate.

## Scope
- **Conjugate-heat-transfer (electronics cooling) query set**: a fixed, versioned menu of design queries (QoIs, tolerances, budgets) with (a) reference CERTIFIED answers and (b) reference compute costs.
- **Benchmark design-task set** for optimizer comparison (adjoint vs CMA-ES/BO; Prop 1/D).
- **Recorded agent design-iteration EDIT TRACES** with known-correct skip sets (Prop 2 kill measurement).
- **Swarm-concurrency merge-trial harness** producing the harmonic-conflict-rate measurement (Prop 10 kill measurement).
- **Elliptic/FEEC MMS battery** with high-precision reference (Prop 9 verifier).
- Everything seeded + deterministic so measurements are replayable (couples to the base plan's Gauntlet G1/G2 registries + fs-roofline).

## Acceptance criteria
The corpus exists as a versioned artifact; every kill-measurement bead above can compute its number against it; reference answers carry their color; the harness is deterministic (bit-stable measurements across runs).

## Testing
G1 (MMS in the battery), G2 (canonical benchmark envelopes), G5 (deterministic measurement replay). The corpus IS a test artifact; its own test is that reference answers are stable and each consumer's kill metric is computable. Detailed logging: per-query reference answer + cost + color; per-trace known skip set.

## Dependencies
frankensim-epic-gtm-jwq8.1 (defines the CHT vertical + cycle-time baseline); base plan Gauntlet G1/G2 + fs-roofline. Feeds the Phase-1 and Phase-2 milestones and the six kill-measurement beads above.

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Corpus-completeness self-test (mirror in Acceptance): an executable check enumerates each consumer kill-metric (Prop 8 planner query set, Prop 1/D benchmark design tasks, Prop A RB-coverage query volume, Prop 2 edit traces with known skip sets, Prop 9 elliptic/FEEC MMS + high-precision oracle, Prop 10 swarm-merge-trial harness, Prop E re-exploration traces, Prop F robust-vs-nominal seismic set) and FAILS if any required fixture class is absent (an incomplete corpus kills those proposals by default). Reference answers record their oracle provenance (how the high-precision reference was computed), not only their color.

title: L6 HELM: orchestration, ledger, and agent interface
description:
## Mission
L6 HELM: orchestration, sessions, and the agent interface. Everything below is callable; HELM makes it programmable, replayable, and governable — for AI agents first, humans equally. This is where P4 (budgets), P9 (provenance), and P10 (agent-first) become running code.

## Core components (plan §11 + patch Rev B)
- FrankenScript IR: THE canonical interface — a typed, versioned intermediate representation with two isomorphic syntaxes (canonical s-expressions + lossless JSON) parsing to one typed AST. Static admission before execution: dimensional analysis in the type system, chart-compatibility via Rep Router, budget feasibility against learned cost models, capability sufficiency. Ill-typed studies rejected in milliseconds with structured diagnoses, not discovered at hour six.
- The Design Ledger (Bet 10): FrankenSQLite as system of record — content-addressed artifacts, event-sourced ops, lineage edges, metrics, autotune cache, session events. Time travel, forkable worlds, and explain() are nearly free because sessions are event-sourced over content-addressed state. A six-month campaign is a database you query, not a directory you fear.
- Evidence/Model Ledger (patch Rev B): Evidence<T> carries numerical + statistical + MODEL-FORM certificates, sensitivity, validity domain, and decision status; model cards for every solver/closure/material law. The system must be able to say "mesh error 0.7%, turbulence-model discrepancy 8–15%, ranking not decision-grade."
- Sessions & capability tokens: budgets ENFORCED not advisory; idempotency keys; estimate() dry runs; errors-as-guidance with ranked fixes ("a refusal that teaches is worth ten silent successes").
- The self-optimizing pipeline (Bet 12): Error Ledger + Time Ledger compose per-operator error/cost models end-to-end; the planner allocates error budget across mesh/order/tolerance/surrogate/samples to maximize accuracy-per-second.
- Five Explicits everywhere: units, seeds, budgets, versions, capabilities — an agent literally cannot express an ambiguous request.

## Members
fs-ledger-core, evidence-model-ledger, ledger-timetravel, fs-ir-core, fs-ir-admission, fs-ir-catalog, fs-session-caps, fs-plan-models, fs-plan-allocator, fs-report, helm-e2e.

## Success Criteria
IR round-trips; admission rejects with teaching errors; ledger survives kill -9 mid-sweep; time-travel replay is bit-exact in deterministic mode; conversational latency ≤100 ms while campaigns saturate the throughput lane.

title: fs-ledger core: Design Ledger schema v0 + extension tables, BLAKE3-class content addressing, WAL/snapshot contract
description:
## What
`fs-ledger` core: the Design Ledger v0 on FrankenSQLite (plan §11.2, Bet 10) — the system of record that makes a six-month campaign a database you query, not a directory you fear.

## Scope
- Schema v0 (STRICT tables, Appendix D): **artifacts** (content-addressed typed blobs — charts, fields, meshes, fronts, images; identical results dedupe to one row forever), **ops** (event-sourced log: every executed IR node with its FROZEN Five Explicits — seeds, versions, budgets, capabilities — plus timing and outcome), **edges** (lineage DAG: op→artifact in/out roles), **metrics** (time series: residuals, e-values, objective traces, ledger balances, roofline attainment), **tune** (autotuner cache keyed kernel × shape-class × machine fingerprint), **events** (fine-grained session stream: tile completions, cancellations, preemptions — powers dashboards and post-hoc flame graphs).
- Extension tables (patch Rev S, added EARLY even if initially sparse): **requirements**, **model_cards**, **evidence**, **scenarios**, **constraints**, **capability_probes**, **imports**, **unsafe_capsules**.
- Content addressing: in-house BLAKE3-class tree hash (P1: in-house); streaming + chunked for multi-GiB fields; hash = artifact identity everywhere.
- Concurrency contract: WAL mode; snapshot-isolated readers so dashboards/agents query freely WHILE a 96-core sweep writes; append-heavy write path batched on the latency lane; predictable checkpointing mid-sweep (the §12 FrankenSQLite contract — we return a punishing OLTP+blob stress suite upstream).
- One file per project; crash safety = WAL recovery invariants tested by kill -9 storms (G4 class).

## Acceptance criteria
Schema migrations versioned; hash dedupe verified (same artifact bytes → one row across forks); concurrent reader/writer stress (sweep-writer + N snapshot readers) green; kill -9 mid-transaction recovery leaves consistent state (no partial ops, orphan edges lintable→zero).

## Testing
Unit: DDL/round-trips per table; property: content-hash stability + collision sanity; crash-recovery battery with random kill points (detailed logs: kill offset, recovery verdict, invariant checks); throughput benchmarks (events/sec sustained during synthetic sweeps) ledgered as its own metric.

## ADDENDUM AMENDMENT (COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md)
The Design Ledger schema is EXTENDED by the addendum's flywheel + epistemic layers. New first-class fields on ledger nodes:
- **`slack`** = `required_tolerance − achieved_error` per node — the resource Proposal 2's tolerance-aware incremental recompute spends (see frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.6).
- **`color`** ∈ {verified, validated, estimated} on every node, with color-specific payloads, type-checked at write time (Proposal 3, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.1).
- Solve nodes gain **`(proposer_id, accepted, bound, iterations_saved)`** for certified-speculation telemetry (Proposal 9, frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.3) — simultaneously the surrogate training signal, the query planner's cost model, and the drift detector.
- Content addressing + the forkable-worlds machinery become the substrate for version control for physics (Proposal 10, frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.9) and re-verifiable evidence packages (Proposal 12, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.6). Pinning: artifacts referenced by an evidence package or a contract are never evicted.

title: fs-session governor: contain submit panics and reject invalid budget values
description:
## Defect
`Governor::submit_once` inserts `IdemState::Pending` before invoking caller work outside the mutex. If that closure panics, no code transitions the key or notifies the condition variable, so every duplicate submission blocks forever. Separately, `open_session` and `charge` accept NaN, infinity, and negative floating-point grants/deltas. NaN makes all enforcement comparisons false; negative deltas refund consumption. The exact-grant boundary also contradicts the documented at-grant throttle rule.

## Scope
- Add a structured terminal idempotency state for panicked work and guarantee all waiters are notified. Preserve panic containment: no unwind escapes `submit_once`; the owning call and all duplicates receive the same structured failure receipt/outcome, with no charge. Define explicit retry semantics rather than leaving a permanent pending entry.
- Validate capability-token floating grants (`core_s`, `wall_s`, `cores`) at session opening and reject non-finite or negative values.
- Validate charge deltas (`core_s`, `wall_s`) and reject non-finite or negative values before mutating meters.
- Enforce/document the exact grant boundary consistently.
- Keep edits limited to fs-session governor API, contract, and conformance tests.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A deterministic multi-thread regression starts one panicking owner plus duplicate waiters; all calls finish within a bounded timeout, work executes once, no waiter remains blocked, the same failure receipt is observed, and meters remain unchanged.
2. NaN, +/-infinity, and negative grants/deltas are structured errors and cannot mutate meters or poison later valid enforcement.
3. A charge landing exactly on a grant yields the documented throttle verdict; past 1.2x yields pause.
4. Focused fs-session tests and clippy pass through RCH; ubs reports no unresolved true positives.

## Root cause and non-goals
The root cause is an incomplete Pending/Done state machine with no unwind finalizer plus unvalidated raw f64 resource values. Do not redesign fs-exec, fs-race, the degradation ladder, cross-process idempotency reconstruction, or ledger persistence in this bead.
close_reason: Governor submission, budget arithmetic, idempotency waiters, and pressure cancellation are panic-total, atomic, and covered by the focused conformance and clippy lanes.

title: fs-session: bind memory-pressure actions to owned session gates
description:
apply_memory_pressure accepts any optional CancelGate separately from SessionId, accepts levels outside 1..=3, and records PauseSerializeResume even when gate is None or belongs to another session. The ledger can therefore claim a pause request that never reached the affected computation, or cancel unrelated work.

Root cause: the governor stores session tokens and meters but not the session cancellation capability; enforcement authority and attribution are passed independently.

Repair: bind an owned/registered session gate or scoped cancellation capability at session open; pressure actions resolve it by SessionId. Reject invalid levels; do not emit a successful pause event unless the correct gate was requested and an acknowledgement/checkpoint receipt follows. Model failure as a structured event/no-claim.

Acceptance: None and wrong-session gates are unrepresentable or refused; levels 0 and >3 fail; level 3 requests only the target session; event identity matches the requested gate; missing checkpoint acknowledgement cannot be reported as PauseSerializeResume complete.
close_reason: Repair shipped (361bb36 — my working tree swept into the tree-sweeper's commit; diff-verified identical). DESIGN: the session's cancellation capability is BOUND AT OPEN (open_session_gated stores Arc<CancelGate> keyed by session id) and level-3 pressure resolves it by SessionId — no gate crosses apply_memory_pressure's API anymore, so None/wrong-session gates went from accepted parameters to UNREPRESENTABLE. Acceptance items, each gated in the new ss-011 battery + updated ss-005: (1) levels 0 and >3 -> Err(InvalidPressureLevel), refused never clamped, nothing ledgered; (2) level 3 on an ungated session -> Err(UngatedSession) ATOMICALLY (gate resolved before any ladder step fires: no partial spill/coarsen, no events; levels 1-2 stay gate-free since spill/coarsen are synchronous); (3) level 3 requests ONLY the target session's gate (two-session isolation gated: B's gate stays un-requested); (4) event identity: the pause event is emitted with new phase=Requested and the pending request is keyed by session; (5) missing checkpoint acknowledgement can never read as complete — phase=Complete exists ONLY via acknowledge_pause(session, receipt) which refuses blank receipts (pending claim preserved), refuses sessions with no outstanding request (NoPendingPause), consumes the claim (double-ack refused), and cites the acknowledged request's ordinal in its attribution; ledger payloads now carry phase so the stream is auditable for unacknowledged Completes. Three new structured SessionError variants with teaching Display text. Lanes: cargo test -p fs-session 11/11 green (incl new battery), clippy --all-targets 0, fmt; xtask check-all: fs-session clean (the single workspace violation is fs-simd/neon 410>300 lines — collaborator's in-flight capsule, flagged on 9ekv); ubs: criticals are the file's PRE-EXISTING poisoned-lock .expect convention (line 225 untouched original) + a 'secret' heuristic false-positive on the identifier 'token' — none introduced by this change.

title: Canonical replay identity: hash every semantic field and version the schema
description:
Fresh-eyes failures exposed replay identities that cover only selected outputs or use unversioned ad hoc encodings. The missed fs-cheb and flagship downstream golden updates are concrete evidence: arithmetic schedule changes propagated through semantic consumers, but no dependency-aware identity audit named every affected artifact. Similar under-binding can make distinct plans, certificates, snapshots, or evidence packages share an identity.

Define a versioned canonical identity schema for replay-bearing artifacts. Inventory every identity producer and classify each field as semantic, provenance-only, or deliberately excluded. Semantic inputs include algorithm and schema versions, deterministic mode, full logical RNG identity, machine/ISA class where the claim requires it, budgets and units, representation choices, ordered operation parameters, certificate regimes, parent artifact roots, and relevant dependency implementation identities. Use typed length-prefixed encodings rather than delimiter concatenation.

Acceptance: field-mutation coverage proves every semantic field changes the root and every excluded field is documented; unknown schema versions fail closed; dependency changes identify all downstream goldens requiring re-verification; collision/adversarial delimiter tests pass; cross-ISA claims either reproduce or carry an explicit platform-scoped no-claim.
close_reason: Canonical replay identity delivered across 4 segments; all acceptance criteria met. SCHEMA (s1): fs_obs::ident — versioned (IDENT_SCHEMA_VERSION, framed into the root), typed (tag byte per field: str/u64/i64/f64-bits/bytes/child/flag — type confusion changes the root), length-prefixed (key and value), with child() binding parent/dependency roots and exclude() recording provenance-only fields in an auditable list; canonical_bytes() exposed so stronger digests can bind the same encoding. ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE: (a) field-mutation coverage — ident-001/002 prove every semantic field (incl kind and child roots) moves the root, all mutants pairwise distinct, replay bit-stable, and documented exclusions never move it; (b) unknown schema versions FAIL CLOSED — check_version refuses past and future versions (ident-006); (c) dependency->downstream-golden identification — child() propagation gated (ident-005) AND interlocked with y4pt's golden-couplings.json: the flagship metric-stream encoding is a registered SURFACE (METRIC_STREAM_ENCODING_VERSION) with 4 dependent golden rows, so an encoding change fails xtask until every dependent is deliberately re-frozen — the fs-cheb/flagship silent-propagation incident class is now structurally impossible; (d) collision/adversarial tests — split, delimiter-injection, key/value-boundary, empty-vs-absent, type-confusion, order, -0.0/NaN cases all gated (ident-003/004) plus the fs-report render-collision pair; (e) cross-ISA — verified on ts2/x86-64 vs M4/aarch64: exposed the ornith roa libm divergence, carried an explicit platform-scoped envelope no-claim citing bead 6ure, and the root fix (fs-bem det:: routing, closed by collaborator) restored cross-ISA reproduction. INVENTORY (s3): all 35 producer files classified by encoding class and exposure; 3 HIGH migrated (fs-substrate CapabilityProbe::fingerprint — persisted machine identity off '|'-joins; fs-report LabNotebook::content_hash — non-injective rendered-markdown hash replaced by structural hash with the adversarial pair gated; fs-thrust-e2e by delegation); s2 migrated fs-evidence ProvenanceHash::chain and fs-flagship-e2e content_hash (4 goldens re-frozen with justifications, metric bits verified unchanged); s4 migrated fs-dfo steer fingerprint (raw-concat section-boundary gap). Remaining MEDIUMs documented as accepted no-claims (numeric-delimiter or self-compared only). title: Roofline staleness must reverify an ordered run manifest
description: Current validate_roofline_row checks each row params, payload artifact, edge, op, build, measured prefix, and reps, but it cannot reconstruct the finalized run receipt from an operation-bound ordered result set. A writer with Ledger APIs can replace one result payload and matching artifact/params while retaining the old run receipt, allowing staleness to classify altered evidence as Fresh. Acceptance: add a versioned op-bound ordered result manifest with kernel/version/ordinal/payload hashes; bind it into the finalized receipt and operation; make staleness recompute and compare the full receipt; reject missing, duplicated, reordered, added, removed, or altered rows as CorruptEvidence; migrate the row schema explicitly; add adversarial tamper tests and preserve valid identical-rerun history.

title: Make VCS identity ledger- and branch-safe
description: The VCS registry is keyed by semantic root alone while CommitInfo and ViewSnapshot carry branch-local and ledger-local identities. Equal roots can overwrite branch metadata, and checkout_delta compares local operation ids that are not portable across ledger instances, so cross-ledger equality and deltas can be false. Acceptance: separate semantic-state identity from commit/envelope identity; scope or key commit lookup by ledger and branch identity; compute cross-ledger deltas from stable semantic leaf identities rather than local row ids; preserve deterministic merge ancestry; add same-root/different-branch, independent-ledger, reordered-import, collision, and replay tests.
close_reason: VCS identity is now ledger- and branch-safe (CloudyFinch). MECHANISM (fs-ledger/src/vcs.rs): (1) SEMANTIC vs ENVELOPE identity separated — the Merkle root stays the semantic-state identity; the commit envelope is CommitId{ledger, branch, root}, where the ledger identity is PERSISTED on first use as a vcs-identity event (domain-hashed path+mint-time; copies share it — same lineage; independent databases differ; first-event-by-rowid is the authority under concurrent minting). (2) The registry, heads, lookup, and checkout are envelope-keyed: equal semantic roots from an undiverged fork or an independent ledger COEXIST instead of overwriting each other's branch metadata; lookup_semantic enumerates all envelopes sharing a root; checkout is envelope-scoped because snapshots carry ledger-local op ids. (3) checkout_delta no longer compares local row ids: it diffs SEMANTIC LEAF MULTISETS (commit_leaf hashes, portable across ledger instances and import orders) and reports DeltaOp{leaf, local_op} with each side's own local id — cross-ledger equality and deltas cannot be false from rowid drift. Doctrine documented: root binds history SEQUENCE, delta binds the SET (reordered import: different root, empty semantic frontier). (4) merge_views/storage_audit/GC untouched — deterministic merge ancestry preserved (vc_004 green unchanged). REGRESSION EVIDENCE (closure lint): tests/vcs.rs vc_008 (same-root/different-branch collision: both envelopes retrievable with their own branch metadata, branch-scoped heads, envelope-scoped checkout, deterministic fresh-registry replay) and vc_009 (independent-ledger + reordered-import: distinct persisted identities, different sequence-bound roots, EMPTY semantic delta where the old id-based diff reported a phantom frontier; real divergence reports the target-local op id bound to its portable leaf) — plus vc_001..007 updated to the scoped API and green. Full fs-ledger: 87 tests, 0 failures (incl. the colors lane's col_015/016 which landed mid-verify and pass); clippy clean in vcs regions; CONTRACT.md vcs section rewritten with the envelope-vs-semantic doctrine. No external consumers existed (verified by workspace grep), so the API break is contained.

title: Define order-independent artifact metadata collision semantics
description: Artifact identity is currently a bytes-only content hash, while kind and metadata are stored on the same row. title: fs-evidence: Evidence<T>/Certified<T> types, composition algebra, model cards + discrepancy/bracketing/escalation
description:
## What
`Evidence<T>` and the Model Ledger (patch Rev B): broaden `Certified<T>` beyond numerical enclosure so the biggest REAL design-error source — model-form uncertainty — is carried inside values, not left in engineers' heads.

## Why (the core argument)
Without this, FrankenSim can produce beautifully certified WRONG answers: mesh error 0.7%, algebraic residual irrelevant — but turbulence-closure discrepancy 8–15%, so the design ranking is not decision-grade. Being able to SAY that sentence is the difference between a solver and an engineering-intelligence system. Named model-form risks: LES closure adequacy, contact-line behavior (vessel flagship), constitutive-law calibration vs actual construction (frame flagship), surrogate out-of-distribution failure, ground-motion model assumptions.

## Scope
- Core types in a LOW-LAYER crate (fs-evidence, usable by L1+ without layer violations): `Evidence<T> { value, numerical: NumericalCertificate, statistical: StatisticalCertificate, model: ModelEvidence, sensitivity: SensitivitySummary, provenance: ProvenanceHash, validity_domain: ValidityDomain, decision_status: DecisionStatus }`. `Certified<T>` = Evidence<T> with a strong numerical certificate + explicit model evidence (type alias + constructor discipline; plan Appendix B's Certified fields — value + interval bound + provenance + adjoint hook — remain intact as the numerical slice).
- Composition algebra: combining Evidence through operations composes certificates conservatively (numerical bounds compose per fs-ivl; statistical per e-value arithmetic; model evidence composes as validity-domain intersection + assumption union) — the machinery the Error Ledger (fs-plan-models) attributes from.
- Model cards (ledger `model_cards` table): for EVERY solver/closure/constitutive law — assumptions, validity domain, known failures, calibration artifacts, promotion level [S]/[F]/[M].
- Four model-form mechanisms: model cards; DISCREPANCY MODELS between fidelity levels trained on ledger data; MODEL BRACKETING for weakly-understood physics (e.g., bracketing contact-angle models, reporting the objective's sensitivity band rather than pretending certainty — exactly the vessel flagship's stated mitigation); DECISION-AWARE ESCALATION (HELM escalates fidelity when MODEL uncertainty, not numerical, dominates the pending decision).
- `evidence` ledger table rows for artifacts.

## Acceptance criteria
Evidence composition laws under G0 (conservativeness: composed validity ⊆ intersection; composed bounds ⊇ true propagation); model cards mandatory at solver registration (lint: a FLUX solver without a card cannot register); a worked end-to-end example where model discrepancy dominates and decision_status correctly reports not-decision-grade.

## Testing
Property tests on composition algebra; serialization round-trips to ledger tables; integration test: two-fidelity discrepancy model trained on synthetic ledger data flags an out-of-domain query. Logs: full evidence trees rendered per artifact (the explain() payload).

## ADDENDUM AMENDMENT (COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md)
The three-color type system (Proposal 3, frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.1) is the TYPE-LEVEL SURFACE of this crate's ModelEvidence / validity-domain machinery: **verified** = a strong numerical (interval) certificate; **validated** = model evidence anchored to experimental data within a declared regime tag; **estimated** = discrepancy-probe / surrogate evidence. The composition algebra here must implement the addendum's laundering-refusal rules (validated auto-demotes to estimated on regime exit; anything ⊕ estimated → estimated). Objective ingredients (loads/hazards/costs) become colored Evidence artifacts under Proposal F (frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.3); gradients become colored Evidence under Proposal 1 (frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.3).
close_reason: Implemented fs-evidence (UTIL layer per the bead scope's explicit low-layer requirement; label said L6 — scope text overrides so L1+ can consume without violations). Core: Evidence<T>/Certified<T> with the four uncertainty slices — NumericalCertificate (Exact/Enclosure/Estimate/NoClaim severity order; plan Appendix B fields intact incl. adjoint hook), StatisticalCertificate (None/EValue/HalfWidth), ModelEvidence (cards, assumption union, validity intersection, additive discrepancy bands, in_domain conjunction), SensitivitySummary. Conservative composition algebra (combine over Add/Sub/Mul/Min/Max): outward-rounded interval composition never claiming Exact after float ops, NoClaim absorption, order-sensitive provenance chaining — G0 conservativeness proven over 300k seeded samples (evd-001). Certified discipline: certified() refuses Estimate-tainted chains and out-of-domain model use with structured CertifyError (evd-006 poisoning law). Model cards + ModelRegistry with THE lint: solver without a card cannot register (evd-002). DiscrepancyModel: two-fidelity fit (observed box + mean/max band) whose query/evidence_at REFUSE out-of-distribution points naming the violated parameter (evd-004, 50-pair synthetic corpus). ModelBracket: contact-angle-style bracketing -> enclosure spanning members + spread as model band (vessel flagship mitigation, evd-005). assess()/UncertaintyBreakdown/escalation_advice: worked example lands the core argument — mesh 0.7% + stat 0.5% + LES closure 10% at 5% threshold -> NotDecisionGrade dominant=model-form with teaching detail + EscalateModelFidelity; calibrated 2% closure flips to DecisionGrade (evd-003). Ledger evidence/model_cards rows canonical + fs-obs-validated. Lanes green: check, clippy -D warnings, fmt, fs-evidence 12 lib + 6 conformance, workspace 61 suites, xtask 0 violations (18 crates), ubs 0 criticals. No-claims: statistical composition conservative-weakest until fs-eproc; discrepancy models are bookkeeping not learning (FrankenTorch later); adjoint composition is fs-ad's; ledger persistence is row rendering until fs-ledger tables.

title: fs-evidence: make Certified opaque and enforce certificate invariants
description:
Fresh-eyes audit found that Certified<T> is a public type alias for Evidence<T>, every Evidence field is public, and certified() checks only NumericalKind plus model.in_domain. Callers can construct or mutate a nominally Certified value with forged certificate fields. Evidence::exact accepts non-finite values, and enclosed does not require finite ordered bounds or prove that qoi/value lies inside the enclosure.

Root cause: certification is represented by constructor convention rather than an unforgeable type and validated invariant boundary.

Repair: replace the alias with an opaque Certified<T> newtype or equivalent private-state representation; centralize checked construction; prevent post-certification mutation from weakening evidence; validate finite exact values, finite ordered enclosures, and scalar containment. Keep explicit escape hatches as unsafe-to-claim Evidence or structured NoClaim, never as Certified.

Acceptance: compile-fail or API tests prove direct forging is impossible; NaN, infinity, inverted bounds, and out-of-enclosure qoi are refused; legitimate exact/enclosure composition remains usable; G0 adversarial constructors and serialization round trips preserve invariants; contract states the trust boundary and migration.
close_reason: Shipped (d0c1e09, swept — diff-verified identical to my tree; pushed). Certified<T> went from 'pub type Certified<T> = Evidence<T>' (certification by constructor convention, forgeable via literal construction or field mutation) to an OPAQUE newtype: private inner Evidence, reads via Deref<Target=Evidence<T>> with NO DerefMut, .evidence() borrow, and .into_evidence() as the explicit downgrade that surrenders the mark — re-certification re-validates, which IS the reconstruction round-trip guarantee (crate has no serializer; stated in CONTRACT). Evidence::certified() is now the FULL validation boundary and validates the ACTUAL numbers rather than trusting the constructor that claimed them: Exact requires finite qoi with BIT-identical bounds (to_bits — fail-closed on -0.0 edge); Enclosure requires finite ordered bounds CONTAINING the qoi; Estimate/NoClaim -> NotRigorous; out-of-domain -> OutOfDomain. Five new structured CertifyError variants (ExactNotFinite, ExactInconsistent, NonFiniteBounds, InvertedBounds, QoiOutsideEnclosure) each carrying the offending numbers with teaching Display; Eq dropped (f64 payloads), Copy+PartialEq retained — grep confirmed no external consumer used Eq. ACCEPTANCE: evd-012 G0 adversarial battery — exact(NaN)/exact(inf), hand-built Exact with contradicting bounds, hand-built inverted/NaN/infinite enclosures, and qoi-outside-enclosure ALL refused with their structured reason; rigorous exact*enclosure composition still certifies and reads flow through the immutable Deref view; downgrade-mutate-recertify refuses both weakened kind and drifted qoi. Direct forging is impossible at the API level (private field, no mutable access — the only door is certified()). MIGRATION: exactly one workspace site moved a field out of a certified value (fs-geom conformance test — now explicit into_evidence); all other consumers (fs-geom Convert trait + router, fs-rep-mesh, fs-recompute, fs-ornith, e2e crates) compile unchanged via Deref — verified by cargo check --all-targets across all of them. CONTRACT.md invariant 8 states the trust boundary + migration. Lanes: fs-evidence 28 tests green across 4 targets incl new battery, clippy --all-targets 0, fmt; xtask check-all 0 violations (125 crates). Coordination note: wa8i's follow-on commit 049538f (fs-sos separating algebraic verification from certified bounds) landed on top of this boundary within the hour — the opaque type is already load-bearing.

title: Preserve exact integer Count literals through admission and enforcement
description: Count.value is f64, so integer byte literals above 2^53 can round before fs-session converts a validated memory budget to u64. The governor enforces its CapabilityToken exactly, but source asks and replay identities can no longer distinguish adjacent large integer quantities. Acceptance: represent integral Count values with an exact integer form (or retain canonical source digits plus checked conversion); define fractional count semantics separately; make unit scaling checked in u128/u64; bind the exact quantity into canonical IR and ledger identities; reject overflow before rounding; add 2^53±1, u64::MAX, 2^64, fractional-byte, unit-scale overflow, round-trip, and replay tests; migrate admission/session without weakening the f64 quantity path.
close_reason: Shipped 2d38567, pushed. ROOT CAUSE closed: NodeKind::Count carried f64, so integer byte literals above 2^53 rounded at PARSE — before admission or the governor ever saw them — making adjacent large integers indistinguishable in source asks and every identity derived from them. DESIGN: CountValue::{Exact(u128), Fractional(f64)} — bare integer literals are EXACT (the common '96GiB'-class grants all take this path); decimal/exponent forms are explicitly Fractional with SEPARATELY DEFINED semantics per the acceptance: fine for 1.5GiB-class asks (still converts exactly: 3<<29 bytes), refused wherever integrality above 2^53 would have to be assumed. CHECKED SCALING: byte conversion is u128 checked_shl + fit-into-u64, refusing overflow BEFORE any rounding; beyond-u128 literals are a structured PARSE refusal (teaching hint), never saturation. IDENTITY BINDING: canonical sexpr AND JSON printers emit exact digits verbatim (the JSON path initially debug-printed the new enum — caught by the existing isomorphism property test, which is exactly what property tests are for); semantic equality compares Exact-vs-Exact by value, Fractional by bit pattern, and treats mixed written forms (2B vs 2.0B) as DISTINCT claims — written-form fidelity for replay identities. CONSUMERS routed through the exact path: fs-ir admission count_bytes (mem-grant validation + projection sites) and fs-session estimate's budget-to-u64 conversion (the exact site the bead named). ACCEPTANCE BATTERY (ir_0xx, green): 2^53 vs 2^53+1 distinct through equality, both canonical syntaxes, and lossless round trips; u64::MAX B admits, 2^64 B refuses; GiB boundary (2^34-1 GiB fits exactly, 2^34 GiB refuses); 2^128 parse refusal; fractional-semantics separation incl big-fractional refusal; mixed-form distinctness. title: fs-ledger time travel: at(t) replay, forkable worlds (hash-shared branches), explain() causal trees
description:
## What
Ledger time travel, forkable worlds, and explain() (plan §11.2): the three expensive-sounding features that become NEARLY FREE because sessions are event-sourced over content-addressed state.

## Scope
- TIME TRAVEL: `at(t)` replays the op log to any instant — materialized state views at historical points; requires deterministic replay semantics (ExecMode recorded per op; replays of Deterministic ops must reproduce artifact hashes EXACTLY, replay of Fast ops re-executes with documented divergence class).
- FORKABLE WORLDS: a fork is a new BRANCH of the op log sharing every artifact by hash — an agent speculatively explores three formulations for the cost of the deltas; branch bookkeeping (parent op, divergence point), merge-view queries (compare branches), garbage-collection policy respecting all live branches (content addressing makes sharing safe).
- `explain(artifact)`: walk `edges` backward and render the FULL CAUSAL TREE — which chart, which mesh, which seed, which solver tolerances, which library versions (constellation lock hash) produced this number; output as structured data + human-readable rendering (fs-report); depth/filter controls for enormous trees.
- Replay validation: replay-vs-original hash comparison as a first-class audit (the G5-at-study-scale primitive; golden ledgers in CI use exactly this).
- Interactive steering integration: MOO's fork-on-reweight lands here (a steering event = fork op).

## Acceptance criteria
Replay of a deterministic fixture study reproduces every artifact hash; forks share artifacts (storage audit: N forks ≈ 1× artifacts + deltas); explain() reconstructs known lineage on fixture campaigns completely (no orphan inputs); at(t) views consistent at arbitrary interior instants (including mid-sweep points).

## Testing
Property: fork independence (ops on branch A never affect branch B's views); replay determinism battery; explain() completeness lint (every artifact reachable from a study is explainable). Crash-interaction: kill -9 during fork creation leaves both branches consistent (G4-class). Logs: replay verdicts, branch trees, lineage renderings.
close_reason: Time travel, forkable worlds, explain(), replay audit, and GC landed as fs-ledger's travel module on schema v2 — the first real migration through the versioned ladder (branches table seeded with main; ops gain branch + exec_mode via ADD COLUMN with defaults so v1 history reads as main-branch deterministic ops; proven by tt-001 migrating a genuine v1 database with history intact). FORKS: a fork is a new op-log branch sharing every artifact by hash; visibility = own ops + ancestors' up to each fork point (min-composed caps down the chain, cycle-guarded); storage audit proven (tt-002: 3 forks over a 5-artifact study cost exactly 3 delta artifacts) with branch-independence property (writes on A never change B's view). AT(t): consistent views at arbitrary instants incl. mid-sweep — ops begun by t appear, outcomes written after t are masked, unfinished ops' outputs invisible; monotonicity + internal consistency proven (tt-005). EXPLAIN: full causal trees (which op, seed, versions/lock-hash, budget, capability, exec mode, branch, inputs recursively), depth-limited, DAG-deduped, JSON + human renderings; orphan inputs fail LOUDLY as LedgerCorruption (tt-004). REPLAY AUDIT (the G5-at-study-scale primitive for golden ledgers): op sequences compared structurally (ir/seed/mode); deterministic ops must reproduce output hashes exactly; fast divergences reported without failing (tt-003 battery: clean/deterministic-failure/fast-divergence all classified). GC: only edge-less artifacts reclaimable, dry-run first, referenced artifacts immortal (P9). Crash: kill -9 during fork traffic recovers lint-clean with all visible ops complete (tt-006, 4 seeded rounds); lint extended with branch-reference checks. 25 unit + 11 conformance + 7 travel tests green; fs-roofline (dependent) green; clippy -D warnings clean; xtask check-all 19 crates 0 violations; CONTRACT.md updated (new no-claims: no branch deletion/merge, caller-timestamp trust). Interactive-steering fork-on-reweight integration deferred to the MOO bead as specified.

title: fs-ir core: FrankenScript typed AST, isomorphic s-expr/JSON syntaxes, versioning, inspectable verb lowering
description:
## What
`fs-ir` core (plan §11.1): FrankenScript — the system's ONE TRUE INTERFACE. A typed, versioned intermediate representation, not a pile of function signatures.

## Scope
- Two ISOMORPHIC concrete syntaxes: canonical s-expressions and a lossless JSON mapping — agents emit whichever their tooling prefers; BOTH parse to the same typed AST (isomorphism is a tested property, not an aspiration).
- Value types are the system's REAL NOUNS: dimensioned quantities (Qty literals: `0.12Pa*s`, `65deg`, `0.5L/s`), Regions and charts, fields/cochains, operators, budgets, studies, capability tokens, scenarios, seeds — the Appendix C study forms (`(study ...)`, `(budget (wall 2h) (mem 96GiB) (qoi-rel-error 2e-2))`, `(let vessel (frep ...))`, `ascent.optimize ... :until (any (grad-norm 1e-5) (e-value 20) (budget-exhausted))`) are the acceptance fixtures.
- Versioning: IR language versions + per-operator semantic versions; older-IR migration hooks; version pinning in every study (Five Explicits' "versions" pillar).
- High-level verbs (`optimize_shape`, `simulate_pour`) exist for terseness but LOWER TO EXPLICIT IR, and the lowering is INSPECTABLE — progressive disclosure with nothing hidden.
- AST design for admission: every node carries source spans (structured errors point at exact locations in agent-submitted programs).

## Acceptance criteria
s-expr ↔ JSON ↔ AST round-trips bit-stable (property-tested on generated programs); Appendix C's spout and frame studies parse to correct ASTs (the canonical fixtures); verb lowering produces valid, inspectable IR; version pinning round-trips.

## Testing
G0: parser fuzzing (no panics, structured rejections with spans); grammar-coverage battery; isomorphism property (parse_sexpr(print_json(x)) == x). Logs: parse diagnostics with spans, lowering traces (verb → explicit IR).

## ADDENDUM AMENDMENT (COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md)
Proposal 8 (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.15) RE-SPECIFIES the public API around DECLARATIVE QUERIES: the operator poses a typed QoI functional with a tolerance/confidence target, a budget, and a deadline; imperative solver access (explicit mesh/solver/timestep) is DEMOTED to an internal/expert surface. A query is an admissible, type-checked, versioned FrankenScript IR object — reuse this crate's admission (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.15 builds on fs-ir-admission) so ill-posed queries are rejected in milliseconds. Every returned answer carries anytime + refusal semantics and a color (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.17).
close_reason: FrankenScript core landed as crates/fs-ir (the system's one true interface, plan 11.1 / P10). TYPED AST: every node carries a byte span; atoms are the real nouns — fs-qty dimensioned quantities (0.12Pa*s, 65deg, 0.5L/s, 0.03m2/s3; the ORIGINAL literal preserved verbatim because fs-qty normalizes to SI — 65deg->rad — so printing must not corrupt round-trips), Count grants (384GiB/96cores — information units deliberately outside fs-qty's SI domain), 0x seeds, strings/symbols/keywords/lists. TWO ISOMORPHIC SYNTAXES: hand-rolled total s-expr reader (comments, escapes, deterministic atom classification — a number with a garbage suffix is a structured spanned error, NEVER silently a symbol) and a lossless single-key-tagged JSON mapping (i/f/q/c/seed/s/sym/kw; Qty/Count/Seed reuse the s-expr literal grammar inside strings so ONE classifier owns numeric semantics for both). ISOMORPHISM PROVEN: 200 seeded generated programs + the verbatim Appendix C spout and frame studies survive sexpr/JSON/cross-syntax cycles shape-stably (acceptance). FIXTURES: both Appendix C studies parse with seeds (0x5EED0001/0xF00D0002), constellation locks, let-bindings, and typed-noun counts asserted. ## What
`fs-ir` STATIC ADMISSION (plan §11.1): before anything executes, the IR passes admission — an ill-typed study is rejected in MILLISECONDS with a structured diagnosis, not discovered at hour six.

## Scope

- Chart-compatibility checking through the Rep Router: does a conversion chain exist within the study's error budget for every geometry-consuming op? (route feasibility as an admission predicate, with the router's explanation attached to failures).

- Capability sufficiency: study's operator set + resource asks vs the session's capability token (fs-session-caps).
- REGIME GATING (patch Rev A integration): solver/model choices checked against RegimeReports — `(assert (regime.allows flux.free-surface-lbm))` enforced; violations rejected or warned per policy with the report attached.
- The Five Explicits enforced structurally: units, seeds, budgets, versions, capabilities are MANDATORY fields — an agent literally cannot express an ambiguous request.

## Acceptance criteria
Admission latency ≤ milliseconds-class on flagship-scale studies (measured); each admission dimension has seeded-rejection fixtures verifying correct, actionable diagnoses (error payloads content-checked, including ranked fixes with cost-model-derived estimates); zero false-admits on the violation zoo; Appendix C studies admit cleanly.

title: fs-session: capability tokens, enforcing governor w/ declared degradation ladder, idempotency keys, estimate() dry runs, teaching errors
description:
## What
`fs-session` (plan §11.3): sessions, capability tokens, and the resource GOVERNOR — budgets are ENFORCED, not advisory. Plus the agent-proofing trio: idempotency keys, dry runs, errors-as-guidance.

## Scope
- Sessions: every IR program executes inside a session holding a CAPABILITY TOKEN — explicit grant of operators, core-seconds, resident memory, wall time, ledger scope. Token checking at admission (fs-ir-admission) and CONTINUOUSLY at runtime (the governor meters actual consumption via Cx budget accountants).
- Resource governor: admission control onto the two-lane executor; per-study core quotas; on memory pressure, GRACEFUL DEGRADATION in a DECLARED ORDER — spill coldest arenas → coarsen adaptively → pause-serialize-resume (P7 makes every solver checkpointable, so "pause the LES, run the urgent trim study, resume" is ROUTINE, not heroic). Degradation events ledgered with attribution.
- IDEMPOTENCY KEYS on every mutating call: a retried request cannot double-spend a budget or duplicate a study (exactly-once semantics over the ledger; key = agent-supplied + content hash).
- DRY RUNS: `estimate(program)` returns predicted wall time, memory, error, and ENERGY from the cost models WITHOUT EXECUTING — agents plan before they spend.
- ERRORS AS GUIDANCE: every failure is a structured value with machine-readable diagnosis + candidate fixes RANKED BY THE COST MODEL (the §11.3 BudgetInfeasible example is the canonical fixture; fs-constraint's infeasibility diagnoses surface through this same channel). "A refusal that teaches is worth ten silent successes."

## Acceptance criteria
Budget enforcement: studies exceeding grants are throttled/paused per policy (never silently killed — structured outcomes); double-submit with same idempotency key = one execution, one charge (concurrency-stress-tested); estimate() accuracy tracked vs actuals (calibration curves ledgered — the cost models' own report card); degradation ladder exercised under synthetic memory pressure with correct ordering.

## Testing
G4-class: governor under storm (many studies, adversarial budgets); idempotency races (simultaneous duplicate submissions); pause-resume-under-pressure equality. Logs: per-session consumption ledgers, degradation events, estimate-vs-actual tables, error payloads.

title: fs-plan models: per-operator error+cost models (quantile fits over tune), Error Ledger + Time Ledger attribution
description:
## What

title: fs-render differentiable: edge-aware silhouette + reparameterized shading gradients, inverse-rendering objectives [F]
description:
## What
Differentiable rendering (plan §10.4 [F]): reparameterized/edge-aware gradient estimators for silhouette-and-shading derivatives — closing the loop where AESTHETIC constraints join physical ones in ASCENT.

## Scope
- Gradient estimators: reparameterized sampling for interior/shading terms (differentiable BSDF/light sampling through the FrankenTorch bridge where learned components appear); EDGE-AWARE handling of visibility discontinuities (silhouette integrals — the part naive autodiff gets silently WRONG; edge-sampling or reparameterization-class treatment, documented choice).
- Chart-level derivatives: image w.r.t. design parameters θ through chart perturbations (fs-xform Jacobian actions composed with rendering gradients — sphere-traced SDF derivatives via implicit differentiation of the hit equation).
- Inverse problems as objectives: match a target photograph, a sketch, or a legacy artifact's appearance as an objective TERM combinable with physics objectives in fs-opt-ir (aesthetic + aerodynamic Pareto — the plan's stated use).
- Bias/variance discipline: estimator bias characterized and documented (Evidence on rendering gradients like everything else); gradient-check battery vs FD-of-renders (expensive but definitive, run on fixtures).

## Acceptance criteria
Gradient checks: silhouette + shading derivatives match FD on fixture scenes (sphere position/radius, SDF blend parameters) within statistical tolerance; inverse-rendering fixtures converge (recover known shape parameters from target images); integration: one combined physics+appearance optimization fixture runs end-to-end.

## Testing
G0: estimator unbiasedness where claimed (interior terms), bias bounds where not (edge terms); variance tracking vs sample counts. Logs: gradient-check tables, inverse-problem convergence traces, per-term variance decomposition.

title: L2 MORPH: geometry kernel
description:
## Mission
L2 MORPH: the geometry kernel. Represent, construct, interrogate, convert, mesh, and parameterize geometry — with certified validity, native derivatives w.r.t. design parameters, and no privileged representation.

## Core thesis (plan §7, Bet 1)
The canonical object is an abstract Region presented through charts (SDF grid, F-rep CSG, NURBS patchwork, half-edge mesh, sparse voxel tree, point cloud, lattice graph, neural implicit). Conversions are functors carrying (cost, error-bound, certificate) labels; the Rep Router solves a Pareto shortest-path over the chart graph to pick the cheapest conversion chain that keeps composed error inside the caller's budget. This turns "which representation should I use" — the perennial unforced error of every CAD/simulation handoff — into a solved planning problem. "The same shape held three ways" is a normal, coherent state; agreement between charts is a checkable proposition.

## Also owned here
- Sheaf-theoretic gluing (Bet 11): watertightness as an interval-verified vanishing-cocycle certificate, H¹ obstructions reported with offending interface cells, plus constructive sheaf REPAIR (Hodge decomposition of mismatch: exact→local fixes, harmonic→true topological obstruction).
- Design parameterizations — the levers ASCENT pulls — each a differentiable map θ→Region with Jacobian action.
- Geometric algebra (PGA/CGA) as the internal kinematics substrate with Vec3/quat façades.
- Shape-program synthesis (patch Rev G): typed constructive-geometry programs, shape grammars, geometric e-graphs with equality saturation — discrete design invention beyond continuous perturbation.
- Import/export quarantine (patch Rev J): dirty external geometry never becomes a trusted Region without a certification receipt.

title: fs-geom core: Region/Chart traits, ChartSample w/ certified Lipschitz, agreement checking, Convert receipts
description:
## What
`fs-geom` core: the Region/Chart abstraction (plan §7.1) — the geometry kernel's founding move. An abstract `Region` (measurable subset of R³ with piecewise-smooth boundary) is NEVER stored directly; it is PRESENTED through charts.

## Scope
- `Chart` trait (Appendix B): query interfaces — inside/outside, signed distance, closest point, ray intersection, curvature, integrals over region/boundary — via `eval(x, cx) -> ChartSample` (value + gradient + certified Lipschitz data), `support() -> Aabb`, `topology_hint() -> BettiBounds`; plus a DECLARED ERROR MODEL relative to the abstract region.
- `Region`: holds one or more charts + the provenance of how each was obtained. "The same shape held three ways" is a normal, coherent state instead of a synchronization-bug factory; AGREEMENT BETWEEN CHARTS IS A CHECKABLE PROPOSITION (sampled + certified agreement tests are API, not folklore).
- `Convert` trait: certified conversion as a functor with a receipt — `convert(budget, cx) -> Result<Certified<Dst>, Diag>` (Evidence-typed per fs-evidence); every conversion's error explicit and composable, feeding the Error Ledger (P4).
- Design-parameter plumbing: `Chart::Param` as the design-lever handle (fs-xform builds on it); charts advertise differentiability class.
- Cancellation + budgets: all queries take &Cx (interruptible geometry — huge queries poll at tile granularity).
- No privileged representation, ever (the anti-CAD-kernel stance): operations request capabilities ("a chart supporting operation X with error ≤ ε under budget B"), the Rep Router picks.

## Acceptance criteria
Trait suite compiles the whole chart zoo (proven by downstream beads); a two-chart Region with deliberate disagreement is DETECTED by the agreement checker with localized diagnostics; error-model composition matches fs-ivl bounds on fixture conversions.

## Testing
G0: trait-law suite (eval consistency: inside(x) ⇔ sd(x)<0 within declared tolerance; gradient vs FD on smooth charts; support() actually bounds). Fixture Regions (sphere/box/torus analytic charts) as the shared test vocabulary for ALL of MORPH. Logs: per-query evidence (values, bounds, chart id, budget spent).

HARD NEW REQUIREMENT: **stable persistent entity IDs**. Patches, interfaces, and load cases must carry IDs that survive topology-changing edits, because Proposal 10's semantic diff/merge (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.10, frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.12) is gated on them (risk R3 — the classic CAD topological-naming problem). Mitigation the addendum mandates: FrankenSim owns its kernel, so IDs are first-class from day one rather than reconstructed heuristically; edits are ledgered operations that transform IDs EXPLICITLY. Also NEW: **fiducial/datum primitives** in the geometry layer (design-for-verification), and the representation registry is explicitly OPENED to measured-data chart types, for Proposal 11's reality-as-a-chart ingestion (frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.4).

title: Sheaf certificates: cellular-sheaf watertightness (interval-verified cocycle bound), H1 obstruction diagnostics [F/M]
description:
## What
Sheaf-theoretic consistency certificates (plan §7.3, Bet 11 [F/M]): the mathematically correct language for "locally represented, globally consistent" — and the WATERTIGHTNESS CERTIFICATE for multi-representation models.

## The construction (concrete, not decorative)
A model whose patches live in different charts is a CELLULAR SHEAF over the patch-adjacency complex: stalks = local chart/function spaces; restriction maps = trace/conversion operators to shared interfaces. Global consistency = existence of a section (H⁰). The watertightness certificate is an INTERVAL-VERIFIED bound ‖δs‖ ≤ tol on the interface mismatch cocycle. If the coboundary can't be driven below tolerance, the H¹ OBSTRUCTION is reported WITH THE OFFENDING INTERFACE CELLS ATTACHED — exactly the diagnostic an agent needs to fix a leaky model. Cellular sheaves are finite linear algebra over an adjacency complex — "the most galaxy-brained component that is nonetheless straightforwardly implementable."

## Scope
- Patch-adjacency complex construction from multi-chart Regions (interface discovery via chart-support overlap + boundary correspondence).
- Restriction-map assembly: discretized trace operators per interface (chart-pair-specific: mesh-edge sampling, spline trace, SDF interface band), assembled as sparse blocks (fs-sparse).
- Coboundary operator δ and mismatch cocycle computation; least-squares section solve (H⁰ candidate) via solver-stack/fs-la; residual → interval-verified per-interface bounds (fs-ivl).
- Certificate output: Evidence-typed watertightness verdict — PASS(‖δs‖≤tol, per-interface margins) | FAIL(H¹ obstruction, offending cells, mismatch magnitudes).
- Second consumer designed-in: the SAME machinery later computes BDDC-style domain-decomposition coarse spaces as approximate harmonic sections of the interface sheaf (solver-dd bead) — Bet 11 earning its keep twice.
- Cross-examination hook: certify-certifiers attacks this with brute-force ray-parity queries on adversarial seams.

## Acceptance criteria
On seeded multi-chart fixtures (known-watertight and known-leaky): verdicts correct with correct localization; interval verification sound (no PASS on a truly leaky seam — ray-parity cross-check); scaling to realistic patch counts (hundreds) within budget.

## Testing
G0: δδ=0 on the sheaf complex (bitwise); property: verdict invariance under patch re-indexing + rigid motions (G3). Adversarial seam zoo (near-tangent interfaces, T-junctions, mixed chart types). Logs: per-interface mismatch norms, obstruction reports with cell ids, solve diagnostics.

## ADDENDUM AMENDMENT (COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md)
Bet 11 gains **merge semantics** as a named deliverable (Proposal 10, frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.12): the SAME sheaf machinery is, unmodified, a merge-conflict classifier — the single most elegant reuse in the addendum. Three-way merge Hodge-decomposes the interface mismatch cocycle (via the sheaf Laplacian / sheaf-repair machinery frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.12 reuses): the coboundary component auto-reconciles by canonical least-squares with a certificate; the harmonic component is a genuine structural conflict, localized and escalated. Merge trustworthiness is conditioned on the spectral gap (Proposal 5, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.3) — degraded-gap merges must be flagged low-confidence.

title: Sheaf repair: Hodge decomposition of mismatch (exact/coexact/harmonic), bounded auto-repair, ranked proposals
description:
## What
Sheaf REPAIR (patch Rev L): upgrade sheaf machinery from diagnosis to CONSTRUCTIVE repair — H¹ obstruction reports become actionable automatic fixes where possible.

## Scope
- Hodge decomposition of the interface mismatch cochain m = exact + coexact + harmonic (discrete Hodge via the sheaf Laplacian; fs-la-eigen/solver-stack for the solves). Interpretation contract: EXACT component → repairable by local potential/patch adjustments; COEXACT → circulation-like inconsistencies, usually orientation/trace errors (points at converter bugs); HARMONIC → true topological obstruction or global inconsistency (no local fix exists — report honestly).
- Repair solvers: least-squares section projection (minimal patch-boundary adjustment killing the exact component); interval-bounded seam correction (repairs that provably stay within each chart's declared error model — a repair must never silently distort geometry beyond budget); minimal chart-conversion replanning (ask the Rep Router for an alternative chart for the worst-offending patch — "reroute SDF→mesh through interval dual contouring").
- Agent-facing repair proposals (the patch's example format): ranked actions with expected post-repair ‖δs‖ ("project NURBS patch P17 boundary control points → expected 4.1e-6 m"), costs from router models, applied only with explicit acceptance or auto-apply policy under budget.
- Obstruction localization refinement: harmonic-component support → minimal cut-set of interfaces that would need topology-level changes.

## Acceptance criteria
On seeded-defect fixtures: exact-component defects auto-repaired to certificate-passing state WITHOUT exceeding chart error budgets; coexact seeding (flipped orientation) correctly diagnosed as converter-side; harmonic seeding (genuinely mismatched topology) correctly declared unrepairable-locally with correct localization; repair proposals' predicted-vs-actual post-repair norms within stated accuracy.

## Testing
Property: repair idempotence (repairing a passing model is a no-op); repair safety (post-repair charts still agree with pre-repair within budgets — G3-style checks). Full decomposition correctness vs dense linear-algebra oracle on small complexes. Logs: decomposition fractions, per-action predictions vs outcomes, refusal reasons.

title: fs-xform manifold harmonics: Laplace-Beltrami eigenbasis shape spectrum for global search [F]
description:
## What
Manifold-harmonic shape bases (plan §7.6 [F]): eigenfunctions of the Laplace–Beltrami operator ON THE CURRENT SHAPE, giving an automatically smooth, hierarchical, low-dimensional "shape spectrum" ideal for CMA-ES-scale global search.

## Scope
- Laplace–Beltrami assembly on surface meshes (cotan weights, robust variants for bad triangles) and on SDF narrow bands (implicit surface Laplacian) — the basis must be available WITHOUT requiring a body-fitted mesh.
- Eigenbasis computation via fs-la-eigen LOBPCG (smallest-k eigenpairs, k ~ 50–300); deflation of rigid/constant modes; deterministic eigenvector sign/ordering convention (P2 — CMA-ES coordinates must mean the same thing across runs).
- Parameterization: θ = spectral coefficients; displacement field = Σ θᵢ ψᵢ · n̂ (normal displacement) or full vector variants; Jacobian action trivially the basis functions (the smoothness is FREE preconditioning — low-frequency exploration first, the reason this pairs with CMA-ES global search; the ornithoid flagship uses ~200 coefficients for global form).
- Basis refresh policy: recompute on large shape changes (drift criterion), with coefficient transfer between bases (projection) so optimizers survive refreshes; refresh events ledgered.

## Acceptance criteria
Spectra match analytic references on sphere/torus fixtures (within discretization error, convergence verified); basis smoothness (Dirichlet energy ordering) holds; coefficient-transfer preserves shape within tolerance across refresh; end-to-end: a 100-coefficient CMA-ES toy shape-matching study converges markedly faster than raw-vertex parameterization (the demonstrable payoff, ledgered).

## Testing
G0: eigenpair residuals, orthonormality in the right inner product (mass matrix); G3 isometry invariance of spectra (bent vs flat developable fixtures); refresh-transfer round-trip. Logs: spectra, refresh events, study comparison curves.
close_reason: Manifold harmonics shipped as fs_xform::harmonics ([F]-gated behind manifold-harmonics; fs-la becomes an optional dep): the Laplace-Beltrami shape spectrum for CMA-ES-scale global search. (1) ASSEMBLY: cotan Laplacian with the robust obtuse-triangle clamp + barycentric lumped mass; (2) EIGENPAIRS: lumped-mass symmetrization M^-1/2 L M^-1/2 fed matrix-free to fs-la LOBPCG via shift-and-negate (Gershgorin shift keeps the largest-mode path exact for smallest-k); numeric kernel deflated and the CONSTANT re-admitted ANALYTICALLY as mode 0 — found the hard way: the ES study stalled at a 0.18 misfit floor because uniform inflation (the mean of any bump field) was deflated away with the kernel; inflation is a design direction, so theta_0 = uniform normal offset; (3) DETERMINISM (P2): ascending-eigenvalue ordering + largest-|entry|-positive sign convention — CMA-ES coordinate j means the same thing across runs; (4) PARAMETERIZATION: displace = normal displacement sum theta_j psi_j n-hat; REFRESH: needs_refresh bbox-relative drift criterion + M-weighted coefficient transfer (project/transfer) so optimizers survive basis recomputation. CONFORMANCE (5 suites): mh-001 the icosphere spectrum hits the ANALYTIC l(l+1) ladder — 2 (x3), 6 (x5) — within 6% with residuals <1e-5, M-orthonormality to 5e-3, torus fundamental self-converges; mh-002 eigenvalues ascend and each mode's Dirichlet energy EQUALS its eigenvalue (smoothness ordering: low coefficients are provably the smooth directions); mh-003 G3 isometry — flat vs isometrically bent strip spectra match (to the documented ~1e-4 robust-clamp tolerance); mh-004 zero-field transfers to zero, self-transfer round-trips the displaced shape to 5e-3, drift criterion gates refreshes; mh-005 THE DEMONSTRABLE PAYOFF, ledgered: seeded (1+1)-ES shape matching at equal 500-eval budget with dimension-normalized mutations — 18 spectral coefficients reach misfit 0.0017 vs 66 raw vertex amplitudes at 0.0487, a 27.9x ratio: smoothness is free preconditioning, exactly the pairing-with-CMA-ES story the bead names. ## What

title: fs-io: accept legal PLY element order without premature face validation
description:
Both ASCII and binary PLY readers validate face indices immediately against positions.len(). PLY headers define element order and legal files may place the face element before the vertex element. Those faces are validated against zero vertices and rejected even though all referenced vertices appear later.

Root cause: parsing order is conflated with semantic validation order.

Repair: parse face lists into bounded pending records, then validate and triangulate against the final vertex count after all elements are consumed, or explicitly constrain and document the supported profile in both parser diagnostics and contract. Preserve resource bounds and exact error offsets.

Acceptance: equivalent vertex-first and face-first ASCII and binary files import identically; out-of-range indices still fail after full parse; oversized lists remain bounded; quarantine receipt distinguishes unsupported profile from malformed data if the deliberate-refusal design is chosen.
close_reason: Legal PLY element order accepted - LANDED. Root cause fixed: parsing order was conflated with semantic validation order (push_face validated indices against positions.len() DURING parse, so legal face-before-vertex files were rejected against zero vertices). Now: faces triangulate into bounded pending records during parse (fewer-than-3 structural check, 1024-item list cap, and MAX_ELEMENTS triangle cap all still enforced immediately); index RANGE validation runs once in read_ply after ALL elements are consumed, against the final vertex count, with the exact offending triangle ordinal as the error offset. ACCEPTANCE MET (ply_face_first_element_order_is_legal): vertex-first and face-first ASCII import identically (positions + triangles equal); binary_little_endian face-first parses to the same triangles; out-of-range index in a face-first file still refuses AFTER the full parse naming triangle ordinal 0 and the real vertex count; oversized list (1025) still hits ResourceBound in face-first order. fs-io suite green, clippy clean. CONTRACT records the deferred-validation profile.

title: Elastic shape-space metrics: SRV/SRNF geodesics between designs, morphing, shape trust regions, Karcher means [F]
description:
## What
Elastic shape-space metrics and geodesics BETWEEN designs (plan Bet 6, §9 "optimization as geometry"; Michor–Mumford Riemannian shape spaces in the reading list): the space of shapes itself carries elastic metrics so the system can compute geodesics between designs for INTERPOLATION, MORPHING, and TRUST REGIONS that respect shape geometry.

## Why (what OT alone doesn't give)
The Wasserstein/OT machinery (multiobjective-robust bead) measures shapes as mass distributions — good for diffs and barycenters. ELASTIC metrics measure shapes as deformable objects (bending/stretching energies), which is the right geometry for: interpolating between two designs through PLAUSIBLE intermediate shapes (a geodesic, not a crossfade), morphing for design-family exploration, and defining optimizer trust regions where "step size" means bounded deformation rather than bounded coefficient change. Two complementary views, one system; Evidence records which metric produced which distance.

## Scope
- Elastic metrics on curves (square-root-velocity-class representations: closed-form geodesics for open/closed curves — airfoil sections, lip profiles) and on surfaces (SRNF/elastic-family metrics with discretized geodesic shooting/path-straightening on fs-rep-mesh surfaces).
- Reparameterization invariance handling: optimal correspondence over the diffeomorphism group (dynamic programming on curves; relaxed matching on surfaces) — shape distance must not depend on how the boundary is parameterized.
- Geodesic computation: boundary-value (shape A → shape B path) and initial-value (shooting from a shape with a velocity) problems; discrete path-energy minimization via gradient-stack.
- Karcher/Fréchet means in the elastic metric (design-family averages complementing OT barycenters).
- Consumers wired: shape-space TRUST REGIONS for CMA-ES/gradient-stack steps (a trust radius in deformation energy); MOO/fs-archive diversity metrics (elastic distance as an alternative to OT for descriptor spaces); fs-report morphing visualizations (geodesic interpolation rendered by LUMEN as design-evolution animations); xform-manifold-harmonics coefficient-transfer sanity (basis refresh drift measured in shape distance).
- Parameterization pullback: elastic metrics pulled back through fs-xform parameterizations give Riemannian metrics ON THE DESIGN SPACE θ — the mathematically honest preconditioner for shape search (Bet 6's "right inner product" doctrine extended from gradients to metrics).

## Ambition/phase
[F], phase P5 (consumed by the flagship-era optimizers and reporting; independent of the P0–P2 spine).

## Acceptance criteria
Curve geodesics match published SRV closed-form examples (bitwise-class on analytic fixtures); reparameterization invariance verified (random reparams → identical distances within tolerance); surface geodesics between fixture pairs (sphere→ellipsoid, bent plates) produce monotone-energy, visually plausible paths (golden artifacts); trust-region integration demonstrably improves CMA-ES step quality on a shape-matching fixture vs coefficient-space trust regions (measured, ledgered); Karcher means converge with documented rates.

## Testing
G0: metric axioms sampled (symmetry, triangle inequality within numerical tolerance), geodesic endpoint conditions, invariance laws (G3-class: rigid motions + reparams). Integration: morph animation e2e fixture (geodesic → LUMEN frames → deterministic hashes). Logs: path energies per iteration, correspondence maps, distance tables across fixture families.

title: fs-rep-mesh: half-edge + tet/hex complexes, generalized-winding-number repair suite, watertight queries

- Repair suite for polygon soup: generalized winding numbers for ROBUST inside/outside on broken input — "the single most effective modern trick in mesh robustness" — accelerated by an octree dipole approximation to run fast on millions of triangles; hole filling, duplicate/degenerate-face removal, orientation unification, self-intersection flagging (certified via fs-ivl broad/narrow phases in validity-certificates bead).
- Chart impl: signed distance via exact point-triangle distance (batched, SIMD) + winding-number sign; ray intersection with watertight ray-triangle tests (shared convention with LUMEN's tracer); curvature via discrete operators (cotan/normal-cycle) with documented convergence class.

## Acceptance criteria

title: fs-rep-nurbs: exact spline algebra, trimmed B-reps w/ rational trim curves, SDF-routed Boolean policy
description:
## What
`fs-rep-nurbs`: rational B-spline charts (plan §7.2) — exact spline algebra, trimmed B-reps, and the HONEST Boolean policy.

## Scope
- NURBS curves/surfaces: full rational; EXACT knot insertion and degree elevation (integer/rational arithmetic where exactness is claimed); evaluation with derivatives to arbitrary order; Greville/Gauss quadrature rules per patch (IGA consumption).
- Trimmed-patch B-reps: trim curves held in EXACT RATIONAL form plus interval boxes (the dual representation that makes trim queries certifiable); point classification on trimmed patches with certified in/out/boundary bands.
- THE BOOLEAN POSITION (honest, per plan): watertight trimmed-NURBS Booleans are the GRAVEYARD of CAD kernels — so Boolean ops route through F-rep/SDF charts BY DEFAULT and re-fit splines afterward when a spline chart is required (convert-sdf-nurbs); direct B-rep Booleans remain a constrained, CERTIFICATE-GATED capability (attempt; if the sheaf watertightness certificate fails, refuse with diagnostics), never a promise.
- Why splines stay first-class anyway: IGA (§8.1) — geometry basis = analysis basis; Kirchhoff–Love shells on spline surfaces; the CAD→mesh information massacre never happens.
- Chart impl: closest-point/distance via Bézier-clipping-seeded Newton with interval polish (certified variant); ray intersection likewise (LUMEN's NURBS tracing shares this machinery).

## Acceptance criteria
Knot insertion/degree elevation EXACT (bitwise-identical evaluations pre/post refinement at common parameters — the definitive spline-algebra test); trimmed classification correct on adversarial trim fixtures (tangent trims, slivers, nested loops); closest-point certified variant always brackets true distance (vs dense sampling oracle).

## Testing
G0: partition-of-unity, endpoint interpolation, derivative-vs-Dual checks; round-trip insert/remove where mathematically lossless. Trim battery with published nasty cases. Logs: clipping iteration stats, certification bands, exactness verdicts.
