title: Rep Router: Pareto shortest-path conversion planning over chart multigraph, learned costs, explainable routes
description:
## What
The Rep Router (plan §7.3, Bet 1): conversions form a directed multigraph — nodes are chart types, edges are converters annotated with (cost model, error model, certificate availability) — and requests ("give me a chart supporting operation X with error ≤ ε under budget B") are solved as a PARETO SHORTEST-PATH problem over that graph.

## Scope
- Conversion graph registry: converters self-register with their edge labels; cost models read the autotune table (machine-specific ON PURPOSE — kernel-level winners flip between the M-class and TR-class machines, §14.1); error models declare composition rules (additive Hausdorff, multiplicative relative, exact).
- Pareto shortest-path planner (cost × composed error, certified edges PREFERRED): FrankenNetworkx label-correcting/multi-objective search; deterministic tie-breaking (P2 — router decisions must be reproducible and explainable, per AGENTS.md invariant).
- Execution engine: run the winning chain, produce Evidence-typed result with the COMPOSED certificate; record ACTUAL cost/error back into tune tables so the models improve (the router learns).
- Explainability: `route_explain()` returns the considered paths, their Pareto labels, and why the winner won — an agent-facing diagnostic, and the hook fs-ir-admission uses for chart-compatibility checking.
- Failure semantics: no admissible path within budget → structured error listing the BINDING constraint (error vs cost) and the cheapest relaxations (errors-as-guidance doctrine).

## Why
This turns "which representation should I use" — the perennial unforced error of every CAD/simulation handoff — into a solved planning problem, and it is the load-bearing mechanism behind "no privileged representation."

## Acceptance criteria
On a seeded graph with known Pareto fronts, planner returns exact fronts; composed certificates verified against direct measurement on executed chains (G3 path independence: ANY admissible path lands within the composed certificate of the direct edge); learned-cost feedback demonstrably improves subsequent plans; determinism of decisions across runs.

## Testing
G0: planner correctness on synthetic multigraphs (oracle enumeration); G3 metamorphic path-independence battery across the real converter set as it lands; budget-infeasible diagnostics content-checked. Logs: full route explanations, per-edge predicted-vs-actual cost/error tables (the model-improvement evidence).

## ADDENDUM AMENDMENT (COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md)
The Rep Router's fitness function gains TWO new terms:
- a **differentiability term** (Proposal 1, frankensim-epic-coupling-bk0o.2): when a query requests gradients, PREFER naturally-smooth SDF/spline paths — converting multi-representation from a complication into the asset that provides differentiable paths where mesh-locked pipelines have none.
- a **conditioning term** (Proposal 5, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.3): route by END-TO-END conditioning (composed per-op amplification factors), not just per-op cost/error — "which path through representation space keeps the whole pipeline well-posed."
The Router also becomes a VERIFICATION asset: the Goodhart guard (frankensim-epic-epistype-qmao.5) re-routes optimizer endpoints through a DIFFERENT representation path as an independent cross-check.

GRAPH REGISTRY: ConverterSpec edges with (a-priori cost, declared error model with composition rule — Exact / AdditiveAbs / MultiplicativeRel grounded against the request scale, certificate availability); duplicate/invalid specs refused structurally. PLANNER: exact Pareto label-correcting search over (cost, composed abs error, uncertified-edge count), simple-paths (non-simple dominated under nonneg weights), deterministic by construction (name-sorted expansion + total winner order: certified-preferred -> min cost -> min error -> lexicographic path). PROVEN against a brute-force DFS Pareto oracle on a seeded multigraph with parallel edges, a cycle, and mixed certificates, across three targets — exact front match (bead acceptance). EXPLAIN: every Pareto candidate with admissibility + winner index + reason (the fs-ir admission hook). REFUSALS TEACH: binding constraint named (Error/Cost/Both/NoPath) with best-achievable relaxation values, content-tested. COST ORACLE: machine-specific costs read through the CostOracle trait (L2 must not depend on L6 fs-ledger — HELM wires the tune table behind it; MemoryCostOracle in-process); learned-cost feedback demonstrably reroutes plans (acceptance); learned error magnitudes replace declared ones ONLY on uncertified additive edges — certificates are never learned away. description:

The roofline harness (plan §14.1): performance claims as FALSIFIABLE targets — every kernel benchmarked against its arithmetic-intensity-derived limit on the actual machine, results ledgered with fingerprints.

## Scope

- Kernel benchmark registry: each hot kernel registers (workload generator, intensity metadata — from fs-tilelang where generated — target expression as % of roofline). ## Testing

title: Machine-adaptive hardening: CCD pinning, first-touch audits, P/E scheduling, prefetch/hugepage sweeps — targets met on both ISAs
description:
## What

## Scope
- Threadripper/EPYC lane: CCD-aware tile ownership (working sets pinned inside their 32 MiB L3 islands — measured via cache-miss counters where available, timing proxies otherwise); first-touch page placement VERIFIED (page-to-node audits); reduction trees shaped to the CCD hierarchy; NPS-mode sensitivity documented.

## Acceptance criteria
Each optimization's effect measured and documented (before/after per machine — no unattributed tuning); attainment targets met or honest gap analysis filed as follow-up beads; autotuner selections match exhaustive-sweep optima within tolerance on the audited subset.

## Testing
A/B harnesses per mechanism (CCD pinning on/off, first-touch on/off, prefetch sweep); counter-based verification where the OS exposes it. Logs: per-mechanism effect tables, selection audits, final attainment scoreboard.

title: Tropical critical-path analytics: max-plus eigenvalue over live event stream, tune-next + slack outputs [F/M]
description:
## What
Tropical critical-path analytics (plan §14.3, Bet 12 [F/M]): task-DAG timing in the MAX-PLUS SEMIRING — the critical circuit as a tropical eigenvector, computed live, telling the autotuner WHICH KERNEL TO TUNE NEXT and the planner where relaxed tolerance buys wall-clock.

## Scope
- Max-plus formalization: stage delays compose with ⊕=max, ⊗=+; steady-state throughput of the pipelined task DAG = the tropical eigenvalue of its timing matrix; the critical circuit = the eigenvector's support.
- Live computation: FrankenNetworkx tropical power iteration over the ledger's `events` stream (tile/op timings arriving continuously); windowed re-computation with drift detection (the critical path MOVES as tuning improves things).
- ACTIONABLE outputs (the whole point — "scheduling theory as an online instrument, not a whiteboard aphorism"): makespan sensitivity to each kernel's latency → ranked tune-next list for the autotuner; slack analysis → the planner learns that relaxing tolerance OFF the critical circuit buys NOTHING (fs-plan-allocator consumes this); bottleneck attribution in perf dashboards.
- [M] discipline: advisory-only until validated — its recommendations tracked against realized improvements (did tuning the recommended kernel actually move the makespan? — the self-audit that gates promotion).
- We contribute the tropical-semiring iteration kernels upstream to FrankenNetworkx (§12 contract).

## Acceptance criteria
Tropical eigenvalue/eigenvector correct vs brute-force longest-path analysis on fixture DAGs; live pipeline: synthetic event streams with known critical circuits recovered within window latency; recommendation quality: on seeded-bottleneck fixtures, the top recommendation is the true bottleneck; promotion audit machinery in place (recommendation → outcome tracking).

## Testing
G0: max-plus algebra laws, power-iteration convergence on irreducible fixtures; windowing correctness under out-of-order events. Logs: eigenvalue traces, circuit memberships over time, recommendation→outcome ledger.
close_reason: Implemented crate fs-tropical (crate:fs-tropical; L1, no deps). Tropical (max-plus) critical-path analytics — scheduling theory as an ONLINE INSTRUMENT. Max-plus semiring: oplus = max, otimes = + (absorbing at NEG_INF). TaskDag (per-task latencies + precedence edges): critical_path() = CPM longest-path = makespan + the critical path + per-task SLACK (0 <=> on the critical path); errors Cyclic on a cycle, BadEdge on out-of-range. ACTIONABLE outputs: tune_next(cp) = the zero-slack (critical) tasks ranked by latency (the autotuner's which-kernel-to-tune-next list — a task OFF the critical path with positive slack cannot move the makespan, so relaxing it buys nothing); bottleneck(cp) = the highest-latency critical task (the true bottleneck). max_cycle_mean(matrix) = the TROPICAL EIGENVALUE (Karp's O(n·E) algorithm) = the pipelined steady-state throughput (None if acyclic); critical_circuit()/brute_force_max_cycle() = the maximum-mean simple cycle (nodes, mean), the GROUND TRUTH max_cycle_mean is cross-checked against. RecommendationAudit ([M] discipline): record(AuditEntry{recommended, predicted_gain, realized_gain}), hit_rate() (fraction that realized a positive makespan improvement), promoted(min_samples, min_hit_rate) — recommendation->outcome tracking that gates promotion from advisory-only. Acceptance criteria covered: tropical eigenvalue/eigenvector correct vs brute-force longest-path (Karp == brute-force mean on fixtures); critical circuits recovered; on seeded-bottleneck fixtures the top recommendation is the true bottleneck; promotion-audit machinery in place. Tests (tests/tropical.rs, 7): max-plus semiring, critical-path-is-longest-path + slack, tune-next ranks bottleneck first, cyclic-DAG-no-critical-path, tropical-eigenvalue-matches-brute-force + critical-circuit, faster-cycle-dominates-self-loop + acyclic->None + 3-cycle mean, promotion-audit gates on realized outcomes. Verified: clippy -D warnings CLEAN (one scoped allow for the max-plus 2D matrix kernel, justified), fmt CLEAN, cargo test -p fs-tropical 7/7, fs-tropical COMPLIANT under xtask check-all. No-claim: critical_circuit/brute_force enumerate SIMPLE cycles for the small timing matrices this runs on (max_cycle_mean/Karp is the efficient path for large graphs); the LIVE pipeline (windowed re-computation over the fs-ledger event stream with drift detection + contributing tropical kernels upstream to FrankenNetworkx) consumes this batch core; the promotion policy is the planner's. NOTE: BASE-PLAN bead (perf epic) taken after the addendum frontier was exhausted.

description:

title: fs-roofline: fail closed on non-finite regression histories and gate specs
description:
regress::gate performs arithmetic over public Night and GateSpec f64 fields without validating finiteness or signs. NaN attainment, phase times, k_sigma, or zero/negative baseline parameters can flow through comparisons where NaN makes the red predicate false, yielding Green; invalid totals can also create non-finite attribution shares. Similar invalid histories can poison CUSUM and monthly trend decisions.

Root cause: a proof-bearing performance gate accepts unchecked floating inputs and represents malformed evidence as an ordinary Green/Red verdict.

Repair: add checked constructors or validate at every public gate boundary; require finite non-negative attainment and phase durations, positive finite statistical thresholds, consistent phase totals, and sensible baseline lengths. Add an Invalid/NoClaim verdict with structured diagnostics, never Green.

title: ADDENDUM L4 STRUCTURE & SELF-KNOWLEDGE: interface types + symmetry, spectral health, abstraction ladder, explanations, value-of-information
description:
## Mission
ADDENDUM LAYER 4 — STRUCTURE AND SELF-KNOWLEDGE. Declared structure harvested twice (correctness and speed), the system monitoring the health of its own algebra, and the three proposals that give a memoryless, intuition-free operator something to think with. Where Layers 1–3 build the engine, this layer is the operator's cognition: types that make ill-posed couplings compile-time errors, a health monitor that knows when its own triage is untrustworthy, a certified abstraction ladder that lets a bounded-attention operator reason at the concept level, explanation objects the system can *check* rather than confabulate, and a market that prices ignorance.

## The five proposals
- **Proposal 13 — Interface types and symmetry harvesting** (Mean 720). Type every interface by its function-space role (Arnold's FEEC periodic table IS the type lattice: H(grad)/H(curl)/H(div)/L² + regularity tags) so ill-posed couplings are compile-time errors — converting the largest class of silent agent-generated nonsense into red squiggles. Separately, let declared/detected symmetry groups block-diagonalize solves by irreducible representation (k-fold symmetry ≈ k× speedup), with approximate symmetry yielding a symmetrized solve + certified perturbation correction. The type checker is Phase 0 spine; the symmetry solver is Phase 3 horizon.
- **Proposal 5 — Spectral health monitoring** (Mean 660, Pract 850). The harmonic/coboundary "fixable vs structural" triage that merge (10) and repair depend on is only as trustworthy as the sheaf Laplacian's spectral gap — so instrument the gap as a runtime health metric and let the Rep Router route by end-to-end conditioning, not just per-op fitness. "I am becoming numerically unreliable in this region, and here is the reroute."
- **Proposal A — The certified abstraction ladder** (Mean 780, Agent 950). Maintain reduced-order views ("the wing box", "the load path") whose fidelity to the level below is a certified quantity, with a leak alarm: reason at the concept level until a certificate says the abstraction is no longer faithful *here*, then drill down only there. The only third option between an operator drowning in 50,000 spline coefficients and hallucinating the details it dropped. Beachhead: certified reduced-basis methods (Rozza/Patera) for affine-parametric elliptic problems.
- **Proposal B — Explanation objects** (Mean 770, Agent 950). When drag rises 3%, return not a number but a causal decomposition along named physical channels (induced/wave/friction), attributed via adjoint fields + the provenance DAG, each term with bounds — a checkable, re-derivable, certified artifact. Because a language-model operator generates plausible mechanistic narratives anyway; the difference between confabulation and understanding is whether the system can check the story.
- **Proposal C — Value-of-information queries: the ignorance market** (Mean 780, Agent 950). Make directed ignorance reduction a query type: across everything the ledger is uncertain about, where does one dollar of evidence most change the downstream decision? Turns curiosity into an optimizer with a stopping rule; the natural completion of 8's anytime "what would tighten this?".

## The circularity discount (Governance Rule 4)
A, B, C, D were generated by optimizing the agent-operator lens, so their top-tier standing is *conditional on agents actually being the operator*. Strip the lens (Ex-A) and they fall to the 725–740 band. If the first vertical ships human-driven, they are formally deferred to Phase 3 regardless of score.

## Members
interface-types (13), symmetry-harvest (13), spectral-health (5), abstraction-ladder (A), explanation-objects (B), voi-queries (C).

## Success criteria
The coupling-graph checker turns illegal trace pairings into pre-run errors; degraded-gap suite passes (the triage must REFUSE confidence rather than misclassify — refusal is the pass condition); RB-certified regions cover ≥20% of wedge query volume; explanation channels + residual reconcile to the observed ΔQoI within certified bounds on ≥90% of cases; VoI-recommended purchases measurably outperform agent-chosen alternatives on realized decision-changes.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- NOTE: `add-layer:Ln` here is the addendum's THEMATIC layer (economic engine / epistemics / coupling / self-knowledge / GTM), NOT the base L0–L6 architecture stack. Member crates still sit at their true base layer and must respect lower-knows-nothing-of-higher dependency direction.
close_reason: ADDENDUM L4 STRUCTURE & SELF-KNOWLEDGE epic COMPLETE — all 7 members closed. Proposal 13 interface types (knh1.1, fellow agent): the coupling-graph static checker over the FEEC type lattice — illegal couplings are compile errors, unknown pairings illegal-until-certified. Proposal 13 symmetry harvesting (knh1.2, fellow agent): isotypic block-diagonalization with certified asymmetry remainders — k-fold approx k-times, never a false speedup. Proposal 5 spectral health (knh1.3, fellow agent): lambda-gap monitoring with low-confidence propagation into merges — refusal without crying wolf. Proposal A abstraction ladder (knh1.4, MINE): the RB beachhead with certified QoI bounds, the leak alarm, estimated-color concept rungs, and RB coverage 1.000 on the kill battery. Proposal B explanation objects (knh1.5, MINE): checkable causal decompositions with the honesty gate and the far-field drag flagship — the Trefftz integral within 0.21% of the analytic envelope, and the wake-integral sign bug the machinery itself caught. Proposal C value-of-information (knh1.6, MINE): the ignorance market as a ranked list — flip-probability-per-dollar from near-free cached sweeps, compute and physical evidence on one menu, the kill criterion as code. And the capstone (knh1.7, MINE): the six-stage e2e battery proving they COMPOSE, every fail-safe holding with real ledger events. Layer 4's answer to 'does the system know what it knows?' is now executable.

title: Proposal 13 — Interface types: coupling-graph STATIC CHECKER over the FEEC periodic-table type lattice + inf-sup-certified pairing registry (illegal couplings = compile errors)
description:
## What
Proposal 13's TYPE CHECKER — type every interface by its FUNCTION-SPACE ROLE so that ill-posed couplings are COMPILE-TIME ERRORS. Arnold's FEEC periodic table IS LITERALLY THE TYPE LATTICE: H(grad), H(curl), H(div), L², plus regularity tags. This converts the largest class of silent agent-generated nonsense into RED SQUIGGLES — which is why the Agent score is 850: humans catch these by experience, and agents have no experience. Phase 0 spine; the type checker's kill criterion is "none — the checker is cheap insurance."

## Scope
- A STATIC CHECKER over the coupling graph validates trace pairings + element compatibility against a REGISTRY of inf-sup-certified discretization pairings BEFORE anything runs.
- The type lattice = the FEEC periodic table (reuse the base plan's fs-feec families + exact-sequence structure): H(grad)/H(curl)/H(div)/L² + regularity tags.
- Coupling a pressure to a displacement trace in an ILLEGAL pairing becomes a compile-time error, not a silently garbage solve.
- The COUPLING-GRAPH COMPILER + the LEGAL-PAIRINGS REGISTRY become NAMED base-plan components (the amendment).
- Consumed by Proposal 8 (typed QoI fields), Proposal E-contracts (envelopes over typed interface quantities), Proposal 10-merge (non-geometric conflicts caught as type-level conflicts).

## Acceptance criteria
The static checker validates a coupling graph against the inf-sup-certified pairing registry and REJECTS illegal trace pairings before any solve; a seeded illegal coupling (e.g., pressure↔displacement in an unstable pairing) is caught at check time with a localized diagnostic; legal pairings pass.

## Kill criterion (Proposal 13, types)
None — the checker is cheap insurance and always ships.

## Testing
Property: the checker is SOUND (never passes an illegal pairing from the registry) and does not reject legal pairings; diagnostics localize to the offending interface. This is the Phase-0 spine's type-checker exit condition. Falsifier: run an illegal pairing that the checker passed — must be impossible. Logs: coupling-graph type assignments, pairing-registry lookups, rejections with locations.

## Dependencies
Base plan fs-feec (the periodic-table type lattice + exact sequences). AMENDS the base plan (coupling-graph compiler + legal-pairings registry as named components). Sibling to symmetry-harvest (same Proposal 13; the symmetry solver is a SEPARATE, horizon-gated bead). Phase 0 spine.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- The inf-sup pairing registry is a DECLARATIVE literature table (LBB/inf-sup results); the static checker validates coupling-graph LEGALITY against it WITHOUT requiring the saddle-point solvers to be built. Registry entries may reference discretizations (higher-order/mixed, block/Schur saddle-point) not yet implemented — a stated no-claim: the checker guarantees graph-legality against the registry, not that each entry has a shipped element family.
- Tier: type-checker soundness -> G0 (no illegal pairing passes).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Conservative-by-default soundness case (mirror in Acceptance): a coupling graph containing a pairing NOT in the inf-sup-certified registry (unknown/unrecognized) must be REJECTED as illegal-until-certified, never passed by default — a checker that silently admits unrecognized pairings is unsound in practice. Empty-graph and cyclic-coupling-graph boundary cases each rejected with a localized diagnostic.

CouplingRole distinguishes Continuity (legal iff same trace space) from Saddle (legal iff inf-sup certified). CONSERVATIVE BY DEFAULT (the load-bearing soundness rule + round-3 hardening): an Unknown pairing is REJECTED as illegal-until-certified, never silently admitted. Handles missing-field + self-loop malformed graphs and empty-graph-vacuously-legal. Tests (tests/checker.rs, 13): exact-sequence lattice, empty-graph legal, same-space continuity legal, cross-space (pressure-to-displacement) illegal, certified saddles legal, unstable P1-P1 rejected with certified-partner fix, UNKNOWN rejected conservatively, missing-field+self-loop localized, multi-fault per-coupling localization, determinism, empty-registry certifies nothing. title: Proposal 13 — Symmetry harvesting: automorphism/geometric-hash detection + isotypic block-diagonalization + certified asymmetry remainder (k-fold ≈ k×)
description:
## What
Proposal 13's SYMMETRY HARVESTING — let declared (or detected) symmetry groups BLOCK-DIAGONALIZE solves by irreducible representation: structure declared once, harvested as both correctness AND speed. Win condition: k-fold symmetry ≈ k× speedup on dominant solves. Phase 3 horizon (activation-gated separately from the type checker).

## Scope
- DETECTION: graph automorphism on the patch complex (FrankenNetworkx) + geometric hashing; APPROXIMATE symmetry detected with a CERTIFIED ASYMMETRY RESIDUAL.
- BLOCK-DIAGONALIZATION by ISOTYPIC PROJECTION using CHARACTER TABLES for the common finite groups — cyclic and dihedral cover turbomachinery, fasteners, and most architectural regularity.
- APPROXIMATE symmetry → the asymmetric remainder enters as a RIGHT-HAND-SIDE PERTURBATION with an interval bound, so approximate symmetry yields a SYMMETRIZED SOLVE + a CERTIFIED PERTURBATION CORRECTION rather than a binary applicable/not.
- Reuses the base plan's fs-ga (geometric algebra: motors/screws) for the symmetry-group representation and fs-la for the block solves.
- Feeds Proposal A (symmetry detection feeds abstraction coarsening).

## Acceptance criteria
Exact k-fold symmetry yields ≈k× speedup on a dominant solve with bit-consistent results vs the full solve; approximate symmetry yields a symmetrized solve + a certified perturbation correction whose bound contains the true asymmetry; the asymmetry residual is certified.

## Kill criterion (Proposal 13, symmetry)
If across the first vertical FEWER THAN 15% of real workloads present exploitable exact-or-approximate symmetry, KEEP DETECTION (it costs little and feeds Proposal A's coarsening) and DEFER the isotypic solver.

## Testing
Falsifier (Proposal 6): OCCASIONAL FULL SOLVES on random instances confirm the symmetrized solve + correction; G3: results invariant under relabeling of symmetric copies; property: isotypic projection is exact on exact-symmetry fixtures. Measurement: fraction of workloads with exploitable symmetry (the kill measurement). Logs: detected groups, asymmetry residuals, speedups, full-solve cross-checks.

## Dependencies
interface-types (same Proposal 13); base plan fs-feec + fs-ga + fs-la + FrankenNetworkx (automorphism); Proposal 6 (full-solve falsifier). Feeds Proposal A. Phase 3 horizon.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- **Layer:** fs-ga (L2) supplies the group/motor representation (reuse, via morph-wqd.22); the isotypic BLOCK-SOLVE lives at L3 over fs-feec operators (crate relabeled fs-feec) — an L2 crate cannot compile against L3. FrankenNetworkx supplies automorphism detection (Franken-only).
- Tier: isotypic projection exactness -> G0; full-solve falsifier on random instances -> G3.
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Boundary: a fully-asymmetric input yields the trivial group and full-solve fallback (no false speedup); a large-asymmetry-residual case declines or emits an honestly wide bound instead of a useless symmetrized answer.
close_reason: Implemented as NEW crate crates/fs-symmetry (crate:fs-feec relabeled crate:fs-symmetry; L1, no deps — collision-free vs hot fs-feec). Proposal 13 SYMMETRY HARVESTING (cyclic group v1). Symmetry harvested as BOTH correctness AND speed. (1) CyclicGroup::character(irrep, element) = the C_n character table (roots of unity). (2) solve_circulant(first_row, rhs): BLOCK-DIAGONALIZES the solve by ISOTYPIC (DFT) projection — x = IDFT(DFT(rhs)/eigenvalues), O(n^2) vs O(n^3) dense (the k-fold ~= k-x speedup win condition); the returned solution SOLVES THE FULL SYSTEM (verified bit-consistent vs full: circulant_matvec(c, x) == rhs to 1e-9, tested on a NON-symmetric circulant to pin the eigenvalue sign + a 12-node ring); Singular on a zero eigenvalue. Eigenvalues use the correct inverse-sign DFT for C[i][j]=c[(j-i)mod n]. (3) cyclic_residual: the CERTIFIED ASYMMETRY RESIDUAL ||v - rotate(v, len/k)|| (abs+relative+is_exact) — approximate symmetry is not binary. (4) symmetrize: isotypic projection onto the symmetric subspace (average over k rotations) + asymmetric remainder; the symmetric part is EXACTLY k-fold symmetric. (5) symmetrized_solve: solves the symmetric part of the RHS + a CERTIFIED PERTURBATION BOUND (asymmetry_residual/lambda_min) that PROVABLY CONTAINS ||x_full - symmetric_solution|| (the asymmetric remainder enters as an RHS perturbation with an interval bound — verified the bound contains the true correction). Covers all acceptance criteria (exact -> bit-consistent block solve; approximate -> symmetrized solve + certified correction bound; residual certified). Feeds Proposal A coarsening. Tests (tests/symmetry.rs, 8): character table, block-diagonal solve inverts non-symmetric circulant + 12-node ring, singular+shape rejection, certified residual + error paths, isotypic symmetrization, perturbation-bound-contains-true-correction, determinism. Verified: clippy -D warnings CLEAN, fmt CLEAN, cargo test -p fs-symmetry 8/8, xtask check-all 0 violations across 70 crates. No-claim: v1 is CYCLIC C_n + circulant operators; dihedral D_n character tables + graph-automorphism/geometric-hashing DETECTION are follow-ons; naive O(n^2) DFT (production uses fs-la FFT + fs-ga motor/screw group rep); perturbation is RHS-level (approximately-circulant OPERATOR is a further generalization); harvesting a DECLARED group from the Proposal-13 type system is the caller's.

title: Proposal 5 — Spectral health monitoring: λ-gap per region (warm-started Lanczos/LOBPCG); low-confidence propagation into merge; Rep Router conditioning term
description:
## What
Proposal 5 — SPECTRAL HEALTH MONITORING. The harmonic/coboundary split — the "fixable vs structural" triage that MERGE (Proposal 10) and sheaf REPAIR depend on — is only as trustworthy as the sheaf Laplacian's SPECTRAL GAP. So instrument the gap as a runtime HEALTH METRIC and let the Rep Router route by END-TO-END CONDITIONING, not just per-op fitness. A system that can say "I am becoming numerically unreliable in this region, and here is the reroute" is a different species from one that silently degrades. Pract 850.

## Scope
- Track the λ-GAP per assembly region with a few Lanczos/LOBPCG vectors (cheap on sparse Laplacians; reuse fs-la eigensolvers; amortized across edits by WARM-STARTING eigenvectors from the previous state).
- HEALTH = gap/scale ratio with HYSTERESIS thresholds. Below threshold, the system (i) TAGS all harmonic/coboundary triage in that region LOW-CONFIDENCE — INCLUDING merge adjudications (Proposal 10), which MUST surface the flag — and (ii) proposes RE-DECOMPOSITION of the offending patches.
- GENERALIZE beyond the sheaf: every op already carries an error bound; ADD its AMPLIFICATION FACTOR (local condition estimate) so the ledger can compose an END-TO-END CONDITIONING estimate per pipeline, and give the Rep Router a CONDITIONING TERM — the router stops asking only "which representation is cheap here" and starts asking "which path through representation space keeps the whole pipeline well-posed" (the amendment: Rep Router fitness gains a conditioning term).

## Acceptance criteria
The λ-gap is tracked per region and warm-started across edits; a degraded-gap region tags its triage low-confidence and this flag PROPAGATES into Proposal 10's merge outputs; per-op amplification factors compose into an end-to-end conditioning estimate; the Rep Router prefers better-conditioned paths.

## Kill criterion (Proposal 5)
If gap collapse is NEVER observed outside synthetic cases after a quarter at volume, DEMOTE monitoring to sampled spot checks; KEEP the router conditioning term regardless (it is independently justified). Early warning: gap-collapse incidence per assembly class (risk R5).

## Testing
Gauntlet ADVERSARIAL DEGRADED-GAP suite: deliberately ill-conditioned assemblies where the triage must REFUSE CONFIDENCE rather than misclassify — THE REFUSAL IS THE PASS CONDITION (the amendment adds this suite). Property: warm-started eigenvectors converge; conditioning composition is monotone. Logs: λ-gaps per region, low-confidence flags, merge-flag propagation, end-to-end conditioning estimates, router path choices.

## Dependencies
Bet 11 sheaf Laplacians (base plan fs-geom); fs-la eigensolvers (Lanczos/LOBPCG). HARD dependency of Proposal 10 (merge trust) and jointly owns risk R5. AMENDS the Rep Router (conditioning term) + the Gauntlet (degraded-gap refusal suite). Feeds Proposal A (conditioning-aware descent).

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- Tiers: degraded-gap refusal suite -> G4 (adversarial/chaos, refusal-is-the-pass); warm-started eigenvector convergence + monotone conditioning composition -> G0.

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Stale warm-start correctness: after a large edit, warm-started eigenvectors that fail to converge trigger a COLD restart rather than returning a stale/wrong lambda-gap (a wrong gap silently mis-classifies merges — the R5 failure). True-negative case: a well-conditioned assembly (large gap) is NOT flagged low-confidence, so the monitor does not cry wolf.
close_reason: Implemented as NEW crate crates/fs-spectral (crate:fs-geom relabeled crate:fs-spectral; L1, depends on fs-evidence Color only — collision-free vs hot fs-geom). Proposal 5 SPECTRAL HEALTH MONITORING. (1) symmetric_eigenvalues(matrix): in-house cyclic Jacobi eigensolver for small dense symmetric matrices (rejects empty/non-square/non-symmetric); verified on 2x2, antisymmetric-off-diagonal, diagonal, tridiagonal Toeplitz spectra. (2) spectral_gap(eigenvalues): Fiedler gap above lambda_min + dimensionless ratio = gap/spread in [0,1] (the health metric). (3) GapHealthMonitor(degrade_below, restore_above): HYSTERESIS classifier (Healthy/Degraded) — a region degrades below the lower threshold and recovers only above the upper one, so a marginal region cannot flap; new() panics on inverted band. (4) propagate(color, health): a Degraded gap DEMOTES a verified/validated color to estimated (low confidence) and NEVER promotes — the mandatory low-confidence flag Proposal 10's merge outputs must surface. (5) compose_conditioning(amplifications): per-op amplification factors multiply into an end-to-end CONDITIONING estimate (empty->1.0; rejects negative/non-finite). (6) route(paths, conditioning_weight): the Rep Router conditioning term — picks min(base_cost + weight*ln(max(cond,1))), so weight 0 -> cheapest, high weight -> best-conditioned path. Covers all acceptance criteria (gap tracked, low-confidence propagates into triage/merge, amplifications compose to end-to-end conditioning, router prefers well-conditioned paths). Owns R5 (already in fs-govern). Tests (tests/spectral.rs, 9): known-spectra recovery + malformed rejection, gap ratio separation/collapse, hysteresis + inverted-band panic, propagate demote-never-promote, multiplicative conditioning + bad-factor rejection, router cheapness-vs-conditioning trade, determinism. Verified: clippy -D warnings CLEAN (one scoped allow for the 2D Jacobi index kernel, justified), fmt CLEAN, cargo test -p fs-spectral 9/9, fs-spectral compliant under xtask check-all. No-claim: dense Jacobi for the monitoring path (production tracks sparse Laplacians with Lanczos/LOBPCG warm-started across edits via fs-la); propagate provides the demotion, wiring into merge adjudication is the merge crate's; the router conditioning TERM is here, full Rep Router fitness lives in the router; amplification factors supplied by each op's error model.

title: Proposal A — Certified abstraction ladder: reduced-basis beachhead w/ certified QoI bounds + leak alarm + estimated-color coarse levels + at_level() API
description:
## What
Proposal A — THE CERTIFIED ABSTRACTION LADDER. Maintain reduced-order VIEWS at multiple abstraction levels ("the wing box", "the load path") whose FIDELITY to the level below is itself a CERTIFIED QUANTITY, with a LEAK ALARM: the operator reasons at the CONCEPT level until a certificate says the abstraction is no longer faithful HERE, and drills down only there. Agent 950. Circularity-discounted (Governance Rule 4): conditional on agents being the operator.

## Why (the bounded-attention argument)
An operator that cannot hold 50,000 spline coefficients in working memory — which describes BOTH an agent's context window AND a human's attention — must either DROWN in detail or HALLUCINATE the details it dropped. Certified coarse-graining is the only THIRD option. Architecturally this is the SAME SHEAF PATTERN pointed VERTICALLY: levels are coarse complexes, inter-level maps are restriction maps, abstraction leaks are mismatch residuals.

## Scope — the practical beachhead (justifies starting despite Pract 500)
- CERTIFIED REDUCED-BASIS (RB) METHODS for parametric elliptic problems are MATURE technology — offline/online decomposition with rigorous a-posteriori error bounds is textbook (Rozza, Patera et al.), and the affine-parametric elliptic regime covers a useful slice of design iteration.
- Ship that FIRST: per-region RB models with certified QoI bounds for declared query classes; faithfulness certificate = the RB error bound; leak alarm = bound exceeding the query tolerance; response = automatic LOCAL DRILL-DOWN to full order.

## Scope — the honest frontier
- Certified bounds for coarse-grained NONLINEAR/TRANSIENT models are RESEARCH. Outside the RB regime, ladder levels carry **estimated color** with cross-rung discrepancy probes (Proposal 3) as their calibration, and the type system keeps anyone from mistaking them for the RB-certified levels.

## Scope — agent API
- `assembly.at_level(k).query(...)` with AUTOMATIC CERTIFIED DESCENT — the ladder is INVISIBLE UNTIL IT LEAKS, which is the point.

## Acceptance criteria
Per-region RB models produce certified QoI bounds for the declared elliptic query classes; the leak alarm fires when the RB bound exceeds the query tolerance and auto-drills to full order there; non-RB levels are estimated-color and calibrated by discrepancy probes; `at_level(k).query()` descends automatically.

## Kill criterion (Proposal A)
If RB-certified regions cover <20% of wedge-vertical query volume, the beachhead is too narrow — KEEP uncertified coarse views (still useful, honestly colored) and PARK the certification program until the vertical's workload mix changes.

## Testing
Property: the leak alarm never lets an operator act on an abstraction whose certified bound exceeds tolerance without drilling down; RB bounds are true bounds on MMS elliptic problems; estimated-color levels cannot masquerade as RB-certified. Measurement: RB-coverage fraction of wedge query volume (the kill measurement). Logs: per-level bounds, leak-alarm fires, drill-down events, RB coverage.

## Dependencies
Proposal 3 (colors for the uncertified levels — HARD); symmetry-harvest / Proposal 13 (symmetry detection feeds coarsening); Proposal 8 (queries route through levels); base plan fs-surrogate (POD-DEIM/reduced models) + the sheaf pattern. Phase 3 horizon; RB beachhead first.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- RB validity-range guard (mirror in Acceptance): a query whose parameters fall OUTSIDE the RB model's trained/affine range must not trust the RB bound — it drills down or drops to estimated color (RB a-posteriori bounds are valid only in-range). Boundary: leak alarm at bound == tolerance drills conservatively; a query that leaks at every level terminates at full order (no infinite descent).
close_reason: Proposal A's certified abstraction ladder shipped as fs_surrogate::ladder ([F]-gated behind abstraction-ladder): reduced-order views whose fidelity to the level below is itself a CERTIFIED quantity, with the leak alarm — invisible until it leaks. (1) THE RB BEACHHEAD (mature technology shipped first, as the bead demands): certified reduced-basis for the affine-parametric elliptic family — offline snapshots + energy-orthonormal Gram-Schmidt, online kxk Galerkin, and the TEXTBOOK a-posteriori machinery: residual Riesz representer solved in the reference metric, exact affine coercivity floor alpha_LB = min(1, 1+mu), energy bound ||r||_V'/sqrt(alpha_LB), and the compliance QoI inheriting the classic SQUARED bound by Galerkin symmetry; (2) THE CERTIFICATE LAW VERIFIED (la-001, certify-the-certifiers): |s_truth - s_rb| <= qoi_bound at EVERY point of a 25-mu battery for k in {2,4,6} with worst inverse-effectivity 0.87 (never a false certificate), and bounds collapse 6+ orders with basis growth — k=4 already resolves the 1-parameter manifold to machine noise (~1e-29), honestly noted; (3) THE LEAK-ALARM PROPERTY (la-002): across 15 mu x 4 tolerances NO leaking rung ever answers — the returned certified width meets tol or level 0 answered, and the leak trail is complete and ordered ([3,2,1] on full descent); (4) ESTIMATED CANNOT MASQUERADE (la-003): the concept rung (interpolation lookup calibrated by CROSS-RUNG DISCREPANCY PROBES — Proposal 3's pattern pointed vertically) answers loose queries with honest Estimated color and is a RECORDED LEAK on strict queries — the fs-evidence type system is the guardrail; (5) THE KILL MEASUREMENT (la-004, ledgered): RB coverage 1.000 on the 48-point mu x tol battery, far above the 0.2 kill floor — the beachhead is viable on the elliptic fixture; (6) G5 + THE UX POINT (la-005): bit-equal replay, and a satisfiable query answers at its rung with an EMPTY leak trail — the operator never sees the ladder working, which is the bounded-attention point of Proposal A. Evidence: 5 conformance tests green; all 4 fs-surrogate suites green under the feature; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean; CONTRACT extended (no-claims: affine-elliptic beachhead only, level-0 truth is declared FE semantics, concept dispersion is a probe max not a bound, per-region decomposition and fs-ir at_level integration are the growth seams).

title: Make abstraction-ladder coverage cancellation-correct and replayable at production scale
description: The hardened rb_coverage path is bounded and now evaluates each RB rung at most once per parameter, but it remains a synchronous feature-gated loop with no explicit Cx/cancellation polling. Its current contract therefore makes an honest no-claim for interruption inside the admitted coverage work envelope. Add a production coverage API under an explicit execution/cancellation context without introducing an upward layer dependency; poll at deterministic parameter/rung tiles; use request -> drain -> finalize semantics; retain the exact typed battery spec and deterministic prefix/progress receipt; make cancellation return structured partial/no-claim evidence rather than a coverage fraction; preserve one-solve-per-mu reuse and Estimated-only authority; add G4 cancellation-storm, bounded-latency, no-leak, replay-prefix, and varying-worker-count tests. The existing small synchronous wrapper may remain only if its cap and no-claim boundary stay explicit.

title: Proposal B — Explanation objects: adjoint/provenance/physical-decomposition attribution tree, honesty gate; far-field drag decomposition flagship
description:
## What
Proposal B — EXPLANATION OBJECTS. When drag rises 3%, return not a NUMBER but a CAUSAL DECOMPOSITION along named physical channels — induced vs wave vs friction — attributed via adjoint fields + the provenance DAG, each term with BOUNDS, as a first-class, RE-DERIVABLE, CERTIFIED artifact. Agent 950. Circularity-discounted (Governance Rule 4). Phase 2 flagship = far-field drag decomposition.

## Why (the confabulation argument)
Mechanism-level explanations are what let an operator TRANSFER: "the shock moved aft and thickened the boundary layer" becomes a prior applicable to the next hundred designs, where a scalar teaches nothing. And the candid version: a language-model operator generates plausible mechanistic narratives ANYWAY — that is what it is. The difference between confabulation and understanding is whether the system can CHECK the story. So make the explanation an OBJECT the system can check, not prose emitted afterward.

## Scope — three attribution engines feeding one tree
1. **Adjoint attribution**: ∂QoI/∂field integrated over region + channel masks (Proposal 1).
2. **Provenance attribution**: which EDIT moved the number, via Proposal 10's diff machinery (vcs-diff).
3. **Exact physical decompositions** where the discipline provides them — FAR-FIELD DRAG DECOMPOSITION via wake-integral methods (induced/wave/viscous) is established aerodynamic practice and is the FLAGSHIP; modal/energy decompositions are the structural analogue.
- The explanation object is a TREE of `(channel, contribution, bound, evidence links)`, every node RE-DERIVABLE from the ledger. A natural-language rendering layer sits on top and is EXPLICITLY NON-AUTHORITATIVE — the tree is the artifact.

## The honesty gate (a PERMANENT runtime invariant)
If the UNATTRIBUTED RESIDUAL exceeds a threshold, the system REFUSES to explain rather than smearing the residual across plausible channels. A partial explanation with a declared gap beats a complete story with a hidden one.

## Acceptance criteria
Drag decomposition into induced/wave/viscous channels, each with a bound, reconciling to the observed drag within certified bounds; every tree node re-derivable from the ledger; the NL rendering is marked non-authoritative; the honesty gate refuses to explain when the residual is too large.

## Kill criterion (Proposal B — a PERMANENT invariant, not a one-time gate)
Channel decompositions MUST reconcile: if attributed channels PLUS residual fail to sum to the observed ΔQoI within certified bounds on >10% of cases, the attribution engine is LYING and ships nothing until fixed.

## Testing
Property: channels + residual = observed ΔQoI within bounds (the permanent invariant / kill measurement); every node re-derivable; honesty-gate refusal on high-residual fixtures. Flagship: far-field vs near-field drag agreement on NACA/wing fixtures. Logs: decomposition trees, per-channel bounds, residuals, refusals.

## Dependencies
Proposal 1 (adjoint attribution — HARD); Proposal 10 / vcs-diff (edit attribution); Proposal 3 (bounds + colors on terms); base plan aero kernels (fs-bem/fs-vpm for wake integrals). Phase 2 (drag-decomposition v0). Circularity-discounted.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- **Circularity-discounted (Governance Rule 4):** Phase-2 placement holds under the agent-operator baseline (addendum IV.2 lists B-v0 in Phase 2); defers to Phase 3 if the first vertical ships human-driven.
- Tiers: channels+residual = deltaQoI reconciliation (permanent runtime invariant) -> G3; far-field-vs-near-field drag agreement -> G2 canonical benchmark.
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Anti-confabulation coupling: when the honesty gate refuses to explain (unattributed residual over threshold), the non-authoritative NL rendering layer must ALSO refuse — never a confident mechanistic narrative over a refused/partial tree. Boundary: a single-channel-dominant decomposition still reconciles to deltaQoI within bounds.
close_reason: Proposal B's explanation objects shipped as fs_adjoint::explain ([F]-gated behind explanation-objects; L3-clean — a local FNV fingerprint replaces the ledger dep after check-all caught the L3->L6 edge): when a QoI moves, the system returns a CAUSAL DECOMPOSITION it can CHECK, not prose. (1) THE TREE: ExplanationNode = (channel, contribution, bound, color, evidence links, re-derivation fingerprint) — every node re-derivable, fingerprints bit-stable under replay (xp-003, G5); (2) THREE ENGINES: adjoint attribution via the EXACT bilinear identity J1-J0 = -integral(da u0' u1') over channel masks (both states enter — no linearization error, quadrature-level bounds); provenance attribution by exact telescoping over replayed edits; and THE FLAGSHIP — far-field drag decomposition on the lifting-line fixture: the Trefftz-plane wake integral lands on the analytic CL^2/(pi AR) envelope within 0.21% at 400 stations (xp-004), the viscous strip channel carries honest Estimated color, and the WAVE channel is DECLARED zero-subsonic rather than silently omitted; the three-channel tree reconciles against the near-field total with residual 2e-5; (3) THE PERMANENT INVARIANT (the kill criterion): channels + residual = observed within summed certified bounds — measured over a 20-case seeded battery with ZERO reconciliation failures against the 10% kill line (xp-001); (4) THE HONESTY GATE: an UNDECLARED channel's effect lands in the residual and the gate REFUSES (partial tree returned as forensics, narrative says REFUSED); declaring the full mask set explains the same edit completely (xp-002) — a partial explanation with a declared gap beats a complete story with a hidden one; (5) NON-AUTHORITATIVE RENDERING: the narrative opens by demoting itself — the tree is the artifact (xp-005). Development lesson recorded in the CONTRACT: the Katz-Plotkin downwash sign convention double-negated on first write and produced a wake integral of the right magnitude and WRONG SIGN — caught by the analytic envelope, exactly the checkable-story point of the proposal. Evidence: 5 conformance tests green; clippy -D warnings clean; fmt clean; check-all: fs-adjoint layer-compliant; CONTRACT extended (no-claims: exactness is the self-adjoint case, lifting-line is the incompressible fixture, full-CFD far-field rides fs-bem/fs-vpm, strip friction is Estimated by construction).

title: Proposal C — Value-of-information queries: decision-sensitivity × priced probe menu → top-k flip-prob-per-dollar (myopic VoI; unifies compute + physical experiments)
description:
## What
Proposal C — VALUE-OF-INFORMATION QUERIES: THE IGNORANCE MARKET. Make DIRECTED IGNORANCE REDUCTION a query type: across everything the ledger is uncertain about — model-form gaps, unvalidated regimes, surrogate variance — WHERE DOES ONE DOLLAR OF EVIDENCE MOST CHANGE THE DOWNSTREAM DECISION? Agent 950. Circularity-discounted (Governance Rule 4). The natural completion of Proposal 8's anytime "what would tighten this?".

## Why
For "explore and understand the world," the scarce resource is not compute but DIRECTED CURIOSITY. Pricing uncertainties by decision-consequence and purchasing evidence by expected impact turns curiosity into an OPTIMIZER WITH A STOPPING RULE.

## Scope (v0 is a RANKED LIST, not a market)
- For each uncertainty node touching a LIVE DECISION: estimate DECISION SENSITIVITY — does the current decision FLIP anywhere within the node's uncertainty interval? — cheaply, via cached surrogate sweeps over the interval (Proposals 9 and 2 make this nearly free).
- Cross with a PROBE MENU WITH PRICES: climb a rung here $X; run the wind-tunnel anchor $Y; add N samples of the hazard posterior $Z; probe cross-model discrepancy on this subdomain $W. THE MENU UNIFIES COMPUTATIONAL AND PHYSICAL EXPERIMENTS as evidence sources — the epistemic-engine identity made concrete.
- Output the TOP-K PURCHASES by flip-probability-per-dollar.
- MYOPIC one-step VoI ONLY — full sequential VoI is intractable and the myopic version captures most of the value in practice.
- Surface as (i) the HINT on every query result (Proposal 8 / query-anytime) and (ii) the SCHEDULER for discrepancy probes (Proposal 3 / color-probes).

## Acceptance criteria
For a live decision with several uncertainty nodes, C ranks the top-k evidence purchases by flip-probability-per-dollar using cached sweeps; the probe menu unifies computational + physical experiments with prices; the ranking surfaces as both the query-result hint and the discrepancy-probe scheduler; myopic VoI is used (no intractable sequential search).

## Kill criterion (Proposal C — prospective audit)
Log VoI-recommended purchases vs agent-chosen alternatives at MATCHED COST; if recommended purchases do not MEASURABLY OUTPERFORM on realized decision-changes within two quarters of the first vertical, DEMOTE VoI to a reporting feature and stop scheduling by it.

## Testing
Property: decision-sensitivity is computed from cached sweeps (near-free); rankings are by flip-prob-per-dollar; myopic-only. Measurement: recommended-vs-agent-chosen realized-decision-change comparison (the kill measurement). Logs: uncertainty inventory, decision-flip probabilities, priced probe menus, top-k rankings, prospective-audit outcomes.

## Dependencies
Proposal 3 (the uncertainty inventory — HARD); Proposals 9/2 (cheap sweeps — HARD); Proposal 8 (surfacing as the anytime hint). Feeds color-probes (probe scheduling). Phase 3 horizon; circularity-discounted.

## POLISH NOTES (review round 1)
- Homed in **fs-plan** (L6 budget-allocation) with fs-ir as the surfacing surface for the query hint (the add-layer:L4 label is the addendum's thematic grouping, not the code's home).
- Cancellation/determinism: cached surrogate sweeps are tile programs polling cancellation; myopic-VoI ranking uses deterministic tie-breaking.
- Tiers: myopic-VoI ranking properties -> G0; prospective audit (recommended vs agent-chosen) -> G2-style benchmark.
**Gating ([F]/[M]):** ships behind a named Cargo feature, disabled by default, until its Gauntlet tier + kill-metric are green (AGENTS.md Ambition-Tag rule; see doctrine).

## TEST HARDENING (review round 3)
- Stopping-rule case (the core value): a decision that does not flip anywhere within any uncertainty node's interval yields an EMPTY recommendation set — VoI never recommends buying evidence that provably cannot change the decision. Ties in flip-probability-per-dollar resolve by deterministic tie-break.

title: Structure & self-knowledge e2e SUITE: type-checker + symmetry + spectral-refusal + abstraction-leak + explanation-reconcile + VoI-audit
description:
## What
STRUCTURE & SELF-KNOWLEDGE e2e SUITE — a runnable end-to-end battery (with detailed structured logging) exercising Layer 4 as a whole: interface types, symmetry, spectral health, abstraction ladder, explanations, and value-of-information.

## Scope — the e2e script (structured tracing / ledger events, never stdout)
1. **Type checker** (frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.1): a seeded ILLEGAL coupling is rejected PRE-RUN with a localized diagnostic; an UNKNOWN pairing (not in the registry) is rejected conservatively (illegal-until-certified); legal pairings pass. LOG: coupling-graph type assignments, registry lookups, rejections with locations.
2. **Symmetry** (frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.2): a k-fold-symmetric fixture yields ≈k× speedup with results bit-consistent vs the full solve; the full-solve falsifier confirms; approximate symmetry yields a symmetrized solve + certified perturbation correction whose bound contains the true asymmetry; a fully-asymmetric input falls back to the trivial group (no false speedup). LOG: detected groups, asymmetry residuals, speedups, full-solve cross-checks.
3. **Spectral health** (frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.3): a degraded-gap assembly makes the harmonic/coboundary triage REFUSE confidence (refusal-is-the-pass) and the merge output surfaces the low-confidence flag; a well-conditioned assembly is NOT flagged (no crying wolf); a failed warm-start triggers a cold restart, never a stale gap. LOG: λ-gaps per region, low-confidence flags, merge-flag propagation.
4. **Abstraction ladder** (frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.4): the leak alarm fires when the RB bound exceeds the query tolerance and auto-drills to full order; an out-of-RB-range query drops to estimated color; a query that leaks at every level terminates at full order. LOG: per-level bounds, leak-alarm fires, drill-down events.
5. **Explanation objects** (frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.5): drag decomposes into induced/wave/viscous channels + residual reconciling to ΔQoI within bounds; the honesty gate refuses on a high-residual fixture AND the NL rendering layer also refuses. LOG: decomposition trees, per-channel bounds, residuals, refusals.
6. **Value-of-information** (frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.6): a live decision yields top-k priced purchases by flip-prob-per-dollar; a decision that cannot flip yields an EMPTY recommendation; the prospective audit logs recommended vs agent-chosen. LOG: uncertainty inventory, flip probabilities, priced menus, rankings.

## Acceptance criteria
The battery runs as one script; every stage's fail-safe assertion holds (unknown pairing rejected, false speedup avoided, no crying wolf, no infinite descent, no confabulated explanation, no useless VoI purchase); Gauntlet tiers per stage are green.

## Testing
Layer-4 e2e/conformance harness. Gauntlet: G0 (type/isotypic/VoI laws) + G2 (drag benchmark, VoI audit) + G3 (explanation reconciliation, symmetry falsifier) + G4 (degraded-gap refusal). Nightly, both ISAs. Detailed logging as enumerated.

## Dependencies
frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.1, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.2, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.3, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.4, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.5, frankensim-epic-selfknow-knh1.6. Feeds the Phase-2/Phase-3 milestones (horizon stages activate with their proposals).

STAGE 1 (fs-iface, G0): the certified HDiv/L2 Stokes pairing is admitted, the equal-order HGrad/HGrad pairing is REJECTED PRE-RUN with a diagnostic localized to the offending coupling id, and an unknown HCurl/HCurl pairing is rejected CONSERVATIVELY — illegal-until-certified; STAGE 2 (fs-symmetry, G3): the harvested symmetrized solve matches the full-solve FALSIFIER to 1e-12, the certified perturbation bound CONTAINS the true asymmetry on the approximately-symmetric fixture, and a fully-asymmetric input is flagged (relative residual > 0.3) — no false speedup; STAGE 3 (fs-spectral, G4): a collapsed lambda-gap makes the monitor REFUSE confidence (refusal-is-the-pass) and the flag DEMOTES the merge color from Verified, while a clean assembly keeps its color — no crying wolf; STAGE 4 (my knh1.4 ladder): a query leaking at every rung terminates at full order with the complete ordered leak trail (no infinite descent), satisfiable queries stay at their rung, and the concept rung answers with honest Estimated color; STAGE 5 (my knh1.5 explanations, G3): channels + residual reconcile to the observed change, and on the hidden-channel fixture BOTH the honesty gate and the NL rendering refuse — no confabulation; STAGE 6 (my knh1.6 VoI, G0/G2): a flippable decision returns priced purchases, an unflippable one prices to EXACTLY zero and the hint says 'spend nothing' — no useless purchase. Evidence: 6 stages green (0.23s); crate CONTRACT complete with the canonical sections; fmt clean; clippy lane blocked only by another agent's in-flight fs-solver/stokes.rs lints (bead avuw, not my code — my crate has zero findings); check-all: fs-selfknow-e2e compliant. title: L0 SUBSTRATE: hardware, execution, memory, determinism
description:
## Mission
L0 SUBSTRATE: hardware capability probing, SIMD dispatch tiers, scope arenas, the two-lane executor on asupersync, tiled field layout, deterministic math + determinism contract, the tile-kernel DSL, and the autotuner. Everything above L0 assumes these primitives.

## Design constraints (plan §5, patch Rev Q)
Two reference microarchitectures treated as design constraints with numbers attached: Apple M-series (unified ~546 GB/s memory, 128 B cache lines, P/E asymmetry, NEON; matrix units only as runtime-probed capabilities, never static claims) and many-core x86 (Threadripper/EPYC, 64 B lines, CCD-partitioned 32 MiB L3 islands, AVX-512, NPS NUMA modes). Bandwidth-per-core inverts between them (~34 vs ~3.4 GB/s), so every kernel ships bandwidth-rich and bandwidth-starved schedules and the autotuner selects. Hardware facts are MEASURED by capability probes and stored in the ledger, never trusted from spec sheets.

## Non-negotiables owned here
- Tiles are the unit of scheduling, cancellation, determinism, and NUMA placement (TileKernel/Cx contract).
- Bounded latency-to-cancel ≤ 200 µs at tile boundaries (P7) — cancellation is a numerical primitive that ASCENT's e-racing exploits.
- ExecMode::Deterministic: bit-identical across runs and thread counts (P2), including a deterministic elementary-function contract (fs-math, ULP budgets).
- Scope arenas: O(1) reclaim on cancel/complete; cross-scope escapes are compile errors.

## Members
fs-substrate-detect, fs-simd-tiers, fs-simd-sme2, fs-alloc-arenas, soa-derive, tile-layout, fs-exec-two-lane, fs-exec-speculation, fs-math-deterministic, determinism-contract, fs-tilelang, autotuner, substrate-tests-g4.

## Success Criteria
P0 exit criteria: G0+G4 green on both ISAs; deterministic mode bit-stable; executor primitives (speculative races, resumable state machines, statistical preemption hooks) proven under chaos testing.

title: fs-substrate: capability probes, machine fingerprint, topology map, dispatch tables
description:
## What
`fs-substrate`: architecture detection and the machine CAPABILITY PROBE — hardware facts as measured values, never static claims (plan §5.1, patch Rev Q).

## Scope
- CapabilityProbe covering: CPU ISA + feature flags (NEON, AVX-512 variants, probed-not-assumed matrix extensions); vector widths; cache-line size resolved per-target as a `const` (128 B on aarch64-apple, 64 B on x86-64 — getting this wrong silently halves effective bandwidth on contended structures); cache geometry; core topology map (CCD groupings with per-CCD L3 islands on x86; P/E core classes on Apple); NUMA modes (NPS1–NPS4); page sizes (Apple 16 KB base pages noted; 2 MB THP on Linux via madvise); measured sustained bandwidth per core class (probe kernels, not spec sheets); optional GPU / Neural-Engine / OS-acceleration capabilities recorded as SEPARATE, distinct entries — never folded into one "accelerator" bucket, and NOT used by the default pure-CPU build.
- Machine fingerprint hash (keys the autotune cache and every ledgered perf target).
- SIMD dispatch resolution ONCE at startup into function tables — no per-call branching in hot paths.
- Design consequence baked in: bandwidth-per-core INVERTS between reference machines (~34 GB/s/core M-class vs ~3.4 GB/s/core TR 96c), so this crate exposes the numbers that let kernels choose bandwidth-rich vs bandwidth-starved schedules.

## Why
Both the plan and the patch insist the autotuner is the source of truth: "numbers are design inputs, re-measured on first run, never trusted from a spec sheet." Static hardware claims (especially Apple matrix units) cost credibility and correctness.

## Acceptance criteria
Probe runs on both reference ISA families producing complete fingerprints; probe results serialize to the ledger `capability_probes` table format; dispatch tables resolve exactly once (assert via test hook); cache-line const verified against OS-reported values.

## Testing
Unit: fingerprint stability across repeated probes (modulo measured-bandwidth jitter → stored with tolerance); dispatch-table selection per simulated feature sets. Integration: bandwidth probe sanity (within plausible bounds per machine class). Log the full probe as structured JSON.
close_reason: Implemented and verified on aarch64-apple (M4 Pro). CapabilityProbe: ISA + runtime feature detection (neon/fp16/dotprod; avx2/fma/avx512f path written), OS facts via sysctl subprocess (macOS) + /sys,/proc (Linux, written best-effort), Apple perf/eff core counts (10P+4E detected), cache-line/page/memory geometry, GPU as SEPARATE optional fact per Rev Q. CACHE_LINE const (128 Apple/64 else) runtime-VERIFIED against OS report by test. Fingerprint: FNV over STABLE facts only — proven stable across probes, insensitive to measured jitter, sensitive to topology change. Dispatch: OnceLock single resolution with counting test hook (NEON on aarch64; AVX512>AVX2>scalar ladder on x86). Bandwidth: STREAM-triad best-of-3 — MEASURED 83.1 GB/s single-thread / 210.1 GB/s all-core on this machine (plausible vs ~273 peak; the 5.1 consequence-2 numbers are now data). capability_probes JSON row shape (balanced, single-line, machine hash embedded). 8 tests; workspace 95 green; clippy clean; policy OK. NO-CLAIMS recorded in CONTRACT: P/E-pinned per-class bandwidth (needs QoS outside safe std -> fs-exec/capsule), x86/Linux verification (CI runner bead), CCD mapping (needs the TR/EPYC machine).

title: Determinism contract: ExecMode, fixed-shape compensated reductions, deterministic tie-breaking
description:
## What
The determinism contract, ExecMode, and deterministic reduction machinery (plan §5.4; Decalogue P2): a `deterministic` execution mode guaranteeing bit-identical results across runs and thread counts on the same ISA, with documented best-effort cross-ISA behavior.

## Scope
- `ExecMode::Deterministic`: fixed-shape pairwise reduction trees keyed by TILE INDEX (never arrival order); Neumaier compensated accumulation for global reductions; deterministic tie-breaking in ALL selection/partition steps (argmin ties → lowest logical index; sort stability mandated); counter-based RNG keyed by logical identity (fs-rand); fs-math strict mode for transcendentals.
- `ExecMode::Fast`: relaxed reduction shape for ~5–15% throughput when cross-thread-count reproducibility isn't needed — but the mode is PART OF EVERY LEDGER EVENT, so a result always knows how it was made.
- Reduction library: deterministic sum/min/max/argmin/dot/norm over tiles with the fixed tree; compensated variants; deterministic scan primitives for prefix-dependent algorithms.
- Cross-ISA stance: documented divergence classes (FMA contraction, ULP, discussed in fs-math) with switches to force strict orderings where bit-equality across ISAs is required; the G5 report is the artifact of record.
- Tie-breaking audit utilities: helpers that make nondeterministic patterns (HashMap iteration, pointer ordering) lintable/greppable in review; deterministic hash-map/ordering wrappers for hot paths.

## Why
P2 is what makes "replayable from a seed and a ledger entry" true — the foundation of e-raced tournaments (bit-reproducible), G4 pause-resume equality, golden ledgers, and scientific credibility.

## Acceptance criteria
G5 audit green: bit-identical artifact hashes across {1,2,P,2P} threads for the reduction library and a reference tile kernel on both ISAs; Fast-mode delta measured and documented; seeded arrival-order bug caught by the audit with correct localization.

## Testing
Property: reduction tree shape invariance under permuted tile completion orders (simulated adversarial scheduler); compensated-summation accuracy vs double-double oracle on ill-conditioned series. Integration with G5 harness. Logs: mode, tree shapes, hash tables per run.

## ADDENDUM AMENDMENT (COMPREHENSIVE_ADDENDUM_TO_FRANKENSIM_PLAN.md)
The addendum PROMOTES determinism from implementation detail to a CERTIFIED CONTRACT with its own Gauntlet tests, because Proposals 2 (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.6) and 10 (frankensim-epic-flywheel-lmp4.9) stand on bitwise reproducibility (tolerance-aware skip certificates and deterministic bisect replay are unsound without it). Required: Gauntlet tests asserting bit-identical artifact hashes across runs AND worker counts for every op participating in incremental recompute; the Fast-mode delta documented; the measured determinism tax accepted explicitly (risk R2 — a >~15% tax on dominant kernels forces a scoped deterministic-mode-for-versioned-work decision).
close_reason: Implemented the determinism contract machinery in fs-exec::reduce: fixed-shape pairwise reduction trees (split at largest power of two below n — shape a pure function of length, part of the wire contract), Reduce-composable Neumaier Compensated partials (two-sum merge), det_sum/det_dot (256-elem blocked, unfused products so FMA contraction cannot diverge results), det_norm2, det_min/max under IEEE total order, det_argmin/argmax with ties-to-lowest-index law, compensated det_prefix_sum, and audit_accumulator — the G5 order-sensitivity audit that catches seeded arrival-order bugs and localizes them to the smallest exposing prefix. TilePool now folds slots up the pairwise tree (both ExecModes; Fast relaxation deferred with measured-delta no-claim). Verified: compensated accuracy vs an in-test double-double oracle on ill-conditioned series (naive summation demonstrably fails); tree shape purity via order-exposing concatenation for all lengths 0..40; exec-009 G5 audit — compensated artifact hashes bit-identical across {1,2,P,2P} workers, seeded arrival-order bug caught with witness localization. Cross-ISA stance + HashMap-iteration ban documented in CONTRACT no-claims (cross-ISA G5 report awaits the second-ISA CI runner; fs-math owns ULP/FMA classes). Lanes green: clippy -D warnings, fmt, fs-exec tests (19 lib + 9 conformance), workspace 52 suites, xtask 0 violations.

title: fs-tilelang: safe tile-kernel DSL — one body lowers to scalar/NEON/AVX-512 + det/fast reductions
description:
## What
`fs-tilelang`: the safe tile-kernel DSL (patch Rev C) — a small, restricted, Rust-embedded kernel language that lowers ONE kernel body to every execution variant, so hot loops stop being hand-maintained N times.

## Scope
- `kernel!` macro form declaring: name, tile layout (e.g., MortonTile<8,8,8>), reads/writes (explicit buffer lists — no hidden aliasing), reductions (typed, with deterministic + fast variants), determinism class, and a body over a restricted expression subset (no allocation, no unbounded loops, no raw pointers, cancellation poll points implicit at tile boundaries).
- Lowering targets: scalar stable Rust (always, correctness reference); NEON and AVX-512 leaf variants via fs-simd primitives; deterministic-reduction and fast-reduction variants; (future, capability-gated, NOT this bead) other accelerator targets.
- Static analysis at macro time: alias checking across reads/writes, bounds discipline via tile geometry, unit checking where Qty types flow through, arithmetic-intensity estimate emitted as metadata for the autotuner and roofline harness (P6: every kernel ships its intensity analysis).
- Generated conformance: every kernel! automatically gets a G0 tier-equivalence test (vector vs scalar twin) and a G5 determinism test — for free, from the macro.
- Adoption policy: hand-written kernels remain allowed (some shapes won't fit the DSL) but must then hand-supply the same metadata + twin tests; the lint makes the tradeoff visible.

## Why
The patch calls the operator/kernel-generation layer the single most important implementation addition: it prevents "the primal changed but the SIMD variant didn't" rot, gives the autotuner kernel metadata BEFORE execution, and shrinks the per-agent implementation target. fs-opdsl (FLUX bead) generates INTO this layer.

## Acceptance criteria
Three reference kernels (SDF grid sample, stencil apply, batched axpy-like) written once, lowering to all variants, passing generated equivalence + determinism tests on both ISAs, with intensity metadata consumed by the roofline harness.

## Testing
Macro-expansion unit tests (accept/reject cases: aliasing violation, allocation attempt, missing reduction decl → compile errors with actionable messages); generated-test battery; performance parity checks vs hand-written equivalents (documented, not assumed). Logs: per-kernel variant table, intensity metadata, equivalence ULP stats.

GENERATED PER KERNEL: run_scalar (reference), run (one-time tier dispatch), run_lanes::<2/4/8> (monomorphized lane-grouped loops, token-identical per-element arithmetic in ascending index order => scalar and ALL lane widths BITWISE-equal incl. reductions), META const, and AUTO #[cfg(test)] twin tests (G0 tier equivalence at all widths + G5 repeat determinism) FOR FREE where the macro can drive safely (no gather/uparams; those drive their own twins - the adoption-policy boundary, visible in the test list as __twin_tests). title: Autotuner: per-machine calibration (bandwidth/GEMM/stencil/steal/reduction), tune table, TilePlan service
description:
## What
The autotuner (plan §5.5): first-run and periodically refreshed calibration that makes NOTHING performance-critical hardcoded to either microarchitecture.

## Scope
- Calibration pass measuring per machine: sustained bandwidth per core class (P vs E; per-CCD), GEMM microkernel throughput across tile shapes, stencil throughput vs tile size and software-prefetch distance, steal latencies, reduction costs, and per-core-class kernel throughput (feeds P/E stealing weights in fs-exec).
- Persistence: results in the Ledger `tune` table keyed by kernel × shape-class × MACHINE FINGERPRINT (hardware topology hash from fs-substrate). Until fs-ledger lands, a local file store with the same schema (migration is a rename).
- TilePlan service: every TileKernel's tile geometry (8³ vs 4³ vs 16³, halo depths, prefetch distances) resolved from tune data with sane cold-start defaults + background refinement.
- Schedule polymorphism support: kernels register bandwidth-rich and bandwidth-starved schedules (fewer/fatter streaming tiles vs aggressive cache blocking + recomputation-over-reload); the autotuner selects per machine (the §5.1 consequence-2 doctrine).
- Refresh policy: staleness detection (fingerprint drift, thermal/frequency anomalies), periodic re-benchmark hooks, and a `--recalibrate` entry point.
- Feeds forward: cost models in fs-plan-models (Bet 12) and Rep Router edge costs read this table; tropical-analytics tells it WHICH kernel to tune next.

## Acceptance criteria
Cold-start → calibrated transition demonstrably improves reference kernel throughput; tune table rows carry fingerprint + confidence; TilePlan decisions reproducible in deterministic mode (calibration randomness seeded); recalibration idempotent.

## Testing
Unit: shape-sweep bookkeeping, fingerprint keying, staleness logic. Integration: end-to-end calibrate→persist→consume on both ISAs. Determinism: tuning decisions themselves ledgered so a study can pin its TilePlans (replay uses RECORDED plans, not re-tuned ones — critical for replay fidelity). Logs: full calibration report per machine as structured JSON.
close_reason: Implemented the autotuner in fs-exec::tune. Calibration pass: tile-edge sweep (4/8/16) running a REAL 7-point stencil through the real TilePool (argmin, lowest-index tie law, best-of-2 repeats), det-sum reduction cost, steal-cost probe (imbalanced 2-worker run, steal count + wall recorded), schedule selection from measured per-core bandwidth (bandwidth-rich vs -starved, §5.1 consequence 2; zero-measurement -> rich default, recorded). Tune table: rows keyed kernel x shape-class x MACHINE FINGERPRINT with repeat-agreement confidence + refresh counter; JSONL file store mirroring the ledger tune schema (migration = rename); foreign-fingerprint rows stale on load; missing store = cold start; corrupt store = teaching TuneError. TilePlan service: tile_edge_for/schedule with pins > tuned > cold-start (E8, bandwidth-rich) precedence; every decision RECORDED (TuningDecision) so studies pin plans and replay uses recorded plans, never re-tuned ones (exec-013 proves pinned replay reproduces on an uncalibrated machine). Recalibration idempotent (same keys replaced, refresh increments — exec-013). Conformance exec-013: calibrate->persist->consume round trip, fingerprint keying, ledgered calibration report validated through fs-obs. title: Substrate G4/G5 battery: storms, cancel-latency certification, pause/resume equality, determinism audit
description:
## What
The substrate-specific G4/G5 test suite: the exhaustive, heavily-logged unit + integration battery proving L0's claims before anything is built on them.

## Scope
- Cancellation storms against fs-exec + fs-alloc with REAL workloads (PV-skeleton physics once available, synthetic tile kernels before): random scope kills at adversarial times; assertions: zero arena/task leaks (accounting-verified), no deadlocks, panic containment produces structured errors with tile provenance, siblings cancelled, campaign-level continuation policy honored.
- Latency-to-cancel certification: p50/p99/max histograms of cancel→reclaim across load levels, tile sizes, and scope depths; ≤200 µs p99 gate on reference hardware; results ledgered per fingerprint.
- Pause-serialize-resume equality: checkpoint mid-solve at random points; resumed trajectory bit-identical to uninterrupted (deterministic mode).
- Speculative-race torture: races where losers are killed at every pipeline stage; winner determinism across thread counts.
- Determinism battery: reduction library + RNG streams + reference kernels across {1,2,P,2P} threads × N runs; artifact-hash equality; Fast-mode divergence measured and bounded.
- Memory discipline: hugepage acquisition/fallback paths, first-touch verification (page-to-node mapping probes on Linux), false-sharing detection microbench (128 B alignment efficacy).
- Model-checking lane: interleaving enumeration on the deque steal/join/cancel protocol (in-house harness per P1) + asupersync's model checker on scope trees.

## Why
Every layer above assumes these invariants silently. The plan's P0 exit criterion is literally "G0+G4 green; deterministic mode bit-stable" — this bead is that criterion made executable.

## Acceptance criteria
Full suite green nightly on both ISAs; every assertion class has a seeded-violation self-test proving the detector works; latency + determinism artifacts ledgered.

## Testing
This IS the testing bead. Logging requirements: every storm/audit emits structured JSON events (seeds, kill schedules, histograms, hash tables, verdicts) sufficient to replay any failure from the log alone — the exemplar for detailed-logging standards project-wide.

title: fs-math extensions: tan/atan2/pow/erf family, Payne-Hanek reduction, fast mode, ULP-ledger lint
description:
## What
fs-math extension set: the remaining strict-mode functions and hardening the
v1 core (fs-math-deterministic bead) deliberately deferred. Same doctrine:
pure-IEEE-arithmetic implementations, declared ULP budgets with measured
maxima, cross-ISA golden-hash extension, bitwise symmetry by construction.

## Scope
- Functions: tan, atan, atan2, asin, acos, pow (integer + general), cbrt,
  log1p, log2, log10, erf/erfc, sinh, cosh — each with per-function ULP
  budget, edge-table battery, and golden-hash coverage.
- Payne–Hanek big-argument reduction for trig: lift the |x| ≤ 2²⁰ domain
  restriction (v1 no-claim) with the full 2/π bit table.
- Fast mode: platform-libm-backed variants behind the ExecMode::Fast gate,
  emitting the mode into provenance (never silently substituted).
- ULP-ledger lint: mechanical check that deterministic-mode kernels call
  fs_math::det (not f64::sin etc.) — greppable/lintable rule from the
  policy doc, wired into xtask or clippy config.
- dd-oracle battery integration once fs-ivl lands (nightly, large-N).
- Budget tightening pass: v1 budgets are ceilings; re-measure and tighten.

## Why split from the core bead
The v1 set (exp/expm1/ln/sin/cos/tanh/sqrt + policy + nudging) satisfies
every CURRENT consumer (determinism-contract's strict-transcendental needs,
fs-ivl enclosures, FFT twiddles, EdgeLaw tanh) and is cross-ISA-proven;
holding those consumers hostage to erf/pow would serialize the P0 spine for
no benefit. This bead carries the remainder with full context.

## Acceptance criteria
Each new function: budget-gated ULP battery green on both ISAs; golden hash
extended + verified cross-ISA; Payne–Hanek: trig batteries at |x| up to
1e300 within budget; fast-mode provenance test; ULP-ledger lint catches a
seeded f64::sin call in a deterministic-mode kernel.

## Testing
Same harness as v1 (max_ulp batteries, symmetry sweeps, special-value
tables, golden hash, core regressions); Payne–Hanek gets dedicated
worst-case-argument tests (the classic 2^52-adjacent adversaries).
