title: fs-simd: scalar baseline + NEON/AVX-512 capsules behind safe facades + experimental portable tier
description:
## What
`fs-simd`: the SIMD tier system — stable-Rust-first, per the patch Rev Q correction (std::simd/portable_simd is nightly-experimental, so it CANNOT be the committed baseline).

## Scope
- Tier 0 (committed baseline): scalar stable Rust, written so the autovectorizer has a fair chance (no aliasing hazards, explicit chunking) — correctness reference for every other tier.
- Tier 1: `std::arch` target-specific leaf kernels behind SAFE FAÇADES — NEON (aarch64) and AVX-512 (x86-64) intrinsics inside registered unsafe capsules (<300 lines each, SAFETY.md per unsafe-safety-cases bead).
- Tier 2 (experimental, feature-flagged): nightly portable-SIMD path for ergonomic exploration; never load-bearing.
- Uniform kernel-facing API: lane-width-agnostic primitives (fma, gather-ish patterns where supported, masked ops, horizontal reductions with FIXED tree shape for determinism), alignment helpers keyed to the 128-byte unconditional alignment policy (superset of both targets).
- Dispatch integration: fs-substrate resolves tables at startup; fs-simd provides the per-ISA implementations. Every intrinsic capsule has a scalar twin, and G0 property tests assert tier equivalence (exact for integer/logic ops; ULP-bounded for float, coordinated with fs-math contracts).

## Why
Plan §5.1 tier list adjusted by patch Rev Q: pretending portable-SIMD is stable would bake nightly into the foundation. The scalar twin + capsule discipline keeps P1 (memory safety) honest while still hitting roofline targets.

## Acceptance criteria
NEON + AVX-512 + scalar tiers for the core primitive set; tier-equivalence property suite green on both ISAs; all capsules registered with SAFETY.md; Miri-clean on capsule tests (via façade where Miri can't see intrinsics, plus interpreter-level checks on the scalar twin).

## Testing
G0 tier-equivalence laws (random inputs incl. subnormals, NaN, ±0); alignment-violation negative tests; per-primitive microbenches feeding the roofline harness. Logs: tier chosen, capability flags, equivalence-test ULP histograms.

title: fs-alloc: scope arenas (O(1) cancel reclaim), 128B alignment, hugepages, pools, site tracking
description:
## What
`fs-alloc`: scope arenas, pools, and hugepage-backed memory — the memory discipline of plan §5.3.

## Scope
- Scope arenas: bump allocators tied 1:1 to asupersync scopes; cancellation or completion reclaims in O(1); cross-scope escapes are COMPILE ERRORS (lifetimes do the enforcement — the arena's allocations borrow the scope). This is what makes speculative-race loser reclamation and e-racing kills instantaneous and leak-free.
- Long-lived artifacts "graduate" explicitly to the content-addressed store (ledger) — no silent promotion.
- 128-byte alignment UNCONDITIONALLY (superset of both targets' cache lines): padding + false-sharing avoidance helpers.
- Hugepage-backed arenas for field storage: 2 MB via madvise/THP on Linux; document Apple 16 KB base-page behavior; graceful fallback with the choice recorded.
- Pools for recurring same-shape allocations (tiles, small matrices) with per-CCD sharding hooks (first-touch by owning worker — the NUMA story from §5.1 consequence 3).
- Allocation-site tracking: lightweight tagging so memory usage feeds the Ledger and regressions are DIFFABLE between runs (§5.3).
- Unsafe capsules: the bump-pointer core and mmap wrappers, registered per unsafe-safety-cases with full SAFETY.md, Miri + fuzz coverage.

## Why
P7 (cancellation) and Bet 8 (e-racing) are only real if reclamation is O(1) and leak-proof; G4 storms assert exactly that via this crate's accounting. Arena scoping is also the anti-fragmentation strategy for 10⁸-cell field campaigns.

## Acceptance criteria
Arena lifecycle correct under G4 storms (zero leaks across 10⁶ random cancellations); escape attempts fail to compile (compile-fail battery); hugepage acquisition verified where supported; accounting reports match actual usage.

## Testing
Unit: alignment, growth, reset, OOM behavior (structured error, not abort). Property: interleaved alloc/cancel sequences preserve accounting invariants. Concurrency: arenas under parallel tile writers (Miri + storm). Logs: per-scope byte counts, hugepage status, allocation-site tables.

Compile-fail battery proves escape/Drop/Sync rejection. Conformance alloc-001..009: G0 shadow-model + disjointness, G4 10^6-cancellation storm (quiescent, zero leaks), G5 deterministic reports. Lanes green: check, clippy -D warnings (crate), fmt, workspace tests (43 suites), xtask check-all (0 violations), cargo miri test --lib (24 tests). asupersync scope BINDING deliberately deferred to fs-exec (wf9.7) per contract; arena lifetime discipline is the primitive it consumes.

title: #[derive(Soa)]: in-house structure-of-arrays proc-macro with alignment + FrankenNumpy views
description:
## What
`#[derive(Soa)]`: the in-house structure-of-arrays proc-macro (plan §5.3) — ours because P1 forbids external runtime deps and because it must integrate with our alignment/arena/tile conventions.

## Scope
- Derive macro turning an AoS struct into an SoA container: per-field arrays, 128-byte aligned, arena-allocatable, with zip-style iteration, gather/scatter to AoS views, and length/capacity management.
- SIMD-friendly accessors: per-field slices exposed in chunk sizes matching fs-simd lane widths; masked tail handling.

- Derive-time diagnostics: clear compile errors for unsupported field types; no silent fallbacks.

## Why
"Structure-of-arrays everywhere hot" is a memory-discipline pillar; batched-small-dense (fs-la-batched) and LBM lattices depend on SIMD lanes running ACROSS elements, which is only natural in SoA.

## Acceptance criteria
Macro handles nested plain-old-data structs, generics with bounds, and Qty-typed fields; generated code passes clippy -D warnings; zero-copy FrankenNumpy view round-trips.

Unit: layout/alignment assertions (addresses mod 128 == 0), AoS↔SoA round-trip equality, iterator equivalence vs scalar reference. Compile-fail battery for unsupported shapes. Property tests over random struct contents. Logs: generated layout descriptions in test output for auditability.

title: Tile layout: Morton 8-cubed tiled fields, TileId identity, halos, CCD sharding, first-touch
description:
## What
Morton/tile-major field layout primitives (plan §5.3): fields live in Z-order tiles (8³ default; 4³/16³ autotuned), the layout that is simultaneously stencil-friendly, sparse-friendly (FrankenVDB leaves align to it), cache-oblivious-ish, and — critically — gives spatial work NATURAL TILE IDENTITIES for the executor (scheduling, cancellation, determinism, and NUMA placement are all keyed by tile).

## Scope
- Morton encode/decode (BMI2 PDEP/PEXT capsule on x86, magic-bits fallback; scalar twin), tile iteration orders (linear, Z-order, boundary-first), tile↔world coordinate maps.
- Tiled field container: dense 3D array of 8³ tiles with per-tile metadata (occupancy mask hooks for sparse use, first-touch ownership tag, dirty flags for incremental algorithms); f32-storage/f64-evaluate option (the SDF chart convention).
- Ghost/halo exchange helpers for stencil kernels: tile-local halo copies with deterministic ordering, prefetch-distance hooks (autotuned later).
- Shard-by-CCD placement: tile→worker affinity map produced with fs-substrate topology; first-touch initialization by the owning worker.
- TileId scheme: stable (grid-hash, tile-coord) identity used by Cx RNG keying, deterministic reductions, and ledger events — the SAME identity everywhere, which is what makes results independent of which worker ran which tile (P2 foundation).

## Acceptance criteria
Encode/decode bijective across domain sizes; halo exchange equivalence vs naive gather; affinity maps respect CCD boundaries on x86 fixture topologies; layout benchmarked vs linear layout on a reference stencil (expect wins documented, not assumed).

## Testing
Property: Morton bijection, neighborhood locality bounds. Unit: halo correctness at domain edges (all BC paddings), tile iteration completeness. Perf smoke into roofline harness. Logs: tile geometry choices, affinity tables, halo timings.

Conformance sub-001..006 incl. tiled-vs-linear stencil smoke (bitwise agreement; timings emitted as benchmark_result events — documented, not claimed). title: fs-exec: two-lane executor — latency lane + CCD/P-E-aware work-stealing tile lane, Cx contract
description:
## What
`fs-exec`: the two-lane executor on asupersync — the beating heart of L0 (plan §5.2).

## Scope
- Latency lane: asupersync's native async scheduling for orchestration — ledger I/O, IR interpretation, progress streaming, watchdogs, inter-study coordination. Milliseconds matter, throughput doesn't. Serves HELM's ≤100 ms conversational guarantee even while campaigns saturate compute.
- Throughput lane: work-stealing fork-join pool — per-core Chase–Lev-style deques; CCD-AWARE STEAL ORDER (steal within CCD first, then socket) so working sets stay in their 32 MiB L3 islands; P/E asymmetry handled by per-core-class throughput weights (E-cores take proportionally smaller tile quanta rather than being ignored or stalling joins — weights measured by the autotuner).
- The TileKernel contract (Appendix B): `tiles() -> TilePlan` (geometry decided by autotuner), `run(TileId, &Cx) -> ControlFlow<Cancelled, Out>` with `Out: Reduce` on a FIXED-SHAPE reduction tree. Tiles are the unit of scheduling, cancellation, determinism, and NUMA placement.
- `Cx` carries: cancellation token (poll at tile boundaries; bounded latency-to-cancel ≤200 µs target), tile-scoped bump arena, counter-based RNG stream keyed by (seed, kernel_id, tile_id, iteration) — LOGICAL identity, not thread identity — budget accountant slice, and ledger handle.
- Failure containment: a panicking tile poisons its scope; siblings are cancelled; a structured error with full tile provenance propagates; the study continues or halts per policy — NEVER a process abort mid-campaign (policy per unsafe-safety-cases decision).
- Every unit of work spawns inside an asupersync cancellation scope (P7).

## Why
This is where asupersync's cancel-correctness stops being plumbing and becomes algorithmic leverage: statistical preemption (Bet 8) needs the ≤200 µs reclaim; determinism (P2) needs logical-identity RNG and fixed reductions; NUMA reality (§5.1) needs CCD-aware stealing.

## Acceptance criteria
G4 storm suite green (leaks, deadlocks, containment); cancel-latency p99 ≤200 µs on reference hardware, histogram ledgered; steal-order verified CCD-local-first on fixture topologies; RNG stream independence from worker assignment proven by shuffling worker counts (G5).

## Testing
Deterministic lab-runtime tests for steal/join/cancel protocols + asupersync model checker (via G4 harness). Unit: TilePlan execution completeness, reduction-tree shape stability. Property: arbitrary DAGs of scopes complete or cancel cleanly. Logs: per-scope lifecycle events, steal statistics, latency histograms — all as structured events consumable by the future ledger.
close_reason: Implemented fs-exec two-lane executor. Latency lane: thin configured handle on the asupersync runtime (block_on + structured spawn/join; request->drain->finalize inherited unmodified); measured 57us turnaround while the tile pool saturates cores (ledgered, no claim). Throughput lane: work-stealing fork-join TilePool — per-worker CachePadded mutex deques seeded with weight-proportional contiguous tile runs (P/E quantum hook), steal-half with CCD-local-first victim order from fs-substrate topology (pure victim_order/weighted_ranges functions verified on TR/EPYC/Apple fixtures), fixed-slot reductions folded in ascending tile order (bit-identical results across 1..8 workers proven with non-associative floats AND non-commutative concat). Cx contract: checkpoint/is_cancel_requested gate polls, tile-scoped fs-alloc arena (lifetime-bound), StreamKey (seed,kernel_id,tile,iteration)->key128 logical RNG identity (worker-shuffle invariance proven), asupersync Budget carried, ExecMode provenance. Failure containment: catch_unwind per tile -> structured TilePanicked with tile provenance, siblings drain via gate, pool survives; RunError::{Cancelled,TilePanicked,Incomplete} all teaching. Conformance exec-001..008: completeness+arena hygiene, G5 bit-identity, key independence, external-cancel drain w/ ledgered latency histogram, 300-run G4 storm w/ panic injection (110 ok/163 cancelled/27 panicked, all structured, quiescent throughout), fixture steal order, lane responsiveness, reduction-shape invariance. Lanes green: check, clippy -D warnings, fmt, workspace tests (52 suites), xtask check-all 0 violations. No-claims: 200us p99 gate deferred to release-build perf harness (histogram measured+ledgered per run); mutex deques v1 (Chase-Lev needs roofline evidence); speculative races + resumable solvers are wf9.8.

title: fs-exec/fs-rand: bind RNG streams to explicit logical run identity
description:
TilePool derives Cx.iteration from a pool-global AtomicU64 fetch_add. Reusing a pool means a kernel stream key depends on unrelated prior runs; concurrent invocation order changes keys. Tests use fresh pools and miss this. Separately fs-exec StreamKey uses four u64 fields and a lossy mixed key128, while fs-rand exposes seed u64 plus kernel/tile u32 and treats iteration as draw index; there is no typed conversion proving collision or replay semantics.

Root cause: execution order is being used as logical identity, and two crates independently define incompatible stream-key contracts.

Repair: require an explicit caller-ledgered RunId or generation in run APIs; derive per-tile keys solely from study, operation/run, kernel, tile, and declared iteration. Provide one canonical collision-analyzed key type or an explicit checked bridge to fs-rand, with versioned field widths and overflow/refusal rules. Pool scheduling and unrelated work must never perturb streams.

Acceptance: same logical run after arbitrary unrelated/concurrent pool activity is bit-identical; distinct declared runs diverge; worker count and arrival order do not affect keys; conversion collision tests cover truncation boundaries; replay reconstructs keys from ledger fields without hidden mutable state.
close_reason: RNG streams bound to explicit logical run identity - LANDED. (1) TilePool's pool-global AtomicU64 iteration REMOVED: stream keys no longer depend on unrelated prior runs or concurrent invocation order (execution order was being used as logical identity). run/run_with_gate now use the fixed implicit RunId(0); the new run_declared(kernel, gate, RunId) takes the caller-ledgered generation/trial/restart id - keys derive solely from (study seed, kernel id, tile, declared run). tune.rs trials now measure IDENTICAL work per trial (the old per-trial stream drift was unintended). (2) Checked fs-exec->fs-rand bridge (in fs-rand, since layering forbids the reverse dep): StreamKey::from_exec_parts(seed, kernel_id, tile, iteration), bridge v1 (EXEC_KEY_BRIDGE_VERSION), REFUSES rather than truncates - KernelOverflow/TileOverflow past u32 slots, IterationUnrepresentable for iteration!=0 (fs-rand's draw index is a within-stream counter, not identity; teaching Display points at ledgering the generation upstream). ACCEPTANCE MET: conformance test proves same logical run bit-identical after pool reuse + 3 unrelated runs + two CONCURRENT probes + arrival-order swap + worker-count change (4 vs 9); distinct declared runs diverge, same declared run replays; keys reconstruct from ledger fields alone (seed, fnv1a64(kernel), tile, run) with no hidden state; bridge collision tests cover every truncation boundary (2^32 refused, 2^32-1 accepted; the (1<<32)|5 vs 5 alias demonstrated refused). fs-exec 38+14 green, fs-rand suites green, clippy clean. CONTRACTs record the declared-identity invariant + versioned bridge. NOTE: accidentally created then removed an empty tests/philox.rs (zero-byte heredoc artifact, never committed) - disclosed per the no-delete rule.

title: fs-exec: speculative races, resumable/forkable SolverState protocol, statistical-preemption kill handles
description:
## What
The three executor behaviors most HPC runtimes lack and FrankenSim treats as core (plan §5.2): speculative races, resumable solvers, and statistical preemption.

## Scope
- Speculative races with loser-cancellation: spawn N strategies as sibling scopes ("try Delaunay refinement AND octree CutFEM concurrently; first to meet the error budget wins"); the loser's scope is cancelled and its arenas reclaimed in O(1). API: race combinator with budget-aware victory predicates and deterministic tie-breaking (P2 — ties broken by logical index, not arrival).
- Resumable solvers: the `SolverState: Serialize` protocol — Krylov, multigrid, and time-stepping loops as EXPLICIT state machines. A paused solve checkpoints to the Ledger, migrates, resumes, or FORKS (two optimizer branches continuing one warm-started solve — the forkable-worlds enabler). Deterministic-mode invariant: pause-serialize-resume reproduces the uninterrupted trajectory bit-exactly (G4 asserts this).
- Statistical preemption: kill-handle registry — the e-process layer (fs-eproc/e-racing) holds handles to candidate evaluation scope-trees; crossing an elimination threshold cancels the candidate's ENTIRE tree mid-flight; cancel-correctness guarantees no torn state, arena scoping guarantees no leaks, cores reclaim within the ≤200 µs bound. This is Bet 8's machinery.
- Graceful-degradation hooks for the resource governor (fs-session-caps): pause-serialize-resume as a first-class operation ("pause the LES, run the urgent trim study, resume" must be routine, not heroic).

## Acceptance criteria
Race combinator: losers always fully drained (G4-verified), winner's result deterministic across thread counts; a reference iterative solver (from PV skeleton) checkpoints/resumes/forks with bit-exact continuation; kill-handles reclaim a deep scope tree within latency budget under load.

## Testing
G4 storms targeting races mid-flight; property tests on serialize/deserialize round-trips of SolverState; fork-divergence test (two forks with different subsequent inputs stay independent); latency measurements ledgered. Structured logs: race outcomes with per-branch progress at kill time, checkpoint sizes, resume verdicts.

## Strategic note: distribution-readiness (plan §17)
The risk register rates "single-machine bias blocks future scale-out" LOW precisely because of this bead: serializable solver states + content-addressed artifacts + event-sourced sessions are EXACTLY the primitives distribution needs later. Design the SolverState protocol and kill-handle registry so that "migrate" can someday mean "to another machine" without API change (no shared-memory assumptions in the serialized representation; artifact references by content hash, never by pointer).
close_reason: Implemented the three §5.2 executor behaviors in fs-exec. (1) Speculative races: Racer/RaceBranch with per-branch gates+arenas+stream keys; deterministic victory = lowest-index ACCEPTED result recomputed from outcomes (timing moves when kills land, never who wins — proven identical winner index+bits across 10 jittered repeats, exec-010); early kills (j dies once i<j accepted); Fast mode = first-arrival, recorded; parent-gate watcher folds kill-handles into the whole tree mid-flight; losers fully drained (scope join) with arena quiescence oracle; panics contained per branch; NoWinner is a teaching error with per-branch JSON reports. Deterministic liveness caveat documented (below-leader branches must terminate on own budgets). (2) Resumable solvers: SolverState protocol on an in-house little-endian codec (floats as raw bits; self-contained bytes, no pointers — distribution-ready per §17), ResumableSolver::step bounded pause granularity, drive() where pause IS the cancellation path (governor hook), fork() round-trips through bytes proving serializability; pause-serialize-resume reproduces an uninterrupted CHAOTIC trajectory bit-exactly at depths 1/137/9999 (exec-011) plus Jacobi reference in unit tests; codec rejects truncation+trailing garbage with teaching CodecError. (3) Statistical preemption: KillRegistry (candidate id -> Arc<CancelGate>), idempotent kill, kill_where batch elimination (ascending, deterministic), release; deep candidate tree (1M-tile pool run) killed mid-flight drains quiescent with latency histogram ledgered (exec-012). Lanes green: clippy -D warnings, fmt, fs-exec 28 lib + 12 conformance tests, workspace 52 suites, xtask 0 violations. No-claims: 50us watcher stride + 200us gate are perf-harness territory; ledger spill of checkpoints is fs-ad/fs-ledger's.

title: fs-exec: make races panic-total and cancellation trees mandatory
description:
Racer::race_with_gate starts a parent watcher whose completion flag is set only by the last branch. With an empty branch vector the watcher never terminates. The branch body is caught, but the accept predicate runs outside catch_unwind; an accept panic unwinds the worker before filling its slot, so the watcher can again run forever. Direct fs-race consumers also construct empty KillRegistry values and ignore kill(false), allowing claimed cancellation storms to exercise no live evaluation tree.

Root cause: drain completion depends on normal branch epilogues and cancellation wiring is optional convention rather than an owned scope invariant.

Repair: reject empty races before spawning; wrap the full branch plus acceptance and finalization path in an unwind-safe guard that always records a terminal slot and releases the watcher; use structured errors, not hangs. Require candidate registration or return a structured missing-handle error from elimination; wire flagship consumers to gates owned by their actual evaluation scopes.

Acceptance: bounded tests for empty races, accept panic, branch panic, parent cancellation, missing candidate handles, and simultaneous completion; all return without leaks; losing evaluation trees observe cancellation and drain; G4 storm proves nonzero registered kills and quiescent arenas.
close_reason: Races panic-total, cancellation trees mandatory - LANDED. (1) Empty races refused with structured NoWinner (empty reports + teaching Display) BEFORE any spawn - the former path hung the parent watcher forever. (2) The branch body AND the acceptance predicate now run inside one unwind guard (an accept panic used to unwind the worker before its slot write, hanging the watcher); the terminal-slot epilogue (slot write + watcher release) is panic-free by construction. (3) Panic-totality: every Mutex use in race.rs and kill.rs is poison-tolerant (PoisonError::into_inner) - a predicate panic in kill_where can no longer cascade panics through the registry. (4) KillRegistry::kill_registered returns structured UnregisteredKill instead of an ignorable false; exported. (5) Flagship consumers wired: fs-race race_field and successive_halving REGISTER all candidate gates at scope start (the race owns its candidates' evaluation trees) and eliminate via kill_registered - a claimed cancellation can no longer exercise zero live trees (coordinated with in-flight 7tv.7.2, whose loss-span refactor is orthogonal; their battery green with this wiring). ACCEPTANCE MET, all bounded via a 20s recv_timeout harness (a hang fails, never wedges CI): empty race, accept panic (contained as Panicked, race terminates, clean branch wins), branch panic (pre-existing test), mid-flight parent cancellation (all branches Cancelled, drained), simultaneous instant completions x32 (deterministic lowest index), missing candidate handle (structured error), and the G4 storm: 12 candidates raced under registry-owned gates with external kill storms - every kill landed registered (12/12 nonzero), every race returned, arenas quiescent, registry drained to 0. fs-exec 38 tests green, fs-race 13+12 green, clippy clean. CONTRACT records the drain-totality invariant.

title: fs-exec: add a versioned self-authenticating solver snapshot envelope
description:
SolverState::to_bytes writes only implementation-defined payload bytes and from_bytes calls the selected type decoder. There is no magic, solver type id, schema version, payload length, checksum, or semantic provenance. A same-length snapshot from another solver or version can decode successfully into plausible but wrong state, and corruption can evade trailing-byte checks.

Root cause: payload serialization is treated as a distribution-ready artifact without an envelope that identifies and authenticates its schema.

Repair: wrap snapshots in canonical bytes containing magic, envelope version, stable solver/state type id, schema version, payload length, payload checksum/content hash, and required provenance. Validate the envelope before invoking the state decoder; provide explicit migrations or structured incompatible-version refusal.

Acceptance: cross-type same-layout bytes, bit flips, truncation, appended bytes, unknown version, wrong type id, and stale schema all refuse; valid pause-migrate-resume remains bit-exact; fork and ledger paths use the envelope rather than raw payloads.
close_reason: Versioned self-authenticating snapshot envelope LANDED (v1). Canonical layout: magic FSEXSNAP + envelope version u32 + stable state TYPE_ID u64 + payload SCHEMA_VERSION u32 + caller-ledgered provenance u64 + payload length u64 + FNV payload checksum u64, then payload — every header field validated BEFORE the payload decoder runs (envelope::open). SolverState now REQUIRES const TYPE_ID (never reused/changed) and const SCHEMA_VERSION (bumped on any layout change) — the compiler forces every state to declare identity; all three existing impls migrated (JacobiState, ChaoticState, fs-session ToySolver). New seal(provenance)/unseal -> (state, provenance) carry run/ledger identity (pairs with wf9.7.1 RunId); to_bytes/from_bytes are the unattributed convenience over the SAME envelope; fork round-trips enveloped bytes; content_hash covers the envelope. Incompatible schema = structured IncompatibleSchema refusal (the explicit no-migration-yet path). ACCEPTANCE MET (envelope_refuses_every_misbinding_class): cross-type same-layout bytes (TwinState with identical payload layout) refused WrongTypeId; payload bit flip -> ChecksumMismatch; magic flip -> BadMagic; header truncation -> Truncated; payload truncation AND appended bytes -> LengthMismatch; unknown envelope version 9 -> refused; stale schema 7 -> IncompatibleSchema{1,7}; valid seal round-trips bit-exactly WITH provenance (0xABCD preserved); existing pause-serialize-resume bit-exact conformance still green. fs-exec 39+14 green, fs-session 10 green, clippy clean. CONTRACT records the envelope contract.

title: fs-math: deterministic elementary functions, ULP budgets, FMA/subnormal/NaN policy, enclosures
description:
## What
`fs-math`: deterministic elementary functions and the floating-point policy contract (patch Rev O). Deterministic reductions and RNG are NOT enough — full determinism requires a math-function contract.

## Scope
- Deterministic scalar + vector implementations of sin/cos/tan/exp/log/log1p/expm1/sqrt/cbrt/atan2/pow/erf with DECLARED ULP contracts per function, identical results across ISAs in strict mode (no platform libm in deterministic paths).
- Strict vs fast modes mirroring ExecMode: strict = cross-ISA reproducible with documented ULP bounds; fast = platform-optimal, permitted only when the mode is ledgered provenance.
- FMA contraction policy: explicit contract for where FMA is allowed (per-kernel declaration), because contraction differences are a top cross-ISA divergence class (G5 report category).
- Subnormal policy (never flush-to-zero silently; document per-ISA behavior), NaN/infinity propagation policy (payloads not relied upon; canonical NaN on production paths), signed-zero handling.
- Interval-safe helpers: directed next_up/next_down nudging utilities and DECLARED ENCLOSURES for every elementary function so fs-ivl's Taylor models and interval evaluation get rigorous elementary-function bounds (this is what makes interval certificates clean — Rev O).
- ULP Ledger: every kernel declares a ULP budget for its sensitive operations; deterministic mode FORBIDS implementation-defined math paths unless wrapped by fs-math (lintable).

## Why
Cross-platform mismatches from libm/FMA/subnormals are a named risk; and fs-ivl's certificates are only as rigorous as their elementary-function enclosures.

## Acceptance criteria
Each function: ULP bound verified empirically against the double-double oracle across systematic + random + adversarial inputs (billions of samples nightly); bit-identical strict-mode results across NEON/AVX-512 for the committed function set; enclosure property (result ∈ declared enclosure) proven by G0 laws.

## Testing
Exhaustive f32 sweeps where feasible; oracle-sampled f64; special-value tables (±0, subnormals, ±inf, NaN); cross-ISA hash comparison in CI (G5). Logs: per-function max-ULP-observed tables, enclosure violation counts (must be 0).
close_reason: v1 CLOSED with cross-ISA proof; remainder split to fs-math-extensions (created, linked). Delivered: det::{exp,expm1,ln,sin,cos,tanh,sqrt} built from pure IEEE arithmetic; policy doc (FMA contraction forbidden-implicit/encouraged-explicit, subnormals never flushed, canonical NaN, strict-vs-fast); nudge_out/next_up/next_down for fs-ivl; ulp_distance. HEADLINE EVIDENCE: golden hash 0xeb79cab7a01643e5 IDENTICAL on aarch64-apple (M4 Pro) and x86-64 (TR PRO 5995WX) across 175k evaluations — cross-ISA bit-determinism proven empirically, not argued. Measured ULP maxima (budgets): exp 1 (3), expm1 2 (3), ln 1 (3), sin 2 (3), cos 2 (3), tanh 3 (5), both ISAs. THREE REAL BUGS found+killed by the test discipline en route, each now a regression test: decimal-rendered Cody-Waite constants losing exact trailing zeros (184 ULP); Taylor cores two terms short (166 ULP at |r|=pi/4); tanh oddness by-luck-not-construction (now sign-applied-to-magnitude). 4-part pi/2 reduction (fdlibm bit patterns) fixed the x=pi near-zero 7-10 ULP cases. NO-CLAIMS: |x|>2^20 trig (Payne-Hanek in extension bead), 0.5-ULP correct rounding, remaining function families. 13 tests green locally + on trj, clippy clean.

title: Benchmark and V&V registry: pinned decks, licenses, acceptance envelopes
description:
BACKGROUND: A family name (TEAM, NAFEMS, CFR, IFToMM, ECN) is NOT an executable benchmark. Every G1/G2 entry needs exact version/edition, source, license, input-deck hash, QoIs, and acceptance envelopes before any solver claims it. This registry is where new-physics admission gets its teeth.

G1 ANALYTIC ENTRIES to seed: Hertz sphere/plane + cylinder/plane contact; bouncing-ball impact maps; block-on-incline stick/slip (tan theta = mu_s for the ideal rigid block); Bennett-linkage mobility (exactly parameterized family, symbolic closure/nullity oracle); involute constant-ratio under declared center-distance/contact assumptions; Geneva closed-form geometry; epitrochoid closed form (derived + symbolically checked, never mnemonic); coaxial cable / sphere-in-uniform-field / Helmholtz coil; Stefan problem; exact Riemann (Sod/Lax) + isentropic nozzle; air-standard Otto/Diesel/Atkinson cycles.

G2 BENCHMARK ENTRIES to seed (exact editions + licenses + decks): IFToMM rectangular-Bricard (redundantly constrained with configuration-dependent dependent-constraint subset) and Andrews squeezer; TEAM 10, 13, 20, 24, 30a, 30b from official COMPUMAG definitions (geometry revision, excitation, material law, circuit, QoI, acceptance data pinned — the problem number alone is not a deck); NAFEMS thermal set + R0083 acoustic (exact case ID/report/license); CFR engine pressure traces + motored p-V loops (versioned/licensed); NASA CAA benchmark decks; Sandia ECN (exact configuration, diagnostic uncertainty, blind/held-out QoIs); oscillating-cylinder + gerotor moving-boundary flow decks.

STATUS DISCIPLINE (Appendix-D rule): each implementation bead consuming a registry row records unread/read/derived/reproduced/independently_falsified and pins the artifact version.

TESTS (detailed logging): registry lint — an entry missing any field (deck hash, license, QoI, envelope) cannot be cited by a Gauntlet test (typed refusal); goldens for registry serialization; a fixture proving an unpinned family-name citation fails CI.
PRIMARY-REFERENCE REGISTRY SEED (complete; anchors definitions and benchmark provenance — never authority-by-citation; every consuming bead records unread/read/derived/reproduced/independently_falsified and pins the exact artifact/version):
1. FEEC stability — Arnold, Falk & Winther, 'Finite element exterior calculus: from Hodge theory to numerical stability' (arXiv:0906.4325): dd=0 insufficient; subcomplex + bounded cochain projection + formulation stability are explicit gates.
2. Cellular sheaf spectra — Hansen & Ghrist, 'Toward a Spectral Theory of Cellular Sheaves' (arXiv:1808.01513): sheaf Laplacians relevant only after explicit stalks/restrictions constructed; L1 spectral machinery stays generic.
3. Sheaf-cosheaf foundations — Curry, 'Sheaves, Cosheaves and Applications' (arXiv:1303.3255): restriction and aggregation directions distinct; the power pairing and commuting diagram are NEW theorem obligations, not borrowed authority.
4. Species thermodynamics — McBride, Zehe & Gordon, NASA/TP-2002-211556: NASA-9 is standard-state MOLAR thermodynamics; amount-of-substance, phase/EOS derivations, reference metadata load-bearing.
5. Entropy-stable discretization — Tadmor, 'Entropy Stable Schemes' (doi:10.1016/bs.hna.2016.09.006): entropy-conservative spatial flux is not the fully discrete/source/boundary theorem; exact scheme and sign convention pinned.
6. Port-Hamiltonian dissipation — Cervera, van der Schaft & Banos, 'Interconnection of port-Hamiltonian systems and composition of Dirac structures' (doi:10.1016/j.automatica.2006.08.014): Dirac relations power-conserving; dissipation is a separate resistive structure.
7. Rigidity/self-stress — Rocks et al., 'Integrating local energetics into Maxwell-Calladine constraint counting' (arXiv:2208.07419): mechanisms = ker J; self-stress = ker J^T; index and energy structure distinct.
8. Contact — Li et al., 'Incremental Potential Contact' (doi:10.1145/3386569.3392425) + 'Convergent IPC' (arXiv:2307.15908): nonintersection/convergence claims list candidate/CCD/solve/refinement assumptions; pin exact preprint version/hash; smoothness regime-specific.
9. Codimensional contact — Li et al., 'Codimensional IPC' (arXiv:2012.04457): shell/rod/seal thickness claims conditional on declared codimensional model, candidates, CCD, accepted solve.
10. Nonsmooth multicontact — Acary, 'Energy conservation and dissipation properties of time-integration methods for nonsmooth elastodynamics with contact' (arXiv:1410.2499) + the exact global impact-law source pinned by the bead: Moreau-Jean energy behavior is law/parameter dependent; pairwise restitution is not a global energy theorem.
11. Validated flowpipes/events — Walawska & Wilczak, implicit validated variational-equation enclosures (arXiv:1509.07388) + a pinned validated-DAE/root-isolation source: true-flow enclosure, DAE regularity, finite-guard isolability are separate obligations.
12. Gear transmission error — Athavale, Krishnaswami & Kuo, SAE 2001-01-1507: TE is angular-position deviation from ideal conjugate motion, not interval width; an executable G2 case needs a complete reproducible deck.
13. Wankel seals/kinematics — Handschuh & Owen, NASA/TM-2010-216353: reduced seal-load/friction reference with explicit assumptions; does not prove universal finite-radius housing geometry.
14. Multibody benchmarks — IFToMM Library of Computational Benchmark Problems: exact input/result artifacts for Andrews, Bricard, slider-crank.
15. TEAM EM benchmarks — COMPUMAG official problem definitions 10/13/20/24/30a/30b: pin exact revision, geometry, excitation, material law, circuit, QoI, acceptance.
16. Thermal benchmarks — NAFEMS thermal index/guide: exact case ID/report/license/QoI required.
17. NASA-9 dev oracle — Cantera 3.2 NASA9 documentation: oracle receipts pin release, species/mechanism hash, temperature region, reference pressure; never a production dependency.
18. Nonholonomic mechanics — Modin & Verdier, 'What makes nonholonomic integrators work?' (doi:10.1007/s00211-020-01126-y) + the exact discrete Lagrange-d'Alembert source per bead: rolling is Pfaffian and generally nonintegrable; no ordinary Hamilton/RATTLE claims inherited.
19. H(curl) auxiliary space — Hiptmair & Xu (doi:10.1137/060660588) + hypre AMS docs: component list and boundary/topology/coefficient assumptions explicit.
20. Switched descriptor impulses — Yildiz, MNA-based unified ideal switch model (doi:10.1142/S0218126613500461): inconsistent switching causes impulses/discontinuous device states; impulse-free continuity conditional.
21. Nonlinear magnetic energy — Mandlmayr & Egger (arXiv:2311.02380): convex energy/coenergy vs merely strongly monotone nonintegrable laws distinguished.
22. Reacting entropy/positivity — Ching, Johnson & Kercher Parts I/II (arXiv:2211.16254, arXiv:2211.16297): constructions tied to exact thermodynamics/chemistry/source/discretization.
23. Acoustics — Burton & Miller combined-field exterior (doi:10.1016/0022-247X(84)90146-X); Ffowcs Williams & Hawkings moving-surface aeroacoustics (doi:10.1098/rsta.1969.0031); NASA CAA proceedings; NAFEMS R0083.
24. Tribology/EHL — Hamrock & Dowson NASA-TP-1342 + independent optical-film/traction datasets: film correlations regime-bounded; full EHL verifies balances and validates held-out.
25. Fatigue/fracture — ASTM E466-21, E647-24 + pinned NASA NASGRO reference artifact as dev oracle: method conformance never validates component life.
26. Assurance — ISO 12100:2010, IEC 60034-1:2026, IEC 60034-2-1:2024: scope/rating/loss-test methods become conformance artifacts; simulation is not regulatory approval.
27. V&V/uncertainty — ASME VVUQ registry, BIPM/JCGM GUM, NASA-STD-7009: context of use, solution verification, experimental uncertainty, calibration/validation split, prediction assessment are separate artifacts.
28. Combustion validation — Sandia Engine Combustion Network: exact configuration, diagnostic uncertainty, blind/held-out QoIs versioned.
29. Interoperability — FMI 3.0.2, SSP 2.0: conformance and quarantined-adapter behavior tested without admitting foreign runtimes to the trusted graph.
30. Gear standards — ISO 6336-1:2019 + exact applicable parts/editions/worked examples: formula conformance inside scope only; drive life needs independent validation.
RULE: a standards calculation earns numerical Verified and/or StandardConformance for the exact edition and scope; its physical prediction is Estimated unless independent held-out evidence for the named QoI and population earns Validated; no color is inherited from a publisher's name.

title: CAD/STEP interchange: import to SDF, certified B-rep re-fit export
description:
BACKGROUND: The engineer workflow starts and ends in the conventional CAD world, and today's generative tools have a notorious last-mile failure: they emit a mesh blob that a human manually re-models in parametric CAD, so the manufactured part is a hand-drawn APPROXIMATION of the optimized one, verified by re-running simulation on the redrawn geometry and hoping. Closing this loop — the optimized geometry ships, within a stated tolerance — is both a workflow requirement (import existing products as starting points) and a differentiator. This complements FMI/SSP (model exchange) with GEOMETRY exchange.

IMPORT LANE [S]: STEP -> tessellate -> generalized-winding-number sign -> SDF chart (the fs-rep-mesh soup-repair + winding machinery and mesh-to-SDF conversion already exist; this bead productizes the path with conversion receipts). title: fs-contact + fs-mbd: Moreau-Jean nonsmooth lane with global impact admissibility
description:
BACKGROUND: Hard impacts and long-dwell stick (Geneva locking, ratchets, backlash rattle) stiffen barrier methods badly; the honest lane is measure-differential-inclusion time-stepping. OWNERSHIP: contact laws + contact-specific cone residuals live in fs-contact; generic conic/nonlinear math in fs-solver; the Moreau-Jean STEPPER lives in fs-mbd (which depends on fs-contact) — keeping the graph acyclic.

SCOPE: (1) Moreau-Jean discrete law: configuration admissibility g(q)>=0 with active-set-supported nonnegative normal impulse measures, complementarity, declared gap stabilization — a velocity-only condition may NOT excuse an already penetrating or drifting configuration (this is not velocity-only penetration repair); (2) Newton restitution embedded in a GLOBALLY ADMISSIBLE multicontact impact law — impulse, kinetic-energy, angular-momentum, and contact-work receipts prevent pairwise restitution coefficients from silently injecting global energy (PO-21); (3) Coulomb cones as a cone-complementarity problem: deterministic PGS as BASELINE only; semismooth Newton, interior-point, and conic solvers are REQUIRED production candidates (in fs-solver); (4) solver receipts: primal/dual feasibility, complementarity, determinacy/nonuniqueness, Painleve/inconsistent classification — set-valued response or an explicitly different calibrated compliant model with discrepancy/limit study, NEVER an arbitrary impulse; (5) the compliant regularized lane is a DIFFERENT PHYSICAL MODEL: its compliance/contact-duration calibration, discrepancy, and refinement/limit study are ledgered, not silently substituted; (6) energy partition: for an assembled pair, action/reaction cancels; total contact work closes stored contact energy + nonnegative dissipation; dissipated work partitioned among declared heat, plastic/damage/surface-energy, lubricant chemistry, exported debris — only the heat share feeds thermal, and the total closes; a passive impact may not increase assembled kinetic+stored energy absent a source.

title: fs-control: sampled-data runtime control with stability artifacts

title: E7 design-optimization studies: two robust improvements plus twin update
description:
BACKGROUND: The mission is SYNTHESIS — the E7 exit demands at least two robust design improvements and one posterior digital-twin update, produced by the optimization stack over flagship models with honest sensitivity lanes (classical adjoints where regular, generalized/derivative-free where not — ASCENT never assumes every nonsmooth machine objective has a smooth adjoint).

CANDIDATE STUDIES (pick two-plus per exit criteria): (1) maximize gear-train efficiency subject to an evidence-typed transmission-error band; (2) minimize motor cogging torque over magnet shape with a force/torque error budget at the claimed rung (shape adjoints through the EM machinery); (3) maximize ICE brake efficiency over cam timing + compression ratio under a knock-integral chance constraint with an anytime-valid statistical bound under declared sampling and model assumptions; (4) minimize Geneva indexing-error CVaR under manufacturing tolerance distributions.

REQUIREMENTS: each study ships its sensitivity-lane declaration (adjoint-verified where claimed, D8 gates), robustness statement (CVaR/DRO machinery exists in fs-robust/fs-dfo), budget receipts, and an atlas artifact with per-elite evidence colors; the digital-twin update satisfies evidence monotonicity.

TESTS (detailed logging): each study replayable end-to-end from its notebook; gradient-verification gates green where adjoints are claimed; chance-constraint coverage validated on synthetic truth; improvement claims carry before/after receipts with matched budgets.

title: E8 summit: independent reproduction and adjudication of theorem cards
description:
BACKGROUND: E8 is the reproduction/adjudication SUMMIT, not the start date — cards open beside their enabling phases and this bead closes the program's research arc.

SCOPE: (1) every card audited for: exact quantifiers, trusted computing base, boring baseline, counterexample generator, executable checker, retained falsifier, reproduction pack; (2) independent reproduction attempts (fresh implementation or independent reviewer per the review-state axis); (3) formal adjudication/promotion: a proved card may promote an [F] lane ONLY after its checker survives independent falsification; (4) the E8 exit: at least THREE independent cards spanning (i) topology/coupling, (ii) mechanisms/hybrids/contact, (iii) thermodynamics/fidelity/life are BOTH KernelChecked AND ScaleQualified; (5) failed moonshots remain versioned/refuted — visible and unavailable, never hidden prerequisites; (6) integration: nonlinear stacks, multisymplectic composition, set-valued hybrid reachability, and adaptive model-category routing attempts recorded with honest state.

TESTS/LOGGING: reproduction-pack completeness lint per card; promotion-gate enforcement (an [F] lane consuming an unproved card refused); the summit report renders the full card portfolio with orthogonal state axes; every adjudication decision logged with reviewer identity and artifacts.

NORMATIVE SUMMIT/PROMOTION CORRECTION: A counterexample candidate never forces Refuted merely by existing. It is adjudicated as ConfirmedCounterexample, SatisfiableWitness, AssumptionViolation, NumericalArtifact, CheckerArtifact, or ClassificationPending under exact quantifiers/domain/assumptions. E8 portfolio success and per-card runtime promotion are distinct. Runtime eligibility requires the dedicated promotion receipt and the full conjunction Stable + SatisfiableWitnessed + Proved or fully discharged ConditionalProof + exact-instance Admitted + strength-matched nonvacuity + no unresolved authority gap + KernelChecked + ScaleQualified + Reproduced + no active invalidation/revocation/source or policy drift. Missing axes remain visible Unknown/Refused; no score or summit vote fills them. Failed or repaired conjectures stay versioned evidence.

title: fs-em: 2-D A_z nonlinear magnetostatics with energy/coenergy lanes
description:
BACKGROUND: Most industrial motor design is 2-D — this single solver unlocks the PMSM/BLDC flagship. New L3 crate fs-em (deps: fs-feec, fs-cutfem, fs-motion, fs-time, fs-solver, fs-matdb, fs-material, fs-symmetry, fs-couple, fs-iface).

FORMULATION: A_z scalar lane on TriComplex2 (or the existing quadtree CutFEM machinery), with a weak residual that DISTINGUISHES impressed winding current from the remanence/magnetization term and records its sign/orientation convention (PM sources are precisely oriented remanence/recoil constitutive offsets + RHS terms, with temperature-dependent demagnetization/recoil limits from magnet cards).

NONLINEAR MATERIAL HONESTY (falsified shortcut to avoid: a monotone scalar spline of nu(B) alone proves neither an SPD tangent, stored-energy integrability, nor Newton convergence): two lanes — (a) POTENTIAL-BASED: fit/enclose a convex magnetic energy w(B) with H = dw/dB, or its admitted Legendre-dual coenergy w*(H); verify symmetric Hessian, convexity/eigenvalue bounds, Legendre duality; this lane may support the declared virtual-work functional; (b) STRONGLY MONOTONE nonintegrable H(B): verify positivity of the symmetric tangent part/coercivity but NO stored-energy/coenergy force claim unless a potential is separately proved. Newton with globalization (fs-solver NK); a solution/convergence ENCLOSURE additionally requires Krawczyk/radii-polynomial or validated inverse-Jacobian machinery on the assembled residual.

REFERENCE PIN: nonlinear anisotropic magnetic interpolation models (registry row) — convex energy/coenergy vs merely monotone laws distinguished per Appendix-D discipline.

TESTS (unit + G1, detailed logging): MMS convergence order per element degree (slope within 0.2); coaxial cable / sphere-in-uniform-field closed forms; PM fixture with orientation-convention round-trip; energy-lane Hessian symmetry/convexity receipts; monotone-lane force-claim refusal fixture; Newton globalization logs (residual/step/forcing per iteration).

title: fs-em: gauged 3-D curl-curl magnetostatics with cohomology handling
description:
BACKGROUND: The Nedelec H(curl) families (r=1..4) have existed in fs-feec with no consumer — their contract explicitly defers a curl-curl solve. This bead is that solve: curl(nu curl A) = J on tet complexes.

SCOPE: (1) curl-curl assembly from WeightedStar over the Nedelec spaces; (2) GAUGE HANDLING, both lanes: tree-cotree gauging with a DETERMINISTIC spanning tree keyed by cell IDs (deterministic gauge = replayable solve), and Coulomb-gauge Lagrange-multiplier saddle formulation (block framework + MINRES admission); (3) multiply-connected domains: harmonic-space handling via existing harmonic_basis/deflate_harmonics — source compatibility checked against the topology (an imposed current through a handle needs its cohomology constraint or the residual is inconsistent); (4) solver: CG under HX for the SPD gauged lane; FGMRES for variable-preconditioner experiments; admission rules enforced; (5) source models: impressed current densities with divergence-compatibility checks; solid-conductor imposed-net-current constraints are formulation-specific (cut/source-field/relative-cohomology selected from topology + BCs — harmonic_basis provides ingredients, not the complete conductor model).

TESTS (unit + G1/G2, detailed logging): 3-D MMS order fits; gauge invariance of B under gauge change of A (metamorphic, G0); source-compatibility refusal fixture (inconsistent J refused with the violated constraint logged); a torus-with-handle fixture exercising the cohomology constraint; TEAM 13 (nonlinear magnetostatics) pinned-deck envelope; per-solve gauge/tree identity logged for replay.

title: fs-em: forces, torques, demagnetization, and loss ownership
description:
BACKGROUND: Torque is the motor QoI, and EM force computation is where honesty is hardest. TWO falsified shortcuts are banned: (a) method agreement (Maxwell stress vs virtual work) earning Verified — both derive from the same field solution, so agreement is an implementation-consistency gate, not physical validation and not a certificate; (b) ordinary DWR supplying a Verified bound — DWR is an ESTIMATE; Verified force bounds require a guaranteed functional majorant/equilibrated or interval-residual bound with stated reliability constants.

SCOPE: (1) Maxwell stress on air/vacuum contours (or an explicitly declared material stress tensor) with the sliding interface's separate compatibility and conservation audits; (2) virtual work with DECLARED held electrical variables and functional (+dW'/dx at constant I, -dW/dx at constant flux, or the coupled-circuit functional), deformation/magnetostriction convention, torque origin and frame — a force theorem is scoped to that material/boundary/gauge/electrical-control choice; (3) cross-check machinery producing consistency receipts; disagreement demotes and LOCALIZES; (4) guaranteed functional-bound lane [F] for Verified claims (feeds the force-enclosure theorem card); (5) DEMAGNETIZATION margins: operating point vs temperature-dependent knee/recoil limits from magnet cards, reported per element; (6) LOSS MAPS: Steinmetz/Bertotti core loss as Validated post-processing ONLY against named material/frequency/temperature/waveform data (D6); hysteresis (Jiles-Atherton/Preisach) stays [M] off-default with internal state + free-energy/dissipation receipts when it lands; (7) LossOwnershipReceipt {loss_id, resolved_or_modelled, upstream_debit, thermal_credit, exclusions} — Steinmetz maps EXCLUDED when resolved hysteresis/eddy physics already contains that loss; winding resistance reconciled with field-resolved copper loss; thermal credit equals upstream debit within the accounting bound (prevents double counting; PO-2); (8) shape-derivative adjoint of the ACTUAL discrete EM residual + force functional, verified against independent perturbations (existing Hadamard machinery is reusable infrastructure, not proof).

TESTS (detailed logging): TEAM 20 (static force) pinned envelope; dual-method consistency on analytic fixtures with localization on seeded discretization error; demagnetization-margin fixture at elevated temperature; loss-ownership double-counting adversarial fixture (must refuse); adjoint-vs-FD force gradients (D8 gate); per-claim held-variable declarations logged.

title: fs-em: moving-conductor MQS (A-phi) and 2.5-D multislice ladder
description:
BACKGROUND: Generators, induction rotors, solid-conductor eddy currents, and motional EMF are INSIDE the funded machine path — a sliding interpolation alone cannot replace the moving-conductor formulation. This rung is mandatory before any generator claim.

SCOPE: (1) magnetoquasistatic A-phi/A-V: solve the coupled weak field + charge-continuity system on EXPLICITLY partitioned conducting/insulating domains, with J = sigma(-dA/dt - grad(phi) + v x B) in the chosen frame, source compatibility, interface/boundary conditions, gauge/cohomology constraints, and energy reciprocity; (2) frame discipline: ALE and rotating-frame variants must AGREE on overlap fixtures (metamorphic gate); (3) time integration via the first-order sparse lanes; time-harmonic via the 2x2 real-equivalent block form (real-f64 doctrine); (4) skin/proximity winding losses; (5) 2.5-D MULTISLICE ladder: 2-D slices + skew + calibrated end corrections, with an ESCALATION TRIGGER from measured end-effect error to full 3-D (assumption A-002 monitored: MQS wavelength/displacement-current regime receipt; electroquasistatic/full-wave escalation is a separate [M] regime, never MQS extended by name); (6) THREE-WAY POWER CLOSURE receipt (PO-13): field/source, Lorentz-mechanical (J x B).v, and conductor-frame Ohmic q = J.(E + v x B) >= 0 for passive resistivity — under the declared sign split J.E = q_Ohmic + Lorentz-mechanical share; fs-em exports DISTINCT receipts and fs-thermal consumes only the loss contribution.

TESTS (detailed logging): moving-slab/rotating-cylinder eddy analytic fixtures; ALE-vs-rotating-frame agreement; three-way power-closure ledger on every fixture (imbalance = failure, logged per term); TEAM 24 / TEAM 30a/30b pinned-deck envelopes (locked-rotor torque, induction-machine behavior); regime-receipt logging with the dimensionless monitors.
MACHINE TAXONOMY (PMSM/BLDC is the first FORCING FUNCTION, not the taxonomy boundary): induction, wound-field, synchronous- and switched-reluctance, axial/radial/transverse-flux, linear machines, transformers, solenoids, magnetic bearings, eddy-current brakes, and electrostatic actuators each SELECT the formulation/material/loss ladder their physics requires — no machine inherits a motor template by name. EXPLICIT MACHINE SUCCESSORS (staged, named so they cannot be silently dropped): lamination homogenization; skin/proximity effects; rotor-bar end rings; common-mode/cable parasitics; bearing currents; insulation stress/partial discharge; conducted/radiated EMC (the E7 assurance program owns the EMC case; this crate owns the field-level source models).

title: EPIC E0a — Units, identity, and schema foundations
EPIC E0b — Constitutive operators and solver spine
description:
PHASE EPIC (new-domains expansion; self-contained bead graph).

WHY: FEEC already separates exact integer topology (dd=0) from metric operators, and complete Nedelec/RT element families exist with NO consumer. The single highest-EV lever of the whole program (scored 62.5 alongside the units migration) is material-weighted mass/Hodge operators plus a typed constitutive graph, because heat, electrostatics, current flow, magnetics, and Darcy all become assemblable from the same machinery. The solver spine (Newton-Krylov globalization, block operators) has four immediate clients (MBD, EM, thermal, gas) — one implementation, four consumers.

SCOPE: oriented 2-D complex substrate (ext-rep-mesh-tricomplex2); WeightedStar/WeightedMass + formulation proof lanes (ext-feec-weighted-operators); executable ConstitutiveGraph in fs-material (ext-constitutive-graph); Newton-Krylov + block/Schur framework in fs-solver (ext-solver-nonlinear-block); versioned PortSchema + four port-thermodynamic primitives + windowed audits in fs-couple (ext-couple-port-schema); sparse/matrix-free implicit integrators (ext-time-sparse-integrators); E0b battery (ext-e0b-test-battery).

KEY DOCTRINE (D2): bulk storage/metric laws (permittivity, reluctivity, heat capacity, density) enter weighted operators; interface laws, reactions, and history-dependent internal variables (plasticity, hysteresis, friction, wear) are DISTINCT typed maps and never forced into a Hodge star. dd=0 is a topology test only — it proves neither stability nor absence of spurious modes; each formulation must establish its subcomplex/commuting-projection/coercivity/inf-sup obligations separately.

title: EPIC E0c — Materials data, V&V artifacts, and benchmark registry
description:
PHASE EPIC (new-domains expansion; self-contained bead graph).

WHY: 'Real material properties of actual materials' is a core program requirement, and honesty about data is the product differentiator: every downstream physics claim inherits its weakest LOAD-BEARING material datum. That requires an immutable L1 data layer (observations, claims, cards, receipts) BEFORE domain solvers exist, so no solver ever grows an ad hoc scalar. Verification-is-not-validation (doctrine D9) similarly requires machine-readable V&V artifacts and a benchmark registry where a family name (TEAM, NAFEMS, CFR) is NOT executable until exact edition, license, deck hash, QoIs, and acceptance envelopes are pinned.

SCOPE: fs-matdb L1 schemas + query receipts (ext-matdb-core); offline pack compiler (ext-matdb-pack-compiler); curated cited seed dataset (ext-matdb-seed-dataset); V&V artifact schemas: ContextOfUse, ValidationPlan, ExperimentArtifact, CalibrationSplit, SolutionVerificationReceipt, PredictionAssessment (ext-vv-artifact-schemas); benchmark/V&V registry (ext-benchmark-vv-registry); E0c battery (ext-e0c-test-battery).

EXIT CRITERIA: one complete material-query dependency closure with source/license/covariance passes end-to-end; a blind calibration/validation split is enforced mechanically; an intentionally invalid pack and an invalid query are REFUSED with typed errors.

OWNERSHIP RULE (load-bearing): fs-matdb owns immutable data and neutral law IDs/versions/state schemas; executable laws and mutable runtime state live in L3 (fs-material and domain adapters); persistence lives in L6 ledger/package. fs-matdb never imports L2 transforms or L3 state types.

title: EPIC E0d — Replayed machine-graph vertical slice
description:
PHASE EPIC (new-domains expansion; self-contained bead graph).

WHY: Before ANY physics lands, the machine-composition runtime must be proven end-to-end on typed toy elements, because retrofitting transactional windows, superdense hybrid time, checkpointing, cancellation, and bit-replay onto live physics is how simulators rot. The slice also forces the machine-graph IR, port schema, ledger receipts, and report rendering to meet each other early.

SCOPE: one minimal admitted machine-graph skeleton using typed toy rotational/electrical/thermal storage, loss, and source elements — explicitly NOT a physical motor claim — with transactional snapshot/cancel/drain/resume and a rendered report (ext-e0d-machine-slice); Theorem Foundry infrastructure + first cards opened (ext-theorem-foundry-infra).

EXIT CRITERIA: an incomplete graph is REJECTED at admission (dimension/orientation/causality/source-closure checks); the admitted graph runs, audits (power + entropy windows), checkpoints, cancels/drains/resumes, and bit-replays at the declared scale; the SAME graph is later rebindable to real E1–E5 domain artifacts without identity drift; initial thermodynamics/identity theorem cards are open.

DESIGN COMMITMENTS the slice locks in: coupled step = propose→solve→audit→commit (never externally commit a half-audited window); SuperdenseTime {physical_time, microstep} for simultaneous resets; MachineStateSnapshot binds graph version, component state codecs, active modes, solver frontiers, IQN history, controller clocks, RNG roots, accounting windows; every component has an explicit state-schema migration/refusal path.

title: EPIC E1 — Prescribed motion and nonlinear kinematics
description:
PHASE EPIC (new-domains expansion; self-contained bead graph).

WHY: The single deepest architectural gap is that geometry is static per-evaluation — rigid-motion algebra (fs-ga PGA motors, screw exp/log) and rotating frame trees (fs-scenario FrameTree) both exist but nothing binds a motor path to a chart. This phase creates certified MOTION (tubes, sweeps, envelopes, clearance-over-time) and NONLINEAR KINEMATICS (configuration graphs, holonomy, tangent rigidity) — everything a mechanism needs BEFORE dynamics, contact, or fields.

SCOPE: CertifiedMotorTube/SpacetimeChart (ext-motion-motor-tube); swept/envelope enclosure charts (ext-motion-swept-envelope); two-sided clearance + chamber volumes (ext-motion-clearance-volume); fs-query geometry upgrades incl. GeometricMoments (ext-query-geometry-upgrades); configuration/holonomy graph (ext-kinematics-config-graph); tangent rigidity/self-stress/singularity margins (ext-kinematics-tangent-rigidity); L1 generic eigensolver service (ext-spectral-eigensolver-service); validated events on PRESCRIBED analytic paths (ext-events-validated-prescribed); fs-scenario typed payloads + one-way FrameTree lowering (ext-scenario-payloads); E1 battery (ext-e1-test-battery).

EXIT CRITERIA: derived (symbolically checked, never mnemonic) trochoid/involute and slider-crank/four-bar oracles pass; a TWO-SIDED clearance range (lower bound + feasible witness upper bound) is produced; Bennett/Bricard finite/tangent checks pass (tangent kernel finds mobility where Gruebler-Kutzbach count fails); prescribed-path isolable-guard complete root accounting works; conjugate/mechanism theorem cards active.

KEY DOCTRINE (D4): finite SE(3) loop closure is non-commutative holonomy, not an additive cocycle; infinitesimal mobility is ker J(q) after gauge fixing; self-stress is ker J(q)^T; unilateral contact is a cone problem; rolling is a Pfaffian velocity distribution. These are five DIFFERENT executable objects, never one H1 slogan.

title: EPIC E2 — Dynamic interaction: multibody, contact, dry tribology
description:
PHASE EPIC (new-domains expansion; self-contained bead graph).

WHY: With motion and kinematics in hand, this phase makes bodies MOVE UNDER FORCES and TOUCH: constrained rigid multibody dynamics on SE(3), validated true-flow hybrid events, body-body contact (smooth barrier lane + nonsmooth complementarity lane), and the dry tribology baseline. The Geneva flagship closes the phase because intermittent motion exercises every piece: events, unilateral contact, dwell retention, tolerance UQ.

title: EPIC GOV — Program governance and cross-cutting spine
description:
PHASE-INDEPENDENT EPIC (new-domains expansion; self-contained bead graph).

WHY: The charter mandates several governance artifacts that are not physics but without which the physics program cannot be trusted or even started: the ratification of normative deltas into the master plan, a fresh commit-pinned audit (the gap analysis was performed on a moving shared repo), the program risk register (E0 planning may NOT close without it), the machine-readable Cargo manifest fixture (same-layer cycles must be impossible, not just discouraged), and the requirement-to-evidence traceability ledger.

STANDING RULES this epic encodes for every bead in the program:
1. Every new crate lands CONTRACT.md (all ten required sections, honest no-claims) BEFORE becoming a dependency target — xtask check-contracts enforces.
2. Dev-only oracles (FEniCS/FEMM for EM, Chrono/Siconos for contact, Cantera for thermochemistry) stay isolated from the production dependency graph.
3. New crates join dsr quality lanes; flagship smoke stages get provenance-pinned metric goldens with explicit tolerances; roofline receipts precede every performance claim.
4. Layer/cycle admission: contact never depends on its solid/mbd consumers; circuits never depend on EM for shared types; L1 spectral services never consume L2/L3 backends; L3 solvers never depend upward on ASCENT.
5. Every [F]/[M] bead names one baseline, activation metric, kill criterion, cost distribution, fallback, and retained falsifier (research-bet ledger).
THE TWELVE DOCTRINE PRINCIPLES (D1-D12, normative for every bead; each new crate CONTRACT cites the ones it implements):
D1 Motion is a first-class citizen (SpacetimeChart; static = identity-path special case). D2 Matter is a typed constitutive graph (storage/metric vs transport/dissipation vs interface vs reaction vs internal-memory maps; no ad hoc scalars; no Hodge-star claim beyond its mathematics). D3 Events are certified (class-valid certificate, typed Unknown/PossibleEvent, set-valued grazing/Zeno, refusal, or Estimated label; silent misses are Sev-0). D4 Mechanisms use nonlinear descent plus tangent cohomology (finite = holonomy; infinitesimal = ker J; self-stress = ker J^T; unilateral = cones; rolling = Pfaffian distributions; never one H1 slogan). D5 Machines compose through typed ports and explicit constitutive relations (power audited per exchange; open-system balances include boundary and advective terms; no private-state reach-through). D6 Correlation predictions are Validated or Estimated, never promoted by code verification alone. D7 Reduced fidelity is a lane, not a lie (0-D/1-D/network/dq lanes are first-class with their own Gauntlets). D8 Every new domain ships its adjoint or its excuse (named regime for generalized/smoothed/derivative-free alternatives). D9 Verification is not validation (separate evidence axes; QoI-specific load-bearing dependency subgraphs; no laundering either way). D10 Real machines age and vary (process, tolerance, wear, degradation are state; definition of done includes uncertainty and life-cycle evolution). D11 Closed-loop operation is part of the plant (sensors, electronics, controllers, faults simulated with the same evidence discipline). D12 One research bet per proof lane, many ambitions in the portfolio (activation criteria, kill criteria, fallbacks, retained falsifiers; ambition accumulates by certified ratchets).

EV OPPORTUNITY MATRIX (Impact x Confidence x Reuse / Effort x AdoptionFriction, 1-5 inputs; drives priority assignments):
R1 weighted constitutive operators 62.5 (E0) | R16 amount-of-substance dimension 62.5 (E0) | R2 typed material/interface data+receipts 20.8 (E0) | R4 certified spacetime/swept enclosures 13.3 (E1) | R15 port-thermodynamic+multirate bus 12.5 (E0-E7) | R3 HX/AMS+block preconditioners 10.7 (E4) | R6 nonlinear/tangent kinematic complex 10.7 (E1) | R13 topological/distributed winding coupling 10.7 (E4) | R7 SE(3) rigid-to-flexible MBD ladder 10.0 (E2-E3) | R17 power-electronics/control/bifurcation 10.0 (E4) | R5 validated true-flow event capture 9.4 (E2) | R11 equivariant conservative interface 9.4 (E4) | R8 conservative 0-D/1-D reactive stack 8.0 (E5) | R12 2-D-to-3-D moving-conductor EM 8.0 (E4) | R14 entropy/invariant-domain flux ledger 8.0 (E5) | R9 body-body contact+rigorous CCD 7.5 (E2) | R10 nonsmooth complementarity lane 4.5 (E2).

title: P0 fs-govern: enforce one active unproven mechanism per independently falsifiable proof lane
description:
ROOT CAUSE: The program documents a one-bet discipline but has no executable admission rule. A naive global singleton would suppress the intended theorem portfolio, while no rule permits unlimited correlated mechanisms inside one proof lane and lets agents spend all resources on favorable variants.

SEMANTICS: Define an authenticated ProofLaneId from statement/quantifiers, admissible domain, assumptions, target authority, baseline, falsifier family, and independence class. Permit multiple active unproven mechanisms across independently falsifiable lanes. Atomically refuse a second active mechanism in the same lane unless the policy explicitly declares a preregistered head-to-head experiment with bounded shared resources. Separately enforce global work, memory, reviewer, and falsification-capacity envelopes so lane partitioning cannot evade portfolio limits. Terminal Refuted, Tombstoned, Withdrawn, or superseded states release a slot only after durable ledger finalization; Unknown or stalled work does not silently release it. Prevent lane-ID spoofing, assumption laundering, split/merge gaming, and concurrent double admission.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Multiple distinct lanes admit concurrently; a second active mechanism in the same authenticated lane refuses atomically; explicit bounded comparison mode admits only its declared candidates; global portfolio caps still bind; terminal/tombstone transitions release exactly once; crash/retry/idempotency and concurrent admissions cannot oversubscribe. G0 state-machine and identity laws, G3 equivalent statement/assumption canonicalization and lane split/merge adversaries, G4 races/cancellation/storage faults with no partial admission, G5 deterministic replay. Mutation tests remove each same-lane, global-cap, terminal-release, and identity guard. Real no-mock E2E registers two independent theorem lanes plus competing mechanisms in one lane through fs-govern, ledger, package, checker, and replay. Bounded logs include lane/mechanism IDs, canonical statement/domain/assumptions, policy/version, resource and falsification reservations, atomic decision, terminal release, idempotency key, and ranked remedy.
close_reason: Complete with executable evidence across three slices (f06f100 lanes module, a813717 cross-crate E2E, 22cbf8a crash-reopen persistence drill) + others' hardening (c0115ef lanes v2) + close repair 5ebbb5d. VERIFIED GREEN by real runs: cargo test -p fs-govern — crate_registry 6/6, governance 9/9, lanes 11/11 (G0 identity/state-machine laws, G3 canonicalization + split/comparison adversaries, retention exhaustion), lanes_e2e 2/2 (two independent theorem lanes + preregistered in-lane comparison through fs-govern→fs-ledger→fs-package→fs-checker→byte-identical replay; crash-reopen durability with dedupe evidence), register 9/9, program_risks 12/12. Every acceptance item of the bead has passing executable coverage.

title: P0 Phase 0B: executable evidence authority, threat allocation, adjudication, and portable replay spine
description:
MISSION: Build the executable authority spine that sits between typed Phase 0 evidence objects and every theorem, simulation, optimization, and production claim. Phase 0A establishes core colors and identities; Phase 0B must make exact-instance admission, threat-directed doubt reduction, revocation, support recomputation, portable checking, and real fail-closed replay one coherent system. This is a leapfrog foundation, not a paperwork phase: new theorem-discovery machinery is welcome, but no candidate acquires production authority merely by being ambitious or internally consistent.

ARCHITECTURE: Six ordered leaves own contract algebra; canonical schema and admission; authenticated support/threat graphs plus anytime consequence-times-doubt allocation; counterexample adjudication and transitive revocation; portable package/checker authority recomposition; and no-mock red-team/cancellation/replay proof. Keep statement truth, satisfiability/nonvacuity, empirical scale evidence, checker result, reproduction, and runtime admission as orthogonal axes. Bind every edge to exact semantic identity, assumptions, domain, units, versions, capabilities, budgets, and source receipts. Preserve Unknown, Refused, Refuted, and partially supported states without collapsing them.

EXIT GATE: The epic completes only after the real E2E leaf proves an exact claim can be authored, admitted, attacked, adjudicated, packaged, checked independently, replayed, revoked by a new counterexample, and removed transitively from downstream authority under cancellation/fault injection. All six leaves have G0-G5 evidence appropriate to risk, mutation tests for every authority guard, bounded structured logging, and DSR proof. The epic depends on the terminal E2E leaf so graph completion cannot precede the executable gate.

title: Phase 0B-A: freeze evidence contract algebra and non-forgeable authority boundaries
description:
BACKGROUND: Exact-instance authority cannot be reconstructed from ad hoc booleans or prose. Freeze the common algebra used by certifiers, checkers, theorem cards, falsifiers, packages, ledgers, and runtime admission before schema implementation.

SCOPE: Define versioned typed objects for ClaimStatement, quantified domain, assumption set, satisfiability and nonvacuity evidence, EvidenceState, AuthorityState, ProofLaneId, support edge, attack edge, counterexample candidate and adjudication, revocation/tombstone, capability policy, checker decision, reproduction state, and runtime admission. Preserve distinct axes for Proved, ConditionalProof, Refuted, Unknown, statement satisfiability, exact-instance admission, KernelChecked, ScaleQualified, Reproduced, and invalidation. Specify partial order/composition laws, no implicit widening conversions, historical migration semantics, identity source/binding tables, Five Explicits, deterministic encoding, cancellation terminality, and no-claim boundaries. State how powerful new theorems can add versioned inference rules without being assumed in the default authority algebra.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: CONTRACT and generated catalog are code-derived and drift-checked. G0 covers lattice/order laws, composition monotonicity, invalid combinations, exact identity binding, schema-version refusal, and nonvacuity/satisfiability separations. Compile-fail tests prevent lower-authority values satisfying stronger APIs. G3 canonical statement/assumption reordering and equivalent units/domains preserve semantic identity while changed quantifiers or assumptions do not. Mutation tests kill every widening guard. Bounded logs name exact object kind, source identity, schema/policy version, authority axes, no-claim, and remediation.

title: Phase 0B-B: canonical evidence schema, exact-instance admission, and immutable receipts
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Correct Rust types do not suffice if serialization, migration, or capability checks can alter meaning. Implement the canonical on-wire schema and the sole exact-instance admission boundary.

SCOPE: Encode every Phase 0B contract object canonically with bounded sizes, sorted set fields, explicit units/seeds/budgets/versions/capabilities, content and semantic identities, source bindings, and schema migrations that never widen historical authority. Admission validates structure, source identities, statement/domain/assumption satisfiability requirements, policy fingerprint, checker capability, artifact availability, budget, and no-claim state before minting an opaque receipt. Receipt identity binds the exact candidate bytes and accepting policy decision; retries are idempotent, policy rotation is explicit, and accepting-verifier lies or mismatched fingerprints fail closed. Unknown fields/versions, ambiguous canonicalization, duplicate IDs, forged receipts, missing artifacts, and source drift refuse with ranked fixes.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: G0 canonical round trips, duplicate/set handling, limits, malformed JSON/binary, nonfinite values, identity collisions, idempotency, policy mismatch, and migration monotonicity. G3 equivalent field ordering/units and historical schema replay. G4 parser/allocation/storage/capability/cancellation faults publish no receipt; concurrent identical admissions mint one durable result. G5 bit-stable bytes across ISAs. Independent schema checker and mutation suite target every bound and authority field. Real fixture logs retain candidate/source/semantic/policy IDs, validation order, budget consumption, decision, receipt, retry key, and ranked remedy.

title: Phase 0B-C: authenticated support and threat graphs with anytime consequence-times-doubt allocation
description:
MISSION: Turn evidence planning into an authenticated graph problem that spends scarce falsification and checking effort where failure would matter most, without Goodharting on favorable evidence.

SCOPE: Maintain content-addressed typed support and attack graphs over exact claim instances, assumptions, artifacts, checkers, falsifiers, consumers, and authority states. Reject cycles where policy requires a DAG and represent legitimate mutual constraints without circular support. Compute consequence from reachable downstream authority and doubt from calibrated uncertainty, attack coverage, independence, and unresolved assumptions. Build an anytime allocator using consequence times doubt plus explicit diversity, holdout, independence, and exploration floors; use e-process or other anytime-valid accounting under optional stopping. Integrate the per-proof-lane one-bet rule and global portfolio caps. Every allocation decision retains the graph snapshot, utility model, priors, correlations, alternative sensitivity, budget, and no-action option. New cohomological or tropical summaries of obstruction/support structure are encouraged behind versioned theorem receipts.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: G0 graph identity, support monotonicity, attack propagation, cycle/circularity refusal, budget conservation, deterministic ties, and anytime validity. G2 seeded high-consequence weak claims receive priority without starving blind falsification. G3 graph relabeling, duplicated correlated evidence, support decomposition, utility/prior perturbation, and lane split/merge gaming. G4 concurrent graph mutation, cancellation, storage faults, optional-stopping adversaries, and allocator restart preserve budgets and publish no partial decision. G5 deterministic replay. Mutation tests remove correlation, independence, holdout, no-action, and portfolio guards. Logs retain graph root, node/edge IDs and states, consequence/doubt components, reservations, e-process state, sensitivity, decision, and terminal outcome.
