title: E10 Fidelity graph: replace the scalar ladder with a context- and QoI-specific model graph
description:
WHY: The current doctrine treats fidelity as a totally ordered ladder (fs-ladder: correlation-Nu < RANS < LES with scalar relative_cost hints), and plan language calls RANS merely a "clearly labeled low-fidelity screen". That ordering is too categorical for industrial engineering: a VALIDATED RANS setup can predict a mean load better than an under-resolved LES; LES carries inflow/wall-model/averaging-time/domain-size errors; different QoIs rank models differently; a model can be high-resolution yet outside its validated context; computational expense is NOT epistemic rank. Fidelity must become a GRAPH whose edges are empirical claims.

TARGET DESIGN: nodes = models (correlation families, low-Re RANS variants, buoyancy/radiation treatments, LBM, surrogates, BEM); edges carry (cost model, discrepancy evidence between the pair, validation domain, and the CONDITIONS under which one model is more informative than the other, per QoI and regime). Selection = admission query (fs-regime distance-to-validity) + discrepancy evidence (fs-evidence DiscrepancyModel fit on FidelityPairs) + cost (fs-plan CostModel), not index comparison. fs-ladder's Transfer machinery (prolongate/restrict) remains the state-map substrate between adjacent models.

CHILDREN: fs-ladder v2 graph data model (backward-compatible: a ladder is a path graph); empirical edge population from corpus runs (adjacent-fidelity probes); escalation-policy integration (certify_or_escalate + EscalationAdvice::EscalateModelFidelity route through the graph, choosing the CHEAPEST edge that fixes the dominant uncertainty); the cooling-vertical graph instance.

DONE WHEN: for at least two cooling QoIs (max junction temp, pressure drop), the graph selects DIFFERENT models under different regimes with recorded justification, and a case exists where the calibrated correlation legitimately outranks a higher-cost model in its validated domain — demonstrating cost != authority. Related existing beads: qmao.7 (ladder registry, closed), t2td (FidelitySheaf crosswalk, open), lmp4.16 (greedy ladder planner, closed).

title: fs-ladder v2: fidelity GRAPH data model (edges carry cost, discrepancy, validity, informativeness conditions)
description:
WHY: fs-ladder's total order (index-ordered rungs, scalar relative_cost) structurally cannot express "the calibrated correlation outranks RANS inside its validated domain for T_mean, but not for recirculation-zone T_max" — which is the actual shape of engineering model choice. The graph model is the substrate for honest escalation (e10_3) and for the corpus to TEACH the system which model to trust where (e10_2).

WHAT: (a) Data model: nodes = model identities (with ModelCard refs); directed edges between comparable models carry: cost relation (fs-plan CostModel refs, per size/regime — not a scalar constant); discrepancy evidence between the pair (DiscrepancyModel refs from FidelityPairs, per QoI); each edge's validity domain (where the comparison has evidence); informativeness conditions (typed predicates over regime + QoI declaring when the target model is MORE informative than the source — empty predicate = unknown, which is an honest state, not a default ordering); (b) backward compatibility: a Ladder is exactly a path graph with total-order predicates — LadderRegistry::cht() and existing consumers keep working via a lossless embedding, migrated not broken; (c) Transfer machinery generalizes to edges (prolongate/restrict along any evidenced edge); (d) queries: best-model-for(QoI, regime, budget), cheapest-adequate, and explain (why this model here) — all deterministic with recorded reasoning; (e) serialization + identity for ledger/report.

DONE WHEN: graph model shipped; ladder embedding proven; queries answer with recorded reasoning on a synthetic graph; the CHT instance migrates.

TESTS: unit (graph construction validation — no self-loops, card refs resolve; ladder embedding round-trip; query determinism incl. tie-breaks); property (query monotonicity: adding evidence to an edge never makes explanations less specific; removing an edge never IMPROVES a recommendation); e2e: synthetic 4-node graph exercising every query with full reasoning logs.

title: Populate fidelity-graph edges empirically from corpus runs (adjacent-fidelity probes as data)
description:
WHY: A fidelity graph with declared edges is the old ladder wearing new clothes. Edges must be EARNED from data: paired runs of adjacent models on shared cases (corpus Level A/B/C) yield FidelityPairs whose fitted discrepancy + measured cost become the edge content, per QoI and regime. This is also where "computational expense is not epistemic rank" becomes measurable fact.

WHAT: (a) Probe campaigns: for each candidate edge in the cooling graph (correlation<->thermal-LBM natural-convection overlap now; correlation<->RANS when e05_8 lands; linearized<->full radiation from e05_4; homogenized<->resolved PCB from e05_6), run both models on every shared-validity corpus case, recording per-QoI pairs + measured costs into the ledger; (b) edge fitting: DiscrepancyModel fits per (edge, QoI) with regime binning (e07_2 machinery — partition-enforced, held-out-checked); informativeness predicates derived where data supports them (model B beats A beyond envelope X in regime R) and left UNKNOWN where it does not — unknown edges are visible gaps that corpus growth fills, and the gap list is itself an output steering e04 acquisition; (c) cost models fit from the same runs (fs-plan power-law fits with residual bands); (d) refresh discipline: edges carry the corpus version + run set they were fit on; stale edges (corpus grew, kernels changed) flagged by a staleness check like fs-plan's freshness machinery.

title: Escalation through the graph: certify-or-escalate + EscalationAdvice choose the cheapest adequate edge
description:
WHY: Escalation advice today is directional (EscalateModelFidelity) and certify-or-escalate is binary (use surrogate | escalate). With a graph, escalation becomes a ROUTED decision: when model-form dominates the budget, move along the specific edge whose discrepancy evidence addresses the failing QoI in the current regime, at the lowest cost that achieves decision adequacy — and REFUSE with a gap report when no evidenced edge helps (the graph's unknown edges become explicit evidence-acquisition demands rather than blind escalation).

WHAT: (a) Escalation planner: input = current model, failing QoI + its budget breakdown (E08), regime, decision tolerance, session budget; output = ranked edge walk (possibly multi-step) with predicted post-escalation uncertainty (from edge discrepancy evidence) and cost, or EscalationGap{missing edges, suggested probes} when the graph cannot help; the prediction is checked after the escalated run (predicted-vs-actual improvement recorded — the planner's own calibration becomes data, feeding e14 metrics discipline); (b) integration: fs-surrogate certify_or_escalate gains a graph-aware variant (Decision::Escalate carries the planned edge); e06_5 orchestration honors escalation plans within budget; EscalationAdvice::EscalateModelFidelity routes here; (c) anti-thrash: hysteresis and a max-escalation budget per run (no oscillating between models on noise — borrow fs-spectral's hysteresis discipline); (d) every escalation ledgered with its reasoning.

DONE WHEN: a fixture where correlation fails on a recirculation QoI escalates along the evidenced edge (or reports the gap pre-e05_8, which is the honest current answer); planner-calibration recording works; anti-thrash proven.

title: E11 CAD admission and CAE interop: from safe file handling toward usable engineering semantics
description:
WHY: fs-io's quarantine design is right (bounded parsers, receipts, promotion-or-refusal, Estimate-only STEP authority), but bounded Part-21 syntax + one pinned triangular FACETED_BREP closure is not production CAD interoperability. Real adoption needs AP242 assemblies, trimmed NURBS B-rep, units, occurrences, attributes, PMI/GD&T, persistent topological naming, healing diagnostics, mesh-to-CAD association, and semantic design diffs. Meanwhile the mission explicitly forbids wrapping OpenCASCADE/gmsh-class kernels in production paths, so the boundary question must be RESOLVED BY EXPLICIT RULING, not drift. The same epic covers letting engineers KEEP their existing pre/post tools (export interop) while FrankenSim earns authority — "customs, not walls", which is exactly the pattern fs-io already implements.

ADAPTER POLICY OPTIONS (child 1 forces the decision): (1) pure-core-only: external tools may produce input files; we ship no adapter; (2) official quarantined out-of-process adapters: we distribute optional adapters whose OUTPUT enters through the same evidence-bearing quarantine boundary and can never confer authority by itself — RECOMMENDED; (3) plugin/FFI ecosystem with backend-specific trust contracts. Option 2 requires a deliberate fs-govern mission amendment; it must not arrive through ambiguous wording about "isolation".

CHILDREN: adapter-policy ratification; alignment with the existing AP242 program (leapfrog i94v.2.2.* tree and 8uxb STEP interchange — LINK, do not duplicate); import healing/diagnostic receipts (small-edge, sliver, gap, overlap, self-intersection); mesh-to-CAD association surviving refinement + semantic design diffs across revisions; CAE export interop tiers (VTU/XDMF first for the product, then Gmsh/Exodus II/CGNS/Abaqus INP/Nastran BDF/OpenFOAM/FMI-FMU/Parquet-Arrow as staged quarantined tiers); retained real supplier CAD corpus with import success/repair/refusal metrics.

title: Import healing + diagnostic receipts: small-edge/sliver/gap/overlap/self-intersection census with repair history
description:
WHY: fs-io's census currently counts degenerate/duplicate faces, unreferenced vertices, and edge-manifoldness — a good start, but real supplier geometry fails in richer ways: near-degenerate slivers that poison meshing, small gaps below tolerance that break watertightness claims, overlapping shells, and self-intersections that flip winding-number classification. The healing receipt (what was found, what was repaired, what remains, at what tolerance) is what lets downstream claims be honest about geometric provenance — "explicit repair history" is a core interop requirement.

WHAT: (a) Extended census diagnostics on quarantined imports: small-edge and sliver-face detection (relative to declared model tolerance); gap detection between near-adjacent boundary loops; shell overlap and self-intersection detection (leveraging fs-rep-mesh winding/intersection machinery within budgeted cost — full exact self-intersection on huge meshes is expensive: the census declares its sampling/exactness level per check, cancellable under Cx); (b) repair taxonomy with receipts: each repair op (weld, collapse, hole-fill within budget, orientation fix) recorded with before/after counts and the tolerance consumed; UNREPAIRED findings enumerated in the promotion receipt so promoted geometry carries its residual-defect list into the evidence chain (a mesh with 3 residual slivers can still promote — but the solve's geometry budget term knows); (c) refusal thresholds configurable per project (a validation-grade run may refuse what a scoping run accepts — the threshold choice is itself receipted); (d) the census feeds e08's geometry budget term and the e11_6 corpus scorecard.

DONE WHEN: extended census runs on the supplier corpus with per-file receipts; residual-defect lists propagate to promotion receipts and the geometry budget term; threshold-policy machinery works.

title: Mesh-to-CAD association surviving refinement + semantic design diffs across revisions
description:
WHY: Two adoption-critical capabilities share one foundation (stable geometric identity): (1) when the mesher refines or the geometry is re-imported, region/BC assignments must FOLLOW the geometry (today only e06_3's selector predicates provide this weakly); (2) when the designer revises the CAD, the engineer needs a SEMANTIC diff (which faces moved, which regions changed, which assignments broke) rather than a re-setup from scratch. Persistent topological naming is a famously hard CAD problem — scope honestly: selector-anchored association with declared robustness, not a general naming oracle.

WHAT: (a) Association model: assignments (regions, interfaces, BCs) bind to selector-anchored identities (e06_3) plus geometric fingerprints (local area/normal/feature signatures at declared tolerance); on re-mesh/re-import, association re-resolution reports per-assignment: STABLE (fingerprint + selector agree), MOVED (resolved with drift metrics), AMBIGUOUS/LOST (typed, requires user action — never silent rebinding); (b) semantic design diff: given two imported revisions, produce a region-level diff (unchanged/moved/deformed/topology-changed per declared tolerance, using existing quality/winding machinery + fingerprints), rendered as a report artifact and consumable by `frankensim compare`; (c) assignment migration: the diff drives assignment carry-over proposals (auto-apply STABLE, propose MOVED, refuse LOST) with receipts; (d) no-claim honesty: association is heuristic-with-declared-tolerances; the CONTRACT states what it cannot promise (adversarial topology changes defeat fingerprints) — ties to the leapfrog persistent-naming work for the eventual stronger substrate.

DONE WHEN: re-tessellation and small-revision fixtures resolve with correct per-assignment verdicts; the diff renders on a real two-revision pair; migration receipts work; LOST paths refuse loudly.

title: E12 Design-build-measure-update loop: 3-D registration, robust assimilation, joint inference, sensor design
description:
WHY: FrankenSim should IMPROVE from experience, not merely archive it. The current pieces are deliberately bounded: fs-asbuilt is 2-D rigid registration with known correspondences (Kabsch/SVD 3-D, scale, and ICP are explicitly deferred; residual_rms explicitly must not be passed as registration variance); fs-assimilate is a dense linear-Gaussian Kalman core capped at state dim 256 with 4D-Var deferred to certified adjoints. The full loop is: design -> simulate -> manufacture -> scan/instrument -> register as-built -> compare prediction vs observation -> infer parameters + discrepancy -> update model -> redesign.

CHILDREN: 3-D rigid registration (Kabsch/SVD + optional scale; then datum/feature-based registration, not only global best fit; correspondence-free ICP as frontier); registration covariance propagated into QoIs; as-built field extraction (thickness, gap, roughness, warpage, material-state fields) [frontier]; nonlinear observation operators + robust sensor data handling (missing, censored, saturated, delayed, correlated); ensemble Kalman + nonlinear weak-constraint variational assimilation beyond the dense-256 cap [frontier]; joint parameter/state/model-discrepancy inference (identifiability-checked, ties to e07 discrepancy work); sensor placement + experiment-design optimization (extend the existing fs-oed-e2e VoI pattern to the thermal vertical: "thermocouple at A or B"); drift detection between manufactured lots and operating regimes (fs-eproc DriftMonitor as substrate).

SEQUENCING: this epic is deliberately AFTER the Level-3 product slice on the critical path — it becomes decision-relevant once predictions and measurements coexist. Individual children may start earlier where they unblock Level-4 calibration.

DONE WHEN: one full loop closes on the instrumented cooling hardware (e04 Level E): scan registered in 3-D with covariance, sensors assimilated, parameters + discrepancy jointly inferred with identifiability evidence, and the UPDATED model demonstrably changes a design recommendation with the change attributed in the report.

title: 3-D rigid registration (Kabsch/SVD + optional scale), then datum/feature-based registration
description:
WHY: fs-asbuilt v1 is deliberately 2-D rigid with known correspondences; its own CONTRACT names 3-D Kabsch/SVD, scale, and correspondence-free ICP as follow-ons. Real as-built data (scans, CMM points) is 3-D, and engineering practice registers against DATUMS (the reference features tolerances are defined from), not only global best fit — a global best fit can hide exactly the local deviation a datum-based scheme is designed to expose.

WHAT: (a) 3-D rigid registration: closed-form Kabsch/SVD over corresponded fiducials (fs-la SVD path), optional similarity (scale) variant with the scale estimate REPORTED with uncertainty (silent scaling hides unit errors — a scale estimate far from 1.0 triggers a units-suspicion diagnostic); well-posedness checks (rank/conditioning of the cross-covariance, degenerate configurations refused with geometric diagnosis: collinear, coplanar); (b) calibrated covariance: extend the existing 2-D calibrated machinery (MetrologyModel, robust Huber weighting, leverage, outlier disposition) to the 3-D pose (6-dof covariance, 2n-6 dof); (c) datum/feature-based registration: register against declared datum features (plane/axis/point hierarchies per engineering drawing practice) with the datum-priority order honored (A then B then C constraint sequencing), residuals reported PER DATUM — the difference between global-fit and datum-based results is itself a diagnostic output; (d) correspondence-free ICP flagged [F] as a separate follow-on, NOT smuggled in here.

DONE WHEN: 3-D fixtures register with correct closed-form results + covariance; degenerate refusals proven; datum-based path matches hand-worked drawing-style cases; scale-suspicion diagnostic fires on a seeded unit error.

TESTS: unit (Kabsch vs analytic rotations; covariance vs Monte Carlo on synthetic noise; degeneracy refusals; datum sequencing); property (rigid-invariance metamorphic: pre-transforming both clouds leaves residuals invariant); e2e: scan-like synthetic dataset through global + datum paths logging poses, covariances, per-datum residuals, and the global-vs-datum diagnostic delta.
close_reason: Landed at 724a2ceb (pushed): fs-asbuilt rigid3 + datum modules. (a) 3-D rigid Kabsch via fs-la's deterministic Jacobi SVD; right-handed canonicalization of both singular frames makes R = V*U^T exact in every admitted case including coplanar rank-2; spectral rank gates refuse coincident/collinear design or measured configurations with geometric diagnosis; coplanar admitted + flagged; reflection-preferring data surfaced as a mirrored-part diagnostic, and the ambiguous hard case (reflection + coincident trailing singular values) refuses fail-closed. Similarity variant reports Umeyama scale WITH first-order SE and a units-suspicion diagnostic naming the nearest common conversion factor (fires on seeded 25.4, proven). (b) Calibrated 6-dof covariance extends the MetrologyModel machinery: scalar-weighted global Kabsch estimator (base weights 3/trace), full-anisotropic sandwich covariance (reduces exactly to GLS when isotropic - tested against a hand-computed axis configuration AND 1500-replicate Monte Carlo), deterministic Huber with re-solve-after-every-refresh, leverage summing to 6, outlier dispositions, domain-separated identity. dof = 3n-6 (bead text said 2n-6, a 2-D carryover typo - noted). (c) Datum-priority 3-2-1 registration: A/B/C hierarchy is STRUCTURAL (B out-of-plane and C transverse perturbations provably cannot move the datum pose - locked by tests), per-datum signed residuals, datum-vs-global delta published as a first-class diagnostic; hand-worked block fixture recovers a seeded pose exactly. (d) ICP stays out as [F] follow-on; CT volume registration remains staged scope (recorded in CONTRACT no-claims with anisotropic-efficiency, 3-D equicorrelation, and datum-covariance no-claims). Honest finding folded into tests/docs: the residual-norm delta's SIGN at a deviated target is geometry-dependent (each fit absorbs deviation per its own leverage structure), so the diagnostic is the disagreement magnitude plus the datum-frame attribution, not a one-sided inequality. Verification: 68/68 fs-asbuilt tests green via RCH on the committed tree; new modules and tests clippy-clean on the pinned nightly (remaining 6 lib warnings are pre-existing uncertainty.rs/lib.rs drift-class debt owned by 3h5ad backlog); xtask check-layers/deps/unsafe/source-manifest all 141/0 with the manifest regenerated and staged same-commit per the new 13.2 gate; fs-cli contract violations are the known .6.2 red, not this crate. title: Compose as-built field extraction with a conduction solve end to end (extend the 5-stage as_built_chain)
description:
WHY: f85xj.12.3 built the L2 as-built field extraction (fs_asbuilt::field, 530266f2) and f85xj.12.9 built the L3 consumption seam (InterfaceSurface::new_mapped + InterfaceResistance::with_measured_value, 5202f645). Both are unit- and property-tested in their own crates, but NOTHING composes them: no lane anywhere takes a registered scan, extracts a thickness field, converts it to per-face R'', and solves. Until that exists, "as-built fields can drive a conduction solve" is an inference from two green crates rather than an observed result, which is exactly the kind of claim this program refuses to make on inference.

WHAT: Extend the existing 5-stage chain in crates/fs-diffreal-e2e/tests/as_built_chain.rs (register -> bind -> propagate -> budget -> render) with a physics stage. EXTEND, do not duplicate: that file already builds a CalibratedRigid3Registration from 8 deterministic literal-noise fiducials and threads one identity through every stage.

(a) New stage: from the registered pose, build paired opposing-face SurfaceSamples over a synthetic bond line, extract a fs_asbuilt::field::ThicknessField, convert per-station thickness to area-specific resistance (R''_i = t_i / k with k from the material card), and bind them through InterfaceSurface::new_mapped + InterfaceResistance::with_measured_value.
(b) Solve with fs_conduction::solve::solve_with_interfaces and assert the physically expected direction: a thicker measured bond line conducts less and raises the hot-side temperature drop relative to the nominal-thickness solve. Direction and monotonicity, not a validated magnitude.
(c) Identity/provenance: assert the registration identity reaching the solve is the SAME one the earlier stages bound, that every per-face resistance reports ResistanceValueOrigin::CallerSupplied, and that the interface flux still cites the one material card.
(d) Forensic log: one JSON line per stage, matching the file's existing `"stage":"..."` marker convention.

DEPENDENCY NOTE - this is the reason the bead exists separately: fs-diffreal-e2e already depends on fs-asbuilt but NOT on fs-conduction. Adding it (dev-dependency; layer-exempt and out of the production graph) requires a Cargo.lock edit. At the time of filing, Cargo.lock carried at least three agents' uncommitted changes (fs-report/xtask deps, the resolved frankensqlite graph, an fs-io -> fs-blake3 edge), so touching it would have swept foreign work into an unrelated commit. DONE WHEN: the extended chain runs green; the thicker-bond-line direction assertion holds; the registration identity is unbroken end to end; the stage log is retained.

It demonstrates that the seam works, not that any number is validated. f85xj.12.3's DONE-WHEN 2 (a real or rig-derived scan) stays open and blocked on Level-E hardware (f85xj.4.5); every field value remains Estimate-class, and its no-claims (supplied correspondence, unfiltered roughness, first-order pose linearization, measured values the card does not endorse) travel into this lane unchanged.

title: Registration covariance propagated into QoIs (geometry term of the error budget goes live)
description:
WHY: A registration is only as useful as what its uncertainty DOES: if the as-built pose is uncertain by 0.3 mm, the heatsink contact area, gap conductances, and therefore T_junction inherit that uncertainty. fs-asbuilt's CONTRACT explicitly warns that residual_rms must not be misused as transform covariance — the CALIBRATED covariance must flow, typed, into the e08 geometry budget term. This is where the budget's geometry slot stops being Unknown for as-built-informed runs.

WHAT: (a) Propagation path: registration covariance (E12_1) -> geometric parameter uncertainty (positions/orientations of as-built parts vs nominal) -> QoI sensitivity (via the e06_7 UQ machinery: sample poses within covariance, or linearized propagation where sensitivities are cheap — method choice recorded, linearization validity checked against a sampling spot-check); (b) the as-built scenario variant: a project may bind PartPlacement::AsBuilt{registration_ref} instead of nominal; solves under as-built placement carry the geometry term populated from the registration record; (c) honest correlation: pose errors are correlated across QoIs (one transform moves everything) — propagate as a correlated block (E08_1 representation), not independent per-QoI noise; (d) report renders nominal-vs-as-built QoI deltas with the geometry term attributed.

DONE WHEN: an as-built-informed reference run shows a populated geometry budget term with correlated structure; linearization-vs-sampling agreement checked; nominal-vs-as-built delta renders.

TESTS: unit (covariance-to-parameter mapping; correlated-block construction; method-choice recording); statistical (synthetic truth: known injected pose error recovered in QoI uncertainty within tolerance); e2e: full as-built pipeline (register -> bind -> solve -> budget) with per-stage logging including the correlation structure of the emitted term.
close_reason: COMPLETE across three commits. Phase 1 (8bb13d3e): fs-asbuilt::propagate — cross-QoI covariance G*Sigma*G^T in one content-addressed record; per-QoI geometry terms cite the shared record so correlation travels; deterministic 12-sigma-point linearization spot-check vs caller evaluator with rejection downgrading terms to Unknown (method recorded). Phase 2 (61c5862e): (b) PlacementBasis::AsBuilt{registration_ref: ContentHash} in fs-scenario — a citation, not a record, so no fs-scenario<->fs-asbuilt dependency edge exists in either direction (L3 vs L2); the all-zero identity is refused at declaration (PlacementRegistrationUnbound) before any mutation so the stronger claim can never cite nothing; as_built_registrations() is the declaration-ordered resolution seam. (d) fs-report::nominal_vs_as_built_markdown — per-QoI shift with the geometry term attributed, shift_resolved() as a TRI-STATE (None when the term publishes no half-width, e.g. after a rejected linearization), and a correlation line DERIVED from the rows: one shared record renders as a correlated block, distinct records render as an explicit refusal of that claim. Phase 3 (7990ac9e): fs-diffreal-e2e/tests/as_built_chain.rs — the full register->bind->resolve->propagate->budget->render chain proving ONE identity survives all five stages, with per-stage forensic logging incl. correlation structure, plus a determinism case. DONE-WHEN satisfied: populated geometry budget term with correlated structure in an as-built-informed run (rho01>0.5, all terms citing one record); linearization-vs-sampling agreement checked (phase 1 spot-check); nominal-vs-as-built delta renders. TESTS satisfied: unit (covariance->parameter mapping, correlated-block construction, method recording), statistical (4000-rep synthetic-truth recovery, phase 1), e2e with per-stage logging. Bug found and fixed by its own test: geometry_half_width read IntervalBound as (upper-lower)/2, but that variant brackets the HALF-WIDTH itself and fs-evidence aggregates its upper endpoint — the midpoint reading reported LESS uncertainty than the budget; ab_002 now fails if it is ever swapped back. title: As-built field extraction [F]: thickness, gap, warpage, roughness maps from registered scans (CT staged)
description:
WHY: Pose is the first-order as-built correction; FIELDS are the second and often decisive one: actual TIM bond-line thickness, actual board warpage changing contact patterns, actual gap distributions under covers, surface roughness governing contact conductance, and material-state fields (local density/porosity from process variation) where measurable. These fields feed directly into the physics (gap conductance maps, contact-resistance spatial variation) and are where design-build-measure-update earns its keep for thermal problems. Frontier-tagged: scan processing is noisy, and every extracted field must carry measurement + registration uncertainty.

WHAT: (a) Field extraction from registered point sets vs nominal geometry: signed-distance deviation maps over declared surfaces (fs-rep-sdf/query machinery for correspondence); derived fields with uncertainty: local thickness (two-surface distance), gap maps (as-built clearance between mating surfaces), warpage (low-order modal fit of deviation on plate-like regions — fit order declared, residual reported); (b) roughness: profile/areal roughness summaries (Ra/Sq-class) from high-resolution scan patches where the instrument supports it, feeding contact-conductance correlations in E05_3's dry-contact models — roughness-informed conductance carries BOTH roughness measurement uncertainty and correlation model uncertainty; (c) material-state fields staged honestly: density/porosity fields require CT-class volumetric data — CT VOLUME REGISTRATION AND FIELD EXTRACTION IS EXPLICIT STAGED SCOPE (recorded as no-claim until a CT data source exists; the schema reserves the field types so corpus retention can hold CT data when it arrives); (d) uncertainty composition: scan noise (from metrology model) + registration covariance (E12_1) + correspondence ambiguity (surface-normal sensitivity) composed into per-point field uncertainty — honest, correlated where the registration term dominates; (e) physics binding: gap/thickness/roughness maps consumable as spatially varying interface-resistance inputs (E05_3's model gains a map-valued variant) with the field's uncertainty entering the budget; (f) staged scope: plate-like and simple mating geometries first; free-form surfaces recorded as no-claim.

DONE WHEN: synthetic-scan fixtures recover known injected warpage/thickness/roughness fields within uncertainty; a real (or rig-derived, e04 Level E) scan produces fields feeding one as-built-informed solve; CT staging + free-form no-claims documented.

TESTS: unit (deviation-map correctness on analytic offsets; modal-fit recovery of injected warpage; roughness-summary arithmetic on synthetic profiles; uncertainty composition arithmetic); adversarial (correspondence ambiguity on near-vertical walls -> flagged, not silently wrong); e2e: scan-to-solve pipeline logging field statistics, uncertainty maps, and the resulting interface-model deltas.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LilacAspen 2026-07-24: core field-extraction slice landed at 530266f2 (fs-asbuilt, L2). 3070 lines across 5 files, ZERO new dependency edges on the crate.

DELIVERED (bead items a, b, d, f, plus the c/f no-claims):
- field::DeviationField - signed normal deviation per supplied correspondence with three separately reported one-sigma terms: range noise (range_sigma*c, which SHRINKS at oblique incidence because a range error there moves the point mostly along the surface), registration pose sqrt(g'Cg), and correspondence ambiguity (lateral_sigma*sqrt(1-c^2)/c from lateral footprint elongation, which GROWS and diverges edge-on). Composed in quadrature, coverage-scaled. The two moving in OPPOSITE directions is pinned by test; a model that just scaled everything by 1/c would pass a one-sided check.
- field::ThicknessField - paired-face local thickness/gap. Its pose term is the quadratic form of the SUMMED face sensitivities, not a quadrature over the two faces: both faces ride one pose, so on opposing normals the translation sensitivities cancel and a rigid motion contributes no first-order thickness uncertainty (as it must - rigid motion cannot change the distance between two faces of one part). Quadrature would have manufactured ~1.41x a single face sigma out of nothing.
- field::fit_form - low-order total-degree warpage form. Rank is checked on the QR diagonal BEFORE solve_ls, so a collinear station set refuses instead of returning an arbitrary member of the solution family with a fabricated cross-line tilt. Warpage is the FITTED surface peak-to-valley with the residual reported alongside.
- field::profile_statistics - Ra/Rq/Rt/Rz after declared form removal, explicitly UNFILTERED.
- measurement_term() projects the field into the EngineeringUncertaintyKind::Measurement budget slot as an IntervalBound bracketing the per-point half-widths. Deliberately NOT a Geometry term: propagate already carries the pose contribution, and emitting it twice would inflate the budget while looking more rigorous.

title: Nonlinear observation operators + robust sensor pathologies (missing/censored/saturated/delayed/correlated)
description:
WHY: fs-assimilate's linear-Gaussian core assumes clean, synchronous, linear observations. Real thermal instrumentation delivers none of that: thermocouples fail (missing), clip at range limits (censored/saturated), lag the state (sensor time constants — delayed), and share calibration/ambient errors (correlated). An assimilation system that ignores these pathologies quietly biases the posterior — the classic silent-wrong-answer shape this project exists to kill.

WHAT: (a) Observation-operator extension: nonlinear h(x) via linearization within the existing Gauss-Newton/Kalman core (Jacobians from fs-ad where the forward map is AD-friendly; finite-difference fallback with step-size receipts), with linearization-validity checks (innovation-magnitude gates) that DEMOTE rather than pretend; (b) pathology handling, each typed and receipted: missing -> exclusion with dof accounting; censored/saturated -> either refusal-from-update or a declared censored-likelihood treatment [staged; refusal is the honest v1]; delayed -> declared sensor time-constant models augmenting the observation map; correlated -> non-diagonal observation covariance admitted (PSD-gated like existing machinery) with shared-error factors (one ambient reference shared across sensors); (c) every accepted/rejected observation logged with its disposition reason (the assimilation audit trail is a first-class output); (d) scope honesty: still the bounded dense core (<=256 dims) — the caps stay until e12_5.

DONE WHEN: synthetic thermal fixtures with each pathology assimilate correctly (or refuse correctly); disposition audit renders; correlated-error case shows the posterior difference vs naive diagonal (the demonstrable bias).

TESTS: unit (each pathology path; PSD gates; dof accounting; linearization gates); statistical (posterior consistency on linear-Gaussian limits — must reproduce the existing core exactly when pathologies are absent); e2e: rig-like synthetic campaign logging per-observation dispositions and posterior evolution.

title: Ensemble Kalman + nonlinear weak-constraint variational assimilation [F] (beyond the dense-256 core)
description:
WHY: The dense linear-Gaussian core caps at state dimension 256 — enough for lumped/network thermal states, not for field estimation (temperature fields over a board have thousands of dofs). The staged successors are known and were always declared (fs-assimilate CONTRACT defers weak-constraint 4D-Var to certified adjoints): ensemble Kalman methods scale via sample covariance; nonlinear variational assimilation leverages the adjoint machinery this workspace already has (fs-adjoint transient heat scaffold is literally the needed ingredient).

WHAT (two independently landable stages): (a) EnKF family: deterministic square-root ensemble filter (no perturbed-obs randomness where avoidable; where sampling is needed, Philox-keyed), localization with declared radii (spurious-correlation control — the localization choice is a model card-like declaration with its own validity notes), inflation as a declared, receipted parameter; ensemble statistics feed evidence (spread-vs-error consistency checks — an overconfident ensemble is a coverage failure, e07_4 machinery applies); (b) weak-constraint nonlinear variational (4D-Var-style) over the transient heat path: adjoint-based gradient of the misfit under model-error weighting, optimizer from fs-ascent (L-BFGS), gradient VERIFICATION gate mandatory before trust (the existing gradient-check discipline — no unverified adjoint drives an update); (c) both paths produce Estimated-colored posteriors with method cards; cross-validation between EnKF and variational results on shared fixtures is itself model-form evidence; (d) caps replaced by resource-governed admission (fs-session budgets), not hardcoded dims.

DONE WHEN: both methods assimilate a synthetic transient board-field fixture; spread-consistency and gradient-verification gates enforced; cross-method agreement recorded; caps governed not hardcoded.

TESTS: unit (square-root update algebra vs dense-core limit on small cases; localization/inflation receipts; gradient-check gate refusal path); statistical (twin experiments: known truth recovered within ensemble spread at declared rates); e2e: twin-experiment campaign logging ensemble diagnostics, cost-function descent, verification gates, and posterior evidence assembly.

title: Joint parameter/state/model-discrepancy inference (identifiability-gated model updating)
description:
WHY: The update step of design-build-measure-update must decide WHAT the data is telling us: is the contact resistance different than assumed (parameter), is the current temperature field different (state), or is the MODEL structurally off (discrepancy)? Joint inference without identifiability discipline produces confident nonsense — parameters absorb model error and then extrapolate it. This bead composes e07_2's discrepancy machinery with e12's assimilation into gated joint updating.

WHAT: (a) Joint formulation: augmented estimation over (parameters, state, discrepancy-model coefficients) with the e07_2 identifiability discipline enforced mechanically: separable-experiment requirements (parameters needing dedicated pinning data refuse co-fitting without it), confounding declarations that demote outputs, and held-out predictive checks after every update; (b) update admission: an inferred update is ADMITTED to the project's model state only when it improves held-out prediction AND passes coverage checks (e07_4) — updates that improve fit but worsen held-out are the signature of error-absorption and REFUSE with that diagnosis; (c) provenance: every admitted update is a ledgered event (what data, what moved, what improved) so model state has a lineage — the "archive experience vs improve from experience" distinction made auditable; (d) the update loop feeds back into DecisionAssessment: post-update assessments cite the update lineage.

DONE WHEN: a synthetic confounded case refuses correctly; a synthetic identifiable case updates and improves held-out; one real rig-data update admitted with full lineage; report renders update history.

TESTS: unit (admission-gate logic; refusal diagnostics; lineage records); statistical (twin experiments with injected parameter error vs injected model error — the machinery must ATTRIBUTE correctly at declared rates, the core scientific test of this bead); e2e: full update cycle on rig data logging the attribution evidence, gate verdicts, and lineage chain.

title: Sensor placement + experiment-design optimization (thermocouple at A or B, priced by decision value)
description:
WHY: "Would a thermocouple at location A or B reduce decision uncertainty more?" is one of the product's canonical questions, and the ingredients exist separately: fs-voi (EVPI, action_value, recommend/STOP), fs-oed-e2e (the Kalman+VoI sensor-placement pattern), and now the thermal forward model with budgets. Composing them makes experiment design a product capability instead of a demo.

WHAT: (a) Candidate-design model: sensor placement candidates (locations from the scenario's sensor objects, e17_4), each with cost, feasibility constraints (mounting, wiring), and predicted information value — computed by simulated assimilation (E12_4 machinery in twin-experiment mode: simulate measuring there, measure the posterior decision-uncertainty reduction on the ACTUAL decision quantity per e08's decision-view attribution, not generic variance); (b) recommendation: ranked designs by decision-value-per-cost (fs-voi ActionValue), with the honest null recommendation when NO candidate changes the decision posture (recommend STOP/no-instrumentation — spending on sensors that cannot flip a decision is waste the tool should name); (c) beyond sensors: the same machinery prices experiment candidates generally (a dedicated TIM measurement vs another thermocouple vs a mesh refinement — unifying with E08_5's recommendations into one priced action menu); (d) validation hook: after a recommended sensor is actually placed (rig, e04 Level E), compare realized vs predicted uncertainty reduction — the planner's calibration is itself tracked (e14 discipline).

DONE WHEN: A-vs-B recommendations compute on the reference project with decision-value reasoning; the null recommendation fires correctly; one realized-vs-predicted comparison recorded from rig data.

TESTS: unit (twin-experiment plumbing; value arithmetic; ranking determinism); statistical (synthetic cases where the informative location is known -> recovered); e2e: full design-menu run logging per-candidate simulated posteriors, values, costs, ranking, and the recommendation narrative.

title: Drift detection across manufacturing lots and operating regimes (models age; catch it)
description:
WHY: A model validated on last quarter's build lot can silently degrade: supplier material shifts, assembly-process drift, and new operating regimes carry the model outside the population it was calibrated on. fs-eproc's DriftMonitor (anytime-valid two-sample e-tests on PITs) and ExchangeabilityCard are exactly the right substrate; what is missing is wiring drift detection into the PRODUCT's ongoing-data path with consequences.

WHAT: (a) Drift channels monitored per model/dataset population: prediction-residual drift (new observations vs calibrated expectations, PIT-based via DriftMonitor); input-population drift (material receipts, as-built statistics shifting vs the calibration population); coverage decay (rolling e07_4 coverage on recent data); each channel anytime-valid (no fixed-window p-hacking — the e-process discipline this workspace already champions); (b) consequences typed: a drift verdict marks affected calibrations STALE, demotes dependent claims (e08_3 demotion machinery reused with cause=drift), and emits a recalibration demand with the drifted channel named; staleness propagates to fidelity-graph edges (e10_2 freshness) and the scorecard; (c) lot/regime segmentation: drift tracked per declared segment (manufacturing lot, operating-regime bucket via the Mondrian pattern) so one drifting lot does not silently poison — or get hidden by — the pooled statistics; (d) all verdicts ledgered with the evidence trail.

DONE WHEN: injected-drift synthetics detected at declared rates with correct segment attribution; staleness/demotion propagation proven end-to-end; a monitoring lane runs on accumulating rig data.

TESTS: unit (channel plumbing; verdict typing; propagation wiring); statistical (detection-power and false-alarm calibration on synthetic drift of varied magnitude/onset — including the no-drift null holding its e-value guarantee); e2e: a simulated multi-lot campaign logging per-segment monitors, verdicts, and the demotion/recalibration audit trail.

title: Map-valued interface resistance: let as-built thickness/roughness fields drive a conduction solve
description:
WHY: f85xj.12.3 landed the L2 as-built FIELD extraction (fs_asbuilt::field, commit 530266f2): per-station thickness, gap, and roughness maps with composed uncertainty. Nothing consumes them yet. fs-conduction still applies ONE face-constant area-specific resistance R'' per named interface surface, so a measured bond-line thickness map or roughness-informed conductance map cannot reach a solve. This bead is the seam that makes as-built field extraction earn its keep for thermal problems, and it is the (e) item of 12.3 that could not land with the L2 slice because fs-conduction is L3 and must consume the L2 type, never the reverse.

WHAT: A map-valued variant of the interface resistance in crates/fs-conduction/src/interface.rs, additive so every existing caller and golden keeps working.

(a) InterfaceSurface currently holds one `resistance: InterfaceResistance` for all face pairs (interface.rs:490, constructor :498). Add a per-face-pair form, e.g. `InterfaceSurface::new_mapped(name, face_pairs, resistances)` with `resistances` index-paired to `face_pairs`, keeping `new(...)` as the uniform case. Storing an enum (Uniform | PerFace(Vec<..>)) keeps the uniform path allocation-free and keeps the existing receipt semantics intact.

(b) THE SYNC HAZARD, which is the whole risk of this bead: ThermalInterfaces::new sorts each surface's face pairs in place (`surface.face_pairs.sort_by_key(|pair| pair.normalized())`, interface.rs:596) and sorts surfaces by name (:582). A parallel resistance array MUST be permuted by the same key, or every face silently gets another face's resistance — a wrong answer with no error. Sort (pair, resistance) as one unit rather than sorting the pairs and hoping. Add a test that a deliberately unsorted input yields the same per-face conductances as its pre-sorted equivalent.

(c) Consumption sites: `let conductance_density = 1.0 / surface.resistance.value_m2_k_per_w` appears at interface.rs:785 (fluxes) and :818 (assembly), with `face_conductance = face.area_m2 * conductance_density` at :797. Per-face area is already carried on BoundFacePair, so the change is indexing the resistance rather than hoisting it. BoundSurface (:554) copies `resistance: surface.resistance` at :663 and needs the same treatment. Check the interface-aware assembly paths in assemble.rs (assemble_operator_with_interfaces, assemble_jacobian_with_interfaces, and the scaled/optional variants) for further hoists.

(d) Uncertainty: InterfaceResistance carries an UncertaintyModel and a PropertyUsageReceipt. A per-face map must retain per-face uncertainty and an ordered receipt, not collapse to one card. The existing SeriesResistanceBudget rule that one Unstated term makes the complete half-width unavailable should hold per face.

(e) The fs-asbuilt binding: a helper turning a `field::ThicknessField` (or a roughness-informed conductance) into the per-face resistance vector. Keep the direction L2 -> L3: fs-conduction may depend on fs-asbuilt, never the reverse. Note fs-conduction does not currently depend on fs-asbuilt, so this is a new edge to justify (both are below HELM; L3 depending on L2 is layer-legal and check-layers should accept it).

DONE WHEN: a map-valued interface solves with per-face conductances; an unsorted-input test proves the sort permutation is correct; existing contact goldens are untouched; the CONTRACT sentence is updated precisely.

TESTS: unit (per-face conductance selection; the unsorted-input permutation test; per-face uncertainty retention; length-mismatch refusal between face_pairs and resistances); regression (crates/fs-conduction/tests/contact.rs asserts `flux.conductance_w_per_k == 10.0` on the two-slab fixture and MUST keep passing unchanged); e2e (a thickness map from fs_asbuilt::field driving a solve and moving the interface flux in the physically expected direction).

CONTRACT: crates/fs-conduction/CONTRACT.md says "one face-constant positive R'' per named surface" — that sentence is what this bead edits. KEEP the adjacent no-claims: a geometry-driven spatial map is NOT a pressure-, gap-, or temperature-dependent constitutive law, and contact remains matching-P1 only. Also keep "contact-resistance adjoints are not exposed" unless this bead adds one.

NO-CLAIM to carry: a measured thickness map entering a solve does not make the solve validated. Every fs_asbuilt::field value is Estimate-class with a declared, not certified, uncertainty composition, and f85xj.12.3's no-claims (supplied correspondence, unfiltered roughness, first-order pose linearization) travel with it.

title: E13 Constellation trust cone: treat the 7 pinned siblings as the trusted computing base
description:
WHY: Production dependencies are restricted to std + the Franken constellation; constellation.lock pins 7 siblings (asupersync, frankensqlite, franken_numpy, frankenscipy, frankentorch, frankenpandas, franken_networkx) by exact commit, and tools/bootstrap verifies source identity with impressive rigor (clean trees, nested submodules, index parsing, case-collision detection, transport default-deny). But that establishes REPRODUCIBILITY AND CONTENT IDENTITY ONLY — not independent review, maintainer diversity/bus factor, security governance, API stability, coordinated versioning, vulnerability handling, release availability, independent verification of load-bearing algorithms, reproducible binary distribution, or archival/escrow. The elaborate bootstrap reduces one risk class; it does not remove common-authorship and governance risk. The siblings ARE part of FrankenSim's trusted computing base and must be audited as such.

CHILDREN: trust-cone assessment document (per-sibling: role, load-bearing surface, risk class, review status); unified SBOM + source manifest generation (xtask, machine-readable, covering the whole cone); vendored reproducible release source bundle that does NOT require the sibling-directory layout (release artifact = one self-contained verified source tree); cross-repository compatibility suite + release-train policy (a sibling bump is a tested event, not an ambient drift); independent review of the most load-bearing sibling components (priority: frankensqlite durability/crash-recovery as the ledger's foundation, asupersync cancellation semantics as the runtime's foundation); maintainership/incident-response/bus-factor policy.

DONE WHEN: SBOM ships with every release bundle; an external user can build Cooling 0.1 from the vendored bundle with zero sibling checkouts; the compatibility suite gates sibling pin bumps in DSR; the trust-cone doc names residual risks explicitly. Related existing beads: sj31i.50 tree (constellation admission, open), 1t8i (blank-box bootstrap, closed), obh8 (lock schema lockstep, closed).

title: Unified SBOM + source manifest for the whole trust cone (xtask-generated, release-attached)
description:
WHY: An external evaluator currently has no single artifact answering "what source, exactly, is this system made of?" — the answer is scattered across constellation.lock, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, and per-repo state. A unified, machine-readable SBOM/source manifest is table stakes for any organization evaluating the tool, and it is cheap because the verification machinery (locks, admission, cleanliness) already exists — this bead AGGREGATES, it does not re-verify.

WHAT: (a) An xtask generator (e.g. `xtask sbom`) emitting a versioned manifest covering: FrankenSim itself (commit, tree state); all 7 siblings (commit, version, remote, verification receipt refs from bootstrap provenance); the pinned toolchain (channel, components, host); workspace crate inventory with layers + unsafe-capsule registry summary; the dev-only oracle boundary (declared external comparison tools/data with their isolation status — the SBOM distinguishes production cone from development references EXPLICITLY, which is the honest rendering of the Franken-only policy); (b) format: an in-house deterministic JSON schema first (identity-hashed like other repo manifests), with a standard-format rendering (SPDX-class) as a staged follow-on once the content is stable — content before ceremony; (c) wiring: generated in the DSR release lane; embedded in the e13_3 release bundle and referenced by evidence packages (a package can cite the SBOM identity it was produced under); (d) drift check: `xtask sbom --check` fails when the committed manifest disagrees with reality (same pattern as other repo checks).

DONE WHEN: manifest generates deterministically; check mode gates in check-all; release bundle + packages embed/cite it; documented for external readers.

TESTS: unit (each section's generator against fixtures; determinism; check-mode divergence detection incl. a seeded sibling-commit mismatch); e2e: full generation + check cycle logged section by section, plus a package-citation round trip.

title: Vendored reproducible release source bundle (no sibling-directory layout required)
description:
WHY: Today a fresh machine needs the bootstrap to materialize seven sibling checkouts in exact filesystem positions — appropriate for development, hostile for evaluation and reproduction (e07_6 depends on fixing this). A release must be ONE self-contained, verified source artifact: vendor the exact pinned sibling sources into a bundle whose internal manifest proves it matches the lock, so `build from bundle` requires no network, no layout, no bootstrap.

WHAT: (a) Bundle assembler (xtask/DSR lane): exports the verified sibling trees (post-admission, clean-tree-checked — reuse the existing cleanliness machinery) plus FrankenSim itself into a content-addressed archive with: the SBOM (e13_2), per-tree content roots, the constellation lock, and a top-level bundle identity hash; path-dependency rewriting for the vendored layout handled mechanically and verified by building; (b) verification: `verify-bundle` recomputes tree roots against the manifest (an evaluator can check integrity without trusting the assembler); build-from-bundle proven on a machine with NO ~/projects siblings; (c) reproducibility: assembling twice from the same repo states yields byte-identical bundles (deterministic archive ordering, no timestamps — the golden-artifact discipline applied to release engineering); (d) policy: release artifacts for the vertical ship as bundles; the sibling-layout path remains the DEVELOPMENT mode, not the distribution mode.

DONE WHEN: bundle builds + verifies + compiles the workspace and passes the e06_11 acceptance lane on a blank environment; byte-reproducibility proven; e07_6's reproduction kit consumes it.

TESTS: unit (manifest/root computation; deterministic archiving; path-rewrite correctness); e2e: assemble -> verify -> blank-machine build -> acceptance lane, fully logged (the 1t8i blank-box precedent extended to bundles); tamper drill (one byte changed -> verify fails naming the tree).

title: Cross-repo compatibility suite + release-train policy (sibling bumps become tested events)
description:
WHY: Sibling pins currently move by ad hoc decision; nothing systematically answers "does FrankenSim still hold its contracts on the new asupersync/frankensqlite commit?" before a bump lands. Coordinated versioning and vulnerability response (the governance gaps the trust-cone assessment names) both require bumps to be TESTED, RECORDED events — a release train, however small.

WHAT: (a) The compatibility suite: a designated test subset exercising each sibling's load-bearing surface FROM FrankenSim (from the e13_1 usage map): ledger crash/durability drills against frankensqlite; cancellation/drain/two-lane semantics against asupersync; the numerics siblings' actually-used APIs; suite runnable against a CANDIDATE pin set (a proposed constellation.lock) in an isolated target dir; (b) bump protocol: a pin change requires — candidate lock, compatibility suite green on it, changelog/severity notes (is this a fix pickup? behavior change?), golden-coupling implications checked (the rand_nla mis-pin lesson: goldens and pins move together with same-commit discipline), and the bump recorded as a ledger/governance event; (c) cadence policy doc: when trains run, what qualifies for out-of-train emergency bumps (security/correctness), who signs off; (d) rollback: the previous verified lock is always one recorded step back.

DONE WHEN: suite runs against current pins green; one REHEARSED bump executed through the full protocol (candidate -> suite -> record -> land or reject); policy doc merged; emergency path documented.

TESTS: the suite is the standing test; protocol drills (a bump attempt without suite-green is refused by the gate; a seeded sibling regression is caught by the suite with the failing surface named); e2e: rehearsed-bump transcript with full per-stage logging.
notes: 2026-07-22 f85xj.13.1 input: derive the first compatibility matrix from the generated measured surfaces, not plan prose. Start with P1 asupersync cancellation/drain/fs-exec adapter and FrankenSQLite WAL/transaction/migration/checkpoint behavior; next include active franken_numpy, frankenscipy oracle, franken_networkx, and frankentorch surfaces. Keep frankenpandas in an explicit pinned-unused/no-runtime-claim state until first-consumer admission.

title: Independent review of load-bearing sibling components (frankensqlite durability, asupersync cancellation first)
description:
WHY: Common authorship across the constellation means an assumption shared between FrankenSim and a sibling is invisible to every internal test. For the components UNDER the certificates — frankensqlite (ledger durability, crash recovery, the WAL/locking semantics all receipts depend on) and asupersync (cancellation request->drain->finalize, structured-concurrency guarantees under panics) — independent scrutiny is the only cure for that blindness. "Independent" is honestly graded: a genuinely external reviewer is ideal; minimum credible = review by an agent/person with no authorship history on the target, against the target's own claimed contracts, with adversarial tests written from the CONTRACT ALONE before reading the implementation.

WHAT: per target (frankensqlite first, asupersync second, others per e13_1 priority): (a) a review charter: the claims under review (from the sibling's docs + FrankenSim's usage assumptions per the e13_1 map), explicitly including the known sharp edges (e.g. the fsqlite IS-NULL/prepare-time-folding incident class — regressions of fixed bugs are prime review targets); (b) contract-first adversarial testing: reviewer writes crash/interruption/concurrency drills from the contract before reading code (ledger torn-write recovery, mid-transaction kill -9, lock-contention storms; cancellation during drain, panic-during-finalize, nested-scope leak hunts); (c) findings filed as beads in the SIBLING repo where fixable there, with FrankenSim-side mitigations tracked here; (d) the review outcome (scope, method, findings, residual concerns) recorded in the trust-cone assessment — a review that found nothing must still record what it TRIED.

DONE WHEN: both priority reviews completed with recorded charters + adversarial suites + dispositioned findings; the assessment's review-status column updates; residual risks named.

TESTS: the adversarial suites join the e13_4 compatibility suite where they are FrankenSim-runnable; drill-quality bar: each suite must include at least one drill that FAILS on a seeded regression of a historically fixed sibling bug.
notes: 2026-07-22 f85xj.13.1 priority input: P1 independent reviews are asupersync scope cancellation, deadline propagation, runtime shutdown, and fs-exec adapter boundaries plus FrankenSQLite WAL durability, transaction boundaries, migration refusal, blob/checkpoint behavior. The generated assessment explicitly records that sibling-local model checks do not prove FrankenSim protocols and that no independent cross-repo durability/cancellation adjudication exists.

title: Constellation maintainership, incident-response, and archival policy (the governance half of trust)
description:
WHY: Technical verification cannot answer governance questions an adopting organization will ask: who fixes a critical frankensqlite bug and how fast; what happens if a sibling repo becomes unavailable; what is the support horizon for a pinned constellation state. These have honest answers today (single maintainer, best effort) — the failure mode is not the answers but leaving them UNSTATED, letting evaluators assume either better or worse than reality.

WHAT: A policy document (docs/, referenced by the trust-cone assessment and the release bundle) stating: (a) maintainership reality: who maintains each constellation member, the bus factor, and the explicit single-maintainer risk statement (honesty over theater — inventing a committee would be its own trust defect); (b) incident response: how a correctness/security issue in a sibling is reported, triaged, and released (the e13_4 emergency-bump path), with the claim-integrity framing applied (a sibling bug that breaks a certificate claim is a P0 here, not just there); (c) archival/escrow: the vendored bundles (e13_3) ARE the archival mechanism — every release bundle is a self-contained restorable state independent of any repo's continued existence; state retention policy for bundles; (d) support horizon: what a pinned release can expect (reproducibility forever via bundle; fixes only via new trains); (e) review cadence for this policy itself.

DONE WHEN: policy merged; assessment + release docs reference it; the incident path has been REHEARSED once (tabletop: a hypothetical fsqlite corruption bug walked through report->triage->emergency train->bundle).

TESTS: doc-presence + cross-reference lint; the tabletop rehearsal transcript retained as an artifact; consistency check between this policy, the e13_4 protocol, and the e02 claim-integrity severity rules.

title: E14 Surrogates and learned components: proposers, never authorities (metrics + evidence contract)
description:
WHY: FrankenSim can get substantially smarter through learned components — solver/preconditioner selection, mesh and refinement proposals, reduced-order models, warm starts, closure-model selection, design proposal generation, anomaly detection, fidelity-sufficiency prediction, retrieval of similar historical studies from the ledger — but ONLY if the authority boundary stays strict: a surrogate may PROPOSE ("this low-fidelity answer is probably adequate"); only a verifier may permit the workflow to ACT on it. The substrate exists (fs-surrogate certify_or_escalate, ConformalBand, empirical_coverage; ladder feature is Estimated-only), but the governance contract and the DECISIVE metrics are not systematized.

DECISIVE METRICS (not just RMSE/R^2): false-safe-decision rate; uncertainty coverage; out-of-domain detection rate; rate of incorrect non-escalation; cost saved per accepted decision; fraction of cases requiring fallback; performance after geometry-family or operating-regime shift.

CHILDREN: learned-component evidence contract (every learned result carries training-data identity + partition policy, geometry/regime domain, calibration + held-out performance, uncertainty calibration, drift statistics, physics residuals, independent discrepancy checks, escalation + fallback policy); decisive-metrics instrumentation wired into campaign/ledger records; proposer/authority boundary enforcement (type-level: learned outputs cannot mint Verified/Validated colors; lint + adversarial tests); ledger retrieval of similar historical studies [backlog/frontier].

DONE WHEN: any surrogate participating in the cooling workflow publishes the full metric set; an adversarial test demonstrates that a deliberately overconfident surrogate is caught by escalation rather than contaminating a decision; no code path exists in which a learned component's output reaches a user-facing claim without passing a verifier.

title: Learned-component evidence contract: mandatory card for every surrogate/learned artifact
description:
WHY: fs-surrogate's certify-or-escalate and conformal bands govern USE of a surrogate, but nothing standardizes what a learned component must DISCLOSE about itself. Without a mandatory contract, learned components will accrete with undocumented training data, unstated domains, and uncalibrated confidence — the classic ML-in-engineering failure — and the authority boundary becomes unauditable.

WHAT: (a) A LearnedComponentCard (extending the ModelCard pattern) mandatory for every learned artifact (surrogates, ROMs, warm-start predictors, selector policies, anomaly detectors): training-data identity (content-addressed dataset refs + the partition policy under which it was trained — e07_1 taint machinery applies to learned components too: training data is calibration data); geometry/regime domain (typed ValidityDomain); calibration + held-out performance (the decisive split, with metrics); uncertainty-calibration status (conformal/coverage evidence refs); drift statistics refs (e12_8 channels); physics-residual checks where applicable (does the surrogate's output violate conservation? measured, not assumed); escalation + fallback policy (what happens on OOD/band-too-wide — must name the fallback path); (b) registration refuses cardless learned components (the fs-evidence ModelRegistry refusal pattern extended); (c) card completeness is typed: a card with Unstated calibration can exist but caps every downstream use at the weakest evidence — visible, not forbidden; (d) existing surrogates (POD, RB ladder, conformal-gated users in campaign crates) migrated to carry cards.

DONE WHEN: card type shipped; registration gate refuses cardless components; existing surrogate users migrated; taint integration proven (a surrogate trained on validation data is caught).

TESTS: unit (card validation per field; refusal paths; taint intersection); integration (migrated campaign crates still green with cards attached); e2e: registry audit script listing every learned component + card completeness table with per-field logging.

title: Decisive-metrics instrumentation for learned components (false-safe rate, OOD detection, escalation correctness)
description:
WHY: RMSE and R^2 flatter surrogates on the cases that do not matter. The metrics that decide whether a learned component belongs in an engineering workflow are: false-safe-decision rate (surrogate said fine, truth said not — the catastrophic direction); uncertainty coverage (its bands vs reality); out-of-domain detection rate (did it KNOW it was extrapolating); rate of incorrect non-escalation; cost saved per accepted decision; fallback fraction; and performance after geometry-family/regime shift. These must be INSTRUMENTED — computed continuously from ledgered decisions, not estimated once at training time.

WHAT: (a) Decision-event records: every certify-or-escalate decision (and every learned proposal acceptance) logs: component identity + card version, input-domain position (in/out/near-boundary), the decision, the band width, the fallback taken if any, and — when ground truth later exists (escalated solve completed, corpus case matched, rig data arrived) — the truth outcome joined back to the decision; (b) metric computation: rolling per-component metrics from the joined records (the false-safe join is the critical one: decision said use-surrogate AND truth was outside band = false-safe event, alarmed immediately, not just aggregated); shift-segmented (per geometry family/regime bucket, Mondrian-style) so aggregate health cannot hide segment failure; (c) thresholds + consequences: per-card declared metric floors; breaching them auto-demotes the component (registration gate consults live metrics, not just the card's training-time numbers); (d) metrics feed the e16 dashboard's surrogate row.

DONE WHEN: decision events flow to the ledger from at least the existing campaign users; metrics compute per segment; a synthetic false-safe injection alarms and demotes; dashboard row renders.

TESTS: unit (event schema; join logic incl. late-arriving truth; metric arithmetic; demotion triggers); statistical (synthetic decision streams with known rates recovered); e2e: a campaign run + truth-arrival simulation logging events, joins, metric updates, and the demotion path.

title: Proposer/authority boundary enforcement: learned outputs cannot mint or influence evidence colors
description:
WHY: The rule "a surrogate may propose; only a verifier permits action" must be structural, not cultural. The dangerous channels are subtle: a learned mesh proposer whose mesh biases the DWR estimate; a warm start that steers which local optimum the certified solve finds; a fidelity-sufficiency predictor whose skipped escalation never gets checked. None of these mint colors directly — they shape what the verifier sees. The boundary must therefore cover both direct minting AND the audit of influence channels.

WHAT: (a) Direct enforcement: type-level — learned-component outputs are wrapped in Proposal<T> (a marker the evidence layer refuses as an authority input: no Evidence color can cite a Proposal as its support); acting on a proposal requires a verifier receipt (the certify-or-escalate decision record, an admission check, a completed certified solve) that references the proposal but derives authority ONLY from the verification; (b) influence-channel audit: for each learned integration point (mesh proposals, warm starts, selector policies, sufficiency predictions) document the influence channel and its guard: warm starts -> certified solve's convergence criteria are start-independent (and a periodic cold-start cross-check drill validates that claim empirically); mesh proposals -> estimator runs on the proposed mesh but its error claim is start-agnostic + ladder-checked (E06_6); sufficiency predictions -> ALWAYS a sampled audit fraction where escalation runs anyway and disagreement feeds e14_2's non-escalation metric (never 100% trust in the skip); (c) adversarial demonstration: a deliberately overconfident/biased surrogate inserted in tests must be caught by the guards, with the catch logged.

DONE WHEN: Proposal<T> wrapper adopted at all learned integration points; the influence-audit doc merged with each channel's guard named + tested; the adversarial demonstration green; lint for new unguarded learned integration points.

TESTS: unit (Proposal refusal in evidence constructors; receipt-requirement enforcement); the cold-start and audit-fraction drills as standing tests; e2e: adversarial-surrogate scenario logging every guard activation and the final uncontaminated decision.

title: Ledger retrieval of similar historical studies (learned retrieval as a proposer) [backlog]
description:
WHY: The design ledger accumulates exactly the experience a new study should exploit — similar geometries, regimes, model choices, what escalated, what the budgets looked like — but nothing retrieves it. Retrieval-as-proposer is the safest possible learned component (it proposes starting points and expectations; verifiers still govern everything), making it a good proving ground for the e14 contract at low risk. Backlog priority: valuable, not on the vertical's critical path.

WHAT: (a) Study fingerprints: deterministic feature vectors over ledgered runs (geometry summary stats from charts/regions, regime/pi-group coordinates, scenario-class tags, model-graph choices, budget outcomes) — engineered features first (interpretable, deterministic), learned embeddings only later under a full LearnedComponentCard; (b) retrieval: given a new project's fingerprint, return ranked similar studies with the SIMILARITY EVIDENCE shown (which features matched — explainable retrieval, in keeping with the explain-everything culture) and the useful payloads: prior model choices + their escalation outcomes, budget actuals (planning priors for fs-plan), settings that failed; (c) integration as PROPOSER only: retrieved suggestions enter as Proposal<T> (e14_3 machinery) — e.g. proposed fidelity-graph starting node, proposed budget allocation — always verifier-gated; (d) privacy/scope note: retrieval operates within the local ledger.

DONE WHEN: fingerprints computed for existing ledgered campaigns; retrieval returns explainable rankings on a held-out study; one proposer integration (budget prior into fs-plan) works end-to-end through the Proposal gate.

TESTS: unit (fingerprint determinism; ranking stability; explanation completeness); retrieval-quality eval (leave-one-out over ledgered studies: does the true sibling rank top-k); e2e: new-project retrieval session logging fingerprint, candidates, explanations, and the gated proposal handoff.

title: E15 GPU/accelerator policy: evidence-driven pilot, never calendar-driven
description:
WHY: There is NO GPU execution path in the workspace (verified: fs-substrate gpu field is a descriptive probe string never consumed; zero CUDA/Metal/wgpu/WebGPU/OpenCL/Vulkan hits; fs-govern lists GPU reductions as a determinism RISK). That absence is a real gap — but GPU must not outrank external V&V, product workflow, CAD admission, or constellation trust merely because it is 2026. Many relevant workloads are bandwidth-bound, irregular, latency-sensitive, or dominated by geometry preprocessing, BC setup, solver convergence, model discrepancy, and human/agent workflow latency; peak FLOPs are the wrong denominator. Also "few percent of machine FLOPs" arguments cut both ways — the decision must be MEASURED.

POLICY (encode, then follow): (1) complete one representative vertical; (2) profile END-TO-END wall time and energy (not kernel microbenchmarks); (3) identify the top three kernels; (4) build ONE accelerator pilot only if GPU-suitable kernels dominate; (5) any GPU path requires: a CPU reference path, a backend-specific evidence class binding device + driver + compiler + kernel identity + reduction policy + numerical equivalence envelope, deterministic-or-bounded-equivalence semantics, cancellation semantics, and machine-scoped performance data. The GPU path does NOT automatically get "lower certainty" — it gets its own evidence class. Plausible pilot candidates if profiling justifies: LBM streaming/collision, SpMV, FFT, batched constitutive updates, volume rendering.

CHILDREN: doctrine + backend evidence-class specification; end-to-end vertical profiling harness (depends on the working Level-3 workflow); conditional pilot [moonshot, gated on profiling evidence, subject to the e16 moonshot displacement rule].

DONE WHEN: the doctrine is in fs-govern with a named falsifier; profiling artifacts exist for the reference cooling project; the pilot decision (go/no-go) is recorded WITH the measured evidence it rests on.

title: GPU/accelerator doctrine + backend evidence-class specification (policy before silicon)
description:
WHY: GPU work approached calendar-first would burn the program's scarcest resource (focused effort) on an unmeasured bet, and approached naively would break the determinism story (fs-govern already lists GPU reductions as a reproducibility risk). Writing the doctrine BEFORE any pilot means the eventual pilot (if profiling justifies one) starts with its evidence obligations defined instead of retrofitted.

WHAT: (a) The doctrine (fs-govern registration + docs): pilot admission requires the e15_2 profiling evidence showing GPU-suitable kernels dominate end-to-end wall time/energy for the ratified vertical; any pilot is [M]-classed and subject to the e16 moonshot displacement rule; a named falsifier (e.g. profiling shows top-3 kernels are bandwidth/latency-bound in ways accelerators do not help at our sizes -> the pilot does not run); (b) the backend evidence class, specified now: any accelerator result must bind device identity, driver/runtime version, compiler + kernel source identity, reduction policy (fixed-order or documented tolerance), and a numerical-equivalence envelope vs the CPU reference path (bitwise where promised, bounded-delta elsewhere — the GPU path gets its OWN evidence class, not an automatic lower-certainty stamp); a CPU reference path remains mandatory forever (fallback + differential testing substrate); cancellation semantics required at kernel-batch boundaries; (c) candidate list recorded with honest suitability notes (LBM streaming/collision, SpMV, FFT, batched constitutive updates, rendering).

DONE WHEN: doctrine registered with falsifier; evidence-class spec reviewed against the fs-evidence/fs-roofline machinery it will plug into; e15_2/e15_3 cite it.

TESTS: governance-record completeness; spec-consistency check (every evidence-class field maps to an existing or explicitly-new record type — no hand-waving fields); doctrine-presence lint.

title: End-to-end vertical profiling: wall-time + energy attribution, top-3 kernels (the GPU go/no-go evidence)
description:
WHY: The GPU decision needs the one artifact nobody has: an END-TO-END profile of the real product workflow (not kernel microbenchmarks) showing where wall-clock and energy actually go — including the unglamorous phases (import, census, assembly, BC setup, report, ledger I/O) that accelerators never help. fs-roofline + fs-substrate provide machine axes and measurement discipline; this extends attribution to the whole pipeline.

WHAT: (a) Pipeline-phase attribution: instrument the e06_5 orchestration stages (already ledgered ops) with wall-time and, where the platform exposes it, energy estimates; within solve stages, kernel-level attribution (assembly, SpMV, factorizations, coupling iterations, radiation exchange, UQ sampling loop) via the existing tune/roofline machinery; (b) runs across the representative workload set (the e06_12 examples + a scaled-up stress case) on BOTH reference ISA families with machine fingerprints (quiet-host discipline for anything feeding decisions — the shared-M4 lesson); (c) the decision artifact: phase/kernel attribution tables, the top-3 kernel identification with their roofline positions (compute-bound? bandwidth-bound? latency/irregular?), and the honest GPU-suitability read per the e15_1 doctrine (a bandwidth-bound SpMV at our sizes is a known-marginal case — say so); (d) the go/no-go recommendation recorded with the evidence, either outcome legitimate.

DONE WHEN: profiles captured on both ISAs; decision artifact rendered deterministically from ledgered measurements; the doctrine's falsifier evaluated against real numbers; e15_3 proceeds or closes-as-refused accordingly.

TESTS: instrumentation-overhead check (profiling changes wall time by a bounded, measured fraction); attribution completeness (phases sum to total within tolerance, gaps named); determinism of the artifact from fixed measurement inputs; e2e: full profiling campaign logged per phase/kernel with fingerprints.
