title: E16 Governance and metrics: maturity registry, critical path, moonshot WIP cap, dashboards, doc truth
description:
WHY: 130+ crates, per-crate contracts, and a very large fine-grained issue graph can reward LOCAL completeness while delaying integrated usefulness. A crate passing its local suite must not move the product score unless it advances an end-to-end supported capability. Governance must make the vertical capability graph the authoritative critical path and make integration ownership real. Also: the README's stale 127-crate count (actual: 135 native workspace fs-* members + xtask + standalone fs-wasm = 136 fs-* dirs) is small but symptomatic — the project evolves faster than its global narrative synchronizes, which is itself a trust defect for a project whose product IS trustworthy claims.

CHILDREN: machine-readable capability maturity registry (levels L1 experimental component / L2 numerically verified / L3 integrated workflow / L4 experimentally validated / L5 supported product capability) + xtask check; vertical capability graph as authoritative critical path (bv label/track conventions + integration-owner annotations); moonshot WIP cap policy in fs-govern (every new [M] workstream must DISPLACE an existing one, name a falsifier, carry a capped budget, and stay off the product critical path — research is not banned, it is budgeted); program metrics dashboard as a deterministic artifact (time-from-CAD-to-decision, blind-experiment error, empirical coverage, false-safe rate, % outputs with complete error budgets, import success/repair/refusal rates, time-to-explain, cross-machine reproducibility, surrogate escalation correctness, independent reproduction success); frozen public schema set with migration policy (project schema, package FORMAT, scenario IR, matdb packs, ledger schema); documentation drift repair + capability matrix distinguishing experimental/verified/validated/supported; e2e-acceptance-weighted DSR gate wiring.

DONE WHEN: maturity states are queryable and enforced (promotion blocked by e02 claim-integrity gate); the critical path is visible in bv; at least one moonshot has been displaced/deferred BY THE RULE rather than by argument; the dashboard regenerates deterministically from ledger + corpus artifacts; README counts are generated or checked, not hand-maintained.

title: Machine-readable capability maturity registry (L1-L5) + xtask check (promotion is a recorded event)
description:
WHY: "Is this capability experimental, verified, integrated, validated, or supported?" currently has no queryable answer — status lives in README prose, CONTRACT no-claims, and folklore. The maturity registry is the spine of program governance: the e02 promotion gate needs promotions to be EVENTS; the capability matrix (e06_10) needs a source of truth; the dashboard needs states to count.

WHAT: (a) A versioned registry file (repo root, identity-hashed like identity-authorities.json) mapping capabilities (product-meaningful units: "steady conduction solve", "correlation convection rung", "evidence packaging", "VTU export" — not crates; one crate can host several capabilities, one capability can span crates) to: maturity level (L1 experimental component / L2 numerically verified / L3 integrated workflow / L4 experimentally validated / L5 supported product), the evidence refs justifying the level (tests/corpus/scorecard entries per level-specific criteria: L2 requires named Gauntlet tiers green; L3 requires e2e-lane coverage; L4 requires corpus validation + coverage; L5 requires support policy + migration promises), owner, and last-review date; (b) xtask check-maturity: registry schema valid; level criteria's evidence refs exist and are green-checkable; promotions since the last committed state flagged for the e02 claim-integrity gate; DEMOTIONS always allowed and logged; (c) level-criteria doc merged (what each level requires, per capability class); (d) initial population for the cooling vertical's capabilities honestly (most start L1/L2 — that is the point).

DONE WHEN: registry populated for the vertical + the load-bearing substrate capabilities; check-maturity in check-all; a rehearsed promotion (with evidence) and a rehearsed blocked-promotion (e02 gate) both demonstrated.

TESTS: unit (schema; criteria-evidence resolution; promotion/demotion event detection); e2e: registry audit run logging per-capability level, evidence status, and staleness (last-review age), plus the two rehearsal transcripts.

title: Moonshot WIP cap: displacement rule, named falsifiers, capped budgets, off the critical path (fs-govern)
description:
WHY: Research is not the enemy — unbudgeted research is. title: Program metrics dashboard: outcome metrics as a deterministic artifact (not vibes, not test counts)
description:
WHY: The program optimizes what it measures, so it must measure OUTCOMES: time from CAD to defensible decision; error vs blind experiments; empirical coverage; false-safe rate; % of outputs with complete error budgets; import success/repair/refusal on the supplier corpus; time-to-explain a surprising result; cross-machine reproducibility; surrogate escalation correctness; independent reproduction status. Kernel throughput and crate/test counts are explicitly demoted to diagnostics. The dashboard is a deterministic artifact so its history is replayable and its claims are auditable like everything else.

WHAT: (a) A dashboard generator (fs-report family) consuming ONLY ledgered/corpus/registry artifacts: each metric a typed row with value, trend (vs prior dashboard states), data source refs, and an honesty cell (what this metric does NOT capture — e.g. time-to-decision measured on OUR examples, not yet real users); metrics with no data yet render NO-DATA loudly (the dashboard ships incomplete from day one rather than waiting for completeness — visible gaps drive acquisition); (b) sources wired incrementally: e06_11 lane timings (time-to-decision), e04_8 scorecard (error/coverage/false-accept), e08_7 audit (budget completeness %), e11_6 (import rates), e14_2 (surrogate metrics), e07_6 (reproduction), e16_1 (maturity distribution); time-to-explain instrumented from ledger explain-query sessions [staged, NO-DATA until then]; (c) render: deterministic Markdown/HTML + machine-readable JSON, versioned in-repo or ledgered so trends are diffable; (d) cadence: regenerated by a DSR lane per release train and on demand.

title: Freeze the public schema set with versioning + migration policy (small, stable, promised)
description:
WHY: A product's trust compounds through stable interfaces; a research workspace's velocity comes from breaking them. The resolution is a SMALL frozen set: enumerate exactly which schemas are public promises (with versioning + migration machinery), and by exclusion everything else remains internal and breakable. Without the explicit list, every serialized format drifts toward accidental-public status and every change becomes a fight.

WHAT: (a) The frozen set, proposed: the .fsim project schema (e06_1); the evidence-package FORMAT (fs-package, already versioned at 8 with checker protocol lockstep — the pattern to copy); the scenario IR (fs-scenario, already versioned with migration receipts); matdb pack formats (FSMATPK family); the ledger schema (already user_version-migrated, v20); the SBOM/bundle manifests (e13_2/3); the maturity registry + dashboard JSON (e16_1/4); everything else explicitly NOT promised; (b) per-schema policy record: version location, compatibility promise (what a minor vs major bump may change), migration obligation (auto-migration receipts vs documented manual), deprecation horizon; (c) an xtask check-schemas: each frozen schema's version constant exists, its migration tests exist and pass, and NEW serialized formats appearing in public-facing crates without a policy record get flagged (accretion control); (d) the promise documented user-facing (README/docs section: what we promise not to break, from which release).

DONE WHEN: the set ratified + policy records merged; check-schemas in check-all; each frozen schema has at least one cross-version migration test; user-facing promise published.

TESTS: unit (policy-record schema; version-constant resolution); per-schema migration round-trips (old fixture -> migrate -> validate, incl. refusal of unmigratable ancient versions with honest errors); e2e: schema audit run logging each frozen schema's version, migration coverage, and any flagged accretions.

title: Documentation truth repair: generated counts, capability matrix, drift checks (the narrative must not lie)
description:
WHY: The README says 127 fs-* crates; the workspace has 135 native members + standalone fs-wasm (136 fs-* dirs). Small drift, big signal: the project evolves faster than its narrative synchronizes, and for a project whose PRODUCT is trustworthy claims, a stale self-description is a credibility defect reviewers WILL find (the external reviews did). WHAT: (a) A consolidation review protocol run at release trains (e13_4 cadence): inputs = the e16_1 maturity registry (capabilities stuck at L1 with no consuming workflow), the e16_2 capability->bead cross-references, and a usage sweep (which crates/modules no vertical, campaign, or e2e lane transitively exercises — mechanically derived from the dependency graph + test coverage); (b) per-candidate disposition, recorded: KEEP (named consumer or named trust-risk rationale), CONSOLIDATE (merge into a neighbor with a migration note), FREEZE (explicitly parked: compiles + tests stay green but no new investment — a visible state, not a quiet death), or RETIRE (removal proposal — requiring the user's explicit approval per the repo's no-deletion rule; agents PROPOSE retirement, never execute it unilaterally); (c) the review outcome is a governance record (what was examined, dispositions, rationale) so the next review starts from state, not archaeology; (d) guard against false economy: consolidation must never break the layering rules or merge crates across determinism classes — the checks (check-layers, check-contracts) gate the consolidations themselves.

title: E17 Scenario semantics: make the model reflect how engineers describe systems (no silent defaults)
description:
WHY: Real engineering intelligence lives more in scenario semantics than in another Krylov solver. fs-scenario today has typed BCs with dimensional expectation tables, load cases + factored combinations (declared, not evaluated), Frictionless/Coulomb/Tied contact, a REQUIRED Environment (gravity/ambient T/ambient p), payload algebra, frames, and stochastic ensembles — a strong base. Missing for engineering use: assemblies/parts/regions/interfaces with PERSISTENT entity identity (region names are currently strings bound solver-side); materials as MANUFACTURED STATES; joints/fasteners/welds/adhesives/gaps and interface conductance; sensors + observation operators as scenario objects; duty cycles and operating envelopes with combination evaluation; design variables + manufacturing constraints; objectives/margins/failure modes; standards clauses + safety factors as versioned policy sources; context of use + intended decision. The Five Explicits doctrine is the philosophical basis; this epic maps it onto familiar engineering objects.

NO-SILENT-DEFAULTS DOCTRINE (enforce, not document): no silent ambient temperature; no implicit zero contact resistance; no unnamed turbulence intensity; no unitless heat-transfer coefficient; no material without state + temperature range + source; no boundary face selected solely by a fragile mesh index; no optimization result without manufacturing and robustness checks. Defaults are rare, visible, and receipted.

CHILDREN: assembly/part/region/interface persistent-identity model; materials-as-manufactured-states binding into fs-matdb cards (state + temp range + source mandatory); interface conductance/joints/fasteners in the scenario model; sensors + observation operators as scenario objects (feeds e12 assimilation); duty cycles/operating envelopes/load-combination evaluation; standards clauses + safety factors + context-of-use records; no-silent-defaults enforcement lint + refusal tests.

DONE WHEN: the Cooling 0.1 project schema (e06) is expressed entirely in these objects; every default that fires leaves a visible receipt; the no-silent-defaults tests demonstrate typed refusals for each doctrine item.

title: Assembly/part/region/interface model with persistent entity identity (strings become identities)
description:
WHY: fs-scenario's region names are strings bound solver-side — workable for fixtures, fatal for products: a renamed region silently orphans BCs; a re-imported geometry cannot prove it still means the same enclosure; diffs across revisions have nothing stable to diff AGAINST. Persistent entity identity is the foundation the import path (e06_3), design diffs (e11_4), as-built binding (e12_2), and the project schema (e06_1) all stand on — which is why this is the epic's first task and a cross-epic blocker.

WHAT: (a) Entity model: Assembly -> Part -> (Region | Surface | Interface) with typed identities: stable IDs (content-derived where possible: geometry fingerprint + declared name + parent path; collision-checked), display names separate from identity (renames do not orphan), and identity RECEIPTS on every rebinding event (import, re-mesh, revision migration — the e11_4 verdicts land here); interfaces as first-class pairs (ordered where physics cares: which side is the TIM applied to) with their own identity; (b) referential integrity: every scenario object (BC, load, material binding, sensor, requirement) references entities by identity; validation resolves ALL references and reports dangling/ambiguous ones with fix hints (extending the existing Violation code/what/fix pattern); (c) evolution: identity migration receipts when geometry changes (ties to fs-scenario's existing IR-migration discipline); (d) compatibility: existing string-based fixtures migrate mechanically (a string name becomes a declared-name identity with a legacy marker).

DONE WHEN: entity model shipped; the reference cooling scenario expressed in it; rename/re-import fixtures keep bindings intact via receipts; dangling-reference validation proven; legacy migration works.

TESTS: unit (identity derivation + collision handling; reference resolution incl. every dangling/ambiguous case; receipt generation); metamorphic (rename invariance of physics meaning; re-import stability); e2e: a scenario lifecycle (author -> import-bind -> rename -> re-import -> validate) logging every identity event and the final binding table.
close_reason:
Landed in fs-scenario: src/entity.rs (+17 in-src unit tests) and tests/entity_identity.rs (9 cases). fs-scenario 105 tests green, including all 32 pinned canonical IR hashes UNMOVED.

(a) ENTITY MODEL: Assembly -> Part -> (Region|Surface|Interface). EntityId = kind + BLAKE3-256 over a LENGTH-PREFIXED, domain-separated preimage (kind tag, parent identity which transitively encodes the parent path, declared name, optional geometry fingerprint, optional interface pair). Length-prefixing closes the ambiguous-serialization collision shape and is pinned by identity_preimage_is_length_prefixed_and_injective. Display names are NOT in the preimage, so renames cannot orphan. Interfaces are first-class Ordered/Unordered pairs with their own identity. Receipts form an append-only hash chain (sequence == index, each digest binds the previous root); verify_receipts detects interior edits, reorders and drops. Datums, tolerances and assembly placements landed as declarations + validation.

WHAT AN IDENTITY PROVES, stated narrowly: two declarations supplied byte-equal derivation inputs. It does NOT prove two revisions describe the same physical part, that the entity exists in any geometry kernel, or that anyone measured anything. Equal fingerprints => equal supplied bytes; UNEQUAL fingerprints prove NOTHING, because a re-export of an unchanged part routinely changes bytes — which is exactly why a mismatch falls back to the weaker DeclaredPath tier instead of concluding 'different part'. 'Collision-checked' is a fail-closed full-preimage comparison (IdentityCollision vs DuplicateDeclaration), not a claim that BLAKE3 collisions are impossible; both branches are exercised.

EVIDENCE IS NEVER LAUNDERED: EvidenceTier Asserted < Declared < PathMatched < ContentMatched < Identical, and resolve() returns the WEAKEST tier on the supersession chain — a content-matched hop after an asserted hop still resolves Asserted.

(b) REFERENTIAL INTEGRITY: EntityRef/ReferenceSite/BindingTable/validate_bindings extending the existing Violation{code,what,fix} pattern, with 8 distinct fault codes each carrying a fix hint. BC, case-BC and contact sites are fully enumerated and enforced. PARTIAL: Load/MaterialBinding/Sensor/Requirement sites are typed and resolvable but their collections do not exist in fs-scenario yet, so those rows are not existence-checked.

(c) EVOLUTION: apply_import is ATOMIC (a refused revision leaves the catalog byte-identical, proven by PartialEq in two tests). Auto correspondence matches fingerprint first, then declared name + CORRESPONDING parent (following the parent's own supersession, which is what lets a renamed sub-assembly keep its children's path match). A tie at either tier is AmbiguousImportMatch naming two candidates — NEVER a first match. ImportScope::Complete retires omitted strict descendants; a binding to a retired entity is entity-retired-reference, not a silent forward-resolve. PARTIAL: receipts are not emitted or persisted by the IR codec (no IR version bump).

(d) LEGACY MIGRATION: migrate_legacy_scenario walks BC/case-BC/contact sites in declaration order; each distinct region string becomes a Surface whose declared name is that exact string, legacy-marked, with NO invented fingerprint and no inferred hierarchy. Idempotent (re-running appends 0 receipts, re-derives the same ids). Proven with the before-state (8x entity-unbound-site) and a drift case.

FIXTURES: rename (6 renames, bindings unchanged), full CAD re-import (16 identities superseded, 13 content-matched, 3 path-matched, all 8 bindings resolving one hop onto identical fingerprints), identical re-import (0 new identities, 16 Unchanged receipts).

HONEST BOUNDARY ON THE 'REFERENCE COOLING SCENARIO': it does not exist as a repo-wide artifact — the phrase appears only in bead prose for .6.1/.6.3/.17.1. A representative cooling stack (SiC die -> TIM -> liquid-cooled plate; 16 entities, 3 datums, 3 tolerances, 2 placements, 8 reference sites) was authored as this crate's fixture, and both the test header and this record say plainly it is not canonical.

DEFERRED, with reasons: BoundaryCondition.region is still a String — changing it would move byte-stable hash-pinned canonical IR, need an IR version bump and migration, and break fs-ir/fs-solid construction sites outside the boundary. Bindings are therefore a SIBLING table validated against the scenario, and CONTRACT states the consequence as a no-claim: a scenario rebuilt from canonical bytes alone has no bindings and reports every site unbound. Persisting them belongs to the versioned .fsim schema (bead .6.1). Entity validation is also not merged into ValidationPlan/Cx: it has its own explicit EntityBudget with fallible reservation before every mutation, but does not poll cancellation — written into CONTRACT rather than papered over.

NOTE: fs-ir and fs-frame fail to compile at HEAD for unrelated committed reasons (fs-ir E0599 ordered_bytes_stream in machine/causalization.rs:4782; fs-frame E0689 ambiguous float abs in tests/battery.rs:647). Neither is ripple from this change — both crates have no uncommitted edits.

title: Materials as manufactured states: binding requires state + temperature range + source (never a name)
description:
WHY: "Aluminum" is not a material — 6061-T6 extruded vs A380 die-cast differ 40% in conductivity; annealed vs work-hardened copper differ meaningfully; a TIM's cured vs uncured state is a different substance. fs-matdb already models cards with provenance and validity; the SCENARIO side must refuse the name-only shortcut so the e17 doctrine item ("no material selected without state, temperature range, and source") is structural.

WHAT: (a) Material bindings in the scenario reference a MaterialCard identity PLUS a declared manufactured state (from the card's state vocabulary: temper, cure, porosity class, finish where thermally relevant — surface finish feeds emissivity for e05_4) and the temperature range the binding expects (checked against card validity at validate time — the e06_4 envelope check made per-binding); a binding missing state or range is a Violation with a fix hint listing the card's available states; (b) source visibility: the binding surfaces the card's provenance (which handbook/datasheet/measurement) in validation output — users see WHOSE number they are trusting at authoring time, not report time; (c) conflicting-claims interaction: where a card carries coexisting conflicting claims (matdb's design), the binding declares which claim lineage it selects (e06_4's no-auto-pick rule, enforced here at the scenario layer); (d) uncertainty defaults: a binding may not silently narrow the card's uncertainty; tightening requires a declared justification record.

DONE WHEN: the reference scenario's every material binding carries state+range+source; each refusal path proven; provenance renders at validate time; the tightening-requires-justification rule enforced.

TESTS: unit (each missing-field Violation with fix-hint quality asserted; range-vs-validity intersection edges; claim-lineage selection; tightening refusal); e2e: validate runs on correct + deliberately sloppy scenarios logging the full binding table (entity -> card -> state -> range -> source -> verdict).

title: Sensors and observation operators as scenario objects (instrumentation is part of the model)
description:
WHY: The design-build-measure-update loop (e12) and experiment design (e12_7) need sensors to be MODELED: a thermocouple has a location (with placement uncertainty), a mount (whose thermal contact biases the reading), a time constant, a calibration record, and an observation operator mapping the simulated field to what the instrument would read. fs-scenario has no sensor layer (CONTRACT no-claim); fs-assimilate expects caller-supplied observation operators — the scenario is where they should come FROM.

WHAT: (a) Sensor objects on E17_1 entities: type (thermocouple, RTD, flow meter, pressure tap, IR-camera region), location binding (entity + local position with placement uncertainty — the corpus retention schema's field, now first-class at authoring), mount model (the bias/contact declaration: an insulated vs heatsunk mount reads differently — even a declared-perfect mount is a DECLARATION), dynamics (time constant for transient staging), calibration reference (certificate ref + date, matching e04's retention schema so scenario sensors and corpus datasets share vocabulary); (b) observation-operator derivation: each sensor compiles to an operator over the solve's fields (point/patch evaluation with the mount model applied) consumable by fs-assimilate (E12_4's nonlinear operators get their producers here) and by the corpus comparison machinery (predicted-vs-measured uses the SAME operator — eliminating the classic probe-mismatch bug where simulation is compared at the wrong point); (c) virtual sensors: the same objects usable in pure simulation for QoI probes (unifying probe definitions product-wide); (d) placement candidates for e12_7 are sensor objects with a candidate flag.

DONE WHEN: sensors declare + validate + compile to operators; one assimilation and one corpus comparison consume compiled operators; the mount-bias path demonstrably changes a reading; candidate flagging works.

TESTS: unit (per-type validation; operator compilation vs hand-built operators; mount-model arithmetic; placement-uncertainty propagation into operator uncertainty); e2e: instrumented-scenario run logging each sensor's compiled operator, simulated reading vs raw field value (the mount bias visible), and the assimilation handoff.

title: Duty cycles, operating envelopes, and load-combination evaluation (from declared to evaluated)
description:
WHY: fs-scenario DECLARES load cases and factored combinations but explicitly does not EVALUATE them, and has no duty-cycle/envelope objects. The vertical needs: an operating envelope (ambient x power x fan-state ranges) driving UQ sweeps (e06_7) and validity checks (e08_3); duty cycles for the transient/reliability staging (e05_9, Level-4 thermal cycling questions); and combination evaluation so "1.2D+1.6L"-style factored cases (or their thermal analogs: worst-case-power + max-ambient + one-fan-failed) become runnable case sets rather than annotations.

WHAT: (a) OperatingEnvelope objects: named axes (ambient T, total power, altitude/pressure, fan states incl. discrete failure modes) with ranges/distributions + declared correlations (hot day and high power co-occur — correlation declared or explicitly unknown, e08 representation rules); envelope drives: UQ sweep domains, validity-domain intersection checks, and worst-case corner enumeration (deterministic corner set with the enumeration rationale logged — corners of correlated envelopes are not the naive hypercube corners); (b) duty cycles: time-fraction or sequence-based profiles over envelope points (steady-state weighted analysis NOW: weighted QoI aggregation with the weighting honestly labeled as steady approximation; true transient staged with e05_9); (c) combination evaluation: factored combinations compile to case sets with per-case provenance (which combination, which factors) and aggregate verdicts (governing case identified per QoI — the report says WHICH condition sizes the design, which is what engineers actually ask); (d) fan-failure combinatorics bounded (declared failure set, not exhaustive 2^n).

DONE WHEN: reference envelope + one duty cycle + governing-case reporting work end-to-end; correlated-corner enumeration proven against a hand-worked case; declared-unknown correlation flows to the budget caveat.

TESTS: unit (envelope validation; corner enumeration with correlations; weighting arithmetic; combination compilation); e2e: envelope-driven run logging the case set, per-case QoIs, the governing case per QoI, and the aggregate verdict with budget caveats.

title: Requirements with sources: standards clauses, safety factors, context of use, intended decision
description:
WHY: A requirement ("T_junction < 100C") without its SOURCE (derating guideline? datasheet absolute max? internal margin policy?) and its safety-factor lineage cannot support an auditable compliance claim — and the DecisionAssessment (e08_6) needs requirement objects with authority, not magic numbers. Context of use and intended decision are the top-level frame: what question is this project answering, within what envelope, for what consequence class.

WHAT: (a) Requirement objects: quantity ref (QoI identity), limit + direction + margin policy (safety factor with ITS source — a factor of 1.2 from company policy vs 1.0 from a datasheet absolute-max are different claims), source record (standards clause with version — the fs-vvreg standards registry and fs-crosswalk vocabulary connect here; datasheet ref; internal policy doc + version), and severity class (what a violation means: reliability derating vs damage limit); (b) ContextOfUse at project level (extending the existing x68z ContextOfUse work): the intended decision (design selection? compliance sign-off? scoping estimate?) — which calibrates how hard e08's machinery gates (a scoping estimate may tolerate Indeterminate; a sign-off may not), the validity envelope the answers are claimed for, and the consequence framing; (c) versioned policy sources: requirement sources are versioned documents; a source version bump flags dependent requirements for review (the standards-drift problem handled like schema drift); (d) report/assessment integration: every compliance verdict cites its requirement's full lineage.

DONE WHEN: reference project's requirements carry sources + factors + severity; ContextOfUse gates assessment strictness demonstrably; source-version bump flagging works; DecisionAssessment renders the lineage.

TESTS: unit (requirement validation incl. sourceless refusal; factor-lineage arithmetic; context-strictness gating logic; version-bump flagging); e2e: two projects (scoping vs sign-off context) on the same physics logging the differing gate behavior, plus the requirement-lineage table in both reports.

title: No-silent-defaults enforcement: the doctrine as lint + refusal battery (defaults are rare, visible, receipted)
description:
WHY: The Five Explicits doctrine's engineering extension — no silent ambient, no implicit zero contact resistance, no unnamed turbulence intensity, no unitless HTC, no stateless material, no mesh-index face selection, no unchecked optimization result — only holds if it is ENFORCED where scenarios are built and validated. Culture plus deadline equals silent defaults; only refusal machinery survives contact with both. This bead is the epic's consolidated enforcement + test lane.

WHAT: (a) The default-policy audit: enumerate every place the scenario/project/solve path COULD apply a default (a mechanical sweep of constructor defaults, Option fallbacks, and unwrap_or sites in the relevant crates — hand-reviewed per the no-script-rewrite discipline); classify each: REFUSE (must be declared: ambient conditions, interface resistance, material state, turbulence/flow intensity parameters when RANS lands, requirement limits), RECEIPTED DEFAULT (acceptable with visible receipt: solver tolerances, output verbosity), or INTERNAL (no user-facing meaning); (b) enforcement: REFUSE-class paths get typed Violations (most exist via e17_2/3 and fs-scenario's required-Environment precedent — this bead closes the sweep's residue); RECEIPTED-class paths emit default-receipts collected into validate output and the report ("defaults applied" section — an empty section is the goal state for validation-grade runs); (c) the doctrine battery: one refusal test per doctrine item, phrased as user stories (author omits X -> named Violation with fix hint), plus receipt-visibility tests; (d) drift guard: new unclassified default sites flagged by the sweep re-run in check-all (the classification table is the allowlist).

DONE WHEN: sweep classification table merged; every REFUSE item has its refusal test; receipts render; drift guard green in check-all and demonstrably catches a seeded new default.

TESTS: this bead IS the battery — per-item refusal tests with message-quality assertions, receipt-emission tests, allowlist drift detection; e2e: a maximally-sloppy scenario validated, logging every Violation and receipt, then repaired step-by-step to clean (the transcript doubles as user education material).

title: Design variables, manufacturing constraints, objectives, and failure modes as scenario objects (schema now, optimization later)
description:
WHY: The scenario-semantics review list explicitly includes "design variables and manufacturing constraints" and "objectives, constraints, margins, and failure modes" — and the no-silent-defaults doctrine includes "no optimization result without manufacturing and robustness checks." No other bead gives these a home: e17_6 covers requirements/margins, but design VARIABLES (what may change), manufacturing constraints (what changes are buildable), optimization objectives, and failure-mode declarations are unowned. They are staged for the post-0.1 optimization phase (forward prediction first), but the SCHEMA must be shaped for them now so the 0.1 project format (e06_1, frozen per e16_5) does not need a breaking change when optimization arrives.

WHAT: (a) Design-variable objects: which scenario quantities may vary (geometry parameters via fs-xform parameterization refs, material selections from declared card sets, fan choices from a catalog, layout positions), each with bounds, discreteness, and units — typed against the entities they modify (e17_1 identities); (b) manufacturing constraints as first-class declarations: minimum wall thickness, fin spacing manufacturability, draft/tooling classes, available stock materials, assembly clearances — the constraints an optimizer must respect and a HUMAN can audit (each with source provenance like requirements); (c) objectives declared, not implied: the optimization target (minimize T_max, minimize fan power at fixed T_max, maximize margin) with the QoI refs and the robustness posture (nominal vs CVaR-class robust per fs-robust) stated explicitly; (d) failure-mode declarations: named failure modes per component class (thermal runaway threshold, solder fatigue proxy limits, connector derating) with severity — these extend e17_6's severity classes into a checkable failure-mode registry that DecisionAssessment and the future optimization loop consult; (e) staging: schema types land NOW (validated, serialized, versioned); the optimization EXECUTION consuming them is e06_14's scope.

DONE WHEN: schema types + validation land with the .fsim format able to carry them (round-trip tested); the reference project gains a worked design-variable/constraint block (validated but unexercised); e06_14 can be written against these types without schema changes; no-silent-defaults battery (e17_7) extended: an optimization request without manufacturing constraints or robustness posture REFUSES.

TESTS: unit (each object's validation incl. bound/discreteness/unit checks; entity-ref resolution; sourceless-constraint refusal; failure-mode registry lookups); round-trip serialization within the versioned schema; the e17_7 battery extension (optimization-without-constraints refusal with actionable message); e2e: reference project with the design block validates and logs the full variable/constraint/objective/failure-mode table with provenance columns.

title: E02 Claim-integrity burn-down: no output may claim more than its evidence proves
description:
WHY: The project's moat is preserving the epistemic status of physical claims. Any bug that lets a surface emit a STRONGER claim than the evidence supports (the topology exact-count-of-one bug class; FlutterReport::boundaries_agree passing on truncated sweeps, bead hukmw; grace-masks-the-mechanism soundness traps) is therefore worse than an ordinary wrong answer — it corrupts the product's core value proposition and silently poisons every downstream composition. The synthesis puts this FIRST among immediate actions: "Any bug that can emit a stronger epistemic claim than the evidence supports should block public capability promotion."

WHAT (children): (1) define the claim-integrity defect class precisely + a label taxonomy so these defects are findable and countable; (2) an audit sweep of claim-emitting surfaces to file/triage new defects; (3) a machine-checkable promotion gate: open claim-integrity P0s block capability-maturity promotion (ties into e16 maturity registry); (4) tests for the gate itself.

PRECEDENT: this continues the existing soundness-audit vein (fs-ivl/fs-iga/fs-lbm/fs-cutfem fixes; bead wa8i certificate-spine audit) but converts it from an episodic activity into a standing, gated program with a countable inventory.

DONE WHEN: claim-integrity label exists and is applied; the sweep has completed at least one full pass over claim-emitting crates (fs-evidence, fs-package, fs-checker, fs-topo, fs-geom seams, campaign crates); the promotion gate runs in xtask/DSR and demonstrably blocks promotion while a tagged P0 is open; zero KNOWN open claim-integrity P0s at Level-4 promotion time.

title: Define the claim-integrity defect class + label taxonomy (make over-claiming countable)
description:
WHY: "Stop the system from claiming more than the evidence proves" is the project's core discipline, but today such defects are scattered across ordinary bug beads and are not countable, so they cannot gate anything. A precise class definition turns an ethos into an enforceable inventory.

WHAT: (a) A written definition with decision rules: a claim-integrity defect exists when any public surface (API return type, evidence color, certificate, report line, README/CONTRACT sentence, WASM export) can assert a STRONGER epistemic state than its actual evidence — e.g. exact topology counts from bounded-component arguments; boundaries_agree true on truncated sweeps (bead hukmw); Verified color reachable from Estimated inputs; validity asserted outside a model card's domain; a golden hash treated as authority for semantics it does not pin. Include severity rules: P0 = reachable in a default/public path; P1 = reachable behind features; P2 = doc-only overstatement. (b) Beads label taxonomy: label `claim-integrity` plus severity; document it in docs/CONVENTIONS.md. title: fs-evidence: ModelBracket::evidence hard-codes in_domain:true, and that literal is what lets it certify
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_evidence::ModelBracket::evidence -> Evidence<f64>.model.in_domain
FILE: crates/fs-evidence/src/discrepancy.rs:637-643

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
ModelEvidence.in_domain is 'False the moment any constituent was queried outside its domain', and certified() requires 'EXPLICIT in-domain non-negative model evidence'. in_domain:true on evidence that NAMES N model cards reads as: every one of those N models was evaluated inside its stated validity domain.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
A ModelBracket holds only (name, qoi) pairs. No validity domain, evaluation point, or card is ever supplied, and evidence() performs no domain check whatsoever; it hard-codes validity: ValidityDomain::unconstrained(), in_domain: true.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
ModelBracket::new().try_with_member("contact-angle-60",0.90)?.try_with_member("contact-angle-120",1.16)?.evidence(p) returns evidence naming two models with in_domain:true whose certified() is Ok - asserted at discrepancy.rs:982. The literal is load-bearing: were it false, certified() would refuse with OutOfDomain and breakdown().model_rel would be +inf instead of the finite spread.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Either compute in_domain honestly from the members' validity domains plus the evaluation point, accept an explicit caller-supplied verdict, or emit in_domain:false until member cards are supplied. Bracket spread quantifies model-CHOICE sensitivity, which is not evidence that any member was used inside its validity range.

GAP SHAPE: Forgeable certificate / laundering - a constructor-supplied literal stands in for a check that never ran
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). ModelBracket::evidence emits in_domain:false with a named assumption that bracket spread is model-CHOICE sensitivity; new evidence_at(prov, validity, point) computes the verdict honestly. Two in-module tests that asserted the forged true were updated.

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
Hull is documented as 'Anything else: the conservative hull of both bounds', and compose as 'Verified bounds combine per op (outward-rounded to preserve enclosure)'. A caller composing under an operation that is neither Add nor Mul is told Hull is the conservative choice and the returned Verified{lo,hi} encloses the result.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
(a0.min(b0), a1.max(b1)) - the union hull of the two OPERAND intervals. That encloses the result only for operations whose value always lies between the operands (min/max, selection, convex combination, envelope folds).

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
Composing Verified{10.0,10.0} and Verified{-10.0,-10.0} under a subtraction - for which the enum's own text directs the caller to Hull - yields Verified{-10.0,10.0}, which does not contain the true difference 20.0. (In-tree Hull uses, e.g. crates/fs-thrust-e2e/src/lib.rs:387, are envelope folds and are sound; the exposure is the documented invitation.)

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
'Hull: the union of both operand intervals. This is an enclosure ONLY for operations whose result always lies between its operands. It is NOT a valid enclosure for difference, ratio, or any other operation; those must compose through fs-ivl.' The compose doc should stop implying Hull preserves enclosure for arbitrary ops.

GAP SHAPE: Conservative-sounding fallback documented as sound for a class of operations for which it is not
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). Hull rustdoc + compose rustdoc + CONTRACT now state Hull is an enclosure ONLY for operations whose result lies between the operands; difference/ratio must compose through fs-ivl. DOC-ONLY: rustdoc + CONTRACT wording; no executable regression exists because compose cannot observe the caller's operation. Covered by the check-claims doc lint, which fails if the CONTRACT sections regress.

title: fs-topo: self_intersection_certificate skips every vertex-sharing face pair yet reports proven_free
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_topo::self_intersection_certificate / SelfIntersectReport::proven_free
FILE: crates/fs-topo/src/intersect.rs:238, :37, :1-9; crates/fs-topo/src/lib.rs:9-15; CONTRACT.md:26-28, :74

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
proven_free() == true means this soup contains no self-intersections, and the proof cannot be false ('A PASS is a PROOF (exact arithmetic - false PASS impossible)', 'A PASS cannot be falsely claimed').

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
Only that no two triangles sharing NO vertex index intersect. Every pair sharing at least one vertex index is skipped before the narrow phase (`if ti.iter().any(|v| tj.contains(v)) { continue; }`) on the rationale that such faces 'legitimately touch' - valid for touching, not for crossing.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
Default features, ~10 lines. Soup{positions:[(0,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0.3,0.2,-1),(0.3,0.2,1)], triangles:[[0,1,2],[0,3,4]]}. T1's edge v3->v4 pierces T0's interior at (0.3,0.2,0) (0.3+0.2 < 1), so T0 cap T1 is a segment, not the shared vertex - a genuine self-intersection. The pair shares vertex 0, is skipped, pairs_tested == 0, proven_free() == true. The failure is not arithmetic, so 'exact arithmetic => no false PASS' does not apply.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
'PASS proves that no two faces sharing zero vertices intersect. Faces sharing a vertex are excluded and may still cross; non-intersection of the surface as a whole is NOT established.' Either scope the accessor (proven_free_among_vertex_disjoint_pairs) or test vertex-sharing pairs and excuse only intersections confined to the shared feature.

GAP SHAPE: Limited-scope argument read as global exactness
CONFIDENCE: HIGH

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). Took the stronger option: shared-vertex/shared-edge pairs are now DECIDED against their shared feature with exact orient2d/orient3d instead of skipped. Tetrahedron and icosphere adjacency still pass (no false FAILs); shared_feature_pairs_tested makes coverage auditable. CONTRACT 'PASS is a PROOF' language rescoped.

title: fs-topo: non-finite vertex coordinates silently pass both self-intersection and manifold certificates
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_topo::self_intersection_certificate (PASS) and fs_topo::manifold_certificate (certified())
FILE: crates/fs-topo/src/intersect.rs:200-234; crates/fs-topo/src/lib.rs:104-205

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
Both certificates are total over their inputs ('Certificates are total over admitted inputs', CONTRACT.md:106) and a PASS is a proof: proven_free() => no self-intersections; certified() => 'the soup is a closed, oriented, manifold surface' with degenerate faces and fold-overs ruled out.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
Nothing at all when vertex positions are non-finite. Neither function admits its input for finiteness. In sweep-and-prune, lo[k].min(NaN)/hi[k].max(NaN) DISCARD the NaN (IEEE minNum), so a NaN triangle gets the inverted box lo=+inf, hi=-inf and every pair containing it is culled before the exact narrow phase - the orient3d finiteness assertion is never reached. In manifold_certificate, n.norm() < 1e-30, den > 1e-30 and (winding_exact(..)-1.0).abs() > 0.5 are all FALSE for NaN, so no defect is recorded. The .expect("finite coords") guard is dead code: lo[0] can be +inf but never NaN.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
(a) Soup{positions:[(0,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0.2,NaN,-1),(0.4,NaN,1),(0.3,NaN,0)], triangles:[[0,1,2],[3,4,5]]} -> pairs_tested == 0, proven_free() == true. (b) Take any closed consistently oriented combinatorial sphere (e.g. shapes::icosphere), set every position component to f64::NAN; manifold_certificate(&soup, Some(any_probe)).certified() == true, because check_invariants never reads positions.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Admit the input first: a soup containing a non-finite coordinate must yield a typed refusal (or Unknown/Indeterminate), never proven_free()/certified(). The geometric red-flag and winding checks must fail closed on non-finite intermediates rather than falling through their comparisons.

GAP SHAPE: Silent-pass / fail-open gate - a certificate returning PASS on malformed evidence
CONFIDENCE: HIGH

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.

REGRESSION TESTS (fs-topo/tests/claim_integrity.rs): non_finite_coordinates_refuse_the_self_intersection_certificate, non_finite_coordinates_refuse_the_manifold_certificate, non_finite_probe_yields_no_outwardness_verdict, out_of_range_indices_refuse_the_self_intersection_certificate, exactly_degenerate_faces_refuse_rather_than_pass. A distinct, non-localized variant - e.g. ManifoldDefect::InwardOrientation{probe, winding} - or an explicit outward: Option<bool> on the report. The localization contract must not be satisfied with a sentinel.

title: fs-topo: ManifoldReport::oriented documents outwardness but omits it entirely when no probe is supplied
description:

FILE: crates/fs-topo/src/lib.rs:80-86, :93-98, :104, :188-198

title: fs-geom: fixture charts publish BettiBounds::exact with a false b2 (and false b1 for the torus)

FILE: crates/fs-geom/src/fixtures.rs:151-153, :227-233, :318-324; type at src/lib.rs:564-597; CONTRACT.md:110-117

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
BettiBounds::exact(b0,b1,b2) is 'Exact known Betti numbers' producing the singleton [b,b] per dimension, with b2 'Enclosed voids'. The only alternative is unknown() = (0,u32::MAX). So SphereChart::topology_hint().b2 == (1,1) reads as: exactly one enclosed void, with 0 excluded.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
Nothing - the values are literals with no derivation, and they are false under the crate's own documented meaning. A Chart presents the region where the SDF is NEGATIVE, so SphereChart is a solid ball (1,0,0), BoxChart a solid box (1,0,0), TorusChart a solid torus (1,1,0). All three publish b2 = 1. fs-topo's conformance suite pins exactly this convention (tests/conformance.rs:285,:320). fs_geom::fixtures::SphereChart{center, radius:1.0}.topology_hint() returns BettiBounds{b0:(1,1), b1:(0,0), b2:(1,1)}, while fs_topo::cubical::verify_topology on the same solid returns (1,0,0) - and its doc positions itself as 'an Estimate-grade refinement of topology_hint()', so a consumer refining the hint against the measurement sees the Estimate contradict an 'exact' claim. A castability constraint of the form enclosed_voids == 0 reads the fixture ball as uncastable.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Either exact(1,0,0)/exact(1,0,0)/exact(1,1,0) under the documented solid-region meaning, or BettiBounds::unknown() until a certificate exists - the honest default the CONTRACT already names.

title: fs-geom: SampledSdf::bound is published as a reconstruction bound but is derived from sample-local Lipschitz maxima
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_geom::convert::SampledSdf::bound() / ::nominal_field_bound()
FILE: crates/fs-geom/src/convert.rs:242-256, :210-212, :515-518, :543-550, :565-568

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
'Reconstruction bound relative to the sampled source field. This is useful even when the source makes no abstract-distance claim.' A caller may infer |SampledSdf::eval(p) - source(p)| <= bound() for every p in the box - that is what a reconstruction bound means, and the doc explicitly advertises it for NoClaim sources.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
nominal_field_bound = outward(l_max * max_cell_diagonal) + roundoff, where for a non-ExactDistance source l_max is the max of per-node ChartSample::lipschitz values - documented as 'Certified LOCAL Lipschitz bound ... near the query', with no radius. The trilinear convex-combination argument needs a Lipschitz bound valid over the whole cell; a maximum of local-at-the-nodes bounds does not supply one. The code knows this (:511-514) and routes it into abstract_distance_kind (forced to Estimate at :590) - but not into bound(), a bare f64 with no NumericalKind.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
The blanket impl<C: Chart> Convert<SampledSdf> for C makes this reachable for every chart. A conforming chart with trace_step_claim() == NoClaim returning lipschitz: Some(1.0) at every query, whose real field has a narrow spike strictly between grid nodes (grid is n <= 96 nodes, so inter-node gaps are known to the chart), passes admission; bound() returns ~cell_diagonal + roundoff while the true reconstruction error at the spike is unbounded by it.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
'Reconstruction radius computed from the source's declared per-node local Lipschitz values. It is a rigorous bound only when the source declares TraceStepClaim::ExactDistance; otherwise it is an Estimate and sub-cell slope spikes may exceed it.' Better: return the kind alongside it so the getter cannot be read out of context.

GAP SHAPE: Local hypothesis applied over a whole cell and published as a bound
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). New nominal_field_bound_kind() -> Enclosure only for ExactDistance sources, Estimate otherwise. The number is unchanged; it now travels with its authority, and the rustdoc/CONTRACT state the condition instead of advertising the bound for NoClaim sources. REGRESSION TEST: the_reconstruction_radius_carries_its_authority (fs-geom/tests/claim_integrity.rs), verified to fail pre-fix (Enclosure vs Estimate). fs-geom suite green.

title: Claim-integrity audit sweep over claim-emitting surfaces (file/triage defects)
description:
WHY: The class definition is only useful against a real inventory. The soundness-audit vein (fs-ivl/fs-iga/fs-lbm/fs-cutfem fixes; wa8i certificate-spine audit) proved this defect family exists and is findable by systematic reading; this task makes one full, recorded pass with the new taxonomy.

WHAT: Sweep, in priority order, the claim-emitting surfaces: fs-evidence (color minting, admitted/identity paths), fs-package + fs-checker (claim admission, release gates), fs-topo + fs-geom seam results (topology claims; the README already documents the seam/no-claim subtleties — verify code matches), fs-adjoint certificates, fs-solver reports, campaign crates (fs-thrust-e2e, fs-flutter-e2e boundaries_agree class, fs-neuroshape-e2e component counts, fs-ornith, fs-flagship-e2e), fs-wasm exports (the WASM layer historically over-reported: exact component count of one from a lower-bound argument), and README/CONTRACT claim sentences vs code. Do NOT fix in this bead (except trivial doc lines) — the deliverable is the verified inventory; fixes are separate beads so the gate has an accurate count.

METHOD: for each surface, write down the STRONGEST claim the type/API/doc permits a caller to infer, then hunt for an input/state where evidence is weaker than that claim. The grace-masks-the-mechanism trap (tests green while the claim fails) means reading tests is not enough — construct adversarial instances.

DONE WHEN: every listed surface has a recorded audit note (clean or defect beads filed); the sweep report artifact lists surface -> verdict -> bead IDs.

TESTS: the sweep report is itself a deterministic artifact; an e2e script verifies every defect bead carries severity + repro fields and logs the full surface/verdict table.
close_reason: Landed 8bbb2ef4.
