title: fs-adjoint: verify_gradient scores a silent-zero gradient as a perfect pass when analytic and FD are both 0
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_adjoint::verify::verify_gradient -> GradientVerdict{pass, max_rel_err}
FILE: crates/fs-adjoint/src/verify.rs:113 (scale), :125 (pass)

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
pass == true means the analytic gradient was independently corroborated by central finite differences along every probed direction to relative tolerance tol. The CONTRACT strengthens it: 'Empty/all-zero directions ... refused as vacuous evidence' and 'the gate itself is tested to REJECT corrupted, non-finite, and vacuous evidence - a gate that cannot fail is not a gate'. ci-gauntlet blocks merges on this bit.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
|analytic - fd| / max(|analytic|,|fd|,1e-12*||d||inf) < tol. When analytic and fd are BOTH exactly 0.0 the numerator is 0, so the ratio is 0 regardless of the floor: the comparison has zero discriminating power for any gradient whose claimed directional derivative is 0 along a direction the objective is bit-insensitive to.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
j = |_p| 7.0 (any J whose forward path drops p), p = [1.0,2.0], gradient = [0.0,0.0] (a silent-zero cotangent), directions = [[1.0,-1.0]], eps = 1e-6, tol = 1e-6 -> analytic = 0.0, fd = (7.0-7.0)/2e-6 = 0.0, relative_error = 0.0, pass = true, max_rel_err = 0.0 (a perfect score). The refusal preflight does not fire: the direction is finite, non-zero, and both perturbations move the stored coordinates. The realistic reach is a seam that drops the parameter dependence - the same broken pipeline produces BOTH the zero gradient and two bit-identical J evaluations. The battery's vacuity test (tests/adjoint_battery.rs:518) covers empty and all-zero DIRECTIONS, not zero-vs-zero PAIRS.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
A direction whose analytic and FD derivatives are both exactly zero is a no-signal probe and must not contribute a passing verdict: refuse ('objective is bit-insensitive along direction k: the experiment carries no evidence') or return an informative_directions count and require at least one.

GAP SHAPE: Silent gradient loss / vacuous certificate; fail-open gate
CONFIDENCE: HIGH

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). GradientVerdict gained informative_directions; a probe whose analytic and FD derivatives are both at the 1e-12*||d||inf floor carries no evidence, and a verification with none fails closed. A mixed set (one no-signal + one real direction) still passes, so this refuses vacuity without over-refusing. The CONTRACT's 'a gate that cannot fail is not a gate' is now true.

title: fs-adjoint: fd_falsifier's acceptance band is absolute, so zero or sign-flipped adjoints pass on small derivatives
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_adjoint::transpose::fd_falsifier -> FdVerdict.consistent (and consumers certs::fd_spot_checks, certs::merge_gate)
FILE: crates/fs-adjoint/src/transpose.rs:346

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
consistent == true is 'the independent cross-check a transpose bug or sign error trips'; merge_gate returning Ok is 'THE CI GRADIENT GATE ... no merge without a passing check'. A caller may infer the adjoint directional derivative agrees with FD to a conditioning-aware RELATIVE tolerance.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
|adjoint_dd - fd_fine| <= base_tol * max(|adjoint_dd|,|fd_fine|,1.0) + 3*|fd(h)-fd(h/2)|. The .max(1.0) term is an ABSOLUTE floor unrelated to problem scale, so the band is never tighter than base_tol in absolute units. Whenever the true directional derivative is smaller than base_tol, every value in [-base_tol, base_tol] satisfies the predicate - including 0 and the sign-flipped truth.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
With the production constants of certs::fd_spot_checks (h = 1e-5, base_tol = 1e-7, certs.rs:656): f(x) = 1e-9*x[0], x = [1.0], dir = [0.4]. adjoint_dd = 0.0 (silent-zero seam) -> tolerance 1.0e-7, |0 - 4e-10| <= tol -> consistent = TRUE. adjoint_dd = -4e-10 (exact sign flip) -> consistent = TRUE. Control: f(x) = 3*x[0], adjoint_dd = 0.0 -> consistent = FALSE. The sealed FdCheckBatch then records consistent = true, fd_all_consistent() is true, and merge_gate returns Ok.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
The acceptance band must be homogeneous in the derivative scale (the sibling verify_gradient already uses 1e-12*||d||inf for exactly this reason). When max(|adjoint_dd|,|fd_fine|) is below the noise floor the verdict is 'no signal / not falsifiable at this step', not 'consistent'.

GAP SHAPE: Forgeable certificate - a tolerance so large it is vacuous; silent gradient loss surviving the mandatory falsifier
CONFIDENCE: HIGH

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). The absolute .max(1.0) floor is replaced by the central difference's own cancellation noise eps(|f+|+|f-|)/h, which is homogeneous under the paired rescaling that leaves evaluation points fixed. On the bead's witness both the zero and the exactly sign-flipped adjoint now FAIL; a constant objective reports falsifiable=false rather than 'consistent'. REGRESSION TESTS: tr_009_fd_falsifier_band_is_scale_relative (fs-adjoint/tests/transpose.rs) and gc_010_small_derivative_cannot_launder_a_zero_adjoint_through_the_merge_gate (tests/certs.rs). Both verified to fail pre-fix on the bead's exact witness. fs-adjoint battery green.

title: fs-adjoint: check_transpose returns the perfect score 0.0 for zero probes or empty dimensions
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_adjoint::transpose::check_transpose -> f64
FILE: crates/fs-adjoint/src/transpose.rs:282-306

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
'Transpose-consistency check max |<Av,w> - <v,A^T w>| over seeded deterministic probes - the G0 suite every registered linear op runs.' A small returned value is evidence that the registered transpose really is the adjoint of the forward apply; callers threshold it.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
The maximum of |lhs - rhs| over exactly `probes` LCG-seeded probes, with the fold seeded at 0.0 and no lower bound on probes, n_in, or n_out, and no normalization by operator or vector magnitude.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
check_transpose(&apply, &apply_t, n_in, n_out, 0) returns 0.0 - the strongest possible score - having evaluated neither operator; the loop body never runs. n_in = 0 / n_out = 0 gives lhs = rhs = 0 for every probe. Separately, because the residual is ABSOLUTE, an operator whose entries are ~1e-20 scores ~1e-40 against any threshold no matter how wrong apply_t is. The hardened sibling in the same crate (certs::adjoint_residual_bound, certs.rs:301) explicitly refuses probes == 0 and 0-row/0-column shapes.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Refuse probes == 0 and empty dimensions with a structured error (as adjoint_residual_bound does), and return the probe count and a scale (e.g. max |Av||w|) alongside the residual so a threshold is relative.

GAP SHAPE: Vacuous / forgeable certificate (empty evidence yields the strongest number)
CONFIDENCE: HIGH

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). check_transpose returns Result<TransposeProbeReport, TransposeProbeError>, refusing zero probes, empty dims, wrong-length and non-finite images, and reporting probes/scale/rel_residual so a threshold can be relative. REGRESSION TEST: tr_008_transpose_probe_refuses_vacuous_requests (fs-adjoint/tests/transpose.rs); existing tr_002 battery updated for the Result return and strengthened to assert the relative residual. fs-adjoint suite green.

title: fs-adjoint: Vjp cotangent lengths are never checked despite the doc claiming the sweep checks them; zip silently truncates
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_adjoint::transpose::Vjp (trait doc) + Tape::transpose
FILE: crates/fs-adjoint/src/transpose.rs:27-30 (claim), :250-265 (code)

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
'produce the cotangents for each input (same arity, same lengths - checked by the sweep)'. A caller may infer a returned leaf gradient has the leaf's dimension and that a VJP violating the shape contract is caught, consistent with the module's 'never a silent zero' doctrine.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
Only ARITY is asserted (assert_eq!(input_bars.len(), node.inputs.len())). Individual cotangent lengths are never compared against self.nodes[src].value.len(); accumulation is acc.iter_mut().zip(&ib), which truncates to the shorter.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
A Vjp returning a cotangent shorter than its input (a masking/slicing bug - precisely the seam-crossing shape this module exists to catch) produces, for a leaf of length n consumed by two ops: first contribution stored verbatim at length k < n, second accumulated under zip and silently truncated to k. The returned map presents a length-k vector as that leaf's gradient; the dropped tail is indistinguishable from a genuine zero cotangent and no TransposeError is raised. Secondary: the sentinel op name "leaf" is not reserved by Tape::apply, so tape.apply("leaf", &[x], v) is skipped by the node.op == "leaf" guard (line 223) WITHOUT a registry lookup - an unregistered op terminates the chain silently instead of raising MissingVjp.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Perform the length check the doc advertises (refuse with TransposeError::VjpShape{op,input,expected,got}) or delete the 'same lengths - checked by the sweep' clause and state that cotangent lengths are an unchecked caller invariant. Tape::apply should reject the reserved op name "leaf".

GAP SHAPE: Silent gradient loss; doc asserting a check the code does not perform
CONFIDENCE: HIGH

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). Cotangent and seed lengths are asserted against recorded primals; Tape::apply rejects the reserved 'leaf' op name. Assertions rather than a new TransposeError variant because fs-diffreal-e2e matches that enum exhaustively and is out of boundary; the trait doc now says violations panic. Fixture tr_003 corrected - it only worked because accumulation silently truncated, which IS the defect. REGRESSION TESTS: tr_005_truncated_cotangent_is_refused_not_zipped, tr_006_short_seed_is_refused, tr_007_reserved_leaf_op_name_is_refused (fs-adjoint/tests/transpose.rs). Fixture tr_003 corrected - it only passed because accumulation silently truncated, which IS the defect. fs-adjoint suite green.

title: fs-solver: SolveReport.rel_residual carries three different quantities under one documented meaning; PMINRES admits a semidefinite preconditioner
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_solver::krylov::SolveReport{rel_residual, converged} as produced by PminresState::run and CgState::run
FILE: crates/fs-solver/src/krylov.rs:34-37, :69-81, :347-349, :377-378, :123-126, :158

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
rel_residual is documented verbatim as 'Final relative residual ||r||/||b||' and converged as 'Tolerance met.' A driver holding a SolveReport - the type shared by all five solvers and the only thing most callers see - may read converged == true as ||b - Ax||_2/||b||_2 < tol.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
Three different quantities funnel into that one meaning. (a) PMINRES: rel_residual = |eta|/bnorm with bnorm = sqrt(b'Mb) - a Givens estimate of the residual in the M-NORM, and converged is decided on it. (b) CG: the RECURSIVELY propagated r, never recomputed as b - Ax, and CG's accessor lacks the 'estimate' qualifier MinresState and PminresState both carry. (c) GMRES/FGMRES do recompute the true residual - so the field means different things by producer.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
(a) Wrong norm: for SPD M = diag(1, 1e-12) (a legal Precond), residual r = (0,1) against b = (1,0) gives ||r||_M/||b||_M = 1e-6 while ||r||_2/||b||_2 = 1.0 - verified numerically. A report of converged:true, rel_residual:1e-6 at tol = 1e-5 accompanies a 100% Euclidean relative residual. (b) Fail-open guard: PminresState::run guards positivity with assert!(vz >= -1e-30) (line 377), which ADMITS vz == 0. A merely positive-SEMIdefinite M then yields beta_next = 2.2e-308, s_k ~ 2.2e-308/|delta|, eta collapses to ~0, and the next check reports converged:true, rel_residual ~ 1e-308 with an arbitrary iterate - the guard whose message is 'preconditioner lost positivity' is fail-open exactly where positivity is lost.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
SolveReport should carry the norm and provenance, e.g. residual: ResidualClaim::{TrueEuclidean(f64), RecursiveEstimate(f64), MNormEstimate(f64)}, and converged should say 'the reported residual claim met tol'. PMINRES's positivity guard should refuse vz <= 0 as breakdown, not admit it as convergence.

GAP SHAPE: Residual in the wrong norm read as a correctness claim; fail-open on unresolved state
CONFIDENCE: HIGH

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: COMPLETE (8493ab35). SolveReport now carries a private ResidualClaim field plus #[non_exhaustive], with from_claim/from_claim_with_diagnosis the only constructors in any crate — so a report WITHOUT provenance cannot be built, by fs-bem or anyone else, and rel_residual/converged are DERIVED inside the constructor so the number and its provenance cannot disagree. The Euclidean reading fails closed: euclidean_rel_residual() returns None and converged_euclidean() returns false for RecursiveEstimate and MNormEstimate. The fs-bem struct literal at panel3d.rs:568 that blocked the previous attempt is migrated (honest: b=0,x=0 gives an exactly-zero Euclidean residual). Newton telemetry no longer launders — linear_relative_residual reads euclidean_rel_residual().unwrap_or(NAN). REGRESSION TESTS: a_report_alone_names_its_residual_and_refuses_the_euclidean_reading and every_report_is_built_from_a_claim_and_cannot_contradict_it (crates/fs-solver/tests/claim_integrity.rs), verified to fail against the old shape (10+ E0599s). Its logged witness IS the defect: a report saying converged=true rel_residual=2.359e-14 whose iterate has a true Euclidean relative residual of 1.668e-8. Suites green: fs-solver all 8 targets, fs-bem 5+8, fs-time operator_integrators 5 (bitwise SolveReport replay, proving the FGMRES constructor refactor is output-identical). Readers proven unbroken: cargo check across fs-adjoint, fs-cutfem, fs-time, fs-topopt, fs-flux, fs-solid, fs-marquee all-targets all-features, exit 0. RESIDUAL GAP (documented in CONTRACT, not hidden): pub rel_residual/converged fields remain readable, so the wrong reading is refused by the typed API but still expressible via the field; making them private breaks 4 field reads in fs-adjoint/fs-cutfem/fs-time and #[deprecated] would become a hard CI error under -D warnings. The CONTRACT names those three readers as the worklist for that slice.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: PARTIAL. Fixed: the concretely exploitable half - PminresState's fail-open positivity guard (assert!(vz >= -1e-30) admitted vz == 0, collapsing eta to ~0 and reporting converged on an arbitrary iterate) is now a scale-relative refusal that still admits happy breakdown; PminresState::new's bz >= 0.0 (singular M on a nonzero rhs) likewise. Added public ResidualClaim::{TrueEuclidean,RecursiveEstimate,MNormEstimate} with residual_claim() on all five solver states, and per-producer docs on SolveReport + CONTRACT. REMAINING: the provenance is NOT on SolveReport itself, so a driver holding only a SolveReport still cannot tell which of the three quantities it has. Blocked because SolveReport is built by struct literal in crates/fs-bem/src/panel3d.rs:568 (outside the fix boundary) and a typed rel_residual would break ~15 reader crates. Needs a coordinated cross-crate slice.

title: fs-solver: the p-multigrid V-cycle discards its coarse PcgReport, so the CONTRACT's symmetry/fixity invariant has no evidence
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_solver::pmg::PMultigrid as Precond + the fs-solver CONTRACT symmetric-V-cycle invariant
FILE: crates/fs-solver/src/pmg.rs:488, :623-624

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
Every V-cycle application solves the r = 1 coarse level near-exactly, so the preconditioner is a FIXED symmetric operator - the precondition plain CG needs, and which the same CONTRACT says is violated by a loosely-solved coarse level.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
fs_sparse::precond::pcg(...) returns PcgReport{iters, rel_residual, converged} and both call sites discard it with `let _ =`. If the coarse AMG-CG exits on its 2000-iteration cap rather than at 1e-13, the V-cycle silently becomes an inexact, application-dependent (hence varying) operator. Precond::apply returns (), so there is no channel to report it and no state to inspect.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
Any CgState::run with PMultigrid as preconditioner, including the shipped StokesBlockDiag. A coarse solve failing to reach 1e-13 within 2000 iterations (ill-conditioned coarse level, near-singular SA-AMG aggregation, catastrophic cancellation in the coarse RHS) is absorbed without a trace, and the outer report still says converged:true - on the recursive CG residual, precisely the quantity that decouples from truth under a varying preconditioner. No seeded fault currently makes the cap fire; the defect is that the receipt is discarded so no surface can ever say it did.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Retain the worst coarse PcgReport in PMultigrid and expose coarse_solves_converged() -> bool so drivers can demote the claim, or make the coarse cap a hard failure. The CONTRACT invariant should say the near-exact coarse solve is REQUESTED, and that V-cycle fixity is an assumption, not an established invariant.

GAP SHAPE: Fail-open on unresolved state; CONTRACT invariant asserted where the code discards the only evidence for it
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). PMultigrid retains coarse PcgReports through atomics; coarse_solves_converged()/worst_coarse_rel_residual()/coarse_solves()/reset_coarse_evidence() expose them. CONTRACT invariant downgraded from an asserted near-exact coarse solve to 'requested at 1e-13; convergence is not established unless the driver consults the receipt'. REGRESSION TEST: pmg_retains_its_coarse_solve_receipts (fs-solver/tests/claim_integrity.rs), verified to fail pre-fix. fs-solver suite green (11 battery + 5 stokes + 4 claim_integrity).

title: fs-adjoint: ift_gradient_matfree zips djdp against the pullback, silently returning a partly-uncorrected gradient
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_adjoint::ift::ift_gradient_matfree -> (Vec<f64>, AdjointReport)
FILE: crates/fs-adjoint/src/ift.rs:45-52

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
The returned vector is dJ/dp = dJ/dp_explicit - (dR/dp)^T*lambda, as stated in both the rustdoc and the CONTRACT. Every component is the full total derivative.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
g is initialized to djdp (or zeros of pullback.len() when djdp is empty) and then corrected by g.iter_mut().zip(&pullback), which truncates to the shorter. There is no length check anywhere in the function - unusual for this crate, whose neighbours assert on every dimension.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
Call with djdp of length np and a drdp_t closure returning a pullback of length k < np (a masked or sliced parameter-space pullback - the ordinary way this goes wrong). The returned vector has the expected length np, components 0..k carry the full total derivative, and components k..np silently carry only the explicit partial with the adjoint term omitted. AdjointReport says converged:true, so nothing in the evidence object contradicts the claim. Symmetrically, k > np silently drops the tail and returns a short vector.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Refuse the mismatch: assert_eq!(djdp.len(), pullback.len()) (matching the crate's 'impossible internal dimension failures are assertions' error model) or return a typed error. The value returned must be the total derivative on every component or nothing at all.

GAP SHAPE: Silent gradient loss
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). assert_eq!(djdp.len(), pullback.len()) plus djdu.len() == jacobian.n(); a truncated pullback can no longer return a partly-uncorrected vector labelled dJ/dp. REGRESSION TEST: ift_gradient_refuses_a_truncated_pullback (fs-adjoint/tests/adjoint_battery.rs), verified to fail pre-fix. fs-adjoint battery green.

title: fs-adjoint: density_misfit_hvp claims EXACT Hessian-vector products behind a convergence assert a caller tolerance can make vacuous
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_adjoint::hessian::density_misfit_hvp -> Vec<f64>
FILE: crates/fs-adjoint/src/hessian.rs:25-30 (guard), :39-45 (claim)

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
The returned vector is the exact second derivative action H*v for the density-linear class - no finite-difference approximation - and the inner assert!(rep.converged, ..) guarantees the four linear solves that produce it actually succeeded.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
Four CG solves at a caller-supplied tol with assert!(rep.converged), where converged is rel_residual < tol on the recursive residual with no lower bound on tol. 'Exact' refers to the FORMULA (linear-in-rho structure, no FD), not to the arithmetic.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
density_misfit_hvp(problem, b, u_star, v, tol) with any tol > 1.0: CgState::run checks rel_residual() < tol at the top of the loop with x = 0 and rel_residual = 1.0, breaks immediately with zero iterations, and returns converged:true. All four solves return the zero vector, so the function returns exact zeros - a silent zero Hessian - while the doc calls it the EXACT H*v and the fail-closed assertion passes vacuously. Intermediate loose tolerances degrade continuously along the same path.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Validate the tolerance (or return the SolveReports), and describe the result as 'the exact IFT Hessian-vector FORMULA evaluated through four linear solves at tolerance tol; accuracy is bounded by the achieved solve residuals, which are returned'. A converged flag a caller's tolerance can make trivially true is not evidence.

GAP SHAPE: Vacuous guard; 'exact' asserted over an iteratively-solved quantity. CONFIDENCE LOW - reaching it needs an absurd caller tolerance; triage may downgrade or close as caller error.
CONFIDENCE: LOW

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). Judged a real defect rather than caller error: tol is caller-controlled, unvalidated, and converged is decided against it, so any tol >= 1 makes the fail-closed assert pass at zero iterations and publishes four zero solves as an EXACT H*v. Now asserts 0 < tol < 1 and the doc says 'the exact IFT FORMULA evaluated through four iterative solves at tolerance tol'.

title: fs-solver: CONTRACT says the transposed-solve battery catches defaulted-transpose violations; it cannot catch client operators
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs-solver CONTRACT.md LinearOp bullet, consumed by the fs-adjoint CONTRACT's 'honesty check' language
FILE: crates/fs-solver/CONTRACT.md:20-22; code at crates/fs-solver/src/op.rs:18-20

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
A reader is told the defaulted-transpose hazard is COVERED: if an operator's apply_transpose is wrong, the transposed-solve battery will catch it, so a converged transposed solve can be trusted as an adjoint solve.

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
The battery exercises one nonsymmetric fs-opdsl convection-diffusion fixture that DOES override apply_transpose, plus CsrOp::general which materializes a real transpose. Nothing at runtime or compile time detects a client LinearOp that inherits the default on a nonsymmetric operator; there is no symmetry probe in the crate.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
A caller implementing LinearOp for a nonsymmetric Jacobian without overriding apply_transpose (the default, and nothing warns) passes it to fs_adjoint::ift_gradient_matfree, which runs GmresState::run(.., transposed = true) (ift.rs:43). GMRES solves J*lambda = dJ/du instead of J^T*lambda = dJ/du, converges normally, and returns AdjointReport{converged:true, adjoint_residual:~1e-12} - a small residual against the WRONG operator, published by the fs-adjoint CONTRACT as 'the honesty check', together with a wrong gradient. fs-adjoint's own DensityOp is genuinely symmetric, so no in-tree fixture exercises the hazard.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
State that the crate does not verify symmetry: an implementor who inherits the default on a nonsymmetric operator gets a silently wrong transposed solve, and the resulting residual is measured against the operator the implementor supplied, not its transpose. The battery pins the crate's own adapters; it cannot cover client operators. A check_transpose-style probe is the missing executable check.

GAP SHAPE: Residual measured against the wrong operator; CONTRACT prose stronger than the code
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: Fixed in ecc-wave commit (see git log for f85xj.2.5..2.43). fs-solver CONTRACT + op.rs carry an explicit NO-CLAIM: the crate has no symmetry probe, the battery pins only its own adapters, and a defaulted apply_transpose yields a small residual against the WRONG operator (with the fs-adjoint consequence spelled out).

title: fs-thrust-e2e: the surrogate validity domain is the 2-D descriptor hull, so 63/84 served designs are off-calibration on the spacing axis
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).

title: Promotion gate: open claim-integrity P0s block capability-maturity promotion (xtask/DSR)
description:
WHY: The synthesis's immediate action #1: any bug that can emit a stronger epistemic claim than the evidence supports should BLOCK public capability promotion. Without a machine gate this is an intention, not a control. This gate is the enforcement seam between e02 and the e16 maturity registry.

WHAT: An xtask check (proposed name: check-claim-integrity) that: (a) reads the beads inventory (issues.jsonl — read-only; never mutate beads outside br) for open `claim-integrity` beads with severity P0; (b) reads the capability-maturity registry (e16) for any capability whose maturity is being PROMOTED (level increase vs the last committed registry state); (c) FAILS the check when a promotion coexists with an open P0 whose scope overlaps the promoted capability (scope = crate/label match; default to global-block when scope is ambiguous — fail closed); (d) emits JSON-lines verdicts like other xtask checks so DSR/agents can parse. Wire into check-all and the DSR quality lane.

HOW: keep the gate dependency-light and deterministic; the JSONL read must tolerate the file being mid-rewrite by another agent (read-then-validate, refuse on parse failure rather than passing silently — a gate that errors open is itself a claim-integrity defect).

DONE WHEN: check-all includes the gate; a synthetic open P0 + attempted promotion demonstrably fails DSR; removing the P0 (closing the bead) lets promotion pass.

TESTS: unit tests with fixture registries + fixture issue snapshots covering: no-P0 pass, in-scope P0 block, ambiguous-scope global block, malformed-JSONL refusal (fails CLOSED), and demotion-always-allowed; e2e drill script that runs the real gate against the live repo state and logs every considered bead + capability with verdicts.
close_reason:
Landed 25fbdcf1. xtask check-claim-integrity, wired into check-all.

(a) INVENTORY: reads .beads/issues.jsonl read-only for open claim-integrity bugs carrying severity:default-path. Program beads are excluded BY TYPE (only issue_type=bug is inventory, per docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md), so the gate cannot block on E02's own epic.
(b) PROMOTIONS: reads capability-maturity.json against its last committed state via maturity::capability_levels; only level INCREASES are weighed.
(c) BLOCKS when a promotion coexists with an in-scope defect. Scope = crate-label overlap, deliberately coarse: over-blocking costs a conversation, under-blocking costs the claim. An UNSCOPED defect blocks GLOBALLY (fail closed) because an unlocalised defect is a reason for more caution, not less.
(d) JSON-lines verdicts like every other xtask check, so DSR and agents parse rather than scrape.

FAIL-CLOSED, the design commitment that matters: an unreadable, oversized, or mid-flush issues.jsonl REFUSES rather than reporting an empty inventory. A gate that errors open is itself a claim-integrity defect, so a truncated row (another agent flushing the store mid-read) returns a structured refusal naming the line.

DEMOTIONS ARE NEVER GATED. Lowering a claim is how the registry stays honest; if that were procedurally harder than raising one, the registry would accumulate false claims by construction.

TESTS (7 unit, fixture-driven so the algebra is pinned independently of the live tree): no_defects_admits_the_promotion; an_in_scope_defect_blocks_the_promotion; an_out_of_scope_defect_does_not_block; an_unscoped_defect_blocks_globally; only_open_gating_bugs_enter_the_inventory (covers open/in_progress/closed, severity:gated, and epic/task program beads); a_truncated_row_refuses_rather_than_undercounting; demotions_and_introductions_never_reach_the_gate.

  B ADMIT  promoting numerics.sparse-assembly (crate:fs-sparse) is admitted, nothing in scope
  C DEMOTE demoting evidence.colour-algebra passes untouched
The drill mutates capability-maturity.json in place and ALWAYS puts the committed copy back via an exit trap (verified clean after every run, including the failing iterations while I was developing it).

DONE-WHEN AUDIT: 'check-all includes the gate' — yes. 'an open P0 + attempted promotion demonstrably fails' — drill A, against a real bead, not a synthetic one. title: fs-thrust-e2e: full_color mints Color::Verified drift bands from an impulse-conservation residual that bounds nothing about drift

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
The admission predicate is |I(T)-I(0)| / sum|Gamma_i| <= conserve_tol - a conservation-residual gate on the LINEAR IMPULSE. The published half-width is res.impulse_error.max(1e-9). Nothing derives an error bound on drift: it comes from fs_vpm::simulate, which is `steps` unchecked RK4 steps (crates/fs-vpm/src/lib.rs:456-467) with no step-size control, no Richardson estimate, no interval arithmetic, no outward rounding. The impulse is also a different functional: for a zero-total-circulation quadrupole, I_y = 0 identically at t=0 and the mean-x drift is not a component of I at all.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Either derive a real enclosure (interval/validated RK4, or step-doubling error estimate with outward rounding) before minting Verified, or downgrade to Color::Estimated{estimator:"vpm-full-impulse-conserving", dispersion: impulse_error} and rename the field to conservation_screened_drift_hull with the doc 'hull of drift +/- impulse-conservation residual over designs that passed the conservation screen; NOT an error bound on drift'.

title: fs-flutter-e2e: witness_color mints Verified{lo,hi} over an unnamed QoI with no outward rounding, excluding a real eigenvalue for mu>1
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity audit sweep (bead frankensim-extreal-program-f85xj.2.2).
Taxonomy and decision rules: docs/CLAIM_INTEGRITY.md

SURFACE: fs_flutter_e2e::FlutterReport::witness_color -> Color::Verified{lo,hi}; WASM export index [8] witness_verified
FILE: crates/fs-flutter-e2e/src/lib.rs:201-212, :117-121; crates/fs-wasm/src/campaigns.rs:266-268, :286-292

STRONGEST INFERENCE (what a caller may infer):
fs-evidence documents Color::Verified{lo,hi} as 'the payload IS the bound / Certified lower bound / Certified upper bound'. The struct field doc says only 'The witness's certificate color (Verified)' and never names the quantity, so a caller reads [lo,hi] as a certified enclosure of the operator's eigenvalue real parts (the source comment says exactly 'a certified negative upper bound on the eigenvalues' real parts').

CODE ESTABLISHES (what is actually proved):
lo is spectral_abscissa(mu) = -1.0 + (mu-1.0).max(0.0).sqrt(), the analytic LARGEST real part, evaluated in round-to-nearest f64 with no outward rounding; hi is the literal 0.0. (i) For mu > 1 the operator has a SECOND eigenvalue with real part -1 - sqrt(mu-1), strictly below lo, so [lo,0.0] is not an enclosure of 'the eigenvalues' real parts'. (ii) Even as an enclosure of the abscissa alone, the subsequent `-1.0 +` rounding can place the computed value up to ~1 ulp ABOVE the exact abscissa, so the 'certified lower bound' can exclude the true value.

REPRO (reachable gap instance):
fs_flutter_e2e::run_campaign(1.2, 1.9, 8) - public API used as documented, also reachable through the shipped WASM export fluttercert(1.2, 1.9, 8). Every sample is Lyapunov-stable (mu < 2), naive staggering diverges (mu >= 1), Aitken converges, so mu = 1.2 becomes the witness and witness_color = Verified{lo: -0.5527864045000421, hi: 0.0}. A(1.2)'s eigenvalue real parts are -0.5527864... and -1.4472135...; the second is outside the 'certified' interval by ~0.89. The default sweep (0.55, 2.45, 20) hides this because its witness has mu < 1, where sqrt(0) makes lo exactly -1.0 and both eigenvalues share that real part - a textbook grace-masks-the-mechanism fixture.

HONEST CLAIM (what the surface should say instead):
Name the quantity on the public surface and round outward: witness_decay_rate_color documented as 'certified enclosure of the LARGEST eigenvalue real part (the asymptotic decay rate) at witness_mu', with lo computed through an outward-rounded fs_ivl interval evaluation of -1 + sqrt(mu-1).

GAP SHAPE: Real-arithmetic theory read as an executable bound; unnamed QoI whose natural reading is falsified on a reachable input
CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM

NOTE: this bead is the INVENTORY entry, not the fix. Fixing is separate work so the gate's open-P0 count stays an accurate measure of exposure.
close_reason: COMPLETE (see the wasm/neuroshape/flutter cluster commit). witness_color renamed witness_decay_rate_color and documented as a certified enclosure of the LARGEST eigenvalue real part (the asymptotic decay rate) at witness_mu; BOTH endpoints now come from a new outward-rounded spectral_abscissa_interval rather than a round-to-nearest f64 with a literal 0.0 upper bound. hi is now the interval's upper endpoint, a narrower but fully self-backed claim that no longer leans on fs-sos's round-to-nearest 1e-9 PSD threshold. REGRESSION TESTS: the_witness_decay_rate_enclosure_is_outward_rounded_and_names_one_eigenvalue, the_decay_rate_enclosure_is_sound_across_the_branch_and_fails_open_to_no_claim, and campaigns::tests::fluttercert_witness_flag_tracks_the_named_outward_rounded_decay_rate. CORRECTION TO THE BEAD TEXT: the default sweep's witness is mu=1.05, not mu<1 — it is graceful because the nearest rounding happens to fall BELOW the exact value there; mu=1.3 is a reachable witness where it falls above. fs-flutter-e2e 6/6 green. fs-flutter-e2e gained fs-ivl (dep) and fs-math (dev-dep, the oracle); both L0/L1, deps still point downward. title: Gate hardening drills: prove the claim-integrity gate fails closed (seeded-fault e2e)
description:
WHY: A false certificate is worse than a wrong answer, and a broken GATE is worse than a missing one — it manufactures institutional confidence. The gate must be shown to fail closed under realistic corruption, concurrency, and drift scenarios, in the spirit of G4 chaos drills.

WHAT: Seeded-fault e2e drills for the promotion gate: (a) truncated/garbled issues.jsonl mid-read (simulating another agent flushing) -> gate refuses with actionable diagnostics, does NOT pass; (b) label variants/typos (claim-integrity vs claimintegrity) -> taxonomy lint catches, gate treats unknown-but-similar labels as suspicious (warn) rather than invisible; (c) registry/bead scope mismatch (P0 labeled with a crate that no longer exists) -> global fail-closed; (d) clock/order drift (promotion recorded before P0 filed in the same commit) -> still blocked; (e) performance sanity: gate completes within a bounded time on the real ~2000-issue JSONL so nobody is tempted to skip it.

DONE WHEN: all drills automated and green under DSR; each drill logs scenario, injected fault, expected verdict, actual verdict; a summary table artifact is produced deterministically.

TESTS: this bead is the G4 drill suite for e02; acceptance requires every drill to have BOTH the failing (fault present) and recovering (fault removed) assertion, with logs sufficient to diagnose which drill failed without rerunning.
close_reason:
Landed 87c4f2ee. scripts/ci/claim_integrity_gate_hardening.sh — five seeded-fault drills, ALL PASS, each asserting BOTH the fault-present and fault-removed direction (a drill that only checked the fault would pass against a gate that refuses everything, which is not a working gate either).

(a) MID-FLUSH: a torn issues.jsonl row REFUSES with a diagnostic naming the line; the intact row still blocks. (b) TYPO'D LABEL: 'claimintegrity' is invisible to blocking — that IS the hazard — so the requirement is that it be SURFACED as suspicious, not that it block; spelled correctly it blocks again. (c) STALE SCOPE: a defect scoped to a crate that no longer exists is globalized and blocks everything, while a real out-of-scope crate correctly does not block. (d) ORDER DRIFT: a P0 filed after the promotion (later in file, later created_at) still blocks — the gate reads state, not chronology — and closing it admits the promotion. (e) PERFORMANCE: 1s against a 30s budget over the real 2151-row inventory.

GATE HARDENING THIS REQUIRED: near_miss_labels() reports labels that collapse onto a canonical label without matching exactly (a typo'd class/severity label is the most dangerous failure mode, because the inventory looks clean precisely because the entry silently left it); globalize_unknown_scopes() rewrites a crate: scope naming no crate in the tree to GLOBAL and reports it, so a rename cannot quietly disarm a P0; and an FSIM_CLAIM_INTEGRITY_BEADS fixture override so faults are injected without ever writing the real .beads store. Using the override is ANNOUNCED in the verdict rows ('this verdict describes the fixture, NOT the repository') — an unannounced override on a security-critical gate would itself be a bypass, which is the exact defect class this program exists to prevent.

DETERMINISM: the summary artifact (.doctor/claim-integrity-gate-hardening.txt, gitignored as a per-run artifact) was diffed byte-identical across two consecutive runs. Drill E's measured duration is logged to stderr and deliberately kept OUT of the table, because a wall-clock number in the artifact would falsify the determinism claim printed in its own header.

TESTS: 9 gate unit tests green, 2 new — near_miss_labels_are_surfaced_rather_than_left_invisible (covers class typo, underscore, case, severity typo, and asserts an unrelated label is NOT flagged, plus that the typo'd entries are genuinely absent from the inventory) and a_scope_naming_a_missing_crate_is_globalized_not_disarmed (covers wholly-stale, mixed real+stale, and intact scopes, and asserts both globalized defects then block an unrelated capability).

SAFETY: capability-maturity.json is mutated (a promotion must be pending for the gate to weigh anything) and always put back from the committed copy by the exit trap; verified clean after every run including the failing iterations during development. The real beads store is never written.

CLOSES E02: this was the epic's last open child.

title: E03 Certified-arithmetic root audit: independent scrutiny of fs-ivl/fs-math (the trust root)
description:
WHY: Every interval certificate, exact predicate, Taylor enclosure, and outward-rounded bound in the workspace bottoms out in fs-ivl + fs-math. Today their oracles are IN-HOUSE ONLY: double-double (fs-math::dd) + error-free transforms, an i128 lattice oracle for predicates, platform-libm point checks, and TWO-ISA golden FNV hashes. That leaves COMMON AUTHORSHIP AND COMMON ASSUMPTIONS in the loop: the same project wrote the code and the oracle. A one-ULP direction error at this layer contaminates many apparently unrelated certificates downstream, and no current test would catch a shared misconception. The synthesis rates this among the four immediate actions.

WHAT (children): (1) external high-precision development oracle lane (MPFR/Arb/MPFI-class, dev-only, isolated from production deps per AGENTS.md policy); (2) exact rational/algebraic test corpus; (3) randomized containment fuzzing near subnormal/overflow/cancellation/signed-zero boundaries; (4) compiler x opt-level x ISA matrix beyond the two golden hashes; (5) directed-rounding audit of the next_up/next_down nudge strategy; (6) independent minimal certified-arithmetic kernel (diverse authorship/method); (7) mutation testing proving incorrect outward rounding is DETECTED downstream; (8) formal proofs for a few load-bearing primitives (frontier, feature-flagged).

CONSTRAINT: all external oracles are development-only comparison references — isolated, documented, never in the production dependency graph (AGENTS.md dependency policy). This is the sanctioned pattern: "Development-only references and comparison oracles are acceptable only when they are isolated."

DONE WHEN: fs-ivl CONTRACT.md can state audited claims with an INDEPENDENT oracle behind them; the audit lanes run under DSR; at least one seeded-fault mutation campaign shows downstream detection; residual unaudited surfaces are listed as explicit no-claim boundaries.

title: External high-precision dev-oracle lane for fs-ivl/fs-math (MPFR/Arb-class, dev-only isolation)
description:
WHY: fs-ivl's rigor is currently conditional on fs-math's DECLARED ulp budgets and checked only against in-house oracles (fs-math::dd double-double, EFT, i128 lattice predicates, platform libm point checks) plus two-ISA golden hashes. Same authors, same assumptions: a shared misconception (e.g. a wrong declared ulp budget, a subtly wrong nudge rule) passes every current test. An arbitrary-precision EXTERNAL oracle breaks the common-mode loop. AGENTS.md sanctions exactly this: "Development-only references and comparison oracles are acceptable only when they are isolated, documented, and not in the production dependency graph."

WHAT: (a) An isolation design decision recorded first: oracle runs as a SEPARATE dev-only comparison harness (options: a standalone non-workspace tool crate like tools/oracle with rug/MPFR or a pure-Rust arbitrary-precision implementation; or precomputed oracle TABLES generated offline and committed as frozen fixtures — zero build-time foreign deps, preferred if coverage suffices). Never a workspace runtime dep; xtask check-deps must keep passing. (b) Harness: for each fs-math elementary function (exp, expm1, ln, sin, cos, tan, atan2, erf, pow, sqrt, tanh) and each fs-ivl interval op, compare against >=200-bit references: verify DECLARED ulp budgets actually hold (not just internal consistency) and interval enclosures actually contain the true value. (c) Report artifact: per-function measured max ulp error vs declared budget, with failing inputs retained as fixtures.

DONE WHEN: the lane runs under DSR as a dev-only job; every declared ulp budget in fs-math CONTRACT.md carries "externally audited" or an explicit no-claim; discovered violations become claim-integrity beads (e02 taxonomy).

TESTS: the lane IS a test; additionally unit-test the harness's own comparison plumbing (known-answer probes where the oracle value is hand-derivable); log per-function histograms of observed ulp error and the argmax input; determinism: fixture-driven mode must be byte-stable.

title: Exact rational/algebraic test corpus for certified arithmetic (ground truth without any oracle)
description:
WHY: Arbitrary-precision oracles are still software; exact cases are not. Inputs constructed so the true result is EXACTLY representable or algebraically known (dyadic rationals through +,-,*,/; sqrt of perfect squares; polynomial roots at constructed rationals; predicate cases on integer lattices with known sign) give unconditional ground truth that catches both code and oracle errors.

WHAT: A curated corpus (committed fixtures, generated by an offline all-integer/rational script kept in-tree, in the spirit of the existing Machin bignum test that self-verifies 2/pi constants): (a) interval arithmetic: exact dyadic chains where the enclosure must be degenerate-or-1ulp; (b) Taylor models at rational expansion points of polynomials (remainder must be exactly zero); (c) Newton/Krawczyk on polynomials with constructed rational roots (certified box must contain the exact root, and refuse when no root exists); (d) exact predicates: lattice configurations spanning all orient/incircle/insphere sign classes incl. exact degeneracies (sign must be Zero, not near-zero) and the SoS ladder on constructed ties; (e) expansion arithmetic identities (Shewchuk sums exactly representable).

DONE WHEN: corpus committed with a generator script + provenance header; wired into fs-ivl conformance as a named G0 battery; failures reported with the exact rational expected value.

TESTS: this bead is a test corpus; acceptance = battery green on both reference ISAs + the corpus generator re-run reproduces byte-identical fixtures; logs list per-case expected/actual with exact rational rendering.

title: Randomized containment fuzzing near floating-point pathology boundaries (subnormal/overflow/cancellation/signed-zero)
description:
WHY: The current G0 containment law samples broadly (100k arithmetic cases vs dd oracle) but pathology lives at the boundaries: subnormal gradual underflow, overflow saturation to WHOLE/inf, catastrophic cancellation, signed-zero branch cuts, and next_up/next_down at boundary values (min-subnormal, max-finite, +/-0, powers of two where ulp changes). Outward rounding errors of exactly one direction-flip at these edges are the highest-consequence, lowest-probability-of-random-detection bugs in the trust root.

WHAT: A targeted fuzz battery: (a) structured samplers biased to boundary neighborhoods (each of: subnormal range, near-overflow, near-cancellation pairs a-b with a~b, signed zeros, ulp-boundary powers of two) for every interval op, affine op, Taylor evaluation, and elementary function; (b) containment oracle = the e03 external oracle when available, dd otherwise, with the oracle choice logged per case; (c) shrinking: on failure, bisect toward a minimal failing input and persist it as a permanent regression fixture; (d) budgeted determinism: seeds are Philox-keyed and recorded so every failure replays.

DONE WHEN: battery runs nightly-scale under DSR with a bounded time budget; at least the seeded-fault self-check (see tests) passes; all persisted minimal cases green.

TESTS: self-validation via mutation: temporarily (in-test, not in-tree) wrap an op with an off-by-one-ulp fault and assert the fuzzer FINDS it within budget for each boundary class — this proves detection power, not just absence of alarms; logs record per-class case counts, oracle used, and minimal counterexamples.

title: Compiler x opt-level x ISA determinism matrix for the trust root (beyond two golden hashes)
description:
WHY: Cross-ISA authority currently rests on golden FNV hashes recorded on exactly two machines (aarch64 M4 Pro, x86-64 Threadripper) at whatever compiler/profile happened to be current. The determinism-incident history (powi build-mode divergence, libm drift, floating-nightly clippy drift) shows build configuration is an active hazard axis. The trust root deserves a systematic matrix.

WHAT: A matrix lane for fs-math + fs-ivl conformance/golden batteries across: {aarch64-apple, x86-64} x {debug, release} x {pinned nightly, next nightly candidate} x {default, -C opt-level variations, and explicitly the codegen flags DSR release lanes use}. Record per-cell pass/fail + golden hash into a matrix artifact; any divergence is a determinism incident (playbook: stage-wise bit bisection, det:: routing doctrine). Where a cell is EXPECTED to differ (documented fast-mode), the matrix must say so rather than skipping. Use rch/DSR remote lanes for the x86 cells (Linux-only rch binaries; ts1/ts2 hosts per the perf-host policy — coordinate via serialized-build-lane protocol).

DONE WHEN: matrix runs on demand + on toolchain-bump events; the artifact is committed or ledgered with machine fingerprints; CONTRACT.md determinism classes for fs-math/fs-ivl cite the matrix instead of two ad hoc hashes.

TESTS: the matrix is the test; add unit coverage for the matrix harness itself (cell scheduling, result aggregation, divergence classification); logs per cell: toolchain hash, target, flags, golden value, verdict; a seeded divergence drill (intentionally perturbed constant in a scratch build) must be caught and classified.

title: Directed-rounding audit: prove the next_up/next_down nudge strategy at every boundary class
description:
WHY: fs-ivl deliberately avoids global FPU rounding-mode state and implements outward rounding by 1-ulp nudges via fs-math next_up/next_down. This is a sound strategy ONLY if the nudge functions are exactly correct at every boundary (subnormals, +/-0, min/max finite, inf, NaN propagation, powers of two where ulp halves/doubles) AND every op site applies the nudge in the correct direction for its monotonicity. A single wrong-direction site silently converts certificates into lies.

WHAT: (a) Exhaustive-by-class verification of next_up/next_down: for each boundary class enumerate ALL representable values in a window (and for f32-analog full-exhaustive if a helper exists) and check successor/predecessor properties against bit-level ground truth (integer increment on the ordered bit pattern). (b) Site audit: enumerate every outward-rounding call site in fs-ivl (mechanical listing, reviewed manually per AGENTS.md no-script-rewrite discipline), classify the op's monotonicity, and assert nudge direction; encode the classification as a table-driven test so new sites must register. (c) Interaction with declared ulp budgets: verify budget-based widening for elementary functions widens by AT LEAST budget ulps in both directions at boundary values.

title: Independent minimal certified-arithmetic kernel (diverse-implementation cross-check)
description:
WHY: Even with external oracles, fs-ivl's ALGORITHMS and their tests share one authorship lineage. A deliberately small, independently implemented certified kernel — different algorithmic choices where possible (e.g. rational endpoint arithmetic over num-free i128/dyadic representation, or ball arithmetic instead of interval endpoints) — provides an N-version check on the load-bearing subset. Disagreement between two independent certified implementations is a loud, cheap tripwire for shared misconceptions.

WHAT: A dev-only crate (test/oracle scope, not production) implementing the MINIMAL certified subset: interval add/sub/mul/div, sqrt, exp, ln with PROVABLY outward endpoints via a different mechanism (dyadic rational endpoint arithmetic with explicit error accounting is the suggested route — exact until rounding is applied once at the end). Scope discipline: this is a check, not a second library — keep it under ~2k lines, no features beyond the checked subset, and document that divergence-resolution authority lies with whichever implementation the exact/rational corpus (sibling bead) vindicates.

HOW: run the two implementations over the shared corpora (exact corpus, boundary fuzz corpus) and assert enclosure-compatibility: intersections non-empty and both contain the reference value; log width ratios (a systematically tighter width in one implementation is diagnostic information, not failure).

DONE WHEN: cross-check lane green under DSR; at least one historical or seeded discrepancy demonstrates the tripwire works; divergence-resolution protocol documented.

TESTS: the cross-check lane is the test; unit tests for the mini-kernel against the exact corpus; logs: per-op agreement stats, width-ratio distribution, any non-overlap case dumped with full bit patterns.

title: Mutation campaign: prove incorrect outward rounding is DETECTED downstream (end-to-end tripwire evidence)
description:
WHY: The scariest failure is not a wrong interval — it is a wrong interval that every downstream consumer happily accepts. We must demonstrate, with evidence, that a one-ulp direction error at the root is caught SOMEWHERE before it reaches a user-facing certificate: by fs-ivl's own batteries, by downstream conformance (fs-geom predicates, fs-cutfem cut classification, fs-neuroshape interval topology), or by the claim-integrity gate. If a mutation survives to a green full-workspace run, that survival is itself a P0 finding.

WHAT: A mutation campaign harness (dev-only; never commits mutated code — apply in a scratch build via rch/DSR isolated target dirs): mutation operators = flip nudge direction per op; drop nudge entirely; off-by-one ulp budget; swap lo/hi on one path; weaken a predicate filter threshold. For each mutant: run the fs-ivl battery, then the cheapest downstream conformance set that consumes intervals/predicates, record which layer killed it. Deliverable: a mutation-kill matrix (mutant x killing-layer) with survival rate; every SURVIVING mutant spawns a test-gap bead.

DONE WHEN: kill matrix artifact exists; survival rate for the defined operator set is 0 at workspace level (or each survivor has a filed gap bead + fix); campaign is rerunnable with one command.

TESTS: harness unit tests (mutant application/reversion integrity — the tree must be bit-identical after the campaign; verify via git status + hash); logs: per-mutant lifecycle (applied -> lanes run -> killed-by/survived) with timings; the final matrix rendered as a deterministic table artifact.

title: Formal proofs for selected load-bearing primitives (frontier, feature-flagged)
description:
WHY: For a small set of primitives where tractable, machine-checked proof is the strongest evidence class available and closes the authorship loop entirely. Candidates in ascending ambition: (1) next_up/next_down successor correctness over the ordered-bit-pattern model; (2) outward-rounded interval add/mul containment given correctly-rounded base ops; (3) the orient2d filter constant derivation (Shewchuk-style error bound); (4) Sterbenz/EFT lemmas used by the expansion arithmetic. This is [F] frontier work: valuable, not on the product critical path, and must respect the e16 moonshot budget discipline.

WHAT: (a) choose the proof vehicle (Lean4 with mathlib flavors of IEEE-754 formalization, or a small bespoke bit-level model proved from first principles — record the decision and its trust assumptions: the proof binds the MODEL, and a slim conformance battery must bind model-to-code); (b) prove primitives (1) and (2) minimum; (3)/(4) stretch; (c) the model-binding tests: exhaustive f32-scale + boundary-class f64 checks that the Rust code agrees with the formal model's extracted/stated behavior; (d) CI: proofs re-checked in a dev-only lane (proof toolchain never enters the production dep graph).

DONE WHEN: proofs check in CI; fs-ivl CONTRACT.md cites them with an honest statement of the model-to-code gap; residual unproven surface listed as no-claim.

TESTS: proof re-check lane + model-binding battery with per-class logs; a deliberate model-divergence drill (perturb a binding test constant) must fail loudly.

title: E04 External V&V corpus for the thermal vertical (evidence portfolio A-E, retained raw data)
description:
WHY: The internal Gauntlet (G0-G5) is necessary but insufficient: it was generated by the SAME code, assumptions, and authors as the predictions it tests. Real-world accuracy requires evidence that is external and independent. Cross-solver comparisons catch independent-implementation and BC-interpretation errors; experiments catch model-form error; blind cases catch calibration leakage; none of these can be replaced by more internal tests. This epic builds a versioned verification-and-validation corpus for the thermal vertical (NOT a "truth corpus" — independent solvers are not truth and experiments have uncertainty).

EVIDENCE LEVELS (portfolio, not a strict pyramid — authority depends on claim and context, uncontrolled field data can be WEAKER than a good lab experiment): A analytic/exact/manufactured solutions; B mesh/time-step convergence + independent numerical implementations (cross-code); C published canonical experiments with retained raw data and uncertainties; D blind held-out experiments selected BEFORE calibration; E field/production data. Independent axes: numerical verification, cross-code agreement, controlled experiment, blind prediction, field monitoring, transferability, independent reproduction.

WHAT (children): corpus schema + retention policy (extends fs-vvreg, bead f1gq lineage); Level A analytic+MMS battery; Level B cross-code frozen references (deal.II/FEniCSx/CalculiX/SU2/OpenFOAM-class, imported as dev-only frozen data — does NOT violate the Franken-only runtime policy); Level C published electronics-thermal experiments; Level D blind protocol with preregistration; Level E instrumented in-house hardware; adversarial case set (recirculation, contact-resistance dominance, radiation dominance, fan stall, vent leakage, material variability); public scorecard (prediction error, empirical coverage, false-acceptance rate, regime limitations — NOT pass/fail counts); portfolio doctrine document.

RETENTION REQUIREMENTS for every dataset: raw sensor data; calibration certificates + dates; sensor placement uncertainty; geometry + as-built measurements; environmental conditions; training/calibration/validation partition; measurement covariance or bounded uncertainty; complete preprocessing lineage; context-of-use limits.

DONE WHEN: >=3 external experimental datasets admitted with full retention metadata; >=1 blind case preregistered; scorecard generated deterministically from corpus + runs; built-in references remain Estimated unless admitted through an external verifier.

RELATED EXISTING BEADS (extend, do not duplicate): f1gq (fs-vvreg registry, closed), 6nb.3 (G2 canonical benchmark registry, in_progress), x68z (ContextOfUse->PredictionAssessment schemas, closed), pooz (materials/V&V registry epic, open), 5kv0 (TEAM decks, open).

title: V&V corpus schema + retention policy (extend fs-vvreg): datasets as evidence-bearing artifacts
description:
WHY: A validation dataset without calibration certificates, sensor uncertainty, partitions, and preprocessing lineage cannot support a Validated color — it is just numbers. The corpus schema is the load-bearing decision of the whole e04 epic: everything downstream (coverage checks, blind protocol, scorecard) consumes it. fs-vvreg (bead f1gq lineage: pinned decks, licenses, acceptance envelopes) is the substrate to EXTEND, not replace.

WHAT: Versioned dataset schema with mandatory fields: raw sensor data (content-addressed, never post-processed-only); calibration certificates + dates per sensor; sensor placement + placement uncertainty; geometry incl. as-built measurements where available; environmental conditions; declared training/calibration/validation PARTITION (typed, checked — feeds e07 partition enforcement); measurement covariance or bounded uncertainty (typed per fs-qty dims); complete preprocessing lineage (every transform recorded); context-of-use limits; license + redistribution terms; provenance (who measured, instrument identity). Datasets carry evidence colors themselves: a dataset with unstated uncertainty admits only Estimated use. Include an ACCEPTANCE-ENVELOPE record type (metric, envelope, regime) and an evidence-level tag from the portfolio doctrine (A analytic / B cross-code / C published experiment / D blind / E field).

HOW: keep the corpus in data/ with content-addressed payloads + a registry crate API returning Evidence-wrapped queries (out-of-partition or out-of-context access REFUSES, mirroring fs-matdb's OutOfDomain pattern).

DONE WHEN: schema documented + implemented; at least one existing fixture (fs-benchmark CHT query set or an fs-vvreg deck) migrated as a worked example; refusal paths proven.

TESTS: unit tests for every mandatory-field refusal (each missing field -> typed error naming the field); partition-access refusal tests; round-trip serialization; an e2e registry-audit script that walks the corpus, validates every dataset against the schema, and prints a per-dataset field-completeness table with warn-level logs for optional gaps.

title: Level B: cross-code frozen references (independent solver results as dev-only fixtures)
description:
WHY: Cross-solver comparison is not physical validation, but it is a powerful INDEPENDENT-IMPLEMENTATION check: it catches our own numerical bugs, wrong BC interpretation, and geometry/units semantics errors that internal tests share blind spots on. Importing FROZEN RESULTS from deal.II/FEniCSx/CalculiX/Elmer/SU2/OpenFOAM-class codes as committed test DATA does not violate the Franken-only runtime policy (they never enter the dependency graph; AGENTS.md dev-only oracle clause).

WHAT: (a) A reproducibility contract for each imported reference: the exact external-solver version, input deck (committed), mesh, solver settings, and extraction script are retained so the number is re-derivable by anyone with that solver — a frozen reference without its deck is folklore; (b) initial set matched to the vertical: steady conduction on a multi-material block (CalculiX/Elmer class), plate-fin heatsink conduction+convective-BC case, a channel-flow forced-convection case at correlation-comparable conditions (OpenFOAM/SU2 class), one natural-convection cavity (benchmarkable against fs-lbm thermal too); (c) each registered as Level-B corpus datasets with declared agreement envelopes (these are Estimated-color references — two codes agreeing is not truth); (d) disagreement protocol: a mismatch beyond envelope opens an investigation bead, never a silent envelope widening (golden-bump discipline applies).

DONE WHEN: >=4 cross-code references admitted with full decks; comparison lane green or discrepancies filed; envelope-widening requires a justified corpus version bump.

TESTS: registry-schema conformance for each entry; comparison harness unit tests (interpolation-to-probe-points correctness on synthetic fields); e2e lane logs per-case: reference identity, our value, delta, envelope, verdict; determinism of the comparison artifact.

description:
WHY: Owned hardware removes the two chronic blockers of published data — missing raw data and unlicensable detail — and enables the design-build-measure-update loop (e12) and future blind cases at will. title: Adversarial validation case set: regimes chosen to break the models, not flatter them
description:
WHY: A validation corpus assembled from convenient cases overstates capability precisely where users get hurt. The corpus must deliberately include regimes where the cheap models are EXPECTED to struggle, so that validity domains and discrepancy bands are honest at their edges and the fidelity graph (e10) has informative failure data.

WHAT: Curate/construct adversarial cases for the thermal vertical, each registered with WHY it is adversarial and WHICH model assumption it attacks: recirculation zones behind obstructions (attacks correlation-rung's attached-flow assumption); contact-resistance-dominated stacks (attacks any zero/known-resistance default; ties to e17 no-silent-defaults); radiation-dominated low-flow cases (attacks convection-only truncation); fan-stall and unstable operating-point cases (attacks fan-curve intersection logic); uncertain vent leakage (attacks BC certainty; pairs with the rig's blockable vents); strong material-property variability lots (attacks single-value material cards; exercises fs-matdb uncertainty models); high-Biot vs low-Biot extremes (attacks lumped assumptions). Each case gets acceptance criteria phrased as HONESTY checks: the system must either predict within envelope OR refuse/demote with the correct dominant-uncertainty attribution — a confident wrong answer fails; a correctly-attributed refusal passes.

DONE WHEN: >=6 adversarial cases registered (mix of analytic, cross-code, experimental, rig-based); wired into the scorecard's regime-limitation section.

TESTS: per-case honesty assertions as above (this is the distinctive part: PASS includes justified refusal); e2e lane logs per-case: regime, attacked assumption, prediction/refusal, attribution, verdict; the false-acceptance counter feeds the e16 metrics dashboard.

title: Evidence-portfolio doctrine: independent axes, not a strict pyramid (written + encoded)
description:
WHY: A naive V&V "pyramid" implies field data always outranks lab data and blind cases outrank everything. False: uncontrolled field observations can be LESS informative than a designed lab experiment (unknown operating conditions, sensor health, latent confounders). Authority depends on the claim and context. Without this doctrine, the scorecard and evidence colors will encode a wrong hierarchy.

WHAT: (a) A doctrine document defining external evidence as a PORTFOLIO with independent axes: numerical verification; cross-code agreement; controlled experimental validation; blind predictive validation; field monitoring; transferability across regimes; independent reproduction. For each axis: what it can and cannot support, and canonical failure modes (e.g. cross-code agreement's common-mode risk under a Franken-only ecosystem; field data confounding). (b) Encoding: the corpus evidence-level tags (A-E) become AXIS COORDINATES, not ranks; the scorecard aggregates per-axis rather than taking a max; claim admission rules state which axes a given claim class REQUIRES (e.g. Validated color for a QoI in a regime requires controlled-experiment coverage of that regime; field data alone cannot mint it without condition provenance). (c) Explicit anti-laundering rule restated for datasets: composing weak-axis evidence cannot upgrade color, mirroring fs-evidence composition.

DONE WHEN: doctrine merged into docs/ + referenced by fs-vvreg/fs-evidence CONTRACTs; scorecard consumes axis coordinates; one worked example shows a field dataset correctly REFUSED as sole support for Validated.

TESTS: unit tests on admission rules (each axis-requirement violation -> typed refusal naming the missing axis); doctrine-presence lint; e2e: scorecard run logs the per-axis aggregation for every QoI so reviewers see exactly which axis is thin.

title: Level D: blind held-out protocol with preregistration (selected before calibration, enforced by type)
description:
WHY: Calibrated models flatter themselves on data they have seen. A BLIND case — selected and sealed before model calibration — is the only cheap way to measure real predictive power. The protocol must be mechanical, because good intentions do not survive deadline pressure.

WHAT: (a) Preregistration record type in the corpus: declares the blind case (geometry, conditions, QoIs, acceptance envelope, evaluation date), content-addressed and SEALED (hash committed; payload access refused until unseal) before any calibration run that could touch it; (b) unseal ceremony: unsealing records who/when/why into the ledger; post-unseal, the dataset is PERMANENTLY marked spent-for-blind-use (it may become an ordinary validation set, never blind again); (c) the type system must make it impossible for a sealed dataset to appear in a calibration partition (partition enforcement from e07 consumes this); (d) at least ONE preregistered blind case created for the vertical (an enclosure or board design, plausibly from the Level-E instrumented hardware or a withheld Level-C dataset), with the seal recorded.

DONE WHEN: protocol implemented + documented; one real blind case sealed; the e07 blind-execution bead can proceed entirely on this machinery.

TESTS: unit tests: sealed-access refusal; double-unseal refusal; spent-flag permanence; calibration-partition exclusion of sealed sets; ledger receipt on unseal; e2e drill script that walks the full lifecycle (seal -> attempt cheating access (must refuse, logged) -> unseal -> evaluate -> spent) with verbose state logging at each transition.
