title: E05 Thermal vertical physics kernels: conduction FEM, correlations, contact, radiation, fans, conjugate coupling
description:
WHY: The declared CHT wedge currently has NO assembled physics. Verified inventory 2026-07-20: fs-ladder::cht() supplies rung names (correlation-Nu cost 1.0 -> RANS cost 40 -> LES cost 2000) with a Refine1d 1-D placeholder transfer and explicitly does not run solves; thermal capability elsewhere = fs-lbm Boussinesq thermal LBM (natural convection only), fs-adjoint transient heat-equation adjoint, fs-couple thermal port schemas, fs-matdb property storage, fs-scenario thermal BC rows (K, W/m^2, W/m^2K). Missing entirely: assembled steady conduction FEM on solids, forced-convection Nusselt correlation library, thermal interface/contact resistance, surface radiation, fan curves + flow network, PCB anisotropic effective conductivity, conjugate solid<->fluid coupling, and thermal QoI extraction. This epic builds exactly those, at correlation/low-fidelity rungs FIRST (the honest, calibratable rungs), because both candidate thermal verticals (full CHT and thermal-design-assurance) need them.

DOCTRINE: every kernel lands with a ModelCard (assumptions, validity domain, discrepancy band, calibration provenance), evidence colors that stay Estimated until anchored (no laundering), G0/G1 Gauntlet tests (MMS via fs-mms where applicable), determinism class in CONTRACT.md, cancellation via Cx at tile boundaries, and Franken-only runtime deps. Fidelity is NOT a scalar: a validated correlation can outrank an unvalidated RANS for a given QoI (see epic e10 fidelity graph).

CHILDREN: steady conduction FEM (FEEC-based, anisotropic k(T)); forced-convection correlation rung; thermal interface/contact resistance; surface-to-ambient + gray-diffuse enclosure radiation; fan curve + flow-network model; PCB layer homogenization; conjugate coupling through fs-couple ports (real CHT ladder transfers replacing Refine1d); low-Re forced-convection RANS rung (gated on wedge ratification); volumetric/surface heat sources + transient staging; QoI extraction (max junction temperature, pressure drop, fan power, temperature uniformity, thermal margin) with evidence.

DONE WHEN: an enclosure/PCB/heatsink/fan fixture solves end-to-end at correlation fidelity with evidence-colored QoIs, G1 convergence orders demonstrated for conduction, and fs-wedge KernelMaturity justification matches the code.

title: Steady conduction FEM solver on solids (FEEC-based, anisotropic k(T), typed thermal scenario BCs)
description:
WHY: Conduction is the backbone of BOTH candidate thermal verticals and is entirely absent as an assembled solver (verified: fs-feec "conduction" is electrical; the only heat PDE code is fs-adjoint's 1-D-style transient adjoint scaffold and fs-lbm's fluid-side thermal LBM). Every downstream capability (contact resistance, conjugate coupling, QoIs, calibration) consumes this solver. It is deliberately the FIRST physics bead.

WHAT: A steady heat-conduction solve over tet/hex complexes: weak-form assembly on fs-feec spaces (0-forms for T, fluxes recoverable), anisotropic and temperature-dependent conductivity tensors k(T) from fs-matdb cards (query receipts retained — property provenance travels with the solve), volumetric heat sources, BC families from fs-scenario's existing thermal rows: Dirichlet T (K), Neumann flux (W/m^2), Robin/convective (W/m^2K with declared T_ref) — the Robin row is the seam the e05 correlation rung plugs into. Nonlinearity (k(T)) via Newton or fixed-point with a declared globalization and stop rule; linear solves through fs-solver (CG/MINRES; matrix-free where practical, deterministic assembly via fs-sparse). Cancellation-correct under Cx at assembly-tile and Newton-iteration boundaries; resumable snapshots via the versioned solver-state envelope.

CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS: determinism class stated (target: bitwise same-ISA); error model (residual norms + DWR hook for goal-oriented estimates targeting QoIs, not generic field accuracy); no-claim boundaries (steady-only; no radiation/convection physics inside this crate — those couple in).

DONE WHEN: G1 MMS convergence orders verified via fs-mms OrderGate (Level-A battery from e04); analytic slab/cylinder/fin cases within envelopes; adjoint consistency wired for at least the linear case (fs-adjoint IFT path); CONTRACT.md + model card complete.

TESTS: unit (assembly symmetry/SPD-ness where applicable, BC application, matdb receipt retention, deterministic assembly across thread counts); G1 MMS ladder with order-fit logs; G4 cancellation drills (cancel during assembly and mid-Newton -> drained, structured error); G5 golden replay on the reference fixture; e2e: enclosure-block fixture solved twice bit-identically with full per-stage logging (assembly time, solver iterations, residuals, energy balance closure).
close_reason:
Landed as crate fs-conduction (L3/FLUX), single authorised line added to the root Cargo.toml members array. 36 tests green.

BUILT: P1 weak form on fs-feec 0-forms with flux recovery; anisotropic (SPD-checked) and temperature-dependent k(T) conductivity from fs-matdb cards with QUERY RECEIPTS RETAINED per grid point and replayed via verify_receipt, so property provenance travels with the solve and a declared constant is marked ProvenanceClass rather than impersonating matdb provenance; volumetric sources; Dirichlet/Neumann/Robin lowered from fs-scenario's existing thermal rows; Newton+Armijo and damped Picard with declared globalization, stop rule and a material-admissibility guard; fs-solver linear solves whose typed ResidualClaim is carried verbatim and whose Euclidean residual is RECOMPUTED and gated on; deterministic fs-sparse assembly; Cx cancellation at assembly-tile (512) and Newton-iteration boundaries with a drill asserting state is UNCHANGED after a mid-iteration cancel; resumable versioned snapshots (TYPE_ID 0xf5c0_4d75_c710_0001) with a tamper-refusal test.

ROBIN SEAM (what E05's correlation rung plugs into): fs-scenario's Robin row carries h only and BoundaryCondition has no T_ref field, so from_scenario_row REQUIRES T_ref be named at the lowering call, defaulting to Environment::ambient_temperature as an explicit declaration rather than inventing a field. A correlation supplies h; the reference temperature stays a property of the row.

MMS (fs-mms OrderGate, grids n=4,6,8,10): isotropic-dirichlet L2 2.0087 / H1 0.9879, anisotropic 2.0065, mixed-neumann 2.000000, robin 2.000000, nonlinear-kt 2.0014 — all inside the 0.2 gate. THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDING OF THIS BEAD: the first ladders used quadratic manufactured solutions, fitted a perfect order 2 with rms ~1e-11, and produced BIT-IDENTICAL errors for isotropic and anisotropic K. Cause: P1 Galerkin on these Kuhn meshes reproduces exact solutions up to CUBIC at the nodes, so such a ladder measures interpolation error and is independent of k entirely. The Dirichlet ladders moved to a quartic solution and the reproduction fact is now pinned by its own test (polynomial_reproduction_at_the_nodes: quadratic 1.9e-12, cubic 1.4e-12, quartic 2.4e-2) so the degeneracy is recorded rather than mistaken for strength. Error norms use a Duffy-transformed 6x6x6 Gauss-Legendre rule exact to degree 9, because a degree-3 rule would carry an O(1) relative error on an O(h^4) integral.

ANALYTIC: slab-dirichlet (nodal 3.06e-11, Q 4499.999999999907 vs 4500), slab-with-source, slab-dirichlet-robin, cylindrical-shell (L2 0.5588 -> 0.1478, ratio 3.782 ~ h^2; conductance 0.35%), straight-fin (Bi 1.25e-4, Q_3d 2.50879 vs Q_1d 2.50883 W). Each envelope states what KIND of agreement it claims; the cylinder's looser conductance envelope is geometry-dominated (polygonal annulus sagitta) and was set after measuring the cause.

ADJOINT: ConductivityDesign through fs_adjoint::ift_gradient_matfree (one transposed solve, never a differentiated Krylov iteration); params=162 free_dofs=48 adjoint_res=8.46e-15 max_rel_err=1.01e-6 informative=5/5 vs central differences. It establishes mutual consistency of assembled dR/dT, pullback and primal solve; it establishes NOTHING about the nonlinear case (ConductivityDesign::new REFUSES a temperature-dependent material rather than silently linearizing), nothing about shape/mesh sensitivity, and nothing goal-oriented — a verified gradient is not a DWR estimate.

CONTRACT.md (all ten sections) + MODEL_CARD.md complete. Determinism: bitwise same-ISA, with reasons enumerated (pure assembly from staged triplets, canonical traversal independent of tile size, fixed-shape reductions, x0=0, no RNG, no platform transcendental — only IEEE sqrt and fs_math::det). Cross-ISA is a G5 audit away and is NOT claimed.

PROMOTION: capability thermal.conduction-solve promoted L1 -> L2 at e5c8061f, admitted by the claim-integrity gate (no severity:default-path defect in scope for fs-conduction/fs-feec/fs-solid). L2 is earned by independent oracles, not a golden.

NOT REACHED, named rather than glossed: matrix-free operator (assembled-CSR only; a second element-loop apply would not be bit-identical to the deterministic assembly, so shipping both meant two determinism claims or one untested path); G5 registered golden (needs a golden-couplings.json row, outside the implementing boundary — determinism evidence is self-consistency replay, which CONTRACT labels as weaker); thread-count assembly invariance (assembly is single-threaded, so the test would be vacuous; CONTRACT records what a parallel version must preserve).

title: Thermal QoI extraction with evidence: T_junction max, pressure drop, fan power, uniformity, thermal margin
description:
WHY: The product's supported quantities of interest are the contract with the user: maximum junction temperature, pressure drop, fan power, temperature uniformity, and thermal margin against requirements. Each must be extracted deterministically WITH evidence (numerical + model + statistical slices populated), because these are the values the error-budget doctrine (e08), the scorecard (e04), and DecisionAssessment (e08) operate on. A QoI without evidence is a naked scalar — the exact failure the project exists to prevent.

WHAT: (a) QoI definitions as typed, goal-oriented functionals: max-T over declared component regions (with the max taken deterministically and its mesh-sensitivity flagged via DWR hooks from E05_1 — a max functional is rough, note the estimator caveat honestly); area-weighted mean and uniformity metrics (max spread, std) over declared surfaces; pressure drop and fan operating-point power from E05_5 records; thermal margin = requirement minus predicted-with-uncertainty (interfaces with e17 requirement objects; margin carries the FULL budget, not the point estimate); (b) each QoI returns Evidence<Qty> with units, the 3-term (later 8-term, e08) breakdown, validity intersection of every model card consumed en route, and provenance/replay references; (c) report/CLI surfaces consume ONLY these records (no ad hoc scalar paths — lint-checked).

DONE WHEN: all five QoI families extract with evidence on the reference fixture; validity intersection demonstrably narrows when any upstream card narrows; margin QoI refuses when the requirement is absent (no default requirement).

TESTS: unit per QoI (analytic fixtures with known extrema/means; determinism of max tie-breaking; unit typing); property (monotonicity: widening any input uncertainty cannot shrink QoI uncertainty — anti-laundering at QoI level); e2e: reference run logging every QoI with its full evidence tree rendered, plus the lint proving no naked-scalar path exists from solver to report.

title: Forced-convection correlation rung: Nusselt correlation library with validity domains + model cards
description:
WHY: The correlation rung is the honest low-cost fidelity level the wedge's cycle-time claim rests on, and it is absent (fs-ladder cht() names the rung; nothing implements it). Correlations are ideal FrankenSim citizens: published closed forms with EXPLICIT validity ranges (Re/Pr/geometry) and stated accuracy bands — i.e., model cards are not an afterthought, they are the correlation's published fine print made machine-readable.

WHAT: A correlation library where every entry carries: the closed form; its validity domain as an fs-evidence ValidityDomain over named dimensionless groups (Re, Pr, aspect ratios — fs-regime pi machinery for group construction); the published uncertainty band (typically +/-10-25%) as the discrepancy band; and source provenance (paper/handbook, edition). Initial set targeted at electronics cooling: internal duct/channel laminar (Nu=3.66/4.36 limits, Shah-London developing flow), turbulent duct (Dittus-Boelter, Gnielinski), flat plate laminar/turbulent, plate-fin and pin-fin heatsink arrays, impinging-jet basics [stretch], natural-convection plates/enclosures (Churchill-Chu class) for fan-off cases. Evaluation REFUSES outside the validity domain (fs-matdb OutOfDomain pattern) or returns demoted evidence per e08 policy — never silent extrapolation. Output = heat-transfer coefficients feeding the conduction solver's Robin BCs, with the correlation's model evidence attached to the resulting h.

DONE WHEN: >=8 correlations admitted with cards + domains + sources; Level-A limiting-behavior checks pass (constant-Nu duct limits); the h -> Robin BC seam works against E05_1 on the heatsink fixture; no unitless h anywhere (fs-qty typed W/m^2K, e17 doctrine).

TESTS: unit per correlation (published table spot values within band; domain-edge refusals; dimensional typing); metamorphic (unit-rescaling invariance of dimensionless evaluation); property test that NO evaluation path returns h without model evidence attached; e2e: heatsink fixture at three flow rates logging Re/Pr, chosen correlation, h field, validity verdicts, and the resulting T solve summary.
notes: Implemented and landed as commit 61ac6613: new L3 fs-convection with 11 source-identified analytic/empirical Nusselt cards; shared ValidityDomain checks over named groups; structured missing/non-finite/out-of-range refusals; deterministic fs-math evaluation; typed Evidence<HeatTransferCoefficient>; and an evidence-paired fs-conduction Robin adapter. Tests cover 3.66/4.36 and rectangular ideal limits, one frozen formula-output spot per nonconstant card, inclusive domain edges and Pe product constraints, G3 coherent-unit rescaling, typed evidence/non-certification, dimensional refusals, and a three-flow-rate deterministic conduction seam. Exact focused lane passed remotely: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --no-self-healing -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${RCH_TARGET_BASE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/rch_target_frankensim_test" cargo test -p fs-convection --all-targets (10 passed, 0 failed; worker vmi1227854). Scoped missing-crate-doc warnings were then fixed; rustfmt --check, git diff --check, exact tracked doc-inventory comparison, and UBS format/clippy/check/test-build all passed. README and CHANGELOG now report the live 137-native/138-total-crate, 138-contract, 519-integration-test reality and explicitly assign fs-convection no maturity level. Proof caveat: shared HEAD moved from e5c8061f while the working-tree lane ran to d4c6a5b8 after concurrent commits, so this is scoped byte-level working-tree evidence, not a same-HEAD repository gate. REMAINS OPEN: v1 empirical bands are labeled engineering allowances, not retained source-published uncertainty; the repo lacks licensed source-table fixtures/cross-code data, interrupted/louver/offset-fin and pin-array interference cards, selection/blending, and experimental validation. Frozen formula outputs are not independent published-table comparisons, so the TESTS wording is not fully satisfied and no closure/L3/L4 claim is made.

title: Thermal interface/contact resistance model (TIM cards, series networks, never-zero-by-default)
description:
WHY: In real electronics stacks, interface resistance frequently DOMINATES the temperature budget; assuming perfect contact is one of the classic silent-wrong-answer defaults the e17 doctrine bans ("no implicit zero contact resistance"). fs-matdb already has InterfaceSystemCard machinery; what is missing is the physics binding into the conduction solve and the refusal semantics.

WHAT: (a) Interface-resistance model: per-interface thermal resistance R''_th (m^2K/W) from fs-matdb interface cards (TIM datasheets with uncertainty; dry-contact correlations as Estimated entries), applied as internal Robin-jump conditions in the E05_1 solve (temperature discontinuity across the interface proportional to flux); (b) series-network utilities for stack-level resistance budgets (die->TIM1->spreader->TIM2->heatsink) with uncertainty propagation across the series sum; (c) scenario binding: e17's interface objects declare WHICH matdb interface card applies; an interface with NO declared card is a validation ERROR, not zero resistance (fail-closed default); (d) adversarial-regime hooks: contact-resistance-dominated corpus cases (e04) exercise dominance attribution — the error-budget must show interface uncertainty as dominant when it is.

DONE WHEN: interface jumps solve correctly (analytic two-slab-with-interface case exact); undeclared-interface refusal proven; uncertainty from interface cards propagates into QoI budgets; corpus contact-dominated case attributes correctly.

TESTS: unit (jump-condition assembly vs analytic two-slab; card-provenance retention; refusal on undeclared interface with actionable message naming the interface); property (series-sum commutativity/associativity, uncertainty monotonicity); e2e stack fixture logging per-interface R'', flux, delta-T, and the resulting budget attribution table.

title: Surface radiation: linearized surface-to-ambient + gray-diffuse enclosure exchange
description:
WHY: At low flow rates and in sealed enclosures, radiation carries a large share of heat (the adversarial radiation-dominated cases exist precisely because convection-only models fail there). Omitting radiation is textbook omitted-physics model-form error — exactly accuracy-hierarchy level 4.

WHAT: Two rungs, each with model cards: (a) linearized surface-to-ambient radiation h_rad = 4*eps*sigma*T_m^3 folded into Robin coefficients (valid for small delta-T; validity domain encodes the linearization bound and the model card carries the linearization error as discrepancy); (b) gray-diffuse enclosure exchange: view-factor computation for the enclosure fixture geometry (closed-form factors for the standard configurations first; Monte Carlo/QMC view factors via fs-rand as the general path with sampling-error evidence), radiosity system solve coupled to the conduction solver's surface temperatures (outer fixed-point with declared convergence criterion). Emissivities from fs-matdb with uncertainty (emissivity is notoriously uncertain — the card must say so; surface-finish state matters, tying to materials-as-manufactured-states in e17). Nonlinearity handled by the same globalization discipline as k(T).

DONE WHEN: closed-form view-factor cases exact; radiosity solve passes an analytic two-surface enclosure; linearized-vs-full discrepancy measured on the fixture and recorded as the linearized rung's discrepancy evidence (a real e10 fidelity-graph edge); energy balance closes (radiative + convective + conducted = source) within stated tolerance.

TESTS: unit (view-factor reciprocity A_i F_ij = A_j F_ji and summation-to-one properties as G0 laws; QMC view-factor convergence with seeded determinism); analytic enclosure battery; e2e radiation-dominated fixture logging per-surface radiosity, view-factor row sums, energy-balance closure, and rung-discrepancy measurement.
notes: Code-first checkpoint implemented in fs-conduction: material-card-backed hemispherical-total emissivity with exact receipt and uncertainty; validity-bounded linearized surface-to-ambient Robin row with measured full-T4 discrepancy; admitted analytic/external-QMC view-factor matrices with explicit seed/sample/generator metadata, row closure, reciprocity, and stable identity; deterministic gray-diffuse radiosity; mesh-bound P1 radiation surfaces; and budgeted outer fixed-point coupling through uniform frozen fluxes on explicit adiabatic remainder faces. Level-A thermal-a-parallel-plate-view-factor now has an executing test-time binding, raising aggregate coverage to 15/19. Stable remote proof at b3b5f2c1c809eec06cde1e40cbc916d6995469b5: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --no-self-healing -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR=RCH_TARGET_BASE/rch_target_frankensim_test cargo test --locked -p fs-conduction --all-targets; 53/53 passed on vmi1149989, 632.1s total. README, CONTRACT, MODEL_CARD, and additive CHANGELOG now state the exact scope. Bead deliberately remains IN_PROGRESS: no internal geometry/QMC ray generator or convergence/error evidence, no radiation-dominated retained e2e corpus fixture, no participating-media/spectral/specular/spatially varying surface model, no nonlinear uncertainty certificate, no radiation adjoint, and no retained registry/L4 authority.

title: Fan curve + flow network model: operating-point solve for enclosure airflow (P-Q curves, vents, leakage)
description:
WHY: The correlation rung needs velocities/flow rates; in electronics enclosures those come from fan pressure-flow curves intersected with system resistance — a lumped flow-network problem, not CFD. This is the cheapest credible airflow model and a hard prerequisite for any forced-convection prediction. Fan stall and vent leakage are first-class UNCERTAINTY sources here (both are e04 adversarial regimes).

WHAT: (a) Fan model: P-Q curve as typed data (fs-qty Pa vs m^3/s) with manufacturer-tolerance uncertainty band and validity (operating-range) domain; affinity-law scaling for RPM with its own validity note; stall region explicitly marked NON-ADMISSIBLE (operating points in stall REFUSE with diagnostics, not extrapolate); (b) system resistance: series/parallel network of loss elements (vents, filters, heatsink channels, sudden expansions) with loss coefficients from correlations carrying uncertainty; vent leakage as an EXPLICIT uncertain element (never implicit); (c) operating-point solve: deterministic robust intersection of fan curve and system curve (bracketed root via fs-ivl newton machinery — a certified bracket is cheap here and eliminates a wrong-root class), multi-fan series/parallel composition; (d) output: per-branch flow rates + velocities feeding E05_2 correlations, with the full uncertainty (fan tolerance + loss-coefficient + leakage) attached for e08 budget propagation.

DONE WHEN: operating points certified-bracketed on the reference fan+enclosure; stall refusal proven; leakage uncertainty propagates to QoI budgets; network solve deterministic across thread counts.

TESTS: unit (curve interpolation typed + monotone-segment validation; network assembly laws — series/parallel composition identities as G0; stall refusal); certified-bracket property test (root enclosure contains sign change); e2e: enclosure network at three fan speeds logging curves, intersection brackets, per-branch flows, leakage sensitivity, and the handoff record to the correlation rung.
notes: Implemented the code-first fs-airflow rung: typed monotone P-Q curves; explicit tolerance authority, speed domain, and stall refusal; identical series/parallel fan laws; recursive quadratic series/parallel loss networks with mandatory explicit leakage; deterministic interval-Newton nominal-root certificate; Estimate-only physical bands and branch flows; typed velocity/Reynolds handoff to fs-convection; and complete semantic provenance binding curve/source/tolerance/bank/network/leakage identity. Exact proof: RCH_REQUIRE_REMOTE=1 rch exec --no-self-healing -- env CARGO_TARGET_DIR="${RCH_TARGET_BASE:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/rch_target_frankensim_test" cargo test -p fs-airflow --all-targets => PASS, 9 passed, 0 failed on ovh-a (job j-29943194691043331, 2026-07-22 21:02:39Z); fs-airflow warning-clean, with only pre-existing dependency warnings. rustfmt --check, git diff --check, jq inventory parse passed; ubs found 0 critical issues. README reality now says 138 native/139 total crates, 139 contracts, 520 integration-test files, L3=27 and states the no-claim boundary. CHANGELOG has additive validation, convection, and airflow entries. KEEP IN_PROGRESS: retained fan/loss fixtures and tolerance allowances are synthetic, not manufacturer data; no retained manufacturer curve/tolerance corpus, no unequal-fan or installation-effects model, no external/CFD/experimental validation, no evidence-budget handoff into E05.10 QoIs, and no retained thread-count/replay artifact. Only the nominal declared mathematical root is Certified; physical bands remain Estimate.

title: PCB anisotropic effective conductivity: layer homogenization with bounds and provenance
description:
WHY: A PCB is a laminate of copper planes and dielectric; modeling it as isotropic FR4 misses in-plane conduction by an order of magnitude, and resolving every copper layer is wasteful at the vertical's fidelity target. Layer homogenization (series/parallel rules per direction from stackup + copper coverage) is standard practice with KNOWN bounds — ideal for evidence-carrying implementation.

WHAT: (a) Stackup model: layer thicknesses, materials (fs-matdb cards), per-layer copper coverage fractions (from design data or declared estimates WITH uncertainty); (b) effective-conductivity computation: parallel rule in-plane, series rule through-plane, yielding an anisotropic tensor for E05_1; Voigt/Reuss-style bounds retained as the rigorous envelope (the point estimate travels WITH its bounds — downstream may choose the conservative bound for margin-critical decisions); (c) coverage-fraction uncertainty propagates to tensor uncertainty (correlated across directions — a correlated block, exercising e08's representation requirements); (d) validity notes: vias/thermal-via arrays as a correction model with its own card [stretch: explicit via-array effective model]; homogenization validity domain (feature-size vs board-thickness separation) declared.

DONE WHEN: effective tensors for reference stackups match hand calculations exactly; bounds bracket the estimate; uncertainty propagates into a board-level conduction solve; via-correction stretch either lands with a card or is recorded as an explicit no-claim.

TESTS: unit (series/parallel rules vs hand values; bound ordering Reuss <= estimate <= Voigt as an invariant; degenerate stackups — single layer, zero coverage); property (tensor symmetry, rotation behavior under stackup frame changes); e2e: reference PCB solved isotropic-vs-homogenized logging the QoI delta (the demonstrated order-of-magnitude in-plane effect) and the bound-bracketed budget entry.

description:
WHY: This is the seam that makes the vertical CONJUGATE: solid conduction (E05_1) and the airflow/convection path (E05_5 flows -> E05_2 h values) must exchange consistent interface conditions with conservation accounting, and fs-ladder's cht() must finally carry REAL transfer operators instead of the Refine1d placeholder that the wedge's KernelMaturity score falsely presumed. fs-couple already provides the port/conservation-role algebra (BoundaryTemperatureReference, EntropyTransfer heat ports) — use it, do not invent a parallel mechanism.

WHAT: (a) Partitioned coupling loop: conduction solve produces surface T; airflow rung produces per-surface h and local air reference temperatures (stream-wise air heating along channels via a 1-D thermal-network air path — air temperature rise is NOT negligible in enclosures); iterate to consistency with a declared fixed-point criterion and (if needed) Aitken/IQN-ILS acceleration already present in fs-couple; (b) conservation audit: interface heat flux balance (solid out = air in per surface) recorded as a G0-style invariant with tolerance, reported in evidence; (c) fs-ladder cht() v2: the correlation rung becomes this coupled solve; transfers between correlation and (future) RANS rung defined over the REAL state (surface T + flow-network state <-> field state), replacing Refine1d; relative_cost hints updated from measured runs (fs-plan CostModel); (d) coupling loop is cancellation-correct and resumable (each outer iteration a checkpoint boundary).

DONE WHEN: coupled enclosure fixture converges with logged iteration history; flux-balance invariant holds; fs-ladder cht() constructs the real rung; fs-wedge KernelMaturity justification updated to match code (closing the E01 overstatement).

TESTS: unit (port wiring type checks; air-path 1-D network vs analytic heated-channel solution; flux-balance computation); convergence battery (loop converges on stiff cases or refuses with diagnosis — no silent max-iter answer: hitting max-iter without criterion = typed non-convergence result); G4 cancel/resume mid-coupling drill; e2e: full fixture logging outer-iteration residuals, flux balances per surface, acceleration behavior, and final evidence assembly.

title: Low-Re forced-convection RANS rung [F] (gated on wedge ratification; honest fidelity-graph entry)
description:
WHY: The correlation rung cannot resolve recirculation, jet impingement details, or complex bypass flows (its adversarial failures are by design). The next fidelity rung for electronics cooling is low-Re forced-convection RANS — NOT aerospace SST-tuning: the relevant physics is low-Re internal flow, conjugate wall treatment, buoyancy augmentation, and porous-media-like approximations for fin arrays. This is [F] frontier work with real model-form controversy, hence gated on wedge ratification and explicitly a fidelity-GRAPH node (e10), not an automatic authority upgrade over a validated correlation.

WHAT (staged, each stage independently landable): (a) incompressible steady RANS with a low-Re closure suitable for channel/enclosure flow (choice recorded via model card with citations; wall treatment declared; transition NOT claimed); (b) scalar temperature transport with turbulent Prandtl closure; (c) conjugate wall coupling into E05_7's loop (replacing correlation h on resolved surfaces); (d) porous-media momentum sink for fin arrays with card-carried coefficients; (e) buoyancy source (Boussinesq — cross-check against fs-lbm thermal on the cavity case, a rare internal independent-implementation check); (f) validation against Level-B cross-code and Level-C experimental corpus entries BEFORE any authority claim: this rung enters the fidelity graph as Estimated until corpus evidence populates its edges.

DONE WHEN: cavity + heated-channel corpus cases within envelopes or honestly attributed; the RANS<->correlation discrepancy measured on shared cases becomes fidelity-graph edge data; CONTRACT no-claims name what the closure cannot do.

TESTS: G1 MMS on the mean-flow + scalar system where constructible; G0 conservation invariants; corpus battery (Level A limits, B cross-code, C experiments) with per-case envelope logs; determinism class stated and enforced (deterministic reductions); e2e: one adversarial recirculation case where RANS must beat the correlation AND the graph must record why.

title: Heat sources + transient staging: component power maps now; thermal-cycling transients later (explicit staging)
description:
WHY: Steady-state first is the deliberate 0.1 scope, but the SOURCE model must be right from the start (component power maps are the primary excitation) and the transient path must be STAGED explicitly rather than discovered later, because duty-cycle reliability (e17 duty cycles, Level-4 questions about thermal cycling) will need it and the architecture (time integration + adjoint) benefits from being planned against fs-time and the existing fs-adjoint transient heat scaffold.

WHAT: (a) NOW: volumetric and surface heat-source model — per-component power dissipation as typed scenario objects (W with uncertainty; component footprint/volume binding to regions via e17 persistent identities), power-map ingestion from tabular input (quarantined via fs-io catalog path), source superposition and total-power audit (sum of sources = declared system power, a cheap catch for entry errors); (b) STAGED (recorded as explicit no-claim until built): transient solve on fs-time primitives with method-of-lines + the checkpointed adjoint pattern from fs-adjoint::timedep scaled up; duty-cycle drivers from e17 envelope objects; lumped-network reduced transient model as the cheap rung (fits the fidelity graph). Each staged item gets its own follow-on bead when scheduled — this bead lands the source model and the staging DECISION RECORD.

DONE WHEN: power maps drive E05_1 solves with provenance; total-power audit refuses mismatched declarations; staging record merged into CONTRACT/no-claim sections; follow-on transient beads exist with correct dependencies.

TESTS: unit (source assembly vs analytic uniform-source cases; power-audit refusal with per-component table in the message; quarantined ingestion rejects malformed maps loudly); e2e: reference board power map -> solve -> logged source audit + QoI summary; staged-path lint: transient API surfaces either absent or explicitly feature-gated no-claim.

title: E06 Cooling 0.1 product workflow (Level 3): schema, CLI, import->solve->report->package, one command
description:
WHY: The README states there is no packaged end-user simulator or stable CLI; the only study runner is the photovoltaic fs-vskeleton (.fsir s-expressions, 2-D scalar Poisson). Years of elegant generic abstraction can hide the substrate gaps that only an end-to-end user path exposes. This epic ships the LEVEL-3 thin slice: one command takes a project from dirty engineering input to an auditable result with evidence. Forward prediction FIRST; optimization is deliberately NOT required for 0.1 (prove a trustworthy forward prediction before optimizing on it).

TARGET FLOW: CAD/mesh + materials + operating envelope -> quarantine and repair -> scenario admission -> deterministic solve at correlation fidelity -> convergence + uncertainty evidence -> visual results -> evidence package + engineering report.

CLI SURFACE (grow in this order): frankensim validate project.fsim; frankensim solve project.fsim; frankensim report <run>; frankensim package <run>; then compare/explain; calibrate/optimize belong to the Level-4 epic. Structured progress, cancellation, checkpoint/restart via fs-exec/fs-session semantics.

CHILDREN: versioned project schema (.fsim, Five Explicits mandatory, defaults rare+visible); CLI binary; quarantined import + region/interface assignment; material-card selection from fs-matdb; deterministic solve orchestration (sessions, budgets, cancellation); convergence-evidence automation (fs-mms ladder + order fits); parameter/BC uncertainty wiring (fs-uq); ParaView-compatible VTU field output; deterministic HTML report upgrade of fs-report; per-run evidence package (fs-package) + support/no-claim capability matrix; end-to-end acceptance test with detailed logging + failure drills; worked examples from real artifacts.

EFFORT ALLOCATION DOCTRINE (program-wide): ~70% vertical, ~20% substrate deficiencies THE VERTICAL EXPOSES, ~10% frontier research.

DONE WHEN: on a fresh machine (after constellation bootstrap), `frankensim validate && frankensim solve && frankensim report && frankensim package` runs the reference cooling project deterministically twice with identical content roots, produces an HTML report with convergence tables + error budget + evidence colors, and the e2e lane runs under DSR. Existing beads ty23 / v6dn (vertical-slice e2e gates) should be linked or absorbed rather than duplicated.

title: Versioned .fsim project schema (Five Explicits mandatory, defaults rare + receipted)
description:
WHY: There is no project format today — only the PV skeleton's .fsir s-expr StudySpec. The project schema is the user-facing contract and one of the FROZEN public schemas (e16): it must be versioned from day one with a migration policy, because breaking a user's project file after 0.1 destroys exactly the trust the product sells. Gated on wedge ratification so the schema freezes against the ratified vertical.

WHAT: (a) Schema content for the cooling vertical, expressed over e17 scenario objects: project metadata + context of use + intended decision; geometry references (imported artifact IDs from quarantine receipts — geometry lives in artifacts, not inline); assembly/region/interface declarations with persistent identities; material bindings (matdb card refs with state/temp-range/source per e17); interface cards (TIM/contact); power maps; fan + vent + leakage declarations; operating envelope (ambient range, altitude/pressure if declared); requirements (T_junction limits per component class, margins); solver settings (fidelity selection or auto, budgets, seeds — Five Explicits: units, seeds, budgets, versions, capabilities all MANDATORY); output requests (QoIs, fields, report options). (b) Syntax: reuse the fs-ir/fs-scenario canonical s-expression discipline with an isomorphic JSON rendering (both already precedented in fs-ir) — one semantic model, two spellings, canonical bytes defined for hashing; (c) schema version + migration receipts (fs-scenario ir.rs migration pattern); (d) defaults doctrine: nearly none; every applied default emits a receipt into validation output (e17 no-silent-defaults).

DONE WHEN: schema documented + parser/validator implemented with typed Violations (code/what/fix triples like fs-scenario validate()); reference cooling project parses; canonical-bytes hash stable; version-bump machinery proven with a synthetic migration.

TESTS: unit (every mandatory-field omission -> named violation; unknown-field refusal; canonical-bytes stability across spellings; migration round-trip); property (parse-render-parse idempotence for both syntaxes); e2e: validate the reference project + a corpus of deliberately broken projects, logging every violation with its fix hint — the broken-project corpus doubles as documentation of the error-message quality bar.

DONE-WHEN met in full: (1) schema documented — CONTRACT.md with no-claim boundaries + doc comments; (2) parser/validator with typed Violations — fs-scenario code/what/fix triples, all 16 mandatory-section omissions named, unknown-field refusal, dims/range/card-hash/duty/entity checks with fix hints; (3) reference cooling project parses strictly and is admissible; (4) canonical-bytes hash stable — canonical s-expr render hashed under org.frankensim.fs-project.canonical.v1, proven identical across the isomorphic JSON spelling and across renders; (5) version-bump machinery proven with the named synthetic v0 migration rule, receipt binds old/new hashes and verifies. Five Explicits mandatory; ONE receipted default exists (power duty=1.0); lenient path issues CanonicalizationReceipt + DefaultReceipts, strict path refuses. Entity declarations recompute persistent EntityIds via fs-scenario (17.1 machinery); optional :id pins catch drift as project-entity-id-mismatch. Broken-project corpus (14 rows) logs every violation+fix as the error-message quality bar. Verified via RCH: clippy --no-deps -D warnings clean, 10/10 tests. UNBLOCKS .6.2 (CLI), .6.3 (import), .6.4 (matdb selection), .16.5 (freeze).

title: Per-run evidence package + support/no-claim capability matrix (reviewer-checkable without the solver)
description:
WHY: fs-package/fs-checker exist precisely so a reviewer can verify claims WITHOUT rerunning the solver, but no product path emits packages. Every Cooling 0.1 run must produce one — this is the differentiator vs incumbent tools and the vehicle for the support/no-claim matrix the reviews demanded ("a public support/no-claim matrix" per capability).

WHAT: (a) `frankensim package <run>` assembles an EvidencePackage (FORMAT 8): claims for each QoI with correct colors (Verified only where a deterministic bound/invariant supports it — e.g. flux-balance and energy-conservation audits; Validated only with corpus anchoring per e04/e07; everything else Estimated, honestly); provenance (commit, constellation lock, machine fingerprint, run content roots); budget/color breakdown; semantic witnesses where the built-in plugin classes apply (exact-interval, bounded-linf-residual); declared falsifiers for certificate-class claims per the Phase-0A pattern; (b) fs-checker verification is part of the package command (emit + immediately check; a package that fails its own check never ships); (c) the capability/support matrix: a versioned document generated from the e16 maturity registry restricted to the cooling vertical — every feature marked experimental/verified/validated/supported, embedded in both the package and the report; (d) crosswalk rendering (fs-crosswalk) so the package speaks ASME V&V 20 vocabulary for thermal reviewers.

DONE WHEN: reference run's package passes fs-checker standalone; colors audited against the no-laundering rule (an Estimated ingredient anywhere caps the claim); matrix generates from the registry; crosswalk section renders.

TESTS: unit (claim-color assembly rules incl. laundering attempts -> refused; falsifier presence for certificate-class claims); integration (emit->check round trip; tamper drill: flip one byte -> checker fails loudly); e2e: package run logging every claim, color justification, and checker verdict; matrix-drift test (registry change reflects in next package).

title: End-to-end acceptance lane: dirty input -> decision artifact, with failure drills and forensic logging
description:
WHY: This is the bead that makes "one command from dirty CAD to auditable decision" TESTABLE and keeps it true forever. E2E acceptance tests are weighted governance-level evidence (e16): a crate suite passing means little; THIS lane passing means the product works. It also feeds the primary metric (time from CAD to defensible decision) with real measurements.

WHAT: (a) The golden path e2e: from a committed dirty input set (STL with defects to repair + faceted STEP + power-map CSV + project.fsim) run validate -> solve -> report -> package on a clean environment; assert: all stages succeed, content roots match frozen goldens (golden-bump discipline applies: bumps need semantic justification), report contains required sections, package passes fs-checker, wall-clock recorded into the metrics artifact; (b) failure drills as first-class cases (fs-flagship-e2e forensic pattern): unrepairable geometry -> refusal with fixes; out-of-domain material -> validate-time refusal; budget exhaustion -> honest partial + resume; SIGINT storm -> resumable; conflicting material claims -> explicit-selection error; missing requirement -> margin QoI refuses; each drill asserts BOTH the refusal and its diagnostic quality (message names the object and the fix); (c) forensic logging: every stage emits structured JSON-lines with timings + artifact IDs; the lane archives full logs as artifacts so any failure is diagnosable from the archive alone; (d) DSR wiring: the lane is a named DSR job (dsr quality integration) and the release gate for the vertical.

DONE WHEN: golden path + all drills green under DSR on both reference ISA families; lane runtime bounded; logs pass the reconstruct-without-rerun review.

TESTS: this bead IS the acceptance suite; meta-tests: golden-bump refusal without justification file; log-schema validation; a seeded regression (perturb a solver constant in scratch) must be caught by content-root mismatch.

title: Worked examples from real engineering artifacts + quickstart docs (examples as tested fixtures)
description:
WHY: Examples based on actual engineering artifacts are how users evaluate the product and how reviewers judge honesty; examples that rot are worse than none. Every example must be a TESTED fixture (compiled into the e2e lane), never prose-only.

WHAT: (a) 3-4 worked examples of ascending complexity, each a complete project directory (geometry, materials, power map, project.fsim, expected-results summary): bare heated plate with natural convection (minimal — teaches schema + validate); heatsink-on-component with fan (the reference fixture — teaches full flow); enclosure with vents + leakage uncertainty (teaches UQ declarations + budget reading); an adversarial example that intentionally FAILS validation (teaches the refusal/fix loop — normalizing that refusals are a feature); (b) each example's README walks through the commands and how to READ the outputs (what the evidence colors mean, how to read the error budget, what the no-claim section says and why); (c) quickstart doc: bootstrap -> first solve in N minutes, with the measured N recorded (feeds time-to-first-result metric); (d) examples run in CI (e2e lane) with frozen summaries so drift breaks the build.

DONE WHEN: all examples run green in the lane; a newcomer (or agent) following only the quickstart reaches a rendered report; docs reviewed against the de-slopified writing bar.

TESTS: example-freshness lane (run all, compare summaries); doc-link and command lint (every command in docs actually executes); quickstart timing capture with logged step durations; the failing example asserts its documented failure exactly.

title: Python bindings + notebook support: policy-gated staging (JSON/CLI path first, native bindings by ruling)
description:
WHY: The reviews list Python bindings and notebook support as required product surface ("Python and notebook bindings" in interop; "Python bindings, Notebook support" in productization) — engineers script studies and read results in notebooks, and adoption without a Python path is measurably harder. But bindings collide with the dependency doctrine: PyO3-class binding machinery is a build-time foreign dependency even though Python would be CONSUMING FrankenSim rather than FrankenSim depending on Python at runtime. That direction-of-dependency distinction must be ruled on explicitly via the e11 adapter-policy framework, not assumed.

WHAT: (a) Policy ruling first (rides e11_1's decision record): classify bindings as a DISTRIBUTION SURFACE (a separate artifact wrapping the Rust core, outside the production dependency graph — the core never links Python; the binding crate is not a workspace member of the certified build) and record the ruling with the same rigor as the adapter decision; (b) design: a thin binding layer over the PRODUCT surface only (project validate/solve/report/package + reading evidence, budgets, DecisionAssessments — NOT raw kernel access, which would bypass the evidence discipline; the binding exposes claims-with-evidence or nothing); JSON-first fallback documented (the CLI's --json mode already gives Python users a zero-binding integration path TODAY — document that pattern with worked notebook examples before any native binding lands); (c) notebook examples: worked notebooks driving the CLI/JSON path for the reference project (immediately shippable, no policy risk), upgraded to native bindings if/when they land; (d) staging: native bindings are POST-0.1 scope; the 0.1 promise is the documented JSON/CLI integration path.

DONE WHEN: the ruling is recorded; the JSON-path notebook examples run against the reference project in CI; the native-binding design doc exists with its evidence-surface boundary stated; staging recorded in the capability matrix.

TESTS: notebook-example freshness lane (executed headlessly in CI against the reference project, outputs compared with tolerance semantics, fully logged); JSON-schema stability tests for the CLI surfaces the notebooks consume (schema drift breaks notebooks -> caught here); when native bindings land: binding-layer unit tests asserting the evidence-surface boundary (no raw-scalar QoI access exposed).

title: Staged optimization phase: frankensim compare, robust design studies, guarded optimization (post-0.1)
description:
WHY: The roadmap's 3-6-month tier explicitly includes "robust design optimization" and "automatic fidelity escalation", and the product's canonical questions include "which design is most robust, not merely nominally optimal". The program deliberately EXCLUDES optimization from Cooling 0.1 (prove a trustworthy forward prediction first — optimizing on an untrusted model launders garbage efficiently), but the capability must not be lost: this bead is the staged optimization phase, written now so its prerequisites (design-variable schema e17_8, fidelity-graph escalation e10_3, error budgets e08) are pulled in the right direction.

WHAT (staged, post-0.1, gated on the working forward workflow): (a) `frankensim compare <run-a> <run-b>`: run-level semantic diff (fs-report semantic_diff machinery over QoIs + evidence + budgets; geometry diffs via e11_4) — the manual design-iteration workflow, shipped FIRST because engineers compare before they optimize; (b) design-study mode: sweep/DOE over declared design variables (e17_8) within manufacturing constraints, each point a full evidence-carrying solve (budgeted via fs-session; fidelity per the e10 graph with e10_3 escalation), producing a ranked comparison with per-design DecisionAssessments — robustness posture honored (CVaR/worst-case over the operating envelope e17_5, via fs-robust machinery), so the ranking is by ROBUST margin, not nominal point performance; (c) gradient-based/derivative-free optimization over the same substrate (fs-ascent/fs-dfo with the existing gradient-verification gates; adjoints from the e05 thermal path where differentiable, DFO where not) — every returned optimum carries KKT/stop-reason context per the existing ASCENT doctrine plus manufacturing-constraint satisfaction receipts and a robustness certificate; (d) the anti-Goodhart guard: optimization may not exploit model error — candidate optima in regions where the model term dominates the budget trigger escalation (e10_3) or demotion before being reported as optima (this is certify-or-escalate applied to DESIGNS).

DONE WHEN: compare ships; one design study on the reference project produces a robust ranking with full evidence; one optimization run returns a certificate-carrying optimum whose model-term guard demonstrably fired at least once in testing; capability matrix updated.

TESTS: unit (diff assembly; DOE generation determinism; constraint enforcement; guard triggering logic); statistical (robust ranking on synthetic truth: the known-robust design wins under injected variability while the nominal-best loses); G4 (cancellation mid-study resumes without losing completed design points); e2e: full compare + study + optimize walkthrough logging per-design budgets, escalations, guard events, and the final ranked table with DecisionAssessment refs.

title: frankensim CLI binary: validate / solve / report / package (deterministic, structured, cancellable)
description:
WHY: The README says it plainly: no stable end-user CLI exists. The CLI is the product surface and the thing every e2e test, user study, and demo runs. Scope discipline: validate/solve/report/package first; compare/explain next; calibrate/optimize belong to Level 4 — a forward prediction users trust precedes optimization on it.

WHAT: (a) A `frankensim` binary (workspace conventions: std arg parsing like existing bins unless a ratified decision adds a parser — keep Franken-only policy; deterministic, documented output per AGENTS.md Output Style): subcommands v0: `validate <project.fsim>` (schema + scenario validation, violations with fixes, exit codes machine-stable); `solve <project.fsim>` (runs the e05 pipeline under fs-session capability tokens + budgets, structured progress events to stderr as JSON-lines, graceful cancellation on SIGINT via Cx — request/drain/finalize, checkpoint on cancel; resumable via `solve --resume <run>`); `report <run-id>` (renders the e06 report from ledger artifacts); `package <run-id>` (emits the fs-package evidence bundle). (b) Run identity: every solve records the Five Explicits + machine fingerprint + constellation lock hash into the ledger; run IDs are content-derived; (c) `--json` mode for every subcommand (agents are first-class users); (d) stdout/stderr contract documented (results vs progress vs diagnostics) so scripts never scrape prose.

DONE WHEN: all four subcommands work on the reference project end-to-end; SIGINT mid-solve produces a resumable checkpoint + structured cancellation report (not a corrupt run); two identical solves yield identical run content roots.

TESTS: unit per subcommand (arg validation, exit codes, --json schema); G4 drills (SIGINT at assembly / mid-Newton / mid-coupling -> drained + resumable, verified by resuming to completion and comparing content root to an uninterrupted run); determinism e2e (double-solve bit-compare); log-quality gate: an agent replaying only the JSON-lines progress stream can reconstruct the run phase timeline.

title: Import path: quarantined geometry -> named regions/interfaces (mesh-index-free assignment)
description:
WHY: Real projects start from dirty geometry. fs-io already quarantines STL/OBJ/PLY and the bounded faceted-STEP closure with receipts and promote-or-refuse; what is missing is the ENGINEERING step after promotion: assigning persistent region/interface/surface identities that the scenario references — WITHOUT fragile mesh indices (e17 doctrine: no boundary face selected solely by a mesh index; indices do not survive remeshing or re-import).

WHAT: (a) Import orchestration in the CLI: project references raw files; import runs quarantine -> census -> repair-or-refuse -> promotion receipt, all recorded to the ledger (fs-io receipts as artifacts); refusals surface with fs-io's actionable fixes; (b) region/surface assignment mechanisms, in preference order: named groups carried by the format where available; geometric selectors (half-space/box/cylinder predicates, nearest-to-datum features) declared in the project file — deterministic, replayable, and robust to re-tessellation within declared tolerances; explicit face-set escape hatch REQUIRED to carry a fragility acknowledgment flag; (c) assignment verification: every scenario-referenced region/interface must resolve to a non-empty, non-overlapping (unless declared) geometric set — resolution report with per-region area/volume sanity stats (catches the classic wrong-units import silently shrinking a board by 1000x); (d) persistent identity: assignments keyed by e17 identity records so downstream diffs survive re-import.

DONE WHEN: reference enclosure imports from dirty STL + faceted STEP, all regions resolve with logged stats, a re-tessellated variant of the same part resolves identically via selectors, and a deliberately broken import refuses with actionable fixes.

TESTS: unit (selector predicates incl. tolerance edges; empty/overlap detection; units sanity checks); metamorphic (rigid-transform + re-tessellation invariance of selector resolution); e2e: full import->assign->verify run with per-region logging (selector, hit counts, area/volume, receipt IDs) + failure drills (broken mesh, mis-scaled units, dangling region reference).

title: Material/interface card selection: matdb bindings with provenance, uncertainty, and no-extrapolation surfaced in the product
description:
WHY: fs-matdb already enforces the right semantics (provenance load-bearing, validity domains, no implicit extrapolation, OutOfDomain refusal, usage receipts) — but the PRODUCT must surface them, or users will experience refusals as friction instead of protection. Material selection is also where the e17 rule binds: no material without state, temperature range, and source.

WHAT: (a) Project-schema material bindings resolve to matdb cards at validate time: every region -> MaterialCard (with manufactured state), every interface -> InterfaceSystemCard; validation FAILS with actionable diagnostics if a binding is missing, ambiguous, or its validity domain does not cover the project's operating envelope (the envelope-vs-domain check is the product's first line of defense against silent extrapolation); (b) uncertainty surfaced: the validate report lists each bound property with its uncertainty model and flags Unstated-uncertainty properties (they force Estimated color downstream — say so UP FRONT, not at report time); (c) usage receipts from every query retained into the run ledger so the report's material section is generated from receipts, not re-queried (replay integrity); (d) conflicting-claims UX: when a card has coexisting conflicting claims (matdb permits them by design), selection must be explicit in the project file — the system never auto-picks between conflicting sources.

DONE WHEN: reference project binds fully with logged receipts; envelope-outside-domain refuses at validate; Unstated-uncertainty warning path proven; conflicting-claim auto-pick impossible.

TESTS: unit (each refusal class with message quality asserted; receipt retention; envelope-domain intersection edge cases); e2e: validate logs the complete material resolution table (region -> card -> properties -> uncertainty -> domain verdict) for the reference + adversarial projects.

title: Deterministic solve orchestration: session, budgets, cancellation, checkpoint/restart wired end-to-end
description:
WHY: The pieces exist separately (fs-session capability tokens + governor + metering; fs-exec Cx + versioned solver snapshots; fs-ledger session receipts) but no product path composes them. Orchestration is where the Five Explicits become enforced reality for a user run, and where cancellation/resume become user-visible features rather than crate-level contracts.

WHAT: (a) A solve pipeline driver that: opens an fs-session with capability token derived from project budgets (core-seconds, memory, wall-clock); executes stages (import-verify -> assign -> material-resolve -> flow-network -> conduction/coupling loop -> QoI extraction) each as ledgered ops with content-addressed artifacts; polls cancellation at stage and tile boundaries; meters budget consumption with warnings at declared fractions; on budget exhaustion, produces the honest partial: a structured budget-exceeded result with the completed stages' artifacts and a resume path — NEVER a partially-published answer presented as complete; (b) checkpoint/restart: stage-level checkpoints via the versioned snapshot envelope; `--resume` re-verifies input identity (project hash + constellation lock) before resuming — resuming across a changed project REFUSES; (c) deterministic replay: rerun of any run ID reproduces content roots (seeds and stream keys from the run record).

DONE WHEN: reference project solves under a realistic budget with a full ledger trail; kill -9 mid-run resumes to an identical content root; budget-exhaustion path proven honest; replay proven.

TESTS: unit (token derivation from budgets; input-identity refusal on resume; stage sequencing); G4 (cancellation storm across stage boundaries — no leaks, losers drained, per the existing test doctrine; crash-recovery drill via ledger); G5 (replay determinism); e2e: full run logging per-stage timings, budget meter readings, checkpoint hashes, and the final artifact graph.

title: Convergence-evidence automation: mesh/discretization ladder with order fits as a product feature
description:
WHY: Users should not hand-build mesh-refinement studies; the product should produce discretization-error evidence automatically, because the error-budget doctrine (e08) requires a defensible discretization term for every QoI, and manual convergence studies are the first thing skipped under deadline.

WHAT: (a) An automated ladder mode: solve the project at a declared refinement ladder (2-4 levels within budget), extract QoIs per level, fit observed orders via fs-mms OrderFit, and produce: extrapolated QoI (Richardson-style where orders are clean), a discretization-error band for the budget, and an honesty verdict when the ladder is NOT in the asymptotic regime (bad order fit -> the discretization term becomes an explicit UNKNOWN-or-bounded entry, never a pretty number from a failed fit — this honesty path is the differentiating feature); (b) budget-aware laddering: the ladder respects session budgets, degrades to fewer levels with a widened band and says so; (c) DWR/goal-oriented hooks from E05_1 as the complementary single-solve estimator, cross-checked against the ladder where both exist (disagreement is diagnostic evidence, logged); (d) results feed the QoI evidence records (E05_10) and the report's convergence tables.

DONE WHEN: reference project produces per-QoI convergence tables with order fits; the non-asymptotic path demonstrably yields UNKNOWN/bounded (adversarial coarse ladder test); DWR-vs-ladder cross-check recorded.

TESTS: unit (order-fit consumption; Richardson arithmetic; degradation logic); G1 (a manufactured case where true order is known -> ladder recovers it within OrderGate tolerance); adversarial (pre-asymptotic ladder -> honest UNKNOWN, asserted); e2e: ladder run logging per-level meshes, QoIs, fit diagnostics, verdicts, and the emitted budget terms.

title: Parameter/BC uncertainty propagation wired into the product (sampling plans under budget, honest truncation)
description:
WHY: Accuracy-hierarchy level 3 (geometry/parameter/BC uncertainty) has good pieces (fs-uq MLMC/PCE/anytime probability; fs-rand QMC; matdb uncertainty models; fan/leakage uncertainty from e05) but no product wiring: a user declaring uncertain inputs must get QoI distributions/intervals without writing UQ code.

WHAT: (a) Uncertain inputs come from the project file: material properties (matdb uncertainty models), interface resistance, fan-curve tolerance, vent leakage, power-map tolerance, ambient range — each already typed at its source; the propagation plan is DERIVED: small input counts -> tensor/QMC sampling or PCE (fs-uq fit_pce constraints respected); expensive-with-cheap-pairs -> MLMC where a coarse rung exists (correlation vs RANS later fits MLMC's coupling contract); anytime probability estimates for threshold QoIs (P(T_j > limit)) via the confidence-sequence machinery so sampling stops when the DECISION is stable (fs-voi posture); (b) correlated inputs honored where declared (matdb JointStatistics once e07 wires them — until then, correlation-unknown is an explicit budget caveat, not an independence assumption silently applied: independence-by-default is BANNED for same-card properties); (c) outputs land in the QoI evidence statistical slice + e08 budget terms with sampling-error accounting; (d) all sampling Philox-keyed for replay.

DONE WHEN: reference project with declared uncertainties yields QoI intervals + P(compliance) deterministically; sampling-plan derivation logged and justified; the correlation-unknown caveat path proven.

TESTS: unit (plan derivation rules; refusals on invalid tolerances — fs-uq admission patterns; replay determinism); statistical validation (synthetic cases with known answers: propagated intervals match analytic propagation within tolerance; anytime stopping validity respected); e2e: full UQ run logging plan choice, sample counts, convergence of estimates, stop reason, and final budget-term emission.

title: ParaView-compatible field output: deterministic VTU/XDMF export of solution fields
description:
WHY: Engineers will not abandon their post-processors, and they should not have to (the interop doctrine: let users keep their tools while FrankenSim earns authority). fs-io currently WRITES legacy ASCII VTK; modern ParaView workflows want VTU (XML unstructured) and XDMF/HDF5-class layouts for larger fields. Visualization is also the fastest trust-builder: engineers believe fields they can see.

WHAT: (a) Deterministic VTU writer in fs-io's export family (write-only, like 3MF/GLB precedent): unstructured grids from the solve mesh, point/cell data for T fields, flux vectors, material/region IDs, h values on surfaces; binary-appended encoding with fixed byte order for determinism (byte-identical across runs — export is part of the replay surface); (b) XDMF-style index over heavy data as the staged second tier for large/time-series fields (transient future-proofing; keep the heavy format within Franken-only constraints — document the container decision explicitly); (c) CLI integration: `solve` emits requested fields per the project's output requests; artifacts content-addressed in the ledger like everything else; (d) round-trip verification tooling: a reader-side checksum/summary utility so tests can verify without ParaView (external ParaView validation is a documented manual step in the e2e checklist).

DONE WHEN: reference run produces VTU files that load in ParaView (manually verified once, checklist-recorded) and are byte-deterministic across replays; field values spot-match ledger QoIs at probe points.

TESTS: unit (writer against tiny hand-checked meshes — vertex order, connectivity, data alignment; encoding determinism); property (probe-point values in the file equal solver values exactly); e2e: export run logging per-field sizes, checksums, and probe comparisons; corrupted-write drill (disk-full simulation -> typed failure, no partial file presented as complete).

title: Deterministic HTML engineering report: convergence, error budget, evidence colors, sensitivities, provenance
description:
WHY: fs-report v0 renders deterministic Markdown with scalar metrics; its own contract stages HTML with embedded tables, convergence tables, error attributions, and renders. The report is what a reviewing engineer actually reads — it must carry the FULL epistemic story (colors, budgets, validity, provenance) or the architecture's honesty never reaches the human.

WHAT: (a) Extend fs-report to a deterministic HTML render (self-contained single file, embedded CSS, no external assets — reproducibility and archivability; content hash covers the bytes): sections = summary + DecisionAssessment block (e08; requirement, margin, P(compliance), flip conditions, recommended next action); QoI table with evidence colors and full error budgets (8-term when e08 lands; 3-term until then, labeled); convergence tables with order fits and honesty verdicts (from E06_6); uncertainty section (inputs, plan, distributions/intervals, stop reasons from E06_7); material/interface provenance tables (from receipts); model cards consumed + validity intersections; import/quarantine receipts; run identity (Five Explicits, machine fingerprint, constellation lock, content roots) and replay instructions; known-gaps/no-claim section AUTO-GENERATED (whatever is Estimated or UNKNOWN says so here — the report must be as loud about ignorance as about results); (b) embedded field imagery via fs-img deterministic renders [staged if needed; text-first is acceptable for 0.1]; (c) machine-readable JSON twin of every table (agents read reports too).

DONE WHEN: reference run renders byte-deterministically; every number in the report traces to a ledger artifact (spot-check tooling); the no-claim section is non-empty and honest for the 0.1 feature set.

TESTS: unit (section renderers on synthetic inputs; HTML validity; determinism); traceability test (sampled report numbers == ledger values); e2e: full render with log of every artifact consumed; adversarial: a run with failed convergence must render the failure prominently (assert the honesty path renders, not just the happy path).

title: E07 Level-4 validation program: calibration partitions, model discrepancy, blind case, external reproduction
description:
WHY: Level 3 (integrated workflow) is not Level 4 (experimentally validated workflow). The reviews' original 90-day plan conflated them; this epic owns the honest 3-9 month program whose clock STARTS ONLY when datasets and a validation partner exist (epic e04 supplies them). The schema for model-form evidence already exists (fs-evidence ModelEvidence: cards, assumptions, validity, discrepancy_rel, in_domain; DecisionStatus; EscalationAdvice) — the REAL gap is empirical population and enforcement: are discrepancy bands based on meaningful data, are validation regimes defined from retained experiments, are flagship outputs forced through the model-evidence path, are intervals empirically calibrated, do discrepancy estimates change actual decisions.

CHILDREN: typed calibration/validation partition enforcement (no leakage, laundering-proof); model-discrepancy estimation (several auditable discrepancy models — Kennedy-O'Hagan-style as ONE method, not the universal ontology, since calibration parameters and discrepancy functions can substitute for each other; require identifiability + held-out predictive checks); correlation-aware propagation of material/BC uncertainty (wire fs-matdb JointStatistics into query receipts); empirical coverage checks at product level (nominal 95% interval must contain ~95% of held-out observations, using fs-eproc Mondrian conformal + fs-surrogate empirical_coverage machinery); preregistered blind validation case execution; independent external reproduction of the full workflow.

DONE WHEN: the Cooling workflow has been calibrated on a declared partition, validated on held-out data with published coverage, survived one preregistered blind case, and been reproduced end-to-end by someone outside the authoring environment from the release bundle (epic e13). Failure of the blind case is a REPORTABLE RESULT with a scorecard entry, not something to bury.

title: Typed calibration/validation partition enforcement (leakage-proof by construction)
description:
WHY: Calibrating and validating on the same data is the most common way simulation tools lie to themselves, and under deadline pressure it happens by accident: a dataset used to tune a discrepancy model quietly reappears in the coverage statistics. The corpus schema (e04) DECLARES partitions; this bead makes crossing them impossible rather than discouraged.

WHAT: (a) Partition-typed access: corpus queries are parameterized by purpose (Calibration | Validation | BlindEvaluation); a dataset's declared partition is checked at query time and a mismatched purpose REFUSES with a typed error naming dataset + declared partition + attempted use; (b) taint propagation: any model artifact (discrepancy model, calibrated parameter set, tuned closure constant) records the content IDs of every calibration dataset it consumed; validation/coverage computations REFUSE inputs whose taint set intersects the validation set (transitive laundering — calibrate A on X, fit B to A, validate B on X — is caught by the transitive taint closure); (c) repartitioning is a versioned corpus event with a receipt (a dataset may move calibration->validation only with justification; validation->calibration moves mark all downstream coverage claims stale); (d) the sealed blind sets (e04 Level D) are a third, stricter tier on the same machinery.

DONE WHEN: refusal + taint paths proven; a deliberate transitive-laundering attempt in tests is caught; repartition receipts recorded in the ledger; e07 coverage and blind beads build on this without exceptions.

TESTS: unit (purpose mismatch refusal per partition pair; taint-set recording; transitive closure correctness on synthetic DAGs); adversarial e2e: scripted laundering attempts (direct, transitive, repartition-then-use) each refused with full audit logging of the taint chains; determinism of taint IDs.
notes:
Code-first partition/taint substrate is implemented and pushed on main in e123b3913361901c84cfea734c34a72858613815.

Implemented:
- Corpus schema v2 adds BlindHoldout and makes raw declared-partition querying crate-private.
- Public purpose-typed access requires Calibration, Validation, or BlindEvaluation and refuses mismatches with dataset/current partition/attempted use.
- Generation-bound repartition, blind-release, and access receipts; repartition stales old access receipts and marks evaluation-to-calibration claim staleness.
- Model registration is the public taint-construction boundary, requires fresh calibration-purpose accesses, and computes deterministic transitive taint paths through parent artifacts.
- Validation refuses exact dataset-content reuse directly or transitively, retaining the full deterministic model path.
- Access identity binds canonical exact query context; validation retains distinct held-out access identities.
- Contract states the receipt proves only exact registered-identity disjointness, never scientific authority.
