title: Model-discrepancy estimation: multiple auditable models, identifiability-checked, held-out-validated
description:
WHY: fs-evidence has the SCHEMA (DiscrepancyBand, DiscrepancyModel.fit on FidelityPairs, OutOfDomain refusal) but discrepancy bands populated from meaningful DATA are what separate a real validation program from decoration. Crucially: Kennedy-O'Hagan-style discrepancy is ONE method, not the universal ontology — calibration parameters and discrepancy functions can substitute for one another (identifiability), so the machinery must support several auditable discrepancy models and force identifiability + held-out checks rather than blessing whichever fit converged.

WHAT: (a) Discrepancy-model families over the corpus: constant/regime-binned relative band (the current DiscrepancyBand, fit honestly per regime); parametric trend models over pi-groups (fs-regime) with uncertainty on coefficients; adjacent-fidelity probes (correlation-vs-RANS, model-vs-experiment) as FidelityPairs feeding e10 graph edges; [F] GP-style discrepancy reserved as a flagged extension; (b) identifiability discipline: when calibration parameters and discrepancy are fit together, require either separable experiments (parameters pinned by dedicated datasets — e.g. contact resistance measured directly, not co-fit with convection) or an explicit confounding declaration that DEMOTES the resulting claims; (c) held-out predictive checks mandatory: every fitted discrepancy model reports held-out error vs its claimed band (a band that fails held-out is rejected, logged, and the rejection retained); (d) all fits partition-enforced (predecessor bead) and ledgered with replay.

DONE WHEN: at least two discrepancy-model families fit on real Level-C data with held-out validation; an identifiability-confounded fit is demonstrably demoted; bands flow into QoI budgets (e08 model term) and fidelity-graph edges (e10).

TESTS: unit (fit refusals on insufficient data — MIN_OBS discipline like fs-plan; band arithmetic; regime binning); statistical (synthetic truth recovery: known injected discrepancy recovered within tolerance; confounded synthetic case correctly flagged unidentifiable); e2e: full fit->held-out->admit/reject cycle on corpus data with logged diagnostics per model family.

title: Wire fs-matdb JointStatistics into query receipts: correlation-aware material uncertainty
description:
WHY: fs-matdb already stores JointStatistics (covariance/correlation across properties, PSD-gated) but query-time propagation is NOT wired (a documented no-claim). Treating correlated properties as independent typically UNDERSTATES output uncertainty (e.g. thermal conductivity and density of an alloy co-vary with composition) — a silent optimism bias in exactly the numbers users trust most. This closes a known, honest gap in the substrate the product depends on.

WHAT: (a) Extend the matdb query path so multi-property samples from one card can return the joint uncertainty block (correlated covariance) in the PropertyUsageReceipt when JointStatistics exist and are valid for the requested condition; (b) downstream: e06_7's propagation consumes joint blocks (correlated sampling via the existing PSD-gated machinery + Philox streams) instead of independent per-property draws; when joints are absent, the receipt says CORRELATION-UNKNOWN and the e08 budget carries that caveat explicitly (the banned path is assuming independence silently); (c) uncertainty-model interactions defined: Unstated + joint cannot combine into a certified anything (no-laundering); (d) validity: joint blocks have their own domain checks (a correlation measured at room temperature does not automatically hold at 120C — domain intersection applies).

DONE WHEN: joint-aware receipts flow end-to-end into a QoI budget on the reference project; correlation-unknown caveat renders in the report; independence-silent path is unreachable (lint/test).

TESTS: unit (joint retrieval + PSD gate; domain intersection; refusal/caveat paths); statistical (correlated propagation vs analytic bivariate cases — variance of a sum with known covariance); e2e: reference run twice (with/without joints on a synthetic card) logging the budget difference, demonstrating the optimism-bias magnitude.
close_reason: Landed at 37716306: NormalizedPack::query_joint + JointUsageReceipt + verify_joint_receipt. The matdb authority surface this bead owns is complete: (a) joint blocks selected and bound at query time — one admitted block covering every SELECTED claim through Scalar members yields the principal covariance submatrix packed in REQUEST order (member-disjointness admission invariant makes it unambiguous; exact-ClaimId matching against the .6.4 selection machinery settles block applicability AND domain validity, since every selected claim already contains the query point); (c) no-laundering proven — an Unstated marginal yields CorrelationUnknown(unstated-marginal), never a joint band; (d) domain checks inherited exactly (member refusals incl. NoClaimInDomain propagate unchanged; no joint machinery weakens the validity gate). The silent-independence path is unrepresentable at this API: absence of correlation is always a named reason (no-block / partial-membership / non-scalar-member / unstated-marginal) in a content-addressed, pack-bound, replay-verified receipt (golden-couplings row org.frankensim.fs-matdb.joint-usage-receipt.v1). Battery tests/joint_query.rs: 5 tests incl. both request orders against one block, analytic bivariate variance-of-sum sanity, every unknown reason, degenerate refusals, receipt determinism + field-level tampering refusals. fs-matdb 62 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean as primary. ROUTED PER THE BEAD'S OWN TEXT: (b) downstream consumption — correlated sampling via PSD machinery + Philox, QoI budget on the reference project, and report-level caveat rendering — is e06.7/e08 scope ('e06_7's propagation consumes joint blocks'); the CONTRACT names it explicitly as their authority. Also not claimed (CONTRACT): portable joint-receipt bytes (ledger transport follow-up), pinned joint queries, curve-knot covariance, card-level blocks.

title: Empirical coverage verification at product level: nominal intervals vs held-out reality
description:
WHY: An uncertainty interval that claims 95% and covers 70% is worse than no interval — it is a confident lie. The machinery exists in pieces (fs-eproc MondrianConformal with per-bucket refusal, DriftMonitor, CoverageClaim/miss_rate, FCR budgets; fs-surrogate empirical_coverage) but nothing verifies the PRODUCT's emitted QoI intervals against held-out observations. This is the "a nominal 95% interval should contain approximately 95% of held-out observations" requirement made operational.

WHAT: (a) A coverage-verification lane: for every (QoI, regime) with validation-partition observations, compare the product's predicted intervals (from e06_7 + e07_2 budgets) against observations; compute empirical coverage with proper small-sample treatment (report coverage WITH its own confidence interval — 3-of-3 covered is not proof of 95%); Mondrian bucketing per regime so pooled flattery cannot hide per-regime failure (a bucket lacking mass REFUSES, mirroring fs-eproc's design); (b) miscalibration response is TYPED: under-coverage triggers a calibration-defect record that demotes affected claims (colors fall; report/no-claim sections update) until recalibration — coverage failure must have consequences, not a dashboard shrug; (c) drift monitoring hooks (fs-eproc DriftVerdict) for ongoing Level-E data so coverage claims age honestly; (d) results feed the scorecard's coverage column and the e16 dashboard.

DONE WHEN: coverage computed per bucket on real validation data; an induced miscalibration (synthetic) demonstrably demotes claims; scorecard consumes the results; small-sample honesty proven in rendering.

TESTS: unit (coverage arithmetic incl. small-sample CIs; bucket refusal on thin mass; demotion triggering); statistical (synthetic generator with known true coverage -> estimator calibrated); e2e: full lane over corpus with per-bucket logs (n, covered, empirical rate, CI, verdict) and the demotion audit trail.

title: Execute the preregistered blind validation case (the program's honesty exam)
description:
WHY: This is the single highest-information event in the program: a prediction made with the full product workflow against a case the models have never seen, with acceptance criteria fixed in advance. Pass or fail, the result is publishable evidence of what the system actually does. The synthesis is explicit that the Level-4 clock runs through exactly this gate.

WHAT: (a) Preconditions verified mechanically: the blind case is still sealed (e04 Level-D machinery); calibration is frozen (a declared model-state content root — predictions must come from THIS state; any recalibration after unseal invalidates the exercise); acceptance envelopes were declared at seal time; (b) execution: unseal ceremony (ledgered); run the FULL product path (validate->solve->report->package) on the blind case within its declared budget; compare per-QoI predictions + intervals against the blind observations; (c) scoring: per-QoI within-envelope verdicts, interval-coverage outcomes, and the honesty checks (did the system's own uncertainty admit the miss where it missed? a miss WITH honest wide bars scores differently than a confident miss); (d) publication: the outcome (either way) enters the scorecard with full workflow provenance; a failed QoI spawns attribution analysis (which budget term was wrong) and corrective beads — failure is data, burying it is the only unacceptable outcome.

DONE WHEN: the exercise completes with ledgered unseal; scorecard updated; attribution analysis for any misses filed as beads; the model-state freeze is verifiable by a third party from the package.

TESTS: precondition gate tests (unsealed-early refusal; post-unseal recalibration detection via content roots); the run itself uses the e06_11 lane; e2e: the whole ceremony scripted with forensic logging (seal check, freeze root, unseal receipt, per-QoI comparison table, verdicts).

title: Independent external reproduction of the validated workflow (someone who does not trust us, from the bundle)
description:
WHY: Every result so far was produced inside the authoring environment. Level 4's final requirement is reproduction by an external party from the release artifacts alone — the strongest test of the reproducibility story (constellation bundle, deterministic replay, self-contained docs) and the first contact with "users who do not already trust the system."

WHAT: (a) Reproduction kit: the vendored source bundle (e13), the reference + blind-case projects, the corpus subset needed, the quickstart, and a reproduction protocol (exact commands, expected content roots, expected report values with tolerance semantics — bitwise where determinism class promises it, banded where cross-ISA policy applies per docs/CROSS_ISA_VERIFICATION.md); (b) recruit an external reproducer (different person, machine, and ideally institution; a clean-room agent on an unconfigured host is the minimum bar) and RECORD their friction log verbatim — every confusion is a docs/UX defect bead; (c) success criteria: reproduction of solve content roots within declared determinism class + independent fs-checker verification of the shipped packages; (d) discrepancies become determinism-incident investigations (playbook exists) or docs fixes; the reproduction outcome joins the scorecard.

DONE WHEN: an external party reproduces the workflow from the kit with zero author intervention beyond the kit itself; friction log triaged into beads; scorecard's independent-reproduction row is TRUE with a citable record. Gated on the claim-integrity promotion gate: reproduction of over-claiming would be reproducing a lie.

TESTS: dry-run the kit internally on a blank VM/host first (the 1t8i blank-box precedent) with full logging; kit-completeness lint (every referenced file present, every command executes); the external run's verification transcript archived as an artifact.

title: E08 Error-budget doctrine + DecisionAssessment: mandatory 8-term uncertainty decomposition at user-facing outputs
description:
WHY: Today fs-evidence::UncertaintyBreakdown has three sources (numerical_rel, statistical_rel, model_rel). An engineering decision needs the full budget: DeltaQ = roundoff + solver + discretization + geometry + parameters + BC + model-form + measurement — where terms need not be additive or Gaussian (representation must allow intervals, distributions, ensembles, correlated blocks, and EXPLICITLY UNKNOWN terms). The three-color model is excellent but currently a compositional substrate; it must become UNAVOIDABLE at every user-facing output of the vertical.

KEY POLICY (the no-promotion rule): no numerical certificate may promote model-form or experimental authority. A well-converged solve is only as trustworthy as its closure model, wall treatment, material state, fan curve, contact resistance, leakage assumptions, and validation regime.

CHILDREN: extend UncertaintyBreakdown to the 8-term budget with rich term representations; enforce the no-promotion policy at type level + lint; automatic evidence demotion outside validated parameter/geometry domains (fs-regime admission at product outputs); typed REFUSAL when an unbounded unknown could change requirement compliance; sensitivity attribution (which uncertainty dominates the decision); DecisionAssessment<Q> as an L6/HELM PROJECTION (explicitly NOT a god type threaded through numerical layers — solvers keep producing evidence-bearing quantities; HELM assembles them with requirement, margin, P(compliance), context of use, validation domain, flip conditions, weakest evidence link, recommended next action, replay package); make budgets unavoidable in report/CLI outputs.

USER QUESTIONS this must answer: will max junction temperature stay under 100C across manufacturing and ambient variation; which assumption contributes most to failure probability; is another mesh refinement valuable or is contact resistance now the dominant unknown; would a thermocouple at A or B reduce decision uncertainty more (ties to fs-voi); which design is robust rather than nominally optimal; what is the cheapest next evidence that could change the decision.

DONE WHEN: every Cooling 0.1 QoI ships with a complete 8-term budget (unknown terms shown as UNKNOWN, never silently dropped), the no-promotion lint gates CI, and DecisionAssessment renders in the report with flip conditions and a recommended next action.

title: Extend UncertaintyBreakdown to the 8-term engineering error budget with rich term representations
description:
WHY: The current 3-term breakdown (numerical/statistical/model) cannot answer an engineer's actual question: WHERE does my temperature uncertainty come from — mesh, material data, fan tolerance, contact resistance, or the model itself? The 8-term budget (roundoff, solver/algebraic, discretization, geometry, parameters, boundary-conditions, model-form, measurement) is the decomposition decisions get made against, and its terms must NOT be forced additive-Gaussian: representation must allow intervals, distributions, ensembles, correlated blocks, and EXPLICITLY UNKNOWN.

WHAT: (a) New budget types in fs-evidence (versioned alongside the existing 3-term, with a lossless projection 8->3 so existing consumers keep working during migration): each term = a TermValue enum {IntervalBound, Distribution(summary+replayable ref), Ensemble(ref), CorrelatedBlock(covariance ref spanning terms), Unknown{reason}, Negligible{justification}} — Unknown and Negligible are DIFFERENT states and both require content (an empty-string justification refuses); (b) composition rules: conservative aggregation honoring correlation blocks; Unknown terms poison totals into bounded-below/unknown-total states rather than vanishing; dominant-term extraction generalizing the current dominant(); (c) sources: roundoff (fs-ivl/det evidence), solver (residual certificates), discretization (E06_6 ladders/DWR), geometry (import receipts + as-built when e12 lands), parameters (matdb + e07_3 joints), BC (fan/leakage/ambient from e05/e06), model (e07_2 discrepancy), measurement (corpus sensor uncertainty when comparing); (d) identity/serialization for ledger + package embedding.

DONE WHEN: 8-term budgets constructible + composable with tests; projection compatibility proven; at least the E05_10 QoIs emit them populated from real sources (Unknown where sources do not yet exist — honestly).

TESTS: unit (each TermValue variant round-trips; refusals on empty justifications; composition laws incl. correlated-block math vs analytic cases; Unknown poisoning semantics); property (anti-laundering: no composition can strengthen a term's class; monotonicity of totals under widening); e2e: reference-run budget rendered with per-term provenance links, logged term-by-term.

title: Enforce the no-promotion policy: numerical certificates cannot upgrade model-form or experimental authority
description:
WHY: The single most dangerous laundering channel in a certificate-rich system: a beautifully converged, tightly bounded SOLVE gets read as evidence the ANSWER is right. A well-converged solution is still only as trustworthy as its closure model, material state, fan curve, contact resistance, and validation regime. The composition rules mostly prevent color laundering already; this bead closes the specific numerical->model-form channel everywhere, by type and by lint.

WHAT: (a) Type-level: in the 8-term budget and in Evidence composition, improvements to numerical terms (roundoff/solver/discretization) must be INCAPABLE of tightening model-form or measurement terms or of upgrading Validated-requiring colors — audit every composition path in fs-evidence for accidental cross-term influence and add sealed constructors where needed; (b) authority-source rule: Validated color requires an anchoring path to corpus evidence (e04 axes doctrine); no combination of Verified numerical inputs may mint Validated — verify fs-package/fs-checker admission agrees (their color-admission bridge must enforce the same rule at package level); (c) lint: an xtask/conformance check over claim-producing crates that flags APIs returning model-class conclusions from purely numerical inputs (heuristic, reviewed — the goal is catching new seams, not proving absence); (d) documentation: the policy stated in fs-evidence CONTRACT and the e09 doctrine, with the RANS example spelled out.

DONE WHEN: adversarial laundering tests (constructed attempts to strengthen model terms via numerical evidence) all refuse across fs-evidence AND fs-package admission; lint runs in check-all; CONTRACT language merged.

TESTS: unit (each constructed laundering attempt -> typed refusal, incl. the subtle ones: intersection of validity domains must not IMPLY in-domain validation; discrepancy-band tightening requires new FidelityPairs, not smaller residuals); integration (package-level admission mirrors evidence-level rules); e2e: a demonstration script logging each attempted upgrade and its refusal reason — doubles as reviewer education material.

title: Automatic evidence demotion outside validated domains at product outputs (fs-regime admission everywhere user-facing)
description:
WHY: Validity domains exist (model cards, matdb, correlations) and fs-regime can rank distance-to-validity — but demotion outside domains must be AUTOMATIC at every user-facing output, not a convention kernel authors remember. The moment a project's operating envelope drifts outside a card's domain, every affected downstream claim must weaken without anyone noticing in code review.

WHAT: (a) Product-output admission: E05_10 QoI extraction and the e06 report/package paths run a final domain-intersection audit — the operating point(s) of the run checked against EVERY model card consumed (correlations, discrepancy models, closures, matdb cards, fan curves); any out-of-domain consumption demotes the affected QoI's color and adds a named regime violation to the budget's model term (with distance-to-validity from fs-regime as severity context); (b) partial-envelope handling: when an UQ sweep (e06_7) spans in- and out-of-domain regions, results split honestly (in-domain fraction with full evidence, out-of-domain fraction demoted; never averaged into one flattering number); (c) demotions are receipts (what card, what axis, how far out, what color change) rendered in the report's no-claim section; (d) override path: an explicit, ledgered user acknowledgment can proceed-despite-demotion but can never restore the color (informed use of estimates is legitimate; silent extrapolation is not).

DONE WHEN: an envelope nudged outside any single card's domain demonstrably demotes the affected QoIs end-to-end (test per card class); the split-sweep path proven; receipts render.

TESTS: unit (intersection audit per card class; severity computation; color-transition rules; override non-restoration); property (demotion monotonicity: shrinking any domain never strengthens output evidence); e2e: reference project + perturbed-envelope variants, logging the full demotion audit trail per variant.

title: Typed refusal when an unbounded unknown can flip requirement compliance (no verdict built on sand)
description:
WHY: The budget's Unknown terms are honest — but honesty must have teeth: if a term is Unknown AND unbounded, and the compliance verdict (T_junction < limit) could flip within any plausible magnitude of that term, then issuing ANY verdict is malpractice. The system must refuse the verdict and name the unknown, converting a hidden gamble into an explicit evidence-acquisition demand (which fs-voi can then price).

WHAT: (a) Flip analysis: for every requirement-bearing QoI, compute the margin against the aggregate of BOUNDED terms; then for each Unknown term, determine whether ANY value (for truly unbounded) or any value within a declared plausibility bound (for Unknown-but-bounded) could flip the verdict; (b) outcomes typed: Compliant{margin, budget} | NonCompliant{shortfall, budget} | Indeterminate{flipping_unknowns: named list with the magnitude each needs to flip, recommended_evidence: the cheapest resolution action per unknown, wired to fs-voi action-value where cost models exist} — Indeterminate is a RESULT, rendered as prominently as pass/fail (tri-state discipline like fs-asbuilt's DecisionState precedent); (c) plausibility bounds for Unknowns are declared data with provenance, never invented at check time; (d) the report's DecisionAssessment block consumes this verdict directly.

DONE WHEN: verdict machinery handles all three outcomes on constructed cases; an Unknown contact-resistance case yields Indeterminate naming the interface and the resistance magnitude that flips it; fs-voi recommendation wiring demonstrated for at least one unknown class.

TESTS: unit (flip arithmetic per TermValue variant; boundary cases where margin exactly equals the flip magnitude — deterministic tie-break DOCUMENTED and tested; refusal of undeclared plausibility bounds); property (adding information never moves Compliant->Indeterminate unless a new unknown appeared); e2e: three fixture projects (clearly compliant / clearly not / indeterminate) logging full flip analyses.

title: E09 Certificate-regime doctrine: match the evidence object to the claim (incl. honest NoUsefulBound)
description:
WHY: "Certified" must not mean "we propagated a pointwise interval as long as possible." For chaotic, strongly nonlinear, or event-rich systems a long-horizon trajectory enclosure becomes rigorous AND useless; a large honest interval is a valid RESULT but not an engineering certificate. The certified OBJECT must change with the claim: from trajectory to observable, event, invariant, or distribution — rigorous numerics still matter, applied to the right object.

DOCTRINE TABLE (to be encoded, not just written): root/event time -> interval root isolation or Taylor enclosure (fs-ivl newton/taylor); short-horizon collision avoidance -> validated reachability tube; conserved quantity -> discrete conservation/balance certificate; local stability -> spectral/Lyapunov evidence within a stated domain (fs-spectral, fs-sos); long-term mean load -> statistical observable with sampling + model evidence (fs-uq, fs-eproc); turbulent spectrum -> distributional/spectral validation; reliability over duty cycle -> sequential/rare-event statistical evidence; exact long chaotic trajectory -> explicit NoUsefulBound, never a cosmetic certificate. Intervals retain valid roles in chaotic systems: short-time event detection, local exclusions, parameter bounds, conservation audits, finite-horizon reachability.

CHILDREN: doctrine document (docs/ + fs-govern doctrine entry with risk linkage); NoUsefulBound as a first-class typed result with honest rendering in reports; a claim-type router mapping claim kinds to evidence machinery with refusal for mismatches; a chaotic-system demonstrator test showing trajectory-enclosure blowup while the observable-level claim stays decision-grade.

DONE WHEN: the router exists and is used by at least one campaign crate; requesting a long-horizon pointwise enclosure of a chaotic fixture yields NoUsefulBound plus a suggested observable-level reformulation; doctrine is cited by CONTRACT.md no-claim sections in affected crates.

title: Write and ratify the certificate-regime doctrine (claim -> evidence-object table)

The doctrine fixes which evidence OBJECT each claim class deserves.

WHAT: A doctrine document (docs/CERTIFICATE_REGIMES.md) + fs-govern doctrine registration containing: (a) the claim->evidence table: root/event time -> interval root isolation / Taylor enclosure; short-horizon collision/reachability -> validated tube; conserved quantity -> discrete conservation/balance certificate; local stability -> spectral/Lyapunov within stated domain; long-horizon mean load -> statistical observable with sampling + model evidence; turbulent/broadband spectrum -> distributional/spectral validation; reliability over duty cycles -> sequential/rare-event statistics; exact long chaotic trajectory -> NoUsefulBound (explicit); (b) the positive statement of interval roles in chaotic systems (short-time events, local exclusions, parameter bounds, conservation audits, finite-horizon tubes) so the doctrine reads as routing, not retreat; (c) the marketing boundary: a large honest interval is a valid RESULT and never an engineering certificate — report language rules; (d) crate mapping: which existing crates serve each row (fs-ivl, fs-sos, fs-spectral, fs-uq, fs-eproc) and where gaps are (validated reachability tubes are currently thin — recorded as staged); (e) worked thermal examples (steady T bound vs duty-cycle reliability claim).

title: NoUsefulBound as a first-class typed result with honest rendering
description:
WHY: Today an uninformative enclosure ([-1e30, 1e30]) is structurally identical to a tight one — the honesty lives in the width, which prose can ignore. NoUsefulBound makes uselessness UNIGNORABLE: a typed outcome that cannot be formatted as a certificate, cannot silently satisfy a requirement check, and carries the reformulation hint (what observable-level claim COULD be supported instead).

WHAT: (a) The type: a bound-producing computation may return Bound{interval, decision_context} or NoUsefulBound{width_achieved, usefulness_criterion_failed, cause: (horizon too long | Lipschitz blowup | domain exit | budget exhausted), suggested_reformulation: claim-class from the e09 table}; usefulness is DECLARED by the caller (a width threshold relative to the decision need — the same enclosure can be useful for one requirement and useless for another, so usefulness is contextual, never absolute); (b) integration: fs-ivl/Taylor/newton drivers and downstream certificate assemblers get bounded variants accepting a usefulness criterion; requirement checks (E08_4) treat NoUsefulBound as Indeterminate-with-cause, never as pass or fail; (c) rendering: report/package show NoUsefulBound as its own visual class with the cause and suggestion (education by interface); (d) no-laundering: NoUsefulBound composes as absorbing (any composition containing it is at best NoUsefulBound for that term).

DONE WHEN: type shipped with driver integration; a chaotic/stiff fixture produces NoUsefulBound with correct cause; report renders it; requirement checks consume it correctly.

TESTS: unit (constructor validation; absorbing composition; contextual usefulness — same bound, two criteria, two outcomes); integration (drivers return it at the right thresholds, not before — a still-useful bound must not be discarded); e2e: fixture run logging the width trajectory to failure, the emitted cause, and the rendered suggestion.

title: [P0] Fail closed on non-finite evidence regimes and emit valid color JSON
description:
## Defect
The three-color evidence path violates fail-closed and canonical-JSON invariants in three related ways:

1. check_regime compares state values with less-than/greater-than only, so NaN satisfies neither comparison and a Validated claim remains Validated. Non-finite regime bounds have the same problem.
2. Composition of two Validated claims with disjoint regimes demotes to Estimated but records dispersion 0.0, falsely encoding perfect agreement when there is no jointly supported state. The existing regime-exit convention correctly uses infinite/no-claim dispersion.
3. Color::payload_json interpolates unescaped identifiers and bare non-finite floats. Regime demotion intentionally produces infinite dispersion, so ordinary demotion rows can contain invalid JSON (inf/NaN); quotes/control characters in dataset, estimator, or axis names can also corrupt structured ledger payloads.

## Scope
- Harden fs-evidence regime/color functions only.
- Non-finite state or non-finite/empty regime bounds must demote/refuse conservatively.
- Disjoint validated regimes must produce Estimated with infinite/no-claim dispersion.
- Color payload JSON must escape strings and encode non-finite values as valid JSON without pretending they are finite numbers.
- Update fs-evidence contract language and focused tests. Touch fs-ledger colors/tests only if required to validate emitted rows end to end.
- Do not redesign Certified<T>, package serialization, signatures, or budget pies in this bead.

## Acceptance
- NaN, +Inf, and -Inf state values cannot preserve Validated color.
- Non-finite regime bounds cannot preserve Validated color.
- Disjoint regime composition demotes with infinite/no-claim dispersion.
- Payloads for infinite dispersion and hostile quote/newline/control-character strings parse as syntactically valid JSON and preserve deterministic output.
- Existing color/ledger conformance remains green.

## Verification
Focused fs-evidence and, if touched, fs-ledger tests/clippy through RCH; rustfmt; ubs on changed files; git diff --check.

title: FrankenSQLite runs ON DELETE CASCADE actions BEFORE deleting the parent row (blocks fs-ledger GC)
description:
UPSTREAM ENGINE DIVERGENCE, diagnosed while repairing frankensim-fs-ledger-latent-failures-xys1z. Four fs-ledger tests are red because of it and were deliberately left red rather than weakened.

DIVERGENCE: real SQLite runs sqlite3FkActions() AFTER OP_Delete removes the parent row. FrankenSQLite runs execute_fk_delete_action BEFORE the table-delete program (/Users/jemanuel/projects/frankensqlite/crates/fsqlite-core/src/connection.rs, Statement::Delete arm, ~25306-25318 vs ~25370).

CONSEQUENCE: fs-ledger's conditional sidecar guards are BEFORE DELETE triggers with WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM artifacts WHERE hash = OLD.artifact_hash) — they deliberately rely on the parent already being gone when the cascade fires (the design intent is stated verbatim in crates/fs-ledger/CONTRACT.md). Under FrankenSQLite's ordering the guard fires DURING the legitimate cascade and aborts every artifact deletion, so gc_unreferenced_artifacts is a hard outage.

PROOF: same DDL reduced to two tables. Real sqlite3 3.51.0 -> DELETE succeeds, artifacts_after=0, sidecar_after=0. FrankenSQLite -> FunctionError('artifact content identity is retained with its artifact'). Control: with PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF, deleting artifact-then-sidecar succeeds, confirming the guard WHEN is false once the parent is gone.

RED TESTS: travel::tests::gc_reclaims_only_unreferenced; qty_crosswalk_artifacts_are_gc_roots (tests/crosswalk.rs); runtime_state_artifacts_are_gc_roots (tests/state_checkpoint.rs); vc_005_gc_never_collects_live_branch_artifacts (tests/vcs.rs).

WHY NOT WORKED AROUND LOCALLY: under FrankenSQLite's ordering, 'cascade delete of the sidecar' and 'bare delete of the sidecar while the artifact lives' present IDENTICAL database state to the trigger, so no WHEN clause can separate them. PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF is a global connection setting and a documented no-op inside a transaction. Every legal delete order is blocked by either the FK or the guard.

TWO CORRECT FIXES:
(a) UPSTREAM (preferred): move check_fk_on_delete/execute_fk_delete_action to after the table-delete program and before the AFTER DELETE triggers, matching sqlite3FkActions() placement, preserving the multi-level propagation fix from abef2e0f7.
(b) fs-ledger schema v21 if upstream will not move: drop ON DELETE CASCADE and the FK from artifact_content_identities.artifact_hash; add AFTER DELETE ON artifacts to delete the sidecar (AFTER DELETE runs post-parent on BOTH engines, so the existing guard stays verbatim and still refuses a bare child delete); restore insert-side integrity with a BEFORE INSERT existence RAISE. That is a table rebuild (edge_content_identities and artifact_semantic_bindings hold FKs into it), a SCHEMA_VERSION bump, and a CONTRACT change — a durable-schema decision for the crate owner.

LATENT SCOPE: the same guard+cascade pattern exists at schema.rs:1117 (edge_content_identities v15), :1284 (op_content_identities v18) and :1330 (tune_content_identities v19). They are green today only by accident — nothing deletes edges, and ops/tune sidecars come from reconciliation rather than a dual-write trigger. Any path that deletes an op or tune row AFTER reconciliation hits the same wall.

NOT A REGRESSION: the ordering dates to d314d32bc (Feb 28) / abef2e0f7 (Mar 11). What is new is fs-ledger 9aa38f7e (Jul 18, 'code-first, batch-test pending') adding the guard, which turned a latent divergence into an outage.

title: Bound TaylorModel1 order and non-finite admission
description:
TaylorModel1 admits arbitrary polynomial orders and non-finite scalar inputs through infallible constructors/operations. factorial overflows at order 171; reciprocal factorial then becomes zero, so exp/sin Lagrange terms can collapse instead of conservatively enclosing truncation. Arbitrary orders also permit unbounded allocation and polynomial work. Separately, CONTRACT.md still says no Taylor models while the type is public, and README calls the arbitrary-order implementation first-order.

Root fix: define and enforce a resource- and numerics-justified maximum order through fallible constructors/operations, reject non-finite domains/scalars before mutation/allocation, keep every admitted factorial/reciprocal finite and enclosure-valid, and make contract/README claims match the public surface. Do not weaken pure-Rust or evidence semantics.

Acceptance: exact max/max+1, order 0/1/170/171, NaN/infinity/domain edge, hostile allocation, exp/sin containment, deterministic replay, and no-partial-mutation tests; arbitrary-order requests fail structurally before allocation/work; contract states supported order, error model, and no-claim boundary.
close_reason: Bounded fallible Taylor admission, sound overflow handling, rigorous reciprocal-factorial/exp enclosures, downstream migration, and exact remote Taylor battery are complete.

title: Pin a dated nightly toolchain to stop CI/local clippy drift
description:
## What
rust-toolchain.toml pins the floating 'nightly' channel. CI runners resolve today's nightly while local rch build workers hold older cached ones, so clippy lint sets diverge: the first CI runs failed on lints (chunks_exact->as_chunks) that no local lane could reproduce, and lint drift will recur every time upstream adds a lint.

## Proposal
Pin a dated nightly (e.g. channel = "nightly-2026-07-01") and bump it deliberately on a cadence, treating a toolchain bump like a dependency bump (own commit, full both-ISA gate run). CONVENTIONS.md already calls each nightly feature a liability with a documented fallback; a floating channel is the same liability without the paper trail.

## Coordination
Changing rust-toolchain.toml invalidates every agent's and rch worker's cache simultaneously — land it at a quiet moment, announce in the tracker, and re-run bv/CI after. Verify fs-qty (generic_const_exprs) and fs-simd portable tier still compile on the chosen date.

## Context
Found while landing frankensim-epic-foundations-huq.4: run 28815907293 failed macOS clippy on lints absent from local toolchains; see docs/CI_GATES.md.
close_reason: Pinned rust-toolchain.toml to nightly-2026-07-06, which is BIT-IDENTICAL to the floating nightly every local agent had active at pin time (rustc 1.99.0-nightly 3659db0d3 2026-07-05, verified by installing the dated toolchain and comparing) - so the pin stops CI lint drift without changing anyone's compiler. ANNOUNCEMENT TO ALL AGENTS: the toolchain IDENTITY changed even though the binary did not, so cargo will re-fingerprint and rebuild the workspace once on your next command - expected, one-time. Bump policy documented in the file per the bead: deliberate bumps only, own commit, tracker announcement, full gate run after. title: Golden sentinel discipline: upstream coupling declarations + justified-bump verification protocol
description:

The re-pin froze release-mode bits while debug still produced the original value, so the sentinel failed or passed depending on profile.

Acceptance: seeded upstream change without re-freeze fails with a pointer to the coupling row; a re-pin PR/commit that skips the two-mode committed-tree reproduction is detectable by review checklist; rand_nla and gemm goldens carry coupling declarations as the first two registry entries. title: fs-ivl TaylorModel1 remainder under-covers on domains with half-width > 1
description:
SOUNDNESS BUG (false certificate) in crates/fs-ivl/src/taylor.rs. Confirmed and fix prototyped; blocked ONLY on a cross-ISA golden-hash re-pin that must be done on an x86-64 host (trj/ts1/ts2).

## The bug
`split_mid(iv, rem)` (taylor.rs) stores a coefficient's midpoint `p_k` and absorbs the deviation `δ_k = c_k − p_k` into the remainder FLAT (as `δ_k·h^0`). But that stored error reaches f(x) as `δ_k·(x−c)^k = δ_k·h^k`, and `eval_interval` adds `rem` once at the end. So for a domain whose centered half-width |h| = max|x−c| exceeds 1, the flat absorption under-covers the true `δ_k·h^k` by a factor |h|^k, silently violating the module's central containment law `f(x) ∈ P(x−c) + rem`. For |h| ≤ 1 the flat form over-covers (safe), which is why it went unnoticed.

## Why tests miss it
Every taylor_battery.rs fixture uses domain [-0.8, 1.2] → center 0.2 → h = [-1, 1], i.e. |h| = 1 EXACTLY (the boundary where |h|^k = 1 and flat absorption is exactly rigorous). The containment test also grants ±1 ulp grace. CONTRACT.md:169 still says "No Taylor models yet (future bead 6ys.13)", so the module is experimental and not part of the certified surface — but TaylorModel1 IS publicly exported (lib.rs:39).

## Reproducer (deterministic, ~26 ulp violation)
f(x) = (x + 0.38371695125150285)·(−1.1202845397051888·x) + (x + 0.15914017704475958)·(2.114360809331372 + x), order-5 TM on domain [−18.72527873358944, 16.653298481159304] (c ≈ −1.036). At x = 16.653298481159304: eval_interval = [−2.31981334891575752, −2.31981334891563540], true = −2.31981334891576907 — truth is 1.15e-14 (~26 ulp) BELOW the enclosure lower bound. Gap is 0 for half-width ≤ 12, nonzero at 17.7 (the |h|^k signature).

## The fix (prototyped; passes containment + convergence locally)
Thread the coefficient power `deg` and the centered-domain enclosure `h = domain − point(c)` into split_mid, and absorb `dev * h.powi(deg)` instead of `dev`:
```
fn split_mid(iv: Interval, deg: usize, h: Interval, rem: &mut Interval) -> f64 {
    let m = iv.midpoint();
    let dev = iv - Interval::point(m);
    *rem = *rem + dev * h.powi(deg);
    m
}
```
Update all 6 call sites to pass (deg, h): scale, exp (final scaling loop), sin (term loop), Add, Sub, Mul. In each, deg is the coefficient/loop index and h = self.domain − Interval::point(self.c). Full working patch saved at /Volumes/USB_NVME/taylor_fix.patch during the diagnosing session (regenerate with git if lost). Since |h|^deg ≤ 1 for |h| ≤ 1, the fix is no looser than the old flat form on the narrow domains it got right.

## Verification status
With the fix applied, `functional_containment` and `subdivision_convergence_beats_intervals` still PASS. ONLY `taylor_golden_hash` fails because the remainder bits change (some coefficient devs are ~1-ulp asymmetric at h=[-1,1], and dev*[-1,1] symmetrizes them). New aarch64 hash observed: 0x3a612d034133f478 (old GOLDEN_HASH = 0xa16d9759a35295d8 at taylor_battery.rs:279).

## What remains (why this is a bead, not a landed fix)
Landing requires bumping GOLDEN_HASH, which is a CROSS-ISA golden ("Recorded on aarch64-apple (M4 Pro); must match on x86-64 (trj)"). Per the golden-bump protocol (and the rand_nla mis-pin lesson), the new hash MUST be verified bit-identical on an x86-64 Threadripper before pinning. The fix only adds standard Interval ops (already cross-ISA stable), so it SHOULD match, but this must be confirmed empirically. Steps: (1) apply the patch, (2) build+run `cargo test -p fs-ivl --test taylor_battery` on trj/ts1, (3) confirm the printed taylor-golden hash == 0x3a612d034133f478, (4) update GOLDEN_HASH, (5) add a wide-domain (|h|>1) containment regression test using the reproducer above, (6) ubs + clippy + commit. Optionally update CONTRACT.md:169 once TMs are certified.

title: Make fs-conform arbitrary-f64 certificates exact or outward-enclosed
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND AMBITION
The hardened fs-conform path now rejects malformed dimensions, non-finite evidence, exact-product residual underflow, complete DD accumulator erasure, and several norm-collapse cases. It honestly labels its current double-double rung as bounded numerical evidence rather than a theorem-strength enclosure. However DD add/mul/div/sqrt are approximate: collapse predicates catch total loss, not every partial rounding error. A converter adversarially placed within the DD error neighborhood of a tolerance boundary could therefore require refusal or stronger arithmetic before FrankenSim may claim arbitrary-f64 certification. False certificates are Sev-0.

MISSION
Ratchet restriction-map certification beyond ordinary commercial plugin harnesses: make every adjoint, identity, functoriality, and manufactured-error comparison either mathematically exact over finite IEEE-754 inputs or proven by outward enclosures. Preserve accepted functionality; do not solve this by broadly refusing scale disparity. Use an adaptive ladder: cheap f64/EFT filter, shared DD with a rigorously propagated error interval, exact floating expansion or deterministic binned/Kulisch superaccumulator near the boundary, and interval-enclosed square-root/norm comparison. A powerful new theorem about sufficient exactness or compositional sheaf-restriction error bounds is explicitly welcome, but it must ship with executable hypotheses and a no-claim boundary.

DESIGN REQUIREMENTS
- Exact signed dot evidence: represent each f64 product and sum without residual-underflow loss, cancellation ambiguity, or order dependence. Support arbitrary finite vector length within an explicit admitted dimension/workspace budget. A fixed exponent-bin superaccumulator spanning the full binary64 product range, a fallible exact expansion, or a proven equivalent is acceptable.
- Exact/enclosed Euclidean distance: retain exact coordinate differences and squared sums; compare norm <= bound without an inward-rounded sqrt. Prefer squared-domain comparison with overflow-free exact scaling and handle zero, subnormal, f64::MAX, opposite-sign extrema, and declared+tolerance addition exactly or outwardly.
- Typed arithmetic evidence: report which rung decided, exact/enclosed lower and upper bounds, operation/dimension budget, refusal reason, and deterministic first inconclusive site. Do not encode arithmetic uncertainty as an ordinary measured failure.
- Resource and cancellation closure: preflight/fallibly reserve all adaptive-expansion or bin work; bound dimension, components/bins, and diagnostic size; add Cx/tile polling if work can exceed the synchronous cold-path envelope. No panic/OOM/partial certified report.
- Preserve deterministic ordering and bit-stable receipts. Bind algorithm/schema version, bounds, budgets, and rung transitions into the certification evidence identity. Keep L2 dependency direction valid and Franken-only.

GAUNTLET
G0 exhaustive boundary fixtures for zero/signed zero, all subnormal transition classes, min-normal neighbors, max finite/opposite-sign extrema, exact and inexact products, cancellation, three-plus exponent scales, exact equality, one-ULP and sub-ULP-beyond-bound cases, bound-sum absorption, and every exact/plus-one resource limit. Cross-check exact sums against an independent integer/rational oracle.
G3 metamorphic laws for vector permutation, zero insertion, power-of-two scaling, sign flips, coordinate splitting/merging when exact, equivalent DD/expansion/bin schedules, and direct versus staged restriction maps. Prove rung choice cannot change the boolean verdict.
G4 injected allocation failure and cancellation at every adaptive growth/bin/tile boundary; no leaks, panics, or partial tier publication; byte-identical retry.
G5 freeze result, arithmetic-rung trace, bounds, and receipt identity across runs/thread counts/supported ISAs. Add exhaustive reduced-format model checking (for example all binary16 or a custom tiny-float universe) so the exact/enclosure algorithm is checked against every representable input pair and tolerance, not merely sampled.

ACCEPTANCE
No finite input inside the admitted envelope can receive a passing axiom verdict when the exact real-arithmetic relation exceeds its admitted bound. Every pass carries exact or outward-bound evidence; every unsupported arithmetic case returns a typed no-claim refusal. Existing well-conditioned and scale-disparate fixtures remain accepted when their bounds truly contain the exact result. CONTRACT and ledger schema state the theorem/hypotheses precisely. Central fs-math/fs-ivl/fs-conform unit, property, metamorphic, cancellation, determinism, clippy, and DSR gates are green with replayable detailed logs.

title: Make truss ground and LP construction fallible and bounded
description:
The fresh solver audit made LayoutLp::solve and diagnostics fallible, but the preceding public construction boundary still trusts programmer-built data. GroundStructure::grid asserts dimensions and accepts non-finite/unsafe extents and rules; public GroundStructure fields allow mismatched lengths, invalid/duplicate/out-of-range member endpoints, zero lengths, and non-finite coordinates; LayoutLp::assemble indexes/divides those fields, accepts non-positive/non-finite sigma_y and non-finite loads, and can panic or manufacture NaN sparse state before solve admission. fs-truss-e2e validates its generated fixture, but direct library callers retain this reliability hole.

Root fix: introduce immutable admitted ground/rule/load values plus fallible try_grid/try_assemble APIs with checked node/pair/triplet/retained-byte work budgets. Validate canonical member identities/order, exact field lengths, distinct in-range endpoints, finite safe coordinates/length consistency, finite positive sigma_y, finite loads, surviving load DOFs, sparse dimensions/nonzeros, and norm-estimation output before construction commits. Prefer correct APIs over compatibility shims. Add cancellation polling for large generation/assembly loops under the execution contract.

Acceptance: overflow dimensions, NaN/Inf/signed-zero scales, zero/negative lengths, endpoint OOB/self/duplicate, field-length mismatch, non-finite rules/loads, all-supported loads, zero sigma, degenerate sparse matrices, exact-cap/limit+1, cancellation, and malformed hand-built structures return structured errors without panic or partial authoritative state; existing valid batteries and frame/truss campaigns preserve deterministic results.

title: fs-constraint unsat core is not verified jointly infeasible (deletion filter can return a feasible set)
description:
CONTRACT-INVARIANT GAP in crates/fs-constraint/src/diagnose.rs:296-319 (the deletion-filter minimal-unsat-core). Found in the deep-review hunt; beaded (not landed) because the fix changes the unsat-core algorithm and needs careful testing against the existing fscon-005 fixtures.

## The bug
`minimal_unsat_core` (deletion filter) guarantees only that EACH single deletion `core \ {member}` is feasible; it never checks that the seeded/filtered `core` is itself JOINTLY infeasible. It assumes the seed (the elastic support = constraints violated at the sum-minimizing elastic optimum) is infeasible "by construction," which is false in general.

## Why the assumption fails
The support is the set of constraints violated at the SUM-optimum x*. A constraint can be violated at the sum-optimum yet be jointly SATISFIABLE with the other support members, because x* is a trade-off pulled by a THIRD constraint that is satisfied there. The loop keeps every member for which `core \ {member}` is feasible, but nothing tests `core` as a whole — so a `core` whose members are jointly feasible can be returned as an "unsat core," violating CONTRACT invariant 5 ("the core is jointly infeasible … dropping any member restores feasibility").

## Trigger (constructible)
Three linear constraints where A and B are jointly feasible over the domain, but a third constraint C forces the elastic optimum x* into a region where A and B are both violated while C is satisfied. Support = {A, B}. Deletion filter: test {B} (feasible) -> keep A; test {A} (feasible) -> keep B. Reported core = {A, B} with feasible=false, but {A, B} is jointly feasible. The conformance fixtures (fscon-005) happen to land on interior-ridge supports and don't exercise this.

## Fix
After seeding (and after filtering), verify the core is actually infeasible: `elastic_solve(problem, specs, domain, skip = all-except-core)` and assert `total_violation > FEAS_TOL`; if it is feasible, expand the seed (add support members / grow the core) rather than returning a non-infeasible set. At minimum, gate the returned core on a joint-infeasibility check so the advertised invariant is enforced by the code, not merely assumed. Add a 3-constraint regression matching the trigger above. CONFIDENCE: medium (data-dependent). Related NaN-feasibility fixes in the same file already landed (commit abe0593).

title: Report fsqlite IS NULL operator-precedence bug upstream (CHECK re-parse mis-association)
description:
## What
While implementing fs-ledger (frankensim-epic-helm-gp3.1), a STRICT-table CHECK constraint written as `CHECK((t_end IS NULL) = (outcome IS NULL))` failed on rows that satisfy it (e.g. t_end=200, outcome='ok').

## Evidence
fsqlite reports: "CHECK constraint failed: (t_end IS NULL = outcome) IS NULL" — i.e. the stored constraint text is re-parsed with `=` binding tighter than postfix `IS NULL`, evaluating `((t_end IS NULL) = outcome) IS NULL` instead of `(t_end IS NULL) = (outcome IS NULL)`. Stock SQLite gives postfix IS NULL higher precedence than comparison, so the parenthesized form must hold. Two different renderings of the same constraint appeared across runs ("t_end IS NULL = outcome IS NULL" vs "(t_end IS NULL = outcome) IS NULL"), suggesting parens are stripped when the schema text is normalized and precedence is lost on re-parse.

## Repro
fsqlite 0.1.14 (constellation lock f92683cc4572a198):
CREATE TABLE t(a INTEGER, b TEXT, CHECK((a IS NULL) = (b IS NULL))) STRICT;
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 'x'); -- should succeed; fails with CHECK violation via UPDATE path in fs-ledger's finish_op

## Workaround in fs-ledger
Rewrote the constraint and the matching lint query in AND/OR form: (a IS NULL AND b IS NULL) OR (a IS NOT NULL AND b IS NOT NULL). See crates/fs-ledger/src/schema.rs and lint() in src/lib.rs.

## Why a bead
Plan §12 constellation contract: semantic disagreements with the reference become bug reports for one side. This one is fsqlite's; file it in the frankensqlite repo with the minimal repro.
close_reason: Reported upstream: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankensqlite/issues/122. Bug RE-VERIFIED against current fsqlite 0.1.15 before filing (it persists past 0.1.14) with a fresh 20-line repro whose output is fully diagnostic: (a) satisfying row (200, 'ok') REJECTED with 'CHECK constraint failed: t_end IS NULL = outcome IS NULL'; (b) satisfying both-NULL row accepted; (c) VIOLATING row (300, NULL) ACCEPTED - constraint effectively inverted; (d) sqlite_master shows the stored schema text with the user's parentheses STRIPPED. All three truth-table rows match ((t_end IS NULL) = outcome) IS NULL exactly, confirming the diagnosis: normalization strips semantically-necessary parens AND the re-parser binds '=' tighter than postfix IS NULL (stock SQLite is the opposite, so even paren-stripped text would evaluate correctly there). Issue names the precedence fix as root cause, notes the paren-preservation hardening, documents the impact class ('these columns are set together' invariants silently invert) and the fs-ledger workaround (AND/OR expansion).

title: EPIC LEAPFROG-2026 — fifteen platform leaps and five theorem ratchets
description:
## Background
The new-domain program establishes a formidable multiphysics machine simulator, but a fresh review identified fifteen mutually reinforcing platform capabilities and five theorem programs that can make FrankenSim qualitatively unlike commercial CAD/CAE stacks. This epic is the durable source of intent for that second leap. It deliberately preserves maximal mathematical ambition: the theorem ratchets are allowed to discover genuinely new mathematics, while every scientific or product claim remains tied to an executable proof state.

## Technical Approach
Organize the work into five portfolios: typed compilers and assurance; electromagnetics and semantic manufacturing; experimental/digital-twin reality loops; periodic-machine dynamics; and a theorem-ratchet foundry. Each of the twenty initiatives owns a granular implementation graph and a proof/integration gate. Reuse the existing machine IR, port schema, ConstitutiveGraph, FEEC operators, material database, V&V schemas, Design Ledger, and Theorem Foundry rather than creating rival foundations. Cross-portfolio edges are explicit where one artifact is a real prerequisite; optional moonshots remain feature-gated rather than silently blocking solid baselines.

## Success Criteria
All twenty initiative gates are closed with replayable evidence; the final summit demonstrates shared identities, units, conservation ownership, derivatives, budgets, cancellation, and lineage across initiatives; the dependency graph has no cycles; traceability has no orphaned requirement; and every claim is classified as proven, validated within a stated domain, empirical, conjectural, refuted, or no-claim.

## Test Plan
The final summit must include G0 algebraic/property tests, G1 manufactured/convergence checks, G2 canonical and physical reference decks, G3 metamorphic/unit-rescaling tests, G4 cancellation/fault storms, and G5 same-ISA/thread-count determinism audits. It must also mutate or remove one required receipt field at a time and prove fail-closed admission.

## Considerations
Do not collapse initiatives merely because they share a crate: independent falsifiers and proof states are essential. Do not equate a moonshot feature flag with low importance. Do not claim universal validity from a benchmark win, or a theorem from numerical evidence alone.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. Completion evidence must name the relevant Gauntlet tiers, run the configured DSR quality lane (or record a precise unavailable/fallback state), retain machine fingerprints for performance claims, and state exact no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition discipline
Ambition class: [M]. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack. A failed conjecture is preserved as knowledge, not hidden; a successful new theorem may be promoted only through its stated checker and independent review.

## Verification-experience architecture
The direct-child LEAPFROG EXPERIENCE & PROOF SPINE (P.7) is cross-cutting infrastructure, not a sixteenth initiative or a reduction of the five theorem ratchets. It supplies generated verification manifests; unit/G0-G5/conformance runners; one-command no-mock E2E; forensic fs-obs/FailureBundles; progressive-disclosure human/agent UX and accessibility; DSR/flake/scale qualification; explicit pre-promotion and post-promotion receipts for all fifteen initiatives; four-receipt theorem journeys for RA-RB-RC-RD-RE; cross-portfolio semantic-seam campaigns; and an independently reproduced/red-teamed core/max experience gate.

Every standard initiative now has a core unit/property/conformance receipt, a core E2E receipt that blocks G4, a maximal unit/full E2E receipt that blocks G7, and separate post-core/post-max user journeys. Every theorem ratchet has a formal/unit checker receipt, an independent falsification/E2E receipt that blocks final disposition, an honest pre-final interaction, and a strongest-surviving-theorem journey. Exact future entry points are `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh`, per-cluster scripts, and generated manifests. This architecture preserves core/max capability stratification while raising—not capping—the ambition of theorem discovery.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: FUTURE-SELF DESIGN RECORD: this epic is an additive leapfrog layer over the existing new-domain graph, not a replacement plan. Preserve all twenty initiative boundaries, because each isolates a distinct trusted-computing base and falsification route. Ratchet ambition upward through stronger statements and checkers; never ratchet it downward merely to make a schedule look easy.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: PLANNING-ESTIMATE SEMANTICS: leaf estimates are first deterministic planning medians for the named implementation plus its required evidence, not promises or elapsed-calendar forecasts. Epic estimates represent governance, integration, adjudication, and reproduction overhead and are not arithmetic rollups of descendants. Before claiming a leaf, split any remaining package above the team atomic-work threshold and record p50/p95 effort, capability, compute, and evidence budgets from current architecture knowledge.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
## Graph and estimation convention — supersedes earlier umbrella estimates

All dotted IDs encode stable program hierarchy, but hierarchy itself is not a scheduling prerequisite. Dependency edges are reserved for real execution order. Every epic/container is completion-blocked by each direct open child, while children depend only on genuine technical or evidence prerequisites. This makes preregistration and foundational artifacts schedulable without waiting for their own umbrella and prevents premature container closure.

Effort estimates live only on independently executable leaves. Epic estimate 0 means “roll up descendant effort”; it does not mean zero work. Coordination, integration, reproduction, red-team, and adjudication labor must be represented as explicit estimated leaves. Do not restore additive estimates on both containers and descendants, because that double-counts the program.

Promotion is capability-lattice based: solid, frontier, and moonshot claims may advance on distinct evidence receipts. A stronger rung never weakens or silently relabels a lower rung, and Unknown/no-claim states remain first-class. The maximal summit still requires every selected ratchet, but baseline capability can become usable while moonshot theorem work continues behind explicit gates.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
## Agent scheduling view after hierarchy normalization

Use `br ready --label execution-leaf --json` for canonical actionable work and `bv --robot-plan --label execution-leaf` for graph-aware leaf planning. Items labeled `rollup` are zero-estimate aggregate closure nodes; they are blocked by every direct open child and should never be claimed as implementation work. Dotted IDs preserve parentage, while dependency edges encode execution order only. This convention avoids the beads_rust child-to-parent `parent-child` edge behavior that otherwise blocks every child on its still-open container.

For each seven-receipt initiative gate, `.4` is the independently consumable core adjudication and `.7` is maximal/frontier-moonshot adjudication. Core consumers depend on `.4`; theorem, maximal, and summit consumers depend on `.7`. The gate container is only a rollup. Similar decomposed theorem and engineering packages expose an explicit terminal checker/adjudication child. Agents must depend on that terminal artifact, not on a manually closable rollup, except the owning parent rollup which tracks direct children.

When new children are added, immediately remove the auto-created child-to-parent edge, add parent-to-child `blocks` for closure, label the parent `rollup` with estimate 0, label executable children `execution-leaf`, and rerun all-edge cycle and readiness audits.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: CAPABILITY-STRATIFICATION INVARIANT: initiative and portfolio proof gates expose a frozen manifest, parallel core reproduction/falsification, a core adjudication receipt, parallel maximal reproduction/falsification, and a maximal adjudication receipt. Scientific consumers depend on receipts, never manually closable rollups. Core and maximal are scope strata; [S]/[F]/[M] remain independent evidence-risk tags. The summit may compose core G4 receipts while its terminal atlas must transitively require every G7 maximum.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
## Atomic-work sizing and honest-estimate invariant

Execution leaves should normally fit a 16–32 hour implementation-and-evidence slice, and 40 hours is the default maximum before decomposition. title: PORTFOLIO — typed machine compilers, evidence allocation, and executable assurance
description:
## Background
Machine-scale multiphysics fails when equations, causality, events, conservation, evidence spending, and standards are hand-wired in separate tools. This portfolio makes them compilable views of one typed machine algebra.

## Technical Approach
Coordinate initiatives 01, 02, 04, 08, 12, and 15. Their shared seam is a versioned equation/evidence graph whose generated residuals, derivatives, causalization receipts, hybrid automata, balance witnesses, budget decisions, and conformance obligations retain stable semantic identity.

## Success Criteria
A representative electromechanical-fluid machine compiles from declarative laws through causalized hybrid execution, emits localized conservation defects, chooses a defensible next evidence action, and discharges a version-pinned executable standard without manually duplicating equations.

## Test Plan
Cross-compiler golden identity tests, mutation tests for missing units/ports/guards/requirements, deterministic recompilation, cancellation at every pass boundary, and full ledger replay.

## Considerations
Keep each compiler pass inspectable and independently reusable. Generated code never upgrades evidence color or theorem status by itself.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. Completion evidence must name the relevant Gauntlet tiers, run the configured DSR quality lane (or record a precise unavailable/fallback state), retain machine fingerprints for performance claims, and state exact no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition discipline
Ambition class: [F]. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack. A failed conjecture is preserved as knowledge, not hidden; a successful new theorem may be promoted only through its stated checker and independent review.

title: I01.G1 Freeze the multi-field equation/compiler claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The multi-field equation/compiler gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I01 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: typed law and port semantics; residual/JVP/VJP actions; block lowering; conservation and exact-sequence obligations; deterministic cancellation-correct replay. The maximal family is: exact-discrete adjoints and DWR; representation-independent coupled action equivalence; generated multiphysics law completeness; solver-hint optimality under certified budgets. Pin the fixture corpus (cross-domain constitutive graphs, coupled field/port MMS decks, singular block patterns, and generated reference laws), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

## Background

## Success Criteria
Circuits, mechanisms, thermo-fluid networks, and coupled machines are deterministically classified; solvable models receive an executable block schedule and initialization obligations; unsound models receive minimal over/under-constrained witnesses.

## Test Plan
Textbook DAE suites, adversarial graph permutations, topology-induced constraints, singular parameter limits, causal choice metamorphics, and comparison to numerical-rank diagnostics without conflating structural and numeric rank.

## Considerations
Structural solvability is not numerical well-conditioning or physical validity. Differentiation/index reduction must preserve units, initialization semantics, and provenance.

This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. title: I02 typed adjudicated receipt keys for downstream causal maps and caches
description:
## Root cause and user impact

Internal admission, Eq, Ord, and Hash honor that six-coordinate tuple, but public getters return raw IdentityReceipt values whose derived Eq also compares limits. A downstream map/set/cache can therefore choose the wrong equality relation accidentally.

## Technical approach
Introduce a public typed CausalIdentityReceiptKey<I> or AdjudicatedReceipt<I> wrapper constructible only from the causal identity roles supported by this module. Implement Eq, Ord, Hash, and stable canonical transport over the exact six-coordinate adjudication tuple while retaining explicit access to the full evidence receipt and limits. Name evidence-object comparison separately and document when each relation is valid. Migrate I02.3 matching/DM/SCC/BLT maps and any later causal caches to the typed key; do not change fs-blake3 global IdentityReceipt semantics.

title: I02 recursive causal identity bundle: fixed-point schema governance and complete child authority
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT

I02 causal identities are recursively composed at the instance level, while the current identity-governance graph accepts only acyclic `schema_dependencies`. `CausalOutcomeIdV1` contains normalized child outcome receipts and therefore has a semantic self-edge. `CausalizationReceiptIdV1` contains full child receipts, while `ConditionalOutcomeSetIdV1` and conditional coverage bind those children back into complete parent receipts, creating a separate evidence SCC. Registering only four top-level producers could make `check-identities` syntactically green while leaving recursive byte-schema evolution outside the constitutional ratchet. A child schema could then move without a provable family-local transition, confusing caches, ledgers, migration, replay, and collision adjudication.

MATHEMATICAL DESIGN: GRAPH-THEORETIC FIXED POINT, NOT HASH ITERATION

Build first-class SCC governance. The fixed point is the least graph-theoretic closure of symbolic owner/domain/role keys and declared dependency edges. Never iterate cryptographic hashes around a cycle looking for `h = H(h)`; such an iteration has no convergence guarantee. For each SCC, canonicalize one bundle preimage containing canonical member order, complete member byte-schema descriptions, and internal edges represented by canonical member indices. Hash that bundle preimage exactly once. Derive each member fingerprint by domain separation over bundle identity plus member owner/domain/role. Collapse SCCs to a condensation DAG; external edges reference already governed child bundle/member identities. A rigorously information-preserving acyclic redesign is acceptable only if typed leaf reference/witness schemas replace the cycles and prove that no semantic or collision-adjudication information was flattened to bare digests.

MINIMAL CONDENSATION PARTITION

Do not create one causal mega-bundle. Preserve the normalized/full quotient through the minimal partition discovered from the live schema graph:

1. Acyclic families: Machine graph/behavior, equation, variable, incidence, normalized structure, provenance artifact, matching set, and any other upstream leaf schemas remain ordinary condensation-DAG nodes unless live dependency analysis proves a smaller SCC.
2. Normalized-outcome SCC: normalized causal outcome plus only the recursive normalized child role needed by conditional outcome semantics. It depends on normalized structure but never on evidence/progress schemas.
3. Full-evidence SCC: complete causalization receipt plus conditional-outcome-set/coverage members and recursive full-child roles. It depends on the normalized-outcome SCC, structure, artifact, matching, and evidence leaves; the normalized-outcome SCC must not depend back on it.

A full/evidence/progress-only schema mutation must not move normalized-outcome bundle version or fingerprint. A normalized-outcome schema mutation must move its own bundle and every dependent full-evidence bundle. Only mathematically necessary SCC members evolve in lockstep.

REQUIRED IMPLEMENTATION

- Give structure, artifact, outcome, full receipt, matching set, conditional outcome set, equation, variable, incidence, Machine graph, and Machine behavior explicit owner declarations or rigorously linked existing owners.
- Bind the actual producer `CanonicalSchema::FIELDS` table, ordered field names, wire/presence/child roles, variant/tag grammar, encoder emission closure, domains, names, contexts, and family-local versions. A manually duplicated declaration is not byte-schema proof.
- Ratchet hard-coded role/domain bytes through named constants or registered child schemas.
- Give independently evolvable structure/artifact/outcome/full families independent versions. Express lockstep only through SCC membership and bundle version, never accidental reuse of a generic transport constant.
- Classify nested coordinates honestly: presentation labels, caller order, normalized lineage, provenance lineage, audited predicate source/audit, port crosswalk audit, clock bridge audit, child artifact/full-receipt/progress coordinates, theorem evidence, and every other included or excluded byte.
- Generate identity schemas, authorities, required-ID inventory, mutation matrices, golden couplings, and migration registry atomically from the governed bundle model. No hand-edited drift or partial central registration.
- Integrate migrations produced by `.1.2.11`; this bead owns bundle/governance integration and goldens, while `.1.2.11` owns typed migration closure for outcome, matching, conditional-set, and related durable families.

ACCEPTANCE AND PROOF

G0 freezes canonical SCC member order, nonsemantic local-alias and member-handle alpha-renaming invariance (owner, domain, and role keys are semantic and mutation-sensitive), exact field/variant/child-role layouts, internal member-index edges, and condensation-DAG edges. Every semantic coordinate has a controlled valid before/after mutation proving both typed ID and canonical-preimage movement; every excluded coordinate proves both remain invariant. Member, role, internal-edge, and external-edge mutations must move exactly the mathematically dependent bundle set. Collision-adjudication coordinates use independent receipts/oracles where construction permits.
