title: I02.2 Extract equations and derivative incidences from generated and hand operators
description:
## Background
The causalizer must see identical semantics whether an equation came from fs-opdsl, a circuit stamp, or a legacy hand operator; otherwise escape hatches become invisible structural hazards.

## Technical Approach
Extract algebraic relations, state updates, constraints, port equations, derivatives, conditional regimes, and parameter-dependent incidences from the generated compiler. Define a conformance adapter requiring hand operators to provide equivalent metadata and runtime monitors. Preserve source hashes and opaque portions explicitly.

## Success Criteria
Equivalent generated/hand systems yield equivalent hypergraphs; missing incidence or state ownership is rejected; conditional structure carries the parameter/guard domain that activates it.

## Test Plan
Generated-vs-hand fixtures, seeded missing cross incidence, conditional zero coefficient, nonlinear hidden dependency, clocked state, opaque escape hatch, and cancellation mid-extraction.

## Considerations
Static extraction may overapproximate nonlinear dependencies; record conservative edges and refinement evidence rather than invent precision.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. The artifact must carry typed units/quantity kinds, frames/orientations where relevant, stable semantic identities, seeds, versions, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, and explicit evidence state. Long work runs under asupersync Cx, polls at bounded tile/pass boundaries, and implements request-drain-finalize cancellation plus deterministic checkpoint/resume. Deterministic mode uses fixed logical identities, fixed reductions, and deterministic ties. Emit structured trace and Design Ledger events; never upgrade evidence from a generated or converged artifact alone. Before closure, update the owning CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, record exact commands/results/artifacts, and state performance and scientific no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition and promotion
Ambition class: [F]. Keep the candidate behind a named default-off feature flag until it beats a declared boring baseline on a preregistered deck and records assumptions, monitored validity domain, activation threshold, kill criterion, compatible fallback, p50/p95/p99 cost fields, retained falsifier, and independent reproduction pack. A refuted theorem or failed candidate remains a valuable versioned artifact.

title: I02.4 Discover hidden constraints and perform provenance-preserving structural index reduction

title: I02.G1 Freeze the machine causalization and structural-index compiler claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The machine causalization and structural-index compiler gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I02 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: equation-variable incidence; deterministic matching/DM/SCC/BLT; scoped index reduction; consistent initialization; executable block plans and repair witnesses. The maximal family is: minimality and presentation-invariance of causal witnesses; hybrid-mode-wide structural completeness; certified hidden-constraint discovery and globally optimal tearing/repair. Pin the fixture corpus (toy machine vertical slice, high-index DAEs, under/overdetermined graphs, hybrid mode families, and adversarial equivalent presentations), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

title: I02 resource closure: streamed identities and lease-admitted causal workspaces
description:
## Root cause and user impact
I02.1 advertises bounded resource-bomb-safe admission up to 1,048,576 incidences, but its current graph/receipt path materializes Vec<Vec<u8>> identity rows, uses infallible BTreeMap/BTreeSet and stable-sort workspaces, and does not charge temporary memory to the active operation lease. A syntactically legal graph can exceed available memory and abort instead of returning a typed ResourceLimit refusal. Weakening the published envelope would reduce capability and is not acceptable.

## Technical approach
After the fs-blake3 streaming leaf lands, migrate causal structure, artifact, outcome, conditional-outcome, matching, and receipt encoders to direct ordered-row streaming. Convert row encoders to exact-length checked sinks so no million-row payload is retained. Preflight every index/sort/adjacency workspace with checked arithmetic and fallible reservation. When Cx carries an OperationMemoryLease, admit all peak-live temporary storage before allocation and hold RAII charges through the true live interval; lease-less compatibility Cx is explicitly unbounded and cannot support a bounded-memory evidence claim. Replace large tree maps/sets with deterministic lease-admitted flat indexes, sorted vectors, CSR-style adjacency, or another fallible representation whose tie/order semantics are identical. Preserve fixed logical ordering, cancellation polling, exact identity bytes, and no-partial-publication.

## Typed refusal and observability
Resource refusals must identify phase/site, requested bytes/items, admitted/used/limit bytes, arithmetic/layout/allocator/lease cause, and whether any prior phase drained. Do not collapse memory exhaustion into generic identity failure. Request -> drain -> finalize applies synchronously to all temporary state and lease charges.

## Tests and evidence
G0 exact-limit and one-byte-below/above lease cases, injected try_reserve failure, empty and max-cardinality reduced-limit fixtures, duplicate/adversarial keys, and byte/receipt parity with the pre-streaming implementation. G3 permutation, representation, chunking, and streamed-vs-materialized equivalence. G4 deterministic cancel-on-N checkpoints through index build, sort, structure hash, artifact hash, outcome hash, receipt hash, and final publication; assert typed refusal, zero leaked lease charge, and no admitted identity. G5 fixed identities and diagnostics across thread counts and row chunk schedules. Add a reduced-cap instrumented allocator harness rather than allocating a real half-gigabyte in routine tests; retain an opt-in hostile-scale E2E script with detailed phase/peak logs. Update fs-ir CONTRACT.md with exact peak-memory accounting and the lease-less no-claim boundary. Central DSR/RCH batch proof is required before closure.

## Dependencies and acceptance
Depends on the fs-blake3 fallible streaming leaf and the landed Cx/LeasedVec operation-lease substrate. I02.1 remains blocked until this leaf is green because its current success criteria explicitly include malformed resource bombs and exact public envelope caps.

title: I02 exact row plans: admit causal identity payloads before allocation
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The first I02 streaming slice retained only one row, but it computes a row length by constructing the full Vec payload inside the row_lengths iterator. This violates the fs-blake3 ordered stream contract: row length must be independently available so field and row limits are admitted before payload construction. An oversized row can allocate or abort before the encoder rejects it.

MISSION
Introduce an exact causal-row plan or equivalent two-phase producer for every ordered-row identity family. The declaration phase must compute exact checked length without allocating the payload. Only after fs-blake3 admits that length may the producer fallibly reserve bounded storage or stream canonical chunks. Preserve byte-for-byte identity parity and all logical ordering.

title: I04 EPIC — conservation-defect microscope and causal balance attribution
description:
## Background
A global energy mismatch says a simulation is wrong but not where or why. Multiphysics machines need a microscope that attributes defects to cells, interfaces, time windows, remaps, constitutive updates, controls, and numerical tolerances.

## Technical Approach
Define a common balance-event algebra over chain/cochain regions and ports; compute local residual measures, interface jump/commutator defects, integrator and remap contributions, loss ownership, and QoI-weighted adjoint attribution. Produce minimal witnesses and uncertainty-aware explanations rather than a single scalar.

## Success Criteria
Injected sign, orientation, dropped-loss, nonconservative-remap, loose-solve, and bad-event faults are localized to the responsible artifact and time interval, while exact transfers cancel without double counting.

## Test Plan
Telescoping partition laws, refinement and repartition invariance, fault mutation campaigns, window recomposition, unit scaling, cancellation storms, and whole-machine conservation decks.

## Considerations
A decomposition may be nonunique; report attribution policy and ambiguity. Never force defects to sum by hiding unowned remainder terms.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. Completion evidence must name the relevant Gauntlet tiers, run the configured DSR quality lane (or record a precise unavailable/fallback state), retain machine fingerprints for performance claims, and state exact no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition discipline
Ambition class: [F]. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack. A failed conjecture is preserved as knowledge, not hidden; a successful new theorem may be promoted only through its stated checker and independent review.

description:

title: I04.G1 Freeze the conservation-defect microscope claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The conservation-defect microscope gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I04 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: local and machine-scale balance attribution; reset/impulse accounting; spatial/temporal/interface localization; counterfactual replay and actionable witnesses. The maximal family is: minimal causal explanations across coupled representations; first-divergence guarantees under hybrid topology changes; certified blame stability and counterfactual completeness. Pin the fixture corpus (manufactured balance defects, missed events, nonconforming interfaces, scale transfers, hidden source terms, and equivalent chart representations), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

title: I08.2 Convert localized defects and evidence gaps into admissible actions
description:
## Background
A planner needs actionable choices tied to diagnosed uncertainty or defects, not a generic menu detached from the current decision.

## Technical Approach
Map numerical, coupling, event, material, model-discrepancy, validation, and standards gaps into candidates: solve tighter, refine, change representation/rung, improve constitutive data, run a coupon/sensor/dyno test, seek a falsifier, obtain licensed evidence, or refuse. Bind applicability, prerequisites, expected affected claims, and fallback.

## Success Criteria
Every recommendation traces to a load-bearing gap and explains expected decision impact; irrelevant weak evidence does not consume budget; no mandatory safety or standards action is omitted.

## Test Plan
Seeded defect classes, ambiguous attribution, no-action decision, infeasible action, irrelevant evidence, stale receipt, and action-catalog mutation.

## Considerations
The map proposes interventions; it does not claim the intervention will produce the modeled information.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default with layer-correct dependencies. Carry typed units/quantity kinds, frames/orientations, stable identities, seeds, versions, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, and explicit evidence state. Long work runs under asupersync Cx with bounded polling, request-drain-finalize cancellation, deterministic logical scheduling/reductions/ties, and checkpoint/resume. Emit structured trace and Design Ledger events. title: I08.4e Independently reproduce and falsify the feasible robust core planner
description:

## Technical Approach

Compare the producer receipt field by field without reusing its objective, constraint, tie-break, tolerance or serialization helpers. Attack proxy gaming, calibration, missing overlap, delayed outcomes, budget arithmetic and adaptive replanning.

## Success Criteria
All exact fixtures agree or yield minimized discrepancies; the known bug is closed or explicitly blocks trust; same-helper TCB overlap is zero or disclosed and compensated; favorable Unknown/extrapolation and anti-Goodhart mutations fail.

title: I08.5 Replan online with scoped cost authority, cancellation, and idempotency
description:
## Background
Evidence arrives asynchronously, costs drift, and actions fail. Replanning must not duplicate purchases, cross authority scopes, or change history after cancellation.

## Technical Approach
Implement transactional proposals, idempotency keys, scoped cost/model authority, action state machines, e-process-safe observation updates, cancellation/drain, checkpoint/resume, deterministic reoptimization, and explicit human approval boundaries. Preserve rejected and superseded proposals.

## Success Criteria
Retries cannot duplicate external actions; stale authority or response models invalidate proposals; cancellation leaves a replayable state; optional stopping retains validity; deterministic replay returns the same ranked frontier.

## Test Plan
Duplicate/reordered results, partial failure, price update, expired authority, cancellation at every transition, retry storms, optional stopping, and checkpoint migration.

## Considerations

title: I08.6 Enforce anti-Goodhart, independence, and falsification-budget guards

title: I08.G Prospectively prove and promote evidence-budget co-design
description:
## Background
Retrospective planner wins are easy to overfit. Promotion requires prospective, preregistered decisions at matched total cost with preserved evidence floors.

## Technical Approach

Known optima, misspecified priors/models, cost overruns, delayed/censored evidence, correlated probes, Goodhart attacks, standards infeasibility, and deterministic replay.

title: I08.G1 Freeze the evidence-budget co-design planner claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The evidence-budget co-design planner gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I08 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: typed evidence actions; calibrated response/cost models; constrained portfolio planning; online idempotent replanning; anti-Goodhart and falsification budgets. The maximal family is: anytime-valid globally adaptive evidence allocation with theorem-aware value of information; robust multi-horizon optimality and self-improving cost/error models. Pin the fixture corpus (cold-plate and motor evidence portfolios, censored costs, dependent tests, optional stopping, adversarial Goodhart loops, and budget shocks), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

Instances landed c1fed8c/baf0407/30459ac/7828c45/f368e0c; family also proven under CloudyFinch's independent 30/30 runs during CP/PD integration. Digest golden freeze remains deliberately deferred per docs/GOLDEN_POLICY.md (tracked in CONTRACT no-claim).

title: I08.G2 Independently reproduce the baseline evidence-budget co-design planner capability
description:
## Background
This bead establishes the first independently usable evidence-budget co-design planner capability. It targets typed evidence actions; calibrated response/cost models; constrained portfolio planning; online idempotent replanning; anti-Goodhart and falsification budgets. It is deliberately separable from the maximal campaign so sound baseline functionality can be admitted while more radical theorems and extreme regimes continue under their own flags.

## Technical Approach
Consume the frozen I08.G1 manifest and the declared baseline upstream receipts. Rebuild all evaluated artifacts from clean content-addressed inputs through an independently owned runner; compare semantic outputs, not incidental bytes, while demanding bit stability wherever the contract claims it. Exercise the pinned fixtures (cold-plate and motor evidence portfolios, censored costs, dependent tests, optional stopping, adversarial Goodhart loops, and budget shocks), manufactured solutions, canonical benchmarks, and held-out cases. Check conservation, units, derivative identities, determinism, cancellation/finalization, replay lineage, structured diagnostics, and capability refusal. Produce a claim-by-claim BaselineReproductionReceipt with raw observations, acceptance-band calculations, environmental fingerprints, and minimal failure witnesses.

## Success Criteria
Every baseline claim is independently reproduced or assigned a localized Failed/Unknown verdict. The receipt proves typed evidence actions; calibrated response/cost models; constrained portfolio planning; online idempotent replanning; anti-Goodhart and falsification budgets; it does not inherit any maximal claim by implication. Independent checker code shares no forbidden production algorithm, tolerance table, or mutable fixture generator. Results replay from the manifest and raw evidence alone, and failures identify the smallest implicated artifact/hypothesis.

## Test Plan
Run applicable G0 algebraic/schema properties, G1 manufactured convergence, G2 canonical/held-out benchmarks, G3 unit/basis/scale/refinement metamorphics, G4 cancellation/fault/leak campaigns, and G5 deterministic replay. Retain detailed per-case logs, seeds, budgets, target fingerprints, residual histories, and comparison math. Negative controls deliberately inject sign, unit, indexing, stale-version, favorable-tolerance, and oracle-correlation defects.

## Considerations
A baseline receipt is valuable on its own but remains scope-bound. It cannot certify regimes, materials, topologies, event structures, hardware, or theorem hypotheses absent from the manifest. Disagreement is evidence, not a reason to widen tolerances.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [F]. Run through the project’s declared DSR/Gauntlet lanes when implementation exists; ledger exact commands and artifacts. Require an independent reviewer and preserve all raw inputs needed for third-party replay.

## Domain-specific independent falsification floor
For small decision portfolios, compare against exact enumeration or a provably exhaustive optimizer and retain optimum/Pareto/regret arithmetic. Prospectively test censoring, dependence, off-policy evaluation, calibration, optional stopping, adaptive replanning, delayed outcomes, budget conservation and proxy gaming. Include anti-Goodhart holdouts and preregistered conventional policies; report realized information gain and decision regret, not only predicted utility. title: I12.G1 Freeze the hybrid mode-automaton compiler claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The hybrid mode-automaton compiler gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I12 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: typed modes/guards/resets/invariants; structural consistency per mode; bounded coverage; deterministic superdense runtime; event-time and generalized derivative protocols. The maximal family is: complete bounded-horizon mode coverage; certified Zeno/accumulation handling; topology-changing reset semantics; global hybrid derivative correctness. Pin the fixture corpus (gear contact and backlash, 0-D gas valves, chatter, simultaneous events, rank-changing DAEs, and topology-changing resets), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

title: I15 EPIC — executable standards compiler with versioned conformance witnesses
description:
## Background
Engineering standards are currently read by humans and reimplemented as fragile spreadsheets, scripts, or tribal knowledge. FrankenSim can compile a licensed, version-pinned normative subset into typed obligations, calculations, tests, evidence requirements, and explicit nonautomatable judgments.

## Technical Approach
Create a standards source/edition registry and formal requirement DSL; encode applicability, definitions, equations, tolerances, exceptions, sampling, evidence, and human-judgment nodes. Golden hand calculations, edition diffs, boundary/tolerance cases, ambiguity/refusal fixtures, license redaction tests, adversarial omitted exception, and generated-test mutation campaigns.

This does not make FrankenSim an accredited laboratory or legal certifier. Preserve exact source/version jurisdiction and do not hallucinate normative text.

title: I15.G1 Freeze the executable standards compiler claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
The executable standards compiler gate must be governed by a frozen evidence contract before implementation results are inspected. Otherwise fixtures, tolerances, claim wording, capability scope, or failure policy can drift toward favorable outcomes. This bead preregisters both the independently useful baseline lane and the maximal frontier/moonshot lane; it performs no promotion itself.

## Technical Approach
Publish a content-addressed I15 evidence manifest naming every artifact identity, schema/version, unit system, seed, budget, target fingerprint, capability flag, deterministic mode, admissible approximation, hypothesis, QoI, acceptance band, falsifier, oracle owner, and no-claim outcome. The baseline claim family is: edition-aware clause identity; typed normative rules and human judgments; applicability; obligation execution; scoped conformance receipts and semantic edition diffs. The maximal family is: proof-carrying cross-standard composition; automated transitive impact completeness; jurisdiction/edition-aware theorem obligations; machine-checkable assurance without erasing human authority. Pin the fixture corpus (gear-rating, motor-method, EMC/V&V packs, edition changes, conflicting clauses, licensed-source boundaries, and declared human judgments), held-out partitions, metamorphic transformations, independent checker routes, cancellation/fault schedule, performance envelope, and rules for changing the manifest. Encode solid/frontier/moonshot claims as separate lattice elements so a weaker receipt can close without being relabeled as the stronger theorem.

## Success Criteria
The manifest is schema-valid, immutable after campaign start, replay-addressable, and complete enough for an unfamiliar agent to run every later campaign without consulting a plan document. Every claim has explicit hypotheses, polarity, units, tolerance semantics, evidence tier, oracle independence, activation/kill criteria, fallback, and Unknown/no-claim boundary. Any amendment creates a new version and invalidates only the affected evidence descendants.

## Test Plan
G0 schema/property tests cover required fields, units, identity stability, claim-lattice monotonicity, and amendment invalidation. G3 mutation tests delete or weaken hypotheses, swap held-out fixtures, loosen bands, reuse a production oracle, and alter flags after freeze; each must fail closed with a minimal diagnostic. G4 tests interruption and resume of manifest assembly. G5 replay proves byte-stable canonicalization on the same ISA.

## Considerations
Preregistration is not proof. It must not freeze a known-wrong theorem, prevent stronger discoveries, or force one fidelity rung to impersonate another. New theorem hypotheses or counterexamples are welcome, but they enter through a versioned amendment with visible lineage.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition class [S] for governance. Use typed safe-Rust schemas, ledgered idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and detailed structured logs. Independent reviewers sign the oracle-separation and semantic-completeness checklist before campaign execution.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;

- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

title: I03.5 Couple electroquasistatic transients to descriptor circuits and regime routing

title: I07 minimum-slice gap: bind AP242 occurrence transforms into fs-geom placements
description:
WHY: I07.2 already owns AP242 product, assembly, configuration, occurrence, and lineage semantics. The EXTREAL cooling vertical needs one narrower first-consumer seam that the existing issue does not name precisely: each admitted AP242 occurrence transform must become an explicit fs-geom placement without merging repeated parts or laundering source-frame ambiguity.

WHAT: Extend the bounded AP242 semantic path after the schema kernel and I07.2 mapping so an occurrence carries source entity identity, parent/child frame identities, handedness, transform convention, canonical length units, and a deterministic fs-geom placement. Preserve repeated identical parts as distinct occurrences. Refuse non-rigid, singular, ambiguous, or unsupported frame mappings with structured semantic-loss evidence. Compose the placement receipt with the per-part tessellation/chart receipt owned by I07.3.

AUTHORITY: This is a leapfrog I07 child and implementation gap, not an EXTREAL-owned duplicate. I07.2 remains authoritative for occurrence semantics; fs-geom remains authoritative for placement semantics; f85xj.11.2 is the first-consumer scope record.

DONE WHEN: A supported enclosure + board + sink assembly imports as three distinct placed occurrences with deterministic identities and replayable transform receipts; repeated-part and nested-assembly cases retain occurrence identity; unsupported transforms fail closed; contract and capability boundaries state that no kinematic joint or persistent topological naming is inferred.

TESTS: G0 transform composition/inversion laws, repeated-part and graph-permutation determinism, unit-rescaling invariance after fs-qty normalization, ambiguous/singular/non-rigid refusals, cancellation at bounded entity batches, and a retained two-import replay fixture. DSR quality evidence and exact artifact paths are required before promotion.

NO-CLAIM: Until implemented and proven, current faceted STEP import does not parse AP242 assembly occurrences or populate fs-geom placements.

title: I07 minimum-slice gap: bind STEP length units into fs-qty at import admission
description:
WHY: The bounded Part-21/AP242 schema program and I07.3 geometry binding require explicit source units, but no existing I07 child owns the fail-closed import-boundary conversion into the canonical fs-qty authority. The EXTREAL cooling vertical cannot safely bind regions or occurrence placements while STEP coordinates remain unitless scalars.

WHAT: Decode only the supported STEP/AP242 length-unit declarations needed by the minimum vertical slice, resolve the applicable context deterministically, and convert all admitted geometry coordinates, tolerances, validation properties, and occurrence translations into fs-qty before fs-geom or project admission. Retain the original declaration, exact conversion factor where representable, source entity/context IDs, rounding policy, and receipt lineage. Reject missing, conflicting, ambiguous, non-length, nonfinite, or unsupported unit contexts instead of assuming millimetres or metres.

AUTHORITY: fs-qty owns dimensional and unit semantics; the bounded I07 schema kernel owns entity decoding; I07.3 owns geometry/chart binding. f85xj.11.2 records this child as a first-consumer gap and does not create a parallel importer.

DONE WHEN: Supported SI and conversion-based length units normalize once at the import boundary; mixed/conflicting contexts fail closed; geometry tolerances and occurrence translations share the same admitted unit receipt; replay is deterministic; contracts and capability records distinguish imported AP242 units from caller-declared project units.

TESTS: G0 unit-rescaling invariance, exact metre/millimetre/inch fixtures, conflicting/missing-context refusals, nonfinite and exponent-boundary cases, graph-permutation determinism, receipt replay, bounded hostile input, and cancellation at entity-batch boundaries. DSR quality evidence and retained fixture hashes are required before promotion.

title: I07.G1 Freeze the AP242 semantic manufacturing round trip claim and evidence manifest
description:
## Background
A AP242 semantic manufacturing round trip promotion campaign is scientifically credible only if its claims, fixtures, tolerances, oracle independence, and no-claim rules are frozen before results are known. This bead preregisters an independently promotable baseline and a separate maximal theorem/engineering rung.

## Technical Approach
Create a content-addressed manifest covering artifact/schema identities, units, seeds, budgets, target and material versions, capabilities, fidelity regimes, hypotheses, QoIs, directed acceptance bands, held-out partitions, checker owners, falsifiers, activation/kill criteria, fallbacks, and amendment rules. Baseline scope: bounded Part-21/AP242 parsing, product/assembly/configuration lineage, certified exact/tessellated geometry, PMI/GD&T/datums/texture, materials/process/lots, harness semantics, and explicit semantic-loss receipts. Maximal scope: lossless safe opaque-extension preservation, kinematic-pair semantics, proof-carrying bidirectional semantic equivalence, and automated edition/schema migration. Pin these fixtures: pinned AP242 subsets, mixed exact/tessellated assemblies, PMI and material lots, harness/EWIS, kinematic joints, unsupported entities, and adversarial reference graphs. Give every claim a Solid/Frontier/Moonshot tag and explicit Failed/Refuted/Unknown/no-claim states.

## Success Criteria
A future agent can execute the campaign from this bead and its linked artifacts alone. The manifest is immutable after start; amendments fork lineage and invalidate only affected descendants. No result can silently change scope, metric, fixture, tolerance, material, fidelity, or oracle.

## Test Plan
G0 validates schema, units, identity, lattice monotonicity, and invalidation. G3 mutations remove hypotheses, swap held-out cases, correlate oracles, or relax bands and must fail closed. G4 checks interrupted freeze/resume; G5 checks canonical replay.

## Considerations
Preregistration is governance, not proof. Stronger discoveries remain welcome through versioned theorem cards and amendments.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [S]. Use typed safe-Rust artifacts, structured logs, idempotency, explicit budgets/capabilities, and independent sign-off.

## Mandatory executable verification manifest
Before any implementation or result is known, freeze a machine-readable VerificationManifest slice that maps every in-scope execution leaf and public claim to:
- exact Rust unit happy/empty/boundary/max/error/unit/tie/cancellation/migration cases;
- G0 generators, validity predicates, laws, shrinkers and replay seeds;
- G1 manufactured-solution and G2 pinned benchmark deck IDs, norms/QoIs and acceptance arithmetic where applicable;
- G3 metamorphic relations; cross-crate/IR/API conformance cases; and independent oracle/checker identity with declared trusted-computing-base overlap;
- G4 fault/cancellation/request-drain-finalize/checkpoint schedule and G5 thread/shard/mode/ISA determinism matrix;
- exact per-cluster manifest and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/*.sh` entry point, smoke/core/max tier, Five Explicits, stable terminal exit state, and DSR lane;
- required fs-obs event kinds, bounded/redacted logging, artifact/FailureBundle retention class, replay command, accessibility/agent-parity obligation, performance envelope and consuming promotion gate.

There are no unnamed skips. A not-applicable or Unsupported entry requires a narrow reason, owner, predicate, expiry/review point and explicit effect on promotion. Every success, failure, cancellation, timeout, Unknown, Refuted, partial-evidence, integrity and infrastructure state remains distinct. The generated no-orphan/waiver/drift lint and independent manifest adjudication receipt are load-bearing inputs; missing or stale fields fail closed.

Create a mixed discrete/continuous design algebra: material/shape fields plus relative-cohomology winding classes and terminal periods. title: I13.2c Certify chain maps and winding-period naturality across mesh and representation changes
description:
## Background
Optimization, remeshing, chart conversion, refinement, and different trees/cuts change the computational complex. Winding and flux-linkage meaning survives only when there is a checked chain/cochain map that commutes with boundaries and transports the integral period lattice and terminal work correctly.

## Technical Approach
Construct or admit chain maps for refinement, coarsening, remeshing, chart conversion, terminal-preserving geometry updates, and tree/cut changes. Verify boundary/coboundary commutation, terminal-relative incidence, induced integral maps, unimodularity or stated index, free/torsion action, and compatibility with distributed/filament winding and circuit duality. Emit WindingClassReceipt with canonical class identity, period vector, map composition/naturality defects, error budgets for geometric/field quantities, and exact lineage. Refuse maps that merge terminals, cross insulation, lose integral periods, or cannot establish their induced action.

## Success Criteria
Equivalent meshes/charts/bases preserve classes and terminal observables; map composition agrees with direct transport; refinement/coarsening round trips preserve integral periods where claimed; filament/distributed realizations agree in declared norms; invalid maps fail closed and invalidate dependent caches.

## Test Plan
Use repeated refinement, remesh and chart round trips, tree/cut changes, conductor and phase permutations, nonunimodular maps, lost terminal cells, insulation crossings, map-composition mutations, winding/circuit duality fixtures, restart replay, and G5 determinism.

## Considerations
Naturality is conditional on a declared admissible map. It does not claim that arbitrary topology-changing geometry has a canonical transport.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [M]. Emit content-addressed WindingClassReceipt and ChainMapNaturalityReceipt artifacts with exact integral actions, terminal work/flux-linkage conventions, defects, provenance, and refusal reasons.

title: I13.2d Classify topology events and emit induced-map, redesign, and invalidation obligations

## Technical Approach
Detect and classify Betti/torsion changes, conductor births/deaths/splits/merges, insulation bridges/breaks, terminal contacts/separations, and near-simultaneous ambiguous events. Compare pre/post integral topology receipts and construct the maximal justified partial class map. Emit one of: certified induced transport; a finite set of admissible class relations; discrete redesign request; or deterministic invalidation obligations for topology, gauge, state, adjoint, preconditioner, surrogate, and gradient caches. Ledger pre/post identities, event ordering/partial order, ambiguity, and restart boundary.

## Success Criteria
No event invents or destroys terminal/winding data silently; ambiguous events preserve alternatives or Unknown; cache and gradient invalidation is complete; split/merge and insulation mutations replay; every continuation or redesign decision cites the exact induced-map witness or absence.

## Test Plan
Create births/deaths, tunnel events, conductor splits/merges, insulation bridges, terminal contact/swap, torsion changes, near-simultaneous events, missing maps, stale-cache mutations, cancellation during event transaction, and restart replay.

This task classifies topology and emits transfer obligations only. I13.4b exclusively owns physical field, circuit, thermal, stress, state, adjoint, and restart transfer; ordinary differentiability stops unless a separate generalized theorem applies.

title: I13.4d Independently adjudicate fixed-topology cohomology-aware optimizer progress and no-event equivalence
description:
## Background
I13's core is intentionally moonshot-level: it seeks cohomology-preserving electromagnetic topology optimization with exact-discrete gradients and auditable design progress. That core, however, must not silently require the still stronger topology-event remesh/restart/generalized-adjoint branch. A separate fixed-topology receipt is needed so future agents can distinguish optimization within one declared topology stratum from optimization that crosses a topology event.

## Technical Approach
Consume the fixed-topology optimizer artifact from I13.4a and the independently adjudicated fixed-topology EM/circuit/motion/loss adjoint receipt from I13.3c. Preregister the admissible design stratum, cell-complex identity, relative/absolute boundary split, harmonic-basis convention, Betti/cohomology invariants, feature-size and persistence margins, objective and constraint graph, optimizer settings, seeds, and error/resource budgets. Recompute objective, constraints, gradients, line-search or trust-region acceptance, and progress using an independently owned checker. At every accepted iterate, evaluate explicit no-topology-event guards and retain chain/cochain, persistence, connectivity, energy, conservation, KKT/residual, and lineage witnesses. If a guard is crossed or cannot be certified, emit Unknown and route to the maximal I13.4b/I13.4c topology-event lane rather than borrowing its conclusion.

## Success Criteria
A content-addressed core receipt identifies the exact admitted topology stratum and independently reproduces claimed objective/constraint values, fixed-topology gradients, conservation balances, and optimizer progress within declared tolerances. The receipt proves that no admitted iterate changed the declared cohomology/topology invariants and that the core dependency closure contains I13.3c but not I13.3d or I13.3e. Near-event, ambiguous, or checker-disagreeing cases deterministically escalate to the maximal lane with a minimal witness. The result is consumable by I13.G2 and I13.G3 without weakening the maximal topology-event theorem program.

## Test Plan
Use pinned fixed-topology motor and winding fixtures; analytic and independent finite-difference/complex-step gradient checks where admissible; KKT and trust-region/line-search replay; unit, frame, basis, mesh, refinement, and representation metamorphics; cohomology and persistence invariance checks; deliberately near-event level-set/density sequences; missed-event and false-event mutations; remesh or harmonic-basis corruption; deterministic checkpoint/resume; cancellation and resource exhaustion; and independent G2/G3 reproduction with raw artifacts. Require the no-event guard to fail closed on every injected topology crossing.

## Considerations
This receipt does not claim a global optimum, topology-changing differentiability, generalized derivatives across events, conservative remesh/restart equivalence, winding manufacturability, or real-machine improvement. Those stronger claims remain first-class maximal work in I13.3d/I13.3e and I13.4b/I13.4c. Keeping the boundary explicit increases ambition by allowing both theorem programs to advance without letting the maximal hypothesis contaminate the independently useful core.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default and preserve layer direction. Carry typed units and quantity kinds, frames and orientations, stable semantic identities, seeds, versions, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, and explicit evidence polarity. Long work runs under asupersync Cx, polls at bounded tile/pass boundaries, and implements request-drain-finalize cancellation plus deterministic checkpoint/resume. Deterministic mode uses fixed logical identities, reductions, and ties. Emit structured trace and Design Ledger events; failed or refuted candidates remain retained evidence. Before closure, update the owning CONTRACT.md, run applicable DSR/Gauntlet lanes, record exact commands, artifacts, machine fingerprints, costs, assumptions, and no-claim boundaries, and require independent checker ownership.

## Ambition and promotion
Ambition class: [M]. Keep this default-off until the fixed-topology receipt beats the declared boring baseline on a preregistered deck, its no-event guard survives adversarial mutation, and an independent reproduction pack is adjudicated. Promotion of this core does not promote the topology-event branch; a refutation or Unknown result remains valuable versioned knowledge.

title: I13.7 Synthesize integer windings and realizable coil routes from distributed targets

Optimized current sheets are not windings. Real coils require integer turns, terminal classes, divergence compatibility, slot fill, insulation, bend radius, end-turn cost, and routable connectivity.

## Success Criteria
The synthesized winding reproduces its target MMF/flux-linkage class within bounds, is integral and connected, passes fill/clearance/route predicates, and agrees between filament and distributed realizations. Nonintegral/disconnected attractive solutions fail.

## Test Plan
Canonical distributed windings, multiple homology bases, turn rounding, terminal swaps, slot constraints, end-turn geometry, filament/distributed cross-check, and adversarial disconnected routes.

## Considerations
Integer synthesis is combinatorial and no global optimum is promised; preserve feasible incumbents and bounds.

title: I14.2a Assemble typed frequency- and temperature-dependent RLGC operators
description:
## Background
A multiconductor transmission-line model is meaningful only relative to ordered conductors, an explicit reference/return topology, port orientation, and a quasi-TEM validity region. I14.2 must not duplicate electrostatic, conduction, PEEC, or MQS field extractors; it assembles their admitted receipts and measured RLGC data into one typed operator.

## Technical Approach
Define MtlOperator with dimensioned per-unit-length RLGC matrices, conductor/reference identities, terminal orientation, geometry/material lineage, frequency/temperature domains, evidence class, reciprocity class, covariance or certified bounds, and QuasiTemValidityReceipt. Accept versioned samples from I03 capacitance/conductance extraction, I14.3a PEEC extraction, moving-conductor/MQS internal-impedance adapters, or admitted measurements. Validate and crosswalk those sources without recomputing their fields. Preserve potential-coefficient versus capacitance quotient semantics, skin/proximity provenance, phasor/sign convention, charge/current continuity, and the map to HarnessGraph/PortSchema. Refuse missing references, inconsistent gauges/quotients, incompatible terminals, invalid material states, ambiguous units, or an extraction claim lacking its own receipt.

## Success Criteria
Coax/two-wire admitted datasets meet analytic envelopes; matrix dimensions, realness/conjugate symmetry, reciprocity obligations, and positive-semidefinite loss preconditions are checked for their declared class; temperature/frequency interpolation preserves evidence and bounds; conductor permutations and reference changes have explicit transforms. The artifact distinguishes computed, measured, and fitted evidence and never upgrades one class to another.

## Test Plan
Use analytic and admitted coax/pair/bundle receipts, conductor/reference changes, potential-coefficient/capacitance quotient cases, lossy/anisotropic materials, temperature sweeps, measurement covariance, stale extraction versions, non-PSD R/G, unit and gauge mismatches, cancellation, and replay.

## Considerations
RLGC are matrix-valued causal operators. Geometry-derived entries exist only when the relevant field-extraction receipt is present; otherwise the lane may use admitted measurements or return Unknown. Full-wave and connector validity are separate.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit content-addressed MtlOperator and QuasiTemValidityReceipt artifacts with source evidence class, units, conventions, validity/error budgets, versions, and no-claim boundaries.

## Deterministic execution floor
Assign semantic logical work identities to every frequency, mode, parameter point, branch, profile slice, matrix block, target artifact, and reduction tile rather than deriving identity from worker order. Deterministic mode uses stable traversal, fixed-shape reductions, deterministic pivot/tie/cluster/branch rules, counter-based RNG where relevant, and versioned serialization. Test thread, shard, schedule, resume and same-ISA replay matrices; any permitted fast-mode or cross-ISA divergence is classified, bounded and ledgered rather than silently accepted.

title: I14.2b Fit passive causal RLGC models and construct modal/common-differential decompositions
description:
## Background
Raw frequency samples are not a safe transient model. Naive interpolation or eigenvector tracking can create noncausal gain, negative dissipation, broken real-valued time response, incorrect DC/high-frequency behavior, mode swaps, and arbitrary phase flips near degeneracy.

## Technical Approach
Fit admitted MtlOperator samples with stable positive-real rational/state-space models when that family can honestly represent the band. Enforce realness and conjugate symmetry, DC and high-frequency asymptotics, passivity, causality, residual/error bounds, and reciprocity only for reciprocal classes. Admit diffusive, fractional, convolutional, or tabulated causal operators when rational approximation would require an unjustified order or distort skin-effect asymptotics. Build power-normalized modal and application-declared common/differential coordinates with deterministic subspace tracking at clustered modes; do not pretend a general bundle has a universal canonical common/differential basis. Carry conditioning, truncation, interpolation, repair perturbation, and inverse maps as receipts.

## Success Criteria
Admitted models are stable, causal, passive, real-valued in time, and asymptotically consistent over the declared region; repeated-mode invariant subspaces remain continuous even when individual modes are not identifiable; transform/recompose preserves terminal voltage/current/charge/power within directed bounds. Noncausal, nonpassive, or unrepresentable data refuses or uses a stronger admitted operator class.

## Test Plan
Exercise exact rational, diffusive skin-effect, delayed/lossy, sparse/noisy, DC-singular, and high-frequency fixtures; repeated/crossing modes; noncanonical bundle groupings; passivity/causality/realness mutations; unstable poles; temperature interpolation; and independent positive-real checks.

## Considerations
Modal labels are coordinate choices. A small fit residual is not a causality or asymptotic proof, and rational order must not hide unsupported physics.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Produce PassiveMtlFitReceipt with raw identity, operator family/order, asymptotic and realness witnesses, residual/perturbation bounds, passivity/causality evidence, subspace identities, and refusals.

## Cancellation, drain, and resumability floor
Long loops poll the explicit asupersync Cx at bounded semantic chunks and record the achieved latency bound. Cancellation is request → drain owned/speculative work → finalize a non-Pass receipt; it cannot drop tasks, arenas, temporary artifacts, optimizer state, partial uncertainty samples, or checker branches. Save versioned resumable state where recomputation is material, verify checkpoint compatibility before resume/fork, and test cancellation before, during and after each expensive phase plus fault/cancel races. Partial results remain useful only with explicit incompleteness and no-claim effect.

title: I14.2c Propagate time/frequency waves through terminations, connectors, and circuits
description:
## Background

## Technical Approach

Support piecewise-uniform sections, oriented terminations, connector/discontinuity models within their validity, application-declared modal coordinates, admitted source waveforms, and descriptor-MNA coupling. Use power-consistent variables and explicit reference conductors; account exactly once for conductor and dielectric loss. Provide stable convolution/state-space realization, multirate boundaries, timestep/error controls, checkpoint/resume, and bounded cancellation drain. Keep switching-device model integration an optional I14.7/source adapter rather than a baseline blocker. ## Success Criteria
Matched/open/short/mismatched analytic lines reproduce delays and reflection coefficients; bundles meet crosstalk envelopes; time/frequency paths agree within stated bounds; terminal power equals stored, transmitted, and dissipated power. Circuit coupling preserves orientation and DAE semantics, and unsupported source/connector spectra escalate.

## Test Plan
Run matched/reflected pulses, dispersive lines, coupled bundles, mode conversion, connector steps, admitted sources, circuit loads, reference mistakes, double-counted loss, partial cancellation, restart, and replay. Test optional switching adapters separately.

## Considerations
A compact connector or source adapter is not a full three-dimensional field/device solution. Radiation, unsupported modes, and out-of-band material behavior require a higher rung.

title: I14.3a Extract gauge-explicit quasi-static and admitted retarded PEEC operators
description:
## Background
PEEC connects conductor/dielectric geometry to circuit variables through partial inductance, coefficients of potential, resistance, and—when admitted—retardation. The potential-coefficient matrix P and Maxwell capacitance matrix C are not interchangeable: inversion or pseudoinversion is defined only on a declared reference/gauge quotient. Symmetry and positive-semidefinite energy properties require reciprocal quasistatic media. Retarded PEEC must preserve charge continuity and Lorenz-gauge coupling across scalar and vector delayed terms.

## Technical Approach
Define canonical volume/surface/filament unknowns, incidence/continuity maps, conductor components, terminal/reference quotient, and gauge. Extract partial inductance, potential coefficient P, quotient capacitance C where invertible/pseudoinvertible under explicit nullspace constraints, resistance, and admitted skin/proximity operators. State reciprocity, symmetry, PSD/energy, dispersion, and anisotropy hypotheses separately. Start electro-/magneto-quasistatic. For retarded paths, co-discretize scalar and vector potentials/delays with discrete continuity-equation and Lorenz-gauge consistency, causal kernels, delay/quadrature error, and wavelength admission. Carry singular self terms, geometry/discretization error, nullspaces, and escalation to full wave.

## Success Criteria
Loop, plate, coax, and busbar oracles converge; P-to-C conversion is performed only on the declared quotient and preserves terminal observables; reciprocal quasistatic fixtures meet stated symmetry/PSD laws while nonreciprocal/dispersive cases use their correct weaker contract; delayed scalar/vector terms satisfy continuity/gauge residuals; electrically large or rank-uncertain cases escalate/refuse; and no passivity claim for assembled/reduced circuits is inferred from extraction alone.

## Test Plan
Analytic inductance/capacitance; floating/disconnected conductors; reference and quotient changes; P inversion/pseudoinversion nullspace; reciprocal and nonreciprocal media; mesh/self-term refinement; skin/proximity limits; retarded continuity and Lorenz-gauge mutations; scalar-only/vector-only delay corruption; wavelength crossover; reciprocity/sign corruption; cancellation and replay.

## Considerations
Compression/FMM must preserve operator and continuity/gauge error. Retarded PEEC has stricter causality semantics than static partial elements. Energy symmetry claims do not apply universally to nonreciprocal or active media. Radiation is an exterior flux phenomenon handled in the power ledger, not a local material loss coefficient.

## Execution and evidence
Use safe Rust, typed SI quantities, stable geometry/terminal IDs, explicit quotient/gauge/material/media class, deterministic quadrature/reductions, bounded cancellation, and content-addressed receipts. Retain analytic oracles, G0 laws, G1 convergence, G2 benchmarks, retarded continuity/gauge falsifiers, and DSR artifacts. Ambition class [F].

title: I14.3b Stamp PEEC models with discrete power, positive-real, and causal semantics
description:
## Background
Extracted partial elements become useful only when stamped into MNA without losing charge/current conservation, reference invariance, field-to-circuit power, passivity, or causal delay semantics. Numerical identity can be exact algebraically while quadrature, solve, extraction, and model discrepancy remain bounded rather than zero. Radiation is boundary/Poynting outflow, not interchangeable with local dissipative loss. Sampled j-omega positivity is not a positive-real theorem in the analytic half-plane.

## Technical Approach
Map PEEC incidence, charge, flux, resistance, controlled sources, and delays into the canonical circuit descriptor with explicit reference quotient and initial/algebraic state. title: I14.8a Generate exact-discrete adjoints within admitted EMC model regimes
description:
## Background
EMC design variables affect MTL, PEEC, circuit, and full-wave solves through coupled geometry, materials, ports, solvers, and fidelity routing. Complex electromagnetic states usually feed real QoIs containing conjugation, norms, absolute values, power, and nonholomorphic material laws, so naive complex-step checks can be invalid. Reverse differentiation of the exact recorded iteration trace and an implicit adjoint of a converged discrete residual are also distinct when stopping, preconditioning, or active branches depend on tolerances.

## Technical Approach
Define independently admissible per-rung computational graphs for MTL, PEEC, circuit, and full-wave operators; lower rungs do not wait for every higher rung. For complex fields, freeze real-variable or Wirtinger derivatives, conjugate-transpose/inner-product convention, and real scalar objective semantics. Implement two typed adjoint lanes where valid: TraceAdjoint for the exact recorded discrete iteration/control-flow trace, and ImplicitResidualAdjoint for an admitted converged residual with differentiability/invertibility and inexact-solve terms. Generate route, shield, bond, termination, filter, ground, aperture, material, and smooth-geometry derivatives. Record primal/adjoint residuals, tolerances, active/router branches, units/scales, loss convention, and event identity. Emit NoGradient/SetValued/Unknown at topology, remesh, active-set, rung, or nonsmooth switches absent a proved generalized derivative.

## Success Criteria
Tangent-adjoint duality and Taylor remainder tests pass at multiple scales by default; finite-difference/dual independent checks agree within conditioning/error budgets. Complex-step is used only when the entire declared path and QoI are proved holomorphic; otherwise it is forbidden. Trace and implicit adjoints agree only under their stated convergence/branch hypotheses and remain separately identified. Discontinuities are localized with one-sided/set-valued evidence. Any cost claim independent of parameter count is scoped to a fixed number of scalar objectives and fixed state/operator regime.

## Test Plan
MTL route spacing, PEEC placement, shield impedance, bond/filter values, aperture geometry, grounding, multiport real power/norm QoIs, holomorphic synthetic complex path, conjugated/nonholomorphic QoI where complex-step must refuse, trace-vs-implicit tolerance sweep, inexact solves, preconditioner/state-dependent stopping, remesh/router/topology switches, corrupt checkpoints, cancellation, and unit-rescaling.

## Considerations
An exact discrete adjoint is exact only for its typed recorded algorithm or residual theorem. Shape derivatives require chart/material-transport conventions. Model discrepancy is separate. Fixed-objective adjoint cost does not imply parameter-independent end-to-end optimization cost.

## Execution and evidence
Carry complex derivative convention, objective count, rung/regime, operator/state hashes, tolerances, branch identities, units, budgets, deterministic reductions, cancellation, checkpoints, provenance, tangent/Taylor/independent checks, G0/G2/G3/G4 evidence, costs, and DSR artifacts. Ambition class [M].

title: I14.8b Model EMC uncertainty, discrepancy, and anytime-valid reliability objectives
description:
## Background
Nominally effective mitigation can fail under source spectra, harness placement, contact/bond state, material dispersion, manufacturing tolerances, measurement error, and fidelity-model discrepancy. These uncertainties have different semantics and dependence; collapsing them into independent Gaussian noise creates unearned reliability claims. Adaptive optimization also invalidates fixed-sample confidence unless optional stopping is handled.

## Technical Approach
Define a provenance-complete uncertainty model separating aleatory variability, epistemic intervals/sets, calibration uncertainty, spatial/process correlation, model-form discrepancy, and fidelity-router uncertainty. Propagate through admitted rungs using deterministic ensembles, QMC, interval/affine bounds, multifidelity control variates, or rare-event methods selected by declared assumptions. Form robust, distributionally robust, chance, and worst-case objectives with anytime-valid e-process/confidence semantics under adaptive sampling. Escalate when discrepancy or tail effective sample size exceeds budget.

## Success Criteria
Coverage/reliability claims meet preregistered calibration and adversarial optional-stopping tests; correlation and tail assumptions are explicit; held-out source/material/layout cases are not leaked into tuning; model-rung disagreement is a ledgered uncertainty term; and insufficient tail information yields Unknown or a conservative bound rather than a nominal percentile.

## Test Plan
Analytic linear-Gaussian and bounded cases; correlated harness/material variables; heavy tails and multimodality; rare emissions; source-spectrum shift; calibration drift; adaptive stopping; fidelity disagreement; interval-vs-Monte-Carlo containment; seed/thread-count determinism; and deliberately misspecified discrepancy.

## Considerations
No distribution-free finite-sample guarantee exists for every dependent/nonstationary process. State exchangeability, martingale, mixing, support, or ambiguity-set assumptions precisely. Compliance limits and measurement uncertainty must use the actual standard/test context.

## Execution and evidence
Carry units, distribution and dependence version, seeds, sample identities, fidelity route, budgets, provenance, and deterministic reduction. Retain null simulations, coverage curves, e-process stopping traces, discrepancy diagnostics, baseline comparisons, independent reproduction, and DSR evidence. Ambition class [M].

## Cancellation, drain, and resumability floor
Long loops poll the explicit asupersync Cx at bounded semantic chunks and record the achieved latency bound. Cancellation is request → drain owned/speculative work → finalize a non-Pass receipt; it cannot drop tasks, arenas, temporary artifacts, optimizer state, partial uncertainty samples, or checker branches. Save versioned resumable state where recomputation is material, verify checkpoint compatibility before resume/fork, and test cancellation before, during and after each expensive phase plus fault/cancel races. Partial results remain useful only with explicit incompleteness and no-claim effect.

title: I14.8c Optimize and independently validate robust EMC mitigations on held-out cases

An independent adjudicator reconstructs designs, reruns selected high-fidelity/physical-oracle cases, checks guard and uncertainty semantics, probes regime boundaries, and compares against fixed-budget catalog and ablation baselines.

## Success Criteria
At least one mitigation improves preregistered held-out EMC QoIs with uncertainty evidence while satisfying every guard, beats or explains failure against fair baselines, exposes model/rung switches and total compute, and reproduces independently.
