title: I05.2a Define exact fixed-point operation, cast, rounding, overflow, and evaluator semantics
description:
## Background
Range analysis and code generation are meaningless until the exact bit-level language is fixed. Signedness, intermediate width, multiply-accumulate behavior, shifts, casts, scaling, tie rules, saturation, traps, and modular wrap change both values and dynamics.

## Technical Approach
Define a versioned numeric semantics for every DeploymentTwinIR fixed-point operation and conversion, including operand/result widths, intermediate precision, scaling exponents, signed and unsigned behavior, round-to-nearest variants, directed rounding, shifts, narrowing casts, saturation, trap, and explicitly admitted modular arithmetic. Specify panic/refusal behavior and serialization independent of host integer overflow. Build a canonical arbitrary-precision evaluator and compact exhaustive truth tables that generated targets and all abstract transfer functions must reference. Treat wrap as modular dynamics and saturation as a nonlinear state update, never as interchangeable overflow policies.

## Success Criteria
Every operation has one unambiguous, host-independent result or structured fault; the canonical evaluator matches exhaustive hand oracles; equivalent encodings preserve semantics; missing policy cannot fall back favorably; toolchain or schema drift changes semantic identity. Downstream range and code generators cannot instantiate an operation without its semantics witness.

## Test Plan
Enumerate small widths, signed extrema, every rounding tie, shifts beyond width, rescale chains, multiply-accumulate intermediates, saturation/trap/wrap, casts, corrupted schemas, and deterministic serialization. Cross-check against independent arbitrary-precision arithmetic and mutation-test every default.

## Considerations
Bit-exact local semantics do not establish reachable ranges or closed-loop stability. They are the foundation those later claims quantify over.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit NumericSemanticsReceipt artifacts with operation tables, policy/version identities, reference vectors, fault behavior, and no-claim boundaries.

title: I05.2b Compile correlation-preserving range and reachable-set enclosures
description:
## Background
With exact numeric semantics fixed, each state, signal, parameter, intermediate, and declared fault still needs a dimensionally meaningful enclosure. Independent scalar extrema lose correlations, while feed-forward interval propagation alone cannot prove state reachability.

## Technical Approach
Lower DeploymentTwinIR domains into signedness, physical scaling, units, initial/fault sets, and interval, affine, Taylor, or admitted reachability objects parameterized by I05.2a semantics. Preserve correlations through arithmetic, casts, lookup tables, guards, resets, saturation, and mode transitions. Use directed rounding, deterministic domain splitting, inductive invariants for stateful fragments, and explicit widening with disclosed loss. Expose assumptions, correlation symbols, contraction steps, coverage horizon/invariant set, and source lineage. Route unsupported nonlinear regions to Unknown or bounded-floating fallback.

## Success Criteria
Every admitted operation and state update has a replayable enclosure; unit rescaling preserves the physical set; all reachable reduced-oracle states remain contained; correlations are neither discarded nor invented silently; fault envelopes are included; unsupported dynamics fail closed. A finite trace is never presented as a proof of reachability.

## Test Plan
Use correlated cancellations, nonlinear boundaries, recurrent state updates, mode guards/resets, nominal and fault envelopes, unit transformations, range-escape mutations, widening stress, cancellation during subdivision, and deterministic replay. Compare small finite-state systems with exhaustive reachability.

## Considerations
Containment and tightness are separate. Conservative widening may make width synthesis infeasible, which is an honest result rather than permission to contract unsafely.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit RangeEnclosureReceipt artifacts bound to exact numeric semantics, domains, method, correlations, directed error, horizons/invariants, budgets, and fallback decisions.

title: I05.2c Analyze coefficient quantization, feedback reachability, and limit cycles
description:
## Background
Feedback makes quantization a dynamical phenomenon. Coefficient rounding, saturation, modular wrap, deadbands, scheduling, and finite-state recurrence can create equilibria, oscillations, or instability that no feed-forward half-ulp budget captures.

## Technical Approach
Instantiate control and estimator fragments with I05.2a semantics and I05.2b initial/disturbance enclosures. Quantize coefficients and states explicitly, compute inductive reachable sets or finite-state abstractions where admitted, detect zero-input and forced limit cycles, and distinguish saturation, wrap, trap, and bounded-floating fallbacks. Preserve sampling and coefficient identities and expose approximation/refinement witnesses. For larger systems, combine invariant search, cycle detection, Lyapunov/IQC or adversarial traces under honest capability limits; return Unknown when no sound abstraction closes.

## Success Criteria
Supported feedback fixtures receive a replayable reachable invariant and cycle/stability classification; exhaustive reduced systems agree; coefficient-quantization and overflow-policy changes alter identity; hidden oscillations and modular-wrap mutations are detected; unsupported systems never inherit a feed-forward stability claim.

## Test Plan
Exercise integrators, IIR filters, PI/PID loops, observers, deadbands, saturation, modular wrap, coefficient perturbation, weakly damped and unstable quantized controllers, mode switches, disturbance sets, abstraction refinement, and cancellation/restart.

## Considerations
This task does not claim arbitrary nonlinear or hybrid stability. I05.6 composes numeric effects with plant, timing, I/O, and fault refinement.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit QuantizedDynamicsReceipt with reachable invariants, cycle witnesses, abstraction/refinement error, sampling and controller identities, counterexamples, and explicit Unknown states.

## Deterministic execution floor
Assign semantic logical work identities to every frequency, mode, parameter point, branch, profile slice, matrix block, target artifact, and reduction tile rather than deriving identity from worker order. Deterministic mode uses stable traversal, fixed-shape reductions, deterministic pivot/tie/cluster/branch rules, counter-based RNG where relevant, and versioned serialization. Test thread, shard, schedule, resume and same-ISA replay matrices; any permitted fast-mode or cross-ISA divergence is classified, bounded and ledgered rather than silently accepted.

title: I05.2d Optimize word lengths under numeric, memory, timing, and capability budgets
description:
## Background
Choosing the widest type everywhere defeats embedded timing, memory, energy, and hardware budgets, while greedy narrowing can violate range, closed-loop, overflow, or QoI constraints. The synthesis problem is mixed discrete, multiobjective, and sometimes infeasible.

## Technical Approach
Search integer and fractional widths, scales, intermediate precision, coefficient formats, and overflow policies subject to I05.2b reachable enclosures, I05.2c feedback obligations, quantization-error, memory, execution-time, instruction-set, and capability budgets. Use deterministic constraint propagation, lower bounds, branch-and-bound or admitted heuristic incumbents, and explicit Pareto/tie rules. Preserve a conservative baseline and every feasible incumbent. Return Infeasible with a minimal conflicting-budget/evidence explanation; never relax constraints, widen budgets, or change overflow semantics silently. Keep estimated target costs distinct from measured timing or WCET proof.

## Success Criteria
All emitted policies satisfy source enclosures, feedback obligations, and declared budgets; deterministic ties replay; under-width and contradictory cases return structured Infeasible; relaxing a budget cannot invalidate a feasible incumbent; every constraint traces to exact operations and target capabilities. Any global-optimum claim carries a closed bound; otherwise report incumbent and gap/no-claim.

## Test Plan
Compare exhaustive optima on small graphs, accumulator and feedback bottlenecks, mixed signedness, memory/time tradeoffs, unsupported instructions, Pareto ties, infeasible budgets, heuristic cutoff/cancellation, checkpoint/resume, and hidden-budget-relaxation mutations.

## Considerations
Target timing models are synthesis inputs, not WCET certificates. A best found policy is not automatically globally optimal.

title: I05.2e Independently certify numeric semantics, reachability, dynamics, and width policy
description:
## Background
The semantics, range, feedback, and width engines can share a mistaken cast, correlation, reachability, or overflow assumption. A structurally independent terminal checker is required before target code, timing analysis, or refinement consumes a synthesized policy.

## Technical Approach
Reconstruct policies from serialized receipts and independently evaluate reduced domains with exhaustive finite-state enumeration and larger cases with arbitrary-precision differential, interval, invariant, and adversarial oracles. Check bit-level operations, enclosure/reachable-set containment, coefficient quantization, cycle classifications, local error composition, budget satisfaction, deterministic tie breaking, and Infeasible explanations. Retain every escaping state or contradictory evaluation as a version-scoped falsifier.

## Success Criteria
All promoted policies have an independently reproducible admission receipt; exhaustive fixtures agree bit-for-bit and state-for-state; no declared nominal/fault state escapes; correlation-loss, rounding, wrap, saturation, overflow, limit-cycle, and silent-budget-relaxation mutations are killed. Checker disagreement blocks all consumers and localizes the smallest semantics, transfer, dynamics, or optimization boundary.

## Test Plan
Use independent big-integer arithmetic, exhaustive small finite systems, random/adversarial traces, correlated cancellation, feedback cycles, under-width policies, stale target profiles, corrupted receipts, cancellation/fault finalization, and same-ISA thread-count replay.

## Considerations
Campaign traces supplement but never replace reachability proof. This receipt certifies fixed-point policy semantics and declared dynamics only; plant-level equivalence and target timing remain separate.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. FixedPointAdmissionReceipt is the terminal I05.2 artifact. Preserve all failed policies, counterexamples, evidence states, and no-claim boundaries.

title: I05.3 Generate reproducible bounded-memory no_std target Rust and trace maps
description:
## Background
Deployment code must preserve evaluation order, rounding, scheduler, state, and monitors without hidden allocators, OS calls, FFI, or nondeterministic runtime behavior.

## Technical Approach
Emit no_std safe Rust plus manifest, source-to-IR trace map, static memory layout, schedule, fixed/bounded numeric operations, checkpoints, monitors, target capabilities, and canonical vectors. Bind compiler/toolchain/target hashes and provide an interpreter for differential checking.

## Success Criteria

## Test Plan
Interpreter differential replay, generated-operation mutations, compiler/version drift, host/target emulator, state checkpoint, build reproducibility, and feature-disable baseline.

## Considerations
A compiler bug is part of the TCB; independent vectors and target execution are mandatory.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default with layer-correct dependencies. Carry typed units/quantity kinds, frames, clocks, stable identities, seeds, versions, validity/error/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, evidence state, asupersync cancellation/drain, deterministic scheduling/reductions/ties, checkpoint/resume, and structured trace/ledger events. ## Ambition and promotion

Preserve negative results.

title: I05.3a Define target ABI, capability, static-layout, and generated-runtime contracts
description:
## Background
Reproducible target generation requires a closed target contract before emitting code: data layout, ABI, allowed language/runtime subset, memory sections, clocks, schedules, capabilities, monitors, checkpoints, faults, and forbidden facilities must be explicit rather than inferred from a host build.

## Technical Approach
Define TargetProfile and GeneratedRuntimeContract artifacts binding ISA/ABI, endianness, alignment, stack and static-memory limits, linker sections, clock/timer model, scheduling interface, atomic/memory-model support, panic/fault policy, monitor and checkpoint ABI, permitted no_std library surface, compiler/linker versions, and capability guards. Specify the deterministic lowering order from DeploymentTwinIR and the exact boundary to audited HAL adapters. Reject ambiguous target features, undeclared runtime services, layout overflow, and incompatible checkpoint schemas before generation.

## Success Criteria
Every generated artifact is admitted by a complete target profile; layout and ABI are deterministic; forbidden allocation, OS, FFI, synchronization, and dynamic-loading facilities are machine-checkable; toolchain/target drift changes identity; unsupported profiles return actionable refusal. The contract is sufficient for an independent interpreter, linker audit, and WCET consumer.

## Test Plan
Use multiple endian/alignment profiles, missing atomics/timers, stack/static overflow, incompatible ABI, unsupported panic behavior, clock ambiguity, feature toggles, schema drift, deterministic serialization, and cancellation during admission.

## Considerations
A target profile describes an assumed platform; it does not prove the silicon, compiler, or board conforms. Later children measure and audit those boundaries.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit versioned TargetProfile, GeneratedRuntimeContract, and layout/schedule manifests with exact capabilities, budgets, identities, and no-claim boundaries.

title: I05.3b Generate safe bounded-memory no_std Rust and deterministic schedules
description:
## Background
Deployment code must preserve evaluation order, bit-level numeric semantics, scheduler state, guards, monitors, and checkpoints without hidden allocation or nondeterministic runtime behavior.

## Technical Approach
Generate safe no_std Rust for state, I05.2-admitted numeric operations, evaluation order, time steps, mode transitions, monitors, safe fallbacks, checkpoints, and deterministic schedules. Use statically bounded storage and queues, explicit error/fault values, bounded loops or proved loop variants, capability-gated operations, and no hidden allocator, OS service, FFI, dynamic dispatch, unbounded lock, or host-dependent overflow. Preserve semantic operation identity through emitted source. Make cancellation a generation-time concern and define target runtime abort/finalization at admitted boundaries.

## Success Criteria
Generated code type-checks for pinned targets, uses only the admitted subset, has statically bounded memory/control flow, reproduces IR order and I05.2 semantics, and exposes all monitor/fallback paths. Feature-disabled generation retains a conservative baseline. Unsupported constructs fail before source emission.

## Test Plan
Differentially mutate operations/order/scales/guards; scan forbidden symbols/features; test maximal static layouts, bounded loops/queues, checkpoint code paths, compiler-version drift, deterministic regeneration, and generated-source review. Use property cases over small IR programs.

## Considerations
Safe source alone does not prove bounded stack/ISR behavior or final binary equivalence. HAL, linker, object, and target evidence are separate children.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit canonical source plus a GeneratedSourceReceipt bound to IR, numeric-policy, target-profile, generator, feature, and toolchain identities.

title: I05.3c Certify bounded runtime, linker layout, ISR/DMA/queue behavior, and HAL isolation
description:
## Background
A no_std source file can still overflow stack, deadlock through atomics, overrun queues, suffer ISR nesting or DMA races, tear checkpoints, or rely on unsafe MMIO behavior. Those target-bound effects must be owned explicitly rather than hidden behind code generation.

## Technical Approach
Define and audit static/stack/linker maps, call-depth and ISR-nesting bounds, queue/ring capacities, DMA ownership and cache/coherency rules, atomics and memory ordering, panic/fault behavior, checkpoint atomicity, brownout/torn-write recovery, and restart permissions. Quarantine unavoidable MMIO or vendor unsafe code behind the smallest versioned HAL facade with documented invariants and independent capability tests; keep generated core code safe. Bind each boundary to TargetProfile and emitted source/object identities and provide fail-closed behavior when a target cannot supply the promised primitive.

## Success Criteria
Static and stack budgets include worst admitted nesting; all buffers and queues have overflow policy; DMA/ISR/atomic interactions have race and ordering receipts; checkpoint commit/recovery is transactional; no undeclared symbol or unsafe region enters the generated core. HAL mismatch or missing capability blocks deployment.

## Test Plan
Stress ISR nesting, queue overflow, DMA races, cache visibility, weak-memory reorderings, linker relocation, stack maxima, panic/brownout, torn checkpoint writes, reset during commit, stale HAL versions, and feature-off emulation. Include G4 fault/cancellation and deterministic recovery.

## Considerations
This task does not certify arbitrary vendor firmware or hardware. Unsafe MMIO is an audited leaf boundary, never a shortcut around Rust ownership or concurrency design.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit BoundedRuntimeReceipt and HalBoundaryReceipt with linker/stack/ISR/DMA/queue proofs, unsafe inventory, recovery protocol, target identity, and explicit no-claim states.

title: I05.3d Emit content-addressed packages and source-to-object-to-binary trace maps
description:
## Background
Source-level lineage is insufficient for timing and deployment assurance. Optimization, inlining, linking, relaxation, dead stripping, and section placement can sever the connection from an IR operation to final object symbols, binary addresses, control-flow paths, and proof obligations.

## Technical Approach
Produce canonical package manifests and bidirectional trace maps from DeploymentTwinIR operations through generated source spans, compiler intermediate identities where available, object symbols/relocations, linked sections and addresses, and normalized binary control-flow graph hashes. Bind compiler, linker, flags, libraries, target, linker script, feature set, and reproducible-build environment. Represent one-to-many and eliminated/fused mappings honestly, including Unknown when optimization prevents a justified mapping. Version schemas and migrations without rewriting historic artifacts.

## Success Criteria
Every load-bearing binary region traces to source/IR or an admitted runtime/HAL component; every IR operation reports its binary realization or explicit elimination/Unknown; rebuilds under pinned inputs are byte-identical or carry a stated semantic equivalence receipt; missing/extra symbols and trace discontinuities block WCET and promotion.

## Test Plan
Exercise inlining, fusion, dead-code elimination, linker relaxation, LTO on/off, symbol stripping, section reorder, compiler drift, stale maps, injected foreign symbols, reproducible builds, migration replay, and CFG-hash mutation.

## Considerations
Debug metadata alone is not a proof-quality trace map. Some aggressive optimizations may require disabling the transform or accepting Unknown.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit content-addressed DeploymentPackage, BinaryIdentityReceipt, and IRSourceObjectBinaryTrace with exact toolchain and migration lineage.

## Deterministic execution floor
Assign semantic logical work identities to every frequency, mode, parameter point, branch, profile slice, matrix block, target artifact, and reduction tile rather than deriving identity from worker order. Deterministic mode uses stable traversal, fixed-shape reductions, deterministic pivot/tie/cluster/branch rules, counter-based RNG where relevant, and versioned serialization. Test thread, shard, schedule, resume and same-ISA replay matrices; any permitted fast-mode or cross-ISA divergence is classified, bounded and ledgered rather than silently accepted.

title: I05.3e Build an independent interpreter, canonical vectors, and emulator differential harness
description:
## Background
A compiler can reproduce its own mistake consistently. Promotion needs a structurally separate executable semantics and canonical target vectors that do not reuse production lowering or generated operations.

## Technical Approach
Implement an independent DeploymentTwinIR interpreter parameterized by I05.2 numeric semantics and TargetProfile timing-independent behavior. Generate canonical state, I/O, monitor, fault, and checkpoint vectors; execute them on the interpreter, host-compiled generated code, admitted emulator, and pinned target when available. Compare bitwise where required or with a directed certified bound. Exercise pause/resume, safe fallback, feature-off baseline, stale inputs, and fault transitions. Keep oracle code, fixtures, and review ownership separate from the generator.

## Success Criteria
Interpreter, generated host path, emulator, and target agree for all admitted vectors; injected generator defects are caught; checkpoint/resume and fault paths reproduce; platform differences are classified rather than hidden in tolerance. No target unavailability is mistaken for conformance.

## Test Plan
Use arithmetic and state-machine microprograms, randomized bounded IR, rounding/overflow edges, mode events, monitors, checkpoint interruption, compiler mutations, emulator/target discrepancies, corrupted vectors, and G5 thread-count replay.

## Considerations
Interpreter agreement proves implemented semantics for tested/admitted programs, not compiler correctness for arbitrary Rust. It complements binary trace and runtime-bound evidence.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit CanonicalTargetVectorSet and DifferentialExecutionReceipt with independent implementation identity, exact inputs, traces, discrepancies, and evidence states.

title: I05.3f Adjudicate reproducibility, bounded runtime, traceability, and target conformance
description:
## Background
Source generation, runtime bounds, binary lineage, and independent execution each prove different facts. A terminal receipt must prevent one favorable lane from masking a missing linker, HAL, checkpoint, trace, or target-conformance obligation.

## Technical Approach
Independently assemble the target contract, generated source, bounded-runtime/HAL receipt, content-addressed binary trace, and differential vectors. Rebuild under pinned tools, audit forbidden runtime symbols and unsafe boundaries, verify stack/static/queue/checkpoint claims, traverse IR-to-binary lineage, and replay interpreter/emulator/target comparisons. ## Success Criteria
Regeneration is byte-reproducible or covered by a justified semantic receipt; no undeclared runtime dependency or unsafe core path exists; memory and recovery bounds close; load-bearing binary regions trace correctly; independent execution agrees; missing target evidence remains Unknown. Any failure blocks downstream WCET, HIL, refinement, and I05 gate promotion.

## Test Plan

## Considerations
This certifies only pinned target profiles and toolchains. It does not claim universal compiler correctness, WCET, or closed-loop refinement.

## Execution and evidence

title: I05.4 Produce static/compositional WCET, jitter, and measured-tail evidence
description:
## Background

## Technical Approach

Start with exact/simple-pipeline or scratchpad targets and exhaustive paths; then explore cache/pipeline/interrupt-aware abstract interpretation and compositional theorem cards. Bind binary hash, target fingerprint, memory map, clock, interrupts/DMA, path coverage, and assumptions.

## Success Criteria
Applicable static bounds dominate every legal measured execution; assumption violation automatically demotes; unanalysed paths remain Unknown; measured tails are never called bounds; deadline composition includes I/O and scheduler jitter.

## Test Plan
Hand-solvable kernels, exhaustive reduced targets, alignment/cache conflict, interrupt/DMA storms, clock error, path mutation, and a legal bound violation falsifier.

## Considerations
No universal WCET claim for arbitrary processors or programs. Preserve measured-tail baseline when proof is unavailable.

## Repository-wide implementation contract
Use safe Rust by default with layer-correct dependencies. Carry typed units/quantity kinds, frames, clocks, stable identities, seeds, versions, validity/error/time/memory/capability budgets, provenance, evidence state, asupersync cancellation/drain, deterministic scheduling/reductions/ties, checkpoint/resume, and structured trace/ledger events. Update CONTRACT.md, run the applicable DSR quality lane, retain exact artifacts and target/machine fingerprints, and state scientific, deployment, manufacturing, privacy, and performance no-claim boundaries.

## Ambition and promotion

Preserve negative results.

title: I05.4a Prove target-qualified static WCET for admitted binaries and memory regimes
description:
## Background
Worst-case execution time is a property of a particular binary, target microarchitecture, memory map/state model, clock regime, and environmental assumptions—not source code in the abstract. General out-of-order processors with uncontrolled caches and DMA may defeat tight static proof, but exact/simple targets and sharply admitted regions can support bold certified bounds.

## Technical Approach
Define StaticWcetBound with binary hash, target and stepping fingerprint, instruction/timing model, memory map, cache/scratchpad policy, alignment, branch/path model, initial-state set, clock bounds, and proof TCB. Implement exact exhaustive analysis for reduced/simple targets, then abstract interpretation, IPET/path constraints, cache/pipeline analysis, and compositional microkernel lemmas for admitted complex targets. Independently validate decoder, control-flow recovery, infeasible-path claims, and timing tables. Demote automatically when firmware, linker layout, microcode, clock, cache policy, or hardware assumptions drift.

## Success Criteria
For admitted finite/exhaustive fixtures, the bound equals or safely dominates every legal execution; for larger fixtures it carries a checkable derivation and explicit slack. Unknown instructions, indirect control flow, uncertain timing, self-modification, uncontrolled DMA/cache state, or assumption drift yield Unknown/NotApplicable. Every seeded legal bound violation refutes the certificate.

## Test Plan
Hand-solvable basic blocks and loops; exhaustive reduced processors; alignment and cache conflicts; branch predictors; indirect calls; compiler/linker mutations; instruction-table errors; scratchpad versus cache; clock tolerance; DMA interference; binary hash changes; proof corruption; deterministic/cancellation replay.

## Considerations
No universal tight WCET claim is made. Hardware vendor timing claims are inputs, not automatically trusted theorems. Sound loose bounds remain useful if resource and deadline decisions record their pessimism.

## Execution and evidence
Use safe Rust checkers, target-qualified schemas, exact units/clocks, deterministic paths/ties, bounded cancellation, content-addressed binaries/models/proofs, and explicit TCB. Retain G0 checker laws, G2 known targets, G3 layout/clock metamorphics, independent exhaustive or FPGA/trace spot checks, and DSR evidence. Ambition class [M].

title: I05.4b Compose task WCET with scheduler, interrupt, DMA, I/O, and clock deadlines
description:
## Background
Even a sound task WCET does not bound closed-loop response when release jitter, preemption, blocking, interrupts, DMA/bus contention, sensor/actuator conversion, queues, communication, clocks, fault handling, and emergency-stop paths contribute. End-to-end timing needs a compositional theorem over the deployed schedule and hardware envelope.

## Technical Approach
Define CompositionalWcetBound and response-time/jitter receipts over tasks, priorities or time partitions, precedence, locks/resources, interrupt service, DMA/bus arbitration, I/O and network stages, clock drift/synchronization, mode changes, and overload/fault policies. Implement exact/simple schedule analysis first, then fixed-priority/EDF/time-triggered and network-calculus-style modules with explicit assumptions. Compose task bounds and blocking/interference lemmas into end-to-end sensor-to-actuator and fault-to-safe-state deadlines; produce minimal critical chains and admission diagnostics.

## Success Criteria
Canonical schedules reproduce analytic response times; every admitted execution trace lies within release/completion/jitter envelopes; emergency and degraded modes are included; incompatible scheduler/resource assumptions refuse; and a mutated interrupt, DMA, blocking, queue, or clock term causes proof failure. Output separates static proof, configured margin, and observed timing.

## Test Plan
Fixed-priority and EDF task sets, time-triggered schedules, priority inversion, nested interrupts, DMA/bus bursts, sensor/actuator latency, network queues, clock drift, deadline miss, overload/fault modes, multicore interference envelope, compositional associativity, cancellation, and proof corruption.

## Considerations
Multicore shared-resource interference may require conservative envelopes or target-specific isolation. A scheduler theorem says nothing about unmodeled firmware or vendor driver behavior; those paths must be in the admitted boundary or out of the proof.

## Execution and evidence
Bind exact deployment configuration, task/binary hashes, timing-model versions, clocks, budgets, critical-chain witnesses, provenance, and deterministic replay. Retain analytic oracle cases, adversarial schedules, independent checker results, G2/G3/G4 evidence, and DSR artifacts. Ambition class [M].

title: I05.4c Run pinned-target measured-tail and adversarial latency campaigns
description:
## Background
Measurement cannot prove a worst case, but pinned-target tail campaigns are essential for finding missing paths, invalid hardware assumptions, pathological interference, and regressions. This bead independently produces empirical evidence; it does not wait for or reconcile static/compositional proofs, and it never calls an observed percentile or maximum WCET.

## Technical Approach
Run preregistered campaigns on exact binary/target/configuration identities with synchronized hardware timestamps, trace/path coverage, warm/cold initial states, cache/alignment variants, interrupt/DMA/bus/I/O/network storms, clock/environment monitoring, thermal/frequency regimes, and fault/overload modes. Report p50/p95/p99/p99.9/p99.999 with dependence-aware uncertainty, censoring/loss, effective sample size, instrumentation error, and optional-stopping policy. Use bounded adversarial search to maximize latency and discover rare legal paths while preserving raw immutable traces. Export MeasuredTailReceipt only; I05.4d owns proof reconciliation.

## Success Criteria
Every measurement binds binary, target stepping, linker layout, clock, scheduler, interference, instrumentation, environment, and campaign identity. Percentiles carry uncertainty/effective support and are never upper bounds. Preregistered modes are covered or explicitly missing; rare injected paths are found within the declared campaign; timestamp/trace loss is quantified; and independent replay reproduces summaries. Insufficient support yields Unknown.

## Test Plan
Known synthetic timing distributions, hand-timed kernels, alignment/cache/branch sweeps, interrupts/DMA/bus/network/I/O bursts, clock perturbation, thermal throttling, rare path injection, binary/config drift, optional stopping, dependent samples, censoring/trace loss, instrumentation overhead, cancellation, and deterministic analysis replay.

## Considerations
Absence of a violation is not proof. Extreme percentile estimation requires dependence-aware intervals and no extrapolation beyond evidence. Instrumentation and clock synchronization are explicit errors. ScaleQualification is related benchmark evidence, not a prerequisite for the campaign.

## Execution and evidence

description:
## Background

## Technical Approach

## Success Criteria

## Considerations

## Execution and evidence

## Test Plan
Parameter-reparameterization invariance, known sloppy models, rank-deficient/noisy/censored data, prior sensitivity, fabrication tolerance, sensor saturation, model-selection calibration, and blind recovery.

## Considerations
Local Fisher information is not global identifiability. A well-identified wrong law remains wrong; preserve discrepancy and alternative-model evidence.

title: I11.3a Define campaign hazards, authority, residual energy, envelopes, and minimum-risk states
description:
## Background
Safe experimental control begins before code generation: the campaign must name hazards, stored/residual energy, operating envelopes, detection and actuation paths, operator authority, independent emergency authority, and minimum-risk states. Waiting on a flagship-level assurance program would invert the architecture.

## Technical Approach
Compile ContextOfUse and campaign intent into a narrow SafetyProtocolContract covering electrical capacitor/inductor energy, rotating inertia, elastic energy, pressure/vacuum, thermal and chemical hazards, moving hardware, environmental exposure, and data-integrity hazards. Define typed limits, warning/trip margins, detection-to-compute-to-communication-to-actuator latency budgets, sensor/actuator fault assumptions, latching/reset permissives, operator roles, hardware-enforced interlocks, common-cause independence assumptions, residual-energy verification, and minimum-risk/de-energized states. Link broader hazard/assurance artifacts when available without making them a circular prerequisite.

## Success Criteria
Every excitation and failure mode maps to named hazards and bounded authority; safe/minimum-risk states include residual energy and verification criteria; software cannot override independent emergency authority; missing containment or independence is explicit Uncontained/Unknown; reset and restart require positive permissives.

## Test Plan
Model capacitor discharge, spinning rotor, pressure/thermal cooldown, stuck sensors/actuators, common-cause loss, delayed detection, emergency stop, operator conflict, brownout, unsafe reset, and missing hardware enforcement.

## Considerations
This contract does not certify a stand or replace trained operators, hardware review, or the wider safety program. It supplies the prerequisite that those programs and runtimes refine.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit CampaignHazardContract and HardwareSafetyObligationReceipt with hazards, authorities, latency/energy budgets, assumptions, uncontained states, and provenance.

title: I11.3b Lower campaigns into timed/superdense protocol automata without inventing event order
description:
## Background
Excitation, settling, triggers, acquisition, holds, and completion occur on multiple clocks with bounded uncertainty and simultaneous events. Forcing a deterministic total order can hide unsafe interleavings even if one replay is repeatable.

## Technical Approach
Lower ExperimentCampaignIR into a timed or superdense SafetyProtocolIR with excitation, settling, arming, trigger, acquisition, hold, completion, and synchronization modes. Preserve physical/logical clocks, timestamp uncertainty, simultaneity, partial-order constraints, deadlines, nondeterministic environment choices, and deterministic tie rules only where the contract truly orders events. Enumerate or symbolically cover all admissible interleavings; if that set exceeds capability or contains an unsafe ambiguity, fail safe. Bind signals, channels, control-runtime interfaces, and replay identity.

## Success Criteria
All admitted schedules preserve required settling/trigger/acquisition relations; clock uncertainty expands behavior rather than being erased; no unsafe interleaving is hidden by arbitrary serialization; restart identities are stable; unsupported concurrency returns structured refusal. Replays reproduce the same set/receipt, not merely one chosen trace.

## Test Plan
Use simultaneous triggers, skewed clocks, out-of-order packets, skipped settling, deadline ties, nondeterministic device latency, partial orders, reordered independent events, state explosion, cancellation, and deterministic set-level replay.

## Considerations
Determinism means reproducible semantics and exploration, not inventing a physical order where none is justified.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit TimedCampaignProtocolReceipt with automaton, clocks, admissible partial orders/interleavings, deadlines, capability bounds, and refusal states.

title: I11.3c Implement interlock, abort, drain, de-energization, recovery, and restart transactions
description:
## Background
An abort is not a dropped task. The system must detect hazards, latch interlocks, stop excitation, drain computation/I/O, remove or contain energy, verify the minimum-risk state, preserve evidence, and permit recovery only under explicit authority.

## Technical Approach
Compose the campaign hazard contract and timed protocol into interlock, trip, abort, bounded-drain, de-energization, residual-energy verification, safe/minimum-risk, recovery, and restart transactions. Account for detection, compute, communication, and actuator latency; stuck/missing sensors or actuators; brownout and torn persistent state; independent emergency paths; latching and reset permissives; operator handoff; and cancellation/fault finalization. Specify idempotency and checkpoint/commit semantics. Emit hardware-unenforced obligations rather than treating software behavior as containment.

## Success Criteria
Every declared reachable fault reaches a verified minimum-risk state within its bound or an explicit Uncontained result; abort drains and records all owned resources; loss of power or partial writes cannot authorize unsafe restart; independent emergency authority remains available; repeated commands are idempotent.

## Test Plan
Inject stuck actuator/sensor, delayed trip, communication loss, queue backlog, operator abort, power loss, torn checkpoint, residual energy, reset races, common-cause failure, cancellation storms, and recovery/restart mutations.

## Considerations
I11.3 authors campaign-level SafetyProtocolIR. I05.5c and I11.4 lower it into deployment and device runtimes; they do not redefine the safety intent.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit SafeTransitionReceipt and RecoveryTransactionReceipt with latency/energy closure, latches/permissives, idempotency, remaining obligations, and exact event lineage.

title: I11.3d Verify a conservative timed/hybrid abstraction for reachability, liveness, and refinement
description:
## Background
Finite model checking is meaningful only if the abstraction conservatively covers the continuous/hybrid plant, clocks, delays, faults, and residual-energy dynamics. A tiny automaton with no refinement witness can prove the wrong system safe.

## Technical Approach
Construct a conservative timed/hybrid abstraction of SafetyProtocolIR and declared plant/envelope dynamics. Prove or bound simulation/refinement from concrete states and disturbances into abstract transitions, including interval clocks, latency, energy decay, stuck components, partial-order events, brownout, and nondeterministic environment action. Check reachability of unsafe states, bounded response, deadlock/livelock, eventual drain/minimum-risk state, latching/reset properties, and authority separation. Refine counterexamples or return Unknown when the abstraction is too coarse.

## Success Criteria
Every promoted property cites a conservative abstraction/refinement receipt; all declared faults are covered; unsafe abstract traces are replayable/refinable; spurious counterexamples are classified; no property is inferred when refinement or bound fails; model-check runs are deterministic and cancellation-correct.

## Test Plan
Use hand-proved timed fixtures, continuous energy decay, latency intervals, partial orders, deadlocks, livelocks, unsafe reset, spurious/real counterexamples, abstraction refinement, state explosion, cancellation/resume, and mutation of omitted transitions/faults.

## Considerations
This is scoped computer-assisted verification, not universal hybrid-system decidability. Unknown is a valid and load-bearing outcome.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [F]. Emit SafetyAbstractionReceipt and ProtocolModelCheckReceipt with concrete/abstract relation, covered assumptions, properties, counterexamples, refinements, and no-claim states.

title: I11.3e Independently fault-inject and adjudicate safe protocol and hardware obligations
description:
## Background
The hazard model, timed protocol, runtime transaction, and formal abstraction can share omitted faults or optimistic latency/authority assumptions. Independent fault injection must ratify both behavior and the honesty of remaining hardware obligations.

## Technical Approach
Build a separate checker and campaign harness that reconstruct hazards, event partial orders, latency and residual-energy budgets, interlocks/latches/permissives, abort/drain/recovery behavior, and abstraction coverage. Inject faults in virtual-HIL or admitted hardware fixtures without reusing production transition code. ## Success Criteria

## Test Plan

description:
## Background

All three representations agree within combined producer, conversion, and independent-check budgets where jointly applicable; stable and unstable canonical candidates survive; near recurrence, collocation underresolution, and harmonic aliasing are each caught; phase/time/segment/mesh transformations preserve observables; disagreement is localized rather than averaged away; and resource exhaustion never yields Consensus. No existence, uniqueness, stability, or basin claim is emitted.

## Test Plan
Harmonic oscillator, Van der Pol, forced Duffing, relative rotor, constrained periodic DAE, unstable orbit, subharmonic cycle, near recurrence, stiff layer, aliasing/truncation, phase/time shift, mesh/segment refinement, blind producer outputs, shared-sign mutation, artifact corruption, cancellation storms, and deterministic replay.

A free autonomous harmonic oscillator is an amplitude/energy family. A phase condition removes time translation but does not remove amplitude degeneracy. ## Background

Topology and gauge invariance alone do not determine constitutive stress or force: a material action or free energy, controlled electrical variables, boundary and corner terms, and a deformation law are indispensable. The Hodge star generally does not preserve an integral lattice, so constitutive metric data cannot silently be treated as an endomorphism of integral differential cohomology.

## Technical Approach
Formulate the conservative core on an oriented and time-oriented spacetime worldtube with terminals, interfaces, and corners as relative pairs. State the degree convention explicitly: a U(1) connection or differential character with curvature F versus its spatial reductions. Bind coefficient lattice or real variant, singular-current policy, gauge group, and twisted excitation/current objects. Couple the character to a real constitutive operator and circuit ports without claiming that the material Hodge map preserves characteristic classes. Pull back along material motion and derive Faraday-Reynolds transgression and motional EMF on material loops and worldsheets. Vary the on-shell discrete and continuum action under admissible spacetime/material diffeomorphisms to derive stress-energy, net force and torque, terminal work, interface/corner traction, and the exact power identity. ## Success Criteria

Gauge, representative, basis, tree, cut, and frame changes preserve net observables. Direct FEEC-circuit assembly, Maxwell or declared material stress, virtual work, and the theorem path produce intersecting guaranteed force/torque enclosures on admitted conservative fixtures. Boundary and corner terms close power. A seeded Hodge-lattice claim, omitted terminal Legendre term, wrong motional-EMF sign, or hidden dissipative state is rejected. Local stress nonuniqueness is allowed while net force remains invariant under the stated hypotheses.

## Test Plan
G0 exact-sequence, gauge, and pairing identities; static capacitor and magnetic-gap fixed-control sign oracles; linked moving loop and Faraday disk; rigid and deforming ALE worldtubes; air/material interface and corner traction; coefficient-lattice counterexamples; Hodge-star lattice nonpreservation; topology-stable motion; direct force-bound cross-check; gauge/tree/cut/frame changes; and formal assumption deletion.

## Considerations
This is intentionally a strong theorem target. If a universal material-force statement fails, preserve the counterexample and prove the maximal conservative, linear, reciprocal, or topology-stable theorem that survives. Do not infer force from topology alone, confuse circle-valued holonomy with an unwrapped engineering linkage, or promote method agreement to physical validation.

## Theorem-lane execution contract
Separate theorem truth, formal kernel checking, discrete conformance, numerical enclosure, and physical validation. title: RA.F1 Specify the spacetime relative-character worldtube and action vocabulary
description:

## Technical Approach

State the differential-character degree convention and spatial reductions. Specify coefficient lattice or real variant; gauge group and terminal trivializations; singular-current policy; curvature, characteristic, cycle and terminal pairings; twisted and untwisted sources; pullback/pushforward domains; material motion and topology-stable assumptions; units, signs, frames, and provenance. Produce a machine-readable theorem-object schema and lemma graph.

## Success Criteria
Every force-theorem object has unambiguous type, degree, coefficient, domain, orientation, and boundary behavior. Four-dimensional objects cannot be substituted for spatial reductions. Gauge, representative, cut, period-basis, and frame transformations execute. Unsupported singularity, topology change, or boundary decomposition fails admission.

## Test Plan

title: RB EPIC — nonnormal/Krein spectral foundry for machines
description:
## Background

Then develop polynomial/nonlinear eigenproblem and structure-preserving linearization objects, nonnormal Arnoldi/Schur and validated enclosures, Krein signatures/collisions, exceptional-point tracking, Floquet/Evans/dispersion objects, pseudospectra, resolvent and transient-growth bounds, and conjectured unifying spectral certificates.

## Test Plan
Defective/Jordan matrices, clustered/repeated spectra, nearly normal limits, structure-preserving perturbations, spectral pollution traps, contour/winding checks, high-precision oracle spots, and cancellation/resume.

## Considerations
Never encode degenerate as a healthy unit gap. Eigenvalues alone do not bound transient growth; solver convergence does not prove spectral completeness.

This issue is self-contained but must obey the FrankenSim substrate: safe Rust by default; layer-correct dependencies; typed units; explicit seeds, accuracy/time/memory/capability budgets, versions, and artifact identities; asupersync Cx cancellation with bounded polling and request-drain-finalize semantics; deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tree reductions in deterministic mode; structured trace/ledger events rather than casual printing; content-addressed replay; and a crate CONTRACT.md before becoming a dependency target. The production-default path remains on a named boring baseline until a feature-gated candidate records: current primary-reference status; assumptions and monitored validity domain; quantitative activation metric; quantitative kill criterion; schema-compatible fallback; p50/p95/p99 time and memory cost (initially explicitly unmeasured); retained adversarial falsifier; and an independently replayable reproduction pack. description:
## Background

More broadly, the current routing vocabulary can let symmetric algorithms or gap heuristics escape their admitted domain and be misapplied to nonnormal, polynomial, monodromy, or indefinite structured problems. ## Technical Approach
Define `SpectralProblemClass` for self-adjoint/generalized, nonnormal, polynomial/QEP, Hamiltonian/symplectic/J-self-adjoint, monodromy/Floquet, and operator-function cases. Define set-valued clusters, algebraic/geometric multiplicity where available, separation, `DegenerateCluster`, `Unknown`, partial, and explicit no-claim states. Correct the zero-spread/gap defect; require operator-property witnesses before routing; fail closed when the class, metric, regularity, or separation assumptions are absent. Preserve historical receipts byte-for-byte while adding a versioned migration/view layer.

## Success Criteria
`[a,a]`, zero Laplacian modes, clustered/repeated and defective cases cannot produce false healthy gaps. A nonnormal operator sent to a self-adjoint Lanczos path refuses with an actionable diagnostic. Missing structure never silently defaults to the most favorable class. Existing receipts remain replayable and historically immutable. The corrected baseline becomes the production default after its regression and migration evidence passes; it does not wait for completion of the ambitious spectral theorem ratchet.

## Test Plan
Add G0 algebraic/property tests for zero spread, repeated clusters, ordering, scale, and unit invariance; G3 metamorphic tests for basis changes admitted by each class; G5 deterministic replay across thread counts; migration/golden tests for old receipts; and negative routing tests for nonnormal matrices, indefinite metrics, polynomial problems, monodromy, missing witnesses, NaN/nonfinite input, and adversarial near-degeneracy. Retain an exact regression for the live `[a,a]` defect and mutation-test the incorrect ratio-of-one implementation.

## Considerations
This fix establishes fail-closed problem classification and gap semantics only. It does not prove completeness of a spectrum, diagonalizability, pseudospectral bounds, Krein stability, polynomial regularity, or Floquet correctness. Those stronger results remain in separate [F]/[M] descendants with their own hypotheses and checkers. After G0/G3/G5 and migration evidence pass, make the fail-closed behavior default-on and remove any path that can emit the known false healthy-gap result. Frontier and moonshot descendants may enrich the classification or prove stronger spectral statements behind their own flags, activation/kill criteria, fallbacks, cost fields, falsifiers, and reproduction packs; their uncertainty must never delay or weaken this solid correction.

title: RB.K Certify regular pencils and expose singular Kronecker/minimal-index structure
description:
## Background
Generalized and polynomial eigenproblems split fundamentally into regular problems, whose finite and infinite elementary divisors define a projective spectrum at a fixed declared grade, and singular problems, whose left/right minimal indices and Kronecker structure carry constraints and hidden freedoms. A singular leading coefficient alone does not decide which case applies. Changing grade, reversing a polynomial, or applying a Möbius transform changes the finite/infinite labeling through explicit laws; it is not naive invariance. Treating a determinant-identically-zero matrix polynomial as an ordinary eigenvalue list can invent completeness, stability, and mode counts.

## Technical Approach
Define exact RegularPencil and RegularMatrixPolynomial witnesses with fail-closed admission before numerical solver routing. Build rank-revealing staircase or Kronecker-like reductions with exact/interval small-case witnesses, finite and infinite elementary-divisor semantics at fixed grade, explicit grade-shift, reversal, scaling, and projective/Möbius transformation laws, left/right minimal indices, descriptor consistency and impulse/strangeness structure for named LTI classes, and structure-preserving linearization maps. Distinguish pencil strict equivalence, matrix-polynomial constant/unimodular/strong equivalence, and strong-linearization minimal-index shifts. Keep approximate sparse diagnostics distinct from verified certificates. Route regular problems to RB.3 and singular problems to constraint/descriptor diagnostics rather than an eigenvalue-only API.

## Success Criteria
At fixed declared grade, admitted equivalences preserve exactly the invariants their theorem states. Grade changes and projective transformations produce checked shift/transport receipts rather than invariance claims. Singular determinant-identically-zero fixtures return minimal-index and constraint evidence or Unknown, never a complete spectrum. Descriptor fixtures distinguish dynamic modes, algebraic constraints, impulses, and inconsistent initial data. Naive companion linearizations that erase/shift structure without accounting or invent roots fail.

## Test Plan
Regular and singular 2x2/3x3 pencils; zero rows/columns; singular-mass QEPs in regular and singular cases; known Kronecker blocks; fixed-grade equivalence; grade increase/decrease; reversal and Möbius maps; scaling; descriptor impulse fixtures; strong and weak linearizations; rank-uncertain intervals; and exact/high-precision oracle comparison.

## Considerations
Full verified Kronecker structure at scale is a moonshot. Partial or Unknown with exact regularity witnesses is successful. Grade is semantic input; numerical rank folklore is not a theorem. Algebraic structure, discretization interpretation, control-system structure, and physical stability are separate evidence states.

title: RB.K1 Certify regular pencils and matrix-polynomial grade/infinite-spectrum semantics
description:
## Background
A square pencil or matrix polynomial is regular when its determinant is not identically zero, even if its leading coefficient is singular. Finite and infinite elementary divisors are defined projectively at an explicit polynomial grade. Increasing grade generally adds or shifts infinity structure; reversal and Möbius maps transport rather than preserve finite/infinite labels. Naive rank tests or companion roots can invent or erase modes.

## Technical Approach
Define RegularPencil and RegularMatrixPolynomial witnesses over exact, interval, symbolic-small, and admitted numerical data. Freeze polynomial degree versus declared grade and homogenized/projective conventions. Distinguish constant nonsingular strict equivalence for pencils; constant, unimodular, and strong equivalence for matrix polynomials; reversal/scaling/Möbius transformations; determinant/minor regularity witnesses; finite/infinite algebraic and partial multiplicities; and strong-linearization structure maps. Implement fail-closed Regular/Singular/Unknown admission with coefficient uncertainty and deterministic rank decisions. For each admitted transformation prove and encode its exact spectral law, including grade-induced infinity shifts and residual/backward-error transfer. Algebraic admission precedes and routes numerical Arnoldi/Jacobi-Davidson work; it does not depend on those solvers.

## Success Criteria
At fixed declared grade, constant nonsingular strict equivalence preserves finite and infinite elementary divisors. Reversal and admitted Möbius transformations carry them through an explicit projective law. A grade change is never labeled invariant: its certified receipt states exactly which infinite partial multiplicities are added, removed, or shifted. Singular-leading-coefficient QEPs are correctly split into regular and singular cases; uncertain rank returns Unknown; and non-strong linearizations or convention changes that invent roots are rejected. Every ordinary eigenvalue API call requires a regularity witness.

## Test Plan
Regular 2x2/3x3 pencils; singular leading coefficient but regular QEP; nilpotent/infinite blocks; trailing/leading zero coefficients; fixed-grade strict equivalence; unimodular but not constant transformations; grade increase/decrease; reversal and Möbius maps; extreme scaling; exact rational/interval coefficients; determinant/minor witnesses; strong and weak companion linearizations; rank uncertainty; and proof corruption.

## Considerations
Determinant expansion is not a scalable numerical algorithm; structured rank/minor or contour witnesses may be needed. Grade is semantic input, not inferred casually from floating zeros. Strong equivalence and strong linearization preserve specified structure with possible predictable minimal-index shifts; name the theorem. Regularity alone says nothing about stability or physical admissibility.

## Execution and evidence
State coefficient field/ring, uncertainty, grade/projective convention, equivalence class, transformation law, TCB, budgets, and no-claim boundary. Retain exact small oracles, interval witnesses, deterministic pivots, G0 laws, G2 fixtures, G3 grade/reversal/Möbius/scaling tests, DSR evidence, and independent reproduction. Ambition class [F].

title: RB.K2 Expose singular Kronecker chains, minimal indices, and descriptor constraints
description:
## Background
When a pencil or matrix polynomial is singular, left/right minimal indices and Kronecker chains encode constraints, hidden freedoms, compatibility, and polynomial nullspaces. Returning only finite/infinite eigenvalues discards the defining information. Strong linearizations can shift minimal indices predictably rather than preserve them literally. Descriptor differentiation, impulse, and strangeness indices also depend on the precise system class; controllability/observability require input/output matrices, not only sE-A.

## Technical Approach
Implement rank-revealing staircase/Kronecker-like reductions with exact small-case and interval-certified witnesses where feasible, plus labeled approximate sparse diagnostics. Construct left/right polynomial nullspace bases and minimal indices, regular finite/infinite blocks, deflating chains, and structure maps under strict/strong equivalence. Encode the exact minimal-index shift law for each admitted strong linearization and reject weak/unclassified transfers. For constant-coefficient finite-dimensional LTI descriptor systems E xdot = A x + B u, y = C x + D u, separately derive consistent-initial-data, hidden-constraint, impulse/nilpotent, differentiation/strangeness, controllability, and observability receipts using the declared B,C,D data. Do not generalize those indices silently to time-varying, nonlinear, or PDE DAEs.

## Success Criteria
Known Kronecker blocks reproduce minimal indices/chains and regular parts; admitted equivalences and strong linearizations satisfy their exact invariant/shift laws; LTI descriptor fixtures distinguish finite dynamics, algebraic constraints, impulses, freedoms, consistent initial data, and B/C-qualified control structure; rank-ambiguous or unsupported classes return partial evidence or Unknown; and no API invents a complete eigenvalue list.

## Test Plan

## Considerations
Full verified Kronecker form at scale is discontinuous and moonshot-hard. Approximate minimal indices require tolerance and pseudospectral interpretation. Descriptor index notions are not interchangeable; every receipt names its definition and class. Physical redundant constraints and algebraic generator redundancy require presentation-aware handling.

## Execution and evidence

title: RC.6a Formalize admitted cover, lift, holonomy, obstruction, and convention kernels
description:
## Background
Several distinct lifting and holonomy problems coexist and must not share an undifferentiated obstruction claim. A path in a covering space lifts uniquely once its starting sheet is fixed. A global lift of a map f:X->SO(n) through Spin(n)->SO(n) has a pullback-cover obstruction in H^1(X;Z2). A Spin structure on an oriented SO(n)-bundle is governed by w2, while Pin+/Pin- structures on O(n)-bundles use convention-qualified w2 and w2+w1^2 conditions. Deck monodromy, connection holonomy, and nonholonomic/constraint holonomy are also different objects with different invariance.

## Technical Approach
Freeze separate theorem cards and typed artifacts for: local/path lifting and uniqueness by starting sheet; global map lifting and its H1 pullback-cover obstruction; Spin structure on oriented bundles via w2; Pin+/Pin- bundle structures via the declared Clifford-sign convention; Cech transition cocycles and relative/boundary variants; deck monodromy as homotopy-class/groupoid data; connection holonomy as curvature-dependent parallel transport; and nonholonomic holonomy from a declared connection/distribution. State component/basepoint behavior, including conjugation rather than literal equality where appropriate. Specify the actual configuration/parameter-space complex carrying every class—never infer H2 from a graph incidence complex. Formalize PGA/dual-quaternion cover and exceptional-locus statements as a separate algebraic theorem family. Orbifold/action-groupoid and braid-monodromy generalization belongs downstream in RC.O.

## Success Criteria
Every theorem names exact quantifiers, carrier space, coefficient system, bundle/map/path object, convention, regularity, component, basepoint, and gauge action. Path lifting is not confused with global section existence. H1 map-lift, w2 Spin, and Pin obstruction fixtures yield their distinct results. Deck monodromy is homotopy invariant where admitted; connection/nonholonomic holonomy varies according to curvature/distribution. Basepoint/gauge changes produce the proved conjugacy/covariance law. False global-section, graph-H2, literal-holonomy-invariance, or convention-swapped claims are rejected.

## Test Plan
Circle and SO(2)/Spin(2); SO(3)/Spin(3) map lifts; oriented bundles with w2 obstruction; reflection bundles for both Pin conventions; disconnected spaces; nonorientable loops; Mobius/projective examples; flat versus curved connections on homotopic loops; nonholonomic rolling loop; periodic quotient paths; corrupt cocycles; basepoint/gauge conjugation; degenerate PGA elements; false graph carrier; and proof corruption.

## Considerations
Formal cover theory does not validate numerical path sampling. Connection holonomy is generally not homotopy-only, and representatives may change by conjugation. Pin conventions vary in the literature. Higher obstruction claims require the real cell/cover/bundle complex. RC.O is a stronger downstream extension, never a prerequisite for this core.

## Execution and evidence
Retain separate theorem manifests, definitions, TCB, carrier/coefficient/convention tables, exact fixtures, counterexamples, deterministic proof builds, budgets, provenance, DSR evidence, and independent reproduction. External proof assistants are development oracles unless admitted. Ambition class [M]; preserve maximal conjectures and exact refutations.

title: RD.V1 Prove scoped tangent-cone viability and transition soundness on stratified dynamics
description:
## Background

Contingent, Clarke, proximal, and model-specific cones are not interchangeable. Local outward crossing is not eventual reachability from an interior set.

## Technical Approach
Define separate theorem cards and verdict types for existential viability, strong invariance, local outward/guard crossing, blocked transition, and bounded-horizon/eventual reachability. For each admitted smooth ODE/DAE, complementarity, sweeping/measure-differential, or set-valued class, name solution concept, tangent/normal cone, regularity, constraint qualification, selection semantics, and quantifier over solutions. Construct validated cone and vector-field/inclusion evidence; state Nagumo-style conditions with exact one-sided necessity/sufficiency strength; handle transversality and set-valued grazing/simultaneous exits; and pursue global reachability only with an explicit flow/reachability argument. State finite-event/non-Zeno hypotheses separately. Runtime lowering is downstream in RD.V2 and is not a prerequisite for the theorem.

## Success Criteria

Canonical contact, Geneva, cusp, and multicontact cases match direct/exact analysis. No local cone test is labeled eventual reachability. Completeness is claimed only for its exact solution/dynamic class. Wrong quantifier, cone, vector direction, regularity, selection, or anti-Zeno assumption is refuted with a witness.

## Test Plan
Inward/outward/mixed inclusions on identical strata; examples where F intersects T but is not a subset; smooth boundary crossing; unilateral contact; stick/slip candidate cones; Geneva dwell/engagement; cusp branches; simultaneous constraints; grazing; non-Lipschitz inclusion; inconsistent DAE; reachable versus locally viable but unreachable set; Zeno sequence; contingent-versus-Clarke cone difference; refinement; and false incidence-to-reachability implication.

## Considerations

Some nonconvex/set-valued dynamics admit only one-sided statements. Preserve maximal theorem ambition, but attach the exact quantifier and solution concept to every result.

title: RD.V2 Conform contact/reset laws and lower viability-qualified exits into hybrid IR
description:
## Background
A viable approach to a boundary still does not define post-event physics. Impact, friction, adhesion, compliance limits, impulses, energy loss, and state projection require constitutive laws. Simultaneous impact generally requires a joint impulse/complementarity or measure law; it cannot be represented faithfully by an arbitrary ordering unless a sequential-impact model is explicitly chosen. Hybrid lowering can also invent a unique trace for set-valued dynamics or fabricate a next mode after Zeno accumulation.

## Technical Approach
Define the interface from viability-qualified exits to HybridAutomatonIR: guards with sidedness/transversality/set-valued status; reset/projection/impulse maps; contact/friction/adhesion law identity and parameter validity; conservation/dissipation or supply-rate closure; and state-dimension/topology transfer. For simultaneous events, make a joint impulse/complementarity/set-valued law the primary artifact. Permit partial orders/permutations only under a declared sequential-impact semantics and preserve order dependence. Represent nonunique outcomes as reachable sets/branches. Define grazing/chatter and Zeno limit receipts. Prove transactional lowering preservation for admitted classes with stable mode/event identities and deterministic enumeration—not false physical selection. Compare set-valued results by reachable-set containment or an identical declared selection rule.

## Success Criteria
Canonical impacts, stick/slip, Geneva engagement, multicontact, grazing, and Zeno cases lower with guards/resets matching declared laws and conservation/dissipation bounds. Simultaneous impacts use joint laws unless sequential semantics are explicit. Missing law or nonunique selection remains explicit. Direct comparison uses set containment or the same selection rule. Wrong reset energy, impulse sign, event order, lost branch, arbitrary selected-trace equality, or fabricated post-Zeno mode fails.

## Test Plan
Elastic/inelastic impact; Coulomb/static friction; adhesion/release; compliant-to-rigid limit; Geneva entry/exit; joint simultaneous impact versus sequential permutations; order-sensitive sequential model; set-valued reachable outcomes; grazing; chatter; bouncing-ball Zeno; DAE projection; state topology transfer; transactional cancellation; checkpoint/resume; and reset mutation.

## Considerations
Contact laws are scoped models. Set-valued physics must not be collapsed for determinism. Regularization can change bifurcation/dissipation. Sequential impact is one constitutive choice, not a universal resolution of simultaneity.

## Execution and evidence

title: RD.H Build higher Kuranishi/L-infinity obstruction models beyond the Jacobian complex
description:
## Background
The two-term tangent complex records infinitesimal mobility and first obstruction or cokernel data, but it does not determine whether an infinitesimal mechanism integrates to a finite branch. Second and higher jets, nonlinear compatibility, syzygies, and formal-moduli operations carry the missing obstruction information. Without them, the derived mobility theorem risks being Jacobian rank analysis with new names.

## Technical Approach
For admitted analytic or semialgebraic constraint germs, construct a presentation-invariant cotangent-complex resolution and a finite Kuranishi model or equivalent L-infinity formal-moduli representation from the tangent complex, relation modules, and higher derivatives. Compute second-order rigidity maps, obstruction classes, brackets and higher operations, branch multiplicity, and convergence or effectivity conditions. Prove invariance under admitted coordinate changes and quasi-isomorphic constraint resolutions; distinguish arbitrary redundant equations from equivalent derived presentations. Provide exact and interval microcase checkers and truncate with an explicit Unknown remainder when effectivity cannot be proved.

## Success Criteria
Regular cases collapse to the implicit-function theorem. Bennett, Bricard, and second-order locked examples distinguish infinitesimal flex, obstructed flex, and genuine finite branch. Adding generated redundant equations or changing an equivalent resolution preserves the formal-moduli receipt. A nonzero tangent vector alone never becomes a motion certificate. At least one theorem links vanishing obstruction data plus precise analytic or effectivity hypotheses to a validated local branch, or records the sharp counterexample.

## Test Plan
Regular linkage; cusp and node; redundant generators and explicit syzygies; infinitesimally flexible but rigid frameworks; Bennett and Bricard cases; higher-order locked germs; coordinate and resolution changes; interval rank uncertainty; truncated-series false positives; and formal-checker mutation.

## Considerations
Vanishing of finitely many obstructions need not imply convergence without Noetherian, analytic, or effectivity hypotheses. Preserve formal versus actual solution states separately.

## Theorem-lane execution contract
Separate formal algebra, exact kernel, interval numerics, local analytic existence, finite-mechanism validation, and physical interpretation. Carry trusted computing base, budgets, deterministic and cancellable searches, baselines, counterexamples, DSR evidence, and independent reproduction.

## Success Criteria

title: RD.X Certify exit-path infinity-category approximations and constructible descent
description:
## Background
A stratum-incidence poset is not generally the exit-path category: nontrivial fundamental groups inside strata and topology of links can create distinct morphisms and monodromy even when incidence is identical. Bind variance correctly: sheaf restriction versus cosheaf corestriction and exit versus entrance or opposite categories. Build constructible descent, monodromy, refinement-equivalence, and obstruction checkers.

## Success Criteria
Two stratified spaces with the same incidence poset but different link or stratum monodromy cannot receive the same certified exit-path artifact. title: RE.1A Define bounded atlas domains, system conventions, and canonical cell identity
description:
## Background
A global-dynamics atlas must first define a bounded domain, system identity, cell ownership, and time/map convention. Geometric cells are not themselves claims or proofs.

## Technical Approach
Define bounded phase, parameter, QoI, model, and uncertainty domains with units; continuous-time versus map convention; topology/phase strata; half-open cell ownership; immutable system/mode/crosswalk versions; branch and symmetry identities; and deterministic cell/frontier keys. Include refinement lineage, overlap semantics, boundary ownership, and explicit out-of-domain states.

## Success Criteria
Every atlas cell has stable content-addressed identity independent of scheduling. Boundaries are owned exactly once; topology/phase/model changes cannot be hidden by numerical proximity; domain extension creates new lineage.

## Test Plan
G0 partition/ownership/identity/unit laws; G3 coordinate, subdivision, equivalent parameterization, and scheduling transforms; boundary, symmetry, topology, and version adversaries; G5 replay.

## Considerations
Cell existence says nothing about invariant sets, reachability, chaos, or physicality.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [M]. Publish typed schemas, canonicalization, budgets, versions, and no-claim state.

title: RE.1B Define polarity-safe global-dynamics claims, witnesses, and Unknown states
description:
## Background
Global dynamics mixes existential, universal, inner, outer, exclusion, nonexistence, transition, basin, game, chaos, measure, and physicality statements. Their quantifiers and polarity cannot be compressed into one confidence score.

## Technical Approach
Define claim families with exact domains, quantifiers over state/parameter/disturbance/control/time/model, inner/outer polarity, witness/counterwitness, refinement behavior, and proof state. Use a partial evidence order with Proven, ComputerAssisted, Validated, Candidate, Refuted, Failed, Unknown, and Inapplicable only where sound; preserve incomparability. Type basin, reach-avoid, viability, Conley/covering, chaos/entropy, invariant-measure, Lyapunov, and physicality claims separately.

## Success Criteria
No outer bound is consumed as an inner guarantee, no existence sample as universal proof, and no chaos certificate as a probability statement. Every claim carries exact quantifiers and no-claim boundaries.

## Test Plan
G0 polarity/quantifier/lattice laws; mutation tests swapping exists/forall, inner/outer, finite/infinite time, model/physical; adversarial incomplete cells and conflicting evidence; deterministic serialization.

## Considerations
Evidence types may be incomparable; Unknown is informative and monotone under honest refinement.

## Execution and evidence
Ambition [M]. Tie every claim state to theorem-card and checker identities.

title: RE.1C Prove claim-family restriction, refinement, descent, and obstruction laws
description:
## Background

## Technical Approach

Define restriction for universal/exclusion evidence, corestriction/union behavior for outer enclosures, and stack/groupoid-style branch data where monodromy or symmetry prevents ordinary unique gluing. For each family state cover topology, overlap compatibility, existence/uniqueness of glued sections, obstruction carrier, refinement maps, and conflict localization. Prove sheaf/descent only on admitted subfamilies.

## Success Criteria
Every gluing operation has a theorem/checker or returns an obstruction/Unknown. Conflicting overlaps localize without poisoning unrelated cells. Branch monodromy is retained rather than averaged away.

## Test Plan

title: RE.M Enclose invariant measures, statistical QoIs, escape rates, and Lyapunov spectra
description:
## Background
A deterministic attractor atlas does not by itself answer long-time engineering questions such as fatigue-driving residence fractions, rare escape rates, mean power, acoustic statistics, or Lyapunov spectra. Chaotic and metastable machines need certified statistical statements, while nonunique invariant measures and finite-time sampling bias must remain visible.

## Technical Approach

Combine adaptive Ulam or spectral partitions with Lasota–Yorke-type inequalities, compactness/mixing hypotheses, interval eigen-enclosures, mass and positivity checks, and certified discretization error. Enclose invariant measures, multiple ergodic components, statistical QoIs, escape rates for open systems, and Lyapunov exponents or spectra under explicit regularity and cocycle assumptions. Treat physical/SRB measure claims as stronger and distinct from mere invariant-measure existence. Route nonhyperbolic, intermittent, or unresolved regions to Unknown.

## Success Criteria
Canonical expanding, intermittent, open, and chaotic systems yield independently checked measure, escape-rate, and Lyapunov enclosures at the claimed order. A machine-relevant rotor, impact, or electromechanical case reports certified long-time QoI bands and distinguishes multiple invariant measures or unresolved selection. Results refine monotonically or carry a validated explanation for partition/topology change.

## Test Plan
Doubling and logistic maps in admitted regimes, cat-map/cocycle spectra, open maps with known escape rates, Lorenz-like return maps where hypotheses can be checked, metastable double wells, nonergodic mixtures, intermittent counterexamples to spectral gaps, partition and coordinate mutations, normalization/positivity checks, independent high-precision eigen-enclosures, cancellation, and deterministic replay.

## Considerations
Finite trajectory histograms do not certify invariant measures. Existence, uniqueness, ergodicity, mixing rate, physicality/SRB selection, and statistical stability are separate claims with separate hypotheses. Ulam convergence is not universal; essential spectrum and lack of a spectral gap must produce Unknown rather than optimistic error bars.

## Theorem contract
The theorem artifact records the map/flow and domain, function space, partition, transfer operator, Lasota–Yorke or alternative compactness evidence, invariant-mass/positivity witness, spectral enclosure, discretization error, and exact statistical claim. An independent checker validates operator bounds and QoI integration. Multiple measures are represented explicitly. No SRB, uniqueness, escape, or Lyapunov claim is inferred solely from simulation.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
Implementation must remain layer-correct, safe Rust by default, cancellation-correct under explicit asupersync Cx scopes, deterministic under logical partition identities, budgeted in time/memory/error/capability, and content-addressed in the Design Ledger. Completion evidence names Gauntlet tiers, retains exact seeds and partition hashes, runs the configured DSR quality lane or records its fallback, and includes independent checker replay.

## Moonshot promotion discipline

Activation requires canonical convergence cases, retained no-spectral-gap falsifiers, a machine demonstration, quantitative error/cost thresholds, and independent reproduction.
