title: RE.Q Certify quantified reach-avoid and viability games over machine uncertainty
description:
## Background
Machine safety and reachability claims are quantified statements, not pictures from sampled trajectories. The answer can change completely between “there exists a control for every disturbance,” “for every disturbance there exists a clairvoyant control,” and open-loop existence. FrankenSim needs a theorem-bearing game semantics that can certify robust reach-avoid and viability regions over uncertain machine states, parameters, contacts, and loads without silently changing quantifier order.

## Technical Approach
Define typed finite- and infinite-horizon game contracts with explicit quantifier prefixes over initial sets, admissible feedback or open-loop controls, disturbances, model parameters, event schedules, and strategy information patterns. Implement validated predecessor, reachable-set, and viability-kernel operators using interval/Taylor set propagation, barrier and SOS witnesses where applicable, adaptive inner/outer approximations, and deterministic subdivision. Couple hybrid guards/resets and differential-algebraic consistency through admitted model classes. Every cell carries Proven, Refuted, or Unknown plus a retained witness, counterexample, or obstruction; approximation widening must never be relabeled as safety.

## Success Criteria
For canonical controlled and adversarial hybrid systems, produce independently replayable inner safe-strategy regions and outer impossible regions with explicit horizons, quantifier order, information pattern, model class, and numerical enclosure. Demonstrate a machine case in which sampled simulation appears safe but the quantified solver finds a certified disturbance strategy, and another in which a retained controller/barrier witness proves robust reach-avoid. Unsupported or unresolved cases return Unknown with ranked refinement options.

## Test Plan
Use pursuit/evasion and double-integrator games, controlled impacts, backlash and friction adversaries, parameter-box uncertainty, switched-actuator faults, known viability kernels, swapped-quantifier mutation tests, unit rescaling, subdivision invariance, independent high-precision replay, cancellation storms, and deterministic thread-count replay. Include adversaries where open-loop control fails but feedback succeeds and where existential-after-universal accidentally assumes clairvoyance.

## Considerations
State compactness, regularity, nonanticipativity, disturbance measurability, DAE consistency, hybrid non-Zeno assumptions, and finite-versus-infinite horizon explicitly. A failed search for a controller is not a proof of impossibility; impossibility requires an outer/exclusion certificate. A numerical trajectory is neither a strategy nor a quantified proof.

## Theorem contract
Hypotheses and quantifier prefixes are machine-readable and hashed into the theorem artifact. The checker independently verifies set inclusions, guard/reset images, barrier or dynamic-programming inequalities, strategy admissibility, and enclosure arithmetic. Claimed inner and outer regions must be monotone under certified refinement or explain a validated topology event. Counterexamples are retained. The theorem makes no claim outside the admitted dynamics, information pattern, uncertainty set, or horizon.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
Implementation must remain layer-correct, safe Rust by default, cancellation-correct under explicit asupersync Cx scopes, deterministic under fixed logical-tile reductions, budgeted in time/memory/error/capability, and content-addressed in the Design Ledger. Completion evidence names Gauntlet tiers, retains machine fingerprints and exact seeds, runs the configured DSR quality lane or records its exact fallback state, and includes an independently replayable checker pack.

## Moonshot promotion discipline
Ambition class: [M]. Use feature flag `moonshot-quantified-viability-games`. The boring baseline is bounded validated forward reachability with no game claim. Activation requires checker-backed canonical and machine cases, quantitative enclosure and cost thresholds, and independent reproduction. Kill on unsound quantifier lowering, non-monotone certified bounds without explanation, checker disagreement, or unbounded cancellation latency. Fallback returns the baseline reachability evidence and Unknown for the game claim; a falsified conjecture remains a retained result.

title: RE.Z Certify Zeno/chatter accumulation, continuation, and global invariant semantics
description:
## Background
Chatter and Zeno behavior are central to impacts, relays, dry friction, backlash, power electronics, and protective control. Ordinary event stepping can execute an unbounded number of transitions in finite time, miss the accumulation state, or invent a post-event trajectory. A global dynamics atlas cannot claim completeness until accumulation, continuation, and invariant-set semantics are explicit.

## Technical Approach
Define an admitted hybrid-system class with typed modes, guards, resets, time domains, complementarity/contact laws, and event identity. Build validated enclosures for event-time sequences and accumulation states; prove finite-event separation where possible and detect certified Zeno accumulation where separation fails. Represent post-Zeno semantics as one of: uniquely certified continuation, set-valued continuation enclosure, terminal accumulation, or Unknown. Derive finite products or renormalized limits for variational/saltation data only under stated summability and transversality hypotheses; never multiply an unverified infinite saltation sequence. Integrate accumulation objects into Conley/Morse and viability reasoning.

## Success Criteria
Certified examples distinguish non-Zeno chatter, true finite-time Zeno accumulation, grazing ambiguity, and numerical event-loop artifacts. Each Zeno artifact encloses the accumulation time/state, records the active transition word or language, and states exactly what post-Zeno continuation is proven. Demonstrate at least one impact or relay machine model with independently replayed accumulation and one case correctly returning Unknown because continuation is nonunique or the admitted hypotheses fail.

## Test Plan
Bouncing ball with restitution families, relay chatter, complementarity contact, grazing impacts, simultaneous guards, zero-time reset cycles, event-time interval overlap, restitution approaching one, post-Zeno sticking versus rebound, Zeno regularization mutation tests, cancellation during dense event sequences, deterministic replay, and independent high-precision interval checks.

## Considerations
A time-step cutoff, event-count cap, or regularized compliance model is not a Zeno theorem. Distinguish physical model semantics from a chosen numerical regularization. State guard regularity, reset contraction, transversality, uniqueness, accumulation compactness, and any summability assumptions. Never infer post-Zeno dynamics from a finite prefix alone.

## Theorem contract
The artifact records the admitted hybrid automaton, event ordering semantics, interval enclosures for event times and states, accumulation proof or finite-separation proof, and the exact continuation category. An independent checker verifies guard hits, reset images, contraction/separation inequalities, and claimed limits. Counterexamples with reordered simultaneous events and nonunique continuations are retained. No theorem transfers across a regularization or model change without a new refinement receipt.

## Mandatory execution and evidence contract
Implementation must remain layer-correct, safe Rust by default, cancellation-correct under explicit asupersync Cx scopes, deterministic under fixed logical-event identities, budgeted in time/memory/error/capability, and content-addressed in the Design Ledger. Completion evidence names Gauntlet tiers, retains exact seeds and model hashes, runs the configured DSR quality lane or records its fallback, and includes independent replay of the checker and event trace.

## Moonshot promotion discipline
Ambition class: [M]. Use feature flag `moonshot-zeno-continuation`. The boring baseline stops with a structured event-density diagnostic and no continuation claim. Activation requires canonical analytic cases, adversarial simultaneous-event cases, a machine demonstration, bounded cancellation, and independent reproduction. Kill on missed certified accumulation, invented uniqueness, regularization leakage, or checker disagreement. Fallback preserves the finite trace and returns Unknown beyond the certified horizon.

title: LEAPFROG EXPERIENCE & PROOF SPINE — user workbench, executable journeys, observability, and replay
description:
## Background
The fifteen Leapfrog initiatives and five theorem ratchets contain unusually strong local Test Plans, but local prose is not executable proof and does not by itself make a system usable. A feature can look complete while its independent oracle, user workflow, scientific-visualization semantics, long-job control, cancellation finalization, failure diagnosis, evidence closure, or replay path remains implicit.

This cross-cutting portfolio is a direct child of LEAPFROG-2026. It is not a sixteenth scientific initiative and does not reduce, merge, cap, or postpone any feature. It gives every current and future capability a common, falsifiable, agent-native route from declared intent to unit evidence, production execution, durable operation, honest scientific adjudication, retained artifacts, and exact replay.

## User and agent outcomes
A user can inspect installation and host readiness; discover capabilities and no-claim boundaries; inspect inferred defaults; estimate cost; author or import a case through supported CLI, Rust API, FrankenScript, and WASM surfaces; select an explicit Core or Max claim stratum and independent campaign profile; submit a durable job; disconnect and reconnect; watch from a cursor; checkpoint, pause, migrate, cancel, resume, or fork with exact authority and lineage; inspect unit/frame/time/uncertainty-aware results and truthful visualizations; verify, report, redact/share, and replay artifacts; and receive ranked repairs for invalid input or environmental gaps.

An agent receives the same semantics through versioned schemas and stable JSONL, never screen scraping or a hidden test-only path. A status query, cancel request, worker attempt, scientific job, and aggregate campaign remain distinguishable, so operational success cannot overwrite scientific truth.

## Technical Approach
Build one additive verification-and-experience spine around fs-obs, shared conformance, G0-G5 Gauntlet, HELM/session execution, DSR, Design Ledger, benchmark and V&V registries, LUMEN/fs-viz, and phase batteries. Own:

1. a generated VerificationManifest mapping every execution leaf and future descendant to concrete tests or a reviewed, narrow, expiring not-applicable rationale;
2. comprehensive Rust unit, boundary, error, doctest, executable-example, compile-fail/UI, type-invariant, property, metamorphic, manufactured-solution, benchmark, conformance, mutation, fuzz, certifier-of-certifier, deterministic-concurrency, chaos, security, and replay runners;
3. one typed protocol shared by product HELM/CLI/session APIs, the fs-test/DSR engine, and hermetic shell adapters, with conformance evidence that wrappers add zero semantics;
4. a canonical no-mock E2E runner plus exact per-family scripts and manifests;
5. one bounded, schema-versioned observability, diagnostic, evidence-retention, FailureBundle, replay, redaction, and share contract;
6. exact identity and causality for DSR runs, campaigns, shards, journeys, cases, submissions, durable jobs, attempts, control/query operations, execution scopes, tiles, leases, cursors, checkpoints, and artifacts;
7. scoped OperationReceipt, AttemptReceipt, JobReceipt, and CampaignReceipt objects with an orthogonal scientific/evidence outcome algebra;
8. a complete durable asynchronous lifecycle with reconnectable observation and fenced control;
9. progressive-disclosure human/agent workbench, first-run doctor, generated help/completions, accessibility, teaching diagnostics, truthful scientific visualization, temporal presentation integrity, and data/image/timeline/report parity;
10. explicit Core and MAX test receipts plus post-promotion journeys for all fifteen initiatives;
11. executable pre-final and post-final journeys for all five theorem ratchets, admitting stronger independently checked theorems and durable refutations;
12. cross-portfolio semantic-seam campaigns, DSR/scale/cross-ISA/release qualification, forty retained family user journeys, executable Core and MAX tutorial corpora, and final independent adjudication.

Generated catalogs, manifests, help, completions, and tutorials come from Beads, contracts, IR, and code rather than hand-maintained parallel lists. Every inferred default is surfaced and ledgered. Legacy suites are admitted only through versioned semantic-diff adapters.

Consume the canonical schemas from frankensim-ext-vv-artifact-schemas-x68z: ContextOfUse, CalibrationSplit, SolutionVerificationReceipt, PredictionAssessment, and the uncertainty waterfall. Every evidence edge is typed as code verification, solution verification, calibration, model validation, prediction assessment, exploratory discovery, or confirmation. None implies another. Exploratory or adaptively selected results may create bold new ClaimRecords and theorem conjectures, but empirical promotion requires independent confirmatory lineage: preregistered/held-out evidence or anytime-valid optional-stopping control, multiplicity/selective-reporting accounting, and an exact ContextOfUse. Formal theorem promotion remains governed by its proof/checker receipts, never empirical fit.

## Protocol and executable-surface contract
There is one typed VerificationProtocol/JourneyEngine semantic authority. Product CLI and HELM/session APIs expose user operations and durable lifecycle semantics. The fs-test command is the test and DSR execution adapter over the same protocol. 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh' is a hermetic, portability-tested adapter that only selects and invokes typed operations; it does not define selection, lifecycle, verdict, artifact, or exit semantics.

V.4.2 owns command grammar, selectors, plan/estimate/explain/diff, and synchronous convenience behavior. V.4.9 exclusively owns Submission/Job/Attempt lifecycle, status/watch/attach, checkpoint/pause/migrate/cancel/resume/fork, reconnect/restart, artifact/report/share/offline verification, and terminal state transitions. Conformance tests compare all surfaces for selection hashes, typed requests, events, artifacts, scoped receipts, and process projections.

## Identity, causality, and receipt scopes
Names are never aliases:

- DsrRunId identifies one DSR invocation; CampaignRunId identifies one canonical manifest expansion/execution; ShardId identifies a deterministic partition.
- JourneyId and CaseId are stable logical definitions, not executions.
- SubmissionId identifies immutable pre-admission client intent within an exact idempotency scope. An AdmissionReceipt records acceptance or rejection; only acceptance creates or links a JobId for the durable logical computation. Repeating the same key and canonical payload returns the same decision, while the same key with a different payload is a typed collision and never aliases. AttemptId identifies one worker incarnation caused by initial execution, retry, resume, or migration.
- OperationId identifies one user/API control or query such as submit, status, watch, cancel, or verify. ExecutionScopeId and TileId identify local work inside an Attempt. ArtifactId and CheckpointId are content-addressed lineage nodes.
- A resume or migration normally creates a new Attempt for the same Job. A fork creates a new Job with an explicit checkpoint/parent edge. Replay creates a new CampaignRun or Submission with a replay-of edge. DSR hosting and scientific causality are separate typed edges.

Within an Attempt, execution containment is a tree. Globally, submissions, jobs, attempts, forks, replays, checkpoints, artifacts, campaigns, and DSR hosting form a typed acyclic causal DAG with explicit multi-parent edges.

Receipts are scoped:

- OperationReceipt describes the current CLI/API operation and alone projects to that process exit code.
- AttemptReceipt describes one execution incarnation, its lifecycle, resources, faults, and produced evidence.
- JobReceipt aggregates the durable computation and carries its exact scientific claim/evidence state.
- CampaignReceipt aggregates deterministic selection, shards, cases, independent reproduction, and promotion effect.

A successful 'status' operation may exit zero while embedding a JobReceipt with ClaimAdjudication=refuted or a failed ExecutionDisposition. An accepted 'cancel' operation may exit zero before a later JobReceipt reaches drained cancellation. No unqualified terminal result is allowed.

## Claim strata and campaign profiles
Scientific scope and campaign intensity are separate axes. Every executable scientific request selects exactly one claim stratum from the grammar {core, max}. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. Cross-facet combinations are allowed only through a versioned manifest-defined composite ProfileId whose ordered inputs, precedence and conflict rules, budgets, capabilities, selection expansion, and semantic-diff hash are frozen before execution; repeated --profile flags or implicit string composition are invalid. Scale remains an orthogonal workload/budget dimension, not a profile ID. Profiles control workload, duration, fault model, platforms, and evidence obligations; they never silently upgrade or downgrade the claim surface.

Selection, defaults, filters, profile composition, budgets, capabilities, and shard expansion are canonicalized, diffable, and ledgered. Legacy SMOKE/MID/FULL names are accepted only by V.4.6 semantic adapters. A mapping is valid only if cases, claims, budgets, capabilities, acceptance rules, negative cases, and artifacts reconcile; otherwise it refuses with ranked migration guidance.

## Orthogonal scientific and evidence outcome algebra
Every ClaimRecord has a stable ClaimId plus immutable ClaimRevisionId, kind, statement, quantifiers, units/conventions, hypothesis set, exact domain, version, and typed relations to other claims. Every implication, refinement, restriction, equivalence, incompatibility, or counterexample edge is itself an evidence-bearing ClaimRelationReceipt with explicit direction, source/target domains and quantifiers, checker identity, proof artifact, and TCB overlap. Relation cycles fail closed except independently certified equivalence components; transitive use requires admitted relation composition. The receipt records separate fields:

- ExecutionDisposition: completed, rejected, cancelled-and-drained, timed-out-and-finalized, budget-exhausted-and-finalized, infrastructure-error, or execution-integrity-error.
- RequestedPredicateOutcome: satisfied, unsatisfied, indeterminate, or not-evaluated for the exact operation/campaign predicate.
- ClaimAdjudication: established, refuted, unresolved, or not-claimed for the exact ClaimRecord.
- EvidenceMethodSet: formal-kernel, computer-assisted-certified, interval/certified-numerical, exact-discrete, independently reproduced numerical, validated-empirical, empirical-only, expert-judgment, or other versioned methods, with provenance and TCB overlap.
- EpistemicGrade: proof, certified, validated, corroborated, preliminary, or conjectural, derived by a versioned policy from claim kind and admitted evidence rather than chosen cosmetically.
- DomainApplicability: in-domain, outside-domain, domain-unknown, or not-evaluated.
- OperationalSupport: available, missing-capability, hardware-unavailable, license-unavailable, policy-denied, data-unavailable, temporarily-unavailable, or not-evaluated.
- EvidenceCompleteness: complete, partial, missing, or not-required.
- EvidenceIntegrity: verified, unverified, corrupt, or conflicting.
- PromotionEffect: eligible, restricted, quarantined, demoted, no-change, or ineligible, with the affected claim/capability set.

Human terms are typed projections, not mixed enum values. For example, a theorem ClaimRecord that is established with proof-grade admitted evidence renders Proven; a validation claim with validated evidence renders ValidatedWithinDomain; unresolved renders Unknown; not-claimed renders NoClaim. Unsupported is a projection of DomainApplicability and OperationalSupport, not a truth value.

'Partial' is never a ClaimAdjudication. A weaker, restricted, or local theorem is a separate hashed ClaimRecord with exact implication/refinement edges and its own adjudication. Incomplete evidence remains EvidenceCompleteness=partial and cannot promote the original claim. This preserves ambitious theorem ratcheting without laundering unfinished closure.

Old ClaimState and combined EvidenceCompleteness/Integrity fields migrate through explicit, loss-reporting adapters. Ambiguous old values do not default favorably.

## Process projection
The typed receipt is authoritative. A process code is a deterministic, versioned projection of the current finalized OperationReceipt only: 0 operation predicate satisfied; 10 unsatisfied; 11 invalid manifest/schema/admission; 12 indeterminate or required operation evidence incomplete; 13 operation unsupported by domain/capability/policy; 14 current operation cancelled and drained; 15 current operation finalized timeout; 16 infrastructure error; 17 integrity/security failure; 18 current operation budget exhaustion. If the client, shell, host, or service dies before a finalized OperationReceipt is durably observable, no 0/10-18 scientific projection may be fabricated: the platform signal/transport status is reported separately and recovery proceeds by SubmissionId, idempotency key, or authorized job discovery.

Thus a sound refutation can be exit 0 for an 'adjudicate' operation and exit 10 for a 'prove' operation. A successful status query is exit 0 even when its embedded JobReceipt has ClaimAdjudication=refuted, a finalized timeout, outside-domain applicability, or unavailable support. Successful execution never implies a claim is established, and a missing receipt never defaults favorably.

## Executable test and logging contract
The future hermetic adapter is 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh', with per-family drivers under 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/<family>.sh' and manifests under 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/<family>.toml'. Typed operations cover list, doctor/capabilities, plan/estimate, submit/run, status, watch/attach, checkpoint/pause/migrate, cancel/resume/fork, inspect/artifacts/report/share/verify, explain/diff, and replay. Pretty output renders the same typed events as stable JSONL.

Every run emits stable identity and typed causal edges; manifest/code/contract/schema hashes; units/frames/clocks; seed and logical RNG/work identity; requested and consumed budgets; capabilities/flags; machine/ISA/thread/mode fingerprint; fixture/input/output hashes; oracle/checker and TCB overlap; tolerance derivation; progress/residual/balance/conservation/uncertainty/error summaries; lifecycle and control events; scoped outcome receipts; diagnostic/repair decisions; artifact, FailureBundle, minimized-witness, report, and exact reconnect/replay pointers; timing and memory. Promotion-critical events are never sampled. Large or sensitive data is content-addressed and policy-redacted; logs are bounded and backpressure-safe.

## Success Criteria
Every current and future execution leaf has mechanically checked coverage. Every Core/MAX initiative gate, theorem final disposition, portfolio gate, and Summit consumes the appropriate executable receipt. The twenty capability families each have Core and MAX post-promotion journeys—forty retained journey receipts—plus executable Core and MAX tutorial branches.

Users can install, preflight, recover long jobs, distinguish operation success from job/scientific outcome, interpret temporal and visual evidence, verify closure, and replay without tribal knowledge. Human and agent surfaces agree. Failures replay from immutable closure. The graph remains acyclic, capability-stratified, ambition-preserving, and explicit about unsupported or unsettled frontiers.

## Test Plan
Self-test manifest compilation with missing, duplicate, stale, cyclic, falsely not-applicable, and ambition-downgrade entries. Exhaustively test valid scoped-receipt products, invalid combinations, process projections, old-field migrations, restricted-claim graphs, and operation-versus-job examples. Mutation-test identity aliasing, causal edges, lease fencing, stratum/profile expansion, legacy adapters, oracle independence, tolerance arithmetic, visualization and temporal transforms, redaction, cancellation/draining, pause/migration, retention, and generated help/tutorials.

Run comprehensive Rust unit, boundary, error, doctest, executable-example, compile-fail/UI, property, metamorphic, model-checking, Miri/sanitizer-or-explicit-OperationalSupport-gap, and certifier tests. Run no-mock production-path E2E at declared profiles; inject client, shell, process, worker, service, artifact, clock, storage, network, license, and security faults; audit boundedness and secret/license leakage; install and run packaged artifacts from clean non-repository hosts; replay same-ISA and supported cross-ISA modes; and independently reproduce promotion receipts from clean stores.

Mutate discovery into confirmation, reuse calibration data as validation or prediction holdout, hide model/parameter selection, optional stopping, multiple looks, forked hypotheses, multiplicity, or uncertainty components, and substitute solution verification for model validation or prediction assessment. Require fail-closed relation edges, independent holdout/preregistration or anytime-valid receipts, and retained rejected discoveries; stronger discoveries remain visible without laundering.

## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. Its aggregate receipt content-addresses and reconciles the exact child receipt set, dependency-graph version, frozen manifest/source/code/contract/schema/policy hashes, selection and profile expansion, stable ClaimRevision/Case/Journey/DSR/Campaign/Shard/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, typed causal edges, artifact roots, and verifier identities. It preserves each child's separate ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reports missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting, corrupt, or outside-scope children explicitly; and never averages disagreement or upgrades a claim. Aggregate progress, cost, timing, memory, diagnostics, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, accessibility state, and exact replay pointers are schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe, and semantically equivalent for human and stable JSONL consumers. Promotion-critical child evidence is referenced losslessly.

Retain ContextOfUseId, CalibrationSplitId, SolutionVerificationReceiptId, PredictionAssessmentId, uncertainty-waterfall components, evidence-stage and dataset-role lineage, preregistration/holdout commitment, adaptive looks/stopping rule, multiplicity family and adjustment/e-process, model/parameter selection history, and independent confirmation relation. Promotion records the exact stage-qualified evidence and never collapses the waterfall or stage distinctions.

## Considerations
This portfolio reuses rather than forks existing infrastructure. Accessibility applies to visual and interactive surfaces; machine APIs retain equivalent information. Successful bulk telemetry may expire under policy, but promotion evidence, refutations, minimized failures, semantic interchange artifacts, and theorem counterexamples are durable. Hardware-, data-, policy-, or license-dependent tests yield explicit support/applicability receipts, never silent green.

A novel theorem may exceed today's conjecture. The harness records the stronger exact ClaimRecord, proof method, domain, implication lattice, and runtime witness rather than imposing an artificial ceiling.

## Background

A generated manifest must make every promised behavior, exact claim revision and boundary, user journey, test case, oracle, retained artifact, and promotion consumer explicit and drift-detectable without letting mutable planning metadata rewrite historical science.

## Technical Approach
Define stable ClaimId and exact ClaimRevisionId, CaseId, JourneyId, fixture, oracle, tolerance, Core/Max stratum, campaign profile, budget, capability, logging, retention, replay, and gate schemas. - Beads define obligations, intent, ownership, and dependency history, not shipped semantics or observed truth.
- Contracts and typed registries define declared implemented semantics and no-claim boundaries.
- Code/test registrations bind executable surfaces and coverage.
- V&V/benchmark records define contexts, fixtures, references, and acceptance policies.
- immutable ledger/evidence artifacts record observations and adjudications.

Conflicts fail closed and remain visible; no source silently overrides another. Every compiled manifest records exact source snapshot hashes and compiler/policy versions. Historical receipts retain their original ClaimRevision and inputs even when Beads, contracts, or code later change.

## Success Criteria
One canonical machine-readable graph covers every current and historical Leapfrog execution leaf. Future leaves fail without test ownership or a reviewed, narrow, expiring not-applicable rationale. Mutable sources cannot alter an old receipt. Schema migration, source conflicts, claim supersession, licenses, golden provenance, relation proofs, and tamper status are replayable.

## Test Plan
Positive, boundary, malformed, stale-version, missing-capability, cancellation, replay, mutation, and deterministic-mode cases. Add frozen-source snapshot, Bead-versus-contract, contract-versus-code, registry conflict, post-receipt source edit, ClaimRevision supersession, relation-direction/quantifier/domain mutation, equivalence-SCC canonicalization, and historical replay tests. Every child emits structured evidence and names its independent oracle or exact no-claim boundary.

## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. Its aggregate receipt content-addresses and reconciles the exact child receipt set, dependency-graph version, frozen manifest/source/code/contract/schema/policy hashes, selection and profile expansion, stable ClaimRevision/Case/Journey/DSR/Campaign/Shard/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, typed causal edges, artifact roots, and verifier identities. It preserves each child's separate ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reports missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting, corrupt, or outside-scope children explicitly; and never averages disagreement or upgrades a claim. Aggregate progress, cost, timing, memory, diagnostics, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, accessibility state, and exact replay pointers are schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe, and semantically equivalent for human and stable JSONL consumers. title: V.1.1 Specify VerificationManifest v1, authority lattice, ClaimRevision, and stable Case/Journey identities
description:
## Background
Without stable semantic identity and source authority, renamed tests, revised Beads, reorganized scripts, or changed contracts can sever evidence from claims or retroactively reinterpret an old receipt.

## Technical Approach
Specify the versioned VerificationManifest schema, authority lattice, canonical normalized graph, and hashing rules. ClaimId identifies a continuing conceptual lineage; ClaimRevisionId binds one exact statement, kind, quantifiers, units/conventions, hypotheses, domain, code/contract surface, and no-claim boundary. Supersession never mutates an old revision.

A manifest record binds exact source snapshot hashes; Bead obligation ID; ClaimRevision; Core/Max stratum; admitted campaign profiles; ambition tag; public surface; Case/Journey IDs; unit/property/conformance/E2E ownership; fixture/oracle/checker IDs; TCB overlap; tolerance derivation; budgets; capabilities; event kinds; retention; replay command; DSR lane; scoped receipt expectations; and consuming gate.

Define typed ClaimRelationReceipt for implication, refinement, restriction, counterexample, and certified equivalence edges. It records direction, proof/checker/TCB, domain/quantifier variance, and policy version. Promotion/fallback transfers only across admitted relations. Reject cycles unless independently certified equivalence; canonicalize a certified-equivalence strongly connected component to one representative without erasing members.

Define additive versus breaking migration, collision handling, and explicit lossy migration reports. Heterogeneous human, JSON, and ledger renderings share one canonical normalized graph/digest and tested semantic projection; they are not required to be byte-identical.

## Success Criteria
Equivalent semantic manifests normalize to the same digest; distinct ClaimRevisions cannot collide; mutable source changes create new snapshots/revisions; every field has units, cardinality, authority, default visibility, and migration semantics; invalid, incomplete, conflicting, or relation-unsound records produce stable diagnostics and ranked fixes.

## Test Plan
Canonicalization/round-trip unit and property tests; duplicate/collision, Unicode, and ordering cases; missing field/wrong unit; source-authority conflict; post-receipt source mutation; old-reader/new-writer compatibility; ClaimRevision supersession; relation orientation, transitive composition, quantifier variance, domain contradiction, favorable relabeling, cycle, and certified-equivalence SCC tests; semantic parity of human/JSON/ledger projections.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit frozen source snapshot IDs/hashes, normalized graph/digest, Claim/ClaimRevision/Case/Journey identities, relation receipts, schema/compiler/policy versions, ownership, stratum/profiles, Five Explicits, capabilities, oracle/TCB/tolerance, expected scoped outcome fields, retention, diagnostics, artifact pointers, and replay. Log the complete scoped outcome algebra when execution occurs; manifest compilation itself never invents a scientific adjudication.

## Considerations
The manifest is metadata and obligation authority, not proof. unresolved/not-claimed ClaimAdjudication language requires an exact ClaimRevision and owned rationale; EvidenceCompleteness=partial is not a claim state.

title: V.1.2 Compile the complete frozen verification inventory from the source-authority lattice
description:
## Background
Manual parallel inventories drift. A naive generator is also unsafe if mutable Beads can override shipped contracts or if a new code registration can rewrite an old scientific receipt.

## Technical Approach
Build a deterministic inventory compiler over content-addressed snapshots of normalized Beads records, crate CONTRACT.md declarations, typed IR/catalog registries, code and test registrations, V&V artifacts, benchmark registry entries, and ledger receipts. Apply the V.1.1 authority lattice rather than last-writer-wins precedence. Emit explicit conflicts among obligation, declared semantics, executable registration, validation context, and observed evidence.

Reconcile aliases, renames, splits, merges, ClaimRevision supersession, and certified equivalence without losing historical lineage. Produce human, JSON, and ledger views as semantic projections of one canonical normalized graph and digest. Store the exact input snapshot set, compiler version, policy versions, conflict set, and output digest so later source edits cannot alter prior results.

## Success Criteria
Every live or historical ClaimRevision has one canonical identity and explicit verification owner. Additions, removals, conflicts, and semantic changes generate reviewable diffs. An old receipt resolves against its frozen source set. Heterogeneous views normalize to the same graph/digest and pass semantic-projection conformance; no false bit-for-bit promise is made across renderings.

## Test Plan
Golden miniature repositories; orphan, duplicate, rename, split, merge, supersession, certified equivalence, stale-code, and closed/refuted-history fixtures; Bead/contract/code/V&V/evidence conflicts; source mutation after receipt; unavailable historical snapshot; mutation tests for every adapter and authority rule; deterministic output across enumeration/thread variations; human/JSON/ledger semantic parity.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit source type, immutable snapshot/hash, authority role, adapter/compiler/policy versions, canonical identities, conflict and reconciliation decisions, normalized graph/digest, view projection hashes, diagnostics, immutable inventory artifact, and exact replay. Inventory compilation uses scoped Operation/Campaign receipts and never writes a favorable Job scientific result.

## Considerations
Generation is read-only with respect to sources. It must not invent defaults, discard closed/refuted history, infer implementation from a Bead, or let current metadata reinterpret historical evidence.

title: V.1.3 Enforce coverage, no-orphan, waiver-expiry, ambition, and no-claim lints
description:
## Background
Coverage percentages can be gamed unless missing tests, broad waivers, hidden skips, and weakened claim language fail closed.

Validate ambition tags against claim prose, require explicit core/max strata, expire waivers, and reject unresolved/not-claimed ClaimAdjudication entries without reason and effect on promotion.

## Success Criteria
A newly added uncovered leaf fails immediately; deleted or renamed cases cannot leave green ghosts; waivers have owner, narrow scope, expiry, and gate impact; ratchets can strengthen but cannot silently weaken statements.

## Test Plan
Seed one defect per rule: orphan, stale case, fake N/A, unbounded wildcard, expired waiver, unnamed skip, ambition downgrade, missing negative/cancel/replay case, and dangling gate. Require minimized diagnostics.

Emit schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable case and journey IDs, manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, seed and logical work identity, requested and consumed budgets, capabilities and feature flags, machine fingerprint, deterministic mode, fixture/oracle/checker identities and declared trusted-computing-base overlap, tolerance derivation, progress and scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, artifact pointers, and minimized witnesses. Large or sensitive payloads are content-addressed and redacted. No unnamed skip or generic success is allowed.

## Considerations
Not every schema-only leaf needs every Gauntlet tier, but omission must be semantically justified and reviewable—not inferred from labels.

## Background
A test can faithfully reproduce the same bug if production and checker share formulas, fixtures, tolerance logic, or serialization assumptions.

Require independent analytic, exhaustive-small, high-precision, alternate-discretization, physical, or formally checked oracles as appropriate. Record generator/checker separation, raw bytes, normalization, tolerance arithmetic, license/export restrictions, schema history, signatures/hashes, and immutable legacy views.

## Success Criteria
Promotion cannot consume an oracle with undeclared circularity; protected or secret data cannot leak; old artifacts remain interpretable without rewriting history; corruption and unauthorized mutation fail closed.

## Test Plan
Same-bug oracle fixture; adversarial tolerance inflation; raw/normalized mismatch; license denial; stale signature; truncated and oversized artifact; migration round trip and non-migratable refusal; bit-flip localization.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable case and journey IDs, manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, seed and logical work identity, requested and consumed budgets, capabilities and feature flags, machine fingerprint, deterministic mode, fixture/oracle/checker identities and declared trusted-computing-base overlap, tolerance derivation, progress and scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, artifact pointers, and minimized witnesses. Large or sensitive payloads are content-addressed and redacted. No unnamed skip or generic success is allowed.

## Considerations
TCB independence is graduated and explicit, never a boolean marketing claim. Dev-only external references remain outside production dependencies.

title: V.1.5 Define deterministic claim-stratum, campaign-profile, filter, budget, capability, and sharding metadata
description:
## Background
Core and Max are claim/capability strata, while smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-ISA, and release describe campaign intensity and evidence obligations. Mixing them into one tier makes a soak run ambiguously change scientific scope, and invisible selection changes across hardware, filters, budgets, or workers can silently omit cases.

## Technical Approach
Define two orthogonal, versioned axes: the stratum enum {core, max} selects the declared claim and capability surface. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. All Core adapters are complete and fail closed. Every selected case and every unsafe invariant is accounted for. Independent replay agrees on canonical selection, scoped receipts, and comparison arithmetic. A gap blocks the affected claim rather than being hidden or globally overgeneralized.

## Test Plan
Clean-store replay; omitted/duplicated/filtered case; false-green OperationReceipt; corrupted closure; tolerance/oracle swap; missing doctest or compile-fail; unsafe instrumentation unavailable without substitute; named support gap; deterministic sharding; status-on-refuted-job; old schema migration.

## Exact execution contract
Manifest: `tests/leapfrog/manifests/core-test-runner-independent-adjudication.toml`. No-mock independent driver: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/core-test-runner-independent-adjudication.sh`. Separately retained canonical execution is `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite core-test-runner-independent-adjudication --stratum core --profile standard`. The verifier independently reconstructs selection, adapter coverage, scoped outcomes, and artifact closure. A missing path, divergent selection, bypass, or incomplete receipt is non-green.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit frozen manifest/source snapshots, adapter versions, Core stratum and profiles, selection/shards, all identity scopes, test-class and unsafe-invariant coverage, Five Explicits, oracle/TCB/tolerance, lifecycle, complete scoped outcome algebra, artifact closure, diagnostics, minimized witness, and replay.

## Considerations
This shared Core infrastructure receipt is consumed by initiative-specific pre-promotion batteries; it does not establish their scientific claims by itself.

title: V.2.7 Integrate G4 chaos/cancellation, deterministic concurrency model checking, G5 determinism, and unsafe-runtime matrices
description:
## Background
Long-running simulation and theorem work must remain honest under cancellation, faults, worker loss, legal schedule interleavings, architecture-specific unsafe code, and different thread/ISA/mode configurations.

## Technical Approach
Register bounded-polling, request-drain-finalize, task/arena/branch leak, checkpoint/pause/migrate/fork/resume, panic/fault containment, thread-count, schedule, same-ISA, cross-ISA envelope, fast/deterministic-mode, and RNG logical-identity matrices. Add deterministic lab-runtime/model-checking exploration for state machines, leases, queues, atomics, cancellation, and scoped receipts, including exhaustive-small and partial-order-reduced schedules with retained counterexamples.

Qualify unsafe concurrent/SIMD/allocator leaves at runtime using admitted sanitizer, Miri-compatible, guard-page, differential scalar oracle, hardware fuzz, and provenance/invariant evidence. OperationalSupport!=available is non-green for an affected unsafe boundary unless an admitted substitute bundle closes the same invariants. Distinguish deterministic hashed content from wall-clock/host envelope data.

## Success Criteria
No leaked work, dual controller, use-after-free/alias/bounds violation, or falsely complete receipt survives. Deterministic claims match their declared class. Cancelled, resumed, migrated, and forked work preserves exact identity/receipt lineage. Every explored schedule and unsafe boundary has coverage or an explicit non-promotable gap.

## Test Plan
Cancellation at every tile/lifecycle boundary; loser-race drain; injected panic, worker loss, OOM, sink outage, and power-loss model; checkpoint corruption; pause/cancel/finalize and lease races; thread/shard/schedule permutations; RNG collision; timestamp-insensitive semantic diff; model-checker schedule replay/shrinking; sanitizer/Miri/guard-page/differential-oracle cases; missing-invariant substitute mutation; same-ISA bit audit and cross-ISA envelope classification.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schedule/model identity, explored/pruned state counts, synchronization/cancellation decisions, unsafe boundary/invariant and instrumentation, thread/ISA/mode, RNG logical streams, identities, faults, lifecycle, scoped outcomes, gap/support state, sanitizer/model-check traces, minimized schedule/witness, artifact closure, and replay. Critical events are lossless or evidence becomes incomplete.

## Considerations
Cross-ISA bit identity is claimed only where specified; otherwise explicit semantic/numerical envelopes apply. Model checking complements rather than replaces long stochastic chaos campaigns.

title: V.2.8 Build mutation, fuzz, adversarial-input, and certifier-of-certifiers campaigns
description:
## Background
Certificate and promotion machinery is security-critical for science; an untested certifier can bless systematically wrong evidence.

## Technical Approach
Mutation-test signs, units, orientations, tolerances, error bounds, certificate verdicts, no-claim states, routing, retention, and exit mappings. Fuzz parsers and typed IR under bounded resources. Independently spot-check interval/Taylor, e-process, conformal, sheaf/topology, and other certifiers with high-precision or analytic oracles.

## Success Criteria
Declared high-value mutants are killed; fuzzing cannot leak, hang, or bypass admission; certifier false-positive rates satisfy preregistered bounds; surviving mutants are explicit risks.

## Test Plan
Seeded mutation corpus, malformed/oversized/deep inputs, adversarial stopping, seam attacks, incorrect enclosures, forged receipts, timeout/cancel, corpus replay and minimization.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable case and journey IDs, manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, seed and logical work identity, requested and consumed budgets, capabilities and feature flags, machine fingerprint, deterministic mode, fixture/oracle/checker identities and declared trusted-computing-base overlap, tolerance derivation, progress and scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, artifact pointers, and minimized witnesses. Large or sensitive payloads are content-addressed and redacted. No unnamed skip or generic success is allowed.

## Considerations
Fuzz absence of failure is not proof. Prioritize mutations that could create false certificates or user-harming green states.

title: V.2.9 Independently adjudicate the MAX test runner and certifier hardening receipt
description:
## Background

## Technical Approach

Cover unit/doctest/compile-fail/type, resource bounds, unsafe invariants, corpus provenance, mutant accounting, model-checking schedules, checkpoint/replay, and cross-mode determinism. ## Test Plan

title: V.3 OBSERVABILITY & FAILURE EVIDENCE — one forensic stream from DSR to tile and replay
description:
## Background
Detailed logging helps only when all layers share typed identity, bounded behavior, redaction, retention, replay, and reconnect semantics. Long jobs outlive clients, workers, shards, and services; a run/case/operation tree alone cannot distinguish immutable submissions, durable jobs, retries, resumes, forks, control authority, or evidence gaps.

## Technical Approach
Extend fs-obs with test, journey, DSR, lifecycle, oracle, visualization, diagnostic, product-verdict, and terminal events. Correlate a typed causal DAG across DSR run/shard, Claim/Journey/Case, Submission/Job/Attempt/checkpoint, asupersync scope, operation, tile, artifact, and receipt. Define monotone reconnectable event cursors, snapshot-plus-delta reconstruction, deduplication, compaction/gap proofs, authoritative lease fencing, immutable terminal receipts, bounded stdout/stderr capture, no-casual-print lint, redaction/share/retention policy, and content-addressed FailureBundles for reproduce/minimize/share. Attack corrupt, truncated, oversized, stale, reordered, duplicated, secret-bearing, and proof-critical-sampled evidence.

## Success Criteria
A user or agent can reconnect to and explain any promotion-relevant run or failure from bounded schema-valid evidence, distinguish job failure from observation loss, reconstruct full attempt/control lineage, and replay or share safely. Stale control cannot mutate a job; promotion-critical events cannot disappear; protected data cannot leak.

## Test Plan
Unit/property tests cover identities, causal DAGs, event schemas, cursors, lease fencing, deduplication, compaction, redaction, retention, and serialization migration. E2E/fault scripts cover disconnect/reconnect, client/service/worker restart, duplicate/out-of-order delivery, cursor gaps, log backpressure, cancellation/drain/finalize, pause/migration, corrupt checkpoints and artifacts, hostile bundles, secret/license canaries, deterministic replay, and independent receipt reconstruction.

## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. Its aggregate receipt content-addresses and reconciles the exact child receipt set, dependency-graph version, frozen manifest/source/code/contract/schema/policy hashes, selection and profile expansion, stable ClaimRevision/Case/Journey/DSR/Campaign/Shard/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, typed causal edges, artifact roots, and verifier identities. It preserves each child's separate ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reports missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting, corrupt, or outside-scope children explicitly; and never averages disagreement or upgrades a claim. Aggregate progress, cost, timing, memory, diagnostics, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, accessibility state, and exact replay pointers are schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe, and semantically equivalent for human and stable JSONL consumers. Promotion-critical child evidence is referenced losslessly.

## Considerations
This is a rollup, not executable work. Its children extend existing fs-obs, HELM, DSR, asupersync, and Design Ledger contracts; they must not create a competing identity, event, scheduler, or evidence dialect.

title: V.3.1 Extend fs-obs with verification, durable-lifecycle, scoped-receipt, oracle, and promotion event kinds
description:
## Background
The existing observability standard is the right substrate, but it must explicitly represent manifest selection, durable identity, scoped operations and jobs, independent oracles, scientific visualization, evidence integrity, and promotion effects. An unqualified terminal event is unsafe because a successful status query, a failed worker attempt, and a refuted scientific job can coexist.

## Technical Approach
Add additive typed event kinds for manifest and source-snapshot selection; Core/Max stratum and campaign-profile expansion; DSR and Campaign runs; submission/admission/queue; Job/Attempt/Operation/lease/cursor identity; attach/detach; journey/case phase; local execution scope/tile progress; heartbeat and observation gap; oracle comparison and tolerance derivation; budget delta; capability and domain decision; fault/cancellation/checkpoint/pause/migration/drain/finalize; visualization and temporal-presentation transform; artifact commit/retention/redaction/share/verify; diagnostic repair; and scoped receipt state.

Every outcome event declares receipt_scope={operation, attempt, job, campaign} and receipt identity. Record ExecutionDisposition; RequestedPredicateOutcome; exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication where applicable; EvidenceMethodSet; EpistemicGrade; DomainApplicability; OperationalSupport; separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity; and PromotionEffect. Not-applicable fields are explicit, never absent by convention. Operation events may embed immutable snapshots or references to Job/Campaign receipts but cannot overwrite them.

Preserve deterministic hashed content separately from wall-clock envelope fields. Proof- and promotion-critical transitions are lossless; inability to persist one makes closure incomplete/indeterminate. Version old ClaimState and combined completeness/integrity migrations with an explicit loss report.

## Success Criteria
All verification layers use registered event kinds. Old readers preserve unknown additive payloads. The full identity DAG, local execution containment, observation gaps, lifecycle, scoped operations, scientific adjudication, evidence method/grade, applicability/support, completeness, integrity, and promotion impact are reconstructible without parsing prose or process codes.

## Test Plan
Schema round trips and old-reader compatibility; unknown kind; required-field deletion; wrong receipt scope; operation/job overwrite attempt; invalid claim/adjudication combination; complete-but-corrupt and partial-but-verified evidence; non-finite quantities; hostile strings; deterministic content hash; lifecycle transition coverage; cursor gap/backfill; proof-event sink failure; critical-event sampling mutation; old-field migration ambiguity; and exhaustive valid scoped-product/process-projection cases.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schema-versioned bounded/redacted JSONL keyed by DsrRun, CampaignRun, Shard, Claim, Case, Journey, Submission, Job, Attempt, Operation, execution-scope, tile, checkpoint, and artifact identities. Include hashes, Five Explicits, capabilities/mode/machine, oracle/TCB/tolerance, progress and budgets, lifecycle/control schedule, scoped product receipts, diagnostics, artifacts/FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, and replay. Pretty output is only a rendering of the typed object.

## Considerations
Extend rather than fork fs-obs; core library code never prints casually. Event-delivery success is not scientific success. Missing or dropped critical evidence is recorded as closure failure, never inferred from a green process.

title: V.3.2 Correlate DSR/Campaign shards with local Attempt execution-containment trees
description:
## Background
Concurrent kernel and solver events need deterministic containment so cost, cancellation, defects, and evidence can be attributed locally. But the global durable lifecycle is not a tree: retries, resumes, forks, replays, checkpoints, and artifacts create typed multi-parent relations owned by V.3.8.

## Technical Approach
Define the local execution-containment model only. DsrRunId identifies one DSR invocation; CampaignRunId identifies one canonical manifest execution; ShardId identifies a deterministic partition; JourneyId and CaseId identify logical definitions; ExecutionOpId, ExecutionScopeId/ScopePath, and TileId identify nested work inside one Attempt. V.3.8 owns SubmissionId, AdmissionReceipt, JobId, AttemptId, OperationId, checkpoints, artifacts, durable causal edges, and idempotency.

Within an Attempt, require one primary containment parent for each execution event and a deterministic tree rooted at the propagated AttemptId. DSR-hosting, campaign-selection, and shard-membership are typed contextual edges, not aliases for a Job, Attempt, or user operation. Cross-process propagation carries all relevant IDs without redefining them. Semantic order comes from logical parent/sequence identities; wall clocks are envelope evidence.

Expose an embedding interface by which V.3.8 places each local Attempt tree into the authoritative global causal DAG. Cross-attempt artifact/checkpoint/replay/fork relations never masquerade as local parentage.

## Success Criteria
Every local execution event has one valid Attempt containment lineage and exact DSR/Campaign/Shard/Journey/Case context. Duplicate delivery is idempotent. Local queries reconstruct complete operation/scope/tile evidence. Global multi-parent queries defer to V.3.8 and cannot be falsely flattened into a tree.

## Test Plan
Unit/property tests cover canonical ID construction, cardinality, collision resistance, deterministic parentage, scope paths, shard/context propagation, serialization/version migration, and tree invariants. Model/E2E tests cover concurrent interleaving, duplicate/reordered events, lost parent, worker handoff, cancellation races, cross-process propagation, wrong Attempt root, DSR/Campaign aliasing, an artifact with multiple causal parents, and embedding into a V.3.8 DAG. Mutate each identity field and local/global edge kind and require rejection or explicit integrity gap.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with DsrRun, CampaignRun, Shard, Journey, Case, propagated Attempt, ExecutionOp, ExecutionScope, and Tile identities; manifest/source/code/contract/schema hashes; seed/logical work; budgets/capabilities/mode/machine; progress; local parent and sequence; scoped receipt reference; artifact pointers; gap/integrity state; and minimized witness. Large or sensitive payloads are content-addressed and redacted; critical lineage events are lossless or closure becomes incomplete.

## Considerations
This bead intentionally does not own durable submission/job/attempt semantics, idempotency, fork/resume, or the global causal DAG. That separation prevents a convenient local tree from corrupting real multi-parent scientific provenance.

title: V.3.3 Capture process streams with loss classes, bounded backpressure, durable gaps, and no-casual-print lint
description:
## Background
Unbounded logs can deadlock or exhaust memory, while ad hoc stdout creates a second untyped truth path. Conversely, claiming bounded sampling while promising that no diagnostic is ever lost is impossible without event classes and explicit failure semantics.

## Technical Approach
Specify process capture, stream framing, event classes, severity, coalescing/sampling, bounded queues, durable spill, truncation, backpressure, child lifecycle, and stdout/stderr policy. Pretty CLI output is rendered from typed events; stable JSONL carries machine events; core libraries never print casually.

Classify events:
1. proof/promotion/lifecycle/identity/control-critical events are lossless. They commit durably or the affected receipt sets EvidenceCompleteness=partial/missing and/or EvidenceIntegrity=unverified with PromotionEffect non-eligible; a sink failure cannot silently green;
2. diagnostic events may coalesce or truncate only with explicit Gap/Dropped counts, range, reason, policy version, and a committed artifact pointer where detail was retained;
3. verbose performance/telemetry events may be sampled/dropped under declared policy with explicit counts and error/coverage implications.

An artifact pointer replaces inline data only after durable content/hash commit. Backpressure is cancellation-aware and cannot hold control/lifecycle locks. Process termination and OperationReceipt reconcile only when a final receipt exists; signal/host death without a receipt remains an explicit observation gap.

## Success Criteria
High-volume runs remain bounded, cancellable, and forensically honest. No proof-critical event is silently lost. Every diagnostic/telemetry drop is quantified. Truncation points to a verified durable artifact or declares loss. A green process cannot coexist with missing required closure.

## Test Plan
Burst/sustained volume; multiple slow/dead sinks; retention-budget and disk exhaustion; proof-event overload; diagnostic coalescing; telemetry sampling; durable-spill crash/recovery; artifact commit before/after pointer; broken pipe; UTF-8/binary/hostile data; child crash; cancellation while backpressured; stdout/stderr separation; signal death without receipt; casual-print mutation; favorable gap-count deletion.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit event class, policy/version, original/emitted/dropped counts and ranges, queue/spill/backpressure metrics, sink acknowledgements, Gap records, artifact commit/hash, cancellation/fault schedule, scoped receipt/evidence effect, process/signal state, diagnostics, minimized witness, and replay. Sensitive data is redacted before persistence; huge payloads are content-addressed.

## Considerations
Boundedness and completeness are reconciled through explicit evidence state, not wishful wording. Operational telemetry may be lossy; proof closure may not.

description:
## Background
Reproducibility must not leak credentials, personal data, export-controlled inputs, or protected standards content.

## Technical Approach
Define field-level sensitivity labels, deterministic redaction, salted/unsalted hash policy, license/export realms, local-only artifacts, share manifests, retention/expiry, and privileged replay. Scan structured events and referenced artifacts before publication.

## Success Criteria
Forbidden content never appears in shareable logs or bundles; redaction preserves enough identity for diagnosis; access denial is explicit; promotion evidence and counterexamples retain their required durable closure.

## Test Plan
Seed secrets in every field and nested artifact; Unicode/encoding bypasses; protected standard excerpts; hash dictionary attacks; privilege downgrade; expiry and legal-hold conflicts; redacted replay.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable case and journey IDs, manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, seed and logical work identity, requested and consumed budgets, capabilities and feature flags, machine fingerprint, deterministic mode, fixture/oracle/checker identities and declared trusted-computing-base overlap, tolerance derivation, progress and scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, artifact pointers, and minimized witnesses. Large or sensitive payloads are content-addressed and redacted. No unnamed skip or generic success is allowed.

## Considerations
Do not log raw credentials even locally. Protected/licensed fixtures may yield an explicit OperationalSupport=license-unavailable public replay while preserving a private auditable receipt.
