title: V.3.5 Independently adjudicate the CORE structured logging and evidence receipt
description:
## Background
Core test and journey runners need a trustworthy forensic stream before they can issue promotion evidence.

## Technical Approach
Independently validate correlation, bounded capture, deterministic content, redaction, terminal reconciliation, and retention on representative unit, property, benchmark, conformance, and E2E events. Publish CoreObservabilityReceipt.

## Success Criteria
A clean checker reconstructs selected cases, verdicts, costs, cancellations, and artifacts; malformed or leaking streams fail closed with stable diagnostics.

## Test Plan
Missing/duplicate/reordered events; wrong parent; false exit; backpressure; secret injection; truncation; cancellation; clean-store query and replay.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Exact execution contract
Manifest: `tests/leapfrog/manifests/core-observability-independent-adjudication.toml`. No-mock independent driver: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/core-observability-independent-adjudication.sh`. Separately retained canonical execution is `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite core-observability-independent-adjudication --stratum core --profile standard`. The checker reconstructs critical-event closure from retained streams without privileged database access. A missing path, divergent selection, bypass, or incomplete receipt is non-green.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable case and journey IDs, manifest/code/contract/schema hashes, seed and logical work identity, requested and consumed budgets, capabilities and feature flags, machine fingerprint, deterministic mode, fixture/oracle/checker identities and declared trusted-computing-base overlap, tolerance derivation, progress and scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, artifact pointers, and minimized witnesses. Large or sensitive payloads are content-addressed and redacted. No unnamed skip or generic success is allowed.

## Considerations
This receipt covers core observability semantics, not the truth of domain results carried by events.

title: V.3.6 Build content-addressed, capability-sandboxed FailureBundle verify/reproduce/minimize/share
description:
## Background
A stack trace or raw log is insufficient for failures involving fixtures, schemas, budgets, schedules, and scientific comparison arithmetic. A FailureBundle is also untrusted input that may attempt path traversal, resource exhaustion, code execution, credential access, or provenance forgery.

## Technical Approach
Define FailureBundle with manifest/source snapshot slice, typed request—not a shell command—code/contract/schema/tool hashes, inputs and normalized events, identity DAG slice, machine/capability fingerprint, seed, budgets, checkpoint, oracle/checker version, comparison arithmetic, scoped outcome receipts, minimized witness, and redaction/share policy. Implement verify, inspect, reproduce, minimize, explain, and safe-share.

Parse and verify in safe Rust under strict size/depth/count/time/memory budgets before materialization. Use a capability-restricted sandbox with deny-by-default network, devices, credentials, host writes, environment, dynamic loading, and subprocesses. Never execute a bundle-supplied shell string. Map approved typed operations only to pinned binaries/components and declared capabilities.

Defend archive/path normalization, absolute and parent traversal, alternate separators, Unicode/case collisions, NUL/reserved names, symlink/hardlink/reparse equivalents, sparse-file/decompression bombs, recursive nesting, duplicate entries, TOCTOU replacement, artifact hash mismatch, and malicious checkpoints. Extraction is into a fresh isolated root using content-addressed verified objects and race-resistant handles. Reproduction promotes no scientific claim merely because a failure reappears.

## Success Criteria
An authorized third party can verify and reproduce the scoped failure or receive a precise environment/capability/domain mismatch. Minimization preserves the exact requested failure predicate. Tampering is localized. A hostile bundle cannot escape isolation, execute undeclared code, read secrets, exhaust unbounded resources, forge closure, or overwrite history.

## Test Plan
Scientific mismatch, panic, cancellation, timeout, corrupt artifact, nondeterminism, secret input, unavailable hardware, migration, minimizer cancellation, and share verification. Security E2E covers traversal, absolute/Unicode/case paths, symlink/hardlink/TOCTOU swaps, duplicate entries, deep nesting, huge declared/expanded/sparse sizes, decompression bombs, hostile filenames, environment/credential probes, network/device access, subprocess/dynamic-code attempts, malicious checkpoint/schema, signature/hash substitution, cancellation during parse/extract/run, and cleanup after crash.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit bundle/schema/hash/signature identity, parser budgets and consumption, normalized entry map, rejected path/link/resource/code capabilities, sandbox policy and granted capabilities, materialization handles, pinned execution identity, scoped receipts, redaction/share decisions, minimization predicate, artifact closure, diagnostics, minimized attack, and exact safe replay. Logs are bounded and themselves outside the untrusted extraction root.

## Considerations
A reproduced infrastructure crash does not reproduce a scientific claim. Sandbox strength and unavailable host primitives are explicit OperationalSupport fields; insufficient isolation is non-green for untrusted replay.

title: V.3.7 Red-team untrusted bundles, corruption, resource bombs, sandbox escape, redaction, and replay semantics
description:
## Background
Failure evidence is a security boundary and a source of false green results. Red-team qualification must attack both semantic integrity and the replay sandbox.

## Technical Approach
Independently mutate bundles, events, manifests, source snapshots, identities, hashes/signatures, versions, privileges, truncation/gap markers, artifact pointers, scoped receipts, comparison arithmetic, ClaimRelations, and redaction. Attack bounded parsing, archive materialization, capability isolation, pinned execution, and partial recovery. Publish MaxObservabilityReceipt with retained minimized attacks and exact support envelope.

Recoverable incomplete evidence is recorded as EvidenceCompleteness=partial with separate EvidenceIntegrity and a non-eligible/restricted PromotionEffect. A weaker surviving scientific statement must be a separate exact ClaimRecord; 'Partial' is never a truth state.

## Success Criteria
No hostile bundle can forge a satisfied predicate, established claim, eligible promotion, or verified closure; escape isolation; execute undeclared code; enumerate secrets; exhaust unbounded resources; bypass redaction/license policy; or rewrite history. Authentic-but-incomplete and complete-but-corrupt states remain distinguishable.

## Test Plan
Bit flips and substitution; hash/signature/version confusion; missing/duplicated/reordered terminal events; split-brain process/receipt states; stale readers; privilege loss; cancelled replay; traversal and normalization variants; symlink/hardlink/reparse and TOCTOU; recursive/decompression/sparse bombs; hostile checkpoint; environment/network/device/subprocess/dynamic-loading probes; policy downgrade; gap-marker deletion; ClaimRelation direction mutation; scoped-receipt overwrite; and clean-host replay.

## Exact execution contract
Manifest: `tests/leapfrog/manifests/max-failure-evidence-red-team.toml`. No-mock independent driver: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/max-failure-evidence-red-team.sh`. Separately retained canonical executions are `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite max-failure-evidence-red-team --stratum max --profile security` and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite max-failure-evidence-red-team --stratum max --profile chaos`. Security and chaos CampaignRuns attack hostile bundles and loss/recovery semantics independently. A missing path, divergent selection, bypass, or incomplete receipt is non-green.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit attack ID/class, mutated field and before/after hashes, parser/sandbox budgets, capability decisions, identity and scoped receipt effects, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, claim/promotion effect, redaction findings, resource peaks, minimized exploit/witness, artifact closure, and exact replay. Critical security evidence is lossless or the qualification receipt is incomplete.

## Considerations
Fail closed without discarding diagnostically valuable authentic evidence. Sandbox or platform limitations are explicit support gaps, never favorable defaults.

title: V.3.8 Specify durable Submission/Admission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, global causal DAG, fenced control, and reconnectable cursors
description:
## Background
Long-running multiphysics, optimization, parameter-sweep, and theorem-search work outlives terminals, client connections, worker processes, DSR shards, and service instances. Local execution containment is necessary but cannot distinguish pre-admission intent, rejection, one durable logical job, worker attempts, control/query operations, retries, resumes, forks, observer position, or authority.

## Technical Approach
Specify versioned identities and exact cardinalities:

- SubmissionId identifies immutable client intent plus actor/project context, idempotency envelope, canonical request digest, and creation receipt. It exists before admission and remains replayable when rejected.
- AdmissionReceipt records accepted or rejected against an exact capability, dataset, license/expiry, quota, device, policy, schema, and host snapshot. Acceptance creates exactly one JobId; rejection creates no JobId and never erases the Submission.
- JobId identifies one durable logical computation with immutable admitted intent and zero or more AttemptIds.
- AttemptId identifies one worker incarnation caused by initial execution, retry, resume, or migration. Resume/migration normally creates a new Attempt for the same Job; a semantic/budget/claim change or explicit fork creates a new Job linked to a parent CheckpointId.
- OperationId identifies one submit/status/watch/attach/checkpoint/pause/migrate/cancel/resume/fork/inspect/verify query or mutation and owns its OperationReceipt.
- DsrRunId, CampaignRunId, ShardId, JourneyId, CaseId, ExecutionScopeId, TileId, CheckpointId, ArtifactId, ControlLease, and EventCursor retain distinct types.

Model the authoritative global provenance as a typed acyclic DAG. Local V.3.2 Attempt trees embed within it. Typed edges include submitted-as, admitted-as/rejected-by, attempted-by, retried-from, resumed-from, migrated-from, forked-from, replay-of, hosted-by-DSR, selected-by-campaign, consumed-checkpoint, produced/derived-from-artifact, and observed/controlled-by-operation. Multi-parent edges are explicit.

Idempotency is exact: the same key plus identical canonical intent returns the original Submission and original Admission/Job or Rejection receipt; the same key plus different intent returns an idempotency-conflict receipt with redacted digests and no mutation. Re-evaluating a rejection after capabilities change requires an explicit new Submission or versioned retry policy linked to the old one.

Define snapshot-plus-delta observation with schema/hash binding, per-stream sequence and deduplication, cursor acknowledgement, deterministic pagination, cursor expiry/compaction proofs, bounded backpressure, and explicit Gap/EvidenceIntegrity state when reconstruction is impossible. Authorized jobs list/search/show supports recovery by SubmissionId or idempotency key, deterministic owner/project/tag/time/state filters, redacted metadata, full attempt lineage, and capability-scoped visibility.

ControlLease authority uses an authoritative issuer epoch plus monotonic server-side time or equivalent consensus-safe source. Every mutation carries a fencing token. Client clocks never grant authority. Terminal scoped receipts are immutable; later attempts and operations link rather than overwrite.

Bind every discovery, search, status, watch, control, checkpoint, artifact, report, share, and offline-verify operation to a typed AuthorizationContext: pseudonymous actor, tenant/project, resource, action, issuer, audience, capability provenance, delegation chain, expiry, revocation epoch, and anti-replay nonce. Observer, controller, exporter, verifier, and delegator rights are distinct least-privilege capabilities; authorization is rechecked on reconnect and immediately before every side effect. Opaque Job/Artifact/Checkpoint IDs aid confidentiality but never replace authorization. Search, pagination, cache, timing, denial, and recovery behavior must not reveal cross-project resource existence.

## Success Criteria
Every intent—including rejection—has stable identity and replay. Every accepted Job, Attempt, Operation, checkpoint, artifact, and receipt has complete typed lineage. Duplicate or concurrent submission cannot duplicate mutation. A lost JobId is recoverable by authorized deterministic search without cross-user enumeration. Reconnect either reconstructs exact state or returns a structured gap; missing events never invent green. Stale controllers cannot commit after a newer epoch.

## Test Plan
Unit/property/model tests cover canonical digests, identity cardinality, admission snapshots, accepted/rejected submissions, idempotency conflict, serialization/migration, causal-DAG acyclicity and edge typing, local-tree embedding, monotone sequences, pagination, deduplication, lease fencing, expiry, and scoped receipt immutability.

No-mock E2E uses 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/lifecycle-identity.toml' and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/lifecycle-identity.sh'. Its separately retained concrete executions are 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster lifecycle-identity --stratum core --profile standard', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster lifecycle-identity --stratum core --profile chaos', and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster lifecycle-identity --stratum core --profile security'. Cover duplicate identical and conflicting concurrent requests; duplicate rejected submission; capability change after rejection; lost client output before/after admission acknowledgement; lost JobId recovery; large/stale pagination; cross-user enumeration resistance; delayed/out-of-order events; reconnect and compaction; client/service/worker restart; retry/resume/migration/fork distinctions; stale checkpoints; artifact tamper; clock skew/rollback; issuer restart; network partition/heal; delayed renewal; split-brain takeover; lease expiry during checkpoint/finalize; and mutation of every identity/edge.

Add no-mock two-actor/two-project authorization E2E: guessed and harvested Job/Artifact/Checkpoint IDs; cross-project list/search/status/watch/control; observer-to-controller escalation; over-broad delegation; confused-deputy audience/issuer mix-up; expired, revoked, replayed, duplicated, or wrong-resource capabilities; revocation during watch/checkpoint/cancel/finalize; cache and timing side channels; unauthorized report/share/redact/offline-bundle access; and recovery after client, issuer, service, or worker restart. Denial must be fail-closed, non-enumerating, idempotent where applicable, and leave no unauthorized side effect.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit identity-allocation, Submission, Admission/Rejection, idempotency, Job/Attempt/Operation, lease, cursor, search/pagination, reconnect, checkpoint, control, artifact, gap, and scoped-receipt events. Retain canonical/redacted digest inputs, admission snapshot, all typed edges, actor/capability/lease epoch, sequence/cursor ranges, dedup decisions, attempt reason, checkpoint compatibility arithmetic, gap proofs, machine/shard/process identities, outcome-product references, minimized race witness, and exact recovery/replay commands. Logs are bounded, redacted, backpressure-safe, and promotion-critical identity events are lossless.

Retain lossless AuthorizationDecision events keyed to OperationId and causal resource identities, with pseudonymous actor/project, policy and revocation versions, capability/delegation-chain hash, issuer/audience/action/resource class, decision/reason, recheck point, and side-effect disposition. Never log bearer material, raw tokens, secrets, or a denial detail that becomes an enumeration oracle.

## Considerations
These identities extend HELM, fs-session, asupersync, DSR, and Design Ledger; they do not create a rival scheduler. Read observation and control authority remain separate. Wall-clock timestamps are evidence, never identity or deterministic ordering.

title: V.4 ONE-COMMAND E2E — Core/Max strata across smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-ISA, and release profiles
description:
## Background
A unit-green feature can still fail at discovery, authoring, admission, planning, durable execution, observation, visualization, packaging, verification, sharing, or replay. Users need one production-path semantic protocol whose scientific scope, campaign intensity, identity, lifecycle, receipt scope, and outcome algebra are explicit.

## Technical Approach
Implement one typed VerificationProtocol/JourneyEngine used by product CLI and HELM/session APIs, the fs-test/DSR adapter, and the zero-semantic hermetic 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh' wrapper. Separate Core/Max claim stratum from smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-ISA, and release profiles.

V.4.2 owns typed command grammar, selectors, list, doctor handoff, dry-run, estimate, plan, explain, diff, and synchronous convenience behavior. V.4.9 exclusively owns immutable Submission intent and AdmissionReceipt, durable Job/Attempt identity, status/watch/attach, checkpoint/pause/migrate/cancel/resume/fork, lease/cursor/reconnect/restart behavior, artifacts/report/share/offline verify, and terminal state machines. V.4.3 enforces isolated fixtures and no mocks. V.4.4 owns scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts and the orthogonal claim/evidence algebra. V.4.6 adapts legacy suites only through semantic diffs.

Provide discovery through replay without a test-only side door. A process code projects only the current OperationReceipt; embedded scientific Job and Campaign receipts remain unchanged. Every wrapper and API surface must prove selection, lifecycle, events, artifacts, and outcome equivalence against the shared protocol.

## Success Criteria
Core and Max journeys under every admitted profile are discoverable, cost-estimable, detachable/reconnectable, controllable with fenced authority, cancellable, checkpointable, migratable, inspectable, verifiable, shareable, and replayable through human and agent surfaces. Submission rejection remains replayable without a JobId. Duplicate idempotency is exact. No silent legacy alias, retry, process code, wrapper discrepancy, partial artifact, corrupt closure, or successful status/control operation can manufacture scientific green.

## Test Plan
Comprehensive parser/API/state-machine, selector, scoped-receipt, outcome-product, stratum/profile, idempotency, and artifact-verification unit/property/model tests. No-mock E2E covers valid and rejected submissions, duplicate admitted and duplicate rejected requests, later-capability-change resubmission, detached and synchronous runs, multiple observers/controllers, disconnect/reconnect, stale lease/cursor/checkpoint, pause/cancel/complete races, worker/service restart and migration, timeout versus budget exhaustion, established/refuted/unresolved and restricted claims, complete/partial/corrupt/conflicting evidence, outside-domain and support failures, tamper, report/share/redaction, accessibility/non-TTY, semantic legacy adapters, deterministic replay, and false-green mutations.

Conformance tests execute the same typed request through product CLI, HELM/session API, fs-test/DSR adapter, and run.sh wrapper and compare canonical normalized request/selection digests, event semantics, scoped receipts, artifacts, and current-operation process projection.

## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. Its aggregate receipt content-addresses and reconciles the exact child receipt set, dependency-graph version, frozen manifest/source/code/contract/schema/policy hashes, selection and profile expansion, stable ClaimRevision/Case/Journey/DSR/Campaign/Shard/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, typed causal edges, artifact roots, and verifier identities. It preserves each child's separate ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reports missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting, corrupt, or outside-scope children explicitly; and never averages disagreement or upgrades a claim. Aggregate progress, cost, timing, memory, diagnostics, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, accessibility state, and exact replay pointers are schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe, and semantically equivalent for human and stable JSONL consumers. Promotion-critical child evidence is referenced losslessly.

## Considerations
This rollup extends canonical HELM, fs-obs, Gauntlet, DSR, and ledger paths. It must not introduce a second scheduler, semantic API, verdict engine, handwritten catalog, or shell-defined science.

title: V.4.1 Specify Journey DSL, scoped receipt algebra, claim strata, campaign profiles, Five Explicits, and process projection
description:
## Background
An E2E suite is trustworthy only when user intent, scientific scope, campaign profile, identity scope, lifecycle, requested operation predicate, scientific claim, evidence closure, and non-success states are typed before scripts proliferate.

## Technical Approach
Specify JourneyManifest and a production phase graph for discover/preflight, author/import, validate, estimate, plan, submit/admit, queue/execute/observe, checkpoint/pause/migrate/cancel/resume/fork, inspect/verify/report/share, and replay. Require the Five Explicits, artifact sandbox, public-surface identity, and exactly one Core or Max claim stratum. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. Cross-facet combinations are allowed only through a versioned manifest-defined composite ProfileId whose ordered inputs, precedence and conflict rules, budgets, capabilities, selection expansion, and semantic-diff hash are frozen before execution; repeated --profile flags or implicit string composition are invalid. Scale remains an orthogonal workload/budget dimension, not a profile ID.

Define distinct OperationReceipt, AttemptReceipt, JobReceipt, and CampaignReceipt schemas. Each scopes ExecutionDisposition and RequestedPredicateOutcome to its own operation or aggregate. Job/Campaign receipts also carry exact ClaimRecord plus ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect. A receipt references another scope without mutating it.

Every ClaimRecord has kind, statement, quantifiers, units/conventions, hypotheses, exact domain, revision, and implication/refinement/restriction/counterexample edges. A restricted or weaker surviving theorem is a new ClaimRecord, never a vague Partial truth state. Unsupported is derived from applicability/support, not adjudication. Old ClaimState and combined evidence fields migrate through loss-reporting adapters.

Process codes project only the current OperationReceipt: 0 satisfied, 10 unsatisfied, 11 invalid schema/admission, 12 indeterminate or required operation evidence incomplete, 13 operation unsupported, 14 operation cancelled and drained, 15 operation timeout finalized, 16 infrastructure error, 17 integrity/security failure, and 18 operation budget exhaustion finalized. A status query may exit 0 while embedding a JobReceipt with ClaimAdjudication=refuted or a failed ExecutionDisposition; cancel acceptance may exit 0 before eventual drained cancellation. A valid refutation is satisfied for 'adjudicate' and unsatisfied for 'prove'. Every conditional skip is a retained typed receipt.

## Success Criteria
Every phase, transition, identity, receipt scope, stratum/profile selection, outcome field, and process projection is unambiguous. Defaults are inspectable and ledgered. Human and agent surfaces parse the same typed result. Timeout and budget exhaustion remain distinct. Scientific adjudication, evidence grade, domain, operational support, completeness, integrity, and promotion effect cannot be laundered into one status word.

## Test Plan
Schema/canonicalization unit tests; legal/illegal phase transitions; stratum/profile composition; all operation codes; exhaustive valid scoped-product combinations and projection properties; status-on-refuted-job and cancel-before-drain; deleted requested predicate; adjudicate-versus-prove refutation; restricted-claim implication graph; complete-but-corrupt and partial-but-verified evidence; missing Five Explicit; malformed phase graph; outside-domain versus missing-hardware; cancellation/pause/migration at every phase; JSONL/pretty semantic equivalence; old/new migration with lossy ambiguity; and favorable projection mutations.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit all identities, receipt scope, stratum/profile, requested predicate, Five Explicits, lifecycle, exact claim/domain/revision graph, evidence methods/grade, oracle/TCB/tolerance, applicability/support, completeness, integrity, promotion effect, projection rule/version, process code, diagnostics, artifacts, and replay pointers in bounded redacted fs-obs JSONL. Retain truth tables and minimized counterexamples.

## Considerations
The DSL describes user intent and typed receipt semantics; it does not duplicate FrankenScript, bypass HELM admission, let a shell wrapper own science, or let process conventions redefine a job's result.

title: V.4.2 Implement typed command grammar, selectors, plan/estimate/explain/diff, and zero-semantic adapters
description:
## Background
Users need one predictable command grammar that exposes selection, cost, uncertainty, assumptions, and repair options before expensive work begins. The front door must not duplicate the durable scheduler/lifecycle owned by V.4.9 or let a shell wrapper define scientific semantics.

## Technical Approach
Define one typed VerificationProtocol command schema shared by product CLI, Rust API, FrankenScript, supported WASM, fs-test/DSR, and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh'. Typed operations include list/describe, doctor/capabilities, plan, estimate, submit, run (synchronous convenience), jobs list/search/show, status, watch/attach, checkpoint/pause/migrate/cancel/resume/fork, attempts, inspect, artifacts, report, share, verify, replay, explain, and diff.

Define selector namespaces and cardinality:
- '--cluster <id>' selects exactly one generated family, portfolio, lifecycle, or conformance cluster.
- '--suite <id>' selects exactly one generated aggregate/meta-manifest.
- '--tutorial <id>' selects exactly one generated tutorial branch.
- case/journey/tag filters refine the chosen target and cannot silently widen it.
Cluster, suite, and tutorial selectors are mutually exclusive unless a versioned composition manifest explicitly says otherwise. Unknown, ambiguous, duplicate, empty, stale, or conflicting selectors fail with stable diagnostics and ranked fixes.

Scientific plan/estimate/submit/run/replay requires exactly one explicit Core or Max stratum and exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId unless a generated tutorial or immutable replay receipt pins them. The --profile flag accepts one ID; suites expand multi-profile obligations into separate CampaignRuns, and composite IDs are admitted only under the frozen, conflict-checked composition contract in V.1.5. Status/control/artifact operations address immutable IDs and inherit the Job's stratum/profile; overrides are rejected. List/doctor/capabilities do not invent a scientific stratum.

V.4.2 owns parsing, canonical request hashing, side-effect-free plan/estimate, explain/diff, generated grammar/help schema, dispatch to the typed protocol, and synchronous wait convenience. V.4.9 exclusively owns Submission/Admission/Job/Attempt, idempotency mutation, status/watch/attach, lifecycle control/restart/reconnect, artifact/report/share/verify behavior, and terminal state machines.

The shell adapter is zero-semantic and portable: resolve its own resources independent of CWD; preserve arguments exactly; separate JSONL stdout from diagnostics stderr; isolate allowlisted environment; handle concurrent invocations, broken pipes, SIGINT/SIGTERM traps, and cleanup; and prevent shell injection. Omitted subcommand compatibility, if retained at all, is an explicit deprecated adapter to 'run', never ambiguous parsing.

Process code projects only a finalized OperationReceipt. SIGKILL, host power loss, shell death, or wrapper crash may terminate with platform signal codes and no receipt; those codes are never scientific outcomes. Reconnect/status over durable identity is authoritative.

## Success Criteria
All surfaces produce the same canonical typed request and selection digest. Plan/estimate are side-effect-free and uncertainty-calibrated. Lifecycle commands dispatch to V.4.9 without a second implementation. Wrapper behavior is correct from arbitrary CWD with hostile-but-valid arguments and environment. Generated help/completions describe the same grammar. A process code is never interpreted without a finalized OperationReceipt.

## Test Plan
Parser/API unit/property tests cover every operation, selector namespace/cardinality, stratum/profile inheritance, unknown/conflicting/empty selectors, leading dashes, spaces, Unicode, quotes, shell metacharacters, path normalization, deterministic hashing, semantic diff, and stable diagnostics. Side-effect audits prove plan/estimate do not mutate durable state.

No-mock conformance E2E sends identical typed requests through product CLI, Rust/FrankenScript/WASM where supported, fs-test/DSR, and run.sh and compares normalized request/selection digests, events, artifacts, scoped receipts, and operation-code projections. Run from arbitrary CWD and paths with spaces/Unicode; test concurrent wrappers, missing tools, environment contamination, stdout/stderr separation, broken pipe, SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup, SIGKILL before submit acknowledgement and after admission before acknowledgement, killed watch/control processes, idempotent reconciliation, shell-injection attempts, and no-test-side-door mutations.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit OperationId, actor/surface/version, raw-argument digest and canonical request, selector expansion, stratum/profile source, inherited immutable IDs, defaults, Five Explicits, capabilities, plan/estimate uncertainty, dispatch target, finalized OperationReceipt/projection, wrapper environment allowlist, signal/trap/cleanup events, diagnostics/repairs, and exact replay. Raw sensitive arguments are redacted; logs are bounded and backpressure-safe.

## Considerations
Do not hide expensive escalation behind defaults. Estimates are calibrated predictions, not guarantees. Generated help ownership is shared with V.5.9's user-facing doctor/completion experience; the grammar source remains typed and singular.

title: V.4.3 Enforce isolated fixtures/artifacts and no-mock, no-test-only-side-door execution
description:
## Background
Mocked or privileged test paths can validate an architecture users never execute.

## Technical Approach
Define hermetic-but-production-real fixture staging, artifact-store namespaces, capability fixtures, temporary credentials, hardware simulators only where the public contract explicitly supports simulation, and cleanup receipts without destructive commands. Detect test-only branches, bypassed admission/governor/ledger, embedded goldens, fixture mutation, and cross-run contamination.

## Success Criteria
E2E invokes the same binaries, parsers, planners, solvers, exporters, and replay paths as users; fixtures are immutable and content-addressed; parallel runs cannot contaminate each other.

## Test Plan
Mutation that activates a test bypass; fixture tamper; shared-state race; missing credential/capability; read-only artifact store; crash/cancel; deterministic clean-room rerun.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Use schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable run/shard/journey/case/op identities; manifest, code, contract, and schema hashes; Five Explicits; capabilities and feature flags; deterministic mode and machine fingerprint; oracle/checker identity and TCB overlap; tolerance arithmetic; progress, budgets, cancellation/fault schedule, scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, diagnostics, artifact pointers, and minimized witness. Pretty output is only a rendering of these events. Logs are bounded, redacted, and backpressure-safe.

## Considerations
Independent oracles may be dev-only, but production computation and artifact semantics may not be mocked.

title: V.4.4 Compose scoped execution, predicate, claim, evidence, applicability, support, and promotion verdicts without laundering
description:
## Background
A zero process exit cannot say whether the current operation succeeded, a worker attempt completed, equations converged, conservation held, an oracle agreed, evidence is complete and authentic, the exact domain applies, required hardware/data/licenses exist, or a theorem is established, refuted, or unresolved. Collapsing these facts loses forensic value and can manufacture a false green.

## Technical Approach
Implement a versioned typed product algebra on explicit OperationReceipt, AttemptReceipt, JobReceipt, and CampaignReceipt scopes.

Each relevant receipt carries:
1. ExecutionDisposition for lifecycle/system completion at that scope.
2. RequestedPredicateOutcome for the exact manifest-declared operation or campaign question.
3. an exact ClaimRecord identity where science is claimed: claim kind, statement, quantifiers, conventions/units, hypotheses, domain, revision, and implication/refinement/restriction/counterexample graph.
4. ClaimAdjudication={established, refuted, unresolved, not-claimed}.
5. EvidenceMethodSet with method provenance and TCB overlap.
6. EpistemicGrade={proof, certified, validated, corroborated, preliminary, conjectural}, assigned by versioned policy.
7. DomainApplicability={in-domain, outside-domain, domain-unknown, not-evaluated}.
8. OperationalSupport={available, missing-capability, hardware-unavailable, license-unavailable, policy-denied, data-unavailable, temporarily-unavailable, not-evaluated}.
9. EvidenceCompleteness={complete, partial, missing, not-required}.
10. EvidenceIntegrity={verified, unverified, corrupt, conflicting}.
11. PromotionEffect={eligible, restricted, quarantined, demoted, no-change, ineligible} with affected claim/capability set.

Numerical convergence, conservation/error bounds, physical validation, oracle comparison, deterministic equality, security, accessibility, and visualization/timeline parity are named evidence subverdicts feeding—never replacing—the product. Human labels are typed projections: theorem+established+proof-grade renders Proven; a validation claim with admitted validated evidence renders ValidatedWithinDomain; unresolved renders Unknown; not-claimed renders NoClaim. Unsupported derives from applicability/support.

'Partial' is not an adjudication. If evidence supports a weaker or restricted result, mint a separate ClaimRecord with exact implication/refinement edges and adjudicate it independently. EvidenceCompleteness=partial blocks promotion of the original claim. Complete-but-corrupt, partial-but-verified, and complete-but-conflicting states remain representable.

Composition is monotone and order-independent where declared, fail-closed on missing/conflicting evidence, and scoped so unrelated failures restrict only their proven surface. Process code is a versioned projection of the current OperationReceipt only; embedded Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts remain unchanged.

Consume the canonical schemas from frankensim-ext-vv-artifact-schemas-x68z: ContextOfUse, CalibrationSplit, SolutionVerificationReceipt, PredictionAssessment, and the uncertainty waterfall. Every evidence edge is typed as code verification, solution verification, calibration, model validation, prediction assessment, exploratory discovery, or confirmation. None implies another. Exploratory or adaptively selected results may create bold new ClaimRecords and theorem conjectures, but empirical promotion requires independent confirmatory lineage: preregistered/held-out evidence or anytime-valid optional-stopping control, multiplicity/selective-reporting accounting, and an exact ContextOfUse. Formal theorem promotion remains governed by its proof/checker receipts, never empirical fit.

## Success Criteria
Every receipt explains inputs, subverdicts, scope, product fields, policy and projection versions, process code, and promotion effect. Reordered composition is invariant where promised. Missing evidence fails closed. Status, cancel, verify, run, attempt, job, and campaign outcomes cannot overwrite one another. A completed refutation is representable without being mistaken for a harness failure, and a restricted theorem is exact rather than 'partial'.

## Test Plan
Exhaustive finite valid-state tables plus invalid-combination rejection; property tests for associativity/commutativity/monotonicity where claimed; contradictory evidence; missing oracle; converged wrong answer; nondeterministic but valid envelope; failed visualization after valid solve; complete-but-corrupt and partial-but-authentic closure; refuted adjudicate-versus-prove; status-on-refuted-job; cancel-accepted-before-drain; timeout/budget distinction; outside-domain versus missing capability/license/data; restricted-claim implication graph; unrelated-surface isolation; favorable default/projection mutation; and loss-reporting old-receipt migration.

Mutate discovery into confirmation, reuse calibration data as validation or prediction holdout, hide model/parameter selection, optional stopping, multiple looks, forked hypotheses, multiplicity, or uncertainty components, and substitute solution verification for model validation or prediction assessment. Require fail-closed relation edges, independent holdout/preregistration or anytime-valid receipts, and retained rejected discoveries; stronger discoveries remain visible without laundering.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Retain every scoped receipt, subverdict, exact ClaimRecord graph, evidence method/grade, applicability/support, completeness, integrity, requested predicate, composition/projection policy version, comparison arithmetic, conflict resolution, affected claim set, process code, artifacts, minimized witness, and replay. Human and JSON renderings are semantic projections of the same typed object.

Retain ContextOfUseId, CalibrationSplitId, SolutionVerificationReceiptId, PredictionAssessmentId, uncertainty-waterfall components, evidence-stage and dataset-role lineage, preregistration/holdout commitment, adaptive looks/stopping rule, multiplicity family and adjustment/e-process, model/parameter selection history, and independent confirmation relation. Promotion records the exact stage-qualified evidence and never collapses the waterfall or stage distinctions.

## Considerations
The product preserves useful evidence and radical theorem ratcheting without laundering unfinished work. Extensible enums require versioned semantics and conservative migration; a new stronger theorem is a new exact claim node, not a favorable reinterpretation of an old state.

title: V.4.5 Independently adjudicate the CORE production-path E2E runner receipt
description:
## Background
Initiative Core gates need an E2E substrate independently adjudicated from maximal flagships and theorem work. The receipt must prove both production integration and honest scoped outcomes without confusing operation success with job science.

## Technical Approach
Run representative Core-stratum journeys under explicit smoke and standard profiles from clean fixtures through product discovery, typed request construction, immutable submission, admission/rejection, planning, durable execution, observation/reconnect, control, scientific inspection, evidence retention, report/share/offline verification, and replay. Independently audit selector expansion, cost estimate, idempotency, lifecycle, scoped verdict composition, artifact closure, and human/agent parity. Publish a CoreE2eRunnerReceipt as a CampaignReceipt containing immutable Operation/Attempt/Job receipts.

Reconstruct ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect. Project the process code only from the current OperationReceipt.

## Success Criteria
Core journeys are stable, detached/reconnectable, diagnosable, and independently replayable. Every selected phase, identity edge, receipt, and artifact reconciles. Injected failures reach the correct scoped state. A successful status/cancel/verify operation cannot hide a failed or refuted JobReceipt. Replay reproduces the semantic receipt or an exact environment mismatch.

## Test Plan
Focused unit/property tests cover receipt scoping, operation projection, identity cardinality, selection, and closure. No-mock E2E covers happy, malformed, rejected admission, duplicate admitted/rejected submission, missing capability, outside-domain request, injected scientific defect, crash, cancel-before-drain, timeout, budget exhaustion, tamper, corrupt/partial/conflicting evidence, checkpoint/pause/migrate/resume/fork, status-on-refuted-job, offline verification, clean-store replay, and no-mock bypass mutation.

## Exact execution contract
Manifest: `tests/leapfrog/manifests/core-e2e-independent-adjudication.toml`. No-mock independent driver: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/core-e2e-independent-adjudication.sh`. Separately retained canonical execution is `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite core-e2e-independent-adjudication --stratum core --profile standard`. The independent verifier uses public artifacts and surfaces only; no test-only path or hidden state is permitted. A missing path, divergent selection, bypass, or incomplete receipt is non-green.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Use schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable DsrRun/CampaignRun/Shard/Journey/Case/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation/scope/tile identities; manifest, source-snapshot, code, contract, and schema hashes; Five Explicits; capabilities and feature flags; deterministic mode and machine fingerprint; oracle/checker identity and TCB overlap; tolerance arithmetic; progress, budgets, lifecycle/control/fault schedules; every scoped outcome field; diagnostics; artifact/FailureBundle pointers; minimized witness; and exact reconnect/replay commands. Pretty output is only a rendering. Logs are bounded, redacted, and backpressure-safe; critical evidence is lossless or closure becomes incomplete.

## Considerations
This receipt deliberately does not wait on maximal flagships. Honest Core capability remains available without turning unsupported, unsettled, or restricted research into a stronger claim.

title: V.4.6 Adapt HELM, vertical-slice, flagship, and tier-promotion suites into the canonical runner
description:
## Background
Existing high-value E2E suites should become first-class journeys without being rewritten or allowed to preserve divergent selection, logging, lifecycle, tier, or verdict semantics.

## Technical Approach
Adapt HELM study-scale, vertical-slice, flagship golden, tier-promotion, and new-domain suites into the canonical runner while preserving domain fixtures and independent oracles. Translate every legacy case to explicit Claim/Case/Journey identity, Core/Max stratum, campaign profile set, durable lifecycle, fs-obs events, scoped outcome product, artifact closure, and replay.

Treat SMOKE/MID/FULL only as versioned legacy inputs. An adapter may propose mappings such as legacy Smoke to Core+Smoke, Mid to Core+Standard, and Full to Max+Standard or Release, but must first emit a semantic diff of selected cases, claim set, budgets, capabilities, acceptance bands, artifacts, negative cases, and promotion effect. Ambiguous or lossy mappings refuse with ranked migration; no silent alias or default is allowed.

## Success Criteria
Existing suites run through one command and emit canonical receipts; adapter/native results agree; no case, acceptance band, fault, artifact, or claim boundary is lost; legacy artifacts replay with exact mapping provenance; changing an adapter mapping invalidates the old receipt.

## Test Plan
Adapter parity goldens; missing/stale fields; old receipt migration; partial suite availability; cancel/checkpoint/resume; deliberate semantic drift; every proposed legacy mapping; swapped Core/Max; dropped negative case; changed acceptance band; alias/deprecation behavior; deterministic mapping; and refusal of ambiguous input.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Retain legacy suite/version/tier and native manifest IDs, complete semantic diff, mapping rule/version, explicit stratum/profiles, selected cases, budgets/capabilities, oracle/TCB, acceptance and artifact crosswalk, scoped outcome product, discrepancies, deprecation/migration diagnostic, and replay. Logs use canonical bounded/redacted fs-obs.

## Considerations
Open flagships are integration consumers, not blockers for adapter infrastructure. Compatibility preserves semantics, not historical ambiguity.

title: V.4.7 Run tamper, crash, cancellation, resume, duplicate, idempotency, and fault drills
description:
## Background
Real journeys fail across process, worker, storage, network, solver, and user-control boundaries; recovery semantics are part of correctness.

## Technical Approach
Inject faults at each phase and scope boundary: corrupt input/artifact/event/checkpoint, process panic/kill, worker loss, delayed/duplicate delivery, disk/memory budget, cancellation race, stale version, lost capability, and partial exporter failure. Verify request-drain-finalize, idempotency, checkpoint compatibility, compensation, FailureBundle minimization, and retained partial evidence.

## Success Criteria
No task or artifact leak; no duplicate mutation; no corrupt resume; scoped lifecycle and receipt dispositions match the failure layer; all losing branches drain; minimized bundles replay; safety and integrity failures dominate favorable scientific results.

## Test Plan
Systematic phase-by-phase fault matrix, randomized legal schedules, cancellation storms, restart loops, stale checkpoint, duplicate key, corrupted ledger, slow log sink, unavailable hardware, bounded-resource fuzz.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Use schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable run/shard/journey/case/op identities; manifest, code, contract, and schema hashes; Five Explicits; capabilities and feature flags; deterministic mode and machine fingerprint; oracle/checker identity and TCB overlap; tolerance arithmetic; progress, budgets, cancellation/fault schedule, scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, diagnostics, artifact pointers, and minimized witness. Pretty output is only a rendering of these events. Logs are bounded, redacted, and backpressure-safe.

## Considerations
Fault injection itself is deterministic and ledgered in deterministic mode; destructive external operations are never part of tests.

title: V.4.8 Independently adjudicate the MAX E2E runner, legacy adapters, and failure semantics
description:
## Background
Maximal initiative and theorem receipts need full suites, legacy integration, and hostile failure qualification.

## Technical Approach

Publish MaxE2eRunnerReceipt with unsupported environments and retained counterexamples.

## Success Criteria
Max runner semantics survive adversarial replay; adapters cannot weaken claims; all failures are attributable and reproducible; no unnamed skip, hidden mock, or unbounded log remains.

## Test Plan
Clean-store full replay, adapter mutation, worker loss, corrupt bundle, unavailable licensed/hardware case, cross-mode comparison, cancellation during minimization, false-green exit mutation.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. ## Exact execution contract
Manifest: `tests/leapfrog/manifests/max-e2e-independent-adjudication.toml`. No-mock independent driver: `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/max-e2e-independent-adjudication.sh`. Separately retained canonical executions are `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite max-e2e-independent-adjudication --stratum max --profile release` and `scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite max-e2e-independent-adjudication --stratum max --profile adversarial`. Release and adversarial CampaignRuns retain distinct selections, attacks, scoped receipts, and replay closure. A missing path, divergent selection, bypass, or incomplete receipt is non-green.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Use schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable run/shard/journey/case/op identities; manifest, code, contract, and schema hashes; Five Explicits; capabilities and feature flags; deterministic mode and machine fingerprint; oracle/checker identity and TCB overlap; tolerance arithmetic; progress, budgets, cancellation/fault schedule, scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, diagnostics, artifact pointers, and minimized witness. Pretty output is only a rendering of these events. Logs are bounded, redacted, and backpressure-safe.

## Considerations
This proves runner readiness, not the truth of every frontier or theorem claim it will execute.

title: V.4.9 Implement durable Submission/Admission/Job/Attempt lifecycle, reconnectable control, recovery search, and artifact verification
description:
## Background
Realistic simulations can run for hours or days. Users and agents must submit intent, survive rejection or admission, disconnect, recover lost identifiers, observe and control durable work safely, recover after worker/service failure, and verify/share results without equating one shell process with the scientific Job.

## Technical Approach
Implement the sole production lifecycle behind the typed V.4.2 command layer across HELM/session and supported adapters. A Submission is immutable pre-admission intent plus idempotency envelope and survives rejection. Transactional admission revalidates and pins exact capability, dataset/version, license/expiry, quota, device, policy, schema, and host facts; doctor output is advisory and never admission authority. Admission yields either a Rejection/AdmissionReceipt with no JobId or an accepted AdmissionReceipt creating one durable JobId.

Expose submit and synchronous wait; authorized jobs list/search/show and recovery by SubmissionId/idempotency key; status; watch/attach from EventCursor; attempt history; checkpoint/pause/migrate/cancel/resume/fork; artifact fetch; report; redact/share; offline verify; replay; explain/diff. Deterministic pagination and capability-scoped visibility prevent enumeration. A lost client acknowledgement reconciles through idempotency and recovery search.

Use explicit SubmissionCreated, AdmissionEvaluating, Rejected or Admitted, Queued, Running, Checkpointing, Pausing, Suspended, Migrating, Draining, Finalizing, and Terminal lifecycle states. Each worker retry/resume/migration creates an Attempt; a semantic/budget/claim change or fork creates a new Job. First SIGINT requests drained cancellation and prints durable recovery identity when possible; disconnect never cancels. Emergency abort records evidence/integrity consequences.

Each command has an OperationReceipt. Attempts have AttemptReceipts; the durable Job has a JobReceipt; aggregate runs have CampaignReceipts. Operation success never overwrites embedded Job science. Status may exit zero while reporting a refuted/failed Job. Cancel acceptance may exit zero before later drained cancellation. SIGKILL or host loss may produce no OperationReceipt; reconnect/status is authoritative.

Control leases use authoritative monotonic fencing. Read-only observers and controllers are distinct. Dataset/license/policy/device/quota revocation after admission is a typed support/lifecycle event with declared continue/drain/quarantine policy, never a silent mutation. Report/share preserves provenance, redaction, and license policy. Offline verify checks identity, schema, signatures/capabilities, closure, evidence integrity, and declared claim links without manufacturing truth.

Bind every discovery, search, status, watch, control, checkpoint, artifact, report, share, and offline-verify operation to a typed AuthorizationContext: pseudonymous actor, tenant/project, resource, action, issuer, audience, capability provenance, delegation chain, expiry, revocation epoch, and anti-replay nonce. Observer, controller, exporter, verifier, and delegator rights are distinct least-privilege capabilities; authorization is rechecked on reconnect and immediately before every side effect. Opaque Job/Artifact/Checkpoint IDs aid confidentiality but never replace authorization. Search, pagination, cache, timing, denial, and recovery behavior must not reveal cross-project resource existence.

## Success Criteria
A human or agent can preflight, submit any admitted Core/Max journey under explicit profiles, retain a rejection, leave, recover a lost JobId, reconnect from another supported client, inspect full attempt history, control only with valid authority, obtain a finalized scoped receipt, inspect/verify artifacts, share a policy-compliant package, and replay. Duplicate intent cannot duplicate mutation; conflicting idempotency cannot mutate; failure cannot erase history or turn unknown into success.

## Test Plan
Unit/state-machine/property/model tests cover every legal and illegal transition, immutable intent, admission snapshots, duplicate identical/conflicting keys, accepted/rejected reconciliation, lease/cursor/search/pagination semantics, scoped receipts, checkpoint compatibility, revocation, report/share/verify, and deterministic human/JSON projection.

No-mock E2E owns 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/durable-lifecycle.toml' and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/durable-lifecycle.sh'. Its separately retained concrete executions are 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster durable-lifecycle --stratum core --profile standard', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster durable-lifecycle --stratum core --profile chaos', and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --cluster durable-lifecycle --stratum core --profile security'. Cover doctor-green followed by license expiry, quota race, device removal, dataset/policy change before/during admission; submit wait/detached; kill before submit acknowledgement and after admission before acknowledgement; lost JobId recovery; duplicate rejected request; cross-user enumeration resistance; large/stale pagination; simultaneous observers/controllers; stale lease; SIGINT/disconnect/SIGKILL; process/service/worker restart; delayed/duplicate events; retry/resume/migrate/fork; repeated pause; every pause/cancel/complete/finalize race; checkpoint/target incompatibility; timeout/budget exhaustion; missing/corrupt/partial artifacts; redaction/license refusal; offline verification; accessibility/non-TTY; and clean-store replay.

Add no-mock two-actor/two-project authorization E2E: guessed and harvested Job/Artifact/Checkpoint IDs; cross-project list/search/status/watch/control; observer-to-controller escalation; over-broad delegation; confused-deputy audience/issuer mix-up; expired, revoked, replayed, duplicated, or wrong-resource capabilities; revocation during watch/checkpoint/cancel/finalize; cache and timing side channels; unauthorized report/share/redact/offline-bundle access; and recovery after client, issuer, service, or worker restart. Denial must be fail-closed, non-enumerating, idempotent where applicable, and leave no unauthorized side effect.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit command Operation, Submission, Admission/Rejection, Job/Attempt, queue, lease, attach/reconnect, cursor, search/pagination, progress/ETA uncertainty, checkpoint/control, revocation, artifact/report/share/verify, scoped product receipt, and terminal events. Retain actor/capability, idempotency and redacted digests, admission snapshot, every transition, cursor/pagination state, predictions/consumption, fault/cancel/drain/finalize schedule, snapshot/event reconciliation, attempt and claim lineage, verification arithmetic, exact recovery commands, bounded stdout/stderr, minimized race witnesses, and replay.

Retain lossless AuthorizationDecision events keyed to OperationId and causal resource identities, with pseudonymous actor/project, policy and revocation versions, capability/delegation-chain hash, issuer/audience/action/resource class, decision/reason, recheck point, and side-effect disposition. Never log bearer material, raw tokens, secrets, or a denial detail that becomes an enumeration oracle.

## Considerations
This task exposes existing execution/session/ledger substrate coherently; it does not invent a second scheduler. Doctor and estimate are point-in-time observations. Force-abort is not successful cancellation. Offline verification validates declared evidence and integrity, not scientific truth.

title: V.5 USER & AGENT WORKBENCH — discoverability, teaching diagnostics, progressive disclosure, and accessibility
description:
## Background
World-class solvers remain unusable if people cannot discover valid workflows, preflight their environment, inspect assumptions, understand cost, repair invalid models, control long work, interpret scientific visualizations and timelines honestly, or consume results accessibly. Scripted UX tests are necessary but cannot alone establish that representative users comprehend claim boundaries and make safe decisions.

## Technical Approach
Define persona and journey grammar for first-time learners, educators, engineers, researchers, validation/safety/compliance leads, manufacturing/test operators, site/release operators, independent auditors, compute/data owners, theorem researchers, assistive-technology users, and agents. Generate discovery, examples, help, and completions from typed catalogs; provide a side-effect-free point-in-time doctor and redacted support bundle; expose inspectable defaults and ranked repairs; enforce human/agent parity, accessibility, non-TTY behavior, and truthful static/temporal scientific visualization with image/data/timeline/report parity.

Maintain two non-substitutable evidence lanes:
1. deterministic no-mock unit/E2E/accessibility/mutation tests prove interface contracts, semantic parity, recovery, and replay;
2. preregistered, consented, independently facilitated user studies measure task completion, severe-error rate, time/assistance, comprehension of units/assumptions/claim/evidence state, safe-decision accuracy, recovery/handoff, and accessibility with representative participants.

Human preference or completion never upgrades scientific ClaimAdjudication. Study data is minimized, consented, redacted, retention-bounded, and not collected as telemetry by default. Build executable Core and post-adjudication MAX tutorial branches for all twenty families.

## Success Criteria
Users reach first valid result and actionable diagnostic within preregistered p50/p95/p99 SLOs, monitor fresh progress, receive cancel acknowledgement, recover lost jobs, repair seeded failures, inspect consequential defaults/transforms, distinguish operation success from job/claim evidence, and reproduce/share safely. Experts retain full controls. Assistive and agent surfaces preserve load-bearing meaning. Representative-user evidence meets preregistered safety/comprehension thresholds or creates an explicit UX restriction.

## Test Plan
Persona no-mock journeys cover first use, expert research, operations, audit, offline/missing capability, invalid input/repair, cost surprise, durable recovery, accessibility/non-TTY/locale/path/focus/zoom/reduced motion, static and temporal visualization truth, exact restricted claims versus incomplete evidence, protected sharing, Core/MAX tutorials, replay, and mutations of defaults, diagnostics, help, transforms, SLO accounting, and human/agent parity.

Run separately preregistered studies with novice, domain-expert, validation/safety, auditor, and assistive-tech cohorts using blinded counterbalanced tasks where appropriate. Record completion, error severity, unsafe decisions, assistance, comprehension, recovery, and handoff; report failures/censoring and uncertainty, not averages alone.

## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. Its aggregate receipt content-addresses and reconciles the exact child receipt set, dependency-graph version, frozen manifest/source/code/contract/schema/policy hashes, selection and profile expansion, stable ClaimRevision/Case/Journey/DSR/Campaign/Shard/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, typed causal edges, artifact roots, and verifier identities. It preserves each child's separate ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reports missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting, corrupt, or outside-scope children explicitly; and never averages disagreement or upgrades a claim. Aggregate progress, cost, timing, memory, diagnostics, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, accessibility state, and exact replay pointers are schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe, and semantically equivalent for human and stable JSONL consumers. Promotion-critical child evidence is referenced losslessly.

## Considerations
Progressive disclosure organizes the full system; it never removes functionality or weakens claims. Doctor readiness is not admission or scientific validity. Visualization and tutorial success are not proof. Human-study participation is voluntary and privacy-preserving.

title: V.5.1 Define personas, journey grammar, progressive disclosure, inspectable defaults, and UX-study protocol
description:
## Background
A single expert-only interface excludes new users, while simplification that hides physics assumptions is dangerous. Synthetic persona walkthroughs also need representative-user validation for comprehension and safe decision-making.

## Technical Approach
Define first-time learner/educator, engineer, researcher, validation/safety/compliance lead, manufacturing partner, test operator, site/release operator, independent auditor, compute/data owner, theorem researcher, assistive-technology user, and agent personas. Specify authority, privacy/license responsibility, handoff, and discovery→intent→doctor→estimate→author/import→repair→submit→observe/control→inspect/verify→share/replay grammar.

Basic, advanced, and expert views are projections of one typed state. Every inferred material, regime, solver, tolerance, unit, frame, clock, temporal transform, budget, capability, ClaimRevision, evidence method/grade, applicability/support, and no-claim default is inspectable and ledgered with source, rationale, domain, and override route.

Define a preregistered independent UX-study protocol: recruitment strata, inclusion/accessibility needs, tasks and seeded hazards, counterbalancing/blinding where appropriate, facilitator script, allowable assistance, severe-error taxonomy, completion and safe-decision measures, comprehension questions, stopping rules, analysis, uncertainty, censoring/failure accounting, privacy/consent, data minimization, retention, deletion, and redaction. No telemetry-by-default or coercive product instrumentation. Human evidence uses canonical EvidenceMethodSet values validated-empirical or empirical-only plus a versioned UX domain/submethod tag; it cannot establish physics or theorems.

## Success Criteria
Every persona has complete happy, failure, recovery, and handoff paths. Disclosure changes no hidden semantics. Preregistered p50/p95/p99 first-result, diagnostic, progress, cancel, reconnect, repair, and share SLOs have explicit host/cohort scope. Human studies can be independently reproduced or audited without exposing participant identity.

## Test Plan
Deterministic persona walkthroughs; hidden-default and disclosure-level semantic mutations; incomplete input; cost escalation; unresolved claim/outside-domain/missing support; cancel/reconnect; agent/human parity; accessibility. Study-protocol tests cover missing consent, unbalanced tasks, facilitator drift, privacy leak, selective exclusion, unreported assistance/failure, unsafe-decision scoring, small-sample uncertainty, retention expiry, and synthetic dry runs before participants.

## Detailed logging and evidence
For automated journeys emit scoped identities/outcomes, defaults, disclosure state, diagnostics, lifecycle, accessibility, artifacts, and replay. For studies emit pseudonymous Study/Protocol/Cohort/Task IDs, preregistration hash, consent/version, accessibility accommodation, task timing/assistance/error/comprehension/safe-decision measures, censoring, analysis version, aggregate uncertainty, privacy/redaction/retention receipts, and audit artifact—never unnecessary raw identity or passive telemetry.

## Considerations
Progressive disclosure reduces cognitive load, never epistemic honesty. UX evidence and scientific evidence remain different methods in the outcome algebra.

title: V.5.10 Enforce truthful spatial and temporal scientific visualization, uncertainty, accessibility, and data parity
description:
## Background
A beautiful image or smooth animation can be semantically false: hidden clipping, bad colormap, missing units, unmarked transforms, omitted NaNs, wrong vector frame, temporal aliasing, interpolation across an impact/reset/topology change, phase-wrap error, or a dropped event frame can change a user's conclusion. Geneva drives, Wankel-like contact, commutation, impacts, and multiphysics clocks make temporal truth load-bearing.

## Technical Approach
Define one ScientificVisualizationSpec/Receipt for interactive views, animations, static images, timelines, reports, and agent data exports. Type quantity, unit/kind, spatial frame/orientation/chart, component/basis, fidelity/regime, support, aggregation, spatial reconstruction, uncertainty/evidence, missing/invalid/out-of-domain semantics, range/normalization/clipping, transform, colormap/glyph/tensor conventions, topology/occlusion, camera/projection/selection, accessibility, and source lineage.

Add a TemporalPresentationSpec:
- distinguish solver step/time, modeled physical time, experiment/DAQ clock, controller clock, wall time, and presentation/playback time;
- retain exact sample/event timestamps, time basis/units, adaptive-step history, synchronization transform and uncertainty;
- declare resampling/filter/anti-alias/interpolation method and validity domain;
- forbid interpolation across reset, impact, contact-mode, discontinuity, topology, commutation, or branch events unless an explicit physically justified operator and receipt exists;
- type periodic phase, unwrap/wrap convention, cycle identity, and Floquet/orbit alignment;
- align asynchronous multi-rate streams with explicit clock uncertainty/gaps;
- record playback speed, cadence, frame IDs, source sample ranges, dropped/duplicated/coalesced frames, event markers, temporal uncertainty, and data/timeline parity.

Rendering may drop presentation frames for responsiveness only if Gap events and counters remain visible and the underlying timeline/data artifact is complete. It may never drop the only representation of a scientific event or smooth across it silently.

Require distinct encodings and data equivalents for uncertainty, bounds, discretization error, invalid cells, NaN/Inf, masks, unsampled/extrapolated regions, topology changes, mixed-fidelity seams, and temporal gaps. Use perceptually appropriate colorblind-safe defaults, redundant cues, keyboard/focus/zoom/reflow, reduced-motion/no-flash, meaningful summaries, and downloadable tables/slices/timelines. Deterministic mode fixes view/sample/tie/label decisions.

Exact suite: 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/scientific-visualization.toml', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/scientific-visualization.sh', and separate concrete runs 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite scientific-visualization --stratum core --profile standard' and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite scientific-visualization --stratum max --profile release'.

## Success Criteria
A reviewer reconstructs every pixel/glyph/curve/frame and its source time/data; audits units/frames/clocks/transforms/ranges/evidence/gaps; obtains data- and timeline-equivalent representations; and reproduces the view. No default hides invalid, uncertain, clipped, temporally aliased, or dropped-event data. Human, agent, image, animation, timeline, and report semantics agree. Latency/artifact SLOs never remove load-bearing annotations.

## Test Plan
Unit/property/conformance tests cover unit/frame/time transforms, ranges/clipping, log domain, NaN/mask propagation, uncertainty, basis changes, camera hashes, time monotonicity, adaptive resampling, multi-rate alignment, clock uncertainty, phase wrapping, interpolation validity, event barriers, frame accounting, accessibility, and semantic/data/image/timeline parity.

No-mock E2E covers scalar/vector/tensor/complex/topological and mixed-fidelity fields; outliers; changed units/moving frames; impacts/resets/contact/topology/commutation; periodic phase; incomplete/ensemble data; narrow/non-TTY/screen reader/reduced motion; report/share/redaction; deterministic rerender. Mutations change cadence, drop/duplicate the only event frame, smooth across discontinuity, alias high-frequency motion, swap clocks, change phase wrap, present same image with different timeline, create smooth animation that hides an event, and alter data without image; all must fail truth parity. Independently compare engineering decisions from raw data and views.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit Visualization/TemporalPresentation specs, source field/artifact hashes, units/frames/clocks, sample/event times, synchronization/interpolation/filter provenance, uncertainty, range/clipping/mask/NaN counts, phase/cycle, frame-source mapping, dropped/duplicated/gap counters, camera/selection, image/data/timeline/spec hashes, accessibility audit, timings/memory, scoped outcomes, diagnostics, and replay. Numeric, semantic, temporal, and image goldens are retained together; critical events are lossless.

## Considerations
Visualization is an epistemic interface, not proof. Semantic and temporal truth take precedence over drama, while expert rendering controls remain fully available through explicit specs.

title: V.5.11 Build executable MAX expert/research tutorial branches and theorem outcome field guide
description:
## Background

title: V.5.4 Enforce non-TTY, color-independent, screen-reader, width, Unicode, locale, and stable-JSON accessibility

## Background

Add visible and programmatic focus, logical focus restoration after updates, keyboard reachability, 200-percent-plus zoom/reflow without information loss, reduced-motion mode, no seizure-risk flash, pause/stop for nonessential animation, stable live-region update policy, and data-equivalent interaction for hover/brush/selection. description:
