title: V.5.8 Build executable twenty-family CORE tutorials and a diagnostic failure cookbook
description:
## Background
Examples become dangerous when decorative, stale, failure-free, or assumption-hiding. The twenty Core journeys need an executable first-success and recovery curriculum; MAX expert/research branches remain separate and post-adjudication.

## Technical Approach
Create one progressive Core tutorial and failure-cookbook branch for each fifteen initiative and five theorem family from the frozen manifest and exact J1 receipt. Each begins with intent; runs doctor/capability preflight; declares Five Explicits, Core stratum, and concrete smoke/standard profile; shows estimate and defaults; submits through production lifecycle; watches/reconnects and recovers identity; explains Operation versus Job/Campaign receipt and exact ClaimRecord/adjudication/evidence/support; injects one realistic mistake and ranked repair; demonstrates cancel/checkpoint/pause/resume and replay; inspects/verifies/shares artifacts; and links to the separate MAX branch.

Sources live under 'examples/leapfrog/<family>/'. The generated aggregate manifest is 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/tutorials-core.toml' and no-mock driver is 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/tutorials-core.sh'. Concrete aggregate executions are 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite tutorials-core --stratum core --profile smoke' and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite tutorials-core --stratum core --profile standard'. Each generated branch substitutes its concrete tutorial ID into either 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --tutorial <id> --stratum core --profile smoke' or 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --tutorial <id> --stratum core --profile standard'. Generate human Markdown/HTML and agent JSON/catalog views from one executable source.

Theorem tutorials visibly separate conjecture, exact claim revision, numerical evidence, proof object, checker/TCB, adjudication, counterexample, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and runtime implication. A weaker theorem is a distinct related ClaimRecord, never 'Partial'.

## Success Criteria
Exactly twenty Core tutorials plus the failure cookbook execute from clean artifacts. Every command, diagnostic, scoped outcome field, receipt, output assertion, accessibility alternative, and replay is checked. Catalog/tutorial versions cannot drift. Novice and expert projections preserve semantics. Protected data never enters output.

## Test Plan
Execute all branches under smoke and selected standard profiles; mutate command, selector, stratum/profile, source version, default, unit/frame/clock, expected Operation code versus embedded Job result, claim relation, evidence method/grade/completeness/integrity, diagnostic ID, artifact link, and accessibility alternative. Test doctor failure, offline/missing support, disconnect/lost JobId/reconnect, cancellation/pause/resume, stale checkpoint, corrupt evidence, redaction, agent-only parse, non-TTY, deterministic replay, and decorative/unexecuted code detection.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit TutorialFamily/CoreBranch, source/generated-output and aggregate-manifest hashes, exact J1 receipt, operations/selectors/stratum/profiles, all scoped identities/outcomes, diagnostics/repairs, lifecycle, accessibility, artifacts/FailureBundles, minimized witness, and replay. Documentation adds no semantic path and critical teaching events are lossless.

## Considerations
Core tutorials organize the full capability without oversimplifying it. MAX tutorial ownership remains V.5.11 so unfinished moonshots never block honest first success.

title: V.5.9 Build first-run environment doctor, capability preflight, and generated CLI help
description:
## Background
First use needs an honest answer about whether this installation, host, data environment, license set, artifact store, and feature configuration appear ready. Trial-and-error admission wastes time. Handwritten help/completion/migration guidance also drifts from typed command and capability schemas.

## Technical Approach
Implement a read-only, side-effect-free first-run doctor and capability viewer across CLI and agent API. Generate help, examples, manpage/reference fragments, completions, deprecation notices, and migration hints from the V.4.2 typed grammar and capability/diagnostic catalog.

Inspect installed artifact and schema/contract versions; runtime versus developer/DSR prerequisites; ISA/topology, memory, disk, devices; deterministic envelope; artifact-store permissions/quota/integrity; material/standard/benchmark datasets and license/expiry; declared network needs; feature/moonshot gates; checkpoint/replay compatibility; locale/Unicode/path/CWD/non-TTY behavior; and requested selector/stratum/profile budgets/capabilities. Return stable diagnostics and ranked non-destructive repairs with cost, semantic, privacy, security, and claim impact. Never auto-install, mutate config, reveal secrets, probe unrelated resources, or imply readiness is validity.

Doctor findings are point-in-time advisory OperationReceipts bound to exact probe time and snapshots. They are never admission authority. V.4.9 transactionally revalidates/pins capabilities, quota, device, datasets, licenses, and policy at admission and reports later revocation distinctly. Support offline mode and a redacted shareable support bundle.

Exact no-mock ownership: 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/environment-doctor.toml', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/environment-doctor.sh', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh doctor', and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh capabilities'. A target-specific check uses the typed selector/stratum/profile grammar without executing science.

## Success Criteria
A first-time user, site operator, or agent can distinguish ready, outside-domain, unsupported, misconfigured, expired, and unknown findings before submission. Every finding names evidence, affected surfaces, safe verification/repair, scope, and expiry. Human/JSON help and completions derive from one grammar. No undeclared side effects, secret/license payload leakage, or favorable TOCTOU assumption. Freeze p50/p95/p99 diagnostic latency and support-bundle size SLOs.

## Test Plan
Unit tests cover every probe/capability/diagnostic/repair, output projection, generated help/completion, expiry, and migration. No-mock E2E covers healthy/minimal/offline/air-gapped installations; stale binary/schema/data/license; unsupported ISA/device; read-only/full/quota stores; corrupt cache; network/feature/determinism gaps; spaces/quotes/Unicode/arbitrary CWD/non-TTY/broken pipe/restricted environment; secret canaries; conflicting repairs; and agent parity. Race tests cover doctor-green then license expiry, quota consumption, device removal, dataset/policy change before/during submit and require V.4.9 revalidation. Mutations make a failed prerequisite appear green.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit DoctorRun/Probe/Capability/Diagnostic/Repair/GeneratedHelp/Redaction Operation events with grammar/catalog/source hashes, probe timestamp/authority/side-effect class, host and dependency snapshots/expiry, requested selector/stratum/profiles, duration, evidence hash, DomainApplicability/OperationalSupport, ranked repair consequences, redaction, support-bundle artifact, and exact rerun. Doctor does not emit a scientific Job ClaimAdjudication.

## Considerations
Runtime, developer, DSR-worker, and scientific readiness differ. V.4.9 owns lifecycle-native admission checks; this bead owns user-facing diagnosis/help/support. Both consume one typed model without duplicate probes or semantics.

title: V.6 DSR QUALIFICATION — deterministic sharding, flake honesty, scale, cross-ISA, and release evidence
description:
## Background
A comprehensive suite must run under the project's actual DSR verification and release model, not merely exist as local scripts. Operational evidence must cover clean packaged use, version transitions, scale, and supported architecture envelopes.

## Technical Approach
Define DSR selections using Core/Max claim stratum separately from smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-ISA, and release profiles. Own deterministic capability-aware sharding; flake classification with expiring quarantine and no green laundering; independent Core/MAX receipts; scale, cancellation, worker-loss, resource, retention, unsafe-boundary, and performance divergence campaigns; and clean-host packaged install/upgrade/downgrade/replay qualification.

DSR consumes the shared VerificationProtocol and emits scoped Campaign/Attempt/Job/Operation receipts, never a separate status dialect.

## Success Criteria
Each promotion names exact DSR lane, stratum/profiles, run/shard identities, artifact closure, and scoped receipt. Skipped, flaky, unsupported, killed, or uninstrumented paths cannot green. Supported Apple Silicon and many-core x86 evidence is comparable within declared determinism/performance classes. Release artifacts work without a source tree or dev toolchain and preserve historical receipts across allowed version transitions.

## Test Plan
Children cover positive, boundary, malformed, cancellation, replay, deterministic, accessibility, adversarial/security, model-checking, unsafe-boundary, scale, clean-host install, offline/arbitrary-CWD use, upgrade/downgrade/refusal, schema/checkpoint/ledger migration, tamper, and hostile failures. Promotion consumes retained structured receipts, not issue status.

## Detailed logging and evidence
This rollup emits no synthetic scientific result. Its aggregate receipt content-addresses and reconciles the exact child receipt set, dependency-graph version, frozen manifest/source/code/contract/schema/policy hashes, selection and profile expansion, stable ClaimRevision/Case/Journey/DSR/Campaign/Shard/Submission/Job/Attempt/Operation identities, typed causal edges, artifact roots, and verifier identities. It preserves each child's separate ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect; reports missing, stale, duplicate, conflicting, corrupt, or outside-scope children explicitly; and never averages disagreement or upgrades a claim. Aggregate progress, cost, timing, memory, diagnostics, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, accessibility state, and exact replay pointers are schema-versioned, bounded, policy-redacted, backpressure-safe, and semantically equivalent for human and stable JSONL consumers. Promotion-critical child evidence is referenced losslessly.

## Considerations
This rollup extends HELM, fs-obs, Gauntlet, DSR, ledger, and release packaging. It introduces neither test-only production behavior nor a second semantic API.

title: V.6.1 Specify DSR lane, named-skip, artifact, timeout, retry, and promotion contract
description:
## Background
DSR is the repository proof runner. Its selections must not confuse scientific Core/Max scope with campaign workload, nor rely on generic quality wording.

## Technical Approach
Specify DSR manifests with exactly one stratum from {core, max}. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. Cross-facet combinations are allowed only through a versioned manifest-defined composite ProfileId whose ordered inputs, precedence and conflict rules, budgets, capabilities, selection expansion, and semantic-diff hash are frozen before execution; repeated --profile flags or implicit string composition are invalid. Scale remains an orthogonal workload/budget dimension, not a profile ID. DSR suite expansion preserves one receipt per atomic profile and never silently alters stratum. Define capabilities, deterministic shards, budgets, retry/timeout/cancel/pause policy, artifacts/log retention, requested predicate, scoped receipt aggregation, and promotion consumers.

Missing workers/cases produce explicit DomainApplicability/OperationalSupport and EvidenceCompleteness fields. Retries create Attempts and never erase originals. Operation process codes project only finalized OperationReceipts. A DSR host/process death without a receipt remains an explicit gap; durable status/reconciliation is authoritative.

## Success Criteria
Every verification bead names an executable DSR selection with separate axes; dry-run shows cases, cost, support, and evidence. Skip, retry, flake, cancel, timeout, budget exhaustion, domain/support gap, infrastructure error, and evidence integrity remain distinct and gate-visible.

## Test Plan
Manifest lint; invalid profile composition; stratum drift; no worker; partial/duplicate shard; timeout versus budget; retry/flake; cancel/pause; killed runner without receipt; missing/corrupt artifact; fallback mutation; unnamed skip; aggregate false-green; profile omission; side-effect-free dry run; complete-but-corrupt and partial-but-verified closure.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit DsrRun/CampaignRun/Shard and Claim/Journey/Case/Attempt/Operation identities; stratum, atomic CampaignProfileId, and suite expansion; selection/cost; capabilities/machine; budgets; retry/flake/lifecycle/fault; complete scoped outcome algebra; artifacts; exact DSR command, run log, and replay closure.

Logging completeness floor: emit frozen source/manifest/code/contract/schema/policy and fixture hashes; ClaimId/ClaimRevisionId, CaseId, JourneyId, DsrRunId, CampaignRunId, ShardId, SubmissionId, JobId, AttemptId, OperationId, execution-scope, checkpoint, and artifact identities as applicable, with typed causal edges; selectors/profiles; units/frames/clocks; seeds/logical work; requested/consumed budgets; capabilities/flags; machine/ISA/thread/mode; oracle/checker/TCB overlap; tolerance/equivalence arithmetic; progress, residual, balance, uncertainty, and error summaries; lifecycle/control/fault/drain/finalize events; separate Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts with the complete outcome product; diagnostics/repairs; FailureBundles/minimized witnesses; artifact closure, process projection, and exact reconnect/replay pointers. Critical evidence is lossless; all output is schema-versioned, bounded, backpressure-safe, policy-redacted, content-addressed for large payloads, and semantically equivalent in human and stable JSONL forms.

## Considerations
GitHub Actions is not required proof. DSR follows AGENTS.md. Campaign intensity is not scientific truth, and retries never rewrite history.

title: V.6.2 Implement deterministic cost-aware sharding and capability routing
description:
## Background
Naive sharding causes long tails, nondeterministic case loss, and hardware-dependent blind spots.

## Technical Approach
Partition semantic case identities using calibrated cost distributions, capability constraints, data locality, anti-affinity for correlated failures, and deterministic tie rules. Record selected worker capability, expected/actual cost, rebalancing, and migration. Preserve shard union/disjointness and logical RNG identity.

## Success Criteria
All required cases execute exactly once logically despite retry; shard plans replay from manifest and capability snapshot; p95 tail and imbalance meet preregistered targets; missing capability fails explicitly.

## Test Plan
Permutation/thread/worker-count properties; cost misprediction; worker loss; capability churn; retry/duplicate; empty shard; large/small mix; deterministic plan replay.

Infrastructure completeness floor: add focused unit, boundary, invalid-state, serialization/version, deterministic-tie, cancellation, and error-propagation tests for every owned type and state transition; property/metamorphic/model tests for declared algebra and scheduling invariants; deterministic concurrency exploration where multiple actors or workers exist; mutation tests for every favorable default, skip, retry, projection, policy, and promotion edge; and bounded fuzzing with minimized replay for untrusted input. Run a no-mock E2E path through the canonical protocol/wrapper for positive, rejected, unsupported, cancelled, timed-out, budget-exhausted, infrastructure-failed, integrity-failed, tampered, restarted, and clean-store replay cases. Assert stable human/JSONL parity, exact scoped receipts, artifact closure, bounded detailed logs, secret/license safety, arbitrary-CWD/non-TTY behavior, accessibility where user-visible, and fail-closed behavior when any required evidence or identity is missing.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Use schema-versioned fs-obs JSONL with stable run/shard/journey/case/op identities; manifest, code, contract, and schema hashes; Five Explicits; capabilities and feature flags; deterministic mode and machine fingerprint; oracle/checker identity and TCB overlap; tolerance arithmetic; progress, budgets, cancellation/fault schedule, scoped Operation/Attempt/Job/Campaign receipts carrying ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, exact ClaimRecord/ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet/EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, separate EvidenceCompleteness and EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect, diagnostics, artifact pointers, and minimized witness. Pretty output is only a rendering of these events. Logs are bounded, redacted, and backpressure-safe.

## Considerations
Dynamic physical placement may change, but logical selection and evidence identity cannot.

title: V.6.3 Enforce flake classification, quarantine expiry, reproducibility, and no-green-laundering

title: V.6.7 Independently adjudicate MAX DSR, scale, cross-ISA, packaged release, and version-transition receipts
description:
## Background
Maximal promotion requires independent proof over runners, hostile failures, UX, scale, supported architecture matrices, and the artifact users actually install. A release handoff is not qualified until it works from a clean non-repository environment and preserves history across version transitions.

## Technical Approach
Independently reproduce the Max-stratum DSR standard/release selections plus required adversarial/soak/security/chaos/cross-ISA profiles. Audit selection, shards, retries/quarantine, unsafe-boundary evidence, scale/cancellation, worker loss, deterministic/performance envelopes, artifact closure, redaction, and support limits.

For every supported release target, verify checksum, signature/attestation, provenance, version, exact feature/capability inventory, schemas/contracts, generated help/completions, and artifact manifest before install. Install from the packaged artifact as a fresh nonprivileged user on a clean host/environment with no repository, source, Rust toolchain, or undeclared dev dependency. Exercise arbitrary CWD and offline operation where claimed.

Run doctor/capabilities, one representative Core tutorial and durable Job, detach/reconnect/recover, inspect/report/share/offline verify, and replay an immutable receipt. Qualify relocation and uninstall with declared config/data preservation. Upgrade N-1→N and migrate or compatibly read ledger, artifact, checkpoint, receipt, manifest, and schema data; verify old immutable receipts retain their original semantics. Test downgrade only where supported; otherwise require explicit preflight refusal with no data corruption or silent history rewrite. Publish MaxDsrReleaseReceipt with target and version-transition matrix.

Treat release trust as a lifecycle, not a one-time signature. Bind each artifact to a machine-readable SBOM, license/NOTICE closure, exact feature and unsafe-boundary inventory, vulnerability-advisory snapshot, source/compiler/linker/flags/dependency graph, binary-hardening inventory, and signed provenance. Require an independent clean builder to reproduce the artifact bitwise where promised or publish a byte-level nondeterminism map and semantic equivalence receipt. Specify trust roots, key scope, threshold policy, timestamp/freshness, rotation, compromise/revocation, transparency/equivocation detection, offline trust bundle, and cryptographic-algorithm migration.

Qualify every declared supported direct, chained, and skip-version upgrade path—not only N-1 to N—and each allowed rolling mixed-version client/service/worker combination. Define future-field and newer-schema refusal, backup/restore, preflight space checks, write fencing, idempotent journaled migration, power-loss/disk-full recovery, rollback boundaries, and immutable semantic comparison of old versus new receipts. Unsupported paths must refuse before mutation with a ranked safe route.

## Success Criteria
No unaccounted Max case, false-green retry, unsupported architecture/feature claim, stale baseline, missing artifact, hidden dev dependency, or retention hole remains. Packaged artifacts install and run from clean environments. Upgrade preserves/rejects data exactly as declared. Downgrade, relocation, uninstall, and replay cannot corrupt or reinterpret history. Exact support/fallback limits are published.

## Test Plan
Clean-store DSR rerun; no worker/worker loss; flaky mutant; scale cancellation; architecture/compiler/performance mismatch; corrupt evidence. Release E2E covers manifest/signature/checksum/provenance tamper; missing feature; clean-user install; arbitrary CWD; offline; no toolchain; path/locale/non-TTY; doctor and Core tutorial; detached Job reconnect/recovery; report/verify/replay; relocation/uninstall; N-1→N migration for each schema/checkpoint/ledger/artifact variant; interrupted migration and rollback recovery; supported downgrade or safe refusal; tampered old receipt; configuration/data preservation; and no-source/dev-dependency audit.

Add dependency substitution and SBOM/license/unsafe-inventory drift; second-builder mismatch; stale, expired, revoked, wrong-scope, rotated, split-view, rollback, freeze, and mix-and-match signatures or metadata; offline trust-bundle expiry; algorithm transition; and transparency-equivocation attacks. Exercise every supported direct/chained/skip migration and rolling mixed-version matrix, unknown future fields, disk-full/power-loss at each journal boundary, repeated retry, concurrent old/new writers, backup corruption and restore, rollback where admitted, and semantic replay of pre-upgrade immutable receipts.

## Exact execution contract
Manifest: 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/max-dsr-release-adjudication.toml'. No-mock driver: 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/max-dsr-release-adjudication.sh'. Separately retained canonical executions are 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite max-dsr-release-adjudication --stratum max --profile release', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite max-dsr-release-adjudication --stratum max --profile security', and 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run --suite max-dsr-release-adjudication --stratum max --profile cross-isa'. A missing clean-builder, trust-lifecycle, migration-path, install, or replay receipt is non-green.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit DSR and release Campaign identities, target/host/user fingerprint, artifact/checksum/signature/attestation/provenance/feature hashes, install/relocate/uninstall actions, doctor and durable lifecycle identities, version/source/target schema matrix, migration plan/steps/rollback, compatibility decisions, scoped outcomes, data-preservation hashes, artifacts, diagnostics, minimized witness, and old/new replay. Logs are bounded, redacted, and independently verifiable.

title: V.7 FIFTEEN INITIATIVE VERIFICATION JOURNEYS — pre-promotion batteries and post-promotion user proof
description:
## Background
The extension portfolio requires executable unit and end-to-end proof per scientific feature cluster. Shared infrastructure cannot by itself prove that each initiative selected the right laws, independent oracles, adversarial cases, capability boundaries, or user workflow. Conversely, a local scientific gate can be sound while the capability remains impossible for a human or agent to discover, estimate, operate, interrupt, interpret, repair, or replay.

This rollup preserves all fifteen initiatives separately. It adds a uniform proof-and-experience skeleton without flattening their domain-specific mathematics, maximal research branches, or no-claim boundaries.

## Technical Approach
Create one family rollup for I01, I02, I04, I08, I12, I15, I03, I07, I13, I14, I05, I06, I10, I11, and I09. Every family owns five independently closable receipts:

1. T1: Core-stratum unit, boundary, error-path, property, metamorphic, manufactured-solution, conformance, independent-oracle, and certifier-of-certifier coverage.
2. T2: Core-stratum production-path E2E under smoke and standard profiles, consumed directly by that initiative's G4/Core adjudication.
3. T3: Max-stratum unit plus production-path E2E under standard and release profiles, extended by admitted adversarial, soak, security, chaos, and cross-ISA campaigns, consumed directly by that initiative's G7/MAX adjudication.
4. J1: a post-Core human-and-agent journey using the Core stratum and an explicit campaign profile.
5. J2: a post-MAX expert/research journey using the Max stratum and explicit standard/release or stronger admitted profiles.

Scientific claim scope and campaign intensity are orthogonal. Every executable invocation selects one stratum from the enum {core, max}. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. Cross-facet combinations are allowed only through a versioned manifest-defined composite ProfileId whose ordered inputs, precedence and conflict rules, budgets, capabilities, selection expansion, and semantic-diff hash are frozen before execution; repeated --profile flags or implicit string composition are invalid. Scale remains an orthogonal workload/budget dimension, not a profile ID. Profiles may intensify workload, faults, platforms, and evidence obligations but may never silently change the ClaimRecord, its exact domain, or its quantifiers. Core and MAX gates depend on T2 and T3 respectively; user journeys consume the resulting adjudications and never circularly prove the underlying science. Each initiative root depends on its family rollup so closure includes operability and honest communication.

Every T2, T3, J1, and J2 leaf names its exact family manifest under 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/<family>.toml', its no-mock driver under 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/<family>.sh', and a concrete invocation through 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run'. T1 receipts name the same family artifacts where integration is required while retaining direct Rust test ownership. All surfaces compile to the same typed VerificationProtocol request and compare selection hashes, causal identities, events, artifacts, receipts, and process projections.

## Success Criteria
All fifteen families retain their distinct physical laws, theorem boundaries, material/interchange semantics, fixtures, oracles, mutations, and maximal branches. Each has exactly five receipts with deterministic selection, positive/boundary/invalid/adversarial cases, comprehensive unit and integration coverage, production-path E2E, accessibility and stable agent output, DSR qualification, bounded structured logs, immutable closure, exact replay, and independently adjudicated promotion dependencies.

No maximal research blocks an honestly useful Core capability. No Core result is presented as MAX. No unsupported hardware, license, material data, oracle, or topology silently passes. The scoped receipt product always distinguishes ExecutionDisposition; RequestedPredicateOutcome; ClaimAdjudication={established, refuted, unresolved, not-claimed}; EvidenceMethodSet and EpistemicGrade; DomainApplicability; OperationalSupport; EvidenceCompleteness; EvidenceIntegrity; and PromotionEffect. EvidenceCompleteness=partial is never a scientific truth value. Unsupported is rendered only from applicability/support fields. A weaker or restricted discovery is a separate exact ClaimRecord connected by independently checked implication, refinement, restriction, or counterexample relations.

## Test Plan
Mechanically verify all fifteen rollups have exactly five direct receipts and the intended parent-to-child dependency direction. Assert every T2 directly blocks its exact G4/Core gate, every T3 directly blocks its exact G7/MAX gate, J1 consumes Core evidence, J2 consumes MAX evidence, and no user journey creates a promotion cycle.

For every family, require focused Rust unit tests for happy, boundary, empty, maximal, invalid, dimensional, deterministic-tie, serialization, and error cases; doctests and executable examples; compile-fail/UI and type-invariant tests where misuse must be unrepresentable; property and metamorphic laws; manufactured solutions; independent analytic, exhaustive, high-precision, or alternate-formulation checks; mutation and certifier attacks; deterministic concurrency/model-checking where scheduling matters; and Miri, sanitizer, fuzz, or explicitly justified equivalent evidence for unsafe or hardware-sensitive boundaries.

Run no-mock production-path E2E scripts covering list/doctor, plan, estimate, submit, watch/reattach, checkpoint/pause/migrate where supported, cancel/drain/finalize, resume/fork, inspect, verify, report/share, corrupt/tamper, and clean-store replay. Exercise explicit stratum/profile products, arbitrary working directories, non-TTY and stable JSONL modes, concurrent clients, signal/process/worker/storage/network faults, and authorization/capability gaps. Delete or mutate a required graph edge, manifest field, script, scoped receipt field, claim relation, oracle identity, tolerance derivation, capability predicate, artifact, or replay pointer and require fail-closed adjudication.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Every receipt emits stable ClaimId and ClaimRevisionId, CaseId, JourneyId, DsrRunId, CampaignRunId, ShardId, SubmissionId, JobId, AttemptId, OperationId, ExecutionScopeId, TileId, CheckpointId, and ArtifactId as applicable, plus typed causal edges. Emit frozen manifest/code/contract/schema/fixture hashes; units, frames, clocks, seed, and logical work identity; requested and consumed budgets; capabilities and flags; machine/ISA/thread/mode fingerprint; oracle/checker and trusted-computing-base overlap; tolerance derivation and arithmetic; progress, residual, balance, conservation, uncertainty, and error summaries; lifecycle, fault, cancellation, drain, and finalize events.

Emit the full scoped outcome product: ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect. Retain ClaimRelationReceipts, diagnostics and ranked repairs, artifacts, FailureBundles, minimized witnesses, reports, and exact reconnect/replay pointers. OperationReceipt, AttemptReceipt, JobReceipt, and CampaignReceipt remain separately addressable; only the current OperationReceipt projects to the caller's process status.

Logs are schema-versioned, deterministic where claimed, bounded, redacted by declared policy, backpressure-safe, and available in semantically equivalent pretty and stable JSONL forms. Proof- and promotion-critical events are lossless and never sampled away. Large or sensitive payloads are committed content-addressed objects rather than dumped inline.

## Considerations
The post-gate journeys establish usability, recovery, interpretation, and claim honesty; they do not retroactively prove the science. Pre-promotion receipts are the evidence consumed by scientific gates. Stronger discoveries remain admissible through versioned ClaimRecords, independently certified relations, and independent checkers. Legacy suite names are accepted only through semantic-diff adapters and never redefine the two-axis contract.

title: V.8 FIVE THEOREM-RATCHET JOURNEYS — executable conjectures, checkers, counterexamples, and strongest-surviving theorems
description:
## Background
A theorem foundry is not user-ready merely because formal notes, symbolic derivations, or numerical experiments exist. Researchers must be able to state a precise quantified conjecture, inspect hypotheses and trusted-computing-base overlap, run formal, symbolic, exact-discrete, interval, numerical, and counterexample checkers, and receive an honest multidimensional adjudication. Operational success, incomplete evidence, unavailable hardware, and out-of-domain execution must never be mistaken for mathematical truth.

This rollup deliberately keeps theorem ambition maximal. Durable refutation, sharply mapped unresolved regions, restricted theorems, and stronger-than-planned theorems are mechanisms for attempting bolder results, not reasons to retreat to trivial claims.

## Technical Approach
Create one family rollup for RA differential-cohomology electromechanics, RB nonnormal and Krein spectra, RC Spin/Pin holonomy, RD stratified-derived machine geometry, and RE computer-assisted global dynamics. Each family owns four independently closable receipts:

1. T1: formal/unit/conformance, law/property/metamorphic, independent-checker, counterexample-generator, and certifier-of-certifier receipt.
2. T2: independent Max-stratum production-path E2E falsification, replay, proof-object integrity, and runtime-domain receipt consumed directly by the final theorem adjudication.
3. J1: a Core-stratum pre-final interaction journey that exposes ClaimAdjudication, evidence grade, applicability, support, completeness, and integrity without implying truth from successful execution.
4. J2: a Max-stratum post-final journey applying the strongest surviving theorem, sharp refutation, restricted result, or unresolved atlas to runtime routing only under an exact domain witness.

Every executable request selects one stratum from the enum {core, max}. Each CampaignRun selects exactly one atomic, manifest-resolved CampaignProfileId. The built-in profile IDs are {smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-isa, release}. A suite that requires several profiles expands them into separate CampaignRuns and separately retained receipts. Cross-facet combinations are allowed only through a versioned manifest-defined composite ProfileId whose ordered inputs, precedence and conflict rules, budgets, capabilities, selection expansion, and semantic-diff hash are frozen before execution; repeated --profile flags or implicit string composition are invalid. Scale remains an orthogonal workload/budget dimension, not a profile ID. Claim stratum controls the admitted mathematical/runtime surface; profiles control workload, attacks, duration, platforms, and evidence obligations. Each leaf names its exact 'tests/leapfrog/manifests/<family>.toml', 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/<family>.sh', and a concrete 'scripts/e2e/leapfrog/run.sh run' invocation.

Every theorem is an immutable ClaimRecord revision containing an exact statement, claim kind, quantifiers, hypotheses, conventions, units, domain, and runtime implications. A new stronger, weaker, local, restricted, or counterexample claim receives its own ClaimId/ClaimRevisionId. Typed implication, refinement, restriction, equivalence, incompatibility, and counterexample edges are evidence-bearing ClaimRelationReceipts with explicit direction, source/target domains and quantifiers, checker identity, proof artifact, and TCB overlap. Relation cycles fail closed except explicitly certified equivalence components; transitive use is permitted only through admitted relation composition.

## Success Criteria
All five ratchets are executable, independently falsifiable, and reproducible from a clean artifact store. No numerical evidence alone becomes a theorem; no failed conjecture, counterexample, checker disagreement, unresolved cell, restricted theorem, or stronger theorem disappears; no runtime activation escapes its exact theorem-domain witness. Formal and computational proof objects expose their trusted kernel and assumptions. Final theorem gates hard-depend on T2; J2 consumes the adjudicated result without cycles.

The canonical outcome product distinguishes ExecutionDisposition; RequestedPredicateOutcome; ClaimAdjudication={established, refuted, unresolved, not-claimed}; EvidenceMethodSet; EpistemicGrade; DomainApplicability; OperationalSupport; EvidenceCompleteness; EvidenceIntegrity; and PromotionEffect. EvidenceCompleteness=partial is never ClaimAdjudication. Human labels such as Proven, Unknown, NoClaim, and Unsupported are deterministic projections of the appropriate fields, not competing truth values. A theorem stronger than the plan can flow through without schema redesign or loss of its exact domain.

## Test Plan
Require focused unit tests for theorem syntax, claim kinds, quantifiers, hypotheses, conventions, orientation, units, domains, proof-object serialization, assumption discharge, checker rejection, runtime witness matching, every outcome field, invalid field combinations, and process projection. Add doctests and executable examples; compile-fail/UI/type-invariant tests for forbidden theorem/runtime combinations; property, metamorphic, and naturality tests; exhaustive-small and analytic fixtures; independent high-precision or alternate-formulation oracles; formal-kernel checks where available; deterministic concurrency/model-checking for distributed search; proof/checker mutation; same-bug TCB traps; fuzzing; and minimized counterexample replay.

Test ClaimRelationReceipt direction, domain restriction, quantifier variance, equivalence-component certification, cycle rejection, composition, incompatible claims, stronger-than-planned discoveries, and restricted theorems independently of the claim checker. Mutation must catch reversed implication, silently weakened hypotheses, widened domains, changed conventions, and common-mode checker faults.

No-mock E2E campaigns state, estimate, submit, monitor, reattach, checkpoint or pause where applicable, cancel/drain/finalize, resume/fork, inspect, falsify, adjudicate, verify, apply, report/share, tamper, and replay each ratchet. Mutate hypotheses, quantifiers, signs, orientation, topology, spectral structure, interval bounds, proof objects, checker code, oracle identity, runtime-domain witnesses, causal edges, and artifact closure. Exercise smoke, standard, adversarial, soak, security, chaos, cross-ISA, and release profiles as appropriate and require fail-closed admission. Kill clients and workers before and after receipt commitment, corrupt proof bundles, remove capabilities, and verify that operation status never rewrites JobReceipt or ClaimAdjudication.

## Detailed logging and evidence
Emit stable ClaimId and ClaimRevisionId, CaseId, JourneyId, DsrRunId, CampaignRunId, ShardId, SubmissionId, JobId, AttemptId, OperationId, ExecutionScopeId, TileId, CheckpointId, and ArtifactId as applicable, plus typed causal edges. Emit theorem statement, quantifier, hypothesis, convention, domain, relation, manifest, code, contract, schema, and fixture hashes; units, frames, clocks, seeds, logical work, budgets, capabilities, and machine/mode fingerprints; formal, symbolic, exact-discrete, interval, numerical, and counterexample artifact identities; checker/oracle identity and TCB overlap; interval and tolerance arithmetic; proof-state transitions; counterexample search and minimization; runtime witness and fallback decisions; and cancellation/fault/drain/finalize events.

Emit separate OperationReceipt, AttemptReceipt, JobReceipt, and CampaignReceipt objects containing the applicable ExecutionDisposition, RequestedPredicateOutcome, ClaimAdjudication, EvidenceMethodSet, EpistemicGrade, DomainApplicability, OperationalSupport, EvidenceCompleteness, EvidenceIntegrity, and PromotionEffect fields. Retain ClaimRelationReceipts, FailureBundles, diagnostics, minimized witnesses, and exact reconnect/replay pointers. Only the current OperationReceipt projects to process status.

Proof-critical events are lossless and never sampled. Logs are schema-versioned, bounded, redacted, backpressure-safe, content-addressed for large objects, and semantically equivalent across human-readable and stable machine forms.

## Considerations
Honest adjudication supports radical conjectures. A refutation can expose a sharper theorem; an unresolved atlas can guide adaptive proof search; a stronger independently checked theorem may supersede the initial target. The journey machinery must never dilute a theorem for UI convenience, confuse checker execution with proof, or turn incomplete or unavailable evidence into a truth value.

STRONGEST INFERENCE: schema V17's doc comment and crates/fs-ledger/CONTRACT.md state that evidence bytes frozen by a semantic binding are immutable. A caller may infer that a successful put_extension never invalidates an existing binding.

CODE ESTABLISHES: nothing on this path. put_extension writes via INSERT .. ON CONFLICT .. DO UPDATE. FrankenSQLite fires the table's AFTER INSERT triggers on the conflict branch and NEVER its UPDATE triggers, so the V17 guard trg_evidence_semantic_binding_guard_source_update never ran on fs-ledger's own public write path. Real SQLite 3.51.0 fires UPDATE triggers there and correctly aborts; verified side by side.

REPRO (default features, public API, no flags, single connection, no caller transaction):
  let ledger = Ledger::open(":memory:")?;
  let name = "gauntlet/exact-evidence"; let body = r#"{\"claim\":\"exact\",\"value\":17}"#;
  ledger.put_extension(ExtensionTable::Evidence, name, body)?;
  let r = ledger.record_identity_migration(/* canonical_bytes = body */)?;
  ledger.bind_evidence_semantic_identity(name, r.receipt_id())?;   // freezes the exact bytes
  ledger.put_extension(ExtensionTable::Evidence, name, r#"{\"claim\":\"reinterpreted\",\"value\":17}"#)?;  // returned Ok(())
Post-state before the fix: get_extension returns the reinterpreted body; the immutable binding row still stores content_id = BLAKE3(ORIGINAL body); and evidence_semantic_binding(name, receipt_id) returns Corrupt PERMANENTLY, because the bindings table refuses UPDATE, DELETE and same-key reinsert. The ledger silently converted a durable verified binding into an unrepairable corrupt one.

HONEST CLAIM: put_extension on evidence frozen by a V17 binding must REFUSE (LedgerError::Invalid) any body that is not byte-identical to the retained body. Only the byte-identical re-put may return Ok(()), and that Ok claims exactly one thing — the frozen bytes are unchanged — never that the new body is bound.

GAP SHAPE: silent-pass / fail-open gate, plus misused pinning authority (the stored content_id is read as pinning the retained bytes and, after the overwrite, pins nothing).
CONFIDENCE: HIGH — reproduced on both engines with the upstream divergence located.
close_reason: Fixed at b4ece64b. put_extension now runs refuse_bound_evidence_reinterpretation inside the same transaction as the upsert (the crate's existing owns_txn pattern, so a caller-owned transaction is respected). The helper mirrors the trigger predicate in Rust: if any evidence_semantic_bindings row names this evidence, the retained body must be byte-identical — an identical re-put stays legal (response-loss retry), any other body is refused with LedgerError::Invalid, and a bound-but-missing/non-text row is Corrupt. The V17 trigger is retained as the engine-level second line of defence for plain UPDATE/DELETE spellings. REGRESSION TEST: exact_evidence_binding_freezes_bytes_and_preserves_receipt_ambiguity (crates/fs-ledger/tests/identity_migration.rs) — the pre-existing test that had been failing; it was NOT weakened. The other two upsert sites were audited for the same bypass and neither is exposed (tune still advances the V20 generation via AFTER INSERT; tune_content_identities' DO UPDATE touches only non-key columns). fs-ledger identity_migration 13/13 green.

title: fsqlite: parameters inside WHERE-clause subqueries of FROM-less SELECT never bind (guarded INSERT...SELECT silently no-ops)
description: UPSTREAM fsqlite engine bug found while diagnosing the two red fs-session program_risk identity tests (807119d / bead cgt07). REPRO (minimal, fsqlite Connection API): CREATE TABLE edges(op INTEGER, artifact BLOB, role TEXT); insert one row (1, x'AA..' 32 bytes, 'out'). Then: (A) SELECT ?1, ?2 WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM edges WHERE artifact = ?1 AND op = ?2 LIMIT 1) with params [blob, 1] returns 0 rows — WRONG, sqlite3 returns 1 row. (B) INSERT INTO seals SELECT ?1, ?2 WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM edges WHERE artifact = ?3 AND op = ?4 LIMIT 1) with distinct param slots inserts 0 rows — WRONG. (C) params only in the outer select list with literal subquery predicates insert 1 row — correct. (D) SELECT EXISTS(...) with params inside the subquery as a PROJECTION expression returns correct results, and FROM-ful queries with params in WHERE subqueries work — the failure is specific to parameters referenced inside subqueries under a WHERE clause attached to a FROM-less SELECT (probe matrix: raw.rs/raw2.rs in session scratchpad sealprobe/, NobleLion 2026-07-16). IMPACT: fs-ledger's guarded seal inserts (seal_artifact_output, seal_op_artifact_edges) silently inserted zero rows for VALID sole producers, failing every v8->v9 seal adoption and production sealing path; worked around at fs-ledger by moving enforcement to the (correctly evaluating, NEW.-based) schema triggers and using plain INSERTs. The engine bug remains: any FROM-less guarded INSERT...SELECT with params in the guard is a silent data-loss shape. Same family as the IS NULL planner bug (bead lar1) and the eval_join_expr linear-scan finding (i3m4i): fsqlite subquery/parameter handling diverges from sqlite3 semantics.
close_reason: RESOLVED UPSTREAM and now PINNED: at fsqlite HEAD the bead's shapes (A)/(B) behave correctly — verified by the new contract suite committed as fsqlite b532362d4 (tests/fromless_where_subquery_params_contract.rs, 4/4 green): FROM-less SELECT binds params inside its WHERE EXISTS subquery with shared (?1/?2) and distinct (?3/?4) slots, the guarded INSERT...SELECT idiom inserts exactly one row for a satisfied guard and zero for an unsatisfied one, and the projection-EXISTS control keeps working. Reaching this verification required un-wedging the local build constellation: asupersync e325f4468 fixes the downstream-feature-set compile breaks (lab E0282 concrete annotations, rate_limit const-safe max, waiter dead_code allow — the same breaks tracked as frankensim-3bwvi) plus the documented-in-workspace uncommitted local overrides (.cargo/config.toml asupersync path patch, lock update, defaults flip) and running under nightly-2026-07-06. DISCOVERED AND FILED while pinning: a live SIBLING bug — params inside ANY subquery under a FROM-FUL outer WHERE never bind (armed #[ignore] test in the same suite; full probe matrix + EXPLAIN evidence in frankensim-fsqlite-fromful-subquery-params-kl17o).

title: Refuse unrepresentable Grid2 edge intersections
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND EXACT WITNESS
edge_crossing proves the real interpolation parameter t is strictly inside (0,1), but it never proves that the computed binary64 point is representably interior to the edge. Interpolated points bypass exact-node deduplication. On a 2x2 grid with both axis bounds [1.0, 1.0.next_up()], iso 0, lower-left sample -f64::from_bits(1), and the other three samples +1.0, both lower-left outgoing edges have a strict real crossing whose displacement rounds away. Both are emitted as bit-identical Interpolated([1,1]) even though that node sample is not iso. A crossing limit of 1 falsely returns CrossingBudgetExceeded; limit 2 returns duplicate supposedly unique intersections.

MISSION
Make representability part of contour evidence. For a strict crossing, require every varying output coordinate to lie strictly between the corresponding endpoint coordinates in the documented total order and require the point to lie on the closed edge without endpoint collapse. If the true crossing cannot be represented, return a typed UnrepresentableIntersection refusal carrying bounded edge indices, endpoint/value bits, iso bits, interpolation evidence, and first collapsed coordinate. Do not silently relabel it Exact.

ACCEPTANCE
- Preserve the exact 2x2 witness and axis-swapped, endpoint-reversed, sign-reversed, min-subnormal/normal, next-up/down, signed-zero, and scale neighbors.
- G0 distinguishes no crossing, exact endpoint, representable strict interpolation, unrepresentable strict interpolation, coincident level edge, nonfinite geometry, and resource refusal.
- G3 proves edge reversal and axis permutation produce equivalent points/refusals; affine/power-of-two coordinate transforms preserve the admitted relation where representable.
- Unique-crossing and budget semantics count only representably distinct admitted intersections; no false CrossingBudgetExceeded from duplicate collapsed points.
- Contract states the floating representability theorem and no-claim boundary. Central fs-viz all-targets, downstream fs-neuroshape-e2e/fs-wasm, clippy, and DSR are required before closure. Code-first slices remain in_progress pending consolidated proof.

title: Make Grid2 contour ownership linear, budgeted, and cancellable
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND ADVERSARIAL FAMILY
isocontour_crossings stores exact_nodes in a Vec and calls contains for every exact crossing. A checkerboard with iso-exact nodes on one parity and positive nodes on the other has no coincident exact-exact edges, Theta(N^2) unique nodes, Theta(N^2) edge events, and Theta(N^4) comparisons. crossing_limit bounds only successful output count and does not bound this pre-publication work. The synchronous primitive has no Cx polling, so admitted grids can monopolize a worker even though output memory is capped.

MISSION
Replace search-based deduplication with deterministic static edge/node ownership or an explicitly admitted near-linear marker/index scheme. Introduce a complete contour operation budget for cells, edge visits, exact-node ownership, interpolations, output, scratch/live bytes, and diagnostics; use checked arithmetic and refuse before work. Add caller-owned Cx with bounded tile polls and atomic publication, while retaining a small explicitly no-cancellation compatibility entry point only if required.

ACCEPTANCE
- Deterministic ownership emits every exact node once without global linear search and preserves the declared edge traversal/tie policy.
- Complexity is O(cells+crossings) or O((cells+crossings) log n) under an executable counter; the checkerboard family pins the bound and exact one-over refusal.
- Checked dimensions and budgets admit all simultaneously live storage, sort/marker scratch, and output before allocation; allocation failure is typed and no partial contour escapes.
- G0 exact boundary/overflow/ownership laws; G3 grid-axis and traversal metamorphisms; G4 pre-requested and stage-injected cancellation, panic/allocation faults, no leaks/partial output, bounded latency, byte-identical retry; G5 deterministic order.
- Detailed E2E logs include dimensions, cell/edge visits, exact/interpolated counts, dedup/ownership counts, requested/admitted/peak memory, polls, cancellation/finalization, refusal, and final artifact identity.
- Central fs-viz plus consumers all-targets, union clippy, and DSR proof required before closure.

title: Doctrine gap: several crates use raw platform libm transcendentals despite Fully-deterministic CONTRACTs
description:
DETERMINISM-DOCTRINE COMPLIANCE GAP found across multiple crates during the deep-review hunt. Beaded (not fixed piecemeal) because it is systemic, needs a workspace-level policy decision, and each fix may change last-ULP output → cross-ISA golden re-pins.

## The doctrine
fs-math/src/det.rs is built exclusively from correctly-rounded IEEE-754 ops so transcendentals are bit-identical cross-ISA ("No platform libm anywhere: cross-ISA determinism holds BY CONSTRUCTION, verified aarch64-apple vs x86-64"). Sibling crates route exp/ln/sin/cos/pow/atan2 through fs_math::det::. Platform std::f64 libm (cbrt/ln/exp/sin/cos/atan2/hypot/powf) is NOT correctly-rounded and differs by ≥1 ULP across ISAs/libm versions. See the determinism-incident-playbook (det:: routing doctrine, libm hazard class).

## Confirmed instances (agents traced these; there are likely more)
- fs-toleralloc: `.cbrt()` (lib.rs:130, feeds every allocated tolerance), `.ln()` (lib.rs:294,303, high-confidence budgets). CONTRACT says "Fully deterministic." Crate does not even depend on fs-math. (`.sqrt()` calls are fine — IEEE sqrt IS correctly rounded.)
- fs-geocon: `.powf` (primitives.rs:49,65), `.sin/.exp` (primitives.rs:108,193,305), `.hypot/.atan2/.cos/.sin_cos` (quotient.rs:42,45,47,69,72,88). CONTRACT asserts "identical inputs give identical reports BITWISE."
- fs-spectral: bare `f64::ln` in `route` (lib.rs:259-260); doc/CONTRACT claim "Fully deterministic." (Noted in an earlier review; would require adding an fs-math dep since fs-spectral depends only on fs-evidence.)

## The policy question (why this is a bead, not a blind fix)
Single-ISA determinism is UNAFFECTED (raw libm is deterministic on one build). The gap is CROSS-ISA bitwise reproducibility. The agents note MANY sibling crates (fs-ad, fs-plan, fs-render, fs-truss, fs-uq, ...) also call raw libm — so either (a) cross-ISA bitwise determinism is only REQUIRED of golden-bearing / lower-layer crates and these L3/L4 report crates are exempt (then the fix is to soften the CONTRACT wording, not the code), or (b) it is a broad latent compliance gap to be swept. Decide the policy first.

## If fixing (option b)
Add `fs-math` as a dep where missing; replace `.cbrt()` with `det::pow(x, 1.0/3.0)` (arg > 0 here), `.ln()`→`det::ln`, `.exp()`→`det::exp`, `.sin/.cos`→`det::{sin,cos}`, `.powf`→det pow, `.atan2/.hypot`→det equivalents. RE-CHECK every golden hash in each crate (the last ULPs shift) and cross-ISA verify per the golden-bump protocol. Consider extending the check-powi lint to also flag raw cbrt/ln/exp/sin/cos/atan2/hypot/powf on non-test paths so the doctrine is enforced, not just documented.

title: fs-scenario: net-flux incompressibility check samples only t=0, fail-open for ramp-from-zero inlets
description:
Deep-review hunt (2026-07-12), MEDIUM — a genuine fail-open; beaded because the fix needs a design decision (which times to sample).

## The gap
check_net_flux (scenario.rs:287-306) sums each inlet's mass_flow_at(0.0) — ONLY at t=0. Incompressible continuity requires the net boundary flux to be ~0 at EVERY instant, but a time-varying (Signal/Table/Ramp) inlet whose declared value is 0 at t=0 contributes nothing to gross at t=0. If every inlet is 0 at t=0, gross==0 and the imbalance branch (scenario.rs:295, guarded by gross>0) is SKIPPED entirely — a physically unbalanced scenario (net inflow for all t>0, incompressible, no pressure outlet) validates clean. Violates CONTRACT invariant 3. The fixture's own inlet is a Table [0.0, 0.75, 0.75] (exactly 0 at t=0); it only passes today because a pressure outlet short-circuits the check first (scenario.rs:284).

## Fix (design decision needed -> bead)
Evaluate the net flux at a REPRESENTATIVE set of times, not just t=0, and flag if imbalanced at ANY. For piecewise-linear signals (Ramp: t_start/t_end; Table: sample times) the net flux is piecewise-linear so its extrema are at breakpoints — collect the union of all BC signals' breakpoint times (+ t=0) and check each. Chebfun has no breakpoints -> sample a grid over its domain (density is the design choice). Alternatively, if 'balanced' is only required at steady state, sample the asymptotic value (signal at t=+large / final table value). Decide the semantics (per-instant vs steady-state) first. Keep the existing pressure-outlet short-circuit and the FLUX_REL_TOL relative test.

Regression: a single incompressible MassFlowInlet with a table [0, 0.75, 0.75] and NO pressure outlet must be flagged flux-imbalance. Current sc-002 (constant 0.9 inlet) still catches the constant case at any sample time.

title: fs-marquee composes CG's recursive residual estimate into a certificate term
description:
Filed by the E02 claim-integrity program; found while completing bead f85xj.2.24.

SURFACE: fs_marquee::study — the composed certificate vector
FILE: crates/fs-marquee/src/study.rs:279 — let cert = [0.0, dwr.eta_abs, sol.rel_residual * j.abs().max(1.0)];
      source at crates/fs-cutfem/src/elastic.rs:1227 — CutElasticitySolution.rel_residual

STRONGEST INFERENCE: a term composed into a certificate vector is a bound on the quantity it scales. A reader takes sol.rel_residual to be the solve's relative residual in the usual (Euclidean) sense.

CODE ESTABLISHES: fs-cutfem drives CgState, whose ResidualClaim is RecursiveEstimate — the recursively propagated residual, never recomputed as b - Ax. On ill-conditioned A it drifts BELOW the true residual by O(u * kappa * ||A||||x|| / ||b||). fs-cutfem publishes that number as CutElasticitySolution.rel_residual with no provenance, and fs-marquee multiplies it into a certificate term.

REPRO: any ill-conditioned CutFEM elasticity solve. The drift direction is what makes this a claim-integrity defect rather than noise: a recurrence estimate that drifts low makes the certificate term SMALLER, i.e. the composed certificate looks tighter than the evidence supports. fs-solver's own claim_integrity battery logs a concrete instance of the same class: a report with rel_residual 2.359e-14 whose iterate has a true Euclidean relative residual of 1.668e-8, six orders apart.

HONEST CLAIM: a certificate term must be built from a recomputed true residual (fs_solver::SolveReport::euclidean_rel_residual(), which now returns Option and fails closed for RecursiveEstimate/MNormEstimate), or the composed value must be labelled Estimated. fs-cutfem should carry the ResidualClaim rather than a bare f64, and fs-marquee should refuse to compose a non-Euclidean claim into a certificate.

GAP SHAPE: laundering — a recurrence estimate composed into a certificate term; enabled by the untyped rel_residual field that bead f85xj.2.24 documented as its residual gap.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH on the mechanism and the data flow (both traced); MEDIUM on how large the drift gets in the shipped marquee fixture.
notes: 2026-07-22 VioletHorizon: Live dataflow correction: Marquee consumes the scalar fs_cutfem::fem::Solution, not CutElasticitySolution, so the implementation covers both scalar and elasticity solve results. Both now recompute explicit b - Ax after CG, retain ResidualClaim::TrueEuclidean, expose a fail-closed euclidean accessor, and gate convergence on the recomputed magnitude; Marquee consumes only that accessor and remains Color::Estimated because the residual-to-goal-error conversion and DWR term are estimates. Proof: remote RCH cargo check -p fs-cutfem -p fs-marquee --features fs-marquee/marquee passed on transferred snapshot 3d133b34fa837bf3; remote cut_007b passed with an independent bit-identical b - Ax recomputation; remote cte_005 passed; remote mq_001_end_to_end_objective_improves passed 1/1 on transferred snapshot af18ec434a2bcd9d. Exact rustfmt and git diff --check pass; UBS reported 0 critical issues on the owned source/test files.
close_reason: Fixed residual-provenance laundering: scalar and elasticity CutFEM solutions now publish only explicitly recomputed b - Ax Euclidean residual claims, and Marquee fails closed on any non-Euclidean claim while retaining Estimated color for its estimated error conversion. Regression evidence: cut_007b_ghost_free_aggregation_accepts_graded_interface_band independently recomputes the residual bit-identically; cte_005_graded_componentwise_patch_reconstructs_midpoints_and_replays validates elasticity provenance; mq_001_end_to_end_objective_improves exercises the composed certificate. title: fs-cutfem scalar Space::build refuses valid ghost-free configs (band check not gated on ghost_gamma)
description:
SPURIOUS BUILD-TIME REFUSAL in crates/fs-cutfem/src/fem.rs (~lines 263-288, the `return Err(CutFemError::CutBandNotUniform ...)` block). Found in the deep-review hunt; NOT fixed by me because fs-cutfem is currently MID-FLIGHT (a concurrent agent has an uncommitted fem.rs diff + new untracked elastic.rs/tests) and multi-agent etiquette forbids editing/committing their in-progress files. Hand off to that agent or apply after their work lands.

## The bug
The scalar `Space::build` enumerates ghost faces and enforces the equal-level "uniform interface band" precondition UNCONDITIONALLY, even when `params.ghost_gamma == 0.0` (ghost penalty disabled). `CutBandNotUniform` is, by its own doc and CONTRACT.md's error model, purely a GHOST-PENALTY precondition ("ghost-penalty faces are assembled between equal-level cells only"). With ghost off (aggregation-only / unstabilized), no ghost faces are assembled, so the band-uniformity requirement does not apply — yet build() still rejects the configuration.

## Evidence it is a bug
The VECTOR sibling gets it right: `elastic.rs:372` wraps the identical neighbor-level check inside `if self.ghost_gamma > 0.0`. The scalar path (fem.rs) does not, so it refuses configs the vector path accepts. `assemble` already guards ghost assembly with its own `if self.params.ghost_gamma > 0.0` (fem.rs:418), so leaving `ghost_faces` empty when ghost is off is fully handled downstream.

## Trigger
Build a scalar `Space` on a graded quadtree (mixed active levels touching the interface — e.g. a `refine_where`-refined tree not passed through `refine_toward_interface`) with `ghost_gamma = 0.0` and `agg = Some(..)` (the documented ghost-free aggregation fallback, CONTRACT invariant 7). A cut cell with a differently-leveled active face-neighbor makes `build` return `CutBandNotUniform` and fail, even though aggregation needs no uniform band. Fails loudly (no wrong numbers) but refuses valid work. No battery test exercises it (cut-007 uses a uniform grid; cut-008 grades the tree but keeps ghost ON), so it is latent.

## Fix
Gate the ghost-face enumeration/refusal block on `self.params.ghost_gamma > 0.0`, mirroring `elastic.rs:372`. `ghost_faces` stays empty when ghost is off, which `assemble` already handles. Add a regression: a graded tree with `ghost_gamma = 0.0` + aggregation builds successfully (and solves). CONFIDENCE: medium.
close_reason: Fixed the scalar fail-open policy boundary: graded interface-band uniformity is now required only when ghost_gamma > 0, while ghost-free aggregation configurations build and solve. Added cut-007b paired regression proving ghost-off success and ghost-on refusal, plus nonfinite/negative ghost_gamma validation. Included in green RCH fs-cutfem test job j-29927301231673401; cargo fmt and git diff --check pass.

description:

- Rogue self-configured and exact-ID PermitAll artifacts fail against an independently retained flywheel acceptance authority; caller-selected pins cannot authorize.

title: Make fs-viz streamline integration admitted, fallible, and cancellable
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT
The public streamline helper allocates Vec::with_capacity(steps+1) with unchecked addition, so steps=usize::MAX can overflow or panic. It admits no finite seed/dt policy, accepts nonfinite field samples and integration states, has no work/memory budget or allocation refusal, and cannot observe cancellation. A visualization convenience API can therefore crash, monopolize a worker, or publish NaN trajectories that downstream reports mistake for meaningful paths.

MISSION
Replace the infallible helper with a typed, budgeted integration service under caller-owned Cx. Admit dimensions, finite seed, finite nonzero signed dt policy, step/work/output/live-byte limits, field evaluation contract, integrator/method/version, units, and termination policy. Use checked arithmetic, try_reserve, bounded tile polls, and atomic success publication. Preserve a small compatibility wrapper only if it is explicitly no-authority and cannot panic.

ACCEPTANCE
- steps=usize::MAX, steps+1 overflow, zero/one/exact/one-over caps, allocation injection, nonfinite seed/dt/field/intermediate, overflow, stagnation, domain exit, and callback panic have typed deterministic outcomes.
- Define whether reverse-time dt is supported; bind it in the receipt. Define zero dt, zero steps, boundary termination, and repeated-point semantics.
- G0 exact boundaries and first offender; G3 constant/affine analytic fields, time reversal where admissible, coordinate/unit rescaling, step refinement/error-order checks, and equivalent callback chunking; G4 pre-requested/stage cancellation, fault containment, no partial authoritative trajectory/leak, bounded latency, deterministic retry; G5 fixed bytes/order.
- Detailed E2E logs seed/units/method/dt/steps, requested/admitted/used/peak work and bytes, field calls, termination/refusal, error estimate, polls/finalization, identities, and no-claim boundary.
- Central fs-viz and downstream consumers all-targets, union clippy, and DSR proof required before closure.

title: fs-query: separation() treats chart eval as exact, not rigorous on enclosure charts
description:
Deep-review hunt (2026-07-12), LOW-MEDIUM — same chart-honesty class as the raycast fail-open fixed in f45a9e8.

## The gap
separation() (fs-query/src/lib.rs:291-367) computes observed/lower_bound from chart.eval(..).signed_distance as if it were EXACT. Its slack accounts only for the field's spatial Lipschitz variation across a grid cell, NOT for the per-sample enclosure error (+/-bound) that TiledSdf / MeshChart carry (they report an Enclosure(v-bound, v+bound) NumericalCertificate). CONTRACT.md invariant 4 claims 'the true separation lies in [lower_bound, observed]' GENERALLY. For an enclosure chart the sampled clearance can under-report the true field by up to 2*bound, so observed is no longer a guaranteed upper bound on the true separation and the rigorous bracket can EXCLUDE the truth. Only tested on exact spheres today (gq-*), so latent.

## Fix (two options, pick per intended scope)
(a) Restrict separation to charts whose sample carries an Exact certificate (check the ChartSample.error / trace_step_claim, refuse NoClaim/Enclosure with a teaching error) — mirrors the raycast fix; simplest and clearly sound.
(b) Widen observed/lower_bound by each field's enclosure bound (read ChartSample.error's band) so the bracket stays valid on enclosure charts.
Note the same crate's raycast was just hardened to fail closed on non-exact/-Lipschitz charts (f45a9e8); separation should get the same treatment. Also: the Separation.lower_bound DOC (lib.rs:277-279) says observed - 2*L*h*sqrt3/2 but the code computes L*hmax*sqrt3/2 (no factor 2) — the code is the correct/conservative value, only the doc is stale; fix the comment while here.
close_reason: Completed in fe68e26 through 9d9040b: separation now requires global ExactDistance authority from both charts, validates finite rigorous per-sample trace enclosures, forms its bracket from certificate endpoints with exact-distance 2-Lipschitz grid slack, fixes the stale lower-bound documentation, and retains structured refusal ordering. gq-004 through gq-004b and matching strict Clippy/tests passed on frozen h0z4 digest 5ad75c9434df9c7b6b511ca52dc30f99069c560af8079b4e8bc3d24f51b5a826.

title: Preserve typed Grid2 localization refusals through native and WASM reports
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT
The migrated native contour consumer calls .ok on both Grid2 construction and isocontour extraction. Invalid bounds, unrepresentable coordinates, nonfinite samples/geometry, coincident level edges, allocation failures, and resource/cancellation refusals all collapse to None and are serialized as the same (count=0, min=NaN, max=NaN) tuple. Operators cannot distinguish a valid empty contour from malformed evidence or resource failure; detailed deterministic diagnostics added by fs-viz are erased at the flagship boundary.

MISSION
Carry one stable typed localization outcome from fs-viz through NeuroShapeReport and WASM ABI/JSON: Localized, ValidEmpty, InvalidInput, Unrepresentable, ResourceRefused, Cancelled, AllocationRefused, and InternalFault, each with bounded structured detail and exact source stage. Preserve useful compatibility fields only as derived non-authoritative views.

ACCEPTANCE
- No .ok or display-string parsing erases Grid2Error/IsoContourError at an authority-bearing boundary.
- Stable versioned status/error codes retain axis/index/edge, first offender, required/limit, cancellation stage/finalization, and bounded context without attacker-sized messages.
- ValidEmpty is distinct from every refusal; NaN sentinels alone never carry status.
- Native and WASM G0 tests cover invalid bounds, unrepresentable coordinates/intersection, nonfinite sample/iso/geometry, coincident edge, output/work/memory budget, allocation, cancellation, and valid empty/nonempty.
- G3 native/WASM/JSON parity and round trips; G4 no partial localization on cancel/fault; deterministic detailed E2E logs include source identities and remedies.
- Central fs-viz/fs-neuroshape-e2e/fs-wasm all-targets, clippy, and DSR proof required before closure.

title: Unify immutable canonical MMS class admission across fs-verify and fs-ir
description: The hardened verifier admits at most six coefficients and checks u(1)=0 by outward interval evaluation, while fs-ir admits 4096 coefficients and requires bit-exact point evaluation, so the planner can pay for solves the verifier must refuse and rejects valid cancelling polynomials such as [0,-0.3,1.3,-1]. Migrate fs-verify, fs-ir, fs-adjoint, flywheel, planner/cache keys, and tests. Adding/mutating any semantic field must change identity; no upper-layer dependency from fs-verify.

title: Budget and cancel chance-constraint sampling with replay receipts
description:
Background/root cause: ConstraintKind::Chance currently admits every nonzero u32 MonteCarlo sample count and evaluate executes the entire synchronous sampling loop without Cx, cost/poll/deadline admission, memory authority, or a retained work receipt. A canonical fscon v2 payload can therefore request up to u32::MAX expression evaluations; dimension-exact noise draws are now checked, but the API still cannot cancel, bound, or explain that work. Adding an arbitrary sample cap would hide the resource contract and weaken the intended agent-native, budget-first architecture.

Design a versioned ChanceWorkPlan and evaluation API that take explicit Cx/admitted budget authority before the first sample. Compute sample x dimension x admitted expression-work cost with checked arithmetic; account for noise generation, shifted-point storage, scalar graph evaluation, accumulator work, and retained certificate bytes. Reject overflow, zero/excess work, deadline-without-clock, exhausted poll/cost quotas, and missing memory lease with typed teaching diagnostics. Tile samples and expression evaluation at deterministic logical identities, poll cancellation/deadline at bounded intervals, fully drain/finalize without emitting partial satisfied evidence, and attach plan identity plus BudgetConsumption/completed-sample receipt to the result and ledger. Preserve deterministic sampling independent of worker count and make seed/stream identity explicit rather than hiding it behind an opaque closure. Consider a compatibility wrapper only if it remains a clearly bounded/no-authority no-claim path.

Statistical correctness must advance with the resource design: retain hits, samples, estimator identity, level, delta, exact confidence-bound inputs, and optional-stopping semantics in the evidence artifact. Hoeffding fixed-horizon claims must refuse adaptive stopping; add an e-process/e-value path behind the appropriate frontier gate for anytime-valid stopping without reducing the current ambition. Noise draws must remain exact-dimension and finite or produce a typed refusal, never a conservative-looking miss that silently changes the sampling law.

Acceptance/Gauntlet: G0 exact/max+1 checked-arithmetic, samples, dimensions, expression-work, receipt-field, nonfinite draw, and policy boundaries; G1 binomial manufactured cases and declared coverage/false-clearance bands; G3 deterministic partition/reordering metamorphics that preserve the declared estimator semantics; G4 pre-cancel, cancellation at every tile family, exact and max+1 poll/cost/deadline budgets, deadline-without-clock, memory-lease exhaustion, injected evaluator/noise failures, no partial positive claim, and bounded post-request work; G5 bit-stable plan/receipt/evidence bytes across replays and worker counts. Emit detailed structured logs with phase, logical sample tile, seed/stream identity, planned/charged work, hits, completed samples, stop reason, and claim/no-claim transition. Update CONTRACT and require retained central RCH/DSR evidence before closure.

title: Variable-exponent f64::powi is build-mode-dependent: purge from deterministic paths, add fs-math powi_det + lint
description:
CONFIRMED with a minimized counterexample: 0.7f64.powi(k) differs by 1 ulp between debug and release builds from k=4 upward (0.7^4 = 0x3fcebb98c7e2823e debug vs ...3f release, cargo-built, pinned nightly 2026-07-05, aarch64). Root cause: std powi precision is documented as unspecified and its lowering (runtime exponentiation-by-squaring vs LLVM const-folding) depends on optimization level. Exponents <=3 are safe (squaring and sequential rounding orders coincide); divergence starts at 4.

This broke the fs-la rand_nla golden (debug observed 0x3e928bac8cf9fd48, release 0xf3dcb63be63f8ab9) and provoked an unjustified re-pin. The fixture is now fixed with a sequential product chain, but the same hazard is LATENT IN PRODUCTION PATHS:
- fs-feec/src/highorder/vecfam.rs (~10 sites): high-order basis monomials xi.powi(order) — G5 bit-stability hazard for r>=4 FEEC spaces across build modes/const-folding contexts.
- fs-ad/src/dual.rs:263-264: powi(n), powi(n-1) in dual-number pow rule.
- fs-dfo/src/cma.rs:245: powi(2*generations) — exponents in the thousands; maximal exposure.
- fs-la/tests/factor_battery.rs:50 fixture (test-only).

Fix: (1) fs-math gains a deterministic integer power (fixed evaluation order, conformance-tested, with a cross-build-mode golden); (2) migrate the sites above, bumping any affected goldens with justification; (3) a lint/xtask check forbids std powi with non-literal exponent or literal >3 outside fast-mode/no-claim paths (fits the existing ULP-ledger lint direction in wf9.14/r6r5).

Acceptance: powi_det golden identical across debug/release and both reference ISAs; migrated sites' batteries green; seeded violation caught by the lint. Found while executing the failure-compounding protocol (frankensim-epic-gauntlet-6nb.9) on the rand_nla golden break.

title: Reject bare carriage returns in strict CSV records
description: ROOT CAUSE: Catalog CSV parser v2 advertises a strict RFC-4180 subset with no embedded record separators, but CsvLines recognizes LF/CRLF only and split_csv accepts a bare U+000D as ordinary unquoted or quoted field data. Thus malformed records can retain hidden carriage-return controls, disagree with strict CSV consumers, and produce line-oriented output ambiguity. MISSION: Reject the first bare CR at its absolute input-byte offset in every parser state; retain CR only as the consumed half of a CRLF record delimiter. Preserve LF/CRLF equivalence, quoted escapes, empty/whitespace record semantics, resource caps, cancellation, and no partial CatalogRead publication. ACCEPTANCE: G0 covers bare CR in header, unquoted, quoted, and after-closing-quote positions plus CRCRLF; G3 proves canonical LF/CRLF inputs remain equivalent and every malformed form reports the first absolute offender. title: Make every session governor mutation retry-idempotent
description:
The plan and closed gp3.7 contract require idempotency keys on every mutating call, but Governor::charge(session, delta) accepts no report identity or monotone sequence. Retrying after an uncertain response double-meters the same usage and can falsely throttle/pause. apply_memory_pressure(session, 1|2) likewise appends duplicate declarations on retry, while a retried level-3 call after acknowledgement/activation starts a new pause generation. submit_once and acknowledge_pause are keyed, but they do not make these public mutators retry-safe.

Root fix: introduce bounded typed MeterReportId and PressureActionId authority. Either accept monotone cumulative meter snapshots or retain same-payload keyed deltas; identical replay must return the original receipt without mutation, conflicting payload reuse must fail closed, and IDs must bind governor/session/scope/generation. title: Persist immutable session mutation receipts for crash-safe replay
description:
The ujhp acceptance requires crash/replay, but fs-session currently keeps all retry registries and flush cursors only in one process. A crash after ledger commit and before in-memory cursor commit can append duplicate audit rows, and a new Governor cannot reconstruct private open, meter, pressure, or submission authorities from events. Arbitrary pending FnOnce work cannot be silently rerun after a crash because its side effects are indeterminate.

Root fix: add an immutable, bounded, typed terminal-mutation registry in fs-ledger and integrate it with fs-session flush in the same transaction as audit events. Registry identity must bind physical LedgerInstanceId, durable governor nonce, scope, session/open receipt, mutation kind and authority hash, exact payload identity, terminal receipt, causal meter ordinal and pre/post snapshots where applicable, and schema version. Insert-if-absent must return exact replay for identical bytes and structured conflict for different bytes. A deterministic flush-batch identity or semantic event uniqueness record must make commit-before-cursor retry append-once. Provide bounded lookup by authority hash so fs-session can rebuild terminal replay state and current meter/generation state after reopening. Recovered Pending executions are RecoveryRequired or Indeterminate and never auto-rerun.

Acceptance: kill/reopen after terminal commit for open, meter, pressure L1/L2/L3 lifecycle, successful submission, and failed submission; exact client retry returns the original receipt with no counter, meter, event, gate, reservation, or audit-row change; altered payload and foreign ledger/governor/session/scope conflict; crash after database commit before cursor publication does not duplicate rows; exact-cap and limit+1 storage/read budgets; corrupt, partial, future-schema, duplicate-conflict, and recovered-Pending cases fail closed; one transaction proves event rows and terminal registry cannot diverge; tests use a real on-disk ledger reopened through a fresh process/handle. This is mutation-level durable terminal replay; study-scale kill storms remain in frankensim-epic-helm-gp3.11.
