title: Roofline Freshness must bind live authority and return a typed recorded receipt
description:
The sealed production roofline protocol now binds registry, pre/post axes, dependency receipt, build identity, manifest, and ledger rows. Two authority gaps remain: staleness_at accepts only a baseline hash and cannot observe that the signing/promotion authority has since been revoked; ProductionRun::record returns a bare i64 op id, so callers can conflate committed recording with a row that has subsequently passed Fresh revalidation.

Extend freshness with an explicit pinned authority/policy context and revocation state. A revoked or policy-rotated baseline must never remain Fresh merely because its bytes/hash are intact. Replace or supplement the bare op id with an opaque RecordedProductionRun receipt carrying the op, run receipt, baseline/dependency authority fingerprints, record time, and a method that revalidates to a typed FreshProductionEvidence under current policy. Report-only/custom/refused runs cannot construct the positive type.

title: Bound roofline staleness history with authenticated snapshots
description:
Roofline staleness currently reconstructs manifested runs by scanning tune history and repeatedly querying sibling rows/artifacts. The integrity checks are strong, but cost grows with retained history and can become quadratic across a large long-lived ledger. An attacker or merely sustained CI can turn verification into an unbounded resource sink.

Define bounded, authenticated history snapshots/checkpoints for production roofline evidence. Index by run receipt/build/baseline/machine, retain the complete ordered manifest root and dependency authority, and verify one snapshot plus bounded deltas rather than rescanning all history. Compaction must preserve tombstones, corrupt-evidence findings, and historical failure knowledge; it must never make a previously corrupt row Fresh.

Acceptance: explicit row/byte/query bounds; adversarial 10^5-row fixture stays within declared time/memory/query budgets; snapshot/delta tamper, missing rows, duplicate manifests, rollback, and compaction interruption fail closed; result matches the exhaustive verifier on bounded randomized histories; cancellation is checked at chunk boundaries; performance evidence and bounds are ledgered.
close_reason: Implemented and landed at 6d39a90: crate::checkpoint module with chained authenticated staleness-history checkpoints. Fast path verified at exactly 2 ledger reads independent of history depth (read_queries asserts, 40-run scale fixture) vs O(H*(K+4)) exhaustive; verdict-lattice equivalence tested across Fresh/Expired/ClockRollback/BuildDrift/NeverMeasured/FingerprintDrift/BaselineUnavailable; tamper, rollback simulation, chain tamper, and ordinal gaps all classify CorruptEvidence or fail closed to exhaustive; tombstone permanence tested through restore+reseal. Battery 8/8 plus scale fixture green, full fs-roofline suite green (91+11+8+1+2+8), CONTRACT.md updated with semantics and no-claim boundary.

title: fs-session: in-memory submission terminals can never flush under the fs-ledger preclaim doctrine
description:
SIX fs-session conformance tests fail deterministically at HEAD (0fba65d): ss_003c, ss_003d, ss_003f, ss_003h, ss_006, ss_013 — all with 'submission authority <hash> requires a committed pre-execution claim and its positive terminalization permit' (fs-ledger session_registry.rs:4265-4272).

ROOT CAUSE (verified, not contention): fs-ledger 3a25a0d's registry doctrine refuses session_terminal groups with claim.kind=='submission' unless a durable PRE-EXECUTION claim exists (with positive permit). fs-session has the durable path (submit_once_durable files the Pending claim, durable_submission_permit threads the permit into BufferedTerminal), but the PLAIN submit_once -> flush_scope_to_ledger path emits KIND_SUBMISSION terminals with permit=None and no pre-committed claim -> the ledger refuses, and because the batch stays fully dirty, RETRY REFUSES FOREVER. The in-memory execute-then-flush contract that ss_003* pins ('open and self-contained terminal submission receipts') is structurally unsatisfiable.

Attribution evidence: 728d631 (2pmb) touched only cost-model surfaces (estimate/sealed/admission) — reds reproduce orthogonally; fs-session/fs-ledger trees clean at time of run; failure is a typed ledger refusal, not contention.

title: Make fs-shapeprog simplification error certificates compositional and cancellation-safe
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND SEVERITY
fs-shapeprog simplification currently treats local rewrite error as a scalar combined with max. That is sound across independent min or max branches only under the right Lipschitz hypotheses, but not across sequential approximations on the same evaluation path. Two individually droppable offsets separated by a constructor can accumulate beyond the published max_error. Separately, consecutive Offset nodes are algebraically merged and labeled Exact even though the interpreter evaluates two rounded subtractions while the rewrite evaluates one subtraction from a rounded parameter sum. Catastrophic parameter cancellation can therefore change the SDF while publishing max_error zero. These are false geometry certificates and therefore P0.

MANDATORY WITNESSES
- Union(sphere(1).offset(0.006), sphere(1).translate([100,0,0])).offset(0.006) at tolerance 0.01 drops two sequential offsets on the active origin branch. Actual discrepancy is 0.012 while the current report says 0.006.
- sphere(1).offset(f64::MAX).offset(-f64::MAX) evaluates to a value one unit away at the origin after the current consecutive-offset merge, yet the rewrite is labeled Exact with max_error zero.
Preserve these as named G0 regressions and add order-reversed, sign, signed-zero, subnormal, overflow, branch-selection, and threshold neighbors.

MISSION
Replace ad hoc max-error bookkeeping with a compositional, outward-safe error algebra tied to the actual floating interpreter. Sequential rewrite errors must add outwardly; independent branch alternatives may use max only with executable 1-Lipschitz hypotheses; affine or scale operations must transform bounds by certified absolute Lipschitz factors; non-finite or unrepresentable propagation must refuse simplification rather than publish a finite claim. Never call a real-arithmetic identity Exact when f64 evaluation order changes observable semantics.

DESIGN AND ACCEPTANCE
- Define combination operators that distinguish sequential composition, alternatives, and scaling. Use exact or outward-rounded nonnegative bounds, validate every operand, and fail closed on overflow or missing hypotheses.
- Either preserve nested offsets exactly or prove a bit-level equivalence predicate for each merged instance. A heuristic near-equality check is insufficient.
- Track the deterministic first lossy rewrite and enough path or node context to replay the accumulated bound. Exact means bit-equivalent under the documented signed-zero and NaN policy.
- Ensure simplification is monotone in tolerance, idempotent at a true fixed point, deterministic, and cannot exceed its reported bound at any admitted finite sample.
- Add focused unit tests and G3 metamorphic tests for rewrite grouping, nesting under Union or Intersection or transforms, evaluation-order changes, permutation where mathematically admissible, power-of-two scaling, repeated simplification, and direct discrepancy verification. Include detailed deterministic diagnostics.
- Document the theorem hypotheses and no-claim boundary in CONTRACT. Do not weaken the system by disabling useful approximate rewrites globally; make the evidence calculus correct.
- Code-first landing may use rustfmt and diff checks only. Keep the Bead in progress until central cargo test -p fs-shapeprog --all-targets, union clippy, and DSR are green with recorded logs.

title: fs-adjoint: bind DWR acceptance to sealed estimate identity
description: ROOT CAUSE: accept consumes a caller-supplied dwr_abs scalar and can set accepted=true without retained DwrOutput evidence or binding the estimate to the problem, candidate, functional/window, and solver provenance. A caller can inject zero or replay an unrelated estimate. Deeper first-principles defect: dwr_integral_qoi admits any finite endpoint-zero P1 candidate but never proves it solves the primal discrete equilibrium. Because the enriched test z_f-I_h z_f vanishes at every coarse node, the constant candidate-slope contribution integrates to zero on each coarse cell; eta therefore measures only the fine-bubble/discretization residual and can remain unchanged under arbitrary interior candidate corruption, omitting coarse-space algebraic residual. Merely sealing the current payload would bind scientifically invalid data. SCOPE: introduce an unforgeable constructor-sealed DWR estimate binding exact problem/operator/mesh/forcing, candidate, functional/window and clipped partition, execution/budget policy, estimator payload, and a primal-solve/equilibrium receipt. Require acceptance to consume and verify that typed estimate; either prove the candidate is the canonical Galerkin solve to a retained residual tolerance or add a sound algebraic-error contribution/bound. Reject query/problem/candidate/solver-policy mismatch; retain Estimated color until a stronger theorem-backed proof exists. TESTS: naked/adversarial zero injection; cross-query/problem/candidate replay; arbitrary endpoint-zero interior corruption; random nonsolution candidates; perturbed solver residual at exact thresholds; stale mesh/forcing; tamper/reforge attempts; deterministic identity; valid solved-candidate acceptance; cancellation and budget boundaries. ACCEPTANCE: no public path accepts a naked estimate scalar; no accepted receipt can arise from an unproved primal candidate or omitted algebraic error; every acceptance is replay-verifiably linked to the exact solved state, functional, estimator partition, and execution policy.

DwrOutput and AcceptOutcome currently expose public mutable fields, so constructor sealing alone is not unforgeability unless all identity-bearing payload is private and access is read-only. The verifier must recompute identity from canonical source data, not trust stored digests. Bind the complete MmsProblem::canonical_bytes() payload; the current pattern of placing a BLAKE3 envelope around a weak 64-bit FNV-derived problem root cannot restore collision resistance. Replace the human label-only DwrQuery with a typed functional specification carrying domain/window, endpoint convention, units/dimension, QoI semantics, and schema version. Negative tests must mutate every private serialized field through supported decoding/tamper paths, attempt cross-functional replay with the same label, and demonstrate canonical-byte identity separation.

SCOPE: make admission lower internally under a versioned policy or accept an opaque validated LoweredProgram that callers cannot forge; bind raw and lowered identities and reject lowering errors before authority checks. title: fs-qty: replace saturating dimension algebra with checked authority
description: ROOT CAUSE: dimension multiplication/division and const-generic support use saturating i8 arithmetic. Overflow aliases an invalid expression to a valid dimension vector, allowing dimensional checks and IR admission to accept false physics. SCOPE: introduce checked authoritative dimension operations and propagate a typed overflow/invalid-dimension state through quantity expressions and fs-ir admission; reserve saturation only for explicitly non-authoritative diagnostics if needed. TESTS: every +/-128 boundary, long multiply/divide/power trees, cancellation after overflow, const/runtime parity, query/admission refusal, and no alias to valid dimensions. title: fs-scenario: bound and linearize whole-scenario semantic validation
description: ROOT CAUSE: Scenario and FrameTree expose public unbounded Vec-backed authority values, but Scenario::validate has no explicit work/heap/cancellation budget. FrameTree::check repeatedly performs linear find scans inside every parent-chain walk, producing O(F^3) worst-case work; case-name, BC-frame, combination-reference, and flux-set checks add further repeated scans and allocations. The default IR syntax budget can still decode cardinalities large enough to make semantic validation an accidental denial-of-service, while directly constructed scenarios bypass IR caps entirely. Identifier integrity is also incomplete: empty scenario/frame/case/combo/ensemble/region names and duplicate combination/ensemble identities are not uniformly refused. SCOPE: define a checked semantic ValidationBudget/work plan; build fallibly reserved deterministic indexes for frame IDs/names, case names, ensemble names, and references; use a linear-time color/parent traversal for cycles and ambiguity; validate BC/combination/contact/flux references without repeated full scans; add bounded cancellation checkpoints while retaining stable all-findings order and actionable fixes. Decide and document canonical identifier rules and duplicate-term/contact semantics. Keep parse syntax budgets separate from semantic admission and bind both plans into later ledger receipts. TESTS: exact budget and budget+1 for every collection family; 100k-node deep/wide acyclic/cyclic frame adversaries; duplicate/empty/non-ASCII identities; duplicate frame direct-pose ambiguity; dangling chains; combination/reference fanout; cancellation at each phase; allocation-refusal injection; equivalence against a small exhaustive oracle; permutation/metamorphic determinism; measured near-linear scaling. ACCEPTANCE: no public scenario can trigger unadmitted superlinear validation or ambiguous identity resolution, validation never panics or silently drops a finding, and retained evidence demonstrates the declared complexity/cancellation envelope.

description: AMBITION RATCHET: derive and mechanize a goal-oriented verified interval theorem for the quantity of interest, not merely an Estimated-color heuristic. A world-class result should produce a replayable interval J(u) in [J(u_h)+Delta_h-E, J(u_h)+Delta_h+E] under explicit hypotheses, where Delta_h is a computable signed correction and E combines independently certified primal and dual approximation factors, algebraic-solve residuals, coefficient/data uncertainty, and quadrature/rounding enclosures. Preserve ambitious branches for superconvergent cancellation, localized sheaf-compatible patch certificates, topology-aware dual localization, and machine-checked theorem artifacts rather than weakening them into unconditional claims. title: fs-flywheel-e2e: isolate speculative branches and commit merge atomically
description: ROOT CAUSE: fs-flywheel-e2e run_loop executes nominally parallel agents against one mutable global RecomputeStore and advances the global headline/evidence during each branch before conflict resolution. A later branch can therefore observe same-iteration writes from an earlier branch, take cache skips, and receive parallel cost credit for work that was not independent. Conflicted or cancelled speculative branches also leave cache artifacts and accepted proposal evidence in the global headline. In the current literal-artifact fixture this already corrupts skips, per-branch costs, speedups, proposal/accept denominators, telemetry, trace hashes, and lineage; with real artifact inputs it becomes cache poisoning and output contamination. SCOPE: give every iteration one immutable start-of-iteration store/headline snapshot; execute branches in isolated overlays that collect cache writes, artifacts, evidence, costs, telemetry, and proposal state; resolve merge before publication; atomically validate and commit a deterministic union only for Resolved/Trivial outcomes or an explicitly serialized resolution. Quarantine conflict evidence outside the authoritative cache/headline, discard uncommitted overlays on cancellation while retaining honest charged work, and detect same-identity/different-artifact collisions before any partial commit. Bind snapshot revision, overlay roots, resolution, committed write set, and resulting revision into replay evidence. Preserve deterministic branch-order independence and request-drain-finalize semantics. TESTS: a cold one-iteration parallel run has no same-iteration cross-branch hits; swapped agent order and forced scheduler interleavings produce identical reports; accepted proposals followed by forced merge conflict leave authoritative cache revision/headline unchanged and the next iteration matches a no-commit control; cancellation after zero/one/all branch completions leaves no writes but charges completed work; identical overlay writes deduplicate, disjoint writes union, conflicting artifacts refuse atomically; inject failure at every validate/commit boundary; replay/tamper checks cover snapshot and commit receipts. ACCEPTANCE: no branch reads another branch's speculative writes; unresolved/cancelled work cannot affect authoritative skip decisions, headline evidence, or future outputs; every committed iteration is one atomic, deterministic, replay-verifiable state transition.

SCOPE: give every descriptor coordinate a canonical semantic property/role identity plus units, orientation/basis conventions, regime, and schema version; define explicit verified crosswalk receipts for aliases/equivalent bases; compare Pi signatures only after exact compatibility or successful crosswalk; bind crosswalk and distance policy into tombstone evidence. title: fs-cheb: make affine domain maps stable across the finite f64 range
description: ROOT CAUSE: Cheb1::eval maps x by 2*(x-a)/(b-a)-1 and sample_first_kind maps back using midpoint + t*(b-a)/2. For valid finite opposite-sign extreme endpoints such as [-f64::MAX,f64::MAX], b-a overflows; evaluation at the legal endpoint b becomes inf/inf -> NaN and construction samples become infinite. The derivative chain-rule scale has the same width-overflow pattern. SCOPE: implement shared overflow/underflow-stable affine forward/inverse maps with exact endpoint handling and deterministic rounding policy; reuse them in evaluation, sampling, differentiation, integration/root coordinate conversion, and multidimensional consumers. Refuse or honestly bound operations whose physical result is unrepresentable. TESTS: [-MAX,MAX], asymmetric extremes, subnormal-width adjacent endpoints, exact endpoints/midpoint, forward-inverse metamorphics, constant/linear coefficients, derivative/integral, Scenario Chebfun evaluation, and cross-ISA bits. ACCEPTANCE: every admitted finite nonempty domain evaluates finite representable polynomials at every finite in-domain point; mapping code has one tested implementation and no direct overflowing width subtraction remains on claimed paths.

This violates canonical identity congruence and makes the strengthened no-alias string policy incomplete. SCOPE: choose and document one semantic law. If signed zero has no physical meaning, canonicalize every float-bearing scenario field to +0 at checked construction/admission and canonical writing while preserving all nonzero finite bits; if replay requires signed-zero distinction, replace derived equality with schema-wide bitwise float semantics. Apply consistently to quantities, signal times/values, frame motors, ensemble parameters, combination factors, contacts, domains/coefficients, migration receipts, and hashes. TESTS: mutate +0/-0 in every float-bearing path; equality implies identical canonical bytes/hash; parse/write idempotence; legacy migration; no accidental normalization of negative nonzero/subnormal values. ACCEPTANCE: scenario semantic equality and canonical identity are congruent by construction and the policy is explicit.

title: fs-asbuilt: make validity claims internally true and coverage-scoped
description: ROOT CAUSE: AsBuiltDiff computes fixed booleans at one supplied registration residual, measurement-noise value, and tolerance, but publishes a ValidityDomain containing entire intervals from zero to those endpoints. The same retained result is false at many points inside its declared domain. It also describes a maximum over corresponding samples as whole-part conformance even though nothing bounds unsampled surface or volume deviation. A BLAKE3 identity cannot rescue an internally false claim. SCOPE: separate exact RunConditions from a theorem-backed ValidityDomain. Default evidence binds only the exact operating point. Wider domains require an immutable monotonicity/generalization receipt whose hypotheses and arithmetic are independently replayed. Replace binary above-noise and within-tolerance authority with Pass, Fail, or Indeterminate under the registration/noise model from sj31i.15. Model the multiple-comparison/noise-floor decision explicitly. Promote sampled conformance to whole-part conformance only with retained geometry-coverage evidence such as sampling density, reach/curvature and Lipschitz bounds, chart/sheaf coverage, occlusion/missing-region disposition, and interpolation error. TESTS: endpoint and interior-domain counterexamples, exact-run round trip, tampered generalization receipt, large registration uncertainty, pure-noise maxima as sample count grows, irregular/occluded sampling, adversarial spikes between samples, certified coverage success, unit rescaling, cancellation and budget refusal, and mutation of every receipt edge. LOGGING: bounded structured events must distinguish measured samples, inferred regions, missing coverage, uncertainty components, theorem/hypothesis version, and no-claim reasons. ACCEPTANCE: every declared validity point is actually supported; sample-only evidence can never masquerade as a whole-part guarantee; undecidable cases remain Indeterminate rather than fail-open booleans.

title: New-domain evidence: bind semantic identity and context of use

Numerically identical meters and millimeters, displacement and temperature states, or incompatible bases can therefore share evidence identities. In-sample misfit reduction is then easy to misread as validation because observations carry no training/calibration/holdout role, model discrepancy, operator uncertainty, context-of-use value, or observability/confounding receipt. SCOPE: define schema-versioned semantic identities for state coordinates, physical quantity dimensions and kinds, frames, bases, support geometry/time, model/operator, experiment/dataset/sample/replicate, instrument/calibration, correlation group, and intended context of use. Require canonical crosswalk receipts for legitimate aliases or basis/unit transformations. Introduce ExperimentArtifact and CalibrationSplit roles, bind blind holdout separation before execution, represent model discrepancy and observation-operator uncertainty, and retain observability/confounding plus posterior-predictive diagnostics. Distinguish content addressing from authenticated calibration authority. TESTS: equal bits under incompatible units/frames/states/bases diverge or refuse; valid crosswalk equivalence; duplicated row versus independent replicate; train/holdout leakage; time/support mismatch; stale calibration/model; unobservable and confounded models; model-discrepancy floor; posterior-predictive falsifier; permutation and replay; tamper of every semantic field. LOGGING: structured evidence records data role, support, transformations, identities, discrepancy assumptions, diagnostics, and explicit no-validation boundaries without exposing sensitive raw data. ACCEPTANCE: no estimator identity is semantically ambiguous, no duplicate datum gains information accidentally, and no in-sample update can be promoted as context-of-use validation without independent retained evidence.

title: fs-assimilate: certify covariance contraction and use stable factor updates
description:
ROOT CAUSE: the production scalar Joseph update checks posterior PSD but does not establish the documented Loewner claim P_prior - P_posterior is PSD, nor fail closed when floating arithmetic makes a claimed contraction unresolved. It constructs dense I-KH products and performs full PSD validation for every scalar observation, giving O(m n^3) work and compounding rounding error. Algebraic correctness over exact reals is not an executable floating-point certificate.

SCALAR SCOPE: add a checked covariance-contraction receipt with interval, factor-residual, or independently checkable scaled bounds and explicit Certified, Refuted, and Unresolved states. Misfit monotonicity is a checked diagnostic rather than a prose assertion. Implement a deterministic square-root, UD, or QR scalar update with O(n^2) work. Retain the dense Joseph path only as a small independent oracle. Use scaled and compensated arithmetic, checked allocation/work plans, bounded cancellation tiles, canonical factor sign/tie rules, and a flat fallible caller-owned scratch plan. Do not wait for shared-correlation modeling: this leaf is the independent scalar substrate. Correlated and block updates are preserved exclusively in dependent P0 leaf sj31i.64.

TESTS AND EVIDENCE: G0 covers algebraic laws, empty/min/max shapes, ill-conditioned, rank-singular and nearly singular covariances, subnormal and near-MAX scaling, exact-zero innovation, rank-deficient operators, Loewner oracle comparison, adversarial rounding where naive Joseph expands a direction, factor reconstruction, checked arithmetic, allocator refusal, and deterministic error order. G1 uses manufactured scalar Gaussian updates with analytic posterior mean/covariance and verifies receipt convergence under controlled conditioning. G2 runs canonical Kalman/square-root filtering benchmarks, including repeated low-noise observations and a high-dynamic-range metrology case. G3 covers equivalent factor representations, state/unit rescaling, legal observation permutations, and dense-oracle differential fuzzing. G4 covers large-n work/retained-byte bounds, exact quota boundaries, cancellation and allocation faults at every phase, drain/finalize, and no partial authority. G5 replays numerics, factor signs, identities, receipts, and logs across thread counts and supported ISAs.

REAL E2E AND LOGGING: Add a no-mock scalar sensor-to-Belief-to-stable-update-to-independent-checker path owned by this leaf. It must run the production API, retain the prior/observation/posterior/contraction roots, independently reconstruct and check the factor/covariance and analytic benchmark, and emit bounded structured logs for units, dimensions, conditioning indicators, method, residual/contraction/misfit bounds, admitted/consumed/remaining work and memory, cancellation/drain/finalize, refusal/no-claim reason, and checker disposition. The broader multi-stage authentic as-built/assimilation evidence pipeline remains in dependent sj31i.38, but .37 does not rely on it for scalar numerical closure.

ACCEPTANCE: every advertised scalar contraction has executable evidence; production scalar updates are O(n^2), stable, budgeted, allocation-fallible, independently checked, and usable before correlated-observation support lands. Closing this leaf requires only the complete scalar substrate and its own evidence above. No feature is removed: correlated batches, whitening, joint calibration/registration covariance and block QR close under sj31i.64 after both this substrate and sj31i.16.

title: Sheaf numerics: convergence-certified decomposition, scale-aware spectra, and explicit Unknown
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Fixed iteration counts, absolute thresholds, partial eigenspectra, and nominal residuals can be mistaken for mathematical decomposition or cohomology authority. Build numerical reports whose claims are exactly scoped.

SCOPE: Define named normalized operators and return absolute plus scale-normalized primal, dual, orthogonality, and reconstruction residuals; stopping reason; iteration/work counts; conditioning and separation scope; nullspace dimension bounds; set-valued eigenvalue clusters; unresolved modes; and Converged, Indeterminate, or Refused state. Account for every admitted connected-component zero mode. A partial spectrum declares its covered range and never implies completeness. Retain witnesses sufficient for independent replay. New theorems may strengthen authority only under versioned admitted assumptions and proof/checker artifacts.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: No spectral-gap, harmonic, exact, coexact, topology, or local-unrepairability claim arises from an unnormalized or unconverged computation. G0 tests exact complexes, repeated/clustered zero modes, scaling, sign/orientation, ill conditioning, empty components, extreme arithmetic, and tolerance boundaries. G1 manufactured decompositions verify residual and convergence order. G3 covers basis, relabeling, unit/weight scaling, subdivision, and equivalent normalization. G4 exhausts work/memory/deadline/cancellation with retained partial reports and no false success. G5 replays reductions across thread counts and ISAs. Independent spot checks and mutations target every residual, threshold, coverage, and completeness guard. Logs retain operator/normalization identity, spectrum coverage, residual bounds, budgets, state, and theorem/no-claim scope.

FRESH-EYES NUMERICAL-AUTHORITY ADDENDUM (2026-07-14): The live repair module still uses a fixed-count least-squares iteration, naive norm/sum arithmetic, absolute/component heuristics, and nominal fractions to label exact/coexact/harmonic-looking pieces. It can overflow, underflow, stagnate, or return a non-orthogonal remainder without an explicit Unknown state; downstream proposal ranking then treats those nominal values as actionable. Required implementation: consume only admitted skeletons and finite cochains; use scale-safe compensated norms and residuals; expose primal normal-equation, dual, orthogonality, and reconstruction enclosures normalized to operator/input scales; declare stopping reason and iteration/work bounds; represent repeated/clustered zero modes and disconnected-component gauges explicitly; refuse unproved component classification and proposal eligibility; and make every allocation/cancellation path transactional. The scalar QoI/evidence rule is also normative: an invalid, unavailable, allocation-refused, or empty sampled-agreement calculation must publish +infinity or a typed absent QoI, never a finite clean-looking zero; a finite QoI may appear only with the exact validity/coverage receipt that justifies it. title: Sheaf repair planning: typed proposal states and component-wise gauge feasibility
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Non-finite sentinels conflate unavailable, infeasible, and over-budget proposals, while a single global gauge shift ignores the independent constant nullspace of disconnected components. Define a typed and deterministic repair-planning algebra.

SCOPE: Predictions use Available(value,witness), Unavailable(reason), Infeasible(witness), or OverBudget(required,available); costs carry units and a declared cost model; metrics name normalization, confidence or enclosure class, and source report. Ranking is deterministic and never converts a non-finite sentinel into a finite preference. Compute connected components including isolated vertices. Intersect every member's possibly asymmetric admitted shift interval per component, select a documented deterministic maximum-slack representative, return actual component offsets, and localize infeasibility. GaugeStepEligible authorizes only that representative choice and cannot erase coexact or harmonic obstruction.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Globally infeasible but component-wise feasible examples succeed with distinct offsets; one infeasible component is localized without laundering other components into complete repair. G0/property tests cover typed-state ordering, unit/cost mismatch, deterministic ties, disconnected/isolated components, asymmetric intervals, unbounded/point intervals, extreme values, and component permutation. G3 covers component and vertex reordering, equivalent gauges, and scaling. G4 cancels proposal generation/ranking/interval intersection with no selection publication. Mutation tests restore sentinels, global shifts, or nondeterministic ties. Logs retain proposal identities/states, metric/cost units, component partition, feasible intervals, chosen offsets, budgets, and GaugeStepEligible scope.

title: Sheaf repair execution: transactional application, independent revalidation, and merge-ready handoff

This leaf may exercise a refusal-only or test-double-free handoff validator, but it MUST NOT claim that base-aware CAS merge, atomic publication, property-specific continuum cover, or topology certification succeeded. Those authorities belong to sj31i.46 and sj31i.44. The final real integration and replay ratchet is preserved in a separate leaf depending on all three implementations.

G4 injects failure/cancellation at every apply, measure, certify, handoff, ledger, and publication boundary with rollback and no leaks. G5 replays across thread counts and supported ISAs. A real no-mock phase E2E constructs a disconnected mixed-chart model, plans and applies repair, independently revalidates phase-local obligations, emits the sealed merge-ready handoff, persists/checks that receipt, and replays from roots. Mutation tests must catch dropped fields/tombstones, unauthenticated parents, and partial commit. A no-mock E2E must merge a mixed geometry/material/BC scenario and replay it from ledger roots. Logs retain base/parent/output roots, exact outcome histogram, per-plane write/conflict sets, units/schemas, budgets, cancellation/finalization, receipt version, and explicit authority/no-claim state.

CONCURRENCY AND PUBLICATION: Every merge begins from an ExpectedBase containing both a strong base artifact identity and an admitted generation or version token. Before publication, compare-and-swap both values against the authoritative store; pathname equality or a content root without generation is insufficient because replacement and ABA can restore an old root after intervening writes. Bind base, left, and right snapshots before and after computation. A stale generation, changed parent, concurrent writer, repository replacement, or publication-target drift returns a typed retry or refusal and publishes nothing. Retry rereads the authoritative base and recomputes; a stale successful receipt cannot be replayed as commit authority. Identical concurrent commits may deduplicate idempotently only when complete output and authority contexts match. Disjoint concurrent commits must not lose updates.

OUTCOME CONSERVATION: Define a complete per-plane outcome algebra for geometry, cochain, and assignment entities: unchanged, one-sided create/update/delete, equal concurrent edit, merged compatible edit, tombstoned, conflict by kind, refused, and any explicitly deferred state. The receipt carries a full histogram plus localized identity sets. Every admitted base/left/right identity in the merge universe appears in exactly one outcome class per applicable plane; histogram totals equal independently recomputed universe cardinalities, and no entity is omitted or double-counted. Geometry repair and gauge outcomes receive the same accounting. The checker recomputes these conservation laws rather than trusting merger-supplied counters.

title: fs-cheb roots: typed real/complex regions, set-valued multiplicity, and certified completeness
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs-cheb currently exposes three distinct root paths whose authority must not be conflated. Cheb1::roots performs a fixed-grid sign scan and is explicitly incomplete; colleague_roots emits policy-filtered, cluster-deduplicated approximate matrix candidates; certified_roots independently invokes fs-ivl adaptive interval Newton over the full normalized domain. The certifier does not consume the grid or colleague candidates. Its live authority defect is that certified_roots projects the underlying RootSearchReport into a plain list, discarding complete, boxes_examined, exhaustion, and domain-coverage metadata, while none of the paths can express certified multiplicity/count clusters or unresolved candidate families. Thus callers cannot distinguish a complete exhaustion receipt from a partial set of boxes, and approximate discovery paths can still miss even-multiplicity, tightly clustered, endpoint, or highly scaled roots if misused as complete.

SCOPE: Preserve distinct discovery, approximation, and certification APIs with non-interchangeable types. Introduce a public RootSearchReport projection that retains disjoint set-valued clusters, multiplicity/count bounds, candidate provenance, domain coverage/exclusion tree, boxes examined, work and memory budgets, stopping reason, and Complete/Partial/Indeterminate/Refused truth state. Combine stable colleague pencils, adaptive interval subdivision, interval Newton/Krawczyk where admissible, derivative/GCD or square-free structure, Bernstein/Chebyshev exclusion bounds, argument-principle or Sturm-like counts for supported real classes, and arbitrary-precision/escalation hooks. Handle zero polynomials, degree drops, endpoint roots, repeated/even roots, extreme affine domains, coefficient dynamic range, underflow/overflow, and complex-conjugate clusters. Keep ambitious new completeness and multiplicity theorems as explicit feature-gated authority that can be promoted only with retained proofs.

ACCEPTANCE: Complete means every root in the admitted domain is covered by exactly one returned cluster and every cluster has certified count/multiplicity bounds; Partial explicitly names uncovered domain/work. The fs-ivl exhaustion metadata is preserved end-to-end rather than inferred from a list. No fixed sample density or colleague-candidate list can silently determine completeness. Domain and physical widths are typed and conservatively mapped. Deterministic ordering/tie-breaking is specified. Existing simple-root callers receive a checked projection only when singleton/simple obligations are proven.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 algebraic and property tests separately exercise the grid, colleague, and interval-certification contracts against analytic polynomials, zero/constant/degree-one, repeated/clustered/endpoint roots, coefficient/domain scaling, and non-finite inputs. G1 convergence of isolation widths. G2 Wilkinson-like and minimax/spectral benchmark families. G3 affine-domain, basis-conversion, coefficient rescaling, factor permutation, differentiation/integration, and equivalent-representation metamorphics. G4 cancellation and budget exhaustion at every subdivision/eigensolve boundary with retained partial state and no false Complete. G5 deterministic replay and two-ISA evidence. Certifier-of-certifier checks use independent high-precision/counting oracles; mutation tests remove exclusion/count/metadata propagation logic and deliberately misuse discovery as certification. Logs bind path kind, coefficients, domain/units, normalization, budgets/consumption, boxes examined, clusters/counts/residuals, uncovered regions, stopping/authority state, algorithm/theorem versions, and verifier artifacts.

POLYNOMIAL AND DOMAIN TRUTH STATES: Classify the admitted polynomial before root search. A proven zero polynomial returns IdenticallyZero or WholeDomainRoots for the declared real interval or complex region; it is never represented as an empty or finite cluster list. A proven nonzero constant returns NoRoots. Coefficients whose uncertainty prevents deciding a degree drop or zero polynomial return IndeterminatePolynomialClass. Preserve the proof basis for classification.

COUNT VERSUS MULTIPLICITY: Distinguish distinct-root count from total algebraic multiplicity. Claim exact multiplicity only when coefficient representation and algorithm support an exact witness, such as exact dyadic or rational algebra, validated square-free/GCD or subresultant structure, or another independently checked theorem. Floating or interval-uncertain coefficients generally return lower/upper count and multiplicity bounds or Unknown, not a guessed integer. A cluster may have exact total root count while individual multiplicities remain unresolved. Repeated, nearly repeated, and unresolved clusters retain set-valued semantics.

REAL VERSUS COMPLEX COMPLETENESS: Parameterize completeness by explicit RootDomain: a real interval with endpoint policy, or a bounded complex region with boundary policy. CompleteReal says nothing about non-real roots; CompleteComplex says nothing outside its admitted region. Complex-conjugate pairing is available only for certified-real coefficients. Boxes or discs touching a domain boundary or each other require explicit overlap and allocation rules and cannot be double-counted or silently discarded. Physical-domain affine mapping conservatively preserves enclosure, count, boundary inclusion, units, and truth state.

REAL NO-MOCK E2E: Build Chebyshev objects through public constructors, serialize/package them, run actual discovery, colleague, and interval-certification paths, persist the full report, and replay it through an independent checker. Include identically zero, nonzero constant, simple real, repeated real, endpoint, tightly clustered, complex-conjugate, real-completeness-only, and exhausted-budget cases. Verify that only an intended typed projection reaches a downstream solver and no list-only adapter launders Partial or Unknown into Complete. Retain detailed logs of coefficient representation, polynomial classification, domain kind, cluster count and multiplicity authority, coverage tree, uncovered region, and checker identity.

title: fs-opt: seal the typed IR and validate all graph/leaf authority
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs-opt describes a typed, valid-by-construction Problem, while CONTRACT says every constructor validates parameter ranges, but the invariant is neither enforced nor sealed. Problem publicly exposes mutable vars, exprs, objectives, constraints, tags, and budget vectors, so callers can construct or mutate inconsistent IDs/shapes/metadata without ProblemBuilder. Public shape, node_dims, and class index arbitrary public NodeId values; route/reachable transitively trust public objective, constraint, root, and child IDs. The builder itself also admits invalid authority-bearing leaves: Sphere ambient < 2, Stiefel p > n, unchecked u32 point/tangent arithmetic, non-finite constants, non-finite objective weights and objective weights whose sign semantics are undeclared, invalid/NaN chance probabilities, zero-level multi-fidelity tags, and weak legacy u64 bilevel identities. These values can panic, wrap, manufacture shapes, drive allocation, or reach finish(), serialization, hashes, routing, and solvers despite the contract.

SCOPE: Make Problem an opaque sealed IR with private fields and read-only checked iteration/accessors. Define a single versioned ProblemAdmission validator and typed errors for graph topology/references, ManifoldSpec, leaves, objectives, constraints, tags, budgets, and aggregate limits. Validate semantic constraints and checked dimensions before VarId/NodeId assignment, graph mutation, shape derivation, allocation, serialization, route/reachability, or identity. Specify Rn zero-dimensional policy; Sphere ambient minimum; Stiefel 1 <= p <= n; checked point/tangent formulas and u32-to-usize portability; finite constant policy; an explicit objective-weight contract (prefer finite nonnegative weights because Sense already carries direction, unless a separately justified signed policy is adopted); probability domains; nonzero/capped fidelity levels; full-width typed bilevel identity; names/units; acyclicity/reference validity; aligned metadata-vector lengths; and per-item/aggregate graph/dimension/work/memory caps. Make currently infallible mutators/accessors fallible or require opaque validated IDs/tokens. Ensure programmatic builder, parser/deserializer, migration, generated catalogs, routing, evaluation, and all consumers use the same validator. Rejection must leave intern tables, IDs, budget, and ordering unchanged.

ACCEPTANCE: No public safe API can create or mutate an invalid Problem, index an unknown ID, or bypass admission. No invalid manifold, constant, objective, constraint, tag, graph edge, or identity can be hashed as an admitted study, produce a Shape, allocate, route, or reach a solver. Dimension arithmetic is checked and correct for every admitted case. finish authority is either genuinely preserved by construction or becomes fallible with a complete validation report. Repeated rejection/retry is deterministic and ID-stable. Historical invalid bytes remain inspectable only as quarantined legacy artifacts with no execution/certificate authority.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 table/property tests cover arbitrary IDs and graph-reference corruption; metadata-vector misalignment; cycles; Sphere ambient 0/1/2/MAX; Stiefel n/p boundaries, p>n and overflow; Rn policy; checked tangent formulas; non-finite/extreme constants and weights; negative-weight behavior under the chosen explicit policy; probability endpoints/NaN; zero/MAX fidelity levels; typed bilevel identities; aggregate caps; builder rollback; and deterministic error ordering. Compile-fail/API tests prove direct Problem mutation/construction is unavailable. G3 programmatic-vs-wire parity, serialization round trip, equivalent valid graphs, units/names, and route/reachability invariance. G4 adversarial graph/dimension/allocation/metadata storms, budget exhaustion, cancellation at validation boundaries, and no partial builder mutation. G5 exact replay. Mutation tests remove every range/reference/finiteness/checked-arithmetic guard. A no-mock E2E parses, builds, routes, solves, serializes, and replays valid sphere/Stiefel/stochastic/bilevel problems while invalid variants fail before graph authority. Structured logs retain source/problem identity, metadata kind/value class, manifold parameters, graph counts, checked dimensions, caps/consumption, validator/schema version, refusal/ranked repair, and explicit no-claim state.

IDENTITY OUTPUT: Successful common ProblemAdmission produces a ProblemSemanticId over normalized admitted meaning. Programmatic construction does not manufacture a WireContentId; that identity exists only after canonical wire serialization under the v3 schema. APIs, tests, receipts, and logs use the domain-separated types and refuse implicit conversion.

title: fs-opt wire v3: split wire-content and problem-semantic identities, add trust anchors, and bound parsing
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs-opt v2 overloads FNV-1a 64 as canonical body hash, study identity, parser source hash, migration anchor, and bilevel reference. FNV is neither collision-resistant nor domain-separated, so distinct studies can alias under current APIs. Parsing is also not total: it lacks aggregate byte, line, directive, variable, node, token, decoded-string, heap, work, depth, deadline, and cancellation budgets, allocates complete line and token vectors, and builds graph state before final canonicality verification. A self-hash establishes content consistency only; it does not authenticate bytes against a writer who can replace both body and digest.

THREE DISTINCT IDENTITIES: Define SourceByteId for exact untrusted bytes received, WireContentId for the canonical schema-versioned v3 wire artifact, and ProblemSemanticId for the admitted typed optimization problem's normalized meaning. These types are domain-separated and non-interchangeable. If v3 accepts only canonical bytes, noncanonical input refuses with a ranked canonicalization remedy. If compatibility parsing accepts alternate presentation, retain SourceByteId, emit a normalization receipt, and compute WireContentId only over canonical re-emission. Programmatic construction produces ProblemSemanticId but no WireContentId until serialization. Parsed and programmatically constructed semantically identical admitted problems yield the same ProblemSemanticId; canonical serialization of either yields the same WireContentId.

REFERENCE SEMANTICS: Packages, caches, exact replay, signatures, and byte-level migration receipts use WireContentId or SourceByteId as appropriate. Bilevel logical references, study deduplication, and semantic graph identity use ProblemSemanticId plus required schema and authority context. A migration receipt binds old SourceByteId or legacy FNV lookup, new canonical WireContentId, new ProblemSemanticId, exact normalization or migration rule, verifier identity, and external trust anchor. Different wire versions may intentionally have different WireContentIds while sharing a proven ProblemSemanticId. No equality or widening conversion between identities is implicit.

TOTAL PARSING: Stream or preflight under explicit byte, line, directive, variable, node, token, decoded-string, aggregate heap/work/depth, deadline, and cancellation budgets. Authenticate schema and enforce caps before graph mutation or large allocation; compute SourceByteId incrementally, validate canonical bytes, and couple parsing to the sealed transactional builder from frankensim-sj31i.48 so error or cancellation rolls back IDs, interning, work accounting, and authority. Preserve v1/v2 FNV only as non-authoritative historical lookup/crosswalk evidence; no silent rewrite, u64 widening, or width truncation.

AUTHORITY: None of SourceByteId, WireContentId, or ProblemSemanticId authenticates its own claims. Expected IDs, signatures, ledger/Merkle roots, attested snapshots, or other independently admitted anchors remain separate AuthorityRef data. Generic parsing returns admitted content with explicitly Unanchored authority. Same-ID/different-preimage adjudication preserves all source, canonical, and semantic encodings and fails closed. Domain/schema confusion, downgrade, and authority-changing ambient context refuse.

ACCEPTANCE: Programmatic and parsed construction yield one ProblemSemanticId only after common ProblemAdmission validation. Canonical serialization yields one WireContentId; exact source-byte replay retains SourceByteId. Whitespace or presentation changes, canonical version changes, semantic normalization, default insertion, and graph-equivalent construction affect exactly the intended identities and no others. Maximum memory/work is derivable from budgets and enforced before breach. Cancellation drains without publishing a Problem, migration authority, or anchored receipt. Current consumers reject bare legacy u64 where a typed identity or AuthorityRef is required.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 unit/property/fuzz tests cover every cap at n-1/n/n+1, huge lines/tokens/escapes, integer boundaries, collision/downgrade/confusion attempts, duplicate/unknown directives, byte and UTF-8 policy, CR/LF variants, transactional rollback, identity domain separation, and exact canonical round trips. Synthetic same-ID/different-byte adjudication and independently anchored migration verification fail closed. G3 proves programmatic/wire and v1/v2/v3 semantic crosswalks. G4 exercises allocation/cancellation storms and fault injection around parser, builder, normalization, trust-anchor, and publication phases. G5 records two-ISA deterministic identities. Mutation tests restore FNV authority, conflate identity types, or remove caps and anchors. A no-mock E2E carries a v3 problem through builder, canonical serialization, package, ledger, bilevel semantic reference, expected-root or signed replay, and unanchored parse. Bounded schema-versioned logs retain identity types, legacy lookup, trust-anchor/verifier state, budgets and consumption, parser phase, graph counts, migration rule, cancellation/finalization, authority/no-claim, and artifact path without echoing unbounded or secret input.

title: fs-voi: include every plausible alternative in EVPI robustness
description: ROOT CAUSE: EVPI uses only the two lowest posterior means. A third alternative with worse mean but large uncertainty may have material probability of being optimal while global EVPI is reported near zero and decision_robust=true. Mean ordering is not stochastic dominance. SCOPE: compute full multi-alternative expected opportunity loss, or produce certified exclusion bounds for every omitted alternative; if only a surrogate is available, rename it and forbid global robustness. TESTS: high-variance third-candidate falsifier, correlated alternatives, permutation invariance, dominance exclusions, Monte Carlo/oracle comparison with confidence bounds, and deterministic seeds. ACCEPTANCE: global robustness is impossible unless all alternatives are included or soundly excluded with retained evidence.
close_reason: Complete at 11329ad (pushed) with live green evidence. fs-voi EVPI_SEMANTICS_VERSION 1->2: expected_opportunity_loss{,_by} computes the FULL multi-alternative E[best - min] via deterministic survival-product quadrature (12-sigma truncation, fixed 256-panel Simpson, allocation-free); the old evpi{,_by} RENAMED top_two_evpi_surrogate{,_by} per SCOPE with robustness-gating forbidden (recommend()'s STOP gate is the full evaluator). Numeric falsifier fixed: total_std and pairwise deviation sums are overflow-safe scaled norms — finite near-sqrt(MAX) components compose representably. TESTS delivered (fs-voi 20/20): high-variance third-candidate falsifier (surrogate ~0, full material, robust STOP impossible), two-design closed-form agreement, full>=surrogate dominance incl. three-way-tie order-statistic constant, permutation invariance, dominance exclusions, seeded deterministic Monte Carlo oracle within confidence bounds, MAX/subnormal/metamorphic scale tests incl. BITWISE power-of-two equivariance. Consumers migrated coherently: fs-oed-e2e (planning policy v4, byte policy v2, gate+trace+action-valuation share ONE full algebra; demo now EARNS robustness by exclusion-certifying C and D, final EOL 0.0099; pins recomputed live; 33/33) and fs-schedule-e2e (robustness gate + retained evpi full; estimator label v2; 6/6); fs-wasm check Finished. ACCEPTANCE met within the crate's declared independent-Gaussian model: every alternative is INCLUDED (no exclusion machinery needed), and no surrogate can claim global robustness. Honest boundaries documented in CONTRACT: the quadrature is Estimated (not a certified enclosure; multi-scale menus resolve at the coarsest window scale), and correlated/heavy-tailed objectives remain the declared no-claim refinement they were in v1. Unblocks sj31i.32 and sj31i.4 (action-valuation science upgrade builds on the now-shared full algebra).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Additional fresh-eyes numeric falsifier: Uncertainty::total_std squares finite standard deviations naively and pairwise EVPI/ranking then squares those totals again. Two finite near-sqrt(MAX) uncertainties can overflow the variance sum even though the correct combined standard deviation is representable via scaled hypot; action pre-posterior mean-shift arithmetic similarly forms prior_std^2 - posterior_std^2. The full-EVPI fix must use scaled norm/difference formulas (or covariance-factor algebra), refuse only mathematically unrepresentable outputs, and retain MAX/subnormal/metamorphic scale tests so finite admissible beliefs do not become false NonFiniteComputation results.

The wrapper now canonicalizes estimates by unique candidate identity before every current approximate EVPI evaluation and retains a multicandidate permutation regression. This is only a determinism repair: it does not satisfy this bead's full multi-alternative EVPI acceptance and must not be mistaken for closing the scientific approximation gap.

title: EPIC: total, source-distribution-safe constellation admission and publication
description:
PURPOSE: Coordinate the complete fail-closed constellation admission and publication program. The current bootstrap, xtask, shell, DSR, and RCH paths can diverge in path authority, child-process bounds, source-distribution identity, environment policy, and publication semantics. This epic is an umbrella only: executable estimates and acceptance live in its children, and it cannot close until every child is complete and the real entrypoint-convergence E2E passes.

PROGRAM INVARIANTS: Every authoritative entrypoint consumes one versioned typed AdmissionContext, admitted descriptor-bound path and repository capabilities, a bounded child-process supervisor, a scrubbed executable/environment/Git/network policy, a collision-resistant source-distribution receipt independent of ambient .git, and generation-checked durable publication. Diagnostic or unanchored evidence remains useful but never silently gains authority. Cancellation is request, drain, finalize. Failure or source drift publishes nothing. All state, budgets, identities, authority references, and ranked remedies are bounded and replayable.

CHILDREN: (A) admission state machine and budgets; (C) process supervisor; (D) path/repository capabilities; (E) execution security and network authority; (F) publication transaction; (B) source-distribution authority; and (G) entrypoint convergence and no-mock release-path evidence. Parent status never substitutes for child proof.

title: Constellation admission core: typed AdmissionContext, state machine, budgets, and truth semantics
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Entry points currently infer authority from booleans, omitted fields, ambient configuration, or ad hoc sequencing. Define the single versioned AdmissionContext and sealed state machine consumed by xtask, standalone bootstrap, shell adapters, snapshot and verify-only paths, DSR, and RCH.

SCOPE: Bind command class, offline or fetch authority, Cx, deadline, work, memory, process, file, output, network, and retry budgets, path and executable capability slots, trust-anchor state, deterministic event ordering, cancellation request-drain-finalize state, and publication authority. Model Diagnostic, Unanchored, Admitted, Refused, Cancelled, and Indeterminate as explicit non-interchangeable states; no Boolean, default, or missing field implies authority. Seal transitions so an entrypoint cannot skip preflight, stability recheck, drain, or finalization. Errors are structured, bounded, deterministic, and provide ranked remedies.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Every legal transition is total and every illegal transition is refused before mutation. Caps are checked before work or allocation; repeated retry is identity-stable. G0 unit/property/API tests cover all states, n-1/n/n+1 cap boundaries, invalid transition permutations, deterministic ordering, rollback, serialization, and unknown schema. G4 injects cancellation and faults at every transition and proves bounded drain with no partial authority. G5 replays across entrypoints and workers. Mutation tests kill every state guard. Logs retain schema, state transitions, capability identities, budgets and consumption, cancellation/drain/finalization, authority/no-claim, and ranked remedy without secrets.

title: Constellation process supervisor: bounded spawn, cancellation, output caps, and kill-tree drain
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Authoritative paths use process APIs that can wait indefinitely, retain unbounded output, leak descendants, and outlive cancellation. Implement one bounded child-process supervisor for Git and every external bootstrap or verification action.

SCOPE: Spawn only through an admitted AdmissionContext. Stream bounded stdout and stderr, enforce per-stream and combined caps, deadlines, process and descendant counts, retries, cancellation, escalation, kill-and-drain, and deterministic output/event ordering. Define supported-platform descendant containment and explicit degraded or refused semantics where containment cannot be established. Model exit, signal, timeout, output truncation, spawn refusal, cancellation, and drain failure as typed states. No authoritative path retains Command::output, unbounded subprocess execution, or orphanable children.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Real no-mock tests launch hangs, output floods, forked descendants, ignored termination, stalled fetches, malformed output, cancellation races, and caps at n-1/n/n+1. Every child and descendant is reaped or authority is refused with a retained containment failure; logs stay bounded and secrets are redacted. G4 fault-injects spawn/read/kill/wait/drain. G5 proves deterministic event ordering. Mutation tests restore an unbounded wait or drop a descendant/output guard. Receipts bind executable, command class, caps/consumption, exit/timeout/kill/drain state, and verifier identity.

title: Constellation path and repository admission: descriptor-bound roots, ownership, and swap defense
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Canonicalized strings and lexical containment do not survive symlink, hardlink, mount, repository, or pathname replacement races. Admit workspace, repository, sibling, source, destination, and publication locations as descriptor-bound capabilities.

SCOPE: Verify containment, filesystem and repository identity, ownership, mode, symlink/hardlink/mount aliases, nested repository and submodule boundaries, destination overlap, and before/after stability before mutation or authority. Detect repository replacement and path ABA even when a pathname or content spelling returns to an earlier value. Bind descriptor identity and generation into downstream receipts. Define explicit per-platform guarantees and refuse authority when the required descriptor semantics are unavailable.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Relative, Unicode, and control-character paths; symlink/hardlink swaps; mount and repository replacement; hostile ownership/modes; overlapping destinations; nested repos/submodules; archive roots; concurrent replacement; and cancellation all fail before mutation unless explicitly admitted. G3 relocation and equivalent-path metamorphics preserve semantic source identity without conflating capabilities. G4 injects swaps at every check/use boundary. Mutation tests remove each identity, ownership, containment, or stability check. Bounded logs retain descriptor identities and states, not merely path strings.

title: Constellation execution security: pinned executables, scrubbed environment, Git policy, and network authority
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Ambient PATH, environment, Git configuration, hooks, credentials, proxies, and network access can alter source or verification semantics without appearing in current receipts. Define one executable and ambient-authority policy used by every supervised process.

SCOPE: Bind approved executable path plus descriptor/content identity and version, invocation class, explicit cwd, scrubbed allowlisted environment, Git config and object format, credential/helper and hook policy, offline/fetch/network permission, redirect and proxy behavior, and trust source. Reject executable replacement, PATH aliasing, environment or Git-config injection, hooks, unsafe ownership, unexpected network access, and authority-changing inherited state. Secrets are never logged, placed in public hashes, or included in diagnostic excerpts.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Unit and real-process tests exercise executable swaps, PATH/config/env injection, hooks, credential helpers, proxies, offline violations, redirects, network stalls, and unknown executable versions with bounded ranked refusal. G4 cancels each external phase and verifies drain. G5 replays the admitted policy deterministically. Mutation tests remove pinning, scrubbing, network, or secret-redaction guards. Receipts bind the public policy and executable identity while recording only secret references or redacted classes.

title: Constellation publication transaction: generation-checked CAS, durable fsync, and ABA-safe receipts
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Pathname rename into a mutable parent is not sufficient atomic authority: the parent, destination, or prior generation can change, ABA can restore old-looking state, and success may be reported before durable persistence. Implement a descriptor-bound publication transaction.

SCOPE: Admit parent and target capabilities; create bounded temporary artifacts in the admitted destination domain; bind exact bytes and semantic identity; fsync content and required metadata; compare-and-swap expected parent identity, target absence or expected prior identity, and generation; publish with no-clobber or explicitly versioned replacement semantics; fsync the authoritative directory; then emit a receipt. Recheck source and destination capabilities before and after. Cancellation or any validate/write/fsync/CAS/rename/receipt fault removes no pre-existing artifact and grants no authority. Idempotent deduplication requires identical content plus identical authority context.

ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: Fault injection at every byte write, fsync, metadata update, CAS, rename, directory sync, and receipt step proves no partial authoritative state. Concurrent identical, disjoint, stale, conflicting, ABA, parent-replaced, and target-replaced writers have deterministic outcomes with no lost update. Cross-filesystem or unsupported atomicity refuses or uses a separately proved protocol. Mutation tests kill each generation/durability guard. Logs bind expected/observed generations, descriptor identities, content roots, durability steps, outcome, and verifier.

title: Constellation source authority: pre-Cargo, Git-independent closure and lockstep cleanliness
description:
ROOT CAUSE: Build identity and verification currently depend on ambient .git and divergent consumers of constellation.lock, submodule, dirty-tree, archive, and source-closure semantics. That breaks exported source distributions and can admit different trees under superficially similar roots.

SCOPE: Remove or demote duplicate authority logic to thin adapters. ACCEPTANCE AND TESTS: A real no-mock E2E starts from both clean clone and verified archive, exercises xtask, standalone bootstrap, shell adapter, snapshot, verify-only, DSR quality/build handoff, and narrow RCH build handoff, then independently replays package and receipts. Every entrypoint produces the same typed outcome and bounded diagnostic class for the same admitted context. No adapter can bypass caps or authority. G5 compares deterministic event and receipt identities; mutation tests reintroduce each bypass. title: fs-opt eval/descent: validate runtime bindings and make execution total
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs-opt public evaluation and descent assume that caller-provided runtime state matches the admitted graph. eval indexes memo by public NodeId before validating bounds; Expr::Var clones a binding without checking the variable manifold point_dim; Component directly indexes runtime vectors; vector add/sub/dot use zip and silently truncate mismatched shapes. descend_fn does not validate x0 length or DescentOptions, and SO3/Stiefel retractions index x/t directly while Sphere/Rn zip may silently shorten. Malformed bindings can therefore panic, compute a different-dimensional objective without refusal, or corrupt optimization semantics. The evaluation budget is also not a hard envelope: when a finite limit is selected, mandatory initial/final evaluations can exceed max_evals. The current max_evals == 0 spelling means Unlimited and must not be reinterpreted as zero work during repair.

SCOPE: Introduce a validated runtime BindingFrame keyed by VarId with exact manifold point shapes, units, finiteness, uniqueness, and aggregate memory/work caps. Validate public NodeId and every node output against the graph's stored Shape/Dims before indexing or arithmetic; vector operators require exact lengths and checked allocation, never zip-truncate. Define typed EvalError/DescentError with node/variable/path attribution. Validate all DescentOptions (finite/positive step, finite learning rate and closure threshold, iteration/evaluation/memory caps, retraction domain) and x0 before the first evaluation. Thread Cx and explicit cancellation through finite-difference coordinate loops, retractions, line/search iterations, and finalization. Replace the overloaded scalar with an explicit EvalLimit::Unlimited or EvalLimit::Limited(NonZeroU64), migrating max_evals == 0 to Unlimited. Turn finite-limit accounting into an exact ledger that includes f0, derivatives/probes, trial points, acceptance checks, and final evaluation; if a finite budget cannot cover the next atomic step, return a resumable partial report without overshoot.

NUMERICAL AND AUTHORITY BOUNDARY: Retractions must return typed set-valued/indeterminate/refused states at singular or invalid points rather than normalize zero, index short storage, or fabricate a manifold point. A finite objective alone is not convergence, feasibility, or stationarity authority. Reports must distinguish completed, budget-exhausted, cancelled/drained, numerical-domain failure, and invalid-input states, and must never publish a final optimum from a partial mandatory step.

ACCEPTANCE: Unknown nodes, missing bindings, unknown or duplicate VarId bindings, short/long/non-finite values, malformed intermediate shapes, invalid x0/options, singular retractions, and insufficient max_evals all fail before unsafe indexing or semantic truncation. Every vector result has the declared exact shape. Budget consumption never exceeds the declared maximum. Cancellation latency is bounded and leaves no partial authoritative output. Valid callers retain deterministic behavior and receive explicit evaluation/iteration accounting.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 unit/property tests cover every public NodeId boundary, binding cardinality and shape, component index, vector op mismatch, all manifold storage shapes, zero/NaN/Inf/extreme fd_h/lr/closure/options, Unlimited and finite max_evals 1/exact/one-short, and checked output shape/dims. G1 manufactured objectives verify descent and budget/order. G3 equivalent binding order, unit-rescaled problems, manifold chart/retraction equivalence, and finite-difference step transformations. G4 cancellation inside every coordinate/iteration/retraction/finalization boundary, panic/fault injection, cap exhaustion, resume equivalence, and no leak. G5 replay across thread counts. Mutation tests restore direct indexing, zip truncation, or budget overshoot. A no-mock E2E exercises programmatic and wire-built problems through eval, descent, cancellation/resume, ledger report, and checker. Logs retain problem/runtime identities, node/variable/path, shapes/units, options, explicit Unlimited-or-Limited mode and exact finite budget ledger, cancellation/drain/finalization, stopping/no-claim state, and bounded diagnostics.

title: EPIC: typed strong identities, canonical encoding, and explicit authority migration
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: fs_evidence::ProvenanceHash is a public u64 FNV-1a accumulator used as evidence provenance across the project. FNV is collision-prone, lacks robust domain/schema separation, and cannot safely bind scientific evidence trees, conversion receipts, merge outcomes, sampled geometry evidence, optimization studies, or migration crosswalks. Local replacements in fs-opt, fs-geom, bootstrap, or packages would create incompatible hash dialects and leave the central Evidence<T> carrier weak. Separately, a self-computed unkeyed digest is content identity/corruption evidence, not authenticity: anyone who may rewrite bytes can recompute it.

SCOPE: Replace ProvenanceHash authority with one shared typed 32-byte identity substrate built on the existing fs-blake3 mode-separated hash_domain implementation and official-vector evidence. Define non-interchangeable types and domains for raw artifact ContentId, schema/domain-specific semantic identities, ordered evidence-composition nodes, source/model/checker identities, and externally anchored AuthorityRef or SignedEnvelope. Use length-delimited canonical preimages, explicit version/domain/context, exact field order, optional/presence tags, and role-specific domains. Preserve legacy FNV only in a quarantined LegacyProvenanceV1 field/crosswalk; never widen u64 and call it strong. Audit all Evidence, Certified, geometry/sheaf, router, merge, fs-opt, bootstrap, ledger, package/checker, generated catalog, cache, serialization, and equality/order consumers. Provide deterministic database/wire schema migration and dual-root receipts anchored to exact old/new bytes plus verifier/schema identity.

AUTHORITY MODEL: Generic construction/parsing computes and returns a ContentId but grants no external trust. Tamper/refusal authority requires a caller-supplied trusted expected ContentId, ledger/Merkle root, signature/MAC, attested source snapshot, or other declared anchor. A changed artifact with a recomputed digest is distinct untrusted content, not generically detectable tampering. Collision resistance is an explicit cryptographic assumption; on any observed same-ID/different-byte event, preserve both byte roots and fail closed for adjudication. Migration receipts authorize a semantic crosswalk only when their verifier/schema and trust anchor are independently admitted.

ACCEPTANCE: No current authoritative API accepts bare ProvenanceHash/u64/FNV where a strong typed identity or trust anchor is required. Every semantic domain and version is non-confusable and mutation-sensitive for every declared field; excluded fields are documented/tested. Parsing/content hashing never claims authenticity. Legacy evidence remains inspectable and crosswalkable without laundering. All migrated consumers derive identical shared identities and cannot accidentally mix artifact, semantic, signature, or authority domains.

TESTS AND LOGGING: Official and independent BLAKE3/derive-key vectors; G0 canonical encoding/composition/field-order/presence/domain/version laws; mutation tests for every semantic and excluded field; same bytes/different domain and raw-vs-domain non-equivalence; legacy crosswalk exact-byte tests; parser width/version/downgrade/truncation cases; recomputed self-hash accepted only as a different untrusted ContentId and refused by expected-ID/signed-root APIs; synthetic collision-adjudication path; schema/database migration, rollback, concurrent readers/writers, and cancellation. G3 equivalent construction/serialization and cross-crate identity parity. G4 bounded hostile input and partial migration faults. G5 two-ISA replay. A no-mock E2E carries evidence from producer through ledger/package/checker/replay with both unanchored and anchored trust states. Logs retain bounded legacy/current content identities, semantic domain/version, anchor/verifier/signature state, migration rule, authority/no-claim state, budgets, and artifacts without presenting hashes as authentication.
notes: UMBRELLA SEMANTICS: This record coordinates the typed-identity migration but is not itself a blocking implementation leaf. Consumers depend on the narrow child that supplies their prerequisite. Close this epic only after every descendant and the global enforcement gate are closed; do not add a reverse blocking edge from this parent to a child because the parent-child relation already owns hierarchy.

title: Identity core: non-confusable typed IDs, canonical preimages, and authority separation
description: ROOT CAUSE: FNV and ad hoc byte layouts currently conflate raw-byte identity, semantic equivalence, and external authority. title: fs-blake3: fallible allocation-free ordered-row canonical streaming
description:
## Root cause and user impact
CanonicalEncoder can stream already-materialized borrowed rows, but large producers must first build Vec<Vec<u8>>. A legal million-incidence causal graph therefore allocates millions of row buffers and roughly half a gigabyte of retained temporary payload before the encoder sees it. Canonical byte caps do not bound actual peak memory, allocator failure can abort the process, and cancellation cannot interrupt individual row construction. This violates the identity-core hostile-length and no-partial-publication contract.

## Technical approach
Add an allocation-free, fallible ordered-row streaming API to fs-blake3 CanonicalEncoder. The caller declares collection cardinality and each row length before bytes are written. An encoder-owned bounded row sink writes the canonical length frame and absorbs chunks directly into the transactional digest/preimage state. It must fail closed on length underflow/overflow, producer error after partial absorption, field/frame/item limit overflow, arithmetic/layout overflow, and cancellation at row, chunk, and final-publication boundaries. Producer failure consumes or permanently poisons the encoder so a partial identity cannot be finished. Keep ordered_bytes for already-materialized slices. fs-blake3 must remain independent of fs-exec/fs-alloc; expose generic fallible/cancellation closures and typed producer errors.

## Invariants and compatibility
For identical rows, the new API must emit byte-for-byte identical canonical frames, schema IDs, typed IDs, preimage roots, counters, and adjudication metadata as ordered_bytes. Existing public domains and schemas do not move. Declared cardinality, encoded cardinality, and collection_items must agree exactly. No callback may retain a mutable sink beyond its row. Safe Rust only.

## Tests and evidence
G0 parity for empty, singleton, variable-length, nested child, and maximum legal rows; exact underwrite/overwrite and wrong-count refusals; producer error before and after partial absorption; arithmetic and limit boundaries. G3 compare both APIs field-by-field and against an independent canonical-frame parser. G4 cancel at every row/chunk/publication checkpoint and prove no finishable partial identity or leaked state. G5 deterministic receipts across row chunking and callback schedules. Add detailed structured test diagnostics naming schema, field, row, declared/written bytes, counters, limit, cancellation phase, and disposition. Update fs-blake3 CONTRACT.md and owner identity declaration if implementation closure changes; run central batch proof before closure.

## No-claim boundary
This leaf bounds encoder-owned streaming state. Consumer-side graph indexes, sorting workspaces, and operation-memory leases are owned by the dependent I02 resource-closure leaf.
