title: Typed snapshot freeze transaction: bind drained executor run to one immutable solver state
description: ROOT CAUSE: DrainFinalizeReport proves that cancellation was requested and all registered worker guards drained for a caller-selected logical run, but its semantic identity contains only version/run/worker counts. A caller can reproduce that report with another tracker, pair it with arbitrary pause-request and gate-generation labels, and seal an S value at a later time. Snapshot v2 therefore has honest caller-relative consistency today, not proof that the serialized state was atomically frozen by the session owning the paused run. GOAL: introduce a typed, non-copyable snapshot freeze transaction spanning fs-exec and fs-session. The session owner initiates one pause request, binds an owner/session/solver-instance generation, closes mutation admission, drains the exact run, freezes or immutably commits the exact solver state/configuration, and receives a single-use SnapshotFreezePermit<S> (or equivalent linear token) carrying the drain report, pause/gate/session identities, state commitment, remaining/consumed budgets, RNG cursor, and finalization-scope budget. Sealing must consume or irreversibly burn that permit; panic, cancellation, encode refusal, or publication failure poisons/burns it and cannot silently permit a second state. Header declarations remain replayable data and can never reconstruct the permit. The ledger records a predecessor-bound freeze receipt before any resume activation. ACCEPTANCE: no public constructor can pair a report with unrelated pause/generation/state; no TOCTOU mutation exists between freeze commitment and encoding; cross-type/session/run/generation/state substitution fails closed; duplicate, stale, copied, replayed, panic-unwound, and cancelled permits cannot publish; exact retry policy is explicit and idempotency-bound; the resulting artifact/receipt states precisely whether bytes were prepared, committed, or activated. If Rust ownership cannot express a required cross-crate transition directly, use a private owner-held registry nonce/capability with burn-before-call and panic poison rather than a copyable boolean or digest-only token. TESTS/LOGGING: G0 typestate laws and compile-fail misuse fixtures; G3 mutation/substitution/metamorphic tests; G4 real executor cancellation/drain/freeze/seal storms, panic injection at every transaction boundary, concurrent seal races, stale-generation and crash-recovery tests; no-mock fs-exec -> fs-ledger -> fs-session script with deterministic structured logs for request, gate, drain, freeze commitment, permit burn, artifact publication, recovery, and activation. NO-CLAIM: until this task lands, DrainFinalizeReport plus caller labels does not prove atomic checkpoint provenance or association with a particular solver state.

title: Snapshot v2 semantic fork lineage with budget and RNG partition proofs

GOAL: add fork_v2 consuming a prepared/admitted parent and an explicit ForkPlan binding parent content/resume IDs, child ordinal, child provenance, budget partition, deterministic RNG substream derivation, solver/context identity, and pause boundary. Produce child sealed snapshot plus a typed lineage receipt; distinguish exact byte clone from semantic branch fork and make ordinal/idempotency/collision rules explicit. No branch activates without normal prepare-resume gates. TESTS/LOGGING: deterministic repeated fork, distinct ordinals, parent substitution, budget over-allocation, RNG overlap/non-overlap, cancellation/fault rollback, lineage traversal/GC, byte-clone versus semantic-fork distinction, thread-count invariance, and no-mock ledger/session branch replay.

TESTS/LOGGING: forged completion tags/reports, resumable/finalized type confusion, wrong result schema/context, cancellation during final publication, duplicate completion, crash recovery, deterministic golden bytes, and no-mock solver-to-ledger result replay. NO-CLAIM: do not infer scientific correctness from executor completion or policy admission.

Acceptance requires exact DSR/RCH logs, machine fingerprints, artifact paths, zero false certificates, and field-rich failure diagnostics; do not close on compile-only evidence.

title: New-domain semantic identity: units, frames, experiments, calibration, and context of use
description: ROOT CAUSE: Equal numeric payloads are not interchangeable observations when units, frames, state meaning, experiment role, calibration or correlation differ. SCOPE: Integrate the semantic model owned by sj31i.36 with the typed identity and evidence substrate. Bind units and quantity kind, frame, basis/orientation, state schema, model/operator, spatial and temporal support, experiment/dataset/sample/replicate, instrument/calibration, covariance group, data role, blind split and declared context of use. Legitimate unit/basis/frame aliases require canonical transformation receipts. Duplicate records never become independent evidence; training, calibration and holdout roles are identity-bearing. Content identity is not calibration authority. ACCEPTANCE: Equal bits with incompatible semantics diverge or refuse; valid transformations produce verified crosswalks; duplicate-versus-replicate, train/holdout leakage, stale calibration/model, covariance alias and context mismatch are tested. TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 field and type laws, G3 unit/frame/basis transforms, G4 cancellation and hostile metadata, G5 replay, and no-mock as-built to assimilation to OED ledger/checker replay with bounded semantic and trust logs.

Expected-root and signed-root APIs expose anchored and unanchored state. Cache keys bind semantic versions, capabilities, determinism mode, machine/ISA only where contractual, and dependency/source receipts. Bootstrap source identity cannot rely on ambient repository metadata. Catalogs derive declarations from code/contracts and refuse unclassified fields. Unknown versions, domain confusion, stale cache, authority mismatch and recomputed self-digests fail closed without generic tamper claims. ACCEPTANCE: In-memory and portable transports agree only under identical gate context; source drift, wrong dependency receipt, stale capability, changed catalog, cache alias and missing/mismatched anchors are typed. title: fs-blake3 authority: prevent foreign permit-all capabilities from minting promotion trust
description: Current AuthorityVerifier and AuthorityAdmitter are public traits whose only success signal is Result<(), _>. Any downstream PermitAll implementation can therefore drive Presented -> Verified -> Admitted, and fs-spectral converts that admitted value into promotion-capable favorable witnesses. This matches fs-blake3's narrow caller-policy no-claim but contradicts the stronger non-forgeable authority boundary consumed by promotion code. AuthorityRef also retains verifier/key-policy only as parsed digest values, discarding their canonical-preimage observations and preventing same-ID/different-bytes adjudication for authority identities. Acceptance: generic caller checks can produce only an explicitly policy-relative non-promotion result; promotion-capable admission requires an opaque domain-owner decision tied to an independently configured trust root; exact subject receipt/preimage, anchor, verifier receipt/observation, and policy receipt/observation remain bound; foreign PermitAll code cannot mint a promotion witness; verifier/policy namespace and preimage metadata survive bounded audit logging; adversarial and compile-fail tests cover bypass attempts; centralized proof pending.

title: Bind promotion to owner-executed capability decisions
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND EXACT BYPASS
AuthorityRef stores only public verifier and key-policy IDs. Generic verify and admit transitions accept any public AuthorityVerifier or AuthorityAdmitter implementation and return no capability-bound decision receipt. PromotionTrustRoot::admit_for_promotion then re-adjudicates only caller-presented public ByteObservations against its configured observations. A foreign PermitAll can therefore present the OWNER verifier and policy IDs, drive both generic transitions, reuse the OWNER receipts public observations, and receive a PromotionWitness carrying the OWNER charter. Private witness fields do not help because the public root mints the witness. Existing tests use rogue IDs and miss exact-ID capability impersonation.

MISSION
Redesign promotion admission so the root executes or verifies an independently anchored owner capability decision; do not accept a generic policy-relative Admitted value plus caller-supplied observations as sufficient. Bind the actual decision producer, decision transcript, subject, anchor, verifier/policy schemas and observations, context, root charter, capability/code identity, versions, budgets, and final disposition. Identity strings alone are not proof of which code ran.

ACCEPTANCE
- A byte-for-byte regression proves foreign PermitAll with owner IDs and owner observations cannot mint or launder an owner promotion witness.
- The root either owns and invokes immutable verifier/admitter capabilities, consumes a nonforgeable capability-bound receipt, or verifies an externally anchored signature/attestation. Any configuration-relative fallback is nominally typed as non-authoritative and cannot reach promotion consumers.
- Root/witness types and canonical identity distinguish capability implementation/configuration/version, verifier decision, admission decision, and external anchor. Same textual IDs with different code/transcripts refuse.
- No public constructor or caller-selected expected value can convert policy-relative admission into authority. Copy/clone/reconfigure/fork/replay semantics are explicit.
- G0 covers exact-ID spoofing, swapped capabilities, stale/replayed decisions, wrong subject/anchor/context, same-ID different bytes, recomputed unanchored receipts, and downgrade. G3 covers legitimate replay and equivalent owner reconstruction only under an admitted crosswalk. G4 covers panic/cancellation/fault between verify, admit, mint, and publication with no partial witness or leaked capability.
- CONTRACT retracts the current false claim until proven. Central fs-blake3 all-targets/doctests/clippy, identity registry regeneration, fs-spectral consumer tests, and DSR are required before closure.
- Keep code-first slices in progress until consolidated proof; no theorem or security claim may rely on private fields alone.

title: Retain and owner-pin promotion authority in fs-spectral
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND EXACT BYPASS
AdmittedSpectralWitnessV1::from_authority accepts expected_root from its caller. Its own adversarial test demonstrates that a rogue root succeeds when the caller passes rogue_root.charter, so this is comparison against attacker-selected input rather than an owner pin. On success the token stores only promotion.audit; PromotionAuditRecord and canonical witness serialization omit root_charter. Downstream truth/problem admission therefore cannot distinguish owner-pinned from rogue-pinned construction, and the favorable token launders the missing authority axis.

MISSION
Move charter/capability adjudication to a non-caller-controlled spectral owner boundary, retain the actual admitted root/capability authority in every favorable token and audit record, and bind it into canonical witness, proposition, problem, result, ledger, and replay identities. Rotate schemas/domains with explicit legacy quarantine. Integrate the owner-executed fs-blake3 decision from sibling .52.9.1 rather than repackaging generic PolicyRelativeAdmitted.

ACCEPTANCE
- Remove caller-selected expected_root from every authority-bearing constructor. An opaque spectral owner authority or independently supplied trusted anchor performs the comparison.
- AdmittedSpectralWitness retains root charter plus capability/decision receipt; witness_bytes and every downstream favorable identity bind them. PromotionAuditRecord exposes bounded structured authority evidence and no-claim state.
- The exact current rogue-root test must reverse: passing a rogue charter is impossible or refused even when all IDs/context match. Mutating/dropping charter, capability, transcript, version, subject, anchor, schema, observation, or context fails before favorable truth publication.
- Inventory and migrate every constructor, adapter, serializer, cache, ledger, truth validator, and problem/result identity. Legacy v1/v2 artifacts remain inspectable but cannot mint current favorable claims without an anchored crosswalk.
- G0 exact-axis and downgrade matrix; G3 equivalent owner replay plus serialization round trips; G4 fault/cancel between core witness, spectral wrapping, problem admission, and publication with no partial favorable state; G5 deterministic bytes.
- No-mock E2E: foreign PermitAll uses owner IDs and public observations, self-configures a rogue root, and attempts every public path; an innocent consumer with an independently retained spectral owner authority refuses. Legitimate owner flow succeeds and survives ledger/package/replay.
- Central fs-blake3 plus fs-spectral all-targets/doctests/clippy, identity regeneration, downstream union, and DSR proof are required before closure.

title: fs-rep-nurbs refit: typed admitted fields, certified geometry error, and budgeted cancellation
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: The legacy `refit_radial` accepts an arbitrary scalar closure and previously exposed field-residual and Lipschitz quantities with certificate-like names. The current hardened implementation now keeps sampled retained-sign-bracket-target-to-spline evidence, sampled field residual, and geometric probe-spacing estimates separate, refuses non-finite values, and applies fixed safety caps. That is an honest baseline, not the final authority model: the closure carries no units, zero-set identity, Lipschitz witness, metric error bound, continuity class, provenance, or cancellation context; ordinary f64 arithmetic is not outward rounded; radial sampling can miss features; fixed process caps are not caller budgets. A scalar field can be 1-Lipschitz while `abs(f)` is still a lower rather than upper bound on distance to its zero set, so SDF-like naming alone cannot authorize a Hausdorff claim. SCOPE: Introduce a typed admitted implicit-field capability carrying units, domain, zero-set semantics, continuity/Lipschitz evidence, a metric-regularity witness such as `dist(x,Z) <= kappa*abs(f(x))` where applicable, source identity, uncertainty and evaluation budget. Separate signed distance, approximate distance, generic level set, occupancy, and min/max CSG truth states. Thread `Cx` plus explicit evaluation, work, memory, subdivision, error, deadline, and cancellation budgets through projection, assembly, factorization, probing, coverage, and finalization, with bounded poll latency and resumable partial evidence. Replace static-only caps with admitted caller envelopes while retaining hard defensive ceilings. Build continuum directed-distance and Hausdorff certificates only from exhaustive source and fitted-surface coverage, interval or affine/Taylor evaluation, outward-rounded hodograph and field bounds, topology/visibility witnesses, and independently checked metric assumptions. Generalize beyond star-shaped radial domains through certified segmentation and atlas coverage; preserve the radial estimator as a clearly typed low-authority lane. SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY: Sampled fit residual, sampled `abs(f(S))`, geometric probe spacing, unit-Lipschitz regularity, and Hausdorff distance are non-interchangeable quantities. A positive result names the exact zero set, domain, norm, direction, units, theorem assumptions, coverage witness, and arithmetic authority. Unsupported fields, hidden components, tangencies, trims, topology ambiguity, exhausted budgets, non-finite arithmetic, or cancellation return typed Unknown or Refused and never promote estimates. ACCEPTANCE: No generic closure can manufacture geometric authority. Every allocation and evaluation is admitted before use; cancellation drains and publishes no partial certificate. Certified directed distances enclose independent analytic oracles in both directions and combine into Hausdorff authority only when both coverage obligations close. Historical estimate artifacts remain replayable with explicit no-claim semantics and cannot be silently relabeled. TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 unit/property tests cover field-kind and unit mismatches, missing/invalid metric witnesses, center/radius/config boundaries, checked size arithmetic, hidden components, exact SDF versus scaled fields, min/max CSG, extreme and non-finite values, outward-rounding containment, and deterministic ties. G1 manufactured sphere/torus/ellipsoid and multi-patch convergence verifies directed-distance orders. G2 trimmed CAD, thin-feature, non-star-shaped, disconnected, tangent, self-intersecting, and mixed-chart zoos. G3 rigid transforms, parameterization, unit rescaling, chart refinement, equivalent field representation, and route round trips. G4 cancellation and cap exhaustion at every projection/assembly/solve/probe/subdivision/finalization boundary with no leak or partial authority. G5 two-ISA and thread-count replay. Mutation tests remove each assumption, coverage, rounding, budget, and authority guard. A real no-mock E2E runs NURBS to admitted field to refit to continuum checker to ledger/package/checker replay. Bounded schema-versioned logs retain field/source identity, units/domain/norm, assumptions and witnesses, budgets and consumption, sample/subdivision coverage, directed bounds, arithmetic mode, cancellation/drain/finalization, theorem/verifier versions, and explicit authority/no-claim state.

DIRECTED-DISTANCE PRECISION: Treat source-to-spline and spline-to-source obligations as separate exhaustive optimization problems with independently retained coverage trees, witnesses, norms, units, and outward-rounded bounds. Do not infer either direction from field residual or the other direction. A Hausdorff result is the maximum of two admitted directed bounds only when both refer to exactly the same source set, fitted surface, ambient metric, closed-domain policy, and authority context. Include independently checked analytic and adversarial examples where one directed distance is small and the other large.

title: fs-cheb: make construction and transforms budgeted, cancellable, and allocation-total
description: ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: Public Cheb1, Cheb2, Fourier, colleague, and certification entry points accept caller-sized coefficient, degree, grid, rank, or sample counts but often describe work as bounded merely because a scalar maximum exists. A caller can select `usize::MAX`, trigger saturating dimensions that still drive impossible ranges, duplicate very large vectors during error-free summation or normalization, or request unbounded O(n^2)/O(n^3) work without `Cx`, memory admission, cancellation, or resumable state. The new expansion summation correctly preserves finite cancellation residuals but allocates one partial per input term, making the missing resource contract more visible. SCOPE: Define typed construction and transform budgets for input bytes, coefficients, degree, samples, rank, grid cells, temporary scalars, operations, recursion/subdivision, eigen work, wall/deadline, and output evidence. Preflight all checked size and complexity formulas before allocation or function evaluation; reject saturating-size ambiguity rather than iterating it. Thread `Cx` through adaptive sampling, DCTs, low-rank ACA, colleague eigensolves, interval subdivision, algebra, calculus, and robust summation at bounded tile boundaries. Provide resumable partial reports where scientifically meaningful, with explicit Complete/Partial/Cancelled/Refused state; keep lightweight trusted-size wrappers only behind validated tokens. Explore bounded-memory exact or faithfully rounded summation and transform strategies so correctness is not traded away to meet caps. ACCEPTANCE: No safe public input can panic through size arithmetic, OOM by an unadmitted allocation, run beyond declared work, or publish a complete root/function claim after cancellation. Maximum memory and work are derivable before admission. Valid ordinary fixtures retain deterministic semantics; numerically robust cancellation and overflow handling remain intact. TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 n-1/n/n+1 tests for every cap, zero/MAX dimensions, checked products/sums, extreme coefficient exponents, exact cancellation residuals, malformed public objects, and deterministic refusal ordering. G1 adaptive convergence under increasing budgets. G3 equivalent grid refinements, affine domains, coefficient rescaling, separable factorizations, and bounded-memory versus reference summation. G4 cancellation at every sample, DCT tile, ACA rank, eigensolve, subdivision, and finalization boundary; allocator fault injection; no leaks or partial authority. G5 thread-count and two-ISA replay. Mutation tests remove each check and poll. A real no-mock E2E builds, transforms, differentiates, integrates, isolates roots, cancels/resumes, and replays a ledgered function object. Bounded logs retain source/function identity, domain and units, dimensions, budgets and consumption, allocation plan, algorithm path, convergence/stopping state, cancellation/drain/finalization, numeric no-claim reason, and artifact/checker identities.

title: fs-rep-nurbs closest/SDF: restore certified rational-surface distance, sign, and field authority
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: The current NURBS closest-point and NURBS-to-SDF implementation has been correctly downgraded to measured DistanceBracketEstimate and NumericalCertificate::Estimate. Its historical certificate-like result was unsound: HULL_EPS is a fixed heuristic in ordinary f64; rational projection, AABB and norm arithmetic are not outward-rounded; patch-center and dense-grid probes are witnesses rather than exhaustive coverage; trimmed kept regions and trim boundaries are not globally covered; shell orientation does not by itself prove inside/outside sign; finite subdivision caps can leave unsearched boxes. Dense sampling can make the implementation useful, but it cannot authorize an enclosure, Hausdorff claim, exact SDF claim, or global 1-Lipschitz field. Users need the measured lane to remain available while a separate fail-closed certifying lane restores the intended world-class authority.

SCOPE AND MATHEMATICAL DESIGN: Build a typed, per-query rational-surface distance certifier on fs-ivl interval/affine/Taylor arithmetic. Convert each admitted knot span to a canonical homogeneous rational Bezier patch or prove an equivalent partition. Require finite strictly positive weights, bound homogeneous numerators and weight denominator outward, and perform directed interval division; retain all conversion, knot, trim, and arithmetic identities. Use coverage-complete branch-and-bound over compact parameter cells. Lower bounds must enclose distance from the query to every point in each remaining rational patch cell (starting with outward Euclidean control-hull/AABB bounds and admitting sharper convex/Taylor bounds only when checked). Upper bounds must come from an actually evaluated, admitted kept-region point with outward-rounded surface and norm evaluation. Refine with interval Newton/Krawczyk stationary-point tests and boundary/trim solvers without treating their failure as exclusion. Deterministically account for patch interiors, ordinary boundaries, corners, trim curves, trim intersections, degenerate spans, and ties. Termination returns Certified only when the retained global lower and witness upper bounds meet the requested metric error budget; exhaustion, uncertain trim classification, nonpositive weight intervals, nonfinite arithmetic, singular parameterization, or unsupported topology returns typed Unknown/Refused with the best measured evidence kept separate.

SIGN AND FIELD AUTHORITY: Separate unsigned distance enclosure, locally oriented sign estimate, globally certified inside/outside sign, and uniform field-chart authority. A signed result requires an admitted closed-shell topology and orientation receipt plus a coverage-complete, degeneracy-aware winding/ray/parity or equivalent topological predicate whose own interval/exact-predicate assumptions are independently checked. Points on or inseparable from the boundary return a three-valued boundary/Unknown classification. Do not promote pointwise distance queries into a globally certified SDF chart or NumericalCertificate::Enclosure unless a declared spatial domain has exhaustive coverage, a uniform error theorem, continuity and sign obligations, and an independently checked Lipschitz bound. Exact distance is 1-Lipschitz mathematically, but an approximate evaluator does not inherit that claim without a proved uniform evaluator error model. Preserve the current estimated signed/unsigned chart names and Estimate/no-Lipschitz semantics as the low-cost fallback.

EXECUTION, IDENTITY, AND CANCELLATION: Thread explicit Cx and admitted work, evaluation, subdivision, memory, error, deadline, capability, and output budgets through conversion, trim classification, heap/frontier growth, interval evaluation, Newton/Krawczyk, sign classification, checking, and publication. Check all size arithmetic and reserve before allocation; bound queue and transcript growth; poll at deterministic tile/cell boundaries; implement request -> drain -> finalize; never publish partial authority after cancellation or panic. Key deterministic ordering by semantic patch/span/trim-cell identity rather than worker order. Bind source WireContentId, ProblemSemanticId, query/domain/norm/units, orientation/topology/trim receipts, arithmetic mode, tolerances, budgets, algorithm/checker versions, ISA/mode, and all no-claim reasons into content-addressed ledger artifacts. Crosswalk this artifact into the refit directed-distance/Hausdorff successor without conflating the two directions.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: (1) No heuristic epsilon or dense sample can produce Certified authority. (2) Certified point-distance intervals contain independent analytic or high-precision oracles and contract monotonically under admitted refinement. (3) Every kept patch/trim cell contributes a retained coverage/exclusion/witness node so an independent checker can replay the global minimum proof. (4) Signed results are impossible without closed-shell, orientation, and inside/outside receipts; open, self-intersecting, nonmanifold, inconsistently oriented, or uncertain shells remain unsigned/Unknown. (5) The measured legacy lane remains behaviorally available and unmistakably lower-authority. (6) Production and an independently structured checker agree on every retained proof object, while checker disagreement demotes authority rather than averaging results. (7) A real no-mock NURBS -> closest-distance -> signed/unsigned field -> ledger/package -> independent replay pipeline succeeds on admitted fixtures and fails closed on adversaries.

TESTS AND LOGGING: G0 unit/property tests cover homogeneous projection, positive-weight interval division, outward AABB/norm containment, exact point/line/plane/sphere cases, trim polarity, boundary three-valued logic, invalid weights/knots/domains, NaN/infinity/subnormal/extreme scales, deterministic ties, units, and typed authority transitions. G1 manufactured polynomial and rational curves/surfaces verify enclosure and convergence orders, including spheres, cylinders, tori, ellipsoids, and known closest points. G2 canonical trimmed CAD shells, thin gaps, high weight ratios, near-tangent queries, seams, periodic patches, multiple equidistant minima, concavities, disconnected components, and points on the boundary. G3 knot insertion/removal where exact, degree elevation, reparameterization, rigid transforms, unit scaling, patch subdivision, chart order, equivalent trim representation, and tolerance refinement metamorphics. G4 cap exhaustion and cancellation at every conversion/frontier/evaluation/Newton/trim/sign/check/publication boundary, allocation failures, corrupt artifacts, checker faults, no leaks, bounded latency, and no partial certificate. G5 bit-stable deterministic replay across thread counts and both reference ISA families. Add mutation tests that remove every outward-rounding, coverage, trim, topology, sign, identity, budget, and checker guard. Emit bounded schema-versioned structured logs with query/source/domain/norm/units, per-cell bounds and disposition, witnesses, coverage counts, trim/topology/sign receipts, budget consumption, cancellation/drain/finalization, authority transitions, independent-checker result, and artifact paths.

title: P0 NURBS measured lanes: admit validation, allocations, retained bytes, and validate-once caches
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: The hardened KnotVector basis path prices its own live scan, but public NurbsCurve, NurbsSurface, TrimLoop, conversion, closest, SDF, ray, and refit wrappers can still validate mutable structure before operation admission. Caller-mutable knot/control storage permits repeated scans before the advertised cap, and conversion, refit, frontier, and table allocations remain incompletely covered by aggregate retained-byte accounting. This creates denial-of-service, cancellation-latency, stale-validation, and validate-many performance risks.

REPRESENTATION AND TOKEN INVARIANT: Replace publicly mutable representation fields with private sealed storage constructed only through checked constructors and generation-checked mutators, or immutable admitted snapshots. A validation token or admitted view must borrow or otherwise bind the exact immutable generation and cannot outlive or survive mutation. Any mutator performs checked structural admission, advances the generation, and invalidates prior tokens before exposing new state. A content hash may identify bytes for provenance but MUST NOT substitute for structural validation, generation authority, or validate-once safety; there is no recompute-at-every-boundary escape hatch. Safe APIs make stale-token use unrepresentable or return a typed stale-generation refusal.

OWNED PRIMITIVE SUBSTRATE: Introduce a cheap checked structure-work estimator and opaque admitted views for knot vectors, curves, surfaces, trim loops, and Bezier data. Enforce knot/control/degree/table/frontier/output work and aggregate retained bytes before the first full scan or primitive allocation. Reuse one validated generation through basis, evaluation, partials, knot conversion, span boxes, and primitive closest/SDF/refit/ray kernels so nested helpers do not rescan. Replace primitive conversion/refit/frontier/table collect, clone, and capacity growth with checked products and fallible reservation. Expose Cx-aware primitive entry points and typed work, memory, evaluation, subdivision, poll, deadline, capability, and output lease seams while retaining hard defensive ceilings.

ORCHESTRATION OWNERSHIP: This leaf owns sealed representation generations, admitted views, primitive allocation/work estimates, and the cancellation/budget hooks required by consumers. It does not duplicate end-to-end orchestration. ShellSdf query composition, checkpointing, trim/sign traversal, and Chart publication belong to sj31i.59; certified closest/SDF authority belongs to sj31i.57; refit orchestration and field/error authority belong to sj31i.53; render ray isolation, tail exclusion, hit/normal authority, and scene publication belong to sj31i.60. Those leaves must consume this substrate and prove that one caller context and affine budgets traverse their whole workflow.

AUTHORITY BOUNDARY: This leaf proves representation well-formedness and measured-lane primitive execution safety only. It cannot promote heuristic closest, SDF, refit, or ray results to Certified. Keep geometry, topology, distance, sign, convergence, replay identity, and authenticated authority separate.

TESTS AND ACCEPTANCE: No safe public primitive performs an unadmitted full scan, and no primitive allocation occurs before aggregate byte admission. A million-span curve, million-control surface, many tiny loops, huge degree, overflowed products, allocator refusal, stale generation, and mutation during a borrowed admitted view fail deterministically without panic or long preflight. G0 covers empty/min/max forms, checked arithmetic, constructor/mutator invariants, generation invalidation, allocation failure, and deterministic error order. Compile-fail or equivalent API tests prove fields cannot be mutated around validation. G3 covers equivalent knot insertion, degree elevation, reparameterization, and admitted-view versus independent validation. G4 cancels at primitive validation, mutation admission, conversion, allocation, assembly, solve, and probe boundaries with bounded latency and no partial primitive artifact. G5 replays generation and primitive scheduling. A real no-mock curve-to-admitted-Bezier-to-primitive closest/SDF/refit handoff test emits bounded schema-versioned logs for source/generation, structure counts, primitive budgets/consumption, allocation stages, cancellation/drain/finalize, downstream obligation handoffs, and explicit no-claim state.

title: P0 ShellSdfChart: explicit Cx and bounded cancellation through closest, trim, and sign work
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND USER IMPACT: ShellSdf and its Chart adapter can execute expensive Bezier conversion, closest-point subdivision, trim classification, polishing, regular-witness sign fallback, and tile publication without carrying the caller Cx through every nested operation. Static caps cannot honor request cancellation, deadlines, shared quotas, or request-drain-finalize semantics. A renderer or simulation can continue expensive NURBS work after cancellation and may publish an apparently complete sample from a cancelled request.

SCOPE: Define Cx-aware ShellSdf query and Chart evaluation APIs with explicit work, memory, evaluation, subdivision, trim, sign, poll, deadline, capability, and output budgets. Consume the sealed admitted primitive substrate from sj31i.58 and thread one context through conversion, queue/frontier orchestration, exact trim refinement, Gauss-Newton polish, sign witnesses, certificate/no-claim assembly, tile quantization, logging, and publication. Poll at deterministic structure/cell/tile boundaries with a documented maximum latency. Cancellation performs request, drain, then finalize. Diagnostic partial work may be retained only as a typed non-authoritative cancelled artifact, never a completed ChartSample. Keep the current Estimate and no-Lipschitz scientific boundary.

CHECKPOINT AND RESUME AUTHORITY: Choose and document exactly one public policy. Under restart-only semantics, expose no resumable checkpoint authority and return a typed Unsupported or Refused result for resume attempts. Under resumable semantics, define a sealed schema-versioned ShellSdfCheckpoint binding source identity and admitted generation, query/units, algorithm/work/poll/schema versions, deterministic complete frontier state, best witness and trim/sign state, RNG streams if any, execution manifest, consumed/remaining non-reissuable budgets, and authority/no-claim disposition. Resume rejects stale generations, mismatched policies, noncanonical/truncated state, duplicated leases, and replenished budgets. Checkpoint creation/resume are budgeted, cancellable, content-addressed, independently validated, and cannot strengthen uninterrupted authority.

DEPENDENCY INTENT: Implement after sj31i.58 so orchestration cannot hide unadmitted primitive scans or allocations. This execution leaf precedes the separate rational-distance/sign certifier.

TESTS AND ACCEPTANCE: Pre-cancel and mid-flight cancellation at conversion, per-patch search, queue split, trim validation, exact subdivision, polish, sign witness, tile storage, and final publication returns typed Cancelled within the declared bound. If resumable semantics are selected, also inject cancellation/faults at checkpoint serialization and resume admission and prove interrupted/resumed output and receipts equal uninterrupted execution. If restart-only is selected, API/type tests prove checkpoint authority is absent and resume requests receive the documented typed refusal without hidden retained state. No leaked task, arena, frontier, lease, or authoritative partial sample; poll/work quotas cannot be reissued. G0 verifies budget units, deterministic boundary order, and the selected policy schema. G3 covers valid resume equivalence or restart-only semantic equivalence. G4 runs cancellation storms, allocator/deadline faults, malformed trim/surface state, and checkpoint mutation/replay attacks when applicable. G5 verifies results, frontier order, identities, and logs. A real no-mock E2E drives renderer Chart evaluation through a trimmed shell and logs source/generation, stage, cell/tile, selected checkpoint policy and identity if any, admitted/consumed/remaining budgets, request/drain/finalize, terminal reason, and no-claim authority.

title: New-domain workflows: enforce admitted deadline, poll, and cost budgets
description: ROOT CAUSE: several workflows hash budget fields into provenance but checkpoint only cancellation or locally consume poll quota; deadline and cost quota are not uniformly enforced. A Budget::ZERO deadline can currently complete successfully. SCOPE: introduce a shared admitted budget accountant tied to the checked work plan; enforce deadline, poll, and cost at deterministic tile boundaries in fs-adjoint, fs-asbuilt, fs-assimilate, and fs-oed-e2e; retain final consumption and refusal reason in evidence. TESTS: exact-boundary and one-below quotas, ZERO, already-expired and mid-run deadlines under a deterministic clock, cancellation precedence, cost exhaustion, replay identity, and no-partial-success receipts. ACCEPTANCE: provenance and runtime enforcement are the same budget contract; exhausted work cannot report success.

ACCEPTANCE MET: provenance and runtime enforcement share the cx.budget() contract; Budget::ZERO can never complete (admission refusal, tested per crate); deadline/poll/cost enforced at deterministic tile boundaries with cancellation precedence; refusals latch (no partial success); final consumption + refusal reason retained in evidence (BudgetConsumption + typed BudgetRefused variants); exact-boundary/one-below/ZERO/expired+mid-run-deadline-under-VirtualClock/cancellation-precedence/cost-exhaustion/replay-identity tests across fs-exec (10 unit) and each crate. Count all setup and finalization work, preserve explicit zero values, use overflow-safe counters and a deterministic test clock, and guarantee cancellation/deadline/cost refusal cannot leave an acceptance-capable partial receipt. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: EXACT FS-ASSIMILATE WORK-PLAN DIAGNOSIS FROM DSR CHECK 4: every failing update attempted planned+1. For state dimension n and observation dimension m, one-observation accounting is: common validation/copy C=n+n^2; update phase U=(3n^3+14n^2+17n+4)/2; belief canonicalization B=(n^3+36n^2+17n)/6. At n=1,m=1 the current planner is net short by one: validation has +4 slack, Joseph update consumes 3 more than planned, PSD/canonicalization consumes 2 more, yielding attempted 302 vs planned 301 in the retained failure. title: P0 fs-render NURBS rays: certified exclusion, caller budgets, and finite typed intersection outcomes
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND CURRENT BASELINE: The legacy ray path now types malformed geometry/settings, resource refusal, cancellation, and bounded Newton exhaustion. Finite scale-safe norms and a dimensionless column-normalized Jacobian prevent parameter-domain or ray-direction scaling from manufacturing convergence or NaN normals, and heuristic exhaustion returns IterationLimit rather than impersonating a miss. The baseline still uses a fixed seed grid, bounded starts and iterations, hard process ceilings, and no coverage-complete exclusion theorem. Result<Option<Hit>> may reserve None only for a proved miss.

SCOPE: Replace fixed legacy admission with caller-owned work, memory, evaluation, iteration, error, poll, deadline, capability, and output budgets plus bounded top-k seed/frontier storage. Reuse the immutable admitted Bezier generation from sj31i.58. Add certified rational-Bezier ray isolation or clipping over every patch/span and trim domain, including boundaries, seams, tangencies, repeated roots, singular parameterizations, and parameter endpoints. Fast Newton remains a witness and refinement accelerator, never exclusion authority.

FINITE AND INFINITE RAY DOMAIN: Every query declares a finite admitted positive-ray interval with units, or separately supplies a checker-recognized tail certificate proving exclusion beyond a finite cutoff. A clean miss requires a coverage-complete exclusion tree over the finite interval plus any required tail certificate. Bounded search over an arbitrarily truncated interval must return a typed interval-local result, never a global miss. If finite extent, compact support, bounding volume, asymptotic behavior, or tail exclusion cannot be certified, return Inconclusive, IterationLimit, or Refused.

HIT AND NORMAL AUTHORITY: A hit retains an independently checkable existence/localization witness for patch/span/trim provenance, world-space point enclosure, positive ray-parameter enclosure, and residual bound. Unique smooth normals are optional stronger evidence, not a universal precondition for geometric intersection. At seams, creases, trim boundaries, singular parameterizations, or other nonsmooth loci, return a typed HitWithNormalCone, HitWithoutUniqueNormal, or equivalent set-valued normal authority. Separate intersection truth from shading/renderability: downstream renderers must explicitly accept a normal policy, choose a conservative set-valued treatment, or refuse the sample, and no arbitrary fallback normal may masquerade as certified geometry.

TESTS AND ACCEPTANCE: Malformed input, invalid configuration, ResourceLimit, WorkLimit, ResourceExhausted, Cancelled, NumericalFailure, Inconclusive, interval-local miss, certified global miss, smooth certified hit, and nonsmooth hit remain distinct. No NaN or infinite hit/normal is constructible. G0 covers finite gates, empty/zero/subnormal/extreme directions, finite interval and tail admission, checked products, allocation failure, singular Jacobians, deterministic ties, exact linear patches, and normal-cone semantics. G1/G2 cover plane, sphere, cylinder, bounded CAD, trimmed/tangent/grazing/multiple-root and seam/crease fixtures. G3 covers knot-domain scaling through at least 1e15, ray-direction scaling through 1e300, rigid transform, unit rescaling, exact knot insertion, patch subdivision, equivalent parameterizations, and finite-cutoff plus tail equivalence. G4 exhausts or cancels every seed, isolation, Newton, checker, tail, and publication boundary with no false miss or hit. G5 replays bit-stably. A no-mock mixed Chart/NURBS/mesh scene proves fail-closed downstream renderability. Logs retain source/generation, patch/span/trim IDs, ray interval and units, tail authority, budgets, isolation cells, residual/conditioning bounds, hit/normal or exclusion disposition, cancellation, checker result, and no-claim state.

title: fs-diffreal-e2e: enforce one non-reissuable invocation budget across nested scientific stages
description:
ROOT CAUSE: stage_as_built_loop passes one Cx through registration, as-built comparison, Belief construction, colored assimilation, and redundant misfit calls, but lower-layer WorkProgress values reconstruct the full ambient poll quota. Outer checkpoints consume no shared allowance. One reported quota can therefore be reissued at each seam, while heterogeneous resource fields are treated as if they shared one counter model.

TYPED BUDGET ALGEBRA: Introduce a sealed invocation admission and ledger whose resource kinds cannot be confused or cloned. Work units, poll opportunities, monetary or energy cost, and evaluation counts are affine consumables. Memory is a reservation lease with current, peak, and retained bytes; child leases may be nested but cannot double-reserve or outlive the parent. Output is bounded capacity charged on retained publication. Deadline is an absolute monotonic horizon checked through a deterministic clock abstraction, not a decrementing copyable counter. Accuracy/error is an obligation or tolerance contract, not spendable work. Capability is authority, not capacity. Child slices are non-cloneable affine leases with unique IDs; unused consumables and released memory may return exactly once to the parent, while spent amounts and elapsed time never replenish. Checked conservation equations and dimensional types prevent cross-kind transfer, duplication, overflow, and negative remaining values.

EXECUTION SCOPE: Preflight the complete cross-crate work, memory, deadline, poll, cost, evaluation, and output shape. Pass capability-scoped child leases to fs-asbuilt and fs-assimilate and use the shared-poll API or typed successor. Remove duplicate misfit traversals because the returned posterior retains before/after values. Charge setup, canonicalization, formatting/log construction, identity hashing, checkpointing if any, and final publication. Retain exact admitted, reserved, consumed, released, returned, peak, remaining, phase, child, and terminal receipts. Raw counters are diagnostics only. Cancellation is request, drain, finalize with no acceptance-capable partial StageLog.

TESTS: G0 exact-boundary and one-below values for every resource kind and child seam; zero and already-expired deadlines under a deterministic clock; memory lease nesting, release, peak and retained bytes; output capacity; cost/work/poll overflow; duplicated, stale, overclaiming, double-return, or post-parent child leases; dimension mismatch; and deterministic error ordering. G3 equivalent legal decompositions conserve the same totals and units. G4 injects cancellation, timeout, allocation failure, and faults at every phase and final publication, proving no task, arena, memory lease, or authority leak. G5 replays numeric results, identities, and ordered receipts across thread counts. Add a production no-mock E2E script with bounded structured logs naming invocation and child IDs, resource kinds/units, admitted/reserved/consumed/released/returned/peak values, deadline observations, cancellation/drain/finalize, and disposition.

ACCEPTANCE: no budget unit can be consumed, reserved, returned, or reissued contrary to its algebra anywhere in the complete stage. Exact-boundary success and one-below refusal are deterministic, nested APIs cannot recreate ambient authority, memory peaks and retained output are honest, and the retained report describes exactly the transaction runtime enforced.

title: fs-oed-e2e: canonicalize once and make EVPI action work and allocation accounting exact
description:
ROOT CAUSE: checked_evpi deep-clones every DesignEstimate, including names, and sorts the full menu on every call. expected_sensor_action_value invokes it at every predictive quadrature node for every action after another vector clone. At the admitted maximum this creates millions of record/string clones and many thousands of sorts, while CampaignWorkPlan charges mostly record visits rather than comparison bytes, allocation, cloning, and deallocation. The receipt therefore understates real campaign work and memory.

REPRESENTATION INVARIANT: Canonicalize unique candidate identity and order exactly once at campaign admission into an immutable opaque CanonicalDesignMenu. Preserve that order through planning and assimilation. Do not mutate and restore shared scratch. Instead expose a typed one-index MeanOverrideView that borrows the immutable menu, validates the selected index and finite overridden mean, and presents the substituted scalar only to the current allocation-free EVPI evaluation. The view is non-owning, cannot escape the call, cannot alter names or unaffected records, and makes stale restoration or cancellation-corrupted state impossible.

SCOPE: Implement an internal no-sort EVPI evaluator whose canonical-menu precondition is encoded by the type. Preflight immutable menu bytes, bounded view state, comparison work, quadrature/action evaluations, and retained outputs; make all allocations fallible. Charge every admission scan, record visit, comparison byte, quadrature evaluation, override read, hash byte, log byte, and finalization step with checked arithmetic. Bind canonical-order, quadrature, work, and identity policy versions into the retained report. Do not weaken the full multi-alternative scientific upgrade in sj31i.5.

TESTS: G0 covers empty, singleton, and maximum menus; duplicate/confusable identity refusal; finite override/index checks; input permutation invariance; exact ties; long bounded names; allocation refusal; work overflow; and exact-boundary/one-below accounting. Type/API tests prove the canonical menu is immutable and the override view cannot outlive or mutate it. G3 compares the old independent oracle with the new evaluator bitwise on canonical fixtures and semantically under permutations, and verifies one-index views equal an independently rebuilt menu. G4 cancels or faults at every admission, action, node, view construction/read, checker, log, and publication boundary with no stale mutation or partial report. G5 replays order, numerics, identity, and receipts across runs and thread counts. Add benchmarks and a real no-mock campaign E2E with bounded structured logs for menu identity/size, canonicalization comparisons and bytes, view target, quadrature/action counts, admitted and consumed work, peak/retained bytes, cancellation/drain/finalize, and disposition.

ACCEPTANCE: canonical sorting occurs once per admitted immutable menu; per-node evaluation is allocation-free and O(n); cancellation cannot corrupt shared state; accounting upper-bounds every resource-driving operation; and maximum-shape campaigns cannot hide clone or sort amplification behind a record-visit receipt.

title: fs-assimilate correlated batches: stable whitening or block factor updates with joint receipts
description:
PURPOSE AND DEPENDENCY INTENT: Preserve and complete the correlated-observation scope split out of sj31i.37 so the independent O(n^2) scalar root fix is not unnecessarily blocked. This leaf starts only after sj31i.37 provides a certified deterministic factor-update substrate and sj31i.16 provides explicit calibration and registration covariance groups. The split changes scheduling, not ambition or functionality.

SCOPE: model correlated observation blocks with declared covariance, units, source identity, grouping semantics, and authority. Admit each block with tri-state PSD certification and fail closed on unresolved covariance. Implement stable deterministic whitening, block square-root information filtering, or block QR without forming avoidable normal equations or dense I-KH products. Canonicalize block order, pivot and factor signs, rank decisions, and tie breaks. Propagate joint calibration and registration uncertainty exactly according to the declared model. Produce source-bound receipts for posterior covariance, Loewner contraction, innovation/misfit, rank, factor residual, conditioning, consumed work/memory/poll/deadline budgets, and explicit Certified, Refuted, or Unresolved dispositions. Use checked work algebra, aggregate fallible scratch allocation, bounded cancellation tiles, request-drain-finalize, and non-authoritative partial diagnostics only.

SCIENTIFIC BOUNDARY: Whitening or a successful factorization is not by itself proof that the covariance model is correct. Separate numerical validity, statistical-model assumptions, provenance, and authenticated authority. Do not silently diagonalize, tolerance-clamp negative curvature, invent independence, or promote an unresolved rank decision.

TESTS AND EVIDENCE: G0 covers 1x1 equivalence to the scalar path, exact singular PSD blocks, indefinite and interval-unresolved blocks, unit/dimension mismatch, duplicate group membership, checked arithmetic, allocator refusal, and deterministic error precedence. G1/G2 cover manufactured jointly Gaussian updates and canonical correlated-sensor benchmarks. G3 covers block permutation under the declared policy, equivalent whitening/factor representations, unit rescaling, splitting and recombining independent blocks, and comparison with a high-precision or dense independent oracle. G4 injects cancellation, deadline, quota, and allocation failure at admission, factorization, solve, covariance update, receipt construction, and publication, proving no leak or partial authority. G5 replays identities and numerical outputs across thread counts and supported ISAs. Add a real no-mock multi-sensor assimilation E2E with structured logs for group/source IDs, units, covariance certificate, factor method, rank/conditioning bounds, admitted and consumed budgets, contraction and misfit receipts, cancellation/drain/finalize, and no-claim state.

ACCEPTANCE: correlated and block updates are stable, budgeted, deterministic, jointly source-aware, independently checked, and never reuse scalar independence assumptions. The 1x1 specialization agrees with sj31i.37, and every advertised joint contraction has executable evidence or an honest unresolved/refused result.

title: fs-scenario: make parsing, validation, and realization fail closed under hostile inputs
description: ROOT CAUSE: scenario IR can recurse and allocate without explicit limits; chebfun decoding calls an asserting constructor and panics on malformed domain/coefficients; spectral realization admits nonfinite duration and unchecked sample/work counts that can return empty NaN results, overflow, run quadratically, or attempt catastrophic allocation; several signal/frame/environment/band validators let NaN pass because comparisons with NaN are false. TESTS: catch_unwind-free malformed cheb cases, nesting/node/byte limits, NaN/inf/subnormal duration and dt, sample/work cap boundaries, allocation arithmetic, NaN table/order/ramp/frame/contact/environment/Carreau bands, PSD overflow, and valid large-budget opt-in. title: fs-qty: reject exponent narrowing traps and nonfinite literals
description: ROOT CAUSE: fs-qty parses unit exponents into i8 before enforcing the public absolute-exponent cap. The value -128 reaches i8::MIN.abs(), which panics in checked builds and may evade the cap in optimized builds. Quantity parsing and scaling also admit nonfinite values such as 1e999m and overflowed prefix products into authoritative Qty/IR paths. SCOPE: accumulate exponents in a wider checked integer, enforce every intermediate and final cap before narrowing, reject nonfinite raw/scaled/affine/final values, and preserve precise parse offsets. TESTS: m^-128, Pa^127, repeated positive/negative products and divisions, exact cap/cap+1, 1e999, 1e999m, 1e308TW, prefix overflow, debug/release no-panic, and IR defensive refusal. ACCEPTANCE: no textual quantity can panic, wrap, saturate, or produce a nonfinite authoritative value; valid boundary exponents remain deterministic.

title: Skip SELL padding in chunk-major SpMV
description: SELL chunk-major and sharded SpMV unconditionally FMA every physical slot through kmax, including zero-filled padding. Guard each lane by its logical row length while preserving explicitly stored zero entries and real-operation order; add a focused cross-format signed-zero regression. title: Admit fs-io catalog schemas and unify bounded CSV/JSON projection
description:
ROOT CAUSE
The public Schema { columns: Vec<ColumnSpec> } is presently an unchecked authority input. Callers can supply an empty or enormous schema, empty or duplicate names, names whose CSV trim semantics alias, and Number bounds containing NaN/infinity or min > max. Both catalog readers then traverse that unchecked vector per row and build numeric projection maps. CatalogJsonLimits bounds parsed JSON syntax/payload, but it does not admit schema cardinality, schema-name bytes, rows-times-columns validation work, numeric projection entries/key bytes, diagnostics, or all simultaneously live output/scratch storage. The CSV path has no equivalent input/row/header/member/string/decoded/output envelope and performs infallible growth and clone-heavy materialization. Duplicate trimmed CSV headers can collapse when inserted into BTreeMap, making the selected value ambiguous. A syntactically bounded document can therefore trigger unbounded schema-driven work/memory or ambiguous projection.

MISSION
Make schema validity and the complete parse-plus-validate-plus-project resource envelope explicit, typed, deterministic, and shared across CSV and JSON. Preserve the strict JSON work already landed; do not weaken accepted functionality. Fail before authoritative work whenever declared limits cannot cover the schema or worst-case projection, and retain precise row/column/byte diagnostics without allocating attacker-sized messages.

DELIVERABLES
- Introduce a fallible admitted-schema constructor/receipt (or an equivalently sealed admitted Schema) with a versioned deterministic identity. Validate bounded nonempty column/name counts and name bytes, unique names under the exact lookup/trim normalization used by each format, and finite ordered inclusive Number bounds. Define empty-schema, optional-field, unknown-column, column-order, and duplicate-header policies explicitly. Keep raw unchecked construction from serving as authority.
- Introduce a common catalog read/projection budget that composes format syntax limits with schema-driven validation work, rows-times-columns visits, numeric conversions, numeric map entries/key bytes, retained Catalog rows/numbers, scratch, and bounded diagnostic witnesses. Use checked arithmetic and reject overflow. JSON limits must cover the whole operation rather than stop at parser output; CSV gains explicit input/header/row/field/token/decoded/aggregate caps.
- Refuse duplicate CSV headers after the documented normalization before map insertion; never silently overwrite/collapse aliases. Specify and test whether extra document columns are preserved or refused and ensure the policy is identical or intentionally documented across CSV/JSON.
- Replace avoidable cell/key/row cloning with ownership-aware projection; use try_reserve/checked growth wherever containers permit it and document unavoidable allocator no-claim boundaries. No partial authoritative Catalog may escape allocation, syntax, schema, budget, or cancellation failure.
- Return structured deterministic errors distinguishing schema-definition refusal, document syntax, document-to-schema mismatch, resource exhaustion, and allocation failure. Error witnesses must be bounded and identify the first deterministic offender.
- Bind schema identity, format/parser version, exact limits, consumed counters, input identity hook, row/member counts, and result/no-claim status into a receipt suitable for HELM/ledger promotion. Do not treat non-cryptographic local fingerprints as authority.

GAUNTLET
G0 covers empty/max/over-limit schemas; empty/duplicate/normalization-alias names; NaN, infinite, equal, inverted, and extreme finite bounds; duplicate/extra/missing headers and object members; every exact resource boundary; checked-arithmetic overflow; allocation refusal hooks; and deterministic tie/first-error behavior. G3 proves CSV/JSON semantic equivalence for the common subset, column/member permutation invariance where promised, whitespace/escape-preserving JSON rewrites, quoted-CSV rewrites, unit-rescaled numeric range cases, and identity sensitivity to every authoritative policy/limit. G4 injects denial/cancellation at every growth and projection boundary and proves no leaks, no partial Catalog/receipt, bounded diagnostics, and byte-identical retry. G5 freezes admitted-schema and receipt bytes across runs/thread counts on the supported deterministic envelope.

NO-CLAIM UNTIL CLOSED
The current Schema is not admitted; CatalogJsonLimits does not bound total schema-validation/projection work or output storage; parse_csv is not a resource-admitted world boundary; duplicate normalized headers and invalid numeric-bound definitions are not certified safe. The strict JSON grammar fix remains useful but does not close these authority/resource gaps.

title: fs-ad Real trait: add acos/asin/atan(2) for eigenvalue-derivative consumers (Ogden hyperelasticity)
description: fs-material's Ogden law needs principal-stretch derivatives, i.e. eigenvalues of C=F^T F differentiated through fs-ad duals. The closed-form symmetric-3x3 eigenvalue route (Cardano/trigonometric) needs acos on the generic scalar, and robust variants want atan2. The fs-ad Real trait currently exposes sin/cos/tanh/exp/ln/sqrt/powi but no inverse trig, and orphan rules prevent downstream crates from extending it. Ask: add acos (and ideally asin/atan/atan2) to Real + the Dual chain rules (d/dx acos = -1/sqrt(1-x^2), guard |x|->1), plus gradcheck coverage. Unblocks the staged Ogden law documented as a no-claim in crates/fs-material/CONTRACT.md.
close_reason: Inverse trig shipped end-to-end. fs-math det: asin/acos via atan2 on the FACTORED complement sqrt((1-x)(1+x)) — endpoint-conditioned (1-x^2 cancels at |x|->1); ASIN_ULP_BUDGET=6, measured worst 3 over 200k samples vs platform libm; asin odd BITWISE; acos(+-1)={0,pi}, asin(+-1)=+-pi/2 exact via atan2's IEEE table; |x|>1 -> NaN; reflection + pi/2 identities gated at the identity's own scale (the pi-acos form inflates conditioning ~16x — measured 7 ULP, documented in battery + CONTRACT). fs-ad: Real trait gained asin/acos/atan/atan2 (f64 -> det::*, verified no external implementors); Dual chain rules — asin' 1/sqrt((1-x)(1+x)), acos' negated, atan' 1/(1+x^2), atan2 binary partials (x dy - y dx)/(x^2+y^2) with NaN-honest origin. Gradcheck: inverse gauntlet vs central FD (500 pts rel<5e-9), primal BITWISE vs scalar path, analytic first derivatives at 5 points + atan2 partials in all quadrants incl. x<0 pi-branch, second derivative asin'' via nested duals to 1e-13, honest endpoints (asin'(1)=+inf; acos'(-1)=-inf since acos DECREASES — the first test draft wrongly expected +inf, caught by the battery). Ogden no-claim in fs-material CONTRACT updated: upstream blocker RESOLVED, staged Ogden law remains that crate's follow-up. Lanes: fs-math full suite green (incl. untouched det golden hash), fs-ad 22/22, clippy -D warnings 0 both, fmt, ubs 0 critical both, xtask clean for these crates.

THIS bead = the scale/fidelity lanes: (a) TuRBO-class trust-region BO for 30-300d (local GPs in adaptive hyperrectangles, success/failure counters for expansion/shrink, restart on collapse; acceptance = published-class performance on 100d benchmarks e.g. Ackley-100 vs the landed CMA-ES baseline, ledgered ERT); (b) MULTI-FIDELITY: cost-aware acquisition (cost-weighted EI / knowledge-gradient class) over a fidelity-indexed kernel (e.g. downsampling kernel k((x,m),(x',m')) or linear discrepancy model per evidence-model-ledger); acceptance = correct cheap-vs-expensive allocation on synthetic two-fidelity fixtures with KNOWN correlation, cost-to-target documented win vs single-fidelity; (c) INDUCING-POINT sparse GPs beyond ~1e4 points (Nystrom/variational, fs-la-randomized machinery) with accuracy-vs-exact gates on subsampled fixtures; (d) FrankenTorch TAPE gradients through the q-EI reparameterization (the fixed-bank acquisition surface is differentiable by construction: mu(X) + L(X)z needs dL/dX through Cholesky - ft has the tape; replaces CMA-ES inner argmax where dimension makes it worthwhile); (e) heteroscedastic noise from UQ variance estimates + e-process-compatible stopping (coordinate with fs-uq bead tfz.25 when it lands). title: fs-roofline tune-ledger write corrupts on x86-64 (fsqlite 'page freed in concurrent transaction')
close_reason: fsqlite upstream regression (frankensqlite#123, bisected to d1a543e); fs-ledger tune_put rerouted UPDATE-then-INSERT in 0e4534c; rf_004 fail->pass verified on ts1, both-ISA suites green

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
DETERMINISTIC x86-64-ONLY CORRUPTION (found via cross-ISA verification on ts1,
Threadripper 5975WX, Zen 3; the ARM-only CI fleet cannot see this). Reproduce:
  cargo test -p fs-roofline --test conformance rf_004 --release
  -> rf_004_staleness_alerts_on_fingerprint_drift PANICS at conformance.rs:373:
     `inject valid-JSON payload corruption: Sql { context: "tune upsert", detail:
      "database disk image is malformed: page 52 was freed earlier in concurrent
       transaction 5" }`
3/3 runs fail with the IDENTICAL page (52) and transaction (5) -> deterministic,
not a flaky race. The failing op is a normal `tune_put` WRITE to the tune ledger
(fs-roofline -> fs-ledger -> fsqlite), during the test's setup that overwrites a
row with "{}" to exercise CorruptEvidence detection; fsqlite's own page manager
reports the DB image malformed BEFORE the write completes.

PASSES on aarch64 (M4) — so it is x86-specific: an fsqlite MVCC/page-management
edge case (a page freed by an internal "concurrent transaction" then referenced),
OR an fs-ledger/fs-roofline transaction pattern (atomic evidence transaction +
rollback + row reuse, crates/fs-roofline/src/kernels.rs:640-838) that fsqlite
tolerates on aarch64 but corrupts on x86.

IMPACT: (1) fs-roofline conformance is RED on x86 (rf_004). (2) The tune ledger is
the SAME fsqlite store the fz2.7 perf-baseline infra (FRANKENSIM_BASELINE_STORE)
writes to — so promoting/writing perf baselines on the Threadrippers likely hits
this too, blocking honest x86 perf rows. Next step: minimal fsqlite repro of the
tune_put write sequence on x86 to localize (fsqlite page-free-in-txn vs fs-ledger
transaction reuse); relates to the existing fsqlite bug bead lar1.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: CLAIMED (CloudyFinch — the cross-ISA forensics lane; also the author of the c40j baseline tooling this blocks). Plan: (1) reproduce rf_004 on ts1 at HEAD; (2) extract the exact tune_put SQL sequence from fs-ledger and replay it in a minimal fsqlite-only program on x86 to classify fsqlite-upstream vs fs-ledger-misuse (lar1 precedent: re-verify against current fsqlite before filing); (3) land the fix or a documented workaround, rf_004 green on BOTH ISAs, close with the classification. Reservations: crates/fs-ledger tune paths if the fault is ours; a scratch repro program otherwise; fs-roofline conformance only if the test itself needs a fix.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LOCALIZED (frankensim-side triage; the residual bug is fsqlite-core). Findings:

1. tune_put is a PLAIN UPSERT (fs-ledger/src/lib.rs:1666): `INSERT INTO tune(...)
   ON CONFLICT(kernel,shape_class,machine) DO UPDATE SET params=..., measured=...`.
   No explicit DELETE/VACUUM; but the DO UPDATE reorganizes the tune B-tree page.

2. tune_put is CLEAN IN ISOLATION on x86 — fs-ledger's own suite (incl.
   tune_upserts, many sequential tune_put) is GREEN on x86 (my batch-3 run). So
   tune_put alone does NOT corrupt. The trigger is ACCUMULATED STATE.

3. The distinguishing element in rf_004 vs the passing fs-ledger tests:
   `record_run(...)` (conformance.rs:277) runs fs-roofline's ATOMIC EVIDENCE
   TRANSACTION (crates/fs-roofline/src/kernels.rs:640-838 — explicit begin/commit,
   op + tune rows written together, rollback-with-retry-marker path). That
   transaction frees B-tree pages onto the freelist. The LATER standalone tune_put
   UPSERT then reuses one of those freed pages, and fsqlite reports "page 52 was
   freed earlier in concurrent transaction 5" — transaction 5 == the evidence txn.

HYPOTHESIS: fsqlite freelist/MVCC page-reuse across a transaction boundary is
mis-tracked on x86-64 (a page freed inside the committed evidence transaction is
still seen as owned by that snapshot when a later write reuses it). aarch64 handles
the same sequence correctly (rf_004 GREEN on M4), so it is an x86-specific fsqlite
core bug, NOT fs-ledger/fs-roofline misuse (both ops are normal).

MINIMAL-REPRO DIRECTION for the fsqlite owner: {open ledger; run one explicit
multi-write transaction that frees a tune/B-tree page; commit; then a standalone
UPSERT that reuses the freed page} on x86 — should reproduce without the rest of
the roofline machinery. FRANKENSIM-SIDE MITIGATION if an fsqlite fix is far off:
force a WAL checkpoint (or a fresh Connection) between record_run and the next
tune_put so the freelist is reconciled before reuse — a workaround, not a fix.
Relates to lar1 (other fsqlite reparse bug). Blocks fz2.7 baseline promotion on x86.

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
MITIGATION TEST — reconnection does NOT work (refines the diagnosis). Inserted a
fresh `Ledger::open(&db)` (new fsqlite Connection to the same file) immediately
before the corrupting tune_put in rf_004, on ts1/x86. STILL FAILS identically
(conformance.rs:374, "page 52 was freed earlier in concurrent transaction 5").

CONSEQUENCE: the malformation is PERSISTED IN THE DB FILE by record_run's evidence
transaction (transaction 5) — it is NOT a live per-connection snapshot/cache
artifact (a fresh connection reads the same corrupt on-disk freelist state). So the
bug is WRITE-SIDE: record_run's committed transaction writes the freelist/MVCC
page-free bookkeeping for page 52 INCORRECTLY on x86, and fsqlite's integrity check
fires when the later tune_put upsert tries to reuse that page. This is squarely an
fsqlite-core freelist/page-free bug on x86-64; there is NO frankensim-side
reconnection workaround. (A full VACUUM between record_run and tune_put would rebuild
the freelist and likely mask it, but that is heavy and still a workaround, not a
fix.) The proper fix is in fsqlite's freelist page-free bookkeeping on x86 —
recommend an fsqlite-direct repro: one committed transaction that frees a b-tree
page, then a fresh write that reuses it, on x86, checking the on-disk freelist +
per-page "freed-by-txn" bookkeeping for an x86 mis-encode (endianness/width/layout).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
LOCALIZED + FIXED (workaround landed 0e4534c). Root cause is an fsqlite UPSTREAM regression, not fs-ledger misuse.

Mechanism: INSERT..ON CONFLICT..DO UPDATE on the tune table corrupts the DB ('page N was freed earlier in concurrent transaction M') when the conflict seek lands after a leaf split. Geometry-gated: needs 3 tune rows with measured ~1265B (600B and 2000B both dodge it); 2 rows fine; plain UPDATE fine; REPLACE INTO fine; DO NOTHING fine; same-size DO UPDATE also corrupts (not about shrinking). Pragmas/journal mode irrelevant.

Bisected frankensqlite 75ba1b7ed..46caaa9 (58 commits) with a raw fsqlite-only repro: first bad commit d1a543e 'fix(btree): rebuild rootless cursor path before INSERT OR REPLACE (bd-kwei8)' - its seek-cache fast path now always leaves a rootless single-entry cursor stack, and the guards it added to delete/table_insert do NOT cover the upsert's DO UPDATE mutation path, so balance treats the leaf as root and double-frees.

Filed upstream with minimal repro + bisect: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankensqlite/issues/123 (lar1 precedent).

NOT ISA-specific: reproduces on M4/macOS too at fsqlite HEAD. rf_004 only LOOKED x86-only because macOS receipt JSON lengths dodge the 1265B window. Heads-up: I fast-forwarded the local Mac frankensqlite clone to 46caaa9 (upstream HEAD, matches ts1) - if any fsqlite-backed test suddenly fails with 'page N freed earlier', it is frankensqlite#123, not your change.

Workaround: tune_put now UPDATE-then-INSERT (equivalent under single-writer-per-connection), doc-marked for revert once #123 fixed. Evidence: ts1 rf_004 fail 3/3 before -> conformance 8/8 + fs-ledger 77/0 after; local fs-ledger 87/0, rf_004 green. (Local rf_001 EnvironmentInvalid on the loaded M4 is the known busy-host artifact, pre-exists this change, passes on ts1.)

title: fs-evidence V&V: reject signed-zero aliases in canonical derived state and metric specs
description: The V&V codec preserves exact IEEE-754 bits, but two semantic/canonical gates use ordinary f64 PartialEq inconsistently. First, VvCase applicability validation compares caller-retained DomainViolation::Numeric values with a freshly derived decision using PartialEq, so +0.0 and -0.0 compare equal even though they encode to different bytes; a forged signed-zero bound survives canonical fixed-point decoding and mints a second content hash for derived state. Second, QoiValidationPlan sorts metric specs by raw-bit key and then deduplicates via semantic PartialEq; [+0.0, 1.0, -0.0] leaves the equal signed-zero endpoints nonadjacent, admitting logically duplicate NormalizedDiscrepancy specs. Acceptance: derived applicability equality is bit-exact for every numeric field; metric canonical keys normalize semantic zero so signed-zero duplicates are adjacent and refused; codec and model share one ordering rule; canonical decode refuses an opposite-sign derived bound and a duplicate signed-zero metric sequence; honest exact-sign values and a single -0.0 remain representable; static checks pass and centralized Cargo/DSR proof remains pending.
close_reason: Completed; centralized RCH union j-29933316048158806 green and fs-evidence signed-zero regressions passed.

title: Canonicalize duplicate bridge nodes before emitting refusal diagnostics
description: RB.M1 sorts theorem nodes only by author-chosen node ID. Rust stable sorting preserves caller order among duplicate IDs, but validation emits per-node issues immediately, so reversing two different same-ID nodes can reverse DuplicateNode and InvalidScopeDimension or other semantic issues. This violates the bridge CONTRACT requirement that diagnostics follow canonical node order. title: Make fs-ivl finite-overflow arithmetic outward-enclosing
description: ROOT CAUSE: Interval::Add/Sub/Mul/Div nudge only finite rounded endpoints. When finite admitted operands overflow a lower endpoint to +infinity (or an upper endpoint to -infinity), down_k/up_k pass infinity through. Examples such as Interval::point(f64::MAX)+Interval::point(f64::MAX) or same-sign finite products yield [+inf,+inf] or [-inf,-inf], excluding the exact finite-real result beyond the representable f64 range. Existing guards cover NaN from indeterminate infinities and exp overflow, but not finite-operation overflow. This violates fs-ivl's foundational claim that every operation encloses the true real image and propagates into fs-rep-neural IBP. MISSION: repair basic interval arithmetic globally with sign-aware representable one-sided bounds (for example [MAX,+inf] or [-inf,-MAX]) or an honest WHOLE fallback whenever finite operands overflow; preserve valid extended-real operand semantics; never turn an actual infinity input into an unsupported finite-real story. Add independent high-precision/exact-sign G0 oracles for positive/negative add/sub/mul/div overflow, mixed cancellation, subnormal boundaries, zero-times-infinity, and nextafter edges; G3 equivalent-rewrite and scaling mutations; one-ULP endpoint mutants; deterministic replay. Audit width/midpoint/intersection consumers and Taylor/Affine layers for inherited non-finite assumptions. Update CONTRACT/no-claim language. ACCEPTANCE: no finite exact-real image is excluded; malformed or indeterminate extended operations fail closed; neural finite-input IBP inherits sound overflow behavior; focused fs-ivl, fs-rep-neural, fs-neuroshape-e2e, nested fs-wasm, clippy, and DSR union green. title: fs-rep-neural: Lipschitz certificate can under-bound (power-iteration spectral norm)
description:
Deep-review hunt (2026-07-12), LOW confidence/priority — a soundness nit, not a practically-triggering bug.

## Claim vs mechanism
fs-rep-neural certifies a Lipschitz UPPER bound L = Π spectral_norm(layer) (× 1-Lipschitz tanh) as safe sphere-trace fuel (safe_step_radius = |f|/L must never tunnel). But spectral_norm (lib.rs ~75) is POWER ITERATION, which approaches sigma_max FROM BELOW (||Wv|| <= sigma_max for unit v). So the recorded L can be slightly BELOW the true global Lipschitz constant — an UPPER-bound certificate computed from a LOWER estimate. spectral_normalize scales by bound/sigma_hat with sigma_hat <= sigma_true, so the normalized matrix's TRUE spectral norm is >= bound, compounding the same direction.

## Why tests stay green
With ~200 iterations on the small, well-separated sample matrices the gap is ~1e-12, and the conformance assertions carry +1e-6/+1e-4 slack (neural.rs the_lipschitz_certificate_is_never_violated, the_gradient_is_bounded_by_the_lipschitz_constant), which absorbs it. The 2026-07-12 test-range fix (commit 44a3dd1, widening points() from [-1,0) to the documented [-1,1)) confirmed the cert holds over the FULL domain to ~1e-6 for the sample net. So this is theoretical, not a live tunneling risk on the tested fixtures.

## Fix (changes numerics -> golden concern, cross-ISA-blocked from M4)
For a GUARANTEED upper bound, round the spectral-norm estimate UP: add a convergence-gap margin (e.g. the last Rayleigh-quotient residual, or one more upper-bounding step), OR use a cheap submultiplicative upper bound (sqrt(||W||_1 * ||W||_inf) or Frobenius) as a guaranteed ceiling and take min with a refined estimate. Any change shifts L's last ULPs -> re-check/repin any fs-rep-neural golden and cross-ISA verify per golden-bump-protocol (cannot verify x86 from this aarch64 host). Coordinates with frankensim-lyms (the det::tanh determinism fix in the same crate also shifts eval bits) — do both together in one golden re-pin.

Kill criterion: if no consumer relies on fs-rep-neural's L as a HARD safety bound (vs an advisory estimate), downgrade to documenting L as 'estimate, not certified upper bound' instead of hardening the math.
