comments.text:
Deep soundness audit of the certificate spine (fs-evidence, fs-ivl, fs-sos,
fs-spectral) via 3 adversarial review agents + independent verification. Each
finding below has a CONFIRMED concrete counterexample. Ranked; [FIX] = fixing
now, [BEAD] = needs careful/research-grade fix, tracked here.

== fs-sos ==
S1 [FIX, HIGH] is_psd / lyapunov_certifies_stability forge FALSE certificates on
   non-symmetric input. min_eigenvalue's cyclic-Jacobi reads only the upper
   triangle; a non-symmetric matrix returns garbage (raw diagonal when upper-tri
   is 0). Counterexample: A=[[0,-1],[-1,0]] (eigenvalues +/-1, UNSTABLE) with
   non-symmetric P=[[1,0],[3,1]] -> lyapunov_certifies_stability = TRUE (false
   cert). Fix: symmetrize (M+Mᵀ)/2 in min_eigenvalue (correct quadratic-form
   semantics; midpoint(x,x)==x so symmetric input is bitwise-unchanged).
   CONFIRMED reproduced + FIXED (regression test added).
S2 [BEAD, MED-HIGH] SosCertificate::verify uses the coefficient ∞-norm, which
   does NOT bound the polynomial's value on ℝ. A tiny-residual cert can have
   p(x0) < lower_bound by an unbounded amount. Counterexample (tol=1e-9):
   squares=[x-1e6], lower_bound=0, p=(x-1e6)²-1e-9-1e-9·x -> residual≈9.3e-10 ≤
   tol -> verify=TRUE, but p(1e6)≈-9.8e-4 < 0. Violation scales with root
   location (unbounded for any fixed tol>0). Fix is non-trivial (rigorous SOS
   needs PSD-Gram verification or exact-zero residual, not a coeff-norm tol) —
   deferred to a careful fix so I don't ship a wrong one.

== fs-evidence ==
E1 [FIX, HIGH] color::compose does NOT round outward, so a composed
   Verified{lo,hi} is not a guaranteed enclosure (the sibling
   NumericalCertificate::compose in lib.rs DOES round outward — one ulp each
   way). Counterexample: compose(V{0.1,0.1}, V{0.2,0.2}, Add) -> lo=hi=
   0.30000000000000004, but the true real sum 0.1_f64+0.2_f64 = 0.3000…0166 is
   below lo -> the "Verified" interval EXCLUDES the exact answer. Also Mul
   (4 round-to-nearest products). Fix: outward-round Add/Mul like lib.rs.
E2 [FIX/BEAD, MED] color::compose Mul (and lib.rs Mul) fold NaN products (0×∞)
   with f64::min/max which DROP NaN -> lo=+∞,hi=−∞ inverted interval marked
   Verified. NaN-guard the fold.
E3 [FIX, MED] disjoint validated regimes demote to Estimated{dispersion:0.0}
   (claims ZERO spread) instead of ∞; the demote() path correctly uses ∞.
E4 [BEAD, MED-LOW] enclosure()/estimate() drop a NaN bound via min/max (silent

V1 [BEAD, HIGH] orient3d_sos violates ANTISYMMETRY (SoS is contradictory). The
   coplanar tie-break orient2d_sos_about ignores the 4th point's position (only

title: fs-sparse-perf: >=85% STREAM SpMV, tiled parallel assembly, SIMD kernels, CCD sharding, fnx/fnp interop
description:

Headline invariant PROVEN AND TESTED: CSR == BSR == SELL SpMV BITWISE (ascending-column mul_add accumulation from +0.0 start; BSR fill zeros provably inert; see crates/fs-sparse/src/bsr.rs module docs for the signed-zero argument). Cross-ISA golden hash 0xbcf552b6c5bfaed6 identical on M4 Pro and Threadripper. CONTRACT.md complete; No-claim boundaries there enumerate exactly what THIS bead owes:

1. ROOFLINE GATE (the original bead acceptance criterion): SpMV >=85% of measured STREAM triad (fs-substrate bandwidth module) at large sizes on BOTH reference machines, release profile, attainment ledgered as fs-obs events. Requires: compact u32 col indices (halve index traffic - CSR spmv is index-bandwidth-bound), per-CCD row-range sharding with first-touch on TR (plan section 14.2 - this is what makes 85% achievable there), software prefetch with autotuned distance (autotuner bead wf9.12), SELL-C-sigma SIMD kernel via fs-tilelang (wf9.11) with lane width = C matched to NEON/AVX-512.
2. DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT on the SIMD lane: SELL SIMD kernel must either preserve bitwise equality with the scalar CSR kernel (per-lane sequential accumulation preserves per-row order - the layout was DESIGNED so lanes are independent rows, making this free) or record a justified golden-hash bump. The pad-slot inertness argument must be revisited if the kernel reads pads: pads are (col=0, val=0.0) and a fused 0*x+acc is exactly acc EXCEPT acc=-0.0 with product +0.0 - the scalar analysis in sell.rs holds because acc starts +0.0 and cannot become -0.0; a SIMD kernel reading pads inherits the same proof shape.
3. Tiled PARALLEL assembly on fs-exec: the accumulation-order contract is already stated in CONTRACT.md Invariant 2 (per-(row,col) contribution order is logical identity) - implement tile-local staging + deterministic merge, verify bitwise equality vs serial assembly across thread counts (the full G5 criterion).
4. SpMM blocked/SIMD lane for block-Krylov/POD workloads.
5. Graph views for FrankenNetworkx + array views for FrankenNumpy (constellation interop; Csr::row already IS the adjacency view - wrap, do not copy).
6. Optional: hash-SPA SpGEMM for very wide matrices (dense SPA is O(ncols) scratch per row today).

Acceptance harness already in place: tests/conformance.rs golden-hash battery (any kernel change must keep it green or justify a bump), 19 in-crate tests incl adversarial patterns. Perf numbers go in the bead comments + ledger. Cross-ISA pipeline: tar minimal workspace (fs-sparse has ZERO deps - single-crate bundle works) to trj:/data/tmp, extract into fresh mktemp -d, private CARGO_HOME/CARGO_TARGET_DIR, cargo test --offline detached, poll.

ROOFLINE GATE (the acceptance criterion): sharded compact CSR attains 0.950-1.083 of measured all-core STREAM on ts1 (Threadripper 5975WX, FS_SPARSE_ROOFLINE_GATE=1 assert GREEN across three runs); M4 Pro reports 0.55-0.72 honestly (loaded dev box +-25% run-to-run; equal-nnz shards let 4 E-cores drag the tail — heterogeneous-core scheduling is fz2.2's scope; FS_SPARSE_THREADS knob provided). title: Make beta and Dirichlet total for tiny positive shapes
description:
Root cause:
Stream::next_gamma uses the mathematically valid alpha<1 boost Gamma(alpha)=Gamma(alpha+1)*U^(1/alpha). For valid finite tiny positive alpha, the powered factor underflows to zero. When every gamma variate in next_beta or next_dirichlet underflows, the current direct normalization divides 0 by 0 and returns NaN components, contradicting fs-rand CONTRACT.md Error model ("Everything else total") and the simplex/range semantics.

Required fix:
Preserve the existing direct gamma values and ordinary-shape bit patterns. When direct normalization has a zero or non-finite total, deterministically replay the same checkpointed stream samples and normalize their log weights with an extended-range/scaled representation. Recovery must consume no additional logical draws, must remain cross-ISA strict-mode deterministic, and must not route through the fast ziggurat path.

Acceptance:
1. next_beta accepts every finite alpha,beta > 0 and returns a finite value in [0,1], including f64::MIN_POSITIVE shapes.
2. next_dirichlet accepts every non-empty finite-positive shape vector and returns finite non-negative components with a positive total normalized to one, including all-tiny and mixed-tiny shapes.
3. Extreme-shape tests prove bitwise replay equality and identical post-stream indices, demonstrating no hidden draw consumption.
4. Existing distribution golden hash and ordinary moment tests remain unchanged.
5. CONTRACT.md documents the fallback, determinism, and no-extra-consumption guarantee.
6. Focused fs-rand tests and clippy pass through RCH; ubs reports no unresolved true positives on changed files.
close_reason: Implemented scaled-log checkpoint replay for zero/non-finite gamma normalization; extreme smallest-subnormal, MIN_POSITIVE, mixed-tiny, and MAX-shape beta/Dirichlet outputs are finite, normalized, bitwise replay-safe, and consume no hidden draws. Distribution battery and -D warnings clippy pass via rch exec, with RCH reporting local fallback because all workers failed preflight; ubs found no unresolved true positives.

title: fs-topo penalty component_voxels mis-attributes two equal-minima excess components
description:
CORRECTNESS BUG in crates/fs-topo/src/penalty.rs (behind the moonshot-topo-persistence feature). Verified by reading the code.

## The bug
`component_voxels` (penalty.rs ~303) seeds its flood-fill by scanning for the FIRST voxel whose value equals `bar.birth`:
```
for (i, &v) in field.values.iter().enumerate() {
    if (v - bar.birth).abs() < 1e-12 { seed = Some(i); break; } // first-index-on-ties
}
```
The birth of an excess (island) component is that island's minimum field value. If two DISCONNECTED islands share the same minimum value, both of their persistence bars carry the same `bar.birth`, so the seed search returns the same (lowest-index) island for BOTH bars, and the flood collects that one island twice. The second island receives NO attribution. `component_voxels` re-derives the component by value-matching instead of tracking the union-find component `persistence0` actually built.

## Impact
`evaluate` (penalty.rs ~228) carves the least-persistent excess bars using these voxel sets. With two equal-minima islands, attribution-guided descent (`apply_attribution_step`) carves the first island twice and never touches the second, so it never reaches target topology — defeating the module's "graded, localized penalty beats count-only" claim.

## Trigger
A field with the main solid plus two disconnected islands carved to the SAME value (e.g. two corner islands at -0.9, main at -1.0, level 0). betti → b0=3; evaluate sees 3 alive bars and carves the two least-persistent (both birth=-0.9); both component_voxels calls seed the lowest-index island. Current tests use only a single island (tp_001, internal_basins), so they miss it. Common in quantized/synthetic fields (values like ±1.0, -0.9), rarer in continuous SDF data.

## Fix (option a, robust)
Localize from the persistence STRUCTURE, not by value. Have `persistence0` return, per bar, a representative voxel (the argmin voxel of that specific component, i.e. the one whose activation created the component) and pass it to `component_voxels` as the seed. Option (b, simpler): in `evaluate`, exclude already-attributed voxels from subsequent seed searches (skip seeds whose index is already in a prior attribution's set) so each excess component gets a distinct island — but (a) is principled since value-equality seeding cannot distinguish equal-minima components even in principle.

## Verification
Add a symmetric two-island fixture (two islands at equal minima) and assert each gets a distinct, non-overlapping attribution set and that descent reaches target topology. Build/test with `--features moonshot-topo-persistence`. Discovered during the deep-review bug hunt (medium confidence; feature-gated, not on the default/certified surface).

title: Stop fs-rep-voxel from minting false continuous distance authority
description: OccupancyChart evaluates a piecewise-constant signed center-to-center voxel metric, yet advertises C0 differentiability, a local Lipschitz constant of 1, and a rigorous plus-or-minus half-voxel-diagonal enclosure relative to the union-of-cubes region. A unit voxel at [0,0,0] queried on the x=1 face returns +1 with enclosure [about 0.134,1.866], excluding the true signed distance 0; the representative jumps from -1 to +1 across that face. Repair by publishing only estimate-grade center-metric error with a conservative full-diagonal resolution band for finite samples, removing continuity/Lipschitz claims, failing closed for non-finite bounds, and pinning the analytic face counterexample. Code-first static proof only; central fs-rep-voxel suite and DSR remain pending.

title: rf_001 conformance asserts NoTarget but contended hosts return EnvironmentInvalid
description:
fs-roofline tests/conformance.rs rf_001_registry_runs_and_reports asserts band == NoTarget for v0 report-only kernels, but on a loaded host (shared M4, load avg 11-17 with ~17 agent sessions) the axes probe classifies the environment as contaminated and the run comes back EnvironmentInvalid, failing the assert at conformance.rs:96. Reproduced twice locally at HEAD (2d38567-era) during u8og verification; same suite is 8/8 green on a quiet ts1. Pre-exists the u8og tune_put change (fails identically with and without it).

Options: assert a set {NoTarget, EnvironmentInvalid} for report-only kernels, or skip/soft-pass when the probe reports contamination (mirroring the environment_invalid neither-pass-nor-fail doctrine from dfh3 baseline governance). Owner of a4d6eb5 (feat(roofline): bind citable runs to trusted baselines) probably best placed - that commit most recently reshaped this test.
close_reason: fixture geometry bug, not contention: synthetic roofs sat below fast-core cache bandwidth, tripping the 1n61 attainment guard; roofs raised beyond any real machine in 34a8876, conformance 8/8 verified on loaded M4 and ts1

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Root cause was NOT host load - it was fixture geometry masquerading as both an ISA split and load-dependence. rf_001's synthetic_axes pinned a 100 GB/s single-thread roof; the conformance kernels run 4096 f64 elements (L2-resident), so an M4 P-core's cache bandwidth outruns that roof, attainment lands above 1.5, and the bead-1n61 guard (correctly) refuses to gate with EnvironmentInvalid. ts1's Zen 3 stays under 100 GB/s at that working set, hence 'passes on x86, fails on aarch64'. Load only moved the margin around.

Fix (34a8876): synthetic roofs raised to 100k/400k GB/s and 50k/300k GFLOPS in both conformance.rs and manifest_tamper.rs fixtures - these suites verify HARNESS logic per their own headers, so no real machine may ever outrun the fixture roof. plausibility_error has floors, not ceilings, so the values are legal; rf_002's BelowBand assertion only gets safer as attainment shrinks. Verified conformance 8/8 + tamper 4/4 on the M4 at load average 26 (rf_001 previously failed at ANY load there) and on ts1.

title: fs-evidence V&V: bind split rows to immutable source-row identities

title: Make Rep Router composition and search authority fail closed

The public oracle also remains mutable/unsnapshotted, PlanCostOracle exposes raw try_record authority, search is exponentially unbounded, learned means/p90 are not conservative bounds, and admission accepts declared certification without downgrade. title: fs-simd: safe GEMM facades permit pointer UB via overflow and post-final advances
description:
Fresh-eyes audit of commits f41c0cb/6d55c1b found two independent soundness failures in safe public SIMD GEMM facades.

1. Normal-input UB: both NEON batched kernels advance raw stream pointers after the final k load, temporarily creating pointers beyond one-past the allocation before rewinding. ptr.add requires the result to remain in-bounds or one-past even when it is not dereferenced. Ordinary fs-la calls with full mb=32 can reach this.
2. Overflow-admission UB: safe facades use unchecked usize multiplication/addition inside pre-unsafe bounds assertions. Release wrapping can make absurd dimensions pass, then raw pointer arithmetic escapes the slice. Affected surfaces include NEON mk8x4/btile4x4/btile4x4p, x86 mk8x4, and feature-gated SME2 gemm_tile_f32.

Root fix: introduce one checked slice-geometry helper in fs-simd; validate every public safe facade with checked_mul/checked_add before unsafe; eliminate post-final pointer advances or recompute offsets from checked bases; update SAFETY.md invariants. Preserve scalar/SIMD twin semantics.

Acceptance: release-mode regressions using usize::MAX dimensions refuse/panic before unsafe for every affected facade; normal full-batch paths have no transient out-of-allocation pointer formation; f32/f64/mixed batched batteries remain correct; relevant fs-simd/fs-la tests and clippy pass; unsafe registry and capsule size gates remain green.
close_reason: Fixed at HEAD, verified green on aarch64 (local) + x86_64 (ovh-a) at 96cae69+: checked slice-geometry refusal before every unsafe facade (d671cf1/b556d54) and rewind-free pointer discipline in all NEON/x86 batched kernels with boundary regression tests. Evidence in final comment.

title: Make fs-constraint interval proofs outward-enclosed and independently checkable
description:
ROOT CAUSE AND SEVERITY: fs-constraint's interval engine currently performs ordinary round-to-nearest binary64 arithmetic. Its dependency-aware interval formulas are mathematically conservative over exact reals, but round-to-nearest endpoints can move inward; a near-zero upper endpoint can therefore clear zero even when the real range does not. CONTRACT correctly discloses an fp-slack no-claim, yet Proven/ProofArtifact is the intended authority surface. A false certificate is Sev-0. Do not solve this by deleting interval proofs or globally widening to useless infinities: build the theorem-strength adaptive kernel the architecture intends.

MISSION: Move executable interval authority onto fs-ivl or a shared BEDROCK certified-arithmetic layer with directed/outward rounding for every supported primitive and composition. Establish an adaptive ladder: cheap directed binary64/EFT bounds, affine/Taylor or exact floating expansions near dependency/cancellation boundaries, and a deterministic exact or independently checkable fallback where practical. Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, powi, sqrt, exp, ln, tanh, min/max/abs, dot, and norm-square must either return an outward enclosure under explicit hypotheses or a typed no-claim refusal. Preserve shared-DAG linear work and logarithmic powi, exact zero-variable constants, one-Rn binding admission, graph caps, signed-zero/domain semantics, proof-subject identity, and the ability to prove useful real mechanisms; stronger new theorems about sufficient endpoint inflation or compositional rounding error are explicitly welcome when hypotheses and checkers are executable.

AUTHORITY AND CHECKING: Version the arithmetic theorem/kernel identity and bind it into ProofArtifact, ConstraintEvidence proof-bound receipts, problem/node/domain identity, operation inventory, capabilities, budgets, ISA/mode, and no-claim reason. A sealed independent checker must replay or validate every proof endpoint without trusting the producer's status bit. Until this successor is green, round-to-nearest results remain measured/fp-slack evidence and cannot silently promote default theorem authority. SOS intent remains distinct and is neither weakened nor simulated by an interval artifact.

GAUNTLET/ACCEPTANCE: G0 exact/max+1 and one-ULP boundary witnesses for every primitive, subnormals, min-normal transitions, signed zero, cancellation, overflow/underflow, division near zero, elementary-function domain edges, extreme powi, and malformed boxes. Exhaustively model-check a reduced floating format against exact rational/real or MPFR-like development-only oracles, plus independent high-precision spot checks for binary64. G1 manufactured polynomial/transcendental range problems verify enclosure and contraction order. G3 inclusion isotony, box refinement, algebraically equivalent rewrites, variable permutation, power-of-two scaling, shared-vs-expanded DAG, and exact-vs-adaptive-rung metamorphics; no rung may change a proved boolean verdict. G4 checked resource admission, allocation failure, cancellation at every graph/arithmetic/checker tile, cap/deadline boundaries, corrupt artifacts, no partial authority, and bounded logs. G5 bit-stable proof/checker receipts across runs, worker counts, and reference ISAs. Seed explicit near-zero false-clearance mutants by removing each outward step; the suite must kill them. Require central fs-ivl/fs-constraint all-targets, conformance, clippy, DSR, and retained checker artifacts before closure.
